item.title: Communications Director
item.description: Communications Director Organization: D.C. Policy Center Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 07/23/2026 ## Position Summary The D.C. Policy Center seeks a strategic, highly organized, and creative Communications Director to lead the organization’s communications strategy and ensure that our research informs policy conversations in the District of Columbia and beyond. Reporting to the Executive Director, this position serves as the bridge between research, communications, and policy engagement, helping shape how the Center’s work reaches policymakers, journalists, funders, and the public. The Communications Director will develop and execute communications strategies for research initiatives, oversee the Center’s website and publications, monitor emerging policy developments, coordinate the organization’s public engagement around legislation, hearings, and policy debates, and support Board engagement. The ideal candidate combines strategic thinking with strong project management skills and has demonstrated experience editing policy publications and producing high-quality communications materials. ## Key Responsibilities ### Strategic communications – Develop and implement the organization’s communications strategy to maximize the visibility, reach, and policy impact of the D.C. Policy Center’s work. – Design communications plans for major research reports, policy initiatives, events, and public announcements. – Identify opportunities to elevate the Center’s research through media, digital communications, newsletters, social media, speaking engagements, and partnerships. – Monitor communications performance and recommend strategies to expand audience engagement and influence. ### Research communications – Partner with policy researchers throughout the research process to develop communications campaigns for publications and events. – Translate complex policy analysis into clear, accessible messaging for policymakers, journalists, funders, and the public. – Coordinate publication schedules to ensure communications activities align with research milestones and organizational priorities. – Work with researchers to develop executive summaries, fact sheets, graphics, presentations, and other communications materials. ### Policy monitoring and public engagement – Monitor local and national policy developments relevant to the Center’s research priorities, including legislation, regulatory changes, committee hearings, budget proposals, and emerging policy debates. – Track opportunities for the D.C. Policy Center to contribute research and expertise to legislative and administrative processes. – Coordinate the preparation, editing, production, and submission of testimony, public comments, briefing materials, and other policy communications. – Maintain an organizational calendar of key policy events, hearings, publication opportunities, and external engagement deadlines. – Work closely with policy staff to ensure the Center’s research is timely, responsive, and positioned to inform current policy discussions. ### Website management – Maintain and continuously improve the D.C. Policy Center website, including coordination with website and hosting vendors. – Publish and update reports, blog posts, testimony, event pages, and other website content. – Ensure website content is accurate, accessible, visually engaging, and optimized for search engines. – Monitor website performance and recommend improvements to user experience and content organization. ### Publications and design – Lead the production and typesetting of research reports, briefs, testimony, presentations, and other publications. – Format publications for both digital and print distribution using Adobe Creative Cloud, including Adobe InDesign, Illustrator, and Acrobat. – Ensure all publications maintain consistent branding, typography, and visual quality. – Coordinate with researchers to prepare charts, tables, figures, maps, and graphics for publication. ### Editorial and brand management – Maintain consistent organizational branding across all communications channels. – Edit publications for clarity, accuracy, consistency, grammar, and style. – Develop and maintain editorial guidelines, publication templates, and communications standards. ### Board communications and governance support – Prepare and maintain board book templates and coordinate the production and distribution of board materials. – Work with the Executive Director and senior staff to compile reports, presentations, agendas, and supporting materials for Board and committee meetings. – Maintain accurate meeting minutes and records of Board actions. – Manage the Board document library, ensuring materials are organized, current, and easily accessible. – Support the Executive Director in preparing presentations and other materials for Board retreats, strategic planning sessions, and special meetings. – Assist with the preparation of the Policy Center’s Annual Report. ## Qualifications We strongly encourage you to apply if you believe you are a great fit for the role, even if you don’t meet every single requirement. – Five or more years of progressively responsible experience in communications, public affairs, journalism, policy, or a related field. – Experience supporting researchers in communicating technical findings accurately and effectively. – Strong project management skills and the ability to manage multiple deadlines simultaneously. – Excellent writing, editing, and verbal communication skills. – Demonstrated experience developing and executing strategic communications plans. – Strong understanding of public policy processes and the ability to monitor and synthesize legislative and policy developments. – Experience coordinating communications around legislative hearings, policy reports, public events, or advocacy campaigns. – Advanced proficiency in Adobe Creative Cloud, particularly InDesign, Illustrator, and Acrobat. – Experience producing professional publications for both digital and print distribution, as well as social media content. – Demonstrated ability to transform quantitative analysis into clear, engaging graphics and interactive visualizations (using Tableau, Flourish, or similar platforms) for policy and public audiences. – Experience managing websites using content management systems, including WordPress, and familiarity with web publishing best practices. – Familiarity with email marketing platforms, including Mailchimp, and customer relationship management systems, such as Salesforce, is highly desirable. – Familiarity with the District of Columbia policy environment and local government is highly desirable. ## Desired assets – Strategic thinker with strong political awareness and sound judgment. – Exceptional organizational skills and attention to detail. – Ability to identify emerging policy opportunities and anticipate communications needs. – Strong collaborator who enjoys working across research, communications, and external affairs. – Comfortable managing multiple complex projects in a fast-paced environment. – Commitment to rigorous, nonpartisan research and evidence-based policymaking. ## Telework Policy This is a hybrid position that requires in-person work. ## Compensation and Benefits The salary range for this position is $85,000–$95,000. Salary is commensurate with experience. Benefits include health, dental, and vision insurance; retirement plan (after a qualification period) with employer match; paid leave. ## How to Apply To apply, please submit a resume and cover letter outlining your interest in the role and relevant experience to [email protected] . The priority application date for this position is August 03, 2026. ## About the D.C. Policy Center The D.C. Policy Center is a non-profit 501(c)(3) think tank focusing on local policy issues in the District of Columbia and the surrounding region. Through data-driven and action-oriented policy research, the D.C. Policy Center’s mission is to bring together policymakers, employers, industry leaders, community advocates, and other stakeholders to advance comprehensive policies that support a strong and growing local economy for all District residents. The D.C. Policy Center is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status, or any other protected status under federal or District law. item.title: Senior Manager, Policy Communications – LUS & Social Impact
item.description: Senior Manager, Policy Communications – LUS & Social Impact Organization: Lyft Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 07/24/2026 ## At Lyft, Our Purpose At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive. Lyft’s Communications team is seeking a **Senior Manager, Policy Communications, LUS & Social Impact** to help lead the company’s efforts across three interconnected areas: public policy, Lyft Urban Solutions (**LUS**), and social impact. This role serves as a key voice on policy issues critical to rideshare, transportation equity, and the future of mobility — shaping narratives with regulators, government officials, media, and the public. It also helps lead communications for Lyft’s bikeshare and micromobility portfolio and drives storytelling around Lyft’s social impact programs and partnerships. This role requires collaboration and executive stakeholder management. It is built for a relationship‑driven communicator who thrives in collaborative environments — someone who brings people together across teams, builds trust with senior leaders and external stakeholders, and is energized by deep partnership that aligns communications with Lyft’s broader strategy and brand voice. — ## Responsibilities ### Policy Communications Strategy – **Policy communications** — Design and execute proactive communications strategies that advance Lyft’s position on transportation, rideshare regulation, driver policy, safety, and mobility equity. – Develop and maintain a rapid response program ensuring accurate and timely information reaches media, regulators, and the public on high‑priority policy issues. – Create and manage a strategic roadmap for public appearances, speaking opportunities, and thought leadership that positions Lyft leadership as credible voices in the policy space. – Partner with Government Affairs and Public Policy teams to align on strategic messaging for emerging legislation, regulatory proceedings, and government engagements. ### Lyft Urban Solutions (LUS) Communications – Help lead communications for Lyft’s bikeshare and micromobility portfolio — including Citi Bike, Bay Wheels, Bluebikes, Divvy, and BIKETOWN — spanning policy, corporate, and consumer dimensions. – Partner with LUS External Affairs to develop earned media strategies and stakeholder outreach for program announcements, expansions, ridership milestones, and market launches. – Manage reactive press inquiries on LUS‑related topics including pricing, ridership, safety, and regulatory developments across operating cities. – Support consumer‑facing communications moments including rebrands, seasonal campaigns, and rider engagement initiatives in coordination with marketing and product teams. – Develop messaging and materials for LUS partnership announcements and corporate milestones. ### Social Impact Communications – Lead communications strategy for Lyft’s social impact programs, including Round Up & Donate, Jobs Access, and Voting Access initiatives. – Develop compelling narratives and materials — including blog posts, press releases, and partner communications — that translate Lyft’s social impact work into accessible public storytelling. – Manage earned media outreach for social impact announcements in coordination with external agency partners, prioritizing local storytelling and community voices. – Support recognition and award opportunities (e.g., Forbes Best Brands for Social Impact) that amplify Lyft’s social commitments. – Partner with the Social Impact team and external nonprofit and corporate partners to develop joint communications plans. ### Media & Stakeholder Relations – Build and maintain strong, trust‑based relationships with policy‑focused journalists, editors, and outlets — including national press, trade media, and local reporters in key markets — cultivated through in‑person briefings, industry events, and regular outreach. – Own proactive media outreach and manage inbound press inquiries on policy, LUS, and social impact topics. – Identify and cultivate third‑party validators, advocates, and coalition partners who can amplify Lyft’s messages. – Collaborate with Legal and Litigation teams in high‑volume, fast‑paced communications environments, providing real‑time counsel and response during active proceedings or regulatory actions. ### Executive & Cross‑Functional Partnership – Prepare senior executives and spokespeople for media interviews, policy briefings, legislative testimony, and public appearances — including developing talking points and providing media coaching. – Partner cross‑functionally with Marketing, Brand, Legal, and Operations teams to ensure alignment between policy, LUS, and social impact communications and company‑wide messaging. – Engage actively with Lyft’s regional teams and travel on‑site to key markets as needed to develop localized communications strategies and drive on‑the‑ground influence efforts. ### Content & Campaign Development – Write and edit high‑quality communications materials including press releases, op‑eds, statements, fact sheets, briefing documents, and messaging guides. – Develop content for owned channels — including blog posts, social copy, and digital campaigns — that translates complex policy and impact issues into accessible public narratives. – Support internal communications efforts that keep Lyft team members informed on policy, LUS, and social impact developments relevant to the business. — ## Experience – 8+ years of relevant experience in communications, with meaningful focus on public policy, government affairs, regulatory environments, advocacy, or social impact. – Proven track record developing and executing strategic communications campaigns at a tech company, in‑house at a major corporation, or in a government/regulatory communications role. – Demonstrated knowledge of the rideshare, mobility, or transportation policy landscape — including familiarity with driver classification, safety regulation, accessibility, or local government dynamics. – Experience with urban mobility, micromobility, or transit communications is a strong plus. – Exceptional written and verbal communicator — including experience producing polished media materials, executive‑ready briefings, and public‑facing content under deadline pressure. – Established relationships with policy and tech press; demonstrated success securing media coverage on policy‑related topics. – Proven ability to build trusted relationships with senior leaders, external partners, and cross‑functional stakeholders across complex organizations. – Ability to manage multiple high‑priority projects simultaneously in a fast‑paced, rapidly changing environment. – Strong judgment and discretion in representing company positions on sensitive policy matters. – Experience with crisis communications and rapid response in regulatory or litigation‑adjacent environments is a strong plus. – Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Public Policy, Political Science, Journalism, or a related field. — ## Benefits – Great medical, dental, and vision insurance options with additional programs available when enrolled. – Mental health benefits. – Family‑building benefits. – Child care and pet benefits. – 401(k) plan with company match. – In addition to 12 observed holidays, salaried team members have discretionary paid time off; hourly team members have 15 days paid time off. – 18 weeks of paid parental leave for biological, adoptive, and foster parents. – Subsidized commuter benefits. – Monthly Lyft credits and complimentary Lyft Pink membership. Lyft is an equal opportunity employer committed to an inclusive workplace that fosters belonging. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, age, genetic information, or any other basis prohibited by law. Lyft also considers qualified applicants with criminal histories consistent with applicable federal, state, and local law. — ## Hybrid Work Expectations Lyft highly values in‑office collaboration to foster a strong work environment and company culture. This role follows a hybrid schedule — team members are expected in the office **three days per week: Monday, Wednesday, and Thursday**. Hybrid roles also include flexibility to work from anywhere for up to four weeks per year. — ## Compensation The expected base pay range for this position in the Washington D.C. area is **$121,440 – $151,800**, not including potential equity, bonus, or benefits. Salary ranges depend on qualifications, experience, and geographic location. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Lead, Global External Affairs
item.description: Lead, Global External Affairs Organization: Cohere Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 07/24/2026 ## Who are we? Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises building AI systems. We believe our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI, and we are looking for people who want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company co-headquartered in Toronto and San Francisco, with key offices in London, New York City, Montreal, Seoul, Germany, and Paris. Join us! ## Why this role? Shaping the future of enterprise AI requires engaging beyond direct legislative advocacy. Leading technology and AI companies understand that long-term policy success relies on building a robust ecosystem of third-party validators, thought leaders, and strategic alliances. As the Lead for Global External Affairs, you will build and direct this critical function within our Government Affairs and Public Policy (GAPP) team. You will define how Cohere engages with the broader policy ecosystem, including think tanks, academic institutions, civil society organizations, and industry coalitions. As the function grows, you will also have the opportunity to scale the team around public affairs and policy narratives. Your work will ensure that Cohere’s narrative around responsible, secure, and highly effective enterprise AI is validated, amplified, and understood by the most influential voices shaping global technology policy. ## In this role you will: **Define the Strategy:** Build and execute a comprehensive global External Affairs strategy that aligns with and amplifies Cohere’s broader public policy and commercial objectives. **Cultivate Strategic Partnerships:** Identify, build, and manage deep relationships with leading technology policy think tanks, academic researchers, civil society organizations, and NGOs. **Drive Third-Party Validation:** Partner with external experts and institutions to generate thought leadership, research, and independent validation of Cohere’s approach to enterprise AI, data privacy, and model safety. **Manage Coalitions & Associations:** Serve as Cohere’s primary representative on key industry coalitions, trade associations, and multi-stakeholder forums, ensuring our unique enterprise perspective shapes broader industry consensus. **Align Internal Stakeholders:** Work seamlessly across the GAPP, Corporate Communications, Legal, and Go-To-Market teams to ensure external partnerships and investments drive measurable business impact. **Convene Key Voices:** Organize and host high-level roundtables, policy briefings, and summits that position Cohere as a central convener in the global AI policy debate. ## You could be a great fit if you have… **External Affairs Leadership:** 10+ years of experience in external affairs, public policy, or strategic partnerships, ideally within a major technology company, leading trade association, or prominent policy institution. **Deep Ecosystem Network:** An extensive, active network of relationships across major think tanks, academic centers, and civil society organizations globally. **Tech & AI Policy Acumen:** A sophisticated understanding of current global debates surrounding artificial intelligence, including data governance, safety, open-source models, and enterprise adoption. **Strategic Investment Mindset:** Proven experience managing budgets for sponsorships, memberships, and grants, ensuring ROI and alignment with corporate policy goals. **Exceptional Communication:** Ability to persuasively articulate complex technical and policy narratives to highly influential external audiences. **Builder’s Mentality:** A self-starter who thrives on establishing a new function from the ground up, designing operational workflows and strategies necessary for scale. ## Nice to have (but not required): Advanced degree in Public Policy, International Relations, Law, or a related field. Experience navigating the nuances between consumer AI policy and enterprise/B2B AI policy. ## Compensation Cohere is committed to fair and transparent pay practices. The salary range listed reflects expected base compensation. Actual compensation will depend on location, level, job-related knowledge, skills, education, and experience. **United States Compensation Range:** $220,000 – $330,000 USD **Canada Compensation Range:** $250,000 – $375,000 CAD ## Full-Time Employee Perks A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency. Full health and dental benefits, including a separate mental health budget. RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme. 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months for either parent. ### Annual enrichment benefits: Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and workspace improvement credit. Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching. 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!). Budget for traveling to other offices if remote, plus an annual company offsite. ## How and Where We Work Cohere is remote-friendly. We have offices in Toronto, San Francisco, New York City, London, Paris, Montreal, and more coming soon. **For those in the office:** daily lunch program, snacks, and regular community/social events. **For those not near an office:** co-working benefit to work alongside others in your city. Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly. If your experience doesn’t align perfectly with the above, we still encourage you to apply. ## Inclusion & Accessibility We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. If you require accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form and we will work with you to meet your needs. We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. These tools help identify potentially qualified candidates but do not limit which applications our recruiters may review. ## Beware of Scams Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with communications coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites, please verify them through our official careers page. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: State and Local Policy Manager
item.description: State and Local Policy Manager Organization: REI Location: Seattle, WA Date Posted: 07/24/2026 ## Job Description ### Overview At REI, we believe a life outdoors is a life well lived. As the State and Local Policy Manager, you will develop strategy and help shape how we engage with state and local governments. You will support public policy efforts that reflect our values, including but not limited to natural resources/public lands policy, tax and trade policy, regulatory compliance, and product sustainability. In this role, you will work across teams and with external partners to build alignment, share insights, and support policy priorities. You will also help connect employees, members, and communities to advocacy efforts that strengthen our impact. — ## Responsibilities and Qualifications – Develop and lead state and local policy strategy on key issues in our priority regions – Track legislation and regulatory policy, and focus engagement where it matters most – Develop clear policy communication, issue briefs, and other materials to inform leaders and support decision‑making – Build and maintain relationships with policymakers, partners, and community organizations – Partner across internal REI teams to align business goals with policy efforts – Create tools and content that support employee and member engagement on our advocacy priorities – Contribute to the culture and connection of the Community and Government Affairs team ### Required Qualifications – 7+ years of experience in public policy, government affairs, or advocacy – Knowledge of state and local legislative and regulatory processes – Expertise in natural resources policy, regulatory compliance, and tax/trade issues, and knowledge related to product sustainability – Proven ability to engage policymakers and stakeholders while working in dynamic, complex environments – Experience developing and implementing policy strategies – Strong communication and collaboration skills across diverse audiences ### Preferred Qualifications – Experience in outdoor industry or conservation advocacy — ## Closing At REI, we believe the outdoors is for all. We are committed to becoming a fully inclusive, anti‑racist, multicultural organization. We know that there’s strength in our diversity — that each employee brings unique skills, experiences, and perspectives. Every day you are driving change, fostering a culture of respect, and knowing you’re backed by benefits that support your whole life. To work towards this commitment and fulfill our brand promise of inspiring and enabling a life outside for everyone, we seek employees who demonstrate different ways of working, create a sense of belonging, and actively listen and learn. ### Pay Transparency We are committed to practices that promote pay equity and transparency. As required by applicable Pay Transparency laws, REI provides a range of compensation for roles that may be hired in locations under these requirements. Factors that may be used to determine your actual salary may include a wide array of factors, including your specific skills and experience, geographic location, or other relevant factors. REI offers all regular employees a generous employee discount, access to health benefits, a retirement savings plan, and accrued time off. Click here for a detailed overview of benefits plans by employee profile. — ## Pay Range $98,300.00 – $157,400.00 per year Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Senior Public Affairs Manager
item.description: Senior Public Affairs Manager Organization: Uber Location: New York, NY Date Posted: 07/24/2026 ## About the Role Our Policy & Communications team is responsible for telling Uber’s story to the media, third parties, and government officials — whether it’s transforming how we get around town and the lives of people who value independent, flexible work; making rides more affordable; or cutting congestion in cities by getting more backsides into fewer cars. As a Senior Public Affairs Manager for the North Region, you will be responsible for managing Uber’s government affairs and public relations strategy for several states in the Midwest and Northeast United States, including New York City. You’ll create and execute issue‑based campaigns to achieve our priorities. This position reports to the Senior Director of Policy & Communications for the North Region. ## What You’ll Do – Engage with local government officials on prospective legislation and regulations – Develop and execute communications strategies to advance our key narratives – Partner with government agencies, state and local leaders, regional 3rd‑party organizations, and coalition partners on shared public policy goals – Direct lobbying strategy and manage relationships with lobbyists and other outside consultants – Manage day‑to‑day relations with Midwest and East Coast–based media outlets to support the reputation of Uber’s Mobility and Delivery businesses, as well as tell our story as an engaged member of the communities in which we operate ## Basic Qualifications Bachelor’s degree, with 8+ years of experience in public policy, campaigns, communications, or government affairs. ## Preferred Qualifications – Outstanding verbal and written communication and presentation skills – Self‑starter: We are a company of entrepreneurs, and we want to work with people who enjoy building things from the bottom up too. Things change fast at a global company like Uber, so you’ll need to be highly adaptable as well as calm under pressure – Great advocate: We want someone who can distill sophisticated ideas into simple but intellectually credible arguments. This person will write well and have the creative ability to tell stories — about our product, people, and the ways we’re helping to improve life for riders, drivers, delivery people, and cities across the United States – Tell our story in the press: Experience developing and executing a public relations plan and working directly with counterparts in print, digital, and broadcast media – Strong campaigner: We succeed by putting together effective campaigns with third parties on behalf of the passengers and drivers who use the app. That means you’ll have a bias for action in everything you do, and also build strong business acumen covering issues related to mobility, delivery, safety, future of work, and/or automation. It would also be useful to display a working knowledge of the regional political environment and strong, existing relationships with elected officials, media, 3rd parties, and key thought leaders – Great teammate: Success at Uber depends on the ability to coordinate different teams (internally and externally) around shared goals. We’re looking for collaborators who get stuff done — and who can deal with the ambiguity that sometimes comes from working cross‑functionally – Experience working with state and local governments in the Midwest and Northeast United States ~~ ~~ For New York City, NY‑based roles: The base salary range for this role is USD $190,000 per year – USD $211,000 per year. You will be eligible to participate in Uber’s bonus program and may be offered an equity award and other types of compensation. All full‑time employees are eligible to participate in a 401(k) plan. You will also be eligible for various benefits. ## Ready to Ride? This isn’t the kind of place where you follow a playbook — it’s where you help write one. If you’re driven by impact, energized by challenge, and ready to shape how the world moves — we’d love to hear from you. You may be eligible for bonuses, equity, and other compensation, as well as a range of benefits. Explore our benefits. Offices remain key to collaboration and Uber’s culture. Unless approved for full remote work, employees must spend at least 50% of their time in‑office. Some roles, like those at greenlight hubs, require full‑time in‑office presence. Ask your Recruiter for details about this role’s requirements. Uber is proud to be an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected Veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know by completing this form. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Lead – US Government Affairs & Public Policy
item.description: Lead – US Government Affairs & Public Policy Organization: Cohere Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 07/24/2026 ## Who are we? Cohere is the leading security‑first enterprise AI company. We build cutting‑edge foundation AI models and end‑to‑end products designed to solve real‑world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises building AI systems. We believe our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI, and we are looking for people who want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us contributes to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more — all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company co‑headquartered in Toronto and San Francisco, with key offices in London, New York City, Montreal, Seoul, Germany, and Paris. Join us! — ## Why this role? Cohere is a fast‑growing company in the dynamic artificial intelligence space. We are building a Government Affairs and Public Policy (GAPP) team with the drive and experience to engage in and shape a nascent and unique policy environment for enterprise AI. We seek a Government Affairs professional to lead our US government affairs strategy, with flexibility to help shape our policy footprint across key emerging markets in the Americas as our commercial presence grows. Candidates will have a proven track record, are analytical, collaborative, driven, and possess a passion for digging deep into the evolving public policy debate at the intersection of enterprise technology and artificial intelligence. There is no better time to join us in building this function as we shape the future of AI in the United States and across the region. — ## In this role you will: **Lead US Advocacy:** Partner closely with Cohere’s senior leadership, legal, public policy, and responsible AI teams to develop, coordinate, and implement a government affairs strategy across US federal and state levels. For the right leader, there is an opportunity to expand this advocacy to support strategic growth across Latin America. **Dig Deep on AI Policy:** Serve as the internal and external expert on US AI policy while monitoring key regulatory shifts in neighboring markets. You will proactively report on trends and work with cross‑functional teams to craft thoughtful responses to governmental initiatives, regulatory issues, and legislative drafts that impact Cohere’s business. **Cultivate Key Relationships:** Guide and coordinate Cohere’s political engagement by cultivating deep relationships and representing the company with key lawmakers, regulators, federal agencies, state leaders, and regional trade bodies. **Bridge the Corporate and Political:** Leverage your dual experience in political and corporate spheres to translate complex technical and business objectives into effective policy advocacy. **Support Strategic Growth:** Work closely with public‑sector sales teams in shaping technology and procurement policies in regulated sectors, ensuring Cohere is a trusted resource and partner for government stakeholders. **Manage External Partners:** Direct government relations consultants, lobbyists, and trade associations in the US, with scope to manage regional external partners as geographic needs evolve. **Ensure Compliance:** Oversee compliance of all lobbying and political activities with federal, state, and relevant international laws. — ## You could be a great fit if you have: **Deep AI Policy Expertise:** Exceptional ability to dig deep on artificial intelligence policy, its applications, and its risks, with a proven track record of shaping relevant tech policies and regulations. **Political & Corporate Experience:** 10 to 15+ years of leadership experience blending corporate government affairs roles within the technology sector and direct political or government experience. **Federal & State Mastery:** Extensive experience navigating intricate and fluid political debates across US federal and state jurisdictions, with adaptability to new regulatory environments. **Bias for Action:** A growth mindset and self‑starter attitude with the ability to work independently, prioritize issues, and push projects to completion. **Exceptional Communication:** Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a proven ability to distill complex AI policy into compelling documents, thought leadership, and briefings for varied audiences. **Educational Background:** Bachelor’s degree in Law, Public Policy, Political Science, or a related field. — ## Nice to have (but not required): **Defense & Military Background:** Prior experience in or working closely with the defense sector, military, or national security apparatus is highly preferred given the strategic importance of AI in these fields. **Regional Acumen:** Experience navigating tech policy, trade, or digital regulatory frameworks in Latin America, along with professional fluency in Spanish or Portuguese. **Procurement Experience:** Proven experience supporting public‑sector sales and government procurement teams. — ## Full‑Time Employees at Cohere enjoy these Perks: – A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency. – Full health and dental benefits, including a separate mental‑health budget. – RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme. – 100% parental‑leave top‑up for up to 6 months for either parent. – Annual enrichment benefits: arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, workspace improvement credit. – Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching. – 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days). – Budget for traveling to other offices if remote, plus an annual company offsite. — ## How and Where We Work: Cohere is remote‑friendly. We have offices in Toronto, San Francisco, New York City, London, Paris, Montreal, and more coming soon. **For those in the office:** daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community/social events. **For those not near an office:** a co‑working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city. Everyone receives a $500 home‑office stipend to set up their workspace properly. If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. — We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form, and we will work together to meet your needs. We may use AI‑enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it does not limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider. **Beware of Scams:** Cohere will never ask for payment or third‑party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with communications coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites, please verify them through our official careers page. — ## Apply for this Job Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Federal Government Relations Executive
item.description: Federal Government Relations Executive Organization: Bank of America Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 07/24/2026 ## Job Description At Bank of America, we are guided by a common purpose to help make financial lives better through the power of every connection. We do this by driving Responsible Growth and delivering for our clients, teammates, communities, and shareholders every day. Being a Great Place to Work and providing a culture of caring is core to how we drive Responsible Growth. We are intentional about fostering an inclusive workplace where every teammate has the opportunity to succeed, build a career, and contribute to our shared success. This includes attracting and developing exceptional talent, recognizing and rewarding performance, and supporting our teammates’ physical, emotional, and financial wellness through affordable, competitive, and flexible benefits. We value the unique perspectives individuals bring from all backgrounds and career paths—whether shaped by military service, community college education, or a wide range of work and life experiences. These journeys foster resilience, leadership, and innovation, strengthening our workforce and positively impacting the communities we serve. Bank of America is committed to an in‑office culture that supports collaboration, engagement, and career development. Our approach includes clear in‑office expectations while providing an appropriate level of flexibility based on role‑specific responsibilities and business needs. At Bank of America, you can build a successful career with opportunities to learn, grow, and make an impact. Join us! — ## Job Description This role is responsible for developing and delivering strategic priorities for Bank of America’s Global Public Policy team. Key responsibilities include advancing Bank of America’s position on key legislative, regulatory, and social responsibility issues and advocating those positions to government officials. Expectations include maintaining strong relationships with public officials, trade associations, and industry organizations, and coordinating with internal stakeholders on important policy issues. The Federal Government Relations role supports the Bank’s engagement and analysis on business matters requiring geopolitical, national security, or foreign policy judgment and relationships. The previous incumbent was relied upon by lines of business, compliance, risk, credit, and legal partners to assess transactions and clients—on a case‑by‑case basis through the business escalation process—for geopolitical considerations that may impact credit decisions within customary risk assessments. This role serves on the Federal Government Relations team, part of the Global Public Policy team, responsible for monitoring geopolitical developments, advising internal stakeholders on international policy risks, and cultivating relationships with key U.S. government and diplomatic stakeholders. The ideal candidate will bring deep expertise in national‑level government, international affairs, U.S. foreign policy, geopolitical analysis, and a well‑developed network across the foreign policy, diplomatic, and national security community. This individual will serve as a trusted advisor to senior leaders and lines of business, helping the Bank assess emerging risks and opportunities across regions, countries, and industries outside the United States. This role reports to the Senior Federal Government Relations Executive. — ## Responsibilities – Builds and maintains relationships with policymakers and public officials – Establishes and advocates legislative and regulatory policies important to Bank of America – Drives Bank of America’s responsible growth strategy and strategic initiatives – Engages senior leaders with legislatures (state and federal), executive offices (governors, mayors, U.S. administration), and other policymakers – Monitors the legislative and regulatory environment and communicates developments to Bank of America stakeholders – Serves as a resource for internal and external stakeholders on the legislative and regulatory environment and status of key policy issues – Coordinates Bank of America positions with key trade associations and industry coalitions – Develops and builds consensus policy positions on legislative and regulatory issues – Serves as the Bank’s internal subject matter expert on geopolitical developments, U.S. foreign policy, and international affairs – Analyzes global political, diplomatic, economic, and security developments and assesses their potential impact on the Bank, its clients, and its lines of business – Advises senior management and business leaders on geopolitical risks related to operating in, investing in, or transacting with countries and industries outside the United States — ## Geopolitical Analysis and Strategic Advisory – Serve as the Bank’s internal subject matter expert on geopolitical developments, U.S. foreign policy, and international affairs – Analyze global political, diplomatic, economic, and security developments and assess their potential impact on the Bank, its clients, and its lines of business – Advise senior management and business leaders on geopolitical risks related to operating in, investing in, or transacting with countries and industries outside the United States – Provide timely insight on issues including political instability, sanctions, trade and investment restrictions, diplomatic tensions, regulatory developments, armed conflict, regime change, sovereign risk, and cross‑border market access – Develop written analyses, briefing materials, and strategic recommendations for executives and business stakeholders — ## Government and Diplomatic Engagement – Maintain and deepen relationships with the U.S. Department of State and other internationally focused U.S. government agencies and departments, including Treasury, Commerce, Defense, and Homeland Security, as well as relevant White House and congressional offices – Serve as a principal point of contact for foreign embassies in Washington, D.C. on matters relevant to the Bank’s international interests and strategic priorities – Monitor policy developments across the executive branch and diplomatic community that may affect the Bank’s global business environment – Represent the Bank in external meetings, forums, policy discussions, and industry roundtables involving international policy and geopolitical matters — ## Business Partnership and Client Engagement – Partner with lines of business to identify and assess country, sector, and regional risks affecting client activity, business strategy, or transaction execution – Advise bankers and business teams on geopolitical considerations relevant to client opportunities, market entry, capital flows, and cross‑border business activity – Support client‑facing teams by developing and delivering presentations, briefings, and thought leadership on geopolitical trends and their commercial implications – Serve as a resource to senior executives and client teams preparing for meetings with corporate clients, investors, foreign officials, and other external stakeholders – Translate complex geopolitical developments into clear, practical, business‑relevant insights — ## Cross‑Functional Collaboration – Work closely with Legal, Compliance, Risk, Regulatory Affairs, Sanctions, Anti‑Money Laundering, Government Relations, Corporate Security, and business leadership – Contribute to enterprise‑wide assessments of geopolitical, sovereign, and sectoral risk – Inform internal governance, escalation, and decision‑making processes related to international business exposure – Support development of internal education materials and executive briefings on geopolitical trends and emerging risks — ## Required Qualifications – Bachelor’s degree in international relations, political science, public policy, economics, law, history, or a related field – Significant experience in public policy, international affairs, diplomacy, geopolitical risk, government relations, or a related field – Deep knowledge of U.S. foreign policy, international institutions, diplomacy, and major geopolitical trends affecting global markets – Demonstrated experience engaging with the U.S. Department of State and/or internationally focused federal agencies – Strong familiarity with the diplomatic community in Washington, D.C., including foreign embassies and senior foreign government officials – Ability to assess complex geopolitical developments and translate them into actionable business advice – Strong executive presence, judgment, and interpersonal skills – Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including presenting to senior executives, clients, and external stakeholders — ## Skills – Executive Presence – Influence – Interpret Relevant Laws, Rules, and Regulations – Networking – Strategic Thinking – Issue Management – Oral Communications – Performance Management – Regulatory Compliance – Regulatory Relations – Advisory – Business Acumen – Policies, Procedures, and Guidelines – Risk Management – Strategy Planning and Development — ## Shift 1st shift (United States of America) ## Hours Per Week 40 Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.description: Government Affairs & Strategic Partnerships Jr. Manager Organization: Flix Location: Los Angeles, CA Date Posted: 07/24/2026 ## At Flix At Flix, we offer a dynamic work environment with competitive pay, strong growth opportunities, and a tech‑driven approach to making travel more accessible, sustainable, and affordable. As a Government Affairs & Strategic Partnerships Jr. Manager, you will support market expansion by securing access to critical infrastructure, managing relationships with key stakeholders, and driving operational success in a highly regulated environment. You will develop strategic partnerships with public and private entities, navigate complex government processes, and ensure compliance while establishing access to high‑value transportation hubs across the country. ## About the Role – Secure high‑impact locations for bus stops and stations by leveraging government relationships and private‑sector negotiation skills – Identify, negotiate, and secure bus stop access agreements with private business partners to support and expand network operations – Align commercial objectives with government policies by identifying opportunities and mitigating regulatory risks – Develop partnerships with businesses, transit agencies, and property owners to enhance station access and amenities – Serve as the primary contact for station‑related and government relations matters, advocating for the company in infrastructure planning forums – Coordinate with teams to standardize documentation and refine processes, enabling improved efficiencies – Up to 30% of travel as needed ## About You – 1+ years of experience in business development, strategic partnerships, or real estate development, including work with government entities – 1+ years of project management experience with knowledge of transportation regulations and public transit systems – Excellent communication and interpersonal abilities, with experience presenting to senior officials and business leaders – Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, including Excel and PowerPoint **Salary Range:** $70,000.00 – $80,000.00 USD We recognize that everyone carries a unique set of valuable skills and experiences. If you think you could have an impact even though you don’t meet 100% of the requirements, we still encourage you to apply. We want to hear from you! ## What We Offer – Comprehensive Wellness Coverage – Competitive Medical, Vision, and Dental plans, including multiple FSAs (Health and Dependent Care). – 401(k) Matching – 401(k) plan with up to 4% company matching contributions. – Flexible Time Off – Take time off when you need it, as you need it, subject to business needs and manager approval. – Paid Parental Leave – 8 weeks of fully paid leave to support new parents and growing families. – Company Paid Life Insurance – Basic company‑paid life insurance equal to your annual salary. – Lifestyle Spending Account – Receive up to $600 per year for eligible lifestyle‑related services. – Tuition Support – Up to $5,250 per year reimbursed for your continued education and development after 12 months of continuous service. – 24/7 Employee Assistance Program – Free, confidential support for mental health, legal, financial, and family issues, including up to 5 free counseling sessions per year. – Free Travel Perks – Complimentary travel on FlixBus and Greyhound for you, family, and friends. – Work from (M)Anywhere – Depending on your role, work from another location for up to 60 days per year. ## Why Join Flix? At Flix, you’ll find teams that rally together to overcome challenges and spark creativity. We believe in ownership culture — giving you the freedom to take initiative, make an impact, and shape your own career path. As we continue to expand across the globe, you can make a real difference in how we work. If you’re ready to grow and lead your journey, Flix is the place for you! item.title: Public Affairs Strategist
item.description: Public Affairs Strategist Organization: Evolv Technology Location: Waltham, MA | New York, NY | Washington, DC Date Posted: 07/24/2026 ## **The Elevator Pitch** At Evolv, we’re helping redefine how public spaces approach safety. Trusted by schools, hospitals, entertainment venues, sports stadiums, and other organizations across the country, our technology is helping communities create safer environments while preserving the welcoming experiences people expect. As a Public Affairs Strategist, you’ll lead Evolv’s work to advance state-level policy that establishes advanced weapons screening as a recognized standard for keeping students and staff safe in K–12 schools. You’ll build the state-by-state game plan — mapping the legislative and regulatory landscape, identifying and engaging the policymakers and community organizations who shape school-safety decisions, and organizing the coalitions that turn a shared goal into enacted policy. You’ll begin with top priority states and carry them forward over time, expanding to new states as the program grows, and you’ll help identify, direct, and manage outside lobbying partners where they can accelerate progress. This role is ideal for a public affairs professional who has moved policy through statehouses before, thrives in complex multi-stakeholder environments, communicates with credibility and diplomacy across the political spectrum, helps identify the funding for new policy mandates, and is energized by work that creates meaningful impact for students and communities. — ## **What Does Success Look Like?** ### **Within the first 30 days, you will:** – Develop a deep understanding of Evolv’s mission, products, customers, and the school-safety policy landscape across priority states. – Build familiarity with the environment in a few high-priority states — existing legislation, recent legislative and regulatory activity, and the associations, research organizations, public-sector entities, and community leaders who influence school-safety decisions. – Establish working relationships with internal partners across Growth, Marketing, Sales, Product, Legal, and Customer Success. – Begin sharpening the prioritization view of where policy progress is most achievable, and put in place a game plan to help drive it forward. ### **Within 90 days, you will:** – Deliver and begin executing a clear, actionable plan for each of the first three priority states — covering the legislative and regulatory landscape, key policymakers and the path to engaging them, the coalition of supporters to organize, the most viable policy vehicle and funding pathway, and a clear-eyed read of likely opposition. – Begin building relationships with key external stakeholders in those states, including legislators and committee staff, school-safety associations, and education and parent organizations. – Help develop evidence-based, locally relevant messaging and supporting materials that communicate Evolv’s impact to diverse audiences. – Recommend where outside lobbying or government-relations partners would accelerate progress and begin scoping and managing those engagements. ### **Within your first year, you will:** – Move the first states forward toward introduced legislation or regulatory action, and stand up the next wave of priority states. – Establish Evolv as a trusted, credible, and engaged participant in school-safety policy conversations. – Build and maintain meaningful relationships with priority associations, research institutions, public-sector organizations, and community influencers. – Develop a repeatable state playbook that allows the program to scale efficiently across many states. – Identify, direct, and manage outside lobbyists and partners across multiple states, ensuring their work aligns with Evolv’s strategy and compliance standards. – Support the development of evidence-based proof points and independent research that strengthen customer confidence and the broader case for advanced screening. — ## **The Work: What Will You Be Doing?** ### **State Policy Strategy & Campaign Development** – Build and own the state-by-state plan to advance advanced weapons screening as a school-safety standard — beginning with priority states and expanding over time. – For each state, map the legislative and regulatory landscape, identify the most viable policy vehicle (legislation, regulation, code, or funding mechanism), and define a realistic path to adoption. – Pair each policy effort with a viable funding pathway so that adopted standards can actually be implemented. – Maintain a prioritization framework that sequences states by feasibility and opportunity and adapts as conditions change. ### **Stakeholder Engagement & Coalition Building** – Identify, map, and engage the legislators, committee staff, public-sector leaders, and community organizations that shape school-safety policy in each state. – Build and organize coalitions of credible third-party voices — parent and education organizations, school-safety associations, principals and superintendents, and other community stakeholders — who can advocate for safer schools. – Develop a tailored value proposition and engagement approach for each stakeholder, and build the relationships and pathways needed to earn the meeting. – Represent Evolv in external forums, industry events, working groups, and standards organizations as appropriate. ### **Outside Partner & Lobbyist Management** – Identify the states where engaging outside lobbying or government-relations partners will accelerate progress, and recommend when and where to do so. – Select, direct, and manage outside lobbyists and consultants, ensuring their work aligns with Evolv’s strategy, messaging, and compliance standards. – Coordinate registration, disclosure, and reporting requirements in partnership with Legal and Compliance. ### **Evidence Development & Messaging** – Work cross-functionally with Growth, Marketing, Sales, Product, and Customer Success to gather customer insights and develop evidence-based proof points. – Support relationships with research organizations and third-party partners to advance independent validation and studies that strengthen market and policymaker confidence. – Develop clear, locally relevant messaging and briefing materials for legislators, community organizations, and the public. ### **Responsible Engagement & Compliance** – Partner closely with Legal and Compliance to ensure all external engagement aligns with company policy and applicable law, including lobbying registration, political neutrality, anti-corruption, and business-courtesy requirements. – Uphold Evolv’s commitment to responsible, neutral, and transparent engagement with public officials, partners, and communities. — ## **Leadership for This Role** The Public Affairs Strategist will report directly to Evolv’s Chief Growth Officer and work closely with senior leaders across Marketing, Sales, Product, Legal, and Customer Success. This is a relationship-oriented and externally facing role that requires regular engagement with customers, associations, research partners, industry events, and federal and state stakeholders. Travel will vary throughout the year based on business priorities and external engagement opportunities, so candidates should be comfortable traveling as needed and reside within reasonable access to a major airport. — ## **Location** Preference: near Evolv’s headquarters in Waltham, Massachusetts. Open to exceptional candidates in strategic U.S. cities, including New York and Washington, DC. This role requires regular engagement with legislators, committee staff, associations, research partners, community organizations, and industry events — including frequent travel to state capitols and stakeholder meetings. Candidates should reside within reasonable access to a major airport. — ## **Notes on Confidentiality & Compliance** This role operates within a sensitive, politically neutral, and externally visible area of the business. The successful candidate must exercise strong judgment, discretion, and professionalism when engaging with legislators, public officials, and other external stakeholders, and when handling confidential information. Public-facing materials, engagement plans, and stakeholder communications should be developed in partnership with the appropriate internal teams and approved through established company processes. Interactions with government officials, public-sector entities, and external stakeholders — including the engagement of outside lobbyists — must align with Evolv’s policies related to political neutrality, business courtesies, anti-corruption, lobbying registration, and compliance. — ## **Compensation & Transparency Statement** The base salary range for this full-time position is **$102,000–$166,000**. In addition to base salary, this role offers a competitive target bonus, equity, and a comprehensive benefits package. This range reflects Evolv’s commitment to pay transparency and equity, aligned with applicable state laws. Compensation is determined based on role, level, location, market benchmarks, and internal equity. Actual compensation will depend on skills, experience, education, and geographic location. During the hiring process, your recruiter will share: – The specific salary range for your preferred location – A general overview of benefits and equity offerings – Insights into how compensation decisions are made Evolv regularly reviews compensation programs to ensure competitiveness, equity, and alignment with company values. — ## **Requirements** ### **Must-Have** – 5+ years of experience in government affairs, public affairs, legislative or regulatory campaigns, stakeholder engagement, chief of staff, or public-sector relations, with direct experience advancing policy at the state level. – Demonstrated success helping develop and pass — or materially advance — state legislation or regulation, ideally across more than one state, from

item.title: Federal Affairs Analyst
item.description: Federal Affairs Analyst Organization: Verisk Location: Washington, DC | Jersey City, NJ Date Posted: 07/24/2026 ## Minimum Salary 60,000 ## Maximum Salary 75,000 ## Division Underwriting Solutions ## Legal Employer Insurance Services Office, Inc. ## Disclaimer Annualized base pay may vary depending on geographic location, job‑related knowledge, skills, and experience. ## Job Description The Verisk Government Relations Department is looking for a highly motivated candidate for a Federal Affairs Analyst position. The position involves experience with legislative and regulatory monitoring. This position is remote in the D.C. area. ## Responsibilities • Handles Verisk’s legislative and regulatory monitoring of federal activities, including gathering information from legislative and regulatory information services, Capitol Hill staff, industry lobbyists, and other relevant sources. • Analyze legislation and regulations for impact on Verisk operations and work with Verisk staff, insurer trade associations, and other industry interests to achieve modification and/or compliance. Includes interface with industry trade groups by exchanging information and providing technical analysis and testimony for use by industry lobbyists to assist them with their efforts. • Work with Verisk staff to respond to newly enacted statutory and regulatory changes. Support corporate goal of timely and consistent response to mandated changes. • Use and integrate generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools into workflow and explore how GenAI can improve processes and increase efficiency. • Research and prepare technical material (status reports, white papers, issues documents, etc.) for senior management and to assist trade associations in matters germane to Verisk. • Complete all special projects and other duties as assigned. ## Qualifications • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience required. • At least 2–4 years’ experience in either P&C insurance (with technical insurance background) or Government Relations work (with appropriate analytical skills). • Research, analytical, and problem‑solving skills. • Willing and eager to learn about and apply skills in new industries. • Interpersonal skills and ability to communicate effectively (verbally and in writing) with internal staff and external stakeholders. • Ability to work independently on multiple projects simultaneously. • Knowledge of GenAI and proficiency in using GenAI. • Proficiency in Microsoft Office software. • Completion of at least 4 CPCU exams (or CPCU designation) a plus. #LI-ZP1 #LI-Remote ## About Us For over 50 years, Verisk has been the leading data analytics and technology partner to the global insurance industry by delivering value to our clients through expertise and scale. We empower communities and businesses to make better decisions on risk, faster. At Verisk, you’ll have the chance to use your voice and build a rewarding career that’s as unique as you are, with work flexibility and the support, coaching, and training you need to succeed. For the eighth consecutive year, Verisk is proudly recognized as a Great Place to Work® for outstanding workplace culture in the US, the fourth consecutive year in the UK, Spain, and India, and the second consecutive year in Poland. In addition, we’ve been recognized by The Wall Street Journal as one of the Best‑Managed Companies and by Forbes as a World’s Best Employer, testaments to the value we place on workplace culture. We’re 7,000 people strong. We relentlessly and ethically pursue innovation. And we are looking for people like you to help us translate big data into big ideas. Join us and create an exceptional experience for yourself and a better tomorrow for future generations. ## Verisk Businesses **Underwriting Solutions** — provides underwriting and rating solutions for auto and property, general liability, and excess and surplus to assess and price risk with speed and precision. **Claims Solutions** — supports end‑to‑end claims handling with analytic and automation tools that streamline workflow, improve claims management, and support better customer experiences. **Property Estimating Solutions** — offers property estimation software and tools for professionals in estimating all phases of building and repair to make day‑to‑day workflows the most efficient. **Specialty Business Solutions** — provides an integrated suite of software for full end‑to‑end management of insurance and reinsurance business, helping companies manage their businesses through efficiency, flexibility, and data governance. **Catastrophe and Risk Solutions** — provides risk modeling solutions to help individuals, businesses, and society become more resilient to catastrophic events. **Marketing Solutions** — delivers data and insights to improve the reach, timing, relevance, and compliance of every consumer engagement. **Life Insurance Solutions** — offers end‑to‑end, data insight‑driven core capabilities for carriers, distribution, and direct customers across the entire policy lifecycle of life and annuities for both individual and group. **Verisk Maplecroft** — provides intelligence on sustainability, resilience, and ESG, helping people, businesses, and societies become stronger. Verisk Analytics is an equal opportunity employer. Verisk invests in a benefits package for all employees that includes the following: Health Insurance, a Retirement Plan, Disability benefits, and a Paid Time Off program. We offer a competitive total rewards package that includes base salary determined based on role, experience, skill set, and location. All members of the Verisk Analytics family of companies are equal opportunity employers. We consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, citizenship, sex, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, veteran’s status, age, or disability. Verisk’s minimum hiring age is 18 except in countries with a higher age limit subject to applicable law. [https://www.verisk.com/company/careers/] Unsolicited resumes sent to Verisk, including unsolicited resumes sent to a Verisk business mailing address, fax machine or email address, or directly to Verisk employees, will be considered Verisk property. Verisk will NOT pay a fee for any placement resulting from the receipt of an unsolicited resume. **Verisk Employee Privacy Notice** Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.description: VP, Public Policy Organization: IQVIA Location: Falls Church, VA Date Posted: 07/24/2026 ## IQVIA – Vice President, Public Policy (U.S.) IQVIA is seeking a Vice President, Public Policy (U.S.) to lead the development and execution of the company’s U.S. public policy and government affairs strategy. This senior leader will operate at the intersection of policy, business strategy, and external engagement, advancing IQVIA’s leadership across key policy domains including health data, clinical research, digital health, privacy, governance, and life sciences innovation. The Vice President will report into the company’s Global Legal and External Affairs function (to the Senior Vice President and Deputy General Counsel) and serve as the principal advisor to senior leadership on policy risks and opportunities in the United States. The role is based in the United States (preference for Washington, DC). — ## Skills and Responsibilities – Define and lead the execution of IQVIA’s public policy strategy with priority on U.S. federal and state engagement, aligning policy priorities with enterprise business objectives and growth initiatives. – Serve as a strategic advisor to executive leadership on emerging legislative and regulatory trends impacting clinical research, health data, and life sciences innovation. – Monitor and assess policy developments across key markets, identifying risks and opportunities and translating them into actionable strategies for the business. – Direct and coordinate U.S. public policy activities across internal stakeholders, ensuring consistency of messaging and strategic alignment. – Build and maintain senior-level relationships with external stakeholders, including policymakers, regulators, trade associations, think tanks, and industry coalitions. – Lead high-impact advocacy efforts, including the development of policy positions, white papers, comment letters, and executive-level communications. – Represent IQVIA in forums, coalitions, and industry groups to shape policy outcomes and reinforce the company’s leadership position. – Partner closely with business units, Legal, Compliance, and other functions to integrate policy considerations into business strategy and operational decision-making. – Oversee the prioritization and resourcing of policy initiatives across a complex, matrixed organization. – Develop and mentor colleagues engaged in public policy activities, fostering collaboration, innovation, and strategic execution. – Drive internal engagement and education on policy issues, ensuring that senior leaders and business teams understand the implications of policy developments. – Anticipate and respond to emerging policy challenges related to data privacy, AI, real-world evidence, clinical trials, and market access. — ## Qualifications – A minimum of 10 years of relevant experience in public policy, government affairs, or regulatory strategy, with significant exposure to healthcare and life sciences policy. – Demonstrated success in shaping policy outcomes at the national level, including engagement with senior policymakers and regulators. – Deep expertise in one or more core areas, including clinical research, life sciences and health innovation policy, health data governance, digital health, or AI in healthcare. – Proven ability to lead complex, cross-functional initiatives in a global, matrixed organization. – Executive presence and ability to influence senior leaders internally and externally. – Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with experience developing materials for sophisticated policy and executive audiences. – Strong strategic thinking and analytical capabilities, with the ability to translate policy developments into business impact. – Experience managing relationships with trade associations, industry groups, and external stakeholders at the highest levels. – Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, dynamic environment and manage competing priorities. – Demonstrated ability to leverage data, digital tools, and insights to inform and enhance policy strategy. — ## Education – Bachelor’s degree in government, public policy, political science, or related field – Advanced degree (JD, MPP, MPH, or equivalent) preferred — IQVIA is a leading global provider of clinical research services, commercial insights and healthcare intelligence to the life sciences and healthcare industries. We create intelligent connections to accelerate the development and commercialization of innovative medical treatments to help improve patient outcomes and population health worldwide. Learn more at [https://jobs.iqvia.com] IQVIA is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, status as a protected veteran, or any other status protected by applicable law. [https://jobs.iqvia.com/eoe] IQVIA is committed to integrity in our hiring process and maintains a zero tolerance policy for candidate fraud. All information and credentials submitted in your application must be truthful and complete. Any false statements, misrepresentations, or material omissions during the recruitment process will result in immediate disqualification of your application, or termination of employment if discovered later, in accordance with applicable law. We appreciate your honesty and professionalism. The potential base pay range for this role, when annualized, is $160,200.00 – $446,200.00. The actual base pay offered may vary based on a number of factors including job-related qualifications such as knowledge, skills, education, and experience; location; and/or schedule (full or part-time). Dependent on the position offered, incentive plans, bonuses, and/or other forms of compensation may be offered, in addition to a range of health and welfare and/or other benefits.
