item.title: Director, Communications
item.description: Director, Communications Organization: Betterment Location: New York City, NY Date Posted: 07/27/2026 ## About Betterment Betterment is a leading, technology‑driven financial services company that offers investing, savings, and retirement solutions for retail investors and investment advisors, as well as financial wellness solutions, including a 401(k) for small and medium‑sized businesses. Our team is passionate about our mission to empower people to build wealth with confidence and ease. We’re headquartered in NYC and offer hybrid NY‑based positions (four days per week in‑office, with no required office days during the summer and winter holidays). ## About the Role The Communications team builds and protects Betterment’s brand position, tells our story in earned media, and supports growth across our three lines of business: retail investing, retirement (401(k)), and RIA custody. As Director, Communications, you will own the strategic direction for external communications, manage an internal team and two external PR agency partnerships, and serve as a senior communications counselor to leadership. Reporting to the VP, Strategy & Communications, you’ll shape how Betterment shows up in the market — from the narratives we pitch to reporters, to media appearances for our CEO, to how we launch products and respond in moments of crisis. This is a highly cross‑functional, highly visible role. The right person is both a sharp strategist and a hands‑on executor who thrives in a fast‑moving, regulated environment and knows how to translate complex financial topics into stories that resonate with consumers, business partners, advisors, and plan sponsors. This role is based out of our NYC office. Below we’ve reflected the base salary range for this position. Actual salaries may vary depending on factors including but not limited to location, experience, and performance. The range listed is just one component of Betterment’s total compensation package for employees. **New York City: $160,000 – $190,000** This job may also be eligible for variable compensation in the form of a company incentive bonus. ## A Day in the Life – Own the overarching communications strategy across all three lines of business, ensuring messaging is cohesive, differentiated, and aligned with company OKRs. – Serve as a trusted strategic advisor to the leadership team on brand reputation, public positioning, and narrative development. – Manage relationships with external PR agencies; collaborate to shape press strategy, identify and prioritize opportunities, and brief them on launches, company news, and proactive storylines. – Lead media relations, expanding relationships with top‑tier reporters, driving PR campaigns and product launches, and identifying earned media opportunities. – Craft and quality‑control press releases, talking points, bylines, and media responses; ensure tone, accuracy, and regulatory compliance. – Partner cross‑functionally with Marketing, Legal, Compliance, and Product on product launches, brand campaigns, and social media amplification. – Drive executive visibility programs including speaking engagements, conference strategy, and award submissions. – Support internal communications efforts in partnership with our People team. – Help oversee compliance review for all public‑facing communications content. ## What We’re Looking For – 10+ years of experience in communications or public relations either in‑house or at an agency, with at least 3 years in a leadership role. – Deep understanding of the financial services or fintech media landscape, with established journalist relationships. – Proven track record developing integrated communications strategies spanning media relations, internal comms, crisis management, executive positioning, and thought leadership. – Exceptional written and verbal communication skills; an ability to find the perfect phrase to inspire an audience or position a product. – Experience managing external agency relationships and balancing in‑house vs. outsourced resources. – Track record supporting C‑suite executive communications, spokesperson programs, and media training. – Experience in a regulated industry (financial services, fintech, or similar) strongly preferred. – A collaborative leader with outstanding judgment and high EQ. ## Join a Team Built on These Core Values ### We change lives Be a part of a community of innovators working to transform financial outcomes for real people. Your work will make an impact, always laddering up to our mission: to empower people to build wealth with confidence and ease. ### We set audacious goals We set them for the company, our customers, and ourselves, and we won’t stop until we reach them. We don’t just show up; we give our all, then celebrate our wins. ### We value all perspectives When we collaborate, we’re at our best. We believe diverse perspectives lead to better outcomes and strive to uphold our supportive and inclusive community. ### We simplify financial services We’re financial services pioneers, always finding new ways to improve, optimize, and enhance. Constant improvement is in our DNA. ## Our Commitment to Your Total Well‑being We offer a competitive suite of benefits, including medical, dental, and vision coverage; life and AD&D insurance; short‑ and long‑term disability; infertility support and WPATH‑aligned transgender health benefits; an Employee Assistance Program (EAP); transit benefits and FSA and HSA options. **Ownership:** Equity for all employees, including new hire and refresher grants. **Time:** Flexible paid time off, paid parental leave, and a fully paid four‑week sabbatical in your sixth year. **Growth:** Company‑paid professional coaching for all employees. **Wealth:** Day‑one 401(k) match plus matching on qualified student loan payments. ## What Happens Next We’ll take a few weeks to review all applications. If we’d like to spend more time with you, we’ll reach out to arrange next steps, which will include 3–4 sets of meetings with your future colleagues. In the interview process, we’ll look to learn more about your skills, experiences, capabilities, and motivators. Many of our questions will be aimed at understanding how you might operate here at Betterment. Depending on the role, we may ask you to complete a case study exercise or technical assessments, as we want to collect a robust set of data points to better inform our decisions. On average, it takes us around 3–5 weeks to make a hiring decision, depending on your availability and sense of urgency. As a best practice, we aim to interview at least 2–3 final‑round candidates before making a hiring decision. Please note that, as we usually receive an overwhelming number of applications for open positions, we’re unable to offer individual feedback during the interview process. We recognize that interviewing for a new role is a big deal. We appreciate you considering Betterment as the next step in your career, and our Recruiting Team is here to support and advocate for you throughout the interview process. Betterment is dedicated to providing accommodations to candidates upon request. If you need accommodations at any point throughout the interview process, please reach out to your recruiter. Please note that in any materials you submit, you may redact or remove age‑identifying information such as age, date of birth, or dates of school attendance or graduation. You will not be penalized for redacting or removing this information. ## Come Join Us! We’re an equal opportunity employer and comply with all applicable federal, state, and local fair employment practices laws. We strictly prohibit and do not tolerate discrimination against employees, applicants, or any other covered persons because of race, color, religion, creed, national origin or ancestry, ethnicity, sex, gender (including gender nonconformity and status as a transgender or transsexual individual), sexual orientation, marital status, age, physical or mental disability, citizenship, past, current or prospective service in the uniformed services, predisposing genetic characteristic, domestic violence victim status, arrest records, or any other characteristic protected under applicable federal, state, or local law. item.title: Copywriter
item.description: Copywriter Organization: Replit Location: Foster City, CA Date Posted: 07/27/2026 Replit is the agentic software creation platform that enables anyone to build applications using natural language. With millions of users worldwide, Replit is democratizing software development by removing traditional barriers to application creation. Brand & Creative defines how Replit shows up in the world and leads the creative work that brings it to market. On the Brand side, the function sets company-level direction: defining the brand, shaping the narrative, and establishing how Replit is understood and expressed in the market. On the Creative side, the function leads the planning, development, and execution of creative work across campaigns, launches, events, and major company initiatives; translating strategy into high-quality outputs across every touchpoint. Brand & Creative ensures that what Replit is and what Replit makes remain aligned, resulting in a clear, consistent, and differentiated brand experience across the company. ## Role The Copywriter is responsible for developing and applying brand messaging and written content across campaigns, launches, product marketing, events, and major company initiatives. The role focuses on writing clear, compelling, and consistent copy across a wide range of brand and marketing surfaces. In partnership with Design, Product, Marketing, and external partners, this role helps shape how Replit communicates across channels while contributing to the ongoing development of the brand voice. This role reports to the Brand & Creative Lead. ## Responsibilities – Write copy across campaigns, launches, social content, web, presentations, product marketing, and brand initiatives – Apply the Replit voice and messaging consistently across multiple touchpoints and formats – Support the development of messaging frameworks, naming, and campaign language – Collaborate closely with Designers, Producers, Marketing, Product, and cross-functional teams to develop integrated creative work – Contribute to concept development and creative ideation across campaigns and launches – Write and refine copy across short-form and long-form formats – Support the creation and maintenance of internal messaging and brand documentation – Review and refine copy to ensure clarity, consistency, and quality – Partner with external agencies and freelancers as needed – Contribute hands-on writing support across high-visibility company initiatives ## Requirements – 3–5+ years of experience in copywriting, brand writing, or creative writing roles at an agency, studio, in-house team, or equivalent environment – Strong portfolio demonstrating writing across campaigns, brand, marketing, and digital experiences – Strong understanding of voice, tone, messaging, and storytelling – Ability to write clearly and concisely across a wide range of formats and channels – Strong collaboration skills across creative and cross-functional teams – Strong attention to detail and consistency in language – Ability to balance conceptual thinking with execution – Experience working within fast-moving creative environments – Familiarity with product, technology, or startup environments is a plus This is a full-time role that can be held from our Foster City, CA office. The role has an in-office requirement of Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. ## Full-Time Employee Benefits Include: 💰 Competitive Salary & Equity 💹 401(k) Program with a 4% match (US Only) ⚕️ Health, Dental, Vision and Life Insurance 🩼 Short Term and Long Term Disability 🚼 Paid Parental, Medical, Caregiver Leave 🏝 Flexible Time Off (FTO) + Holidays 🚗 Commuter Benefits (In-Office Only) 📱 Monthly Wellness Stipend 🧑‍💻 Autonomous Work Environment 🖥 In Office Set-Up Reimbursement (In-Office Only) 🚀 Quarterly Team Gatherings ☕ In Office Amenities (In-Office Only) ## Want to learn more about what we are up to? Meet the Replit Agent Replit: Make an app for that Replit Blog Amjad TED Talk Interviewing + Culture at Replit Operating Principles Reasons not to work at Replit To achieve our mission of making programming more accessible around the world, we need our team to be representative of the world. We welcome your unique perspective and experiences in shaping this product. We encourage people from all kinds of backgrounds to apply, including and especially candidates from underrepresented and non-traditional backgrounds. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Global Trade Compliance Manager
item.description: Global Trade Compliance Manager Organization: Epirus Location: Torrance, CA Date Posted: 07/27/2026 ## About Epirus Epirus is a high-growth technology company dedicated to overcoming the asymmetric challenges inherent to the future of national security. Epirus’ flagship product, Leonidas, is a software-defined system built using intelligent power management techniques which allow power-hungry systems to do more with less. ## Job Summary The ideal Global Trade Compliance (“GTC”) Manager candidate is experienced in import and export compliance within a manufacturing environment. In this role, you will report to the Director of Contracts and Compliance and work closely with Engineering, Legal, Contracts, and Industrial Security team members. This role will oversee compliance with ITAR, EAR, U.S. Customs, OFAC, and other domestic and international trade laws and regulations. By partnering with internal stakeholders and external advisors, the GTC Manager will oversee the compliance program to bring predictability and standardization to business operations. As a subject matter expert, you will advise the most senior leaders and collaborate on strategic initiatives. As the leader of the GTC program, you will draft, manage, and deliver training on relevant policies and procedures, create standard processes and checklists, and develop efficient methods for routine import and export activities. You will monitor changes in pertinent regulations and deliver updates to employees as necessary. You will collaborate with engineers to complete jurisdiction classifications to support new product development. This position will begin as an individual contributor; however, direct reports will be added as the business grows. ## Responsibilities – Manage the import and export compliance program – Draft export licenses for commodities and technical data – Manage all authorizations and technology transfer plans – Prepare written jurisdiction classifications for commodities and technical data – Draft and implement policies and procedures – Oversee the denied-party screening program – Support internal investigations – Supervise and assist with audits – Utilize IT systems that contain and manage export-controlled technical data ## Basic Qualifications – Bachelor’s degree from an accredited university – 5–7 years of import/export experience, preferably in a defense and/or manufacturing business environment – Extensive knowledge of the ITAR, EAR, and OFAC regulations – Basic knowledge of import regulations – Demonstrated export licensing experience – Experience working with U.S. government IT systems, including DECCS and SNAP-R – This is a hybrid position with a minimum of 3 days onsite and 2 days remote ## Preferred Skills and Experience – U.S. Customs Broker License, CUSECO or other industry certifications – Master’s or other graduate-level degree – Strong written and verbal communication skills – Proactive and collaborative mindset with a willingness to solve complex problems – Knowledge of lean process improvement and/or Agile systems and tools – Familiarity with OCR-EASE – A positive attitude and the ability to influence others – Superior administrative skills to manage multiple areas of a compliance program ## Additional Requirements Regular travel is not anticipated for this role; however, occasional trips could be necessary to support customer meetings, attend training events, and/or meet with government regulators. ## ITAR Requirements To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here. People are the most important part of Epirus – and always come first. We don’t believe in the word impossible and are always asking “why not” as we work to usher in a new paradigm of power efficiency. Our fast-growing team is agile, creative, and innovative. We support a culture of constant learning and sense of belonging among our team members and know that mentorship matters. We embrace diversity, equity, and inclusion in the workplace and beyond. To deliver on our mission, we are always looking for problem solvers, changemakers, and innovators to join our fast-growing team. ## Compensation As required by the Equal Pay Transparency Act, Epirus provides a reasonable range of minimum compensation for roles that may be hired. Actual compensation is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to skill set, level of experience, and specific office location. For the state of California only, the range of starting pay for this role is: **$129,600 – $165,200 USD** Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Specialist, Paid Search
item.description: Specialist, Paid Search Organization: Centerfield Location: Playa Vista, CA Date Posted: 07/27/2026 ## The Opportunity Centerfield is looking for a talented **Specialist, Paid Search** to join our team. In this role, you will work closely with our Media Buying team to learn best practices for managing Pay‑Per‑Click (PPC) campaigns. You will support the launch, maintenance, and optimization of PPC campaigns, including ad scheduling, tracking, reporting, and performance optimization. Paid Search Specialists play a key role in supporting Centerfield’s Media Buyers with both pre‑ and post‑campaign activities. You will be responsible for coordinating campaign traffic, monitoring advertising campaign delivery, and assisting with ongoing campaign maintenance to help ensure successful performance and execution. — ## How You’ll Contribute • Help identify and resolve issues that negatively impact campaigns. • Bid management, account architecture, and day‑to‑day monitoring of campaign performance. • Conduct keyword research for optimization, including adding new keywords and eliminating underperforming keywords. • Run weekly and daily performance reports and work with media buyers to produce campaign recap and verification reports for clients as needed. • Assist with any additional duties required to enable ad revenue growth, ensure efficient ad delivery, and organize campaign assets to help expedite efficient trafficking. • Extract campaign data and generate reports that summarize campaign performance. • Create and interpret performance reports to provide actionable insights. • Help execute PPC campaigns including account setup, uploading keywords, ad creatives and ad extensions, strategy and tactical development, and organization. — ## What We’re Looking For • Bachelor’s Degree preferred but not required. • Minimum 1–2 years of experience creating, managing, and optimizing **Paid Search campaigns**. • Advanced Excel skills with the ability to complete VLOOKUPs and Pivot Tables. • Experience working with Google AdWords and AdWords Editor (Bing Ads, Yahoo!, Bing, etc.). • Basic understanding of marketing KPIs and search metrics such as CPC, CTR, CPA, and conversion rates. • Highly analytical mindset — comfortable digging into data, questioning what the numbers are telling you, and turning insights into action. • Entrepreneurial spirit — you take initiative, move with urgency, and treat every campaign like it’s your own. • Passion for digital media and the ability to thrive in a fast‑paced, entrepreneurial environment. • Strong interpersonal and verbal communication skills, with the ability to articulate clearly and effectively in person and in writing. • Excellent organizational skills and the ability to juggle multiple responsibilities at once. • An independent worker with strong time management and organization skills. — ## Bonus Points • Experience using Tableau. • Experience with Claude or other enterprise‑level AI tools. • Bonus points if you’ve run a side business, freelanced, or built something on your own — we love people who know what it means to have skin in the game. — ## Life at Centerfield • This is a hybrid position — employees work in our Playa Vista, CA office every Tuesday, Wednesday & Thursday. • Competitive salary + semi‑annual bonus. • Unlimited PTO — take a break when you need it. • Industry‑leading medical, dental, and vision plans + generous parental leave. • 401(k) company match plan — fully vested on day 1. • Outside patio overlooking Playa Vista, monthly happy hours, catered lunches + daily food trucks. • Free onsite gym, award‑winning culture, paid volunteer days, and career growth — we promote from within. Compensation$70K – $72.5K • Offers Bonus Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Organizing Manager
item.description: Organizing Manager Organization: EveryTown for Gun Safety Location: New York, NY | Washington, D.C. Date Posted: 07/27/2026 ## Salary Range $71,000.00 to $73,000.00 Annually Everytown for Gun Safety is looking for two (2) Organizing Managers to join the Advocacy Campaigns team to continue the development and success of the organization. Each Organizing Manager oversees several state‑level volunteer chapters of Moms Demand Action, which also includes Everytown Survivor Network volunteers and collaboration with Students Demand Action volunteers. The role focuses on growing the volunteer base in their states, training chapter leaders and leadership teams, and building inclusive, equitable chapters that represent the diversity of each state. Organizing Managers work with chapter leadership to develop strategic growth plans and grassroots organizing as well as electoral campaigns for each state. They assess needs, collaboratively set priorities, identify resources, and support chapters in communications, partnerships, educational work, and advocacy efforts. Organizing Managers conduct site visits, hold regular meetings with leaders, and run campaigns alongside members of other Everytown teams. Organizing Managers receive training and resources upon starting, including background on the gun violence prevention movement, Everytown’s policy positions, managing for equity and inclusion, and volunteer management training. They are expected to provide strong support to volunteers, including timely and thoughtful communication. This position is based in the NY or DC offices with a hybrid schedule, though remote work may be considered for the right candidate. The role requires some travel, flexibility across time zones, and occasional evening and weekend availability. — ## RESPONSIBILITIES ### Chapter Growth and Building Power – Implement innovative strategies to recruit new volunteers and mobilize action on priority campaigns. – Collaboratively create and oversee growth plans for chapters, developing both breadth and depth of knowledge. – Ensure volunteer chapters build sustainable, diverse grassroots field power to prevent gun violence. – Utilize data on gun violence, chapter growth, and volunteer retention to guide chapter priorities. ### Develop Volunteer Leaders – Mentor, train, and manage volunteer leaders to support and grow volunteer engagement; regularly assess engagement and development needs. – Build diverse teams using management skills for equity and inclusion and equip volunteer leaders with the same skill set. – Value different perspectives and proactively engage people with varied backgrounds to build a strong movement, while teaching volunteers to do the same. – Lead by example through integrity and professionalism. – Share direct feedback and listen to and implement feedback received. ### Organizing Strategy and Campaign Development – Work closely with the Field Leadership Team, regional Organizing Directors, and cross‑departmental teams to develop national and local strategies. – Collaboratively set long‑ and short‑term priorities with chapters; ensure work remains focused while maintaining flexibility to respond to new opportunities. – Seed, encourage, and support tactical innovations from volunteers and help replicate successes. – Ensure campaign plans reflect realities on the ground; act as a bridge between volunteers and stakeholders to ensure plans are realistic and set up to succeed. ### Represent Moms Demand Action and Everytown – Serve as a thought partner between volunteer leaders and the organization; build confidence and excitement about priorities and choices. – Maintain timely and regular communication with Chapter Leadership; serve as first point of contact and connect them to staff as needed. – Serve as a public spokesperson when appropriate and approved. ### Other Duties – Develop knowledge on gun violence prevention policy, local and regional politics, and relevant issues. – Monitor social media and public platforms for appropriate content; ensure Chapter Leadership adheres to the Social Media Code of Conduct. – Manage regional budgets and approve chapter budget requests. – Serve as liaison between the Organizing Team and other departments. – Other duties as assigned. — ## QUALIFICATIONS – Understanding of stereotypes, bias, and forms of racism in America—including structural racism, implicit bias, gender bias, religious bias, ageism, and bias based on gender identity or sexual orientation—and ability to articulate their connection to the disproportionate impact of gun violence on specific demographic groups. – Understanding of power, voice, and privilege in interactions, and commitment to using them to make the movement more equitable. – Passion for the organization’s mission. – Strong volunteer or staff management skills, particularly experience working with diverse or marginalized communities and volunteer leaders. – Passion for and demonstrated experience developing and mentoring volunteers or staff. – Organizing or campaign experience (issue or electoral). – Experience writing and leading trainings. – Ability to understand, evaluate, and articulate policy and strategic planning issues. – Strong interpersonal skills. – Ability to work with deadlines, under pressure, and with flexibility. – Ability to travel within the US; up to 25% travel may be required. – Self‑motivated and proactive problem solver. – Comfort with social media, data management, and technology including VAN, Google Suite, and Slack. – Fluency in Spanish is a plus but not required. The salary range for this position is $71,000 to $73,000 per year. Everytown offers a generous benefits package including medical, vision, and dental insurance, paid time off, 401K match, education assistance, and more. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions. **Please note:** Information provided in the application process, including education, is verified. — ## How to Apply Please attach a thoughtful cover letter and resume with your application. Label your materials with your full name. — ## ABOUT MOMS DEMAND ACTION Moms Demand Action for Gun Sense in America is a grassroots movement of Americans fighting for public safety measures that protect people from gun violence. The organization campaigns for stronger solutions to lax gun laws and loopholes that jeopardize family safety. Moms Demand Action has chapters in every state and, along with Mayors Against Illegal Guns, Students Demand Action, and the Everytown Survivor Network, is part of Everytown for Gun Safety—the largest gun violence prevention organization in the country with over 10 million supporters and more than 350,000 donors. — ## ABOUT STUDENTS DEMAND ACTION Students Demand Action is a grassroots movement created by and for teens and young adults to channel their energy into the fight against gun violence. Volunteers work within schools and communities to educate peers, register voters, and demand common‑sense solutions. Together with Everytown for Gun Safety and Moms Demand Action, Students Demand Action volunteers are part of a network of over 10 million supporters committed to gun violence prevention. — ## ABOUT EVERYTOWN FOR GUN SAFETY Everytown for Gun Safety Action Fund (“Everytown for Gun Safety”) is the largest gun violence prevention organization in the nation, with nearly ten million supporters including parents, students, survivors, educators, gun owners, and others. Through victories in Congress, statehouses, corporate America, the courts, and town halls, Everytown is helping change how Americans think about this public health threat. At its core are Moms Demand Action and Students Demand Action. Learn more at everytown.org and follow @Everytown. You can learn about the framework guiding our work by viewing Everytown’s Organizational Values. Everytown for Gun Safety provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, amnesty, or veteran status in accordance with applicable laws. Candidates from historically underrepresented groups are strongly encouraged to apply. A diverse workforce and open culture are vital to our success. item.title: Policy Counsel
item.description: Policy Counsel Organization: EveryTown for Gun Safety Location: New York, NY | Washington, D.C. Date Posted: 07/27/2026 ### Salary Range $110,000.00 to $120,000.00 Annually Everytown for Gun Safety, the largest gun violence prevention advocacy group in the country, is seeking a passionate, dedicated attorney to join its Policy team. The Policy team works to advance Everytown’s mission to reduce gun violence by improving gun-related laws and regulations in all 50 states and at the federal level, generating groundbreaking original research, and contributing to Everytown’s position as a thought leader in the gun violence prevention movement. A key part of the role will be to work as part of an internal, cross-departmental team to develop, advise on, and implement a complex, multi-state policy strategy in a region. You will also need to work in collaboration with state legislators, advocacy organizations, lobbyists, and other influencers to seize opportunities to pass and protect lifesaving gun violence prevention laws at the state level. This is a full-time position based in New York City or Washington, DC, reporting to the Director of Policy Advocacy. — ### Responsibilities – **Draft legislation** to promote gun safety at the state and local level – **Analyze legislation**, legal opinions, and criminal court records – **Perform research** on Second Amendment and other firearm-related jurisprudence and gun laws around the country – **Contribute to reports** and draft other public-facing materials – **Support cross-functional teams** engaged in Government Affairs, Political, Research, Communications, and Digital projects – **Review materials** for accuracy, including reports, speeches, op-eds, emails, and social media posts – **Represent the organization** before legislative bodies and in other public forums — ### Qualifications – **J.D. degree** and membership in a state bar – **2+ years of experience** of relevant professional experience – **Ability to build relationships** across the organization and work toward a common goal – **Excellent research and writing** skills with outstanding attention to detail – **Ability to explain legal concepts** to a general audience – **Strong work ethic**, sense of humor, flexibility, creativity, and a professional demeanor – **Ability to manage multiple projects** in a fast-moving environment and deliver timely, high-quality work – **Willingness to travel** on occasion, possibly on short notice – **Comfort in open-plan office** environments – **Commitment to gun violence prevention** — The annual salary range for this role is $110,000 to $120,000 per year. Everytown offers a generous package including medical, vision, and dental insurance, paid time off, 401K match, education assistance, and more. — ### How to Apply Applications will be accepted until the position is filled. Please include a thoughtful cover letter, including any salary requirements, and a resume. — ### Diverse Workforce and Open Culture Candidates who identify as members of historically underrepresented groups are highly encouraged to apply to Everytown. A diverse workforce and open culture are at the heart of our organization and vital to our success. Everytown for Gun Safety Support Fund provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, amnesty, or status as a covered veteran in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws. You can learn about the framework that guides our work by viewing Everytown’s Organizational Values. — ### About Everytown for Gun Safety Support Fund Everytown for Gun Safety Support Fund (the “Everytown Support Fund”) is the education, research, and litigation arm of Everytown for Gun Safety, the largest gun violence prevention organization in the country with more than 11 million supporters and more than 800,000 donors. The Everytown Support Fund seeks to improve our understanding of the causes of gun violence and help reduce it by conducting groundbreaking original research, developing evidence-based policies, communicating this knowledge to the American public, and advancing gun safety and gun violence prevention in communities and the courts. Learn more at [ www.everytownsupportfund.org ] Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.description: Deputy Director, Government Affairs Organization: EveryTown for Gun Safety Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 07/27/2026 ## Salary Range $135,000.00 to $147,000.00 Annually The Government Affairs team leads advocacy and campaign strategy across federal, state, and local government. This role will serve as a senior member of the federal affairs team, helping drive lobbying strategy on Capitol Hill while also supporting integrated state legislative campaigns. The ideal candidate brings deep federal experience, strong political instincts, and proven management ability. This person should be comfortable operating in fast‑moving legislative environments, managing relationships with senior policymakers and staff, and overseeing team members running campaigns across multiple states. — ## We Trust You to Take On the Following Responsibilities – **Federal lobbying leadership** — Lead federal lobbying portfolio and advocacy efforts before Congress and the Administration – **Legislative strategy development** — Develop and execute legislative strategies tied to organizational priorities – **Relationship management** — Build and maintain relationships with Members of Congress, congressional staff, coalition partners, and external stakeholders – **Legislative tracking** — Track and analyze federal legislative and political developments and advise senior leadership on strategy and engagement opportunities – **Team management** — Manage and mentor up to two Associate Directors with their own government affairs portfolio that includes leading state, federal, and local campaigns in multiple states – **Campaign support** — Support state and local campaign strategy, manage and contribute to other priority government affairs projects as needed, and support broader team development – **Integrated advocacy oversight** — Oversee and support integrated advocacy campaigns that may include federal, state, and in‑district organizing and legislative activity – **Cross‑team partnership** — Partner with communications, policy, political, and research teams to align advocacy strategy and messaging – **State legislative support** — Support state legislative and in‑district efforts as needed, including stakeholder engagement, coalition management, legislative strategy, and campaign execution – **Representation** — Represent the organization in coalition meetings, briefings, advocacy events, and external engagements – **Cross‑functional coordination** — Help coordinate cross‑functional efforts during key legislative moments, including hearings, markups, floor votes, and campaign activations — ## The Ideal Candidate Will Have – **Government affairs experience** — 7+ years of relevant experience in government affairs, Capitol Hill, political campaigns, advocacy, or related fields – **Congressional or executive experience** — Significant experience working in Congress, the Executive Branch, or senior‑level political campaigns preferred – **Staff management** — Demonstrated experience managing staff and leading complex advocacy or legislative efforts – **Federal process knowledge** — Strong understanding of the federal legislative process and political landscape – **Multi‑level government experience** — Experience working across multiple levels of government and supporting coordinated campaigns – **Relationship building** — Strong relationship‑building skills with policymakers, staff, coalition partners, and external stakeholders – **Communication skills** — Excellent written and verbal communication skills – **Priority management** — Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast‑paced environment – **Strategic thinking** — Strategic thinker with strong political judgment and execution skills – **Capitol Hill relationships** — Existing relationships on Capitol Hill and within national advocacy coalitions — ## Preferred Experience – **Managing lobbyists** — Experience managing federal lobbyists, campaign staff, or legislative teams – **Inside/outside advocacy** — Background supporting both inside‑the‑building and outside‑the‑building advocacy strategies – **State/local campaigns** — Familiarity with state‑government and local‑government legislative campaigns and in‑district organizing — ## What Success Looks Like – Strong federal engagement strategy and execution – Effective management and development of Associate Directors – Seamless coordination between federal lobbying and state/in‑district campaigns – Clear communication and strong cross‑team collaboration – Ability to move quickly and strategically during high‑pressure legislative moments — The salary range for this position is $135,000 to $147,000 per year. Everytown offers a generous package including medical, vision, and dental insurance, paid time off, 401K match, education assistance, and more. — ## About the Hiring Process We are accepting applications on a rolling basis and will review them and reach out to candidates who meet the requirements of the position. *Please note: To be considered for the role, you must submit a cover letter and an updated resume with your application. Applications missing a cover letter and/or a resume will not be reviewed by the Hiring Team.* — ## Diverse Workforce and Open Culture Candidates who identify as members of historically underrepresented groups are highly encouraged to apply to Everytown. A diverse workforce and open culture are at the heart of our organization and vital to our success. Everytown for Gun Safety Support Fund provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, amnesty, or status as a covered veteran in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws. You can learn about the framework that guides our work by viewing Everytown’s Organizational Values. — ## About Everytown for Gun Safety Everytown for Gun Safety Action Fund (“Everytown for Gun Safety”) is the largest gun violence prevention organization in the country with nearly 11 million supporters and more than 700,000 donors, including moms, mayors, survivors, students, and everyday Americans who are fighting for common‑sense gun safety measures that can help save lives. For nearly 30 years, we have partnered with impacted communities and those we represent to pursue justice and prosperity for all through policy advocacy, strategic litigation, research, coalition‑building, and support for grassroots action. The North Carolina Justice Center is seeking a Director of the Immigrant and Refugee Rights Project to lead efforts to work for and with low‑income immigrants and refugees in North Carolina. This position oversees legal services, policy advocacy, community engagement, public education, and related programmatic work to advance the rights and wellbeing of immigrant and refugee communities. — ## Key Responsibilities ### Project Leadership & Management – Lead the design, implementation, and evaluation of assigned projects and initiatives. – Develop detailed workplans, timelines, deliverables, and performance metrics. – Provide strategic feedback and insight to executive leadership regarding NCJC’s work with immigrants and refugees. ### Organizational Leadership & Supervision – Supervise project staff, consultants, and interns. – Provide coaching, performance feedback, and professional development support. ### Legal Practice & Litigation Leadership – Oversee the provision of quality legal representation for individual clients. – Oversee strategic approaches for litigation impact. – Manage a litigation caseload. – Oversee immigration and civil litigation matters on behalf of immigrant clients. ### Policy Advocacy – Manage efforts to advance public policies that improve the wellbeing of immigrants and expand opportunities for economic security. – Oversee community engagement and education initiatives. – Support and manage relationships with immigrant organizations throughout North Carolina. – Lead workgroups and coalitions of advocates and community leaders to coordinate advocacy and education initiatives. ### Budget & Grant Management – Oversee and manage fundraising efforts for IRRP, including strategic funding plans. – Serve as primary grant writer and manager for IRRP grants in coordination with the development team. ### Stakeholder Engagement & Strategic Communications – Serve as a primary liaison with community partners, funders, and external stakeholders. – Build and maintain effective partnerships to support project goals. — ## item.title: National Communications Director
item.description: National Communications Director Organization: TechTonic Justice Location: Remote Date Posted: 07/27/2026 ## **Lead TechTonic Justice’s national communications strategy to expose AI harms, build public power, and advance justice for low-income communities** ### **About TechTonic Justice, Inc.** Governments, landlords, employers, and other powerful actors use artificial intelligence (AI), algorithms, and related technologies to make decisions about how low-income people work, live, learn, and survive. When people are hurt by AI decision-making, they have few places to turn. TechTonic Justice exists to change this. TechTonic Justice fights the ground-level harms AI causes low-income communities. We do this mainly by supporting local justice movements—legal aid organizations, frontline service providers, grassroots organizers, and affected communities—to identify and fight harmful uses of AI. We emphasize a multidimensional advocacy approach that blends litigation, community activation and organizing, public education, and narrative advocacy. We are based in Los Angeles and offer our services nationwide, with emphasis on the South and the West Coast. — ## **Description** Governments, landlords, employers, and other powerful actors use artificial intelligence (AI), algorithms, and related technologies to make decisions about how low-income people work, live, learn, and survive. When people are hurt by AI decision-making, they have few places to turn. TechTonic Justice (TTJ) exists to change this. TTJ fights the ground-level injustice AI causes low-income communities by blending legal advocacy, community organizing, public education, and storytelling to (1) reduce immediate harms and (2) build the long-term power needed to win systemic protections. To these ends, we focus on and work with local justice movements—legal aid organizations, frontline service providers, grassroots organizers, civil rights advocates, and affected communities—to identify and resist harmful uses of AI. The primary substantive issue areas our work touches on are public benefits (primarily Medicaid, SNAP, Social Security, and Unemployment Insurance), K–12 education, workers’ rights, and housing. TTJ publicly launched in November 2024. The Communications Director will be the 13th member of our fast-growing team. We are inspired by dozens of collective years of justice work in the U.S. South with an ongoing commitment to the region, have teammates in several states/regions (California, the South, the DC area, and New England), offer services nationwide, and do state-level work in Arkansas and California. — ## **Position Description and Responsibilities** The Communications Director is a permanent, full-time, remote role. Candidates must live in the continental U.S. (unfortunately, we cannot hire someone in Hawai’i or Alaska for this role) and, due to the many time zones involved, should anticipate working a schedule that maximizes availability between 9 am and 2 pm Pacific time. The Communications Director will ensure we communicate effectively to key national, state, and local audiences, prioritizing: 1. Low-income communities 2. Grassroots movement partners 3. Legal aid and frontline advocates, and their direct advocates in antipoverty efforts and grassroots movements 4. Policymakers 5. Professional policy advocates who are more distant from the ground 6. Institutional funders 7. Targeted parts of the general public The aim of all such communication is to build trust with our audiences so that we increase engagement with our issues and approach, expand the reach of our harm reduction efforts, strengthen our organizing, and maintain and expand funding opportunities. Successfully balancing various audiences, focuses, and purposes (e.g., state comms needs may differ from those of our national strategy) is a critical feature of the role. The Communications Director will develop and execute a strategy aligned with these priorities, understanding that we see the narrative landscape as a critical front in our multi-dimensional fight against AI injustice. Put otherwise, we want someone who sees themselves as an advocate whose primary tool (or weapon) is communications. The Communications Director will supervise TTJ’s Digital Manager, who manages our day-to-day social media work, and future Comms roles we may add. The senior-level position reports directly to TTJ’s President and includes the following activities: ### **Key Responsibilities** – Bolstering TTJ’s presence in traditional media through strategies that could include cultivating relationships with key reporters and outlets, proactively pitching stories and securing coverage, positioning TTJ staff as expert sources, and placing OpEds. – Bolstering “new media” presence by reaching influencers, streamers, podcasters, YouTubers, and related content creators and outlets and preparing our team to engage with them successfully. – Supervising and expanding our digital engagement efforts, including via social media (text, photo, and video platforms), partner toolkits, newsletters, webinars, our website, and alternative spaces, with particular focus on increasing audience size, intensifying audience engagement, and recruiting activated people into our digital organizing pipeline. – Managing the design, graphics, and distribution of written work (e.g., guides, toolkits, frameworks, fact sheets, and reports). – Amplifying the reach and impact of a first-in-the-field model of a Story Fellow with a distinguished background in journalism. – Building and institutionalizing TTJ’s Communications Department, including developing operating procedures, cross-team information flows, performance indicators, a departmental spend budget, and relationships with ecosystem partners. – Strengthening organizational communications practices by developing strategy, devising narrative campaigns, building storytelling vehicles (audio, visual, animation, zines, etc.), executing plans, testing messages, training teammates, harmonizing language, and doing rapid-response work when appropriate. — ## **Requirements** The successful candidate must possess the skills and experience needed to fulfill the responsibilities above, including: – Extensive experience working as a communications professional with high-stakes responsibilities meeting deadlines in a fast-paced environment, including at least modest experience supervising paid full-time teammates. *Note: To succeed in this role, we estimate that a person would need at least 8–10 years of experience and at least 2 years of supervisory experience, but these are not strict thresholds.* – Experience thriving in a dynamic start-up environment where systems and processes are still being built, immediate needs may shift, and teammates must adapt flexibly. – Extensive networks among some combination of established journalists and news outlets, new media creators and platforms, and social change organizations or movements, with concrete plans to build out missing networks. – Deep familiarity with current topics, trends, and personalities sufficient to take advantage of often-narrow windows of cultural relevance. – Outstanding writing skills. – Strong sense of visual design and experience working iteratively with and managing graphic designers. – Ability to work independently with minimal supervision, including proactively identifying needs, exercising good judgment, executing tasks with attention to detail, synthesizing complex topics into digestible written work, and knowing when to ask questions. – Significant experience in justice-focused work in a nonprofit or nonprofit-adjacent environment, preferably within anti-poverty, tech justice, or civil rights ecosystems. *Note: We do not expect the Communications Director to possess all needed substantive expertise upon starting; we will provide support and time to learn.* – Empathy, righteous fury, and a sense of humor. – Collaborative spirit, cultural competence, and skills needed to work affirmingly with diverse teammates, partners, coalition members, consultants, and the communities we serve. – Comfort articulating intersections between poverty, race, ethnicity, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, language, age, disability, and related characteristics. ### **Desired but not required** – Ability to create compelling graphic designs. — ## **Be Encouraged to Apply** If you meet many, but not all, of the requirements, please still consider applying or email us to ask about where you fall short. We encourage applications from Black, Indigenous, and other people of color, women, LGBTQI+ people, people with disabilities, formerly incarcerated people, and people most impacted by systemic injustice. Employment decisions are made based on qualifications and organizational needs, without regard to race, national origin, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, religion, citizenship status, disability, marital status, veteran status, or any protected characteristic under applicable law. — ## **Salary** $120,000 – $140,000 per year, depending on experience. Current budget projections anticipate annual cost-of-living salary increases. Service time raises are anticipated but still to be determined. The position is exempt. Employment is at-will. — ## **Schedule Flexibility** TechTonic Justice allows flexibility in scheduling regular work hours to fit the successful candidate’s personal situation, including health needs or caregiving responsibilities. This flexibility is limited by organizational needs, including availability for internal and external meetings. Candidates should anticipate working a schedule that maximizes availability between 9 am and 2 pm Pacific time (with some flexibility). Candidates should also anticipate regular deviation from scheduled work hours to complete deadline-driven projects. ***Presently, we do not anticipate offering regular four-day workweeks.*** — ## **Benefits** The benefits pack

item.title: State Communications Strategist
item.description: State Communications Strategist Organization: The Clean Slate Initiative (CSI) Location: Remote Date Posted: 07/27/2026 ## About The Clean Slate Initiative The Clean Slate Initiative (CSI) is a national, bipartisan organization advancing policies that automate and expand eligibility for record sealing. Our work helps ensure that a past arrest or conviction does not remain a lifelong barrier to employment, housing, education, and full participation in civic life. Today, one in three people in the United States has a record. For millions, that record limits their opportunities, even long after they’ve completed their sentence and remained crime-free. Our vision is a society where no one is defined by their past, and everyone has a fair shot to achieve their full potential. Clean Slate laws have been enacted in 14 states and Washington D.C., impacting more than 18 million people. We work alongside partners, directly impacted individuals, and community leaders to shape policy, drive implementation, and reframe the public conversation around second chances — turning hope into opportunity. — ## About the Opportunity CSI is hiring two State Communications Strategists to lead the development, execution, and optimization of strategic communications supporting our state work. We are hiring for two distinct focus areas: – **State Communications Strategist – Campaigns**, who will support active state legislative campaigns. – **State Communications Strategist – Implementation**, who will support colleagues and state partners in states with newly enacted state laws, including increasing knowledge and awareness among impacted individuals and communities. People hired for these positions will craft and support communications strategies that drive public awareness and mobilize support for Clean Slate policies. They will partner closely with our Director of Campaign Communications, other members of the Marketing & Communications team, campaign strategists, implementation managers, and external advocacy partners. Depending on the position, they will support either Clean Slate campaigns or implementation efforts at the intersection of marketing, communications, and strategy—advancing high-impact partnerships, digital engagement, earned media, and partner communications. — ## Responsibilities – Serve as CSI’s representative on communications working groups in state coalitions. – Develop and maintain public-facing communications and educational resources that support CSI’s emerging notification practice by helping impacted individuals understand record sealing relief and navigate the process of checking or confirming whether their records have been sealed. – Provide hands-on support for partners as they create educational materials (web, flyers, social media, etc.) for impacted individuals after Clean Slate laws are passed. – Create media strategies for legislative and implementation successes and to influence government actors during legislative campaigns or when there are implementation problems. – Serve as the primary communications partner to state coalitions, building trusted relationships while supporting the development of collaborative communications plans, messaging, and opportunities to amplify state efforts through CSI channels. – Collaborate with CSI campaign strategists and implementation managers to ensure communications are aligned with legislative strategy, implementation goals, and partner needs. – Collaborate with partners to expand their visibility and media confidence by helping them craft compelling stories, connect with journalists, and develop long-term media relationships that position them as reliable and trusted sources for journalists. – Coordinate content creation and deployment: collateral (flyers, one-pagers, toolkits), digital assets, video/story assets, campaign microsites, etc. – Create and disseminate outreach guidance, templates, and training materials for coalition partners that are informed by best practices. – Serve as a subject-matter contributor and communications advisor to internal teams and external stakeholders, guiding partner organizations, coalition members, and state teams in communications best practices. — ## Qualifications ### Required – Minimum 5–7 years of strategic marketing/communications experience, preferably in a nonprofit, advocacy, or policy-campaign setting. – Proven ability to develop and implement integrated communications plans that include digital, earned media, partner/collaborator channels, and storytelling. – Demonstrated success in education-oriented communications: translating complex guidance into accessible and usable information. – Strong writing and editing skills: able to translate complex policy/data into accessible, compelling messages for multiple audiences. – Demonstrated success in educational or issue-oriented communications strategies: aligning communications strategy with organizational, legislative, and post-legislative goals. – Strong collaboration skills: able to partner across teams (campaigns, research/data, program, external partners) and manage multiple stakeholders. – Solid analytical and metrics-driven mindset: comfortable interpreting data, setting KPIs, and adjusting strategy accordingly. – Commitment to equity, inclusion, and centering directly impacted voices in narrative work. – Ability to work in a remote environment, across time zones, with minimal supervision and strong self-management. ### Preferred – Experience working in or with state/federal policy campaigns, legislative or advocacy environments. – Background in narrative change, brand building, and social justice/justice-reform communications. – Prior experience with public relations and media placements (national or regional). – Familiarity with and passion for the mission of Clean Slate, criminal legal system reform, and second-chance initiatives. – Lived experience (or close family experience) with the criminal legal system is valued at CSI. — ## Success Metrics – Build and facilitate active state communications working groups. – Foster strong, trusted partnerships with state communications leads. – Develop collaborative communications plans aligned with campaign goals. – Increase participation of directly impacted leaders in communications efforts. – Drive effective use of CSI messaging, narrative, and communications resources. – Ensure timely, consistent communication and aligned messaging across state coalitions. – Strengthen partners’ communications, media, and storytelling capabilities. — ## Compensation and Benefits Comprehensive benefits package that includes 100% employer-paid health, dental, and vision insurance, a 6% employer match towards 401k retirement, pre-tax transportation benefits, and paid holidays, vacation, sick, and casual time off. The Clean Slate Initiative is committed to transparent and fair compensation. The hiring range for this position is **$90,000–$95,000 per year**. The final salary within this range will be determined based on qualifications and relevant experience. Once an offer is made, CSI does not negotiate the compensation package. This is a full-time, exempt, remote position. CSI is location agnostic within the United States, though hybrid or in-office work may be discussed for candidates near the Orlando office. You will need to: – Reside in the United States and be authorized to work in the United States. – Work collaboratively with a team across time zones. – Be close to a major airport with the ability to travel approximately 10–15%. – Attend required onsite planning meetings at least twice a year in various locations. – Attend one all-staff learning trip and the annual convening each year. CSI is a 501(c)(3) public entity that passes and implements laws that automatically clear eligible records for people who have completed their sentence and remained crime-free, and expands who is eligible for clearance. CSI is committed to attracting, developing, and retaining exceptional people, and to creating a work environment that is dynamic, rewarding, and inclusive. — ## How to Apply Applicants are encouraged to review CSI’s website: **cleanslateinitiative.org**. Interested candidates may submit their application via the Talent Portal . Questions should be directed to ** [email protected] **. — ## Tentative Timeline – **Application Period:** July 21, 2026 – August 11, 2026 – Applications reviewed continuously; early submission encouraged. – **First Interviews:** Weeks of August 17, August 24, and August 31, 2026 – **In-Basket Exercise:** After first interviews – **Panel Interviews:** Weeks of September 14 and September 21, 2026 – **Finalist Interview with CEO:** Week of September 28, 2026 – **Reference Checks:** Week of September 28, 2026 – **Offer Extension:** Week of October 5, 2026 – **Tentative Start Date:** October 19, 2026 CSI reserves the right to adjust the timeline. — ## Reasonable Accommodations CSI provides equal employment opportunities to qualified individuals with disabilities. If you require an accommodation during the hiring process, contact ** [email protected] **. — ## Other Employment Standards Applicants must have work authorization that does not require visa sponsorship now or in the future. Candidates will not be required to disclose sealed or expunged records. — **Pay Range: $90,000.00 to $95,000.00 Annually** Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Southern Regional Manager
item.description: Southern Regional Manager Organization: VoteRiders Location: Remote Date Posted: 07/27/2026 # OVERVIEW The **VoteRiders Southern Regional Manager (SRM)** leads VoteRiders’ programming across the Southern region and grows the organization’s impact there. This individual works closely with VoteRiders’ National Field Director, Department Directors and Deputy Directors, the Chief Operating Officer, and the Chief Executive/Executive Director to plan, manage, and execute voter ID–focused field programs across the South. The Southern Regional Manager will lead overall regional programming and partnership work, serving as the primary contact for state-based partners in **Alabama, Mississippi, and Louisiana**, and will oversee the work in **Georgia and Florida**. VoteRiders does not maintain a physical office, but candidates must be physically based in or willing to relocate immediately to the Southern region and be able to travel regularly within the specified states. While candidates from AL, FL, GA, LA, and MS will be considered, there is a preference for candidates based in or willing to relocate to **Alabama, Louisiana, or Mississippi**, where VoteRiders does not currently have field presence. The Southern Regional Manager reports to the National Field Director and directly supervises the **Georgia State Director** and **Florida State Director**. This position sometimes requires irregular hours, including evenings and weekends. This grant-funded position is funded through **July 2027**, with the possibility of extension. — # PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES ## Partner Outreach and Relationship Management **Strategic Planning:** Develop and implement state-specific strategic plans for Alabama, Mississippi, and Louisiana for partner outreach and engagement, supporting a broad and diverse range of partners to incorporate and sustain voter ID education, assistance, and advocacy. **Partnership Development:** Identify, establish, maintain, and deepen partnerships with regional, statewide, and local organizations. Support voter ID outreach and assistance to at-risk communities using VoteRiders’ resources, tools, and services. **Cross-Program Leverage:** Use relationships with AL, MS, LA, and regional partners to support partnership development in other states or nationally. — ## Voter and Community Engagement **Community Events:** Participate in virtual and in-person community events to engage voters and at-risk communities, offering voter ID education and assistance. **Event Collaboration:** Coordinate with the Voter Outreach & Data Manager to co-host volunteer events with key partners, maintaining a presence throughout events to provide expertise and technical support. **Media:** Coordinate with Communications and Digital teams for website updates and earned media opportunities. Follow brand and messaging guidelines and route all media inquiries through the Communications Director or designee. — ## Policy Monitoring and Engagement **Legislative Monitoring:** In coalition with partners and the VoteRiders Legal team, monitor state-level legislative developments related to voting rights and voter ID laws. — ## Reporting, Staff, and Program Management **Data and Tracking:** Lead and maintain resource development and reporting efforts for AL, MS, and LA field programs, including weekly and monthly reports, metrics collection, partner tracking, website updates, and other internal/external updates. **Staff Supervision:** Supervise and mentor the Georgia and Florida State Directors; track goals quarterly; provide feedback; review weekly reports; and ensure accountability for metrics, voter stories, event attendance, and data entry. Enforce organizational policies and ensure staff are informed of programmatic changes. **Development Support:** Collaborate with the development department on region- and state-specific grant proposals and reporting. **Goal Setting:** Develop, track, and report on goals/metrics for AL, MS, and LA relevant to field programs and regional work. **External Representation:** Represent VoteRiders externally with partners, media, and stakeholders. **Cross-Functional Collaboration:** Work with other VoteRiders teams to ensure aligned and successful outcomes. **Budget Management:** Track and monitor AL, LA, and MS expenses against the approved budget. Flag variances and request modifications as needed. — # ORGANIZATIONAL STEWARDSHIP **Relationship Building:** Build respectful, trust-based relationships with voters, volunteers, partners, and colleagues. **Collective Goals:** Work effectively with cross-functional colleagues, share information, invite input, and follow through on commitments. **Problem Solving:** Approach challenges proactively with sound judgment. Identify opportunities to strengthen workflows, relationships, or program implementation. **Professionalism:** Represent VoteRiders professionally and uphold the organization’s nonpartisan values. **Continuous Improvement:** Seek and respond to feedback, adapt to changing priorities, and contribute to team-wide improvement. **Team Participation:** Participate actively in internal activities, meetings, brainstorms, debriefs, culture-building, and professional development. **Ad Hoc Projects:** Support organizational efforts and special projects as assigned. — # QUALIFICATIONS ## Required – Must live in or be willing to relocate immediately to AL, FL, GA, MS, or LA (no relocation funds provided). – Must be willing to travel regularly within the Southern states, with reliable transportation. Candidates in FL or GA should expect **up to 40% travel**. – At least **6 years of relevant professional experience**, including community organizing in democracy, voting rights, or political spaces, with extensive coalition-building; at least **3 years remote**. – At least **3 years of managerial and project management experience** in remote environments. – Existing relationships with organizations in democracy, voting rights, civil rights, direct service, and/or community-based organizations in AL, MS, or LA. – Proven track record of recruiting, building, and maintaining collaborative relationships with external stakeholders. – Demonstrated experience managing campaigns, working groups, coalitions, and short- or long-term projects. – Ability to manage complex details, solve problems, and follow through under tight deadlines. – Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including public speaking and presentations. – Experience working with diverse, marginalized, and at-risk communities. – Strong data tracking, analytical, problem-solving, and reporting skills. – Ability to work effectively with people with differing views; maintain transparency about personal beliefs while supporting the organization’s nonpartisan mission. – Reliable computer, internet, and cellphone; strong skills in Slack, Microsoft Suite, Google Suite, and ability to learn new systems. – Willingness to work evenings and weekends as required. ## Preferred / Plus – Spanish or additional relevant language skills – Experience with VAN, Mobilize, EveryAction, or similar platforms – Experience with digital storytelling – Experience drafting data-driven program reports — # COMPENSATION Starting salary: **$70,000–$80,000/year**, plus comprehensive benefits: – Health benefits – 401K with 4% employer contribution – Generous paid time off: – 4 weeks/year accrued vacation – Paid sick time – All federal holidays – 5 personal days – Paid office closures at Thanksgiving and winter holidays – Equipment and home office stipends – Lifestyle Spending Account – Calm meditation app subscription — # EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY POLICY VoteRiders is an equal opportunity employer. All employment decisions are based on mission needs, job requirements, and individual qualifications, without regard to legally protected characteristics. VoteRiders does not tolerate unlawful discrimination or harassment. Studies show marginalized communities may hesitate to apply unless they meet every qualification. VoteRiders encourages candidates who believe they are a strong fit to apply even if their experience does not perfectly align with every requirement. References will not be contacted without permission. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Director, Head of Global Public Affairs
item.description: Director, Head of Global Public Affairs Organization: Intuit Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 07/27/2026 ## Company Overview Intuit is the global financial technology platform that powers prosperity for the people and communities we serve. With approximately 100 million customers worldwide using products such as TurboTax, Credit Karma, QuickBooks, and Mailchimp, we believe that everyone should have the opportunity to prosper. We never stop working to find new, innovative ways to make that possible. — ## Job Overview Intuit—the global financial technology platform behind TurboTax, Credit Karma, QuickBooks, and Mailchimp—is seeking a **Director Head of Global Public Affairs** to lead and direct the company’s global public affairs function. Based in Washington, DC and reporting to the Vice President of U.S. Federal Advocacy and Global Public Affairs, this executive owns Intuit’s public affairs strategy at the global, federal, state, and local levels. The Director of Global Public Affairs is accountable for translating the Global Corporate Affairs and Public Policy (GCAPP) strategy into measurable business outcomes on behalf of Intuit’s customers. This is an executive leadership role. The Director defines the vision, strategy, and roadmap for the global public affairs function; leads a team of public affairs professionals; and exercises broad discretion over how Intuit tells the story of its customers to policymakers. The role leads the team responsible for paid media, strategic alliances, grassroots advocacy, third-party influencer outreach, and Intuit’s political action committee (PAC) and policy association engagement — the campaign infrastructure that creates the conditions for Intuit’s policy priorities to win. This position serves as part of the GCAPP team and works directly with colleagues across Legal, Compliance, and Policy (LCPO), Intuit Brand and Marketing, Corporate Communications, Global Business Solutions Group (GBSG), Consumer Group (CG), and Corporate Responsibility teams. This is a hybrid role with on-site expectations of 3 days per week in our Washington, DC office. We prioritize being together to promote connection and belonging, creativity and innovation, as well as speed, agility, and productivity to accelerate getting work done. — ## Responsibilities – Lead and build a high-performance team of six direct reports, and multiple external agencies, with a mandate to strengthen Intuit’s brand and reputation among policymakers. – Develop and execute proactive, integrated public affairs communication strategies and content that articulate and support Intuit’s legislative, regulatory, and public policy objectives, ensuring alignment with business priorities and reputation goals. – Oversee Intuit’s political action committee (PAC) and policy association engagement, ensuring rigorous compliance, a clear political giving strategy, and alignment with the company’s advocacy priorities. – Direct Intuit’s grassroots and grasstops advocacy capability, mobilizing customers, employees, and allied voices in support of the company’s policy objectives. – Build close, durable relationships with senior leaders across the LCPO organization and the broader business (including Intuit Brand Marketing and Corporate Communications), aligning Intuit’s global public affairs objectives with concrete business outcomes and ensuring strategy moves in lockstep with business and reputational priorities. – Translate complex policy topics into accessible, persuasive narratives for policymakers, advocacy organizations, community groups, trade associations, think tanks, and media. – Identify opportunities, venues, and creative communications tactics to meet Intuit’s objectives. – Strengthen message discipline, ensuring alignment across Public Affairs, Government Affairs, Legal, and functional partners. – Proactively identify and remove friction across and beyond Legal, Compliance, and Policy Organization (LCPO) to increase the velocity at which Intuit delivers for its global stakeholders. — ## Qualifications – Candidates must have a minimum of 15+ combined years of experience on political campaigns, in government work, or in public affairs and/or public relations with a major corporation, an agency, and/or trade association. – Experience working on political campaigns or in capitals — in the US or internationally — is preferred. – Proven track record of converting public affairs initiatives into concrete business results — measurable shifts in policymaker perception, coalition and grassroots scale, and campaign wins that created the conditions for legislative or regulatory outcomes. – Experience managing external agencies and significant campaign budgets, with accountability for results. – Familiarity with PAC operations and the compliance environment governing corporate political activity, or demonstrated ability to lead a regulated political program with the highest standards of integrity. – Strong writer, with the ability to distill key messages and present them in a compelling and visually interesting way. Proficiency with design, digital content production, and digital ad buying preferred. – Operates and makes an impact across organizational boundaries and at the industry and policy level. – Strong critical thinking and analytical skills, effectively analyzing and assessing opportunities and threats, prioritizing focus, and interpreting developments. – Capacity and drive to understand fully the business and operational elements of Intuit, including parsing what is mission critical from the trivial. – Ability to connect policy outcomes to business value by tying policymaker engagement and outcomes to the company’s growth priorities. – Experience operating across multiple geographies and policy contexts. – Executive acumen, with experience advising and preparing senior executives for high-stakes policy engagements. Reputation for having the highest ethical standards and integrity. – Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree (JD, MBA, or master’s in a relevant field) strongly preferred. – Willingness and ability to travel internationally as business needs require. — ## Compensation Intuit provides a competitive compensation package with a strong pay-for-performance rewards approach. This position may be eligible for a cash bonus, equity rewards, and benefits, in accordance with our applicable plans and programs. Pay offered is based on factors such as job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and work location. To drive ongoing fair pay for employees, Intuit conducts regular comparisons across categories of ethnicity and gender. **Expected base pay range:** Washington: **$247,000 – $334,500** — ## How to Apply Apply here: [ https://jobs.intuit.com/job/washington-d-c/director-head-of-global-public-affairs/27595/97798689632 ] Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today.
