item.title: NRRI Strategic Engagement Manager
item.description: NRRI Strategic Engagement Manager Organization: University of Minnesota Location: Duluth, MN Date Posted: 07/27/2026 ## About the Job The Strategic Engagement Manager serves as an operational leader within NRRI’s Office of Strategic Partnerships & External Affairs, helping translate institutional priorities into coordinated engagement strategies, relationships, and action. Reporting to the Director of Strategic Partnerships & External Affairs, this role serves as a force multiplier across NRRI’s growing portfolio of externally facing initiatives by stewarding relationships, coordinating strategic platforms, and maintaining continuity across complex multi‑partner efforts. The ideal candidate is highly organized, relationship‑oriented, politically and publicly aware, and comfortable operating in fast‑moving environments that span industry, Tribal Nations, government, philanthropy, academia, and communities. — ## Job Duties ### Strategic Platforms, Convenings & Institutional Coordination (40%) – Coordinate and help operationalize major institutional initiatives, including the Midwest Industrial Transformation Initiative (MITI) and other strategic platforms that advance NRRI priorities. – Lead planning and execution for advisory panel meetings, forums, workshops, stakeholder working groups, and major external convenings. – Maintain continuity across initiatives by tracking priorities, timelines, decisions, action items, and follow‑up responsibilities. – Translate complex discussions into concise summaries, briefing materials, strategic memos, and decision‑support documents. – Identify coordination gaps, stakeholder needs, and emerging risks across initiatives and partnerships. – Support executive‑level relationship management working with NRRI Executive Director and ensure strong follow‑through across external commitments. – Coordinate and communicate across researchers, leadership, communications, and external partners to keep strategic initiatives moving forward. ### Relationship Management & Stakeholder Engagement (30%) – Serve as steward of NRRI’s institutional CRM and maintain relationship intelligence across industry, Tribal, philanthropic, government, academic, and community partners. – Develop engagement plans and track institutional touchpoints, relationship history, next steps, and opportunities. – Prepare stakeholder profiles, briefing materials, presentations, and partner background documents. – Lead logistics, follow‑up, and relationship management activities tied to strategic partnerships. – Support relationship development across partner organizations, collaborators, and institutional stakeholders. – Operate thoughtfully within culturally, politically, and publicly sensitive engagement environments. – Ensure alignment with University of Minnesota partners, government relations teams, and other institutional offices as appropriate. ### Communications Integration, Institutional Positioning & Intelligence (30%) – Engage closely with communications staff to ensure alignment between engagement activities, partnerships, and institutional priorities. – Support messaging development, presentations, and strategic communications tied to high‑priority initiatives. – Develop written content including briefing documents, outreach materials, talking points, and executive presentations. – Contribute to horizon scanning for emerging opportunities, funding trends, policy developments, and strategic risks relevant to NRRI priorities. – Help strengthen proactive planning and institutional positioning across major initiatives. – Support development of partner communications and executive materials. – Coordinate with University communications, foundation, and external partners as directed by Executive Director and Director of Strategic Partnerships and External Affairs. – Identify opportunities to elevate NRRI’s visibility and strengthen relationships through strategic communications. – Lead planning and execution of signature events and institutional convenings. **Please note:** This position is not eligible for H‑1B or Green Card sponsorship. This position does not offer a STEM OPT training program. — ## Qualifications ### Required Qualifications – Bachelor’s degree plus at least 4 years of relevant experience – Excellent written and verbal communication skills – Ability to work in person from NRRI’s offices in Duluth, Minnesota, with occasional travel to Twin Cities, Iron Range, and other domestic travel as needed ### Preferred Qualifications – Experience in public affairs, stakeholder engagement, government relations, strategic communications, policy, or related fields – Exceptional writing, synthesis, organizational, project management, and coordination skills – Ability to manage complex stakeholder relationships and multiple concurrent projects – Strong judgment, professionalism, discretion, and attention to detail – Ability to navigate ambiguity and shifting priorities within fast‑moving environments – Experience working across government, nonprofit, academic, Tribal, industry, philanthropic, or community contexts preferred – Experience supporting executive‑level leadership or complex multi‑partner initiatives preferred – Ability to operate collaboratively within politically and publicly sensitive environments and lead by influence ### Physical/Environmental Demands Office environment; no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands. — ## About the Department The Natural Resources Research Institute was established by the Minnesota legislature in 1983 as an applied science and engineering research organization to inform state citizens and decision‑makers while leveraging the power of the University of Minnesota. NRRI is guided by the forward‑looking charter provided by the Legislature to foster the economic development of Minnesota’s natural resources in an environmentally sound manner to promote private sector employment. NRRI’s mission is to deliver integrated research solutions that value our resources, environment, and economy for a sustainable and resilient future. We are a mission‑driven, project‑focused team working to create opportunities for natural resource stewardship. — ## Pay and Benefits **Pay Range:** $77,651 – $98,358, depending on education, qualifications, and experience **Time Appointment:** 100% Appointment **Position Type:** Faculty and P&A Staff Please visit the Office of Human Resources website for more information regarding benefit eligibility. ### Benefits Package Includes – Competitive wages, paid holidays, and generous time off – Continuous learning opportunities through professional training and degree‑seeking programs supported by the Regents Tuition Benefit Program – Low‑cost medical, dental, and pharmacy plans – Healthcare and dependent care flexible spending accounts – University HSA contributions – Disability and employer‑paid life insurance – Employee wellbeing program – Excellent retirement plans with employer contribution – Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) opportunity – Financial counseling services – Employee Assistance Program with eight sessions of counseling at no cost While salary ranges provide a framework, initial pay may not reach the maximum of the range. Compensation reflects each candidate’s credentials and experience while maintaining equity within the organization. — ## How to Apply Applications must be submitted online. To be considered for this position, click the Apply button and follow the instructions. You will be able to complete an online application and attach a cover letter and resume. Additional documents may be attached after application by accessing your “My Job Applications” page and uploading documents in the “My Cover Letters and Attachments” section. A cover letter and resume are required to be considered for this position. To request an accommodation during the application process, email ** [email protected] ** or call **(612) 624‑8647**. — ## Diversity The University recognizes and values the importance of diversity and inclusion in enriching the employment experience of its employees and in supporting the academic mission. The University is committed to attracting and retaining employees with varying identities and backgrounds. The University of Minnesota provides equal access to and opportunity in its programs, facilities, and employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, national origin, gender, age, marital status, disability, public assistance status, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. Learn more: [http://diversity.umn.edu] — ## Employment Requirements Any offer of employment is contingent upon the successful completion of a background check. Criminal convictions do not automatically disqualify finalists from employment. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Senior Director, Global Brand Management Systems & Operations
item.description: Senior Director, Global Brand Management Systems & Operations Organization: Visa Location: San Francisco, CA Date Posted: 07/28/2026 ## About Us Visa is a world leader in payments technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions, and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories, dedicated to uplifting everyone, everywhere by being the best way to pay and be paid. At Visa, you’ll have the opportunity to create impact at scale — tackling meaningful challenges, growing your skills, and seeing your contributions impact lives around the world. Join Visa and do work that matters – to you, to your community, and to the world. Progress starts with you. ## Job Description We are seeking a senior transformation leader to modernize the operating model, workflows, platforms, and capabilities that enable our Global Brand organization to deliver work at global scale. As the Senior Director, Global Brand Management Systems & Operations, your mission is to strip out operational friction, drive global platform adoption, and lead the practical integration of AI, automation, and agent-enabled workflows to scale our brand’s global impact. You will ensure our Brand teams globally have the workflows, tools, and capabilities required to operate with greater speed, clarity, consistency, and confidence while protecting our brand equity. Reporting to the Vice President, Global Brand Management, this leader is responsible for improving how the Global Brand organization executes its work—from the platforms that support brand content and governance, to the workflows that move ideas from brief to market, to the practical use of AI within approved brand processes. This leader will own the Global Brand transformation roadmap for workflows, brand platforms, content systems, and approved AI use cases. They will define business requirements, prioritize use cases and pilots, establish adoption standards, recommend governance improvements, and provide executive visibility into progress, barriers, and value delivered. This leader will also help Global Brand move from individual tool adoption to connected, governed operating systems that improve how brand work is created, reviewed, scaled, and measured. The Senior Director will lead a focused expert team and partner across Marketing, Product, Technology, Legal, Privacy, Creative, agencies, Sourcing, and regional teams to improve how work is planned, created, reviewed, approved, stored, reused, adapted, and scaled. The ideal candidate has led transformation inside a large, complex marketing, brand, creative, content, or marketing operations environment. They know how enterprise marketing work actually gets done and have a record of improving workflows, platforms, governance, adoption, and organizational capability at scale. The role is expected to improve speed to market, increase reuse of approved assets, reduce duplicative effort, strengthen content governance, and increase the value the organization receives from its brand platforms and approved AI capabilities. — ## Architect the Global Brand Operations Redesign the end-to-end workflows that bring our brand to life. Modernize priority workflows across planning, briefing, creative development, approval, localization, asset delivery, reuse, and measurement to build a more connected, scalable, and measurable brand content supply chain. Eliminate operational drag between internal brand teams, in-house studios, and external creative agencies. — ## Lead Brand AI Enablement & Innovation Serve as the Global Brand business lead for identifying, prioritizing, testing, and scaling approved AI use cases within brand workflows. Apply AI agents, automation, context-aware workflows, and evaluation loops where they can reduce manual effort, improve decision quality, and strengthen consistency without removing human judgment or enterprise controls. Identify and scale practical AI use cases that automate asset adaptation, accelerate creative workflows, improve reuse, and create measurable operational leverage. Partner with Legal, Privacy, Security, Risk, and enterprise AI governance teams to translate approved AI standards into practical guidance, playbooks, and workflows for Global Brand teams. — ## Drive Brand Platform Strategy, Adoption, and Value Serve as the Global Brand business owner for requirements, adoption, governance, and value realization across key brand platforms, including DAM, creative workflow, approval systems, and brand portals. Partner with IT and Marketing Technology teams to translate high-level brand and creative strategy into actionable technology roadmaps. — ## Drive Global Capability Building & Change Leadership Lead the change management, training, adoption, and capability-building required to help brand, creative, and marketing teams adopt new workflows, platforms, and approved AI-enabled ways of working. Shift organizational behavior by proving that new workflows, systems, and AI-enabled capabilities make the work better and faster, not simply cheaper. Lead transformation portfolio reporting, executive updates, cross-functional governance, and adoption scorecards that make progress, barriers, and business impact visible. Success will be measured by reduced workflow cycle time, increased platform adoption, improved asset reuse, reduced duplicate work, stronger content governance, practical adoption of AI-enabled and agent-enabled workflows, and improved stakeholder satisfaction. The right leader will be an enterprise operator, systems thinker, and change leader with strong credibility across marketing, creative, technology, legal, agencies, and senior executives. Visa requires at least 3 days in office; expectations of these days will be confirmed by your Hiring Manager. — ## Qualifications ### Basic Qualifications 12 or more years of work experience with a Bachelor’s Degree, or at least 10 years of work experience with an Advanced Degree (e.g., Masters/MBA/JD/MD), or a minimum of 5 years of work experience with a PhD. ### Preferred Qualifications 15 or more years of experience with a Bachelor’s Degree, or 12 years of experience with an Advanced Degree (e.g., Masters, MBA, JD, or MD), or a PhD with 9+ years of experience. 12+ years of experience in marketing operations, brand operations, creative operations, content operations, marketing technology, business transformation, or related enterprise operating roles. Experience leading transformation in a large, matrixed, global organization. Proven record improving workflows, operating models, platform adoption, or organizational capability across marketing, brand, creative, or content teams. Experience working with DAM, workflow management, content systems, marketing planning tools, creative production platforms, or related enterprise platforms. Practical experience applying AI, automation, AI agents, or context-aware workflows to improve business operations, creative workflows, or marketing processes. Strong understanding of change management, adoption strategy, and capability building. Experience partnering with Product, Technology, Legal, Privacy, Procurement, Finance, agencies, and senior marketing leaders. Ability to translate ambiguous business problems into clear roadmaps, governance models, operating routines, and measurable outcomes. Strong executive communication, stakeholder management, and transformation portfolio leadership skills. Experience in a Fortune 500 or similarly complex global organization. Experience modernizing content supply chains or large-scale creative production workflows. Experience leading DAM transformation, taxonomy redesign, metadata strategy, rights governance, or asset lifecycle improvement. Experience applying AI agents, loop-based workflows, context intelligence, or governed automation within approved enterprise standards. Experience influencing global and regional teams without direct authority. Experience managing vendor, agency, platform, or technology partner relationships. Experience leading a small team of senior specialists or cross-functional transformation leads. — ## U.S. Applicants Only The estimated salary range for this position is $207,600.00 to $332,300.00 USD per year, which may include potential sales incentive payments (if applicable). Salary may vary depending on job-related factors which may include knowledge, skills, experience, and location. In addition, this position may be eligible for bonus and equity. Visa has a comprehensive benefits package for which this position may be eligible that includes Medical, Dental, Vision, 401(k), FSA/HSA, Life Insurance, Paid Time Off, and Wellness Program. — ## Work Hours Varies upon the needs of the department. ## Travel Requirements This position requires travel 5–10% of the time. ## Mental/Physical Requirements This position will be performed in an office setting. The position will require the incumbent to sit and stand at a desk, communicate in person and by telephone, and frequently operate standard office equipment such as telephones and computers. — ## Visa is an EEO Employer Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, or protected veteran status. Visa will also consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the EEOC guidelines and applicable local law, including the requirements of Article 49 of the San Francisco Police Code. item.title: Head of Government Relations
item.description: Head of Government Relations Organization: Cape Location: Arlington, VA Date Posted: 07/28/2026 ## About Cape Cape is America’s privacy-first mobile carrier. Our mission is to be a force for good in global wireless. Cape was founded in 2022 by people who believe privacy is a fundamental right, not a luxury to be traded away. Our journey began when our founder recognized a critical vulnerability in our modern world: everyone relies on the same stagnant cellular infrastructure and legacy systems that track our every movement, monitor and profile our connections, and lose and sell our personal data. Instead of accepting the status quo, we decided to fix it. National security professionals, journalists, parents, and everyone in between can stay connected and have privacy. We didn’t just build a layer on top of old tech; we built America’s most private and secure mobile carrier from the ground up. By building our own network from scratch, we are able to design and build a suite of privacy and security features that no other carrier on the planet can offer. Today, Cape provides our secure network to consumers, businesses, and government agencies alike. We closed our Series C in March 2026, and we are scaling rapidly, with the goal of giving people back control of their most personal information. ## The Team At Cape, we are the architects of a privacy-centric movement that is just getting started. We are relentless builders, constantly innovating at the edge of what’s possible in telecommunications. We operate on a foundation of high trust and high expectations. Our structure is flat, and collaboration matters more than hierarchy. As a member of our team, you will collaborate with world-class engineers, architects, and visionaries, and work across organizational lines to solve “impossible” problems and deliver mission-critical results for our users every single day. ## The Mission We are seeking a high-ownership Head of Government Relations to serve as a critical driver of Cape’s growth. In this role, you will take full accountability for government engagement and policy-based results through your management of external stakeholders. In addition, you will develop and maintain organized tracking systems to ensure cross-functional alignment on key lines of effort. Your mission is to bridge the gap between the company’s most pressing intragovernmental challenges and the government institutions that can solve them. You will optimize external engagement through clearly communicated long-term strategies, while remaining responsive to the fluid nature of technology and defense policy. ## Outcomes: How You’ll Make an Impact – Developing a long-term milestone-based government strategy – Mapping key government stakeholders to company needs – Forecasting political, policy, budgetary, and regulatory changes and volatility – Shaping new policies beneficial to the company and its customers – Forming and maturing partnerships with third parties in the federal ecosystem – Optimizing relationships with external advisors, experts, and lobbyists – Engaging resource sponsors to achieve established strategic endstates – Establishing, attending, and managing events that cross between industry and government affairs ## Requirements **Operational Pedigree:** Prior experience in fast-paced environments. We value a background of “ownership” where you’ve been responsible for end-to-end outcomes. **External Relationship Development:** Ability to network among a diverse set of external stakeholders, build connections with them, and maintain strong ties. **Executive Communication:** Clear and concise professional correspondence and awareness of protocol in political and bureaucratic offices. **Knowledge of the Legislative Process:** First-hand knowledge of the federal legislative process through experience in lobbying, Congressional fellowship, PSM/MLA, or similar. **Strategic Planning:** Ability to establish a multi-year government engagement plan that aligns company goals with government cadences. **Professional Background:** Relevant background in Political Science, Public Administration, Public Policy, or similar professions. ## Bonus Points (The Ideal Candidate) – **Experience as a Professional Staff Member:** First-hand experience as a PSM inside the federal legislative process. – **Telco Literacy:** Familiarity with telecommunications, including cellular network architecture. – **Graduate Expertise:** Graduate-level education in Political Science, Public Administration, Public Policy, or similar professions. ## Compensation We offer competitive compensation that is geo-adjusted based on your location, along with meaningful equity so you share in the value you help create. Salary range for this role in Arlington, VA is $250,000–$350,000 depending on experience and interview performance. Our benefits include: – 401(k) match – 100% coverage of medical, dental, and vision premiums for you and your dependents – 12 weeks paid parental leave (for all parents, no waiting period) – Stipends for: – Family-forming needs – Gender-affirming care – Unlimited PTO ## Our Culture & Values We hire excellent people, give them outsized responsibility, and trust them to execute. Every person at Cape has a proven track record of tackling hard problems and winning. We believe that personal privacy and national security are not at odds, and that they can be reconciled through strong technology. We believe companies exist to build awesome things and take care of the people who build them, so we offer top-tier healthcare, 401(k) matching, and a generous vacation policy that our team actually uses to recharge. We believe that a stronger company and a better product are built by people from all walks of life. We hire without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital status, disability, or Veteran status. If you are great at what you do, you belong here. ## How to Apply Click the link below to apply. We reserve the right to make use of any unsolicited resumes received from outside recruiting agencies and/or individual recruiters without being responsible for payment of any fees asserted from the use of unsolicited resumes. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, or national origin, and without regard to disability or status as a protected veteran, or any other status protected by law. item.title: Public Policy and Government Affairs Manager, State/Local
item.description: Public Policy and Government Affairs Manager, State/Local Organization: Samsara Location: Remote Date Posted: 07/28/2026 ## Who we are Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency, and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale. Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term. ## About the role Successful navigation of the policy landscape is critical to deploying and scaling a business. Samsara is looking to grow its Public Policy and Government Relations team by adding an experienced, agile, and capable Manager to forge new relationships, represent the company, and advance our interests in U.S. State and Local markets. Our team works closely with lawmakers, regulatory bodies, trade associations, industry experts, and others to proactively engage in initiatives that advance Samsara’s business interests. Internally, our efforts support innovative work across the business, including the engineering, product, strategy, legal, and partnerships teams. The ideal candidate will enjoy serving as a key contributor on a diverse range of substantive advocacy initiatives, aid in identifying opportunities for sales enablement and engagement, developing creative strategies and content, and representing Samsara externally to key stakeholders in state and local government and allied third parties. Samsara values collaborative individuals who excel in a dynamic, fast-paced environment, can work across multiple teams and on multiple projects, can take in many inputs and communicate clearly and effectively, and provide colleagues with practical insight and guidance. This role is open to candidates residing in the US except the San Francisco Bay Metro Area, NYC Metro Area, and Washington, D.C. Metro Area. ## You should apply if – You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely. – You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development and opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper‑growth environment. – You’re energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers. – You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together, and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high‑caliber team that will encourage you to do your best. ## In this role, you will – Help develop and execute policy strategies that advance Samsara’s business goals in key U.S. state and local markets on the East Coast, Northeast, Midwest, and Southeast. – Identify and track proposed bills, regulations, and policy positions at the state and municipal levels that are relevant to Samsara, assessing their potential impact, developing strategies for engagement, and keeping the business informed. – Work closely with the sales teams to help create new tailwinds and affect the adoption and usage of Samsara’s technologies through policy initiatives. – Build and maintain strong relationships with relevant governors, mayors, state legislators, regulatory officials, and trade associations. – Assist with filings, comments, testimony, and other input for legislative committees and regulatory bodies. – Manage outside consultants to expand our reach in key state markets. – Collaborate with other Samsarians in the creation of content (collateral, blog posts, etc.) that articulate Samsara’s vision and values in a manner that is compelling to policymakers. – Champion, role model, and embody Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team). ## Minimum requirements for the role – Bachelor’s degree required. – 5+ years of relevant public policy, political, and/or government experience and an in‑depth understanding of the policymaking process and government relations in the United States. – Demonstrated knowledge and experience in state and local government affairs and advocacy (e.g., legislative wins, relationships with officials, involvement with third parties, etc.). – Skilled at persuasively and diplomatically advocating complex policy positions before a wide variety of audiences. – Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, and the ability to concisely summarize policy issues and advocacy points. – Experience managing multiple high‑priority projects simultaneously in a fast‑moving, dynamic environment. – Ability to thrive in new situations, learn quickly, jump in, and responsibly manage one’s own time and deliverables in a remote work environment. – Teammate with a strong willingness to pitch in as necessary. ## An ideal candidate also has – Passion for and knowledge of emerging technology and related public policy issues. – Experience in state or local government, in advocacy, or in‑house on issues facing highly regulated industries. – Knowledge and experience with privacy, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, transportation, or other public policy issues related to data‑driven industries. – In‑house experience at another technology company. – The ability to effectively translate government‑to‑business and business‑to‑government issues. – The ability to issue spot, identifying potential opportunities for sales enablement and challenges before they materialize. ## Annual Base Salary $90,737.50—$137,250 USD ## Total Rewards At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high‑impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above‑market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance‑based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high‑growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above‑market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time. Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long‑term success: a flexible, employee‑led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here. ## Flexible Working At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in‑person, and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on‑site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable. ## Belonging at Samsara At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact. ## Accommodations Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email [email protected] or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process. ## Our Commitment to Authenticity We use Tofu, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information. ## Fraudulent Employment Offers Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process. Official communication about your application will only come from emails ending in @samsara.com, @us-greenhouse-mail.io, or @mail3.guide.co. For more information regarding fraudulent employment offers, please visit our blog post here. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Government Relations Manager – Europe
item.description: Government Relations Manager – Europe Organization: Vertiv Location: Brussels, BE Date Posted: 07/28/2026 ## Government Relations Manager The **Government Relations Manager – Europe** will play an important role in advocating for the policy interests across governments in Europe and within industry groups. The role requires a strategic thinker with an understanding of regulatory environments and the ability to develop and implement advocacy strategies that protect and promote the company’s business interests and growth. The Government Relations Manager will show expertise in interactions with government officials, regulatory agencies, and industry groups. At Vertiv, we’re on a mission to empower the people that will power the future. From a simple swipe to life‑changing medicines, from push notifications to generative AI — we design, manufacture, and service the products and solutions that keep the world connected. With **$6.9 billion in sales**, a strong customer base, and global reach spanning nearly **70 countries**, we are uniquely positioned to deliver greater value to our customers and create new opportunities for our people. **LOCATION:** Brussels, Belgium — ## Responsibilities ### Advocacy and Representation – Support relationships with key stakeholders to influence policy and regulatory decisions. – Support advocacy for the company on legislative and regulatory issues. ### Regulatory Analysis and Strategy – Monitor and analyze regulatory changes in key geographies where the company operates. – Assess the impact of regulatory developments on the company’s operations and business strategy. – Help implement advocacy strategies to address trade challenges and opportunities. ### Collaboration and Communication – Communicate regulatory and legislative developments to internal stakeholders. – Prepare briefing materials, reports, and presentations on government relations activities. – Support the government relations team on other specified projects as needed. ### Industry Engagement – Participate in industry associations and coalitions to advance the company’s interests. — ## Qualifications ### Minimum Job Qualifications – Minimum 7 years of related work experience. – Good understanding of regulatory processes and government structures. – Proactive, decisive, and able to work independently on a broad variety of subjects. – Strong detail orientation and demonstrated ability to manage multiple tasks. – Strong interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills, including the ability to remain objective and use discretion in all situations. – Highly collaborative and team‑oriented, able to build relationships at all levels of the organization. – Resourceful, with a problem‑solving aptitude and ability to manage and resolve complex and sensitive situations while managing confidential information appropriately and professionally. ### Preferred Qualifications – Preferred 10+ years of related work experience. — ## Education and Certifications – Bachelor’s Degree required (preferably in Political Science, Public Policy, or Law) — ## Physical Requirements – No special physical requirements. — ## Travel Time Required – Occasional travel. — If YOU are the person we are looking for, feel free to apply and let’s start drafting your future career in a healthy and growing environment! The successful candidate will embrace Vertiv’s Core Principles & Behaviors to help execute our Strategic Priorities. — ## Our Core Principles Safety Integrity Respect Teamwork Diversity & Inclusion ## Our Strategic Priorities Customer Focus Operational Excellence High‑Performance Culture Innovation Financial Strength ## Our Behaviors Own It Act With Urgency Foster a Customer‑First Mindset Think Big and Execute Lead by Example Drive Continuous Improvement Learn and Seek Out Development **#LI‑CB1** — ## About the Team ### Work Authorization No calls or agencies please. Vertiv will only employ those who are legally authorized to work in the United States. This is not a position for which sponsorship will be provided. Individuals with temporary visas such as E, F‑1, H‑1, H‑2, L, B, J, or TN, or who need sponsorship for work authorization now or in the future, are not eligible for hire. — ## Equal Opportunity Employer We promote equal opportunities for all with respect to hiring, terms of employment, mobility, training, compensation, and occupational health, without discrimination as to age, race, color, religion, creed, sex, pregnancy status (including childbirth, breastfeeding, or related medical conditions), marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression (including transgender status or sexual stereotypes), genetic information, citizenship status, national origin, protected veteran status, political affiliation, or disability. item.title: International Senior Program Analyst
item.description: International Senior Program Analyst Organization: CACI Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 07/28/2026 ## The Opportunity CACI is currently seeking an **International Senior Program Analyst** to support the Program Executive Office (PEO) for Aircraft Carriers in Washington, DC. The International Senior Program Analyst will provide direct support to the **US–IN Joint Working Group on Aircraft Carrier Technology Cooperation**, with the goal of enhancing the US–IN partnership in aircraft carrier technologies and methodologies up to the preliminary design phase. Key responsibilities include managing responses to information requests, ensuring compliance with existing exchange agreements and policies, drafting and maintaining meeting minutes from joint discussions, and leading the planning and logistics for all in‑person engagements, both within the Continental United States (CONUS) and outside CONUS (OCONUS). — ## Responsibilities As directed by the PEO Aircraft Carriers, assistance will be provided to facilitate development efforts for Foreign Military Sales (FMS) cases, responses to letters of request for pricing and availability, as well as letters of request for letter of offer and acceptance. This includes consolidation of inputs, foreign disclosure approvals, and maintaining records for tracking on a government‑approved repository. – Assist with the development of overall FMS Case & Data Exchange Agreement (DEA) documentation. – Coordinate action item responses from the PEO Carriers and its stakeholders. – Interface with 05V personnel to monitor and resolve open action items. – Provide support (process foreign visit requests, escort for demonstrations, etc.) to requested foreign visits to the US in support of specific potential FMS programs or in anticipation of LOR development. – Track all released deliverables in an approved network location. – Coordinate visits both CONUS and OCONUS, including agendas, transportation, lodging, and required documentation for travel. – Support efforts to help develop requirements, country team assessments, and COCOM endorsements while in country. – Support defense article and training need discussions with international partners, escort contractors to meetings with partners, etc. – Prepare all read‑ahead materials for briefs and presentations. – Develop meeting agendas and after‑meeting minutes. – Develop and monitor overarching budget profile for NAVSEA support to the Future French Carrier Working Group. – Develop point papers, coordinate PEO responses, and consolidate inputs for briefs and reports related to the Future French Carrier Program (FFC). – In response to foreign partner or COCOM requests, work with industry to support specific FMS opportunities or to draft and monitor Pricing & Availability (P&A) through execution of the Letter of Offer and Acceptance. – Support development of policy and FMS guidelines. – Track all deliverables from industry and program offices related to the FFC. — ## Qualifications – Bachelor of Arts degree in international studies, political science, or a related field required; Master’s degree preferred. – Minimum of seven to ten years of relevant Foreign Military Sales (FMS) experience; more than ten years desirable. – Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office (SharePoint) products. – Excellent organizational abilities. – Business process‑oriented mindset. – Direct experience in Foreign Military Sales. – Experience with Naval Correspondence. – NAVSEA and/or PEO Carriers experience. – Planning and coordination experience. – Record management experience. – Program management experience. – Active Secret Clearance. — ## What You Can Expect ### A culture of integrity At CACI, character and innovation are at the center of everything we do. As a valued team member, you’ll be part of a high‑performing group dedicated to our customer’s missions and driven by a higher purpose — ensuring the safety of our nation. ### An environment of trust CACI values the unique contributions that every employee brings to our company and our customers. You’ll have the autonomy to take the time you need through a flexible time‑off benefit and access to robust learning resources to help make your ambitions a reality. ### A focus on continuous growth Together, we will advance our nation’s most critical missions, build on our long track record of business success, and find opportunities to break new ground — in your career and in our legacy. — ## Pay Range There are a host of factors that can influence final salary including, but not limited to, geographic location, Federal Government contract labor categories and contract wage rates, relevant prior work experience, specific skills and competencies, education, and certifications. CACI offers competitive compensation, benefits, and learning and development opportunities. Our broad and competitive mix of benefits options is designed to support and protect employees and their families, including healthcare, wellness, financial, retirement, family support, continuing education, and time‑off benefits. **Proposed salary range:** **$78,700 – $165,200** CACI is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, age, national origin, disability, status as a protected veteran, or any other protected characteristic. item.title: Government Relations Leader
item.description: Government Relations Leader Organization: Owens Corning Location: Toledo, OH | Washington, D.C. Date Posted: 07/28/2026 ## Position Purpose The Government Affairs Lead is an enterprise‑level, strategic role responsible for maximizing Owens Corning’s influence as a leading building products manufacturer across the policy and trade association landscape. The role shapes and advances policy advocacy and trade association strategies that support long‑term growth, protect market access, and reinforce Owens Corning’s competitive advantages. This includes influencing legislative, regulatory, incentive‑based, insurance‑driven, and standards‑based policy outcomes that directly affect the building products industry. The position spans multiple businesses and trade associations and is a key enabler of Owens Corning’s standardized operating model for external engagement, ensuring advocacy efforts are enterprise‑aligned, intentional, scalable, and focused on the issues that matter most to the business. ## What Success Looks Like Owens Corning is positioned for maximum influence across trade associations, policy forums, and standards‑based processes that are most critical to business performance. External engagement is enterprise‑aligned, intentional, and repeatable, rather than dependent on individual roles or relationships. Business leaders have clear ownership of priorities and decisions, supported by strong enterprise‑level governance, advocacy, and coordination. Policy objectives—whether legislative, regulatory, incentive‑based, insurance‑related, or standards‑based—are integrated and mutually reinforcing, rather than operating in silos. Engagement intensity and focus are aligned to business priority, risk, and opportunity, not equally distributed across all issues or businesses. ## Key Responsibilities ### Enterprise Trade Association Strategy & Influence Develop and advance enterprise‑level strategies for engaging trade associations as platforms for influence. Advise on governance structures, committee participation, leadership roles, and escalation pathways to ensure Owens Corning is positioned to shape outcomes. Align trade association engagement with enterprise priorities, business strategies, and long‑range growth objectives. Partner with business leaders to determine where trade associations provide the greatest leverage against priority risks and opportunities. ### Policy & Advocacy Strategy Monitor, analyze, and assess legislative, regulatory, and policy developments affecting Owens Corning’s businesses, customers, and end‑markets. Partner with business leaders, Legal, Sustainability, and other functions to develop integrated advocacy strategies addressing key policy objectives, which may include: – manufacturing competitiveness and housing affordability – sustainability initiatives (e.g., recycled content, circularity, EPR) – incentives and tax credit structures – insurance‑driven building requirements – building codes and product standards adoption Coordinate engagement through trade associations, coalitions, and external advisors to advance aligned policy outcomes. ### Cross‑Business Enterprise Alignment Provide enterprise‑level policy insight, issue framing, and context to inform business‑led prioritization and decision‑making. Enable visibility, consistency, and alignment across businesses on policy and trade association activities. Support coordinated enterprise positions while respecting business ownership of priorities. ### Governance, Risk, and Operating Model Enablement Ensure adherence to lobbying, disclosure, and trade association governance requirements. Institutionalize scalable processes, playbooks, and engagement frameworks that support consistent execution across the enterprise. Strengthen continuity by reducing reliance on individual facilitation and enabling repeatable engagement approaches. Support effective knowledge transfer and role transitions related to policy and trade association engagement. ## Scope of the Role Enterprise‑level, multi‑BU in scope Covers multiple trade associations and policy advocacy platforms Strategic in nature, with emphasis on direction, leverage, and influence, rather than day‑to‑day facilitation or committee management ## Qualifications & Experience ### Required Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree in public policy, law, business, engineering, or related field preferred. 8–12+ years of relevant experience in government affairs, public policy, regulatory engagement, and/or trade association leadership. Experience operating within complex, matrixed organizations, with the ability to navigate ambiguity and drive alignment across stakeholders. Ability to influence without authority, including advising business leaders and cross‑functional partners. Strong strategic thinking, analytical capability, and clear, executive‑ready communication skills. ### Preferred Experience within building products, manufacturing, construction materials, or related industrial sectors. Familiarity with how policy, trade associations, and standards‑based advocacy intersect to shape market and regulatory outcomes. Experience supporting advocacy across multiple business segments or geographies. ## Why This Role This role exists to ensure Owens Corning engages externally with discipline, scale, and strategic intent—maximizing influence where it matters most and enabling the business‑led operating model required to succeed in a complex and dynamic policy environment. #LI-SN1 #LI-onsite ## About Owens Corning Owens Corning is a branded building products leader with three complementary market‑leading businesses providing roofing, insulation, and doors primarily for residential markets in North America and Europe. The company operates with an integrated go‑to‑market strategy and a unique set of OC Advantages™ – including its iconic brand, unparalleled commercial strength, leading technology, and winning cost position – to help customers win and grow in the market. Owens Corning is committed to helping build better and achieve more through winning partnerships, leading performance, and engaging people. Founded in 1938 and headquartered in Toledo, Ohio, Owens Corning is listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE: OC). For more information, visit [www.owenscorning.com]. Owens Corning is an equal opportunity employer. Except in limited circumstances such as formal apprenticeship programs, Owens Corning does not employ anyone under the age of 18. item.title: Government Affairs Director
item.description: Government Affairs Director Organization: Microsoft Location: Brussels, BE Date Posted: 07/28/2026 ## Overview European Government Affairs – Political Affairs Director ### Overview Microsoft’s European Government Affairs (EGA) team serves as the company’s primary interface with the European institutions, national governments, and key stakeholders across the region. Operating at the intersection of technology, policy, geopolitics, and business, EGA advances Microsoft’s public policy objectives by fostering trusted relationships and promoting policies that strengthen Europe’s competitiveness, innovation, resilience, and digital transformation. The team engages on a broad range of issues including artificial intelligence, cloud computing, cybersecurity, competition, trade, digital infrastructure, and technology sovereignty. As Europe navigates an increasingly complex political and regulatory environment, effective engagement with the European Commission, European Parliament, and Council of the European Union is critical to Microsoft’s success. Policymaking is increasingly shaped through cross‑institutional dynamics, requiring sophisticated stakeholder engagement, political intelligence, and the ability to build trusted relationships across party lines, institutions, and Member States. The EGA team in Brussels is seeking a Political Affairs Director to strengthen Microsoft’s engagement with the European institutions, especially the European Commission and Council of the European Union, by providing strategic political counsel, facilitating senior‑level access, and advancing relationships with key decision‑makers and influencers. — ## Responsibilities ### Strategic Political Engagement – Act as a key member of the Strategic Relations team to identify and address political developments, institutional dynamics, and stakeholder engagement strategies across the European institutions, especially Commission and Council. – Provide political intelligence and strategic recommendations regarding key legislative, regulatory, and geopolitical developments. – Support the design and execution of engagement plans targeting priority policymakers and influencers. ### Institutional Strategy and Political Counsel – Advise on key stakeholders, coalition‑building strategies, and approaches to influence across the legislative process. – Help anticipate emerging political trends, institutional priorities, and stakeholder concerns that could impact Microsoft’s business and policy objectives. – Support the implementation of strategies focused on digital resilience, to alleviate concerns about tech sovereignty and strengthen Microsoft’s role as a partner. ### Executive Engagement – Advise on messaging to prepare and support senior Microsoft executives for meetings with European policymakers and political leaders. – Contribute to the development of strategic messaging, briefing materials, stakeholder profiles, and engagement plans. – Provide insights on protocol, institutional expectations, and political considerations for high‑level engagements. – Support executive participation in major political, policy, and geopolitical events across Europe. ### Internal Collaboration & Coordination – Partner closely with EGA policy leads, country government affairs teams, communications, legal, business, and corporate strategy teams. – Develop creative strategies to strengthen Microsoft’s role as a partner, collaborating across EGA as well as with colleagues in European capitals. – Share political insights and stakeholder intelligence that strengthens advocacy efforts across the region. – Contribute to strategic planning and prioritization efforts within the European Government Affairs team. — ## Qualifications ### Required Qualifications – Extensive experience within one or more European institutions (especially European Commission, Council of the European Union, Permanent Representation, or closely related EU institutions). – Extensive experience in government affairs, public policy, political advisory, public administration, or related fields. – Demonstrated ability to build and maintain senior‑level relationships across the European policy ecosystem. – Strong understanding of EU decision‑making processes, institutional interactions, and political dynamics. – Proven track record of advising senior leaders on complex political and stakeholder engagement challenges. – Excellent judgment, diplomacy, and ability to operate effectively in highly political and sensitive environments. – Exceptional communication, relationship‑building, negotiation, and influencing skills. – Ability to collaborate effectively in a highly matrixed, multinational organization. ### Preferred Qualifications – Advanced degree in Political Science, European Affairs, Public Policy, International Relations, Law, or a related field. – Experience working directly with senior political leaders, Commissioners, Members of the European Parliament, ministers, ambassadors, cabinet members, or senior government officials. – Established network across multiple European institutions and Member State representations. – Strong understanding of technology policy and the issues shaping Europe’s digital agenda. – Experience operating in multinational corporate, consulting, trade association, or public affairs environments. – Demonstrated success designing and executing high‑impact stakeholder engagement strategies. — ## Other – Embodies Microsoft’s culture and values. – Demonstrates integrity, sound judgment, and discretion. – Thrives in a fast‑paced and evolving political environment. – Contributes to a collaborative, inclusive, and high‑performing team culture. – Able to manage multiple priorities and deliver results through influence rather than authority. #CELA — Government Affairs IC5 – The typical base pay range for this role across Belgium is €131,000.00 – €220,900.00 per year. Certain roles may be eligible for benefits and other compensation. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Director of Government Affairs
item.description: Director of Government Affairs Organization: National Council of Farmer Cooperatives (NCFC) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 07/28/2026 ## THE ROLE The Director of Government Affairs advances the federal policy priorities of the National Council of Farmer Cooperatives (NCFC) and its members by developing and executing effective advocacy strategies, strengthening relationships with policymakers and stakeholders, and translating policy outcomes into meaningful business and operational impacts for member cooperatives. The role is designed to remain flexible and adaptive as policy priorities and political environments evolve. — ## AT A GLANCE **SALARY** $135,000–$150,000 Commensurate with experience **LOCATION** Washington, DC — ## CORE RESPONSIBILITIES ### Federal Advocacy & Representation – Represent NCFC and its members before Congress, federal agencies, and the Administration, in coordination with senior leadership – Build and maintain productive relationships with Members of Congress, congressional staff, and agency officials across parties and committees – Monitor legislative and regulatory developments and assess implications for members ### Policy Strategy & Execution – Translate member priorities into clear federal policy strategies and execution plans – Develop and advance advocacy positions through written comments, testimony, briefings, and meetings ### Member Engagement & Communications – Provide timely, clear, and actionable policy analysis to NCFC members – Prepare issue briefs, updates, and background materials to support member understanding and engagement – Support member advocacy activities, including fly‑ins, briefings, and Hill meetings ### Coalition Building & External Engagement – Identify, cultivate, and manage relationships with allied organizations, coalitions, and stakeholders – Serve as a liaison to external partners to advance shared priorities – Represent NCFC at meetings, conferences, hearings, and events — ## KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & COMPETENCIES – Demonstrated ability to develop and execute federal advocacy strategies – Strong political judgment and comfort operating in dynamic policy environments – Excellent written and verbal communication, including translating complex policy for diverse audiences – Proven ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver results with minimal supervision — ## TRAVEL ~10% typical Up to 20% in peak periods — ## APPLY BY Fri, Aug. 14, 2026 — ## OBJECTIVES – Expand and sustain NCFC’s influence with Congress, federal agencies, and allied organizations – Deliver disciplined, member‑driven advocacy that adapts to shifting policy environments – Serve as a trusted strategic resource to members, staff leadership, and external partners – Strengthen member engagement with timely, actionable insights and meaningful ways to shape advocacy — ## EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE – Bachelor’s degree – Minimum 5 years in government affairs, congressional offices, federal agencies, or advocacy organizations – Understanding of the farmer‑owned cooperative system, including Capper‑Volstead, preferred – Relationship‑builder with credibility among policymakers, members, and stakeholders – Collaborative mindset, working effectively across teams and leadership levels – A self‑starter who takes initiative in ambiguous environments with a growth‑oriented mindset – Openness to adopting new technologies and data‑driven tools to enhance policy, communications, and efficiency — ## ABOUT NCFC Since 1929, NCFC has been the voice of America’s farmer cooperatives. Our members are regional and national farmer cooperatives, which in turn consist of more than 1,600 local farmer cooperatives across the country. NCFC members also include state and regional councils of cooperatives. Farmer cooperatives allow individual farmers the ability to own and lead organizations that are essential to continued competitiveness in both the domestic and international markets. America’s farmer‑owned cooperatives provide a comprehensive array of services for their members. These diverse organizations handle, process, and market virtually every type of agricultural commodity. They also provide farmers with access to infrastructure necessary to manufacture, distribute, and sell a variety of farm inputs. Additionally, they provide credit and related financial services, including export financing. NCFC is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of age, sex, sexual orientation, race, national origin, religion, disability, or marital status in determining suitability for employment. — ## TO APPLY Send a cover letter, resume, and writing sample to: [email protected] Deadline: Friday, Aug. 14, 2026 Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Grassroots Advocacy Manager
item.description: Grassroots Advocacy Manager Organization: Indiana Farm Bureau Location: Indianapolis, IN Date Posted: 07/28/2026 ## Job Details ### Description ### Minimum Knowledge and Job Requirements Bachelor’s degree required, with preference for an agricultural‑related field or public affairs. Strong verbal and written communication skills and the ability to make presentations to a wide range of audiences. Ability to coordinate projects and manage timelines across multiple stakeholders. ### Preferred Qualifications Experience working in agriculture, rural development, or related policy areas. Familiarity with Indiana agriculture, commodity groups, rural communities, and the policy issues affecting them. Understanding of legislative and regulatory processes at the local, state, and federal levels. Skilled in translating technical or regulatory content into accessible materials for non‑expert audiences. Strong ability to analyze complex policy issues, synthesize information, and develop clear recommendations. Ability to build and maintain relationships with elected officials, agency staff, and policy partners. Comfort representing the organization in public forums, hearings, or coalition meetings. Ability to identify emerging issues and communicate their relevance to members. Exceptional communication skills, including writing, public speaking, and interpersonal communication. Proactive and self‑directed, able to manage multiple priorities in a fast‑paced environment. Highly organized and detail‑oriented, with the ability to manage complex policy cycles, multiple deadlines, and large volumes of information with accuracy. — ## Job Functions Translate complex policy topics into accessible formats for member and stakeholder education. Assist counties and Regional Managers in creating opportunities for member engagement and leadership development in local, state, and national advocacy. Ensure member input and feedback directly informs policy development and messaging. Collaborate with the Marketing team to develop clear, accurate materials that highlight member‑driven policy priorities. Support cross‑team efforts to increase visibility and understanding of policies that advance Indiana agriculture. Coordinate efforts to share policy information with members, increase engagement in policy discussions, and support robust dialogue across the organization. Support the drafting of model policies, resolutions, and legislative proposals in collaboration with grassroots members, coalition partners, and the public policy team. Support policy planning cycles and annual agenda‑setting processes, including Issue Advisory Committees, the Resolutions Committee, Delegate Session preparation, and Annual Meeting policy activities for INFB and AFBF. Monitor emerging trends to identify issues and opportunities. Synthesize member feedback and policy insights into briefs, reports, and educational materials. Conduct research and analysis on key issues impacting INFB members. Track relevant legislation and regulatory developments at all levels of government. Work with County Farm Bureaus and Regional Managers to guide discussions, gather member feedback, facilitate grassroots input, and ensure the diversity of Indiana agriculture is well represented throughout the policy process. Represent INFB in coalitions, legislative meetings, and public hearings on issues related to policy development and member priorities, in coordination with the public policy team. Provide policy briefings and updates to members through presentations, webinars, and written communications. Build relationships with elected officials, agencies, and policy partners. Support the implementation of grassroots lobbying strategies in collaboration with Regional Managers and the public policy team to elevate member voices. — ## Working Conditions Position requires a valid driver’s license and physical mobility for effective job function while conducting INFB business, including locations such as hotel meeting facilities, convention centers, and farms. May occasionally require the ability to lift 25 lbs. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. This position involves regular in‑state travel and occasional out‑of‑state travel. Additional evening and weekend work is expected during key policy and member‑engagement periods, particularly during Legislative Session, INFB’s Delegate Session, and the INFB Ag Gathering. item.description: Government Relations Specialist Organization: Arizona Technology Council (AZTC) Location: Phoenix, AZ Date Posted: 07/28/2026 ## Job Summary The Arizona Technology Council (AZTC) is seeking a knowledgeable and proactive Government Relations Specialist to monitor, maintain, and advocate for clean energy legislation and climate‑friendly infrastructure investments at various governmental levels. This role involves advising the CEO, engaging with public officials, managing communications, and supporting AZTC’s mission in promoting clean energy and technology initiatives in Arizona. — ## Key Responsibilities ### Legislative Monitoring Keep abreast of current and proposed legislation and regulations related to clean energy and climate‑friendly infrastructure at the city, county, and state levels. ### Strategic Advising Provide weekly updates to the CEO to discuss AZTC’s positioning on legislative matters and recommended actions. ### Communication Draft informational paragraphs about clean energy initiatives for inclusion in the Council’s newsletter. ### Stakeholder Engagement Contact and advocate to elected and appointed officials across various government levels to support clean energy policies aligning with AZTC’s Public Policy Platform. ### Partnership Development Build and maintain relationships with non‑profits and businesses in the clean energy sector to foster collaborative projects. ### Grant Monitoring Identify and highlight state or federal grants and financing programs suitable for AZTC members, including success stories related to federal grant implementations. ### Educational Programs Initiate and conduct roundtable sessions to educate members and the public about clean energy policy, federal investment opportunities, and relevant legislation. ### Policy Engagement Participate in monthly calls focused on renewable energy projects and policy updates, and guide AZTC’s involvement in local renewable energy siting efforts. ### Community Outreach Arrange educational tours and media campaigns showcasing local businesses that have implemented clean energy projects. ### Representation Serve as AZTC’s representative at all relevant public meetings and state legislature sessions to advocate for clean energy policies and investments. ### Public Policy Committee Attend meetings twice per month. ### Collaboration Work closely with AZTC’s contract lobbyists. — ## Position Specifications ### Employment Type Full‑time staff member ### Requirements Exceptional communication skills (written and verbal), strong computer and phone skills, willingness to travel across the state, and a keen interest in clean and renewable energy. ### Desired Qualities Direct experience in dealing with elected officials, familiarity with local government offices and agencies, and an understanding of clean energy, sustainability, and infrastructure initiatives. — ## Additional Considerations – Compliance with all federal, state, and local laws regarding grant usage, as outlined in funding agreements. – Regular reporting and recordkeeping to ensure accountability and adherence to grant requirements. — ## Application Process Interested candidates should submit a resume, cover letter, and any relevant certifications to Leslie Marquez at [email protected] . — ## Benefits AZTC provides medical, dental, vision, and life insurance benefits, a 401(k) with 4% matching, and generous PTO and holidays. — ## Requirements Minimum 5 years of experience, with a BS in public policy or political science preferred. item.description: Director, Grassroots Advocacy Organization: Independent Community Bankers of America (ICBA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 07/28/2026 **The Director, Grassroots Advocacy** will support and expand the scope of ICBA’s grassroots advocacy to advance policy change with the Executive, Congressional, and Judicial branches of government as well as the bank regulatory agencies. The Director, Grassroots Advocacy will expand advocacy engagement from grasstops bankers, state‑level groups, and like‑minded trade associations and organizations. — ## Duties & Responsibilities Develop grassroots messages on federal legislative and regulatory issues and facilitate routine dissemination of such information to members of Congress, congressional staff, and community bankers nationwide. Support and maintain grassroots tools (Quorum) and technologies to execute and monitor advocacy campaigns. Develop and support a robust system to ensure community bankers can comment directly on bank regulatory agency proposals and requests for information (RFIs). Increase the number of community banker grassroots and grasstops engagements with the regulatory agencies on bank regulatory proposals. Assist in preparing advocacy materials, toolkits, fact sheets, and social media content. Build and deploy a network of like‑minded associations and trade groups to join in ICBA advocacy efforts. Grow the grassroots advocacy engagement from ICBA affiliated state groups. Facilitate regional advocacy engagement and in‑state meetings and provide needed grassroots advocacy materials to community bankers across the country. Work closely with other Government Relations team members and partners to align advocacy efforts to amplify the impact. Assist in tracking and analyzing grassroots advocacy engagement metrics to assess the effectiveness of outreach efforts and adjust strategies as needed. Establish and maintain relationships with other grassroots professionals, trade associations, and coalitions. Support the Government Relations team and Grassroots team on the execution of ICBA’s annual Capital Summit advocacy fly‑in. Represent the association at industry events. — ## Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in public policy or related field of study required. Minimum of three years of related government or trade association experience required. Familiarity with the federal legislative and regulatory process. Initiative‑taker with the ability to work independently and contribute to a team effort. Experience in establishing or managing a formal grassroots program. Familiarity with current grassroots tools (Quorum) and technologies to execute and monitor an advocacy campaign. Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills, including the ability to work effectively with internal and external colleagues as needed. Ability to interface well with member bankers. Ability to showcase advocacy as a key member benefit. Ability to travel as needed. — ## Compensation and Benefits ICBA offers competitive compensation and benefits and is conveniently located in the nation’s capital. The target annual salary range for this role is currently **$84,000 to $105,000** based on a regular, full‑time schedule. The amount of compensation offered will be determined by several factors, including but not limited to experience, qualifications, market data, and internal equity. — ## Equal Employment Opportunity ICBA is an equal opportunity employer committed to hiring a diverse workforce and sustaining an inclusive culture. ICBA does not discriminate on the basis of race, ethnicity, religion, sex, color, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, mental or physical disability, genetic information, veteran status, or on any other basis prohibited by applicable law. — ## About ICBA The Independent Community Bankers of America (ICBA)’s guiding mission is to create and promote environments where community banks flourish. We are: • Dedicated advocates providing community bankers, policymakers, and the public with authoritative insights and resources to support and strengthen community banking. • Knowledgeable, applying our expertise to offer personalized service that addresses the distinct challenges and opportunities facing community banks. • Community‑centered, driving meaningful change that strengthens community banks and the communities they serve. We turn commitment into action and deliver real results. — ## ICBA’s Workplace Culture ICBA’s workplace culture is built on our core values: • **Caring** – We support and prioritize your well‑being and professional growth. • **Connected** – We foster strong relationships that create meaningful impact. • **Collaboration** – We are team‑oriented and results‑driven, where diverse perspectives are valued and innovative ideas are encouraged to achieve our common goals. — **Join ICBA and further your career while making a lasting impact!** Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council!
