item.title: Director, Communications
item.description: Director, Communications Organization: R Street Institute Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 07/29/2026 ## The R Street Institute — Communications Director The R Street Institute—a free‑market think tank headquartered in Washington, D.C., with staff located across the country—seeks a collaborative Communications Director. If you are the right fit, you will report to the Senior Director of Communications. If you want to join a mission‑driven organization and work toward pragmatic policy solutions, this may be the opportunity for you. Your typical day at R Street may include leading media relations and short‑form editorial operations for the organization, supporting an executive team member on commentary or remarks for an event, or working with the team to identify and cultivate new media channels, all while ensuring that the organization’s voice is clear, credible, and consistently represented across public platforms. This role manages a team of communications professionals responsible for media engagement, short‑form editorial content, and proactive outreach to journalists and opinion editors. Working closely with the Senior Director of Communications, this person will help design and implement strategies that amplify R Street’s research, strengthen relationships with media partners, and position the organization as a trusted voice in public policy conversations. This person will also play a key role in staff development, workflow improvement, and coordination across Communications, Policy, and External Affairs functions to advance R Street’s visibility and mission. This role will serve as part of the communications department. — ## Other Aspects of Your Role – **Media & Editorial Strategy** — Partner with the Senior Director to design and execute media and editorial strategies aligned with organizational goals, including brand strategy and executive thought leadership. – **AI‑Driven Messaging** — Anticipate how AI is disrupting traditional product‑centric messaging and build a communications strategy suited to a world where discovery, trust, and attention work differently than they did five years ago. – **Audience‑First Strategy** — Build audience‑first communications strategies rather than product‑first messaging—starting from who we’re trying to reach and working backward to the right channels, formats, and moments. – **Press & Editorial Oversight** — Oversee planning and execution of R Street’s press outreach, op‑eds, short‑form commentary, and editorial calendars to amplify R Street’s brand presence in key external channels, including major media outlets, newsletters, and opinion venues. – **Policy Alignment** — Collaborate with the government affairs teams to ensure communications align with policy and legislative priorities. – **Executive Support** — Support the executive team with key thought leadership pieces, speeches, media, and external affairs. – **Media Relationships** — Maintain and deepen relationships with journalists, producers, and editors; ensure consistent and proactive media engagement. – **Editorial Quality** — Oversee the editing and publication of opinion and short‑form commentary for the RSI website, ensuring quality, timeliness, and adherence to organizational voice. – **Communications Approvals** — Approve key communications outputs, including external newsletters, advisories, and high‑impact press releases. – **Media Tracking** — Track and report on media outcomes and engagement to inform communications planning. – **Ninja Vigilance** — Remain vigilant against ninja infiltrations. — ## Skills and Qualifications – **Media Relationships** — Strong relationships with journalists, editors, new media influencers, and other communications professionals. – **Leadership** — Ability to lead and manage multiple communications departments and ensure alignment with organizational goals. – **Writing Skills** — Excellent attention to detail to ensure media content is accurate, timely, and impactful. – **Decision‑Making** — Sound decision‑making ability in a fast‑paced media and organizational environment. – **Results‑Driven** — No particular educational background required—a proven record of achieving results is far more meaningful than credentials. – **Mission Alignment** — Support for R Street’s passion for free markets and limited, effective government. – **Growth Mindset** — A sense of humor and a desire to grow within a multifaceted organization. The R Street Institute consistently offers pragmatic, real solutions that foster American innovation, bolster competition, and safeguard individual liberty—all with the understanding that life in a democratic society sometimes requires compromises that don’t necessarily represent first, best solutions. We focus on deep scholarship and pragmatic policy solutions that many groups tend to neglect. Our goal is to publish timely, relevant research and analysis that advances a market‑oriented society and limited, effective government. To that end, our motto is **“Free Markets. Real Solutions.”** — ## Workplace Candidates located in the Washington, D.C. area are preferred; however, excellent candidates outside of D.C. will be considered with the understanding that significant travel may be required. We offer a flexible working arrangement. This is a full‑time position that can either work the majority of the week in our D.C. office or be fully remote. Occasional travel may be required for events and conferences. — ## Compensation, Benefits, and Perks R Street strives to offer a compensation and benefits package that is competitive, transparent, and supportive of employee well‑being. The salary range for this position is **$115,000–$135,000**, commensurate with experience. In addition to this competitive salary, we provide: – **Unlimited paid time off**, including all federal holidays, the day after Thanksgiving, and two‑week holiday closure in December – **Alternating Fridays off** – **Employer‑paid health insurance**, including family coverage – **Dental and vision insurance** – **401(k) contributions** with up to a 4% match – **HSA employer contribution match** – **Quarterly wellness reimbursement** – **Mobile equipment/mobile plan reimbursement** – **Home internet subsidy** – **Annual educational and professional development reimbursement** – **Choice of child care assistance, pet care assistance, or student loan repayment assistance** — ## Culture At R Street, we strive for preeminence in every area in which we engage, driven by our commitment to excellence and innovation. Our culture thrives on action, creativity, and courage, with an unwavering focus on quality, credibility, and impact. We believe progress requires diverse experience and expertise, which is why we champion non‑traditional yet prudent approaches to public policy. We approach our mission with intellectual rigor, embracing free inquiry and honesty to ensure our work is grounded in solid research and thoughtful analysis. While serious about our purpose, we value the joy of collaboration and the fun that comes from working together. Our collaborative spirit fosters trust and transparency, with respect and openness guiding our actions. We celebrate our individual contributions while recognizing that we are stronger as one team. R Street does not discriminate on the basis of age, sex, race, creed, color, national origin, sexual orientation, era of military service, gender identity or expression, relationship structure, or anything else that’s illegal, immoral, or stupid to use as a basis for hiring. — ## Application Process We plan to accept applications for this job until filled. We will contact qualified individuals for telephone screenings and conduct them on a rolling basis. Interviews take place virtually via Zoom. To apply, please copy and paste your cover letter into the text box and upload your resume as a Microsoft Word document or PDF at: **[ https://street.applytojob.com/apply/Hu6jjD5Ipc/Director-Communications?source=PAC ]** We encourage thoughtful use of AI tools. If you use them, please describe how they contributed to your work. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Writer/Editor​
item.description: Writer/Editor​ Organization: Colonial Williamsburg Foundation Location: Williamsburg, VA Date Posted: 07/29/2026 ## Who We Are Founded in 1926, the Colonial Williamsburg Foundation is a private, not-for-profit educational, historic, and cultural institution that owns and operates one of the largest and best-known museum complexes in the world. Our mission is “that the future may learn from the past” through preserving and restoring 18th-century Williamsburg, Virginia’s colonial capital. We engage, inform, and inspire people to learn about this historic capital, the events that occurred here, and the diverse peoples who helped shape a new nation. Today, Colonial Williamsburg is the largest living history museum in the U.S. The Historic Area is the 301-acre restored colonial capital with 88 original buildings and 525 buildings reconstructed to how they appeared in the 18th century through extensive archaeological, architectural, and documentary research. The Historic Area is staffed by highly trained, historically dressed interpreters and expert tradespeople who bring the 18th century to life. The Foundation also owns and operates two world-class museums — the DeWitt Wallace Decorative Arts Museum and the Abby Aldrich Rockefeller Folk Art Museum — and a renowned research library, the John D. Rockefeller Jr. Library. ## About the Position The Writer/Editor will generate and write original articles and edit features and other content as needed for *Trend & Tradition: The Magazine of Colonial Williamsburg*, as assigned by the Editorial Manager. Works with all editorial staff on best practices. In addition, provides writing and editing support for book publishing. ## Main Duties Responsibilities include but are not limited to: – Use news judgment to propose, research, conduct interviews, and personally write original articles whose subject matter pertains to The Colonial Williamsburg Foundation’s mission, activities, research, programming, and general news. The position is responsible for writing a minimum of 12 original articles per issue, ranging from 200 to 2,000 words, including (but not limited to) profiles, “Behind the Scenes,” general-interest stories, and Foundation updates. – Exercise independent editorial judgment and participate in idea sessions on stories and illustrations. Find and propose potential articles and bring fresh ideas and approaches to long-standing features and columns. – Offer original headline suggestions and caption writing, and suggest and produce complementary content to package with articles, including illustrations and photography. – Work with the editorial staff, exercise editorial judgment, and help expand and produce stories based on ideas from the staff. – Conduct fact-checking using Associated Press Style, edit features and news articles, and make suggestions to further align stories with the Foundation’s mission. Work with the editorial team to execute long-term planning for stories and magazine issues. – Cultivate relationships with other departments across the Foundation, including Development, Museums, and Digital Marketing, to collect material for regular magazine features. – In concert with the Editorial Manager, proofread final galleys of the magazine before submission for printing. – Support book publications as a Writer and/or Editor/Proofreader. Generate potential book projects. This job description reflects the general responsibilities of the position and is not intended to be an exhaustive list. Duties and responsibilities may evolve over time based on operational needs. ## Required Education and Experience – Bachelor’s degree, preferably in English, Journalism, or History – Three (3) to five (5) years of professional feature writing and editing experience – To be considered, applicants must provide three (3) published writing clips, résumé, and references. ## Preferred Qualifications – Experience in book publishing is desired – 3+ years’ experience in a magazine setting – Familiarity with InDesign is desirable – Familiarity with project management tools such as Trello is a plus ## Key Skills / Competencies – Knowledge of American colonial history – Knowledge of AP Style – Strong organizational skills; must demonstrate ability/willingness to take direction and work independently – Must be comfortable using both Mac and PC environments – Knowledge about Colonial Williamsburg and the surrounding region, particularly its 18th-century history ## Physical and Environmental Demands Stand: Constantly Walk: Frequently Sit: Constantly Use hands/fingers: Constantly Climb or balance: Rarely Stoop/kneel/crouch/crawl: Rarely Reach with hands/arms: Frequently Talk or hear: Constantly Lifting up to 10 lbs.: Rarely Lifting up to 25 lbs.: Rarely Lifting up to 50 lbs. (with assistance): Rarely Lifting up to 100 lbs. (with assistance): Rarely More than 100 lbs. (with assistance): Rarely Wet/humid conditions: Rarely Work near moving mechanical parts: Rarely Fumes/airborne particles: Rarely Extreme cold: Rarely Extreme heat: Rarely Risk of electrical shock: Rarely ## Typical Work Schedule Monday–Friday, 9 AM–5 PM ## Compensation Disclaimer The compensation listed below for this position represents the anticipated hiring range and is provided in accordance with Virginia pay transparency requirements. Actual compensation will be determined based on factors such as the selected candidate’s skills, qualifications, experience, education, certifications, internal equity, and the specific requirements of the role. **Range:** $69,700 to $104,500 Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Public Relations Lead, Association & Membership
item.description: Public Relations Lead, Association & Membership Organization: PGA of America Location: Frisco, TX Date Posted: 07/30/2026 Join a team of proud, passionate, and caring people that together share their diverse talents and backgrounds to serve our members and grow the game of golf. Being at the PGA of America means you are supported, respected, and appreciated for your contributions. The Public Relations Lead, Association & Membership promotes and elevates the visibility of more than 30,000 PGA Golf Professionals and the Association’s work. This role oversees media relations and strategic communications to tell the story of PGA Members, highlight major Association initiatives, and build awareness of key programs, including Governance, Career Services, Education, Coaching & Player Development, and the PGA of America REACH Foundation. The position serves as a connector between internal teams, external media, and the broader community, ensuring consistent and engaging communications that support the organization’s strategic priorities. Responsibilities Specific areas of responsibility include but are not limited to: Write, edit, and proofread press releases, media pitches, scripts, executive talking points, and Q&A documents that clearly and accurately represent the approved strategy. Develop and maintain a consistent editorial voice across all earned media materials, ensuring adherence to Associated Press (AP) style and PGA of America brand guidelines. Prepare and update media kits, fact sheets, bios, and backgrounders to support both proactive outreach and responses to media inquiries. Develop and nurture relationships with traditional, new, and non-traditional media outlets, including local, regional, national, and diverse publications, by pitching relevant stories and customizing messaging for each audience and platform. Collaborate with teams across the PGA, including Membership, Governance, Career Services, Education, PGA Sections, and the REACH Foundation, to identify newsworthy stories and ensure messaging accuracy. Manage editorial calendars and deadlines to ensure timely, high-quality content delivery. Serve as the primary liaison for internal teams, PGA Sections, and PR agencies by collaborating on strategic plans, generating awareness, securing media coverage, and overseeing the PR hub and calendar for internal news release coordination. Collaborate with agencies on monthly and quarterly media coverage reporting, including editing and distributing reports to leadership. Partner with Digital and Marketing teams to distribute content, generate awareness, and track engagement across digital platforms. Support and coordinate media interviews and speaking opportunities for senior management and leadership. Maintain a strong understanding of the PGA of America’s strategic plan, golf industry issues, and external opportunities to inform and prioritize PR planning. Coordinate interview tracking and Association fact sheets, and support media monitoring and daily distribution of industry headlines to keep stakeholders informed. Use wire services, MailChimp, and other PR technologies for distribution and reporting metrics. Shared Values Embody the organization’s shared values and help ensure the organization’s values-based culture thrives by proactively identifying and addressing any shared values challenges and opportunities impacting you and your team. Keep Leadership aware of the pulse of the workforce by recognizing, discussing, and addressing any cultural concerns. Inclusive Statement Contribute to a respectful and inclusive team environment by welcoming and respecting others’ beliefs, backgrounds, identities, abilities, and individuality to help ensure a supportive and engaging experience for Association Members, partners, customers, and guests. PGA of America respects the uniqueness of each employee and offers everyone the means to find their place and thrive. Supervision No supervisory responsibilities. Financial Responsibility Assist with the development and management of the annual budget for the Public Relations department, as well as management of purchase requisitions and needed contracts. Education and Experience Bachelor’s Degree (B.A.) in Journalism, Communications, English, Public Relations, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience. Five years of experience in public relations, journalism, or corporate communications. Portfolio demonstrating published writing experience required. Exceptional writing, editing, and proofreading skills with close attention to grammar, clarity, and AP style. Proven ability to write for multiple formats and audiences, including press releases, social copy, executive messaging, and long-form articles. Experience working with media outlets and building relationships with reporters and editors. Familiarity with the golf industry is preferred. Job Knowledge/Technology Must have knowledge of national, regional, and local media, gained through experience in public relations or a related field. Demonstrated ability to develop and maintain strong working relationships with cross-functional teams, providing valuable insight into project timelines and communication needs. Proven track record of building and sustaining media contacts. Strong project management skills with the ability to handle multiple writing assignments and deadlines simultaneously. Proficiency with Gmail, Google Drive, Google Sheets, and Google Docs is required. Basic fluency in artificial intelligence (AI) tools and concepts is also expected, including the ability to use AI to enhance business operations and drive innovation while supporting the mission to better serve Members and stakeholders. Additional Information Ability to travel up to 5%. This position is not eligible for immigration sponsorship. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this position. PGA does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, creed, religion, gender, age, disability, sexual orientation, national origin, citizenship, veteran status, gender identity or expression, marital or familial status, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law. In addition, to ensure full equality of opportunity in all operations and activities of the organization, every staff member employed by the PGA shall be selected under fair employment procedures that provide equal employment opportunities to all people. item.title: Account Director
item.description: Account Director Organization: Reputation Ink Location: Jacksonville, FL Date Posted: 07/30/2026 Reputation Ink Reputation Ink is a fully remote, woman-owned public relations and marketing agency specializing in B2B professional services — including law firms, architecture, engineering and construction (AEC) firms, asset management firms, and other complex industries where expertise matters. We’re a fast-growing agency (3x Fastest-Growing Companies honoree and recently shortlisted for PRWeek’s Outstanding Boutique Agency of the Year), and we’re looking for an Account Director to step into a senior leadership role, owning client relationships, guiding strategy, and developing high-performing teams. This is not a task-management role. This is a role for someone who wants to lead accounts, influence strategy, and help shape the future of a fast-growing agency. While this is primarily a public relations role, our work is inherently integrated. Many client programs also include content marketing, social media, and select digital initiatives, so comfort operating across disciplines is important. What You’ll Do As an Account Director, you will serve as the strategic lead and trusted advisor for your clients, with full ownership of account performance, team management, and client satisfaction. You will: Lead Client Strategy and Relationships Serve as the primary point of contact and strategic advisor to clients. Develop and oversee annual strategic plans. Guide clients through complex communications challenges, including crisis situations. Identify opportunities to grow accounts organically. Oversee Integrated PR and Marketing Execution Lead and execute primarily PR-driven campaigns, including media relations and earned media strategy, while supporting integrated efforts across thought leadership, content marketing, social media, and select digital and creative initiatives. Ensure all deliverables are high quality, on time, and aligned with client goals. Maintain a strong pulse on media trends and industry opportunities. Manage and Develop Teams Lead, mentor, and develop account team members. Delegate effectively while maintaining accountability for outcomes. Conduct regular check-ins, performance reviews, and career development planning. Build and retain high-performing teams. Own Account Performance Manage budgets and ensure account profitability. Meet billability and utilization targets. Oversee reporting and ensure clients clearly see the value of our work. What We’re Looking For We’re looking for someone who combines strategic thinking, strong writing, and natural leadership. You likely have: 5–10 years of agency experience, ideally in B2B or professional services. A track record of managing and growing client accounts. Experience leading teams and developing talent. Exceptional writing and editing skills. A strong foundation in public relations is essential; experience with integrated marketing disciplines like content and social is a plus. You also bring: A proactive mindset — you’re always thinking about what’s next. High emotional intelligence and strong client presence. The ability to translate complex ideas into clear, compelling narratives. Comfort working with senior-level clients, including attorneys, executives, architects, and engineers. Why Reputation Ink Fully remote (and always will be). Fast-growing agency (Jacksonville Business Journal Fastest-Growing Companies, 3x). Shortlisted for PRWeek’s Outstanding Boutique Agency of the Year. High-impact work with sophisticated B2B clients. Collaborative, low-ego, high-performance culture. Opportunity to grow into senior leadership. Benefits Two weeks of paid vacation in the first year, three weeks in years two through four, and four weeks after year five. 11 recognized public holidays. Bonus week off between Christmas and New Year’s (the entire company is off). Health, dental, disability, and life insurance. 401(k) company match (beginning after one year of employment). Our Hiring Process Because writing is central to this role, finalists will complete 2–3 paid writing assignments as part of the interview process. Ready to Apply? Please send a resume and cover letter to [email protected] . Applications without a cover letter will not be considered. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Director of Global Initiatives (EX9874)
item.description: Director of Global Initiatives (EX9874) Organization: Stetson University Location: DeLand, FL Date Posted: 07/30/2026 Job Description The Director of Global Initiatives provides strategic leadership for the institution’s global engagement initiatives. Reporting to the Office of the Provost and Academic Affairs, the Director leads the development, implementation, and assessment of comprehensive international education programs, including education abroad, international student and scholar services, global partnerships, and campus internationalization. The position advances the University’s global mission through collaboration with faculty, staff, students, alumni, donors, and international partners. Essential Job Functions and Responsibilities Employment duties include, but are not limited to: Strategic Leadership Provides strategic counsel to the Provost and to Academic Affairs on issues of campus internationalization to implement collaborative initiatives that strengthen the institution’s global presence and engagement. Advise the Provost and Academic Affairs on institutional strategies and policies related to international education and global engagement. Provide strategic leadership for study abroad, international student and scholar services, international partnerships, and campus internationalization initiatives. Collaborate across academic and administrative units to integrate global learning throughout the student experience and curriculum. Develop and implement long-range strategic initiatives that expand international learning opportunities and institutional global engagement. Global Partnerships and International Programs Lead the cultivation, negotiation, and management of strategic global partnerships that support student and faculty exchanges, collaborative research, and academic initiatives with legal counsel. Establish, cultivate, and maintain strategic partnerships with universities and organizations worldwide to support student and faculty exchange, collaborative research, and academic programming. Negotiate, develop, and oversee Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs) and partnership agreements in collaboration with the University’s external legal counsel. Direct the University’s international exchange programs, including the recruitment, orientation, and support of J-1 exchange students, scholars, interns, and visiting faculty. Education Abroad Leadership Provide strategic leadership for operational policies and compliance of all student and faculty education abroad programs and experiences. Provide management protocols for international travel and education abroad programs. Lead the creation and expansion of innovative global learning initiatives designed to increase student participation and access. Foster faculty engagement through professional development initiatives that support the design and implementation of high-quality faculty-led study abroad programs. Recruit and provide oversight of the first-year study abroad programs such as the Global Gateways Program currently in Dublin, Ireland. Faculty Development and Campus Internationalization Develop and administer faculty development opportunities focused on international education, including seminars, workshops, travel grants, and professional learning communities. Collaborate with faculty to integrate global learning outcomes into academic programs and curricula. Serve on institutional committees responsible for international learning policies, curricular innovation, academic advising, and global engagement initiatives. Student Success and Compliance Serve as a university Designated School Official (DSO) for F-1 students and Responsible Officer (RO) for J-1 exchange visitors, ensuring compliance with all federal immigration regulations and SEVIS reporting requirements. Provide leadership for international student success initiatives that promote recruitment, retention, academic achievement, and campus engagement. Respond to and manage student, scholar, and education abroad emergencies on a 24/7 on-call basis. Budget, Advancement, and Administration Provide strategic leadership and oversight for international education professional staff, departmental budgets, and collaborative resource-raising. Develop and manage departmental operating budgets, endowed funds, and financial resources supporting international education initiatives. Prepare reports and assessments for senior leadership, donors, and the Board of Trustees demonstrating program effectiveness and strategic impact. Partner with University Advancement to identify funding opportunities, prepare donor proposals, and secure philanthropic support for international initiatives. Supervise professional staff within WORLD: The David and Leighan Rinker Center for International Learning and provide leadership for departmental planning, assessment, and operations. Institutional Service Provide leadership and counsel to institutional committees and professional organizations that influence the strategic direction of international learning. Serve on university-wide committees supporting international education, academic advising, student success, and institutional planning. Participate in institutional emergency management and crisis response efforts related to international students, scholars, and education abroad programs. Represent the University in regional, national, and international professional organizations and partnerships. Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities The knowledge, skills, and abilities for this role include: Comprehensive knowledge of international education best practices, including education abroad program design, international student and scholar services, and global partnership development. Working knowledge of federal immigration regulations governing F-1 and J-1 visa holders, including SEVIS reporting and compliance requirements. Demonstrated skill in strategic planning and the ability to translate institutional priorities into actionable global engagement initiatives. Strong financial acumen, including experience developing and managing operating budgets, endowed funds, and grant or donor-funded accounts. Ability to supervise, mentor, and develop professional staff in a fast-paced, service-oriented environment. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to represent the University persuasively to faculty, students, donors, and international partners. Skill in negotiating and administering international agreements (MOUs) in coordination with legal counsel. Ability to exercise sound judgment and make timely decisions during student or program emergencies, including outside of normal business hours. Cultural competence and demonstrated ability to work effectively with individuals from diverse national, cultural, and linguistic backgrounds. Ability to analyze program data and prepare clear, compelling reports for senior leadership and the Board of Trustees. Proficiency with relevant software systems (e.g., SEVIS, study abroad management platforms, database and reporting tools). Commitment to supporting the University’s Mission and Values. Required Qualifications This position requires: Master’s degree required. At least five (5) years of progressive leadership experience in international education, higher education administration, or a related field. Demonstrated expertise in education abroad, international student and scholar services, immigration compliance (F-1/J-1), and global partnership development. Experience managing budgets, supervising professional staff, and leading strategic initiatives. Proven success in fundraising, grant development, and donor relations preferred. Strong interpersonal, organizational, and communication skills with the ability to collaborate across diverse constituencies. Demonstrated commitment to global learning, intercultural competence, student success, and inclusive excellence. Ideal Candidate Qualifications Doctoral or terminal degree in international education, higher education administration, or a related field. Seven-plus (7+) years of progressive leadership experience in international education, with direct oversight of both education abroad and international student/scholar services functions. Prior experience serving as a Designated School Official (DSO) and/or Responsible Officer (RO). Established international partnership network or prior experience developing partnerships in one or more target regions. Fluency or proficiency in a second language. Experience living, studying, or working abroad. Demonstrated success securing philanthropic or grant support for international programming. Experience with a private, residential liberal arts institution or comparable university setting. Familiarity with study abroad risk management and international crisis response protocols. Work Environment Primarily an indoor office environment with standard lighting, temperature, and noise levels. Some regional, national, and international travel is required, including occasional travel to partner institutions and program sites abroad. Availability required outside of standard business hours to respond to student and program emergencies (24/7 on-call responsibilities as needed). Fast-paced environment with competing priorities and periodic seasonal demands (e.g., peak study abroad application and departure cycles). Flexible Work Arrangement (FWA) may be available in accordance with University policy. Work authorization sponsorship may be available for this position. However, sponsorship is contingent upon the non-applicability of the visa petition fees outlined in the relevant Executive Order signed September 19, 2025. Due to the recent federally mandated increased financial expense, the university is not in a position to absorb this significantly increased cost of sponsorship for new H-1B petitions at this time. item.title: New Jersey State Director
item.description: New Jersey State Director Organization: Humane World for Animals Location: Trenton, NJ Date Posted: 07/30/2026 **The general salary range for this position is $90,000 – $115,000. Salary offers will be commensurate with experience, qualifications, skills, training, and education.** Humane World for Animals, a global leader in animal advocacy and protection, is seeking a **State Director, New Jersey** for the State Affairs department. In this position you will operate from a home office under the supervision of the Regional Director. You will be responsible for developing and executing state‑specific strategies to advance the organization’s legislative and programmatic goals. **You will be responsible for:** – Advances public policy priorities through direct lobbying; influences and builds relationships with agency officials, lawmakers, executives, and staff in support of the organization’s priorities; manages and directs policy reform through each stage of the process. – Builds and engages a diverse coalition of stakeholders in support of the organization’s strategic plan and public policy goals in New Jersey. – Develops state‑specific strategy with program teams and other internal stakeholders and implements the plan in New Jersey, including passing public policy, defending against attacks to weaken animal protection laws, and working on priority issues within New Jersey. – Serves as a spokesperson for the organization with government officials, key stakeholders, and the media; seeks out media opportunities to advance public policy goals and increase public awareness of priority issues. – Complies with internal, local, and statewide lobbying regulations; manages the state’s budget; updates and maintains social media sites with information regarding organizational priorities. – In collaboration with organizational experts, provides guidance, training, and support for local investigators and enforcement officials, and provides hands‑on assistance when appropriate. – On occasion, works with the Humane World Action Fund to carry out State PAC work or political activity. – Performs other duties and responsibilities as assigned. **Qualifications and Requirements:** – Bachelor’s degree in Political Science, Government/Public Affairs, Communications/Media, or a related field, or equivalent work experience required. – A minimum of five (5) years of progressive work experience in animal protection/advocacy work or other related experience required. – Legislative/lobbying experience strongly preferred. – Volunteer management experience preferred. – Grassroots advocacy and political campaigning experience is a plus. – Strong knowledge of and interest in the animal welfare movement preferred. – Strong knowledge and understanding of the legislative and political process, particularly at the state level. – Excellent written and verbal communication skills. – Ability to prioritize and manage multiple projects simultaneously and be flexible with regard to workload and assignments. – Ability to work with a wide range of stakeholders across diverse political, cultural, and socioeconomic spectrums; uphold organizational values related to diversity, equity, and inclusion. – Comfortable in a fast‑paced environment with frequent deadlines; high energy, self‑motivated, and proactive. – Excellent organizational skills; ability to analyze and manage problems in advancing legislative strategy and effectively provide solutions. – Strong interpersonal skills. – Strong knowledge of Microsoft Office (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Outlook); comfortable learning new technological platforms as introduced by the organization. – Attention to detail and commitment to excellence, demonstrated by the delivery of quality and timely outcomes. – Ability to work both independently and as an effective team member. This is a full‑time remote position based from a home office in the state of New Jersey. Candidates must live within a one‑hour commute from Trenton. Extensive travel across the state with occasional out‑of‑state travel required. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, marital or parental status, or protected veteran status. item.title: Manager, Marketing & Communications
item.description: Manager, Marketing & Communications Organization: National Alliance on Mental Illness (NAMI) Location: Arlington, VA Date Posted: 07/30/2026 ## What Started as a Small Group What started as a small group of families gathered around a kitchen table in 1979 has blossomed into the nation’s leading voice on mental health. The National Alliance on Mental Illness (NAMI) is the nation’s largest grassroots mental health organization dedicated to building better lives for the millions of Americans affected by mental illness. Today, we are an alliance of hundreds of local affiliates, state organizations and a national office that work in communities across the United States to raise awareness and provide support and education that was not previously available to those in need. NAMI advocates for all who are affected by mental illness, both the individuals and the people in their lives. We work to address disparities and injustices and to promote dignity and inclusion for all people with mental illness and their families. In addition to being advocates, we educate, we listen, and we lead as evidenced by our public awareness campaigns, the range of programs we provide, and our strong public policy. — ## Position Summary: Manager, Marketing and Communications NAMI is seeking a dynamic and creative Manager, Marketing and Communications to play a pivotal role in shaping our outreach efforts. Responsibilities include working with departmental colleagues to create multi-channel marketing and communications strategies in collaboration with the Senior Manager, Marketing and Communications. Additionally, the Manager, Marketing and Communications will play a large role in developing compelling content and creative to promote NAMI’s programs, initiatives, events, and development. This role works closely with the Senior Manager, Marketing and Communications and the broader Marketing and Communications team to ensure alignment and consistency across initiatives. To ensure alignment with NAMI’s strategic goals, the Manager will help drive key performance indicators (KPIs), offer strategic oversight of marketing and communications initiatives, and recommend adjustments based on performance data to ensure continuous improvement and mission alignment. This position is also responsible for providing support for production and promotion of *Hope Starts With Us*, NAMI’s popular podcast. This full-time position is based out of our Arlington, VA office 2–3 days per week.* **Salary Range:** $68k–$74k — ## Essential Duties and Responsibilities – Serve as Marketing and Communications liaison to highlight work of internal clients across the organization and promote NAMI programs, initiatives, events, and strategic campaigns – In collaboration with the Senior Manager of Marketing and Communications and MarCom team, help create marketing and communication plans aligned to organizational strategic priorities – Help create omnichannel campaigns using the PESO model and utilizing a variety of tactics including but not limited to digital and OOH advertising, social media, email marketing, NAMI’s website, partnerships, print collateral, media outreach, video and new media – Work with Marketing and Communications department colleagues to execute communications and marketing plans and provide project management support – Conduct project brief meetings to align on strategic priorities and project goals, establish clear project timelines, schedule related activities, and actively participate in meetings – Write content for marketing and communication campaigns and review creative, acting as a guide and account manager between Marketing and Communications and internal clients – Develop clear, concise, and compelling marketing and communications talking points that align with organizational strategy and brand messaging for various internal and external audiences – Gather campaign analytics, reporting on progress and providing analysis to internal and/or external stakeholders – Ensure timely delivery of marketing and communication collateral, resources, and national office updates to support NAMI’s State Offices and Affiliates effectively – Provide vital support for the creation and logistical coordination of a wide range of marketing deliverables for NAMI’s development outreach – Support production and promotion of NAMI’s podcast *Hope Starts With Us* through episode research, content creation, and promotion activities – In coordination with marketing and communication team members, conduct research and analysis on current marketing trends and target audience behavior to refine messaging and optimize campaign performance – Monitor, track, and evaluate Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) for marketing and communication deliverables; report findings and recommendations to optimize strategies to align with NAMI’s strategic priorities – Support NAMI’s communication strategy development and execution – Perform other duties as assigned — ## Minimum Qualifications – Bachelor’s degree in marketing, communications, or related field with 3–5 years of work experience – Cause-related communications, fundraising/development, or agency background preferred; experience in marketing or communications at a non-profit or public health organization is highly desirable – Ability to maintain flexibility and foster teamwork in a fast-paced, demanding work environment – Experience using a project management software such as Asana – Experience measuring and analyzing metrics and KPIs and providing reports – Demonstrated knowledge in using marketing analytics tools and software; ability to build customized tracking dashboards, conduct comprehensive marketing analysis, and generate reports – Creative thinker and self-starter, with ability to work well independently and within a team – Ability to define and meet deadlines, manage multiple tasks, and ensure quality marketing communications outcomes – Ability to respond quickly and effectively to challenges, with keen problem-solving skills and adaptability – Strong collaboration skills and ability to work across a matrixed organization – Relies on extensive experience and judgment to plan and accomplish goals – Organized, detail-oriented, and able to thrive in a fast-paced environment – Excellent writing and verbal communication skills – Knowledge of the AP Style Guide with an enthusiasm for applying its principles – Working knowledge or proficiency with MailChimp or similar email marketing platforms – Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite – Ability to travel up to 10% – Must pass background check *This position operates under a hybrid work model and requires regular onsite presence 2–3 times per week. In-office attendance is essential to facilitate collaboration, support cross-functional communication, engage with stakeholders and senior leadership, and manage projects that cannot be done remotely. Candidates must be able to reliably work onsite and adapt to evolving operational requirements.* — ## Benefits Your salary is only one component of the total compensation package. NAMI offers a range of standard and unique benefits that are reviewed annually: – Generous and comprehensive Health, Dental, and Vision Plans – Paid Time Off: Vacation, Personal, and Sick Leave – Paid Parental Leave – 403(b) retirement plan – Flexible Spending Accounts for health care, dependent care, and commuter expenses – Life Insurance and Disability coverage paid by NAMI – Flexible Work and Telework programs – Professional Development Reimbursement program – A variety of wellness offerings to support team members – Employee Referral Program – The Employee Assistance Program (EAP), which provides support for personal and family problems common in contemporary life — ## Equal Opportunity Statement NAMI is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workforce. item.title: Senior Research Scientist – Policy
item.description: Senior Research Scientist – Policy Organization: ETS Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 07/30/2026 ## About ETS ETS is a global education and talent solutions organization enabling lifelong learners worldwide to be future-ready. For more than 75 years, we’ve been advancing the science of measurement to build benchmarks for fair and valid skill assessment across cultures and borders. Our worldwide impact extends through our renowned assessments including TOEFL®, TOEIC®, GRE® and Praxis® tests, serving millions of learners in more than 200 countries and territories. Through strategic acquisitions, we’ve expanded our global capabilities: PSI strengthens our workforce assessment solutions, while Edusoft, Kira Talent, Pipplet, Vericant, and Wheebox enhance our educational technology and assessment platforms across critical markets worldwide. Through ETS Research Institute and ETS Solutions, we’re partnering with educational institutions, governments, and organizations globally to promote skill proficiency, empower upward mobility, and unlock opportunities for everyone, everywhere. With offices and partners across Asia, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Americas, we deliver nearly 50 million tests annually. Join us in our journey of measuring progress to power human progress worldwide. — ## Research Scientist Position – Policy Research Foundational Research Program The ETS Research Institute invites applications for an open-rank Research Scientist position in the Policy Research Foundational Research program. We seek quantitative scientists with expertise in one or more of the following areas: – Causal inference and quasi-experimental designs in education policy – Analysis of large-scale assessment data (e.g., NAEP, PISA, PIAAC) and equity-forward reporting – Responsible AI/ML for policy and practice (including bias detection and mitigation) – Measurement and validation of durable skills and civic capacities – Longitudinal systems analysis – Program evaluation that translates research into actionable policy guidance The successful candidate will join a collaborative team advancing ETS’s policy research agenda that translates policy research and measurement science into systems change that benefits all students. — ## Primary Responsibilities – Conduct and publish rigorous policy research on education systems, including K–12, postsecondary, and workforce pathways, using causal inference methods (e.g., regression discontinuity, difference-in-differences) and other quantitative designs. – Contribute to the development, evaluation, and translation of research frameworks that inform state and federal education policy, with attention to effectiveness for all, opportunity, and systems change. – Collaborate with internal research teams and external partners—including state education agencies, school districts, foundations, and research organizations—on projects spanning program evaluation, policy analysis, and field-building initiatives. – Provide policy consultation and technical assistance to policymakers, practitioners, and other stakeholders seeking to apply research evidence to decision-making. – Participate in proposal development for foundation grants, federal funding, and philanthropic partnerships to support the policy research agenda. – Mentor junior staff, postdoctoral fellows, and interns, contributing to the development of boundary-spanning professionals who can bridge research, policy, and practice. – Disseminate research findings to diverse audiences through peer-reviewed publications, policy briefs, convenings, legislative testimony, and accessible formats (e.g., data visualizations, newsletters, blogs). **Location:** Washington, DC — ## Experience and Skills – Demonstrated expertise in at least one of the following: causal inference methods (e.g., regression discontinuity, difference-in-differences, instrumental variables), mixed-methods research design, policy analysis, or program evaluation. Candidates are not expected to have expertise in all areas. – Experience with statistical programming (e.g., R, Stata, Python) and analysis of administrative, survey, or longitudinal data in education or social policy contexts. – Strong record of research productivity, including peer-reviewed publications, policy briefs, or technical reports for applied audiences. – Ability to work collaboratively in multidisciplinary teams and communicate complex research findings to policymakers, practitioners, and other non-technical audiences. – Commitment to advancing equity and evidence-based decision-making in education policy. — ## Preferred Qualifications – Experience conducting research in partnership with state education agencies, school districts, or federal programs (e.g., NAEP, PISA, state longitudinal data systems). – Familiarity with education policy domains such as K–12 accountability, postsecondary access and admissions, workforce development, competency-based education, or AI in education. – Track record of translating research into actionable insights for policy audiences through briefs, testimony, convenings, or technical assistance. — ## Education A Ph.D. or equivalent in Education, Public Policy, Economics, Sociology, or a closely related quantitative field with at least eight years of experience in an applied policy research or academic/statistical analysis environment is required. — ## ETS Is Mission Driven and Action Oriented We are passionate about hiring innovative thinkers who believe in the promise of education and lifelong learning. We are energized by cultivating growth, innovation, and continuous transformation for the next generation of rising professionals as leaders. In support of this, ETS offers multiple Business Resource Groups (BRG) for you to learn and advance your career growth. As a not-for-profit organization, we encourage you to lean into your passion for volunteering. At ETS, you may qualify for up to an additional 8 hours of PTO for volunteer work on causes that are important to you. The base salary range advertised represents the low and high end of the anticipated salary range for this position. The base pay actually offered will take into account internal equity and also may vary depending on the candidate’s geographic region, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience among other factors. The base pay is only one aspect of the Total Rewards Package that will be offered to the successful candidate. **Salary Range:** $155,000 – $165,000 — ETS is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other characteristic protected by law. We believe in creating a work environment where all individuals are treated with respect and dignity. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Policy Analyst (Junior)
item.description: Policy Analyst (Junior) Organization: FiscalNote Location: Remote Date Posted: 07/30/2026 ## About the Position FiscalNote is hiring a Policy Analyst to serve as a core member of our Professional Services team and a trusted resource for our clients. Policy Analysts are curious, detail‑oriented, and self‑motivated — they thrive on staying current with legislative and regulatory developments and translating complex policy into clear, actionable insights. In this role, you will support a portfolio of clients across issue areas, executing high‑quality analytical work with accuracy and consistency. You will be a critical participant in day‑to‑day client delivery, taking ownership of your work and building the foundational expertise and habits that define a strong career at FiscalNote. ## About the Professional Services Team Our Professional Services team is the consulting arm of FiscalNote — the human‑in‑the‑loop that helps clients get the most out of their engagement, primarily through U.S. federal and state legislative and regulatory analysis. We build and support offerings across our core product portfolio and custom client engagements, partnering closely with Business Development and Account Management to deliver projects that help clients work smarter. We’re a dynamic, hard‑working team that thrives on constant learning, ownership, and growth. ## About You You have a passion for policy — at the federal, state, or local level — and a genuine curiosity about how legislation and regulation shape the world. You are a strong writer and communicator who can synthesize complex information for a wide range of audiences, from analysts to executives. You are organized, reliable, and take pride in delivering accurate, high‑quality work on time — even when juggling competing priorities. You seek out feedback, apply it quickly, and are committed to building your skills and growing your career. You are a team player who contributes positively to those around you and takes accountability for your own work and outcomes. You are comfortable working with technology and data, and you are open to adopting new tools — including AI‑assisted workflows — to improve efficiency and output quality. The salary range for this position is $52,000–59,500 per year. #LI‑HR1 ## What To Expect In This Position Independently produce accurate, on‑time policy analysis for assigned jurisdictions or issue areas, covering federal, state, and local legislative and regulatory developments. Deliver recurring written outputs — summaries, trackers, reports, and briefings — that meet quality standards with routine review and guidance from senior team members. Demonstrate reliable use of FiscalNote tools, data sources, and standard delivery workflows to execute client work efficiently. Apply feedback consistently to improve the accuracy, structure, and clarity of your work across deliverables. Manage your personal workload across multiple deadlines without delivery slippage, flagging risks or blockers early. Join client calls and meetings to support senior team members in managing client relationships and communicating on project status. Communicate clearly and professionally in writing and in internal discussions, using established formats and templates. Become an expert in FiscalNote’s current products and solutions, contributing to the delivery of new technical and professional services offerings over time. Relay client and product feedback to product, engineering, and go‑to‑market teams to inform continuous improvement. ## What Sets You Apart 1–3 years of relevant professional experience in policy research, government, consulting, or a related field. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to convey complex policy analysis in clear, audience‑appropriate formats. Demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects or workstreams simultaneously while maintaining attention to detail. A strong interest in the intersection of politics, policy, and technology. A Bachelor’s degree in political science, government, economics, public policy, or a related subject. Experience using data to support analysis and communicate targeted, concise insights. Exceptional organizational skills and the ability to learn new tools and workflows quickly. Comfort working alongside AI‑assisted tools and a willingness to adopt new workflows that improve speed and quality. Experience working in a client‑focused or customer service‑oriented environment preferred. Excited about this role, but don’t meet 100% of the expected qualifications listed above? We’d still love for you to apply! When applying to FiscalNote, rest assured that your application is reviewed by a living, breathing human being and evaluated based on key competencies needed for success in the position. Our Recruiting team maintains awareness of all open roles which means your application may be assessed against multiple positions and we will reach out to gauge your interest in other opportunities as appropriate. Questions or concerns? Contact [email protected] — we’d be happy to connect! As part of FiscalNote’s commitment to creating an accessible and inclusive hiring process, we strive to provide reasonable accommodations for persons with medical conditions or disabilities that will enable their access to the hiring process. If you need an accommodation, please send an email to [email protected] to let us know the nature of your request. ## About FiscalNote FiscalNote is a leader in policy and global intelligence. By uniquely combining data, technology, and insights, FiscalNote empowers customers with critical insights and the tools to turn them into action. Home to CQ, FrontierView, VoterVoice, and many other industry‑leading brands, FiscalNote helps organizations stay ahead of political and business risk. ## At FiscalNote, We Lead with Values Know your Audience ∙ Find the Truth ∙ Drive Alignment ∙ Level Up ∙ Own the Job ∙ Bias for Action ∙ Support the Family ## Company Benefits FiscalNote supports our people by enabling team members with flexibility and benefits to promote well‑being and balance, ensuring all FiscalNoters can bring their authentic selves to work. We start by offering competitive salaries, retirement accounts, and equity packages to ensure we’re all FN owners. Plus, our comprehensive benefits packages align with regional requirements and expectations no matter where you are located across the globe. Learn more at [https://careers.fiscalnote.com/benefits/]. FiscalNote values diversity. We are committed to equal opportunities and creating an inclusive environment for all our employees. We welcome applicants regardless of ethnic origin, national origin, gender, race, religious beliefs, disability, sexual orientation, or age. FiscalNote is an EEOC employer. FiscalNote uses E‑Verify to confirm the employment eligibility of all new employees. To learn more about E‑Verify, including your rights and responsibilities, please visit `www.DHS.gov/E‑Verify` Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.description: Coordinator, Communications Organization: Washington Nationals Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 07/30/2026 ## Description Reporting to the Director, Communications, the Communications Coordinator will support the day‑to‑day functions of the corporate communications vertical and provide administrative support to the entire communications department. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: compiling and sending daily clips; assisting with the distribution of all media communications; handling credential and parking requests from media; working with seasonal associates on distribution list maintenance and media monitoring reports; assisting with proactive media pitching for business‑related stories and events; and other written communications as needed. The Nationals are a military‑friendly organization actively recruiting veterans and spouses. This is a full‑time position. The Coordinator must be available to work in person in Washington, D.C. — ## Essential Duties and Responsibilities – Compile daily media clips on weekdays and during weekend homestands. – Distribute press materials via email, the Nationals website and the @NationalsComms X account. – Serve as the primary contact for media credential and parking requests. – Manage the department’s administrative tasks, including subscription services, invoices, etc. – Build, update and maintain press lists. – Write press materials and media pitches as needed. – Assemble and format coverage recaps for assigned campaigns and full season. – Assist with VIP and media escorting as needed. – Serve as the staff representative on media interviews as requested. – Maintain department calendar for upcoming announcements, events and other media materials. – Assist with the recruitment, training and development of seasonal corporate communications associates. – Assist with events, including media tours, Opening Day media, DC Sports Hall of Fame induction ceremony, Heroes Day, etc. – Other duties as assigned. — ## Qualifications ### Education **Required** Bachelors or better. ### Experience **Required** – Office: Working conditions are normal for an office environment. Position will require weekend and occasional evening work. – Must be detail‑oriented with excellent communication, organization, writing and editing skills. – Ability to work nights and weekends. – Uphold Core Values: Innovation, Integrity, and Teamwork. These core values set the tone in everything we do, help us succeed on and off the field, make a difference in the community and provide the best guest experience in sports. It is important that the person in the position commits themselves to these core values so that we can constantly move forward in the same direction – Together. – Must successfully clear a background check. – Must have U.S. work authorization. – 1 year: Minimum of one year experience in public relations, preferably in sports. **Preferred** – Familiarity with Adobe programs (Photoshop, InDesign) and Canva preferred. – Familiarity with social media platforms and emerging outlets is preferred. – Experience using Major League Baseball’s credential system and desktop publishing software such as Adobe InDesign is preferred. — ## Equal Opportunity Employer This employer is required to notify all applicants of their rights pursuant to federal employment laws. For further information, please review the **Know Your Rights notice** from the Department of Labor. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Director, Government Affairs
item.description: Director, Government Affairs Organization: The Hertz Corporation Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 07/30/2026 ## Job Description ### A Day in the Life The Director of Government Affairs will strategize, coordinate, and execute public policy objectives on behalf of the company. They will assist with the development and implementation of government affairs strategies in relation to local, state, and federal legislative bodies and government agencies, to represent and protect the organization’s business plans and interests. The starting salary for this role is $140,000 with bonus and equity eligibility; base salary is commensurate with experience. — ## What You’ll Do – Research, track, and monitor public policy and government activities including bills, proposals, regulatory actions, government grants, rebates, and other incentives that could affect the organization’s business and clients – Draft internal analysis and reports regarding policy development impacting the company – Draft analyses and statements of corporate positions on incentive programs and policies – Assist leadership with strategic planning for known and potential regulatory activities related to the business and industry – Support the government, impact, and communications teams on public–private partnership initiatives — ## What We’re Looking For – Bachelor’s degree required – 5+ years of experience in public policy, government affairs, or legislative processes, preferably within mobility, autonomous vehicles, AI, car rental, hospitality, or tourism industries – Passion for transportation and the future of mobility, with a strong understanding of mobility‑related issues and trends – Highly organized, results‑driven professional with demonstrated success managing multiple priorities and meeting deadlines in fast‑paced environments – Strong leadership and people management skills, with the ability to effectively collaborate across cross‑functional and multi‑faceted teams – Analytical, strategic, and resourceful thinker, capable of using logic, reasoning, data analysis, and report modeling to solve complex problems and drive decisions – Excellent verbal and written communication skills – Strong resource allocation, time management, and prioritization skills, with the ability to manage workload and deliver results efficiently – Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite — ## What You’ll Get – Up to 40% off the base rate of any standard Hertz rental – Paid Time Off – Medical, Dental & Vision plan options – Retirement programs, including 401(k) employer matching – Paid Parental Leave & Adoption Assistance – Employee Assistance Program for employees & family – Educational Reimbursement & Discounts – Voluntary Insurance Programs – Pet, Legal/Identity Theft, Critical Illness – Perks & Discounts – Theme Park Tickets, Gym Discounts & more — ## About Us The Hertz Corporation operates the Hertz, Dollar Car Rental, and Thrifty Car Rental brands in approximately 9,700 corporate and franchisee locations throughout North America, Europe, The Caribbean, Latin America, Africa, the Middle East, Asia, Australia, and New Zealand. The Hertz Corporation is one of the largest worldwide airport general‑use vehicle rental companies, and the Hertz brand is one of the most recognized in the world. — ## US EEO Statement At Hertz, we champion and celebrate a culture of diversity and inclusion. We take affirmative steps to promote employment and advancement opportunities. The endless variety of perspectives, experiences, skills, and talents that our employees invest in their work every day represent a significant part of our culture – and our success and reputation as a company. item.title: Manager of Legislative Affairs and Government Relations
item.description: Manager of Legislative Affairs and Government Relations Organization: ML Strategies Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 07/30/2026 ## Manager of Legislative Affairs and Government Relations ML Strategies seeks a Manager of Legislative Affairs and Government Relations with at least 1–3 years of relevant experience to sit in our Washington, DC office. ML Strategies is a full‑service, bipartisan government affairs and policy consulting group. We offer the ability to work in a multidimensional team that represents and advises a diverse range of clients — from cutting‑edge start‑up companies to established Fortune 100 corporations — who rely on us for creative solutions and proactive strategies at the local, state, and federal levels. ## Responsibilities This is a junior‑level position responsible for supporting the government relations function and representing the company on legislative and regulatory matters pertaining to ML Strategies. This position will develop, implement, and lead a strategic approach to engage leadership with the goal of identifying and prioritizing proactive legislative and regulatory initiatives. As assigned, the Manager of Legislative Affairs and Government Relations will engage in advocacy initiatives and problem‑solving around escalated issues, including advocating before federal policymakers. This position will support key business objectives and drive business development opportunities. Experience areas should include health care, energy/environment, defense, and appropriations. Collaboration with team members is an important component of any role at Mintz. Therefore, the firm requires working from the office approximately 60% of the time in accordance with the firm’s published guidelines. ## Qualifications – Bachelor’s degree required – 2–4 years of relevant legislative affairs and government relations experience in Congress, a federal agency, lobbying, or a law firm – Ability to demonstrate a strong track record of smart, creative, and effective strategies in legislative affairs and government relations work – Background and experience on issues related to energy/environment, health care, financial services, and/or technology/telecom preferred – Essential skills include exceptional written and verbal communication, attention to detail, good judgment, a team‑oriented attitude, solid interpersonal and analytical skills, and the ability to handle multiple projects across multiple clients at one time – Committed to excellence, teamwork, and superior client service ## About ML Strategies ML Strategies delivers superior government relations and consulting services. With deep knowledge in a range of issues including energy, transportation, health care, financial services, real estate, education, and telecommunications, our professionals in Boston and Washington, DC use their extensive experience in federal, state, and city government — as well as in the private sector — to build creative, informed, and strategic solutions that meet the goals of our clients. item.title: Communications Director
item.description: Communications Director Organization: Fairfax County Federation of Teachers (FCFT) Location: Springfield, VA Date Posted: 07/30/2026 **Status:** Full-Time, Exempt, In Person (Field and Office), Based in Northern Virginia, Non-Bargaining Unit Position **Reports to:** FCFT President **Works closely with:** Organizing Department, Representation Department, Political Director ## About FCFT FCFT is a labor union based in Northern Virginia representing the Operational and Instructional workers of Fairfax County Public Schools, including transportation workers, custodians, teachers, counselors, social workers, maintenance and trades staff, food service workers, and clerical staff. We are an organizing union focused on building worker power and engaging the community around well-funded and supported public schools. ## Position Summary The Communications Director works under the direction of FCFT’s President and oversees and executes all internal and external communications. This role will lead multi-media and digital strategy to strengthen FCFT’s public presence and brand, with a strong emphasis on lifting up workers’ voices. Key areas of focus include social media, website management, digital and print communications, media relations, newsletters/email campaigns, short-form video production, and content creation. ## Key Responsibilities – Develop and implement a comprehensive strategic communications plan for the organization targeting both internal and external audiences. – Develop and implement the organization’s internal communications strategy including drafting and issuing regular digital newsletters, urgent digital updates, mailings, flyers, and graphics; and maintaining accurate and updated lists for email and text communications. – Develop and implement the organization’s external communications strategy including managing and creating content for all social media platforms, maintaining and regularly updating the organization’s website, and strategically engaging partner organizations and individuals. – Develop and implement the organization’s media strategy including developing and maintaining relationships with the media; serving as the primary point of contact with the press and responding to media inquiries; identifying strategic media opportunities; organizing public press events; writing and pitching targeted op-eds; issuing press releases and media advisories; and providing support to spokespeople for interviews, speaking engagements, and opinion writing. – Lead crisis communications planning and response, including rapid messaging and media engagement during high-pressure moments. – Design branded merchandise and manage the budgeting and ordering of merchandise, mailers, and posters. – Ensure high-quality, consistent, and creative content in all communications that centers members and aligns with FCFT’s branding, mission, and goals. – Seek out members’ stories and develop and promote narratives based on worker input, highlighting organizing activities and campaigns. – Bolster an affirming image of FCFT among internal and external stakeholders, while proactively combating negative anti-union or anti-public education narratives. – Coordinate with the President on messaging production and delivery and provide a monthly report to the Executive Board on meeting departmental and broader organizational goals. – Collaborate with other departments to support their communications needs as assigned. – Perform other duties as assigned. ## Required Qualifications – Minimum of five years experience in media, communications, and/or digital campaigns, ideally in labor organizing or political advocacy – Proficiency in graphic design (Photoshop, Illustrator, Canva, Adobe Express), video editing software (Adobe Premiere, Final Cut), and social media video editing (reels) – Proficiency in web development and troubleshooting (Wix, WordPress) – Highly fluent with social media platforms, trends, and content scheduling – Strong, fast, and accurate writer with an ability to center workers in messaging – Experience crafting speeches, op-eds, newsletters, and/or reports – Ability to integrate media strategy into organizing, political, or advocacy campaigns – Knowledge of local and/or digital media landscapes – Ability to work effectively with elected member leaders, staff, and community stakeholders in complex and sometimes politically sensitive environments – Ability to balance multiple projects, set priorities, and meet deadlines ## Preferred Qualifications – Familiarity with Fairfax and Virginia education and political issues – Experience working with community partners and organizations – Labor and/or Capitol Hill experience – Experience in crisis communications – Multilingual proficiency ## Salary and Benefits The starting salary range for the position is $80,000–$90,000, commensurate with experience. Benefits include paid health benefits (medical, dental, and vision); paid time off; phone stipend; and mileage and expense reimbursements. Employees are eligible to participate in the 401(k) retirement plan after six (6) months of employment; the organization will match employee contributions up to 6%. ## How to Apply Please submit here : – A cover letter describing your interest in building worker power in Fairfax County Public Schools, including examples of organizing work or campaigns you’ve contributed to (and your role in those efforts) – Your résumé – Three professional references – Three samples: one written (speech, testimony, press release, published work, etc.), one graphic design, and one video or website you’ve created At FCFT, we value a diverse, inclusive workforce, and we provide equal employment opportunities for all applicants and employees. All qualified applicants for employment will be considered without regard to an individual’s race, color, sex, gender identity, gender expression, religion, age, national origin or ancestry, citizenship, physical or mental disability, medical condition, family care status, marital status, domestic partner status, sexual orientation, genetic information, military or veteran status, or any other basis protected by federal, state, or local laws. We welcome applicants with a range of experiences and encourage you to apply, even if you don’t meet all qualifications listed. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today.
