item.title: Senior Manager, Federal Affairs
item.description: Senior Manager, Federal Affairs Organization: American Institute of Architects (AIA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 07/30/2026 **Salary Range:** $89,600 – $100,000 **Location:** Washington, DC Metro Area (Hybrid – DC, MD, VA) **Travel:** Approximately 10% The American Institute of Architects (AIA) is seeking a Senior Manager, Federal Affairs to advance the organization’s federal legislative and advocacy priorities. Reporting to the Senior Director, Federal Affairs, this position represents AIA before Congress, the Executive Branch, and national stakeholder organizations on issues affecting the architecture profession and the built environment. This is an exciting opportunity for a government affairs professional who is passionate about public policy, coalition building, and strategic advocacy to help shape federal policy on behalf of one of the nation’s leading professional associations. — ## Key Responsibilities ### Federal Advocacy – Develop and execute federal lobbying strategies that advance AIA’s legislative priorities. – Build and maintain relationships with Members of Congress, congressional staff, Executive Branch officials, and federal agencies. – Coordinate AIA’s annual Capitol Hill Day and other advocacy events. – Organize congressional meetings, policy briefings, fly-ins, and in-district engagement opportunities. – Recruit, prepare, and support AIA members as effective federal advocates. – Develop advocacy materials, testimony, issue briefs, and talking points. – Support grassroots and grasstops advocacy initiatives in collaboration with internal stakeholders. ### Policy Development – Monitor and analyze federal legislation, regulations, and administrative actions affecting architecture and the built environment. – Draft legislative language, regulatory comments, policy statements, and other advocacy documents. – Coordinate the work of AIA’s Government Advocacy Committee (GAC). – Anticipate emerging policy issues and recommend updates to AIA’s federal agenda. – Collaborate across departments and with external organizations to advance AIA’s policy objectives. ### Political Engagement (ArchiPAC) – Support ArchiPAC fundraising and political engagement activities. – Ensure compliance with lobbying, ethics, and campaign finance requirements. – Provide strategic recommendations regarding political contributions. – Represent AIA at political and fundraising events. ### Communications & Stakeholder Engagement – Brief AIA leadership on federal legislative and regulatory developments. – Develop federal affairs communications for members and external audiences. – Represent AIA at conferences, meetings, and industry events. – Coordinate partnerships with federal agencies and allied organizations. – Support rapid-response communications on federal policy developments. — ## Qualifications – Bachelor’s degree in Political Science, Public Policy, Government, or a related field required; J.D. or Master’s degree preferred. – Minimum of five (5) years of relevant professional experience in federal government relations, public policy, or advocacy. – Experience as congressional staff or an Executive Branch political appointee is strongly preferred. – Demonstrated knowledge of the federal legislative and regulatory process. – Proven success developing and implementing federal advocacy strategies. – Excellent written, verbal, analytical, and presentation skills. – Strong relationship-building, negotiation, and coalition management abilities. – Experience managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. – Proficiency with Microsoft Office and online research tools. Experience with policy issues including housing, tax, climate and resilience, federal procurement, design and construction, or equity initiatives is desirable. — ## Compensation & Benefits AIA offers a competitive salary and comprehensive benefits package, including: – Medical, dental, and vision coverage – 401(k) retirement plan – Generous paid time off – Parental leave – Flexible spending accounts – Employer-paid life and disability insurance – Tuition and professional membership reimbursement – Employee Assistance Program – Transportation benefits – Fitness discounts – Identity theft protection – Flexible hybrid work environment — ## About AIA The American Institute of Architects is committed to advancing the value of architecture and empowering architects to design a better future. Guided by principles of equity, sustainability, resilience, and community impact, AIA advocates for policies that strengthen the profession and improve the built environment for all. AIA is an equal opportunity employer and encourages applications from qualified individuals of all backgrounds, including protected veterans and individuals with disabilities. Interested applicants should apply here: ** Sr. Manager, Federal Affairs ** Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Sr. Manager, Codes and Standards Policy
item.description: Sr. Manager, Codes and Standards Policy Organization: American Institute of Architects (AIA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 07/30/2026 # The American Institute of Architects (AIA) AIA provides opportunities to advocate for the value of architecture and equips architects and design professionals with the resources they need to do their best work. The collective voice of architects is essential, and our work drives positive change through the power of design. Each one of us at AIA is a leader committed to demonstrating our mission and values and designing a better future for our country and planet. Even in times of change, AIA’s values remain constant: – We stand for equity and human rights – We stand for architecture that strengthens our communities – We stand for a sustainable future – We stand for protecting communities from the impacts of climate change – We stand for economic opportunity – We stand for investing in the future – We speak up, and policymakers listen The American Institute of Architects, as part of the global community, is building a culture of equity, diversity, and inclusion within the profession of architecture to create a better built environment for all. Achieving this vision directly impacts the relevance of the profession of architecture and the world’s prosperity, health, and future. — # Job Summary Reporting to the Senior Director, State and Local Affairs, the Senior Manager will manage and support AIA’s priorities in policy and technical areas affecting the architecture profession and the built environment. This includes engagement in building and energy code development, policy implementation at the federal, state, and local levels, and participation in inter‑industry initiatives. The Senior Manager will conduct research, analyze regulatory and policy developments, and collaborate on strategies to advance AIA member interests. This role serves as the staff liaison for assigned policy issue areas affecting state and local government affairs, with primary engagement in building and energy codes, and represents AIA on national association boards, commissions, and committees as directed by the Senior Director. Responsibilities include managing AIA policy programs through issue and program oversight, communications, and coordination with the Government Advocacy Committee, Codes and Standards Committee, Knowledge Communities, other AIA Committees, and the Chapter Network. The Senior Manager will represent AIA before federal policymakers, agencies, codes development bodies, and public forums, advocating for AIA positions and engaging with stakeholders across the built environment sector. The role also involves shaping AIA policy and positions through program management, volunteer engagement, research, outreach, education, and strategic communications. — # Job Duties – Assist the Senior Director in the development and implementation of an operating plan and budget proposal for assigned issues and program areas. – Assist with the preparation of departmental reports, including maintaining program activity logs for high‑priority projects and initiatives. – Ensure timely response and follow‑up to AIA members and leadership on issues within the Codes & Standards portfolio. — ## Committee Management – Serve as the day‑to‑day staff liaison to the AIA Codes and Standards (C&S) Committee, managing meeting logistics, agendas, action item tracking, and member communications. – Coordinate committee participation in national code development cycles (ICC, ASHRAE, NFPA), including proposal review schedules, testimony preparation, and position documentation. – Implement and track deliverables outlined in the C&S Committee Strategic Plan, including roundtables, continuing education sessions, and code article publications. – Maintain a document and resource library for committee and member use. – Develop and execute a committee member onboarding kit. — ## State and Local Adoption Support – Develop toolkits, model language, and advocacy resources that enable state and local components to advance code adoption priorities aligned with AIA’s climate, resilience, and housing policy goals. – Serve as the codes liaison to the State and Local Affairs team, ensuring that code development outcomes are translated into actionable adoption campaigns for components. – Rebuild and manage the C&S Network, recruiting 2 to 3 engaged code professionals per state component to serve as the field communication infrastructure between the national committee and local advocates. — ## Cross‑Departmental Integration – Identify and staff codes liaison connections to relevant GAC subcommittees and Knowledge Communities. – Partner with COTE, the 2030 Commitment, and other knowledge communities to ensure codes work is positioned for climate action. – Coordinate with AIA Communications to maintain an accurate, current, and member‑facing codes web presence. — ## Member Education and Advocacy – Develop and deliver member‑facing communications that clearly articulate architects’ obligations under building codes. – Coordinate three virtual roundtable sessions per year on priority code topics. – Support committee members in publishing annual code articles and delivering at least one continuing education session per year. – Identify opportunities to engage emerging professionals and academic programs on building code literacy. — # Basic Qualifications – Skilled at building and maintaining relationships with members, policymakers, and stakeholders. – Experience managing or participating in the codes and standards development process. – Experience in the legislative, policy, and federal regulatory process. – Ability to perform policy and regulatory research and analysis. – Superior organizational skills. – Sound judgment and initiative to work independently. – Commitment to producing excellent work and meeting required deadlines. – Proficient in drafting and disseminating policy‑related communications. – Experience in strategic policy analysis and government relations. – Ready to be a leader in public policy initiatives. – Demonstrated experience analyzing complex subjects quickly and providing logical presentations both orally and in writing. — # Preferred Qualifications – Experience in federal, state, and/or local government, policy, or regulatory affairs. – Experience working for federal, state, and/or local government policymakers. – Working knowledge of architecture and the design and construction industry preferred. – Ability to learn new and complicated concepts quickly and convey them to others. – Experience managing issue areas such as artificial intelligence, building codes, energy efficiency, urban/community design, residential/housing, permitting and zoning, historic preservation, and/or small business. – Experience working at an accredited standards development organization or code development organization is a plus. – Non‑profit or trade association experience. Bachelor’s degree, preferably in political science, public policy, or related field, and a minimum of 5–7 years of relevant experience. Supervisory: N/A — # What We Offer We offer a comprehensive benefits package that reflects our company values and workplace culture, including: – Medical, vision, and dental – 401(k) – Flexibility – Paid time off – Parental leave – Flexible spending accounts – Income protection (Life Insurance Coverage up to 2× salary) & disability plans at no cost – Tuition and membership reimbursements AIA employees also have access to additional programs: – Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for employees and family members – SmartBenefits transportation program (up to $55 monthly in public transportation and pretax METRO parking) – Computer purchase program – Fitness club discounts – Prepaid legal services program – Identity theft protection — # Travel Requirements 10–20% — # Work Location Hybrid from the Washington, DC metro area only (DC, MD, VA). This position will periodically be required to be on‑site at AIA Headquarters in Washington, DC. — # Equal Opportunity Statement Equal opportunity employer as to all protected groups, including protected veterans and individuals with disabilities. item.title: Director, Government Affairs Programs & Communications
item.description: Director, Government Affairs Programs & Communications Organization: American Institute of Architects (AIA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 07/30/2026 **Director, Government Affairs Programs & Communications** **Salary Range:** $115,000 – $120,000 **Location:** Hybrid (Washington, DC Metro Area – DC, MD, VA) **Travel:** Approximately 10% **Shape the Future of Advocacy for the Architecture Profession** The American Institute of Architects (AIA) is seeking a strategic, collaborative Director of Programs & Communications to help grow and strengthen our national government affairs and member advocacy programs. Reporting to the Managing Director of Government Affairs, this position serves as the critical link between Government Affairs, Communications, and AIA members. The Director will lead advocacy communications, member engagement initiatives, and cross-functional programs that expand architect participation in public policy and strengthen AIA’s advocacy infrastructure nationwide. This is an outstanding opportunity for an experienced public affairs, advocacy, or communications professional who thrives at the intersection of policy, strategic communications, member engagement, and organizational leadership. — **About AIA** The American Institute of Architects is dedicated to advancing the value of architecture and empowering architects to design a better future. Our advocacy priorities are grounded in our commitment to: – Equity and human rights – Strong, resilient communities – Sustainability and climate action – Economic opportunity – Investing in the future of the profession – Effective public policy advocacy AIA is committed to fostering a culture of equity, diversity, and inclusion that strengthens both the profession and the built environment. — **Key Responsibilities** **Member Engagement & Advocacy** – Develop and lead AIA’s national Government Affairs Member Engagement Program. – Design scalable advocacy pathways that increase member participation. – Create advocacy training, leadership development programs, webinars, and toolkits. – Partner with state and local components to strengthen advocacy capacity. – Measure engagement and continuously improve program effectiveness. **Strategic Communications** – Serve as the primary liaison between Government Affairs and Communications. – Translate complex legislative and policy issues into compelling communications. – Develop advocacy messaging across digital, print, and executive communications. – Manage Government Affairs’ website content, newsletters, and social media strategy. – Support rapid-response communications on emerging policy issues. **Advocacy Campaigns** – Lead member-facing advocacy campaigns and communications. – Manage action alerts and digital advocacy campaigns through Quorum and related platforms. – Coordinate communications supporting Hill Day, Leadership Summit, fly-ins, and legislative priorities. – Ensure messaging aligns with AIA policy positions and strategic objectives. **Cross-Functional Leadership** – Coordinate projects across Government Affairs, Communications, Member Relations, Public Policy, State & Local Affairs, and other AIA teams. – Support departmental planning, project management, and operational improvements. – Represent Government Affairs internally and externally as appropriate. — **Qualifications** Successful candidates will bring: – Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Public Policy, Political Science, Public Administration, Marketing, Nonprofit Management, or a related field. – Seven or more years of progressively responsible experience in government affairs, advocacy, communications, membership, nonprofit management, public affairs, or related fields. – Experience developing advocacy campaigns, communications strategies, or member engagement programs. – Strong understanding of public policy and government affairs. – Exceptional writing, presentation, and relationship-building skills. – Experience managing complex, cross-functional initiatives. – Familiarity with advocacy platforms such as Quorum is preferred. – Strong project management skills; PMP certification or equivalent experience is a plus. — **Why Join AIA?** AIA offers a collaborative, mission-driven environment where your work directly supports architects and strengthens communities nationwide. **Our comprehensive benefits include:** – Medical and dental insurance – 401(k) – Generous paid time off – Flexible hybrid work environment – Paid parental leave – Flexible spending accounts – Employer-paid life and disability insurance – Tuition and professional membership reimbursement – Employee Assistance Program – Transportation benefits – Fitness discounts – Identity theft protection – Prepaid legal services — **Work Location** This hybrid position is open to candidates located in the Washington, DC metropolitan area (DC, Maryland, or Virginia). Periodic onsite work at AIA Headquarters in Washington, DC, is required. The American Institute of Architects is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds, including protected veterans and individuals with disabilities. Location: Dallas, TX Date Posted: 07/30/2026 General Summary Working under the direction of the Director of Business Development + Marketing and the Chief Business Development + Marketing Officer, the Marketing Communications Manager will develop and coordinate the Firm’s external and internal communications strategy to strengthen brand visibility, thought leadership, and attorney engagement. This role contributes to content creation across all platforms—including press releases, blogs, social media, website, newsletters, and advertisements—and works closely with attorneys to amplify their expertise. The ideal candidate is a strong writer, proactive communicator, and strategic storyteller who thrives in a fast-paced professional services environment. Essential Duties and Responsibilities Public Relations: Monitor opportunities for attorneys to serve as expert resources and thought leaders. Prepare and edit press releases regarding Firm updates and news to proactively communicate successes to the media. Media Monitoring + Pitch Support: Monitor relevant legal, business, and industry news to identify opportunities for attorney commentary, media outreach, and timely client-facing content. Social Media + Website: Promote Firm news, events, and successes across various social media platforms, and assist attorneys in developing personal profiles that align with the Firm’s messaging. Approve and edit social media posts in scheduling platforms. Blogs + Newsletters: Coordinate the production and distribution of multiple external newsletters and blogs for various practice groups, balancing distinct timelines and managing cross-team collaboration effectively. Internal Communications: Create and distribute internal communications on behalf of the Firm, including the Firmwide monthly newsletter and Firmwide communications regarding events, conferences, news, and awards. New Content Development: Create, edit, and contribute ideas for a wide range of content, including Firm news, award announcements, speaking engagements, and case highlights. Survey + Award Submissions: Coordinate award and ranking submissions, including collaborating with the Business Development team on Chambers USA submissions. Prepare timely attorney award submissions and communicate deadlines. Adhere to Firm policies and procedures as outlined in the Firm Handbooks. Education and Experience Required Bachelor’s degree, preferably in English, Marketing, Communications, or a related field. 5+ years of relevant experience in a law firm, professional services, or media environment. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Required Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Outlook, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint). Knowledge of Adobe Creative Suite, Adobe InDesign, Illustrator, Canva, and Photoshop is a plus. Excellent writing and proofreading skills with exceptional attention to detail. Must live in the Dallas area (no relocation offered and no fully remote work). Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to build relationships with a wide range of individuals with diverse personalities. Ability to complete projects with minimal supervision and effectively manage multiple priorities. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Senior Product Manager – Advertising Data Platforms Compliance
item.description: Senior Product Manager – Advertising Data Platforms Compliance Organization: Warner Bros. Discovery Location: Burbank, CA | Bellevue, WA | Culver City, CA Date Posted: 07/30/2026 Welcome to Warner Bros. Discovery… the stuff dreams are made of. Who We Are When we say, “the stuff dreams are made of,” we’re not just referring to the world of wizards, dragons and superheroes, or even to the wonders of Planet Earth. Behind WBD’s vast portfolio of iconic content and beloved brands are the storytellers bringing our characters to life, the creators bringing them to your living rooms, and the dreamers creating what’s next. From brilliant creatives to technology trailblazers across the globe, WBD offers career-defining opportunities, thoughtfully curated benefits, and the tools to explore and grow into your best selves. Here you are supported, here you are celebrated, and here you can thrive. At HBO Max, storytelling takes center stage. We’re one of the world’s most iconic entertainment brands—home to bold originals and unforgettable characters. While audiences binge award-winning content, breaking news, and sports around the clock, our teams stay busy creating what’s next in streaming. From Succession , Euphoria , and The Sopranos to global franchises like Game of Thrones and Harry Potter , our content sparks conversation and shapes culture. HBO Max delivers boundary-pushing stories across genres and platforms, connecting millions of viewers across 90 countries globally—and we’re just getting started. We’re home to the most talked-about shows and movies, granting audiences access to the worlds of HBO, Harry Potter, DC, Warner Bros., ID, Adult Swim, A24, and more. Turn your streaming obsession into a career—we’re hiring! Your New Role We are looking for a passionate and driven Senior Product Manager to join the DTC Data Product Compliance team. In this role, you will report to the Sr. Director of Privacy, Data Product Compliance. You will work cross-functionally within the Product & Design organization across multiple product verticals, including engineering, legal, data science, and analytics, with a focus on privacy-preserving advertising platforms and technical frameworks. You will define scalable solutions that integrate across WBD’s DTC platforms, supporting a wide range of advertising partners, internal stakeholders, and data use cases. You will be motivated to dive deep into the rapidly evolving technology landscape, changing regulatory environment, and legal nuances across multiple global regions where we operate. We value product management that drives with discipline and attention to detail. You’re a good fit for this role if you are customer-obsessed, collaborative, and data-driven. You are a highly effective communicator who can build trust with all areas of the business. You must be comfortable regularly engaging with executive leadership to effectively communicate governance and compliance requirements and secure alignment on product roadmap priorities. You can work autonomously, have strong organizational and analytical skills, and are a proven collaborator and problem solver. Your Role Accountabilities Own the product vision and execution for large-scale, privacy-preserving advertising workflows powered by data clean rooms, including advertiser first-party data onboarding, identity matching against our first-party datasets, audience creation and activation, and attribution and measurement across the modern ad tech ecosystem. Partner with engineering and advertising teams to design and ship scalable, standardized, privacy-preserving solutions that operate within clean room and signal-restricted environments, delivering products that meet the needs of advertisers, agencies, third-party measurement vendors, and other ad tech providers. Provide product expertise and thought leadership in the areas of backend data compliance and privacy, with an understanding of how regulations and partner requirements impact and influence the use of data across various business processes and functions. Gather, define, and clearly document data use cases through partnership with stakeholders, including Data Platform Engineering, Data Science (ML/AI), Advertising, Marketing, Analytics, Experimentation, Research, and Fraud & Abuse. Operate well in the face of ambiguity and imperfect knowledge, drilling into business data and research results to identify clear direction and focus. Stay informed on the latest industry trends, emerging technologies, and advancements in data handling to assess their impact on maintaining compliance and their potential for novel privacy solutions. Cultivate and maintain strong relationships with key stakeholders across the business to enable customer-focused features with a “privacy by design” approach. Promote a culture of privacy awareness and compliance throughout the organization. Build healthy, trusting relationships and contribute to a culture of respect by giving feedback respectfully, exchanging ideas openly, and receiving feedback humbly. Qualifications & Experience 5+ years of backend/platform Product Management experience within a technology or digital organization. 2+ years of experience with technical frameworks in the digital advertising ecosystem. Strong knowledge of privacy and compliance for consumer data used in the advertising space. Built and delivered a roadmap for data clean room and advertising measurement products by evaluating build-versus-buy options. Experience collaborating with data clean room providers, ad measurement providers, advertisers, and agencies. Proficiency in analyzing technical architecture diagrams and creating data flows. Experience partnering with technical teams on highly complex projects. Commitment to fostering an inclusive team culture built on empathy. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a focus on documentation that communicates complex subject matter simply and clearly. Proven ability to partner effectively with stakeholders across legal, product, and engineering functions. Excellent problem-solving, critical thinking, and analytical skills. Detail-oriented, self-starter, accountable, and empowered. Curiosity and a willingness to learn. How We Get Things Done This last bit is probably the most important! Here at WBD, our guiding principles are the core values by which we operate and are central to how we get things done. You can find them at www.wbd.com/guiding-principles/ along with insights from the team on what they mean and how they show up in their day-to-day work. We hope they resonate with you and look forward to discussing them during your interview. Championing Inclusion at WBD Warner Bros. Discovery embraces the opportunity to build a workforce that reflects a wide array of perspectives, backgrounds, and experiences. Being an equal opportunity employer means that we take seriously our responsibility to consider qualified candidates on the basis of merit, without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, mental or physical disability, genetic information, marital status, citizenship status, military status, protected veteran status, or any other category protected by law. If you’re a qualified candidate with a disability and require adjustments or accommodations during the job application and/or recruitment process, please visit our accessibility page for instructions on how to submit your request. Compensation & Benefits In compliance with local law, we are disclosing the compensation, or a range thereof, for roles in locations where legally required. Actual salaries will vary based on several factors, including but not limited to external market data, internal equity, location, skill set, experience, and/or performance. Base pay is just one component of Warner Bros. Discovery’s total compensation package for employees. Pay Range: $119,000.00 – $221,000.00 per year. Other rewards may include annual bonuses, short- and long-term incentives, and program-specific awards. In addition, Warner Bros. Discovery provides a variety of benefits to employees, including health insurance coverage, an employee wellness program, life and disability insurance, a retirement savings plan, paid holidays, sick time, and vacation. If you’re a qualified candidate with an arrest or conviction record, please know that your application will be considered in accordance with the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers and the California Fair Chance Act. item.title: State Government Relations Director
item.description: State Government Relations Director Organization: American Heart Association (AHA) Location: Salt Lake City, UT Date Posted: 07/30/2026 Overview Since our founding in 1924, we’ve cut cardiovascular disease deaths in half, but there is still so much more to do. To overcome today’s biggest health challenges and accelerate this progress, we need passionate individuals like you. Join our movement, be part of the progress, and help ensure a healthier future for all. You matter, and so does the impact you can make with us. The American Heart Association has an excellent opportunity for a State Government Relations Director . Location Requirement: In order to be considered for this role, you are required to live in the state and be within commuting distance of the State Capital. Location: Salt Lake City, UT The State Government Relations Director is responsible for serving as the primary representative of the American Heart Association to the assigned state legislature, state agencies, and local governments, generating awareness and support for the American Heart Association’s public policy agenda. This role strategically coordinates and leads efforts to advance the Association’s state public policy priorities. The Director works closely with American Heart Association staff, volunteers, coalitions, and partner organizations to build support for policy initiatives and integrate advocacy messaging into relevant Association programs and events. The Association offers many resources to help you maintain work-life harmonization through your changing needs and life situations. To help you be successful, you will have access to Heart U, our award-winning corporate university, along with additional local training and support. #TheAHALife is more than a company culture—it is our way of life. It embodies our commitment to work-life harmonization and is guided by our core values, allowing employees to thrive both personally and professionally. Discover why you will Be Seen. Be Heard. Be Valued. by following the American Heart Association on LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, and at heart.jobs. Responsibilities Meet one-on-one with members of the state legislature, legislative staff, and other state and local government officials to gain support for the American Heart Association’s advocacy priorities. Monitor and engage on state and local legislative and regulatory issues affecting the American Heart Association and keep volunteers and staff informed of emerging advocacy issues. Provide policy research, develop support materials, recruit spokespersons, prepare testimony, and perform other activities needed to advance the Association’s legislative agenda. Participate in coalition-building efforts and collaborative partnerships that advance the American Heart Association’s advocacy priorities. Recruit members for volunteer state advocacy committees and provide ongoing staff support. Collaborate with committees to develop an annual legislative agenda. Provide strategic direction for statewide grassroots and key contact recruitment, retention, and mobilization efforts. Provide strategic direction and support materials for state lobby days and local in-district meetings. Collaborate with communications staff on the development and timing of media advocacy efforts. Prepare required reporting information, including local, state, and federal lobbying reports and other required documentation. Provide advocacy presentations and training opportunities for volunteers and staff as needed. Attend and participate in relevant American Heart Association meetings throughout the year, including national and affiliate staff training, affiliate and state-level meetings, and metro board meetings. Represent the organization in public settings, including legislative convenings and media interviews. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Public Policy, Political Science, Law, a related field, or equivalent work experience. Three (3) years of successful legislative and regulatory lobbying experience. Three (3) years of demonstrated experience building and managing issue advocacy coalitions. Three (3) years of experience developing and implementing grassroots and media advocacy strategies. Outstanding oral and written communication skills. Strong policy analysis and legislative/regulatory writing skills. Ability to simultaneously manage multiple complex projects in various stages of development while meeting deadlines. Knowledge of strategic planning, budgeting, and work management principles. Knowledge of state legislative and regulatory processes. Preferred Qualifications Knowledge of voluntary health organizations or nonprofit organizations. Experience working in health care policy. Experience in volunteer management. Understanding and appreciation for technology and information systems. Experience managing contract employees. Compensation & Benefits The expected pay range for this position is $79,000–$95,000 . Compensation is commensurate with experience, and geographic pay differentials may apply. The American Heart Association reserves the right to pay above or below the posted range. The American Heart Association invests in its people through a comprehensive total rewards package. Compensation: Competitive base salary with regular market reviews and salary adjustments as appropriate. Performance & Recognition: Annual salary planning and incentive programs based on position type and individual performance. Benefits: Comprehensive medical, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance coverage, plus a robust retirement program with employer matching and automatic contributions. Employees also receive access to an Employee Assistance Program (EAP), wellness program, telemedicine, and medical consultation services. Professional Development: Opportunities to participate in Employee Resource Groups (ERGs), professional mentoring programs, and Heart U, the Association’s online learning platform offering more than 100,000 educational resources. Work-Life Harmonization: New employees receive a minimum of 16 days of Paid Time Off (PTO) annually, increasing with seniority. Employees also receive 12 paid holidays each year, including several days off at the end of the year. Tuition Assistance: Financial support is available for employees pursuing education related to their current responsibilities or future career opportunities within the organization. About the American Heart Association The American Heart Association’s 2028 Goal is to build on more than 100 years of trusted leadership in cardiovascular and brain health by driving breakthroughs and implementing proven solutions in science, policy, and care to create healthier people and communities. The Association is committed to ensuring that the greatest discoveries in health reach everyone, wherever they are. At the American Heart Association and American Stroke Association, our mission is to be a relentless force for a world of longer, healthier lives, regardless of race, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, religion, age, language, sexual orientation, national origin, or physical or cognitive abilities. Additional Information In accordance with applicable local and state laws, qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment. item.title: Senior Public Information Representative
item.description: Senior Public Information Representative Organization: University of California San Francisco (UCSF) Location: San Francisco,CA | Oakland, CA Date Posted: 07/30/2026 Job Description Job Summary Please note that this is a hybrid role requiring regular in-person attendance in both San Francisco and Oakland. The position requires onsite work three days per week. Salary Range: $101,300–$216,700 UC San Francisco (UCSF) Public Affairs seeks a seasoned health and science communicator and collaborative team member to join our team as a Senior Public Information Representative (SPIR) supporting UCSF Benioff Children’s Hospitals (BCH). UCSF is one of the world’s leading health sciences universities, with top-ranked programs in biomedical research, education, and clinical care. UCSF Health, including UCSF Benioff Children’s Hospitals in San Francisco and Oakland, is nationally recognized for excellence in pediatric care and its commitment to serving diverse and underserved communities. The SPIR plays a key strategic role in advancing BCH’s reputation and visibility by developing and leading proactive media relations strategies and comprehensive communications campaigns. This individual identifies high-impact storytelling opportunities aligned with institutional priorities and ensures consistent, strategic positioning across earned and owned media channels. The SPIR serves as a trusted advisor to faculty, clinicians, and senior leadership, providing counsel on media engagement, message development, and reputational risk. This includes preparing spokespeople for media interactions and advising on communications approaches for complex or sensitive issues. This role requires a high degree of independence and judgment. The SPIR anticipates emerging issues, evaluates reputational opportunities and risks, and develops proactive communications strategies to address them. The individual collaborates across UCSF Public Affairs, Marketing, Health Communications, and other internal teams to align messaging and maximize impact. The SPIR communicates through a range of formats, including news releases, feature stories, media pitches, talking points, and multimedia content, translating complex medical and scientific information into clear, compelling language for diverse audiences. The Office of Communications actively supports UCSF’s PRIDE Values of Professionalism, Respect, Integrity, Diversity & Excellence. Candidates representing California’s diverse communities are encouraged to apply. Department Summary As UCSF’s enterprise communications team, the Office of Communications (OC) provides comprehensive and coordinated leadership in planning, creating, and implementing integrated strategies across all media to foster increased awareness and support of UCSF’s mission, vision, accomplishments, and strategic priorities among its diverse internal and external constituencies. Its Public Affairs team serves as the official voice of UCSF to regional, state, national, and international news media. UCSF Public Affairs is dedicated to supporting UCSF’s enterprise strategic goals and communicating UCSF’s excellence across the breadth of its mission through traditional and evolving news media, as well as our own channels. The team serves as the front line for media and as the primary external communications liaison with UCSF’s approximately 3,900 faculty members, with responsibility for managing those relationships and guiding them in promoting their work. Public Affairs is a dynamic and collaborative team made up of bright, talented, motivated colleagues who bring a variety of communications skills to their roles and provide significant support to one another. Qualifications Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in a related field. Minimum of 5 years of relevant experience in media relations, journalism, or strategic communications. Experience using digital and social media platforms to amplify communications efforts. Experience managing complex, high-visibility communications initiatives. Advanced knowledge of media communications, media relations, and strategic communications planning. Demonstrated success developing and executing communications strategies with measurable outcomes. Advanced verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills. Advanced judgment, analytical, and decision-making skills, including navigating sensitive issues. Ability to advise senior leadership and influence communications strategy. Strong organizational and project management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities. Ability to work independently with a high degree of autonomy. Preferred Qualifications Master’s degree or equivalent experience. Established network of national and regional media contacts. About UCSF The University of California, San Francisco (UCSF) is a leading university dedicated to promoting health worldwide through advanced biomedical research, graduate-level education in the life sciences and health professions, and excellence in patient care. It is the only campus in the 10-campus University of California system dedicated exclusively to the health sciences. We bring together the world’s leading experts in nearly every area of health and are home to five Nobel laureates who have advanced the understanding of cancer, neurodegenerative diseases, aging, and stem cells. PRIDE Values UCSF is a diverse community made up of people with many skills and talents. We seek candidates whose work experience or community service has prepared them to contribute to our commitment to Professionalism, Respect, Integrity, Diversity, and Excellence. Learn more about UCSF’s mission and values: https://www.ucsf.edu/about/mission-and-values UCSF is committed to equity in both how we deliver care and how we build our workforce. We are committed to fostering a broadly diverse community, nurturing a welcoming and supportive culture, and embracing diverse ideas to provide culturally competent education, discovery, and patient care. Additional information about diversity at UCSF is available at: https://diversity.ucsf.edu/ Join us to build a rewarding career while contributing to improving healthcare worldwide. EEO Statement The University of California is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, age, protected veteran status, or any other protected status under state or federal law. item.title: Policy Manager
item.description: Policy Manager Organization: The Sequoia Project Location: Remote Date Posted: 07/31/2026 Starting Salary: $97,000 – $116,000 depending on experience Position Summary The Policy Manager plays a key role in advancing The Sequoia Project’s mission by developing, refining, and maintaining policy documents that support organizational initiatives and strategic objectives. This role supports the end-to-end policy development process, including policy research, drafting, iterative revision, analysis of reviewer feedback, and production of high-quality final documents. Additionally, this position ensures effective execution of organizational strategy and priorities related to policy, in collaboration with the Director of Policy and Governance. Working with subject matter experts and organizational leadership, the Policy Manager evaluates proposed revisions, researches policy issues, analyzes reviewer feedback, and develops recommendations that improve the quality, clarity, and consistency of trust framework policies. This position requires exceptional analytical thinking, superior writing and editing skills, sound judgment, and the ability to manage multiple complex policy initiatives simultaneously. What is The Sequoia Project? The Sequoia Project is a non-profit with a public service mission to lead in an interoperable health information sharing ecosystem to improve the health and welfare of people in the United States. The Trust Framework Team supports public and private-sector-led trust framework programs by providing leadership and support for policy, governance, technical, operational, and stakeholder engagement efforts. Essential Functions Policy Development Research industry trends, regulations, standards, and organizational priorities to support policy development and updates. Draft new policies, guidance documents, white papers, implementation guidance, and supporting materials. Analyze existing policies to identify opportunities for clarification, improvement, modernization, and consistency. Research policy issues and develop recommendations that improve policy clarity, consistency, and effectiveness. Ensure policy documents are logically organized, internally consistent, and aligned with organizational objectives. Policy Review & Iteration Lead multiple iterative review cycles for policy documents from initial draft through final publication. Collect, organize, track, and analyze reviewer comments to identify common themes, conflicting recommendations, and areas requiring clarification. Review proposed revisions and recommend changes that improve clarity, consistency, and alignment with policy objectives. Incorporate approved revisions into successive policy drafts while maintaining document integrity and consistency. Prepare comment disposition logs and documentation describing how feedback was addressed. Maintain comprehensive documentation of revisions, comment resolution, and policy evolution throughout the drafting process. Manage document version control and ensure publication-ready quality. Research & Documentation Conduct policy and industry research to support policy development and document revisions. Monitor changes in industry practices, regulations, and organizational priorities that may require policy updates. Prepare policy briefs, executive summaries, issue analyses, FAQs, and supporting documentation. Ensure all policy documents are accurate, well-written, and supported by appropriate references. Policy Management Support multiple policy initiatives simultaneously while maintaining project schedules and document milestones. Maintain organized repositories of policy documents, supporting research, revision history, and published materials. Coordinate document reviews and ensure timely completion of revision cycles. Support publication and ongoing maintenance of organizational policy documents. Strategic Initiatives Support special projects and strategic initiatives, including research, planning, and implementation support, as requested. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Excellent analytical, research, and critical thinking skills, including the ability to synthesize complex information into clear insights, recommendations, and actionable materials. Excellent communication skills, including the ability to communicate complex policy topics to diverse audiences. Exceptional writing, editing, and proofreading skills. Strong organizational and project management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously. Strong knowledge of healthcare interoperability, health IT, HIE, trust frameworks, and/or related policy environments, preferred. Strong understanding of federal and state legislative, regulatory, and policy development processes impacting interoperability and health information exchange, preferred. Ability to work independently with sound judgment while contributing effectively within a collaborative and mission-driven organization. Proficiency in Microsoft 365 Suite, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, and SharePoint. Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Word, including document formatting, styles, tracked changes, and document comparison. Education, Training, and Experience Bachelor’s degree in public policy, public health, political science, healthcare administration, health informatics, law, English communications, or a related field required; Master’s degree preferred. 5–7 years of progressively responsible experience developing, analyzing, or managing policy, technical, regulatory, or operational documentation. Experience managing complex document review cycles involving multiple revisions. Experience in healthcare, health information technology, interoperability, standards development, or a related field, preferred. Experience developing policy guidance, implementation guidance, technical documentation, or issue briefs, preferred. Experience working with complex technical or regulatory subject matter, preferred. Physical and Mental Requirements Ability to work on a computer for extended periods of time, including typing and working on a computer monitor. Ability to stand or sit for extended periods of time. Extended working hours and travel may be necessary. Occasional lifting of 15 to 20 lbs. Work Authorization Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. The Sequoia Project does not provide visa sponsorship or facilitate employment-based immigration processes (e.g., H-1B, OPT, CPT, or other work visas). Candidates must have valid work authorization that does not require employer sponsorship, either now or in the future. Equal Employment Opportunity All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religious creed, national origin, ancestry, citizenship status, age, sex or gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, and related medical conditions), gender identity or expression (including transgender status), sexual orientation, marital status, military service and veteran status, physical or mental disability, protected medical condition as defined by applicable state or local law (such as cancer), genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws and ordinances. item.title: Director, Legal Policy, Governance, and Compliance
item.description: Director, Legal Policy, Governance, and Compliance Organization: The Sequoia Project Location: Remote Date Posted: 07/31/2026 Starting Salary Range $210,000 – $250,000 , depending on experience. Position Summary The Director, Policy, Governance, and Compliance is responsible for directing the development, interpretation, and oversight of policy, governance, and compliance frameworks supporting the Trusted Exchange Framework and Common Agreement (TEFCA) and other programs of The Sequoia Project. This role ensures that policies and governance structures enable trusted, scalable, and compliant health information exchange among health information networks. The Director serves as a senior advisor to executive leadership on policy, governance, and regulatory alignment, ensuring consistency with the TEFCA Common Agreement and applicable federal requirements. This position translates complex legal, regulatory, and programmatic requirements into clear, enforceable policy and governance frameworks and provides oversight to the legal and compliance team to ensure adherence across the network. This role is distinct from operational functions and focuses on policy development, governance execution, and compliance oversight in coordination with operational teams. This position operates in a collaborative, mission-driven environment supporting national health information exchange through TEFCA and other programs. The role works closely with governance bodies, executive leadership, and internal teams to ensure policies are effectively developed, maintained, and enforced. What is The Sequoia Project? The Sequoia Project is a nonprofit with a public service mission to lead an interoperable health information sharing ecosystem that improves the health and welfare of people in the United States. The Trust Framework Team supports public- and private-sector trust framework programs by providing leadership and support for policy, governance, technical, operational, and stakeholder engagement efforts. Functional Responsibilities Policy Leadership and Strategy Direct the development, refinement, and lifecycle management of standard operating policies, procedures, and governance artifacts for TEFCA and other programs. Interpret the TEFCA Common Agreement and associated materials to ensure consistent and authoritative application. Monitor federal and state policy and regulatory developments and assess implications for TEFCA and related interoperability initiatives. Provide strategic recommendations to executive leadership on policy direction, governance priorities, and areas of risk. TEFCA Governance and Governing Bodies Establish, support, and oversee governance structures required under TEFCA, including committees, workgroups, and decision-making bodies. Develop and maintain charters, governance processes, and decision frameworks to ensure transparency, consistency, and accountability. Provide policy guidance and support to governing bodies to enable informed and timely decision-making. Ensure governance processes align with the Common Agreement and are consistently applied across the network. Compliance and Oversight Lead the development and oversight of the legal and compliance team regarding compliance frameworks supporting TEFCA policy adherence. Define and maintain policy interpretation processes to ensure consistent application across Qualified Health Information Networks (QHINs) and related entities. Support governance processes related to compliance determinations, issue escalation, and policy enforcement. Partner with internal teams to ensure appropriate alignment between policy requirements and compliance monitoring activities. Legal and Regulatory Alignment Apply legal and regulatory expertise to inform policy development and governance structures, including interpretation of agreements and program requirements. Work closely with General Counsel to ensure policies are legally sound, enforceable, and aligned with risk management strategies. Support the development, maintenance, and interpretation of governance documents, agreements, and policy frameworks. Governance for Other Programs Direct the development and maintenance of policy and governance frameworks for additional programs as appropriate. Ensure alignment and consistency of governance approaches across programs where applicable. Establish governance processes that are transparent, enforceable, and aligned with program objectives and contractual requirements. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Strong understanding of health IT interoperability, including governance, policy, and compliance considerations for nationwide exchange. Deep familiarity with TEFCA, the Common Agreement, and governance models supporting trust frameworks preferred. Familiarity with applicable standards such as FHIR and USCDI preferred. Ability to translate complex legal, contractual, and regulatory requirements into clear, enforceable policy and governance frameworks. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to support executive- and governance-level decision-making. Demonstrated ability to lead and influence across teams while maintaining clear boundaries between policy, governance, and operations. Strategic thinker with the ability to balance policy intent, regulatory requirements, and practical implementation considerations. Education, Training, and Experience Bachelor’s degree required; Juris Doctor (JD) or equivalent legal training strongly preferred. 10+ years of experience in health policy, governance, regulatory affairs, compliance, or health IT interoperability. Demonstrated experience working with national interoperability frameworks, including TEFCA, health information networks, or similar trust frameworks. Experience interpreting and applying legal agreements, regulatory requirements, and governance frameworks. Proven ability to lead complex policy, governance, and compliance initiatives in a regulated environment. Physical and Mental Requirements Ability to work on a computer for extended periods of time, including typing and working at a computer monitor. Ability to stand or sit for extended periods of time. Extended working hours and travel may be necessary (approximately 10%). Occasional lifting of 15 to 20 pounds. Work Authorization Requirements Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. The Sequoia Project does not provide visa sponsorship or facilitate employment-based immigration processes (e.g., H-1B, OPT, CPT, or other work visas). Candidates must have valid work authorization that does not require employer sponsorship, either now or in the future. Equal Employment Opportunity All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religious creed, national origin, ancestry, citizenship status, age, sex or gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, and related medical conditions), gender identity or expression (including transgender status), sexual orientation, marital status, military service and veteran status, physical or mental disability, protected medical condition as defined by applicable state or local law (such as cancer), genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law. item.title: Policy Research Associate
item.description: Policy Research Associate Organization: QED-C®, the Quantum Economic Development Consortium Location: Arlington, VA Date Posted: 07/31/2026 About the Job QED-C®, the Quantum Economic Development Consortium, seeks an intellectually sophisticated and analytically rigorous Policy Research Associate to develop and contribute to a portfolio of projects at the intersection of technology policy, scholarship, and practice. QED-C is an industry association with the mission to grow the quantum economy through community-building and collaboration. QED-C serves member organizations operating in more than 20 countries. CHECK OUT QED-C! The portfolio includes member-funded and externally funded research and policy initiatives. The Policy Research Associate will conduct research that informs policy, strategy, and decision-making on issues of interest to the quantum industry and will work a hybrid schedule from the SRI International office in Arlington, VA. The Policy Research Associate, working closely with QED-C management and volunteer leadership in a dynamic research environment that values intellectual rigor, perspective on emerging challenges, and collaboration, will apply sophisticated methodologies, including quantitative and qualitative techniques, to develop findings and recommendations and convey them in a variety of formats. This position reports to the QED-C Deputy Director. You will also contribute to proposal efforts to promote the development and sustainability of QED-C’s research portfolio. Responsibilities Success in this role requires intellectual versatility, methodological rigor, and the ability to translate complex findings into actionable insights for policymakers, sponsors, and other audiences. Contribute substantively to the conception, development, and dissemination of research and policy analysis. Support a portfolio of projects by conducting rigorous inquiry, producing high-quality and persuasive written analyses, engaging with stakeholders, and assisting in the development and stewardship of externally funded research awards. Lead the production of a wide range of research products, including policy briefs, technical reports, white papers, journal articles, presentations, sponsor deliverables, and executive-level briefing materials. Undertake original research on issues of strategic importance, including identifying and evaluating relevant sources, conducting literature reviews, collecting and analyzing data, monitoring developments in relevant policy and technology domains, and synthesizing findings and recommendations. Exercise independent judgment in framing research questions, assessing evidence, and identifying implications for policy and practice. Produce near-final publication, presentation, and proposal drafts that require minimal rework. Support interviews and convenings designed to advance research objectives and inform policy discussions by preparing background materials, summarizing discussions, capturing key insights, and cultivating productive relationships with collaborators and sponsors. Contribute to the development and sustainability of QED-C’s research portfolio. Assist with proposal development by conducting background research for funding opportunities, preparing supporting materials for sponsor engagement, and contributing to the articulation of future research directions. Translate ambiguous needs into structured work plans, clear research questions, and appropriate methodologies. Proactively communicate risks and recommend mitigations to QED-C management. Support the dissemination and public impact of the institution’s work, including assisting with presentations, marketing, and outreach activities designed to extend the reach and influence of research findings. Represent the organization in professional settings, as needed. Qualifications Application Requirement: Applicants must submit a cover letter and a list of publications demonstrating relevant work in academic, governmental, nonprofit, consulting, or industry settings. These may be submitted with the resume or as a separate attachment. Master’s degree in Economics, Science & Technology Studies, International Relations, Security Studies, or a related interdisciplinary field bridging technology and policy. Experience selecting and implementing quantitative and qualitative methods to answer policy questions. Demonstrated written and verbal communication skills with the ability to inform and persuade diverse audiences, including executives. Ability to travel occasionally to QED-C and closely related meetings. Ability to work a hybrid schedule from the SRI office in Arlington, VA. Preferred Qualifications Demonstrated interest in addressing real-world technology policy challenges and familiarity with proposal development activities. Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple concurrent workstreams. Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a project-based research environment with multiple stakeholders and evolving priorities while conducting independent analysis. Experience employing quantitative analytical tools and methods, including statistical analysis, econometrics, data visualization, or computational research techniques. Experience mentoring junior staff and coordinating contributions across multidisciplinary teams. Familiarity with policy analysis frameworks and applied research methodologies. Writing samples will be requested during the interview process. Salary and Benefits Salary Range: $63,873–$84,636 annually. Salary ranges vary based on factors including geographic location, market competitiveness, and internal equity among employees in similar roles. Positions may also qualify for SRI’s Pay for Outstanding Performance program or the annual Performance Based Compensation program. SRI offers a competitive benefits package. Details are available at: https://www.sri.com/resources/benefits/ . SRI will accept applications until the position is filled. About SRI SRI is an independent nonprofit research institute headquartered in Menlo Park, California, with a rich history of supporting government and industry. We create and deliver world-changing solutions for a safer, healthier, and more sustainable future. For more than 75 years, SRI has collaborated across technical and scientific disciplines to discover and develop groundbreaking products and technologies, bringing innovations and ideas to the marketplace. item.title: Federal Health Policy Manager or Director
item.description: Federal Health Policy Manager or Director Organization: National Center for Health Research (NCHR) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 07/31/2026 About the Job Before applying, please take the time to carefully read the job description. Applicants must be based in the Washington, D.C., area, must have the federal policy experience described below, and must submit a resume and cover letter by email to [email protected] following the instructions in the job description below. Incomplete applications or candidates who do not have the required experience will not be considered. This is a terrific opportunity for a former Capitol Hill staffer, or someone who has worked effectively with Capitol Hill staff, who wants to influence health policy and the quality of medical care while working more reasonable hours than are typical of the Hill. Must have experience working on Capitol Hill in Washington, DC, or directly with Hill policy staff. Excellent oral and written communication skills are also required. The successful candidate will have at least 2 years of experience working on Capitol Hill on health issues, preferably with HELP, Finance, Ways and Means, or Energy & Commerce staff, and will have an educational background that includes knowledge of medicine, healthcare, health policy, or public health. Apply now for a position starting in August, September, or October. Send a resume or c.v. and cover letter explaining how your experience fits with our work and this job description, and including your available start date and salary requirements to Ava at [email protected] . The title of Manager or Director and salary will depend on expertise and experience. Make a Difference The National Center for Health Research (NCHR) has a national reputation for influencing healthcare quality, patient safety, and the use of scientific evidence in policy decisions to prevent and treat the health problems that affect our lives. The Health Policy Manager or Director will work with Capitol Hill staff and federal agency officials to shape how research evidence informs laws and regulations, federal agency decision-making, and public understanding of the impact of federal programs and policies on the quality of healthcare in the U.S. NCHR is a nonprofit public health think tank that conducts research, analyzes evidence, works with experts nationwide as well as patient advocates, and explains the implications and ramifications of health-related policies to policymakers and their staff, the media, and the public. We do not accept funding from pharmaceutical companies, medical device companies, chemical companies, or companies with a financial interest in our work. For more information about our Center’s policy work, see the “Speaking Out,” “We’re in the News,” and Research sections of www.center4research.org and the Monthly Digests listed in our “About Us” section. Additional Information Our office is in Washington, DC, facing Farragut Square, convenient to the Red, Orange, Blue, and Silver Metro lines. We all work in the office 2 days per week, usually Tuesdays and Thursdays, and remotely on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays. Excellent benefits and salary commensurate with experience and relevant skills, with a starting salary ranging from $75,000 to $140,000. No calls, please. Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Public Policy Specialist
item.description: Public Policy Specialist Organization: ICF Location: Reston, VA Date Posted: 07/31/2026 Are you looking to work on current and emerging policy issues? Do you want to apply your education and experience to help government agencies improve the way they develop and implement regulations, policies, and programs? Our Regulatory, Policy, and Economics Portfolio has over 30 years of experience supporting the design, implementation, and improvement of programs for a broad range of federal agencies and is seeking a Public Policy Analyst to join the team. Join our multidisciplinary team of rulemaking specialists, policy analysts, economists, and attorneys. We combine legal, policy, economic, and scientific research and analysis to solve unique public policy challenges through innovative, accurate, timely, and high-quality products and services. Our dynamic environment involves working on multiple projects simultaneously, supporting a variety of federal clients, and providing a wide range of support services. Our clients’ portfolios address numerous program areas, including: Environment Homeland security and immigration Transportation Labor and workforce issues Public health and nutrition Natural resource management Energy and nuclear power Other national priorities The position will be primarily located in our Reston, Virginia headquarters (DC Metro area), with flexibility for a hybrid work schedule. Job Responsibilities Participate in short- and long-term engagements supporting federal clients responsible for developing policies, crafting regulations, explaining the rationale behind rulemakings, and implementing regulatory requirements. Support federal agency efforts to transparently manage and analyze public comments received on proposed agency rules. Assist in drafting and editing documents related to federal agency rulemakings and develop style guides for new rulemakings. Quickly immerse yourself in varied projects for multiple clients. Provide verbal and written progress updates to project staff. Synthesize information from rulemaking documents, literature, and other technical reports. Assist in developing recommendations by collecting and analyzing both qualitative and quantitative data. Draft reports and presentations. Interact with clients to discuss ICF’s analyses. Basic Qualifications Master’s degree or Juris Doctor (JD). OR a Bachelor’s degree plus a minimum of two years of relevant experience in public policy, government, environmental science, natural or physical science, political science, or a related field. U.S. citizenship is required per federal contract requirements. Ability to obtain and maintain a moderate-level government security clearance. Preferred Qualifications Understanding of the federal rulemaking process. Strong analytical, problem-solving, organizational, time management, and decision-making skills. Ability to prioritize and manage multiple projects under strict deadlines in a fast-paced environment. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Strong attention to detail and a collaborative, team-oriented approach. Proficiency with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint) and one or more AI assistants such as Microsoft Copilot, Gemini, Claude, or ChatGPT. Indeed: #Indeed Reference Codes: #LI-CC1 | #RPEJBS Working at ICF ICF is a global advisory and technology services provider, but we’re not your typical consultants. We combine unmatched expertise with cutting-edge technology to help clients solve their most complex challenges, navigate change, and shape the future. We can only solve the world’s toughest challenges by building a workplace that allows everyone to thrive. As an equal opportunity employer, ICF empowers employees to share their expertise and collaborate to achieve personal and professional goals. Please review our Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) policy for additional information. Qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records will be considered for employment. Reasonable Accommodations Reasonable accommodations are available throughout all phases of the application and employment process for disabled veterans, individuals with disabilities, and individuals with sincerely held religious beliefs. To request an accommodation, email [email protected] . All information provided will remain confidential and will only be used as necessary to provide reasonable accommodations. Learn more about workplace discrimination rights and benefit offerings available under the Transparency in Coverage Act. Candidate AI Usage Policy ICF is committed to ensuring a fair interview process based on each candidate’s own skills and knowledge. The use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools to generate or assist with interview responses, whether during virtual or in-person interviews, is not permitted. This policy helps maintain the integrity and authenticity of the interview process. If you require an accommodation involving the use of AI, please contact [email protected] before your interview. ICF is committed to providing the necessary support to ensure all candidates have an equal opportunity to succeed. Pay Range Final compensation is determined based on multiple factors, including relevant work experience, skills, certifications, competencies, geographic location, education, and applicable contract provisions related to the position.
