item.title: Compliance Manager, Marketing
item.description: Compliance Manager, Marketing Organization: Brex Location: Seattle, WA Date Posted: 08/03/2026 Why Join Us Brex is the intelligent finance platform that enables companies to spend smarter and move faster in more than 200 markets. By combining global corporate cards and banking with intuitive spend management, bill pay, and travel software, Brex enables founders and finance teams to accelerate operations, gain real-time visibility, and control spend effortlessly. Brex’s AI-native automation and world-class service eliminate manual expense and accounting tasks for customers so they can focus on what matters most. Tens of thousands of the world’s best companies run on Brex, including DoorDash, Coinbase, Robinhood, Zoom, Plaid, Reddit, and SeatGeek. Working at Brex allows you to push your limits, challenge the status quo, and collaborate with some of the brightest minds in the industry. We’re committed to building a diverse team and inclusive culture and believe your potential should only be limited by how big you can dream. We make this a reality by empowering you with the tools, resources, and support you need to grow your career. Compliance at Brex The Compliance team helps the company grow responsibly, advocating for Brex and for the tens of thousands of growing businesses we serve. We own the compliance policies for Brex, provide strategic advice and guidance to all Brex teams, protect Brex from financial crime and other compliance risks, and represent the company externally on key regulatory and policy issues. Reimagining the financial system in a highly regulated environment requires creativity and resourcefulness, and we welcome the challenge. What You’ll Do As a Manager, Compliance Marketing, you will play a key role in executing and scaling Brex’s marketing compliance program across payments, cards, banking, and broader product lines. You will operate at the intersection of compliance, marketing, and product, ensuring that customer-facing materials are accurate, compliant, and aligned with Brex’s standards. This role is hands-on and execution-focused, supporting high-volume marketing review workflows while helping improve processes, guidance, and training as the program continues to mature. You will partner closely with Marketing, Legal, Product, and other cross-functional teams to enable compliant, high-quality marketing at scale. Where You’ll Work This role will be based in our Seattle office. We are a hybrid environment that combines the energy and connections of being in the office with the benefits and flexibility of working from home. We currently require a minimum of three coordinated days in the office per week: Monday, Wednesday, and Thursday. As a perk, we also offer up to four weeks per year of fully remote work. Responsibilities Review and approve marketing materials across channels (e.g., web, SEO, campaigns, email, product marketing, and promotional content) for compliance with internal policies and applicable regulations (e.g., UDAAP and FTC advertising standards). Ensure marketing claims are accurate, substantiated, and appropriately disclosed, including validation of performance-related claims. Manage a high-volume intake of marketing reviews by triaging requests, prioritizing based on risk, and meeting turnaround expectations in a fast-paced environment. Partner with Marketing, Product, and Legal teams to translate regulatory requirements into clear, actionable, and solutions-oriented guidance. Track, document, and maintain records of marketing reviews to support audit readiness and reporting expectations. Identify and escalate higher-risk or complex issues with clear recommendations to senior compliance leadership. Support and improve marketing compliance policies, procedures, training, and review workflows to increase efficiency and reduce rework. Take ownership of recurring issues or gaps and drive practical, scalable solutions while supporting partner bank expectations, audits, and regulatory inquiries. Requirements 4–6 years of experience in compliance, legal, risk, or a related function within banking, financial services, or fintech. Experience reviewing marketing materials or customer-facing content in a regulated environment. Working knowledge of key marketing and consumer protection regulations (e.g., UDAAP and FTC advertising rules). Familiarity with Regulation Z, CAN-SPAM, TCPA, or similar regulations is a plus. Strong attention to detail and the ability to assess risk and apply regulatory requirements pragmatically. Clear and effective written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to provide concise, solutions-oriented feedback. Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines in a high-volume, fast-paced environment. Demonstrated ownership and strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to navigate ambiguity and improve processes. Collaborative, hands-on working style with a focus on execution and cross-functional partnership. Nice to Have Experience supporting or scaling a marketing compliance review program. Familiarity with fintech products across payments, card programs, and complex banking products. Experience working with partner banks or within a bank partnership model. Experience or familiarity with AI tools or AI-generated marketing content, including an understanding of associated compliance risks and review considerations. Compensation The expected salary range for this role is $159,000 – $198,000 . However, the starting base pay will depend on several factors, including the candidate’s location, skills, experience, market demands, and internal pay parity. Depending on the position offered, equity and other forms of compensation may be provided as part of a total compensation package. Important Notice Please be aware that job seekers may be targeted by malicious actors attempting to obtain personal information. Brex recruiters will only contact candidates via LinkedIn or an email address with a brex.com domain. Any outreach claiming to be from Brex through other sources should be ignored. item.title: Senior Manager, Policy & Governance
item.description: Senior Manager, Policy & Governance Organization: Upstart Location: Remote Date Posted: 08/03/2026 About Upstart At Upstart, we’re united by a mission that matters: to radically reduce the cost and complexity of borrowing for all Americans. Every day, we bring creativity, experimentation, and advanced AI to reshape access to credit, helping millions move forward financially with clarity and confidence. As the leading AI lending marketplace, we partner with banks and credit unions to expand access to affordable credit through technology that’s both radically intelligent and deeply human. Our platform runs over one million predictions per borrower using more than 1,800 signals, powering smarter, fairer decisions for millions of customers. But the numbers only hint at the impact. Every idea, every voice, and every contribution moves us closer to a world where credit never stands between people and their financial progress. We’re proudly digital-first, giving most Upstarters the flexibility to do their best work from wherever they thrive, alongside teammates across 80+ cities in the US and Canada. Digital-first doesn’t mean distant. We’re intentional about in-person connection through team onsites, planning sessions, and moments that spark creativity and trust. And whether you choose to work primarily from home or collaborate in-person from one of our offices in Columbus, Austin, the Bay Area, or New York City (opening Summer 2026), you’ll have the support to work in the way that works best for you. If you’re energized by tackling meaningful problems, excited to innovate with purpose, and motivated by work that truly matters, we’d love to hear from you. The Team Upstart’s Enterprise Risk Management team helps ensure Upstart Bank operates with a strong, scalable governance framework that supports responsible growth. The team partners across Risk, Compliance, Legal, and business functions to maintain effective policy governance, strengthen regulatory readiness, and provide high-quality reporting to executive leadership and the Board. As the Senior Manager, Policy & Governance, you will lead Upstart Bank’s policy governance program and oversee the processes, documentation, and governance records that support effective risk management and regulatory oversight. You’ll partner across the organization to maintain a robust policy framework while ensuring board and committee governance activities are accurate, timely, and audit-ready. How You’ll Make an Impact Lead the enterprise policy governance program, ensuring the policy library remains accurate, current, accessible, and aligned with regulatory expectations. Oversee the end-to-end policy lifecycle, including policy reviews, approvals, exceptions, version control, and ongoing governance processes. Partner with Risk, Compliance, Legal, business leaders, and policy owners to coordinate policy development and approvals across the organization while maintaining efficient execution. Manage governance activities supporting Board and Risk Committee meetings, including coordinating materials, governance records, decision logs, committee charters, and meeting documentation. Ensure governance documentation and reporting are complete, timely, and audit-ready to support OCC examinations, internal audit activities, and regulatory engagements. Lead and develop a small Policy & Governance team while continuously improving governance processes that enable the bank to scale responsibly. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience. 7+ years of experience in policy management, governance, enterprise risk management, or compliance within a regulated bank, bank holding company, or other regulated financial institution. Experience owning or administering an enterprise policy governance framework, including policy lifecycle management. Experience supporting Board, Risk Committee, or senior executive governance processes within a regulated financial institution. Experience producing executive- or regulator-facing governance documentation and reports with a high degree of accuracy and quality. Preferred Qualifications Knowledge of OCC supervisory expectations and regulatory examination practices. Experience supporting a de novo bank, charter application, or rapidly growing regulated financial institution. Experience with governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platforms. Background in Enterprise Risk Management, Internal Audit, or Compliance. Ability to use generative AI tools responsibly to improve drafting, editing, summarization, and consistency of governance documentation while applying appropriate human judgment for regulatory-facing content. Position Location Remote Time Zone Requirements The team operates on the East and West Coast time zones. Travel Requirements As a digital-first company, the majority of your work can be accomplished remotely. Most employees can live and work anywhere in the U.S. but are encouraged to spend high-quality time collaborating in person through regular onsites. The cadence of these in-person sessions varies depending on the team and role. Most teams meet once or twice per quarter for 2–4 consecutive days at a time. #LI-REMOTE Compensation At Upstart, your base pay is one part of your total compensation package. The anticipated base salary for this position is expected to fall within the range below. Your actual base pay will depend on your geographic location. With our digital-first philosophy, Upstart uses compensation regions that vary by location. Individual pay is also determined by job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for your preferred location during the hiring process. In addition, Upstart provides employees with target bonuses, equity compensation, and generous benefits packages, including medical, dental, vision, and a 401(k). United States | Remote – Anticipated Base Salary Range $172,000–$270,000 USD What You’ll Love At Upstart, our benefits are designed to support your health, financial well-being, family, and personal growth. Here’s what you can expect: Competitive compensation, including base pay, bonus opportunities, and annual equity grants that vest quarterly. Retirement benefits, including a 401(k) or Group Retirement Savings Plan with a company match of $2 for every $1 contributed, up to $15,000 annually (USD in the US, CAD in Canada). Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) with discounted stock purchase options for eligible employees (US only). Comprehensive health coverage for you and your family, including medical, dental, vision, wellness resources for U.S. employees, and supplemental health coverage for employees in Canada. Health Savings Account contributions from Upstart for eligible plans (US only). Income protection benefits, including life insurance and disability coverage. Paid time off, sick leave, and company holidays in accordance with local requirements. Paid family and parental leave to support caregiving and major life moments (duration varies by country). Family-centered benefits supporting fertility, parenthood, and caregiving needs. Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering mental health support and life-centered resources. Financial wellness resources, including financial planning tools and a financial concierge service (US only). Annual wellness allowance to support your physical and emotional well-being and personal development. Annual productivity allowance to invest in the tools and resources you need to do your best work, wherever you work. Connection and community through team events, all-company updates, and Employee Resource Groups (ERGs). Onsite perks, including catered lunches and fully stocked micro-kitchens when working from offices in the Bay Area, Austin, Columbus, and New York City (opening Summer 2026). For roles based in Canada, please note that we are not currently able to hire in Quebec. Equal Opportunity Employer Upstart is a proud Equal Opportunity Employer. Just as we are dedicated to improving access to affordable credit for all, we are committed to inclusive and fair hiring practices. If you require reasonable accommodation in completing an application, interviewing, completing any pre-employment testing, or otherwise participating in the employee selection process, please email [email protected] . item.title: Senior Program Manager, Community Violence Intervention
item.description: Senior Program Manager, Community Violence Intervention Organization: Bonterra Location: Remote Date Posted: 08/03/2026 US Salary Range: $98,000 – $115,000 About Us Bonterra exists to propel every doer of good to their peak impact. We measure that impact against our vision to increase the giving rate as a percentage of GDP from 2% to 3% by 2033. We know that this goal is lofty, but we are confident that the right technology and expertise will strengthen trust in the sector, allowing the social good industry to accelerate growth and reach peak impact. Bonterra’s differentiated, end-to-end solutions collectively support a unique network of over 20,000 customers, including over 16,000 nonprofit organizations and over 50 percent of Fortune 100 companies. Learn more at bonterratech.com . About the Role The Senior Program Manager leads delivery for Bonterra’s Community Violence Intervention (CVI) and public safety program, driving product execution, delivery discipline, stakeholder alignment, and customer outcomes. This role directs a matrixed team—including Advanced Support Consultants (ASCs), Implementation Consultants, and Project Managers—and coordinates cross-functional partners to ensure clear ownership, timely execution, and risk management across all workstreams. This role is organized around three core delivery areas: Program Delivery & Stakeholder Management: Building and maintaining delivery structure, cadence, and accountability across a complex stakeholder ecosystem spanning Bonterra, government agencies, community partners, coalition partners, and internal cross-functional teams. Technology Execution: Coordinating delivery of Bonterra’s Apricot-based technology that supports a CVI model, including implementation milestones, product dependencies, data workflows, reporting needs, and roadmap commitments. Technology Adoption & Technical Assistance: Supporting agencies, community leaders, and program partners in implementing and adopting the technology, data practices, and operating workflows that enable the CVI model. The Senior Program Manager will work directly with national CVI leaders and Bonterra’s Strategic Initiatives Director to advance program goals. Internally, this role collaborates cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, Professional Services, Customer Success, and Account Management teams to track milestones, manage risk, and drive sustained customer outcomes. What You’ll Do Own end-to-end delivery for a CVI and public safety program powered by Bonterra’s technology. Coordinate implementation and product execution for Bonterra’s Apricot-based technology, managing delivery commitments across case management, data collection, and reporting workstreams while escalating product dependencies and risks to the appropriate internal teams. Support technical assistance related to technology implementation, adoption, data workflows, reporting, and program operations for government agencies, community partners, and other stakeholders. Serve as a primary point of contact and strategic liaison with CVI partners and leaders. Collaborate closely with Bonterra’s Strategic Initiatives Director and PMO Director to ensure program alignment with organizational strategy, customer commitments, and strategic program goals. Create and manage the program operating rhythm, including internal workstream meetings, partner touchpoints, executive updates, decision logs, risk reviews, and escalation pathways. Define, monitor, and drive success across multiple program KPIs, using data to surface insights and inform decision-making. Engage directly with Product and Engineering teams to surface customer needs, track feature milestones, and mitigate risk in product delivery. Create and manage long- and short-term program delivery plans, including milestone targets, resource allocation, and client-aligned deadlines. Manage program scope, budget, revenue, and utilization in partnership with Professional Services, Finance, Customer Success, and Account Management. Identify scope changes, budget risks, resource constraints, and delivery tradeoffs early, and support clear decision-making with internal and external stakeholders. Lead difficult conversations with partners and community stakeholders regarding program budgets, timelines, and strategic priorities. Serve as a point of executive presence for the program, representing Bonterra and the program’s mission in high-visibility settings with senior government and nonprofit leaders. Proactively identify and respond to risks that could impact program outcomes, customer satisfaction, or partner relationships. Perform quality control on program deliverables and adjust plans as client and stakeholder needs evolve. Improve program effectiveness by refining delivery processes and recommending practical enhancements. Occasional onsite meetings with government agencies, community partners, or program stakeholders may be required. Requirements 5+ years of project or program management experience, including complex, cross-functional programs with multiple workstreams, stakeholders, timelines, and delivery risks. Professional experience in public health, human services, social services, social work, public sector programs, nonprofit programs, criminal justice reform, public safety, or a related social-impact field. Demonstrated ability to drive program success across multiple KPIs with data-informed decision-making. Strong executive presence with the ability to communicate effectively with senior government officials, law enforcement leadership, and community stakeholders. Experience partnering with cross-functional teams to track milestones, manage dependencies, escalate risks, and support customer-facing technology delivery. Outstanding communication and analytical skills, with the ability to translate complex data into actionable program insights. Detail-oriented and highly organized, with experience managing multiple workstreams in a fast-paced environment. Problem-solving mindset with technical agility and creative thinking. Ability to analyze and visualize program data to support strategic decision-making. Preferred Skills PMP, PgMP, or equivalent program management certification. Experience managing technology-enabled programs, SaaS implementations, data-system implementations, or complex customer delivery programs. Experience with ETO, Apricot, Penelope, or similar human services data platforms. Experience in nonprofit, government, law enforcement, or foundation-funded contexts. Familiarity with public safety data systems, case management platforms, dashboards, or other data-informed public sector programs. Experience working within CVI ecosystems, community-based organizations, violence interruption programs, or other community safety initiatives. Experience supporting executive reporting, steering committee meetings, business reviews, or cross-functional governance routines. At this time, we are unable to consider candidates who require current or future sponsorship for employment authorization. Our Culture At Bonterra, we’re innovating with a higher purpose: to increase giving to 3% of US GDP by 2033, creating $573 billion more in global impact every year. At Bonterra, we foster an inclusive, equitable culture where every team member belongs and contributes to meaningful impact. Read more about our values and culture here . Compensation & Benefits We offer a comprehensive benefits package that supports your health, well-being, and growth. Explore full details here . Compensation and benefits for this role apply to full-time employees in the United States and may vary based on local standards, laws, and norms. Pay is determined by location, skills, experience, and education, and is one part of Bonterra’s total rewards package, which may also include bonuses, incentives, equity, and a comprehensive benefits program. Equal Opportunity & Accommodations At Bonterra, we are proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. We provide equal employment opportunities without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, or gender identity), national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. item.title: Executive Director
item.description: Executive Director Organization: Texans for Affordable Healthcare (TAHC) Location: Austin, TX Date Posted: 08/03/2026 Job Description Texans for Affordable Healthcare (TAHC) is an independent, nonpartisan organization dedicated to advancing policies that make healthcare more affordable, transparent, and accessible for Texas families and employers. TAHC is seeking a dynamic, mission-driven Executive Director to serve as the organization’s chief executive, lead advocate, and public voice. Specifically, this contract position will lead TAHC’s advocacy, public affairs, coalition-building, and organizational efforts, working with policymakers, employers, healthcare stakeholders, and coalition partners to advance practical policy solutions that improve healthcare affordability and strengthen Texas’ healthcare system. This role is ideal for a passionate advocate who excels in building relationships and bringing people together around a common purpose. Serving as the voice of the organization, the successful candidate will be an effective communicator capable of translating complex healthcare issues into meaningful policy solutions that align with TAHC’s mission. Candidates may come from a variety of backgrounds including advocacy organizations, trade associations, nonprofit leadership, healthcare, public policy, government affairs, communications, grassroots organizing, business organizations, or related fields. Experience working with the Texas Legislature or in government affairs is valuable but not required. The position offers a flexible schedule with occasional travel required for legislative meetings, conferences, and stakeholder events. Key Responsibilities Advocacy & Public Policy Serve as TAHC’s principal advocate and representative before the Texas Legislature, state agencies, coalition partners, and other stakeholders. Lead the organization’s public policy and advocacy agenda by developing and implementing strategies that advance healthcare affordability, transparency, competition, and consumer access. Build and maintain productive relationships with legislators, legislative staff, executive agencies, business leaders, healthcare organizations, and community stakeholders. Prepare policy briefs, testimony, talking points, educational materials, and advocacy resources. Monitor legislative and regulatory developments and identify opportunities to advance TAHC’s mission. Represent TAHC at legislative hearings, stakeholder meetings, conferences, and public events. Coalition Building & Stakeholder Engagement Build and maintain strong relationships with employers, business organizations, healthcare providers, consumer advocates, local organizations, and other stakeholders. Develop strategic partnerships that expand TAHC’s statewide influence. Organize and lead coalitions around shared policy priorities. Engage grassroots supporters and community leaders to strengthen advocacy efforts. Organizational Leadership Provide strategic leadership for TAHC’s advocacy, communications, and organizational priorities. Develop strategic plans, advocacy objectives, and organizational goals. Provide regular updates to stakeholders regarding legislative developments, organizational initiatives, opportunities, and challenges. Support fundraising, organizational growth, and long-term sustainability. Public Affairs & Communications Serve as the primary spokesperson and public representative for TAHC. Develop compelling messages that educate policymakers and the public about healthcare affordability and transparency. Collaborate on media relations, opinion pieces, digital communications, and public education campaigns. Oversee digital advocacy efforts, including email communications, social media, online engagement, and grassroots campaigns. Required Qualifications Demonstrated leadership experience in advocacy, nonprofit leadership, public policy, healthcare, government affairs, communications, coalition building, community organizing, trade associations, or a related field. Passion for improving healthcare affordability and expanding access to high-quality healthcare. Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills. Ability to build trust and productive relationships with diverse stakeholders. Strong strategic thinking, organizational skills, and sound judgment. Ability to inspire others, build consensus, and advance organizational goals. Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. Willingness to represent TAHC professionally before policymakers, stakeholders, media, and the public. Preferred Qualifications Experience working with the Texas Legislature, state government, or public policy. Experience in government affairs, lobbying, legislative advocacy, or political campaigns. Knowledge of healthcare affordability, insurance markets, prescription drug policy, healthcare transparency, or healthcare delivery systems. Experience leading coalitions, advocacy campaigns, nonprofit organizations, or statewide initiatives. Existing relationships with Texas policymakers, business leaders, healthcare organizations, or advocacy groups. Location Austin, Texas is preferred, with regular engagement at the Texas Capitol and travel throughout the state as needed. Why Join TAHC? Healthcare affordability is one of the most pressing challenges facing Texas families and employers. As Executive Director, you will have the opportunity to lead an established statewide organization, build coalitions, shape public policy, educate decision-makers, and champion practical reforms that improve the lives of millions of Texans. TAHC is committed to building a collaborative, nonpartisan movement that brings together diverse voices in support of a more affordable, transparent, and competitive healthcare system. How to Apply Interested candidates should submit a resume and a brief cover letter outlining their interest in the position and relevant experience to: [email protected] Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled. Texans for Affordable Healthcare is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes candidates from diverse professional backgrounds who share a commitment to improving healthcare affordability and access for all Texans. Additional Information Information about the job can be found on our website: https://www.texansforaffordablehealthcare.com/news/executive-director Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Vice President, External Affairs and Strategic Communications
item.description: Vice President, External Affairs and Strategic Communications Organization: Tides Location: Remote Date Posted: 08/03/2026 About Tides Tides is a nonprofit and philanthropic organization committed to advancing social justice. We work across the social sector to shift power to communities of color and other groups historically denied power. Centering equity and justice in everything we do, we collaborate in deep partnership with movement leaders, nonprofits, donors, foundations, and corporations to amplify the impact of their work by providing services like fiscal sponsorship, donor advised funds, grant making, and a variety of innovative solutions. Learn more at tides.org. About this Role Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer and serving as a member of the executive team, the Vice President for External Affairs and Strategic Communications is responsible for shaping and advancing Tides’ external voice, public positioning, and narrative. The Vice President owns external organization’s voice; brand, market, and sector positioning strategy; narrative strategy; external affairs; executive communications; crisis response; and external stakeholder engagement, which includes, but is not limited to, relationships with national and regional media, philanthropic partners, fiscal sponsorship peers, policy allies, and movement-aligned organizations, cultivated and maintained in service of the organization’s communications and narrative goals. The Vice President is responsible for protecting and advancing the Tides reputation and brand, building audience and constituent engagement, aligning marketing and communications with fundraising and programmatic strategy, and ensuring the organization speaks with clarity, courage, and discipline in a contested environment. The Vice President will work across Tides to ensure alignment between institutional priorities and external messaging, partnering with colleagues to translate programmatic work, partnerships, and impact into compelling, coherent narratives. The Vice President will oversee a marketing and communications team currently comprising four full-time staff and will lead both the strategic direction of the function and the evolution of its structure, resourcing, and operating model in support of Tides’ work. What You Will Do Shape and Lead Tides’ Narrative in a Complex Environment Develop and execute an integrated communications and external affairs strategy aligned with organizational goals, theory of change, and financial sustainability plan. Serve as principal counsel to the CEO and Executive Team on public positioning, message discipline, crisis response, and sequencing of public statements. Advise the Executive Team and Board of Directors on reputational risk and narrative exposure. Own Tides’ brand architecture, persona, voice, and narrative frame across all external channels and audiences. Drive Tides’ narrative proactively in the broader social sector landscape. Monitor and track how mission-related issues are being framed, weaponized, or reshaped across media, political, and cultural spaces. Exercise disciplined judgment on when to lead public conversation, when to amplify coalition partners, and when strategic restraint better serves the mission. Elevate Brand Positioning and Public Presence Oversee content strategy spanning earned media, owned channels, executive thought leadership, annual reports, and Tides publications. Lead integrated marketing strategy across brand, digital, email, social, advertising, and campaign channels to build awareness, engagement, and action among target audiences. Set and manage marketing/engagement growth goals and KPIs, including digital reach, audience growth, and supporter acquisition, that build Tides’ brand visibility and public presence, translating results into conversion metrics in partnership with Business Development. Oversee Tides’ website, digital properties, and marketing technology stack; ensure data-informed decision-making and appropriate investment in analytics, CRM, and automation tools. Direct brand and creative development, including visual identity, design systems, and campaign creative, working with in-house staff and agency partners. Partner Across the Organization to Align Strategy and Messaging Partner with Tides Foundation, Tides Center, and Business Development leadership to lead public-facing campaigns, mobilization moments, and integrated marketing calendars. Partner with the Chief Programs Officer to align communications with fundraising strategy, donor stewardship, and major-gift engagement. Partner with Tides Foundation, Tides Center, and Business Development to co-develop donor-facing content that demonstrates impact, addresses current-moment concerns, and reinforces the case for sustained and expanded investment. Support Board communications, including board meeting preparation, board-facing updates, and ambassadorship materials. Partner with the Executive Team, the People Team, and Internal Communications staff to ensure external positioning and internal messaging are coordinated, particularly ahead of significant announcements, crises, and politically sensitive external statements. Lead and maintain a shared messaging architecture so talking points, positioning documents, and narrative frames are consistent across staff-facing and public-facing channels. Enhance and Modernize the Communications Function Lead, develop, and retain a high-performing marketing and external communications team; coach direct reports and cultivate strength within the function. Manage the marketing and external communications budget, including agency, consultant, platform, production, and paid media spend. In partnership with the Chief People Officer, co-lead Tides’ internal communications team, integrating internal and external communications strategies and messaging as applicable. Select, manage, and hold accountable external agency and vendor partners; build a trusted “extended team” model that scales capacity without permanent headcount. Establish KPIs and reporting cadence across marketing performance, external communications, reputation health, earned media impact, and audience growth. Strengthen Media and External Relationships Lead proactive national media strategy, cultivating relationships with reporters, editors, and opinion leaders across mainstream, movement, and ideologically diverse outlets. Direct executive visibility strategy, including speaking engagements, op-ed placement, broadcast appearances, and conference presence. Prepare the CEO and designated spokespeople for high-stakes interviews and public-facing events. Build and maintain relationships with peer national organizations, state and regional affiliates, philanthropic intermediaries, and sector communications networks. Represent Tides in sector-wide narrative coordination, shared-research efforts, and joint response on issues where collective voice amplifies impact. Serve as a public representative of Tides at select conferences, convenings, and sector events. Build Crisis Response and Reputation Management Capacity Partner with the Chief Legal and Compliance Officer to manage the intersection of communications with regulatory, legal, financial, and investigative risk. Own organizational crisis communications planning, playbook maintenance, and live response. Coordinate with Executive Team and Senior Leaders during incidents, whether internal or external. Maintain a pre-approved response architecture for attack vectors so the organization can move with speed when required. As an executive leader, the Vice President must execute duties and responsibilities while embracing and exhibiting Tides’ core competencies: Leading Self Self-awareness JEDI practice Continuous learning Project management Leading People Building trusting relationships Team leadership Decision making Developing teammates Leading Results Strategic planning Change leadership Driving outcomes What You Will Bring The successful candidate will demonstrate, through ideas, words, and actions, a deep and sustained commitment to Tides’ mission and JEDI values. This calls for grounding their work in an equity-centered approach that advances justice, builds transformative partnerships, centers community power and agency, and fosters trust through accountability and service. The successful candidate will bring many of the following qualities and experiences: 15 years of relevant experience. Ten years of experience must be in a senior-level leadership capacity. Demonstrated experience as principal marketing and communications counsel to a CEO, Executive Director, or equivalent senior principal. Proven track record in crisis communications at national scale, including politically or ideologically charged incidents. Deep national media relationships with demonstrated placement across mainstream, political, and movement press. Demonstrated marketing and brand leadership, including brand strategy, digital marketing, audience growth, and measurable campaign results. Experience with mission-driven, advocacy, or politically active organizations (nonprofit, 501(c)(3)/(c)(4), political, or public-interest). Demonstrated ability to build and execute narrative strategy, not just message discipline. Experience managing lean teams and extended vendor networks under resource constraints. Excellent judgment when handling sensitive legal, personnel, and political matters. Excellent written and verbal communication, including executive speechwriting and op-ed drafting. Ability to ground all work in a deep commitment to the Tides mission and JEDI values, applying an equity-centered lens to strategy, practice, and engagement. Ideal Experience Preferred qualifications include: Experience at or with organizations that have faced regulatory scrutiny, congressional investigation, or politically motivated attacks. Demonstrated experience communicating for organizations advancing social justice, equity, or syst

item.title: Associate General Counsel, Nonprofit Compliance
item.description: Associate General Counsel, Nonprofit Compliance Organization: Tides Location: Remote Date Posted: 08/03/2026 About Tides Tides is a nonprofit and philanthropic organization committed to advancing social justice. We work across the social sector to shift power to communities of color and other groups historically denied power. Centering equity and justice in everything we do, we collaborate in deep partnership with movement leaders, nonprofits, donors, foundations, and corporations to amplify the impact of their work by providing services like fiscal sponsorship, donor advised funds, grant making, and a variety of innovative solutions. Learn more at tides.org. About the Role The Associate General Counsel (AGC), Nonprofit Compliance advances Tides’ most fundamental legal and regulatory work across its core activities—grantmaking, fiscal sponsorship, and advocacy—translating nonprofit legal and regulatory frameworks into robust, well-calibrated compliance and risk mitigation systems and practices. Reporting to the Chief Legal & Compliance Officer, the AGC serves as an expert and internal resource on nonprofit 501(c)(3) and corporate legal and regulatory requirements, supplementing and deepening the Legal, Risk & Compliance (LRC) Team’s existing expertise, including on matters involving charitability, nonprofit tax law and UBIT, lobbying regulations including disclosure and reporting requirements, advocacy and partisan activities, and ballot measure and campaign compliance matters. The AGC oversees and leads the legal compliance team and program, ensuring policies and systems for 501(c)(3) and general corporate compliance are rigorous, calibrated for effectiveness and efficiency, and operationally sound. The role directs the internal assessment and audit function, corporate compliance and reporting obligations across jurisdictions, and the organization’s legal policy development. This is a supervisory position, managing a team that includes the Compliance Manager, the Senior Compliance Associate, and the Sr. Paralegal & Operations Analyst. As a people leader and member of the Senior Leadership Team operating under executive direction, the AGC builds and develops a high-performing legal compliance function and partners across LRC, finance, and partner-facing functions to embed compliance into daily workstreams, thereby protecting Tides and its partners while enabling mission impact. The AGC role is an exempt position. Exempt employees are expected to work the appropriate and necessary time to complete key assignments and related tasks on schedule. As a Senior Leadership Team member and People Leader, the AGC is responsible for modeling and demonstrating Tides’ core competencies. What You Will Do Legal Compliance Program Oversees, maintains, and advances organizational compliance with applicable laws and regulations, including those specifically applicable to 501(c)(3) charitable organizations, and ensures robust, effective, efficient, and well-calibrated policies and systems covering relevant nonprofit and corporate legal compliance matters. This includes: Leading Tides Legal Compliance and directing the Internal Assessment Program, including setting annual internal audit priorities, planning, and execution. Overseeing federal and state corporate registration and reporting obligations, including those involving charitable fundraising, lobbying, gifts to public officials, campaign finance rules, and others as relevant. Leading the development and maintenance of legal policies and practices for managing key risks associated with operations, businesses, and programs, such as OFAC and anti-corruption and bribery processes and other payment and KYC functions, in each case ensuring policies remain current and compliant with evolving legal and regulatory requirements. Overseeing Tides’ insurance program, including renewals, claims coverage and disputes, and exploring alternative and complementary risk mitigation strategies. Overseeing the development of training and capacity-building resources to strengthen compliance literacy across the organization and its fiscally sponsored projects. Driving adoption of technology solutions, including automation tools, to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of the Legal Compliance Program. Setting short-term priorities and long-term compliance strategy to ensure the organization’s program is effective in identifying and mitigating compliance risks. Nonprofit Legal Expertise Serves as an expert and internal resource on nonprofit 501(c)(3) and corporate legal and regulatory requirements as an integral member of LRC, working closely with other in-house legal team members responsible for other legal areas including philanthropy and fiscal sponsorship. Representative responsibilities include: Providing exempt organizational tax advice, such as assisting with charitability determinations, expenditure responsibility reviews, and solving complicated issues involving partisan and advocacy-related activities. Responding to federal, state, and local inquiries and investigations, such as inquiries from the IRS and other agencies and legislative bodies. Advising on compliance with lobbying reporting and disclosure requirements, including the Lobbying Disclosure Act (LDA), Foreign Agents Registration Act (FARA), and state lobbying, ethics, and gift laws, as well as ballot measure and election-related laws. Contract drafting and advising, such as negotiating vendor agreements relating to compliance-focused systems, as well as drafting and reviewing legal policies and procedures. Counseling senior leadership and other Tides teams on novel and complex legal compliance questions arising from new program models, partnerships, and advocacy strategies. Monitoring legislative, regulatory, and enforcement developments affecting the nonprofit sector and translating them into actionable organizational guidance. People Leadership Leads, develops, and supervises the legal compliance team, including hiring, performance management, coaching, and professional development. Sets team priorities, allocates resources, and builds team skills aligned to LRC departmental goals and organizational strategy. Manages functional and team efficiency, effectiveness, and alignment, and models Tides’ values in fostering an inclusive, accountable, high-performing team culture. What You Will Bring Strong alignment with Tides’ values, mission, and impact goal. The AGC must embody Tides’ JEDI values and demonstrate the organization’s core values: future focus, accountability, transparency, respect, and collaboration in all aspects of their work. Deep expertise in laws and regulations governing 501(c)(3) public charities, and an understanding of relationships among affiliated tax-exempt organizations such as 501(c)(3) and 501(c)(4) nonprofits. Authoritative command of federal and state lobbying, political activity, and campaign finance rules as applied to (c)(3) organizations, including ballot measure activity and issue advocacy at the federal, state, and local levels. Experience translating complex legal requirements into well-calibrated, effective, and efficient policies, practices, and systems, and building robust compliance systems. Demonstrated ability to lead and develop teams, including people leaders, and to manage a function’s outcomes and alignment. Effective and creative problem-solving skills that result in solution-oriented, business-forward, actionable advice and guidance. Ability to distinguish material risk from theoretical risk and advise accordingly. Excellent written and verbal communication, including the ability to counsel executives, senior leaders, and non-lawyers on complex topics. Exercises excellent judgment in handling confidential and sensitive information. Proficiency with Salesforce and the Microsoft Office Suite is a plus. Ideal Experience Juris Doctor and active California law license or registered in-house counsel required. Practicing attorney with 8+ years of experience advising nonprofit tax-exempt organizations, at least 3 of which includes supervising or leading compliance teams and full-time staff. Experience advising nonprofits on federal and state tax laws and regulations including charitability; inurement and private benefit; political, advocacy, and partisan activities; state and federal lobbying limits; and related lobbying reporting, disclosures, and registrations. Adept at advising clients on legally complex and high-profile activities, such as compliance with federal and state laws regarding voter registration and ballot measures. Proficient advising on general corporate legal compliance matters such as conflicts of interest, OFAC, anti-bribery and other payment-related regulations, and Foreign Agents Registration Act obligations. Hands-on experience designing, maintaining, and/or overseeing compliance programs and systems for nonprofit organizations. Experience with fiscal sponsorship, grantmaking, and multi-entity nonprofit structures is strongly preferred. Equal Employment Opportunity We look forward to reviewing applications from all qualified job seekers. We strongly encourage applications from women, people of color, and bilingual and bicultural individuals, as well as members of the LGBTQIA+ communities. No applicant will be discriminated against because of their race, religion, sex, national origin, ethnicity, age, disability, political affiliation, sexual orientation, gender identity, color, marital status, or medical condition including acquired immune deficiency syndrome (AIDS) and AIDS-related conditions. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we encourage and will consider qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. Where required by state law, we utilize E-Verify as a part of our employment authorization process. Applicants with Disabilities Reasonable accommodation will be made so that all who are interested may participate in our interview pr

We work across the social sector to shift power to communities of color and other groups historically denied power. Centering equity and justice in everything we do, we collaborate in deep partnership with movement leaders, nonprofits, donors, foundations, and corporations to amplify the impact of their work by providing services like fiscal sponsorship, donor advised funds, grantmaking, and a variety of innovative solutions. Learn more at https://tides.org. About the Role The Senior Counsel, Philanthropy, is a senior individual contributor on the Legal, Risk and Compliance (LRC) team, exercising principal-level authority over charitable and exempt-organization sector law as applied across Tides’ entities and activities. Operating with general executive direction, the Senior Counsel serves as an authoritative internal legal resource within an assigned practice portfolio spanning charitable philanthropic services, including donor advised funds (DAFs), mission- and program-related investments, and the laws and regulations governing charitable exempt organizations—including charitability, partner due diligence and risk mitigation practices and policies, nonprofit tax, and election and advocacy activity for 501(c)(3) organizations. The individual portfolio assigned is based on organizational need and will emphasize Tides Foundation’s philanthropic, grantmaking, and investment-related activities, with shared coverage of Tides Network and other separate entities as needed. The Senior Counsel translates nonprofit legal and regulatory frameworks into robust, well-calibrated compliance and risk mitigation advice, practices, and policies; leads legal projects and initiatives with cross-departmental scope; and provides technical direction to LRC staff and cross-functional partners through subject-matter leadership rather than supervision. As a Senior Leader, the Senior Counsel, Philanthropy is responsible for modeling and demonstrating Tides’ core competencies of Leading Self, Leading People, and Leading Results. What You Will Do Senior Legal Counsel Serves as an authoritative internal resource on the laws and regulations governing charitable exempt organizations within the assigned portfolio, including grantmaking practices, partner due diligence, tax-exempt and charitable compliance, and compliant investment portfolios and programs. Advises executive leadership and Tides staff on complex legal grantmaking (including grants from DAFs, international grantmaking, and grants to non-501(c)(3) entities) and investment questions, recommending solutions and risk mitigations and determining appropriate escalation. Leads legal vetting of new and existing service offerings and programs for Tides Foundation, including Tides-led initiatives, DAFs, and other philanthropic giving and investment vehicles, identifying, investigating, and resolving legal issues while supporting Tides’ mission. Reviews and negotiates day-to-day contracts, primarily those entered by Tides Foundation, complex contracts, grant agreements, and investment and fund offerings and terms and conditions; leads development and revision of Tides’ legal documents, template libraries, and legal and operational policies. Responds to subpoenas, legal inquiries, and investigations, directing work with outside counsel as needed; tracks and reports on ongoing matters and prepares privileged memoranda on significant issues. Philanthropic Activity and Fiscal Sponsor Advising Provides authoritative counsel on the appropriateness of political activities for 501(c)(3) entities, including as it relates to grantmaking, investments, election-related work and partisan activity, and associated communications and messaging. Forms organizational guidance on relevant state and federal regulation, donor disclosure, and advisory committee roles and responsibilities. Advises on the permissible scope of joint 501(c)(3)/501(c)(4) activity, including agreements, grant proposals from (c)(4) entities, and grants from Tides to (c)(4) entities. Supports and provides guidance on Model A and Model C fiscal sponsorship requirements. Supports compliant messaging of election and advocacy activity in partnership with Marketing and Communications. Risk Management and Compliance Translates legal and regulatory frameworks into practical compliance tools, policies, and procedures; provides technical direction to LRC compliance staff in developing and operating the compliance program. Issue spots, investigates, and evaluates the legal implications of compliance matters and directs recommended operational changes or alternative policies and procedures. Advises on legal due diligence and policy compliance for mission-related and program-related investments in collaboration with the Investments team. As needed, advises on legal matters relating to Tides entities that own, lease, and sublease property, including property tax exemptions, tax-exempt bonds and covenants, and tenant leases. Functional Leadership and Enablement Leads legal projects and initiatives with cross-departmental scope, including the design and delivery of staff training on relevant legal topics. Monitors legislative, regulatory, and enforcement developments affecting the charitable sector; translates developments into strategic advice protecting Tides’ charitable mission, partners, and staff. Mentors and shares advanced technical knowledge with LRC team members; supports legal team education and management of resources. Maintains individual continuing education to ensure Tides remains compliant with evolving laws. What You Will Bring Leads by example and stewards commitment to Tides’ mission, impact goals, and JEDI principles. Principal-level expertise in charitable and exempt-organization sector law, including 501(c)(3) charitability, nonprofit tax (including expenditure responsibility rules), fiscal sponsorship structures, and election and advocacy regulation. Experience advising charitable organizations, including public foundations, both in-house and in private practice. Holds self and others accountable for high-quality, timely, and effective results. Adapts easily to working with a variety of stakeholders and to the varying needs of the organization while maintaining a strong voice for legal compliance. Sound, well-calibrated risk judgment—able to distinguish material risk from theoretical risk and advise accordingly. Exercises excellent judgment in handling confidential information and other potentially sensitive matters. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to counsel executives and make legal concepts accessible to non-lawyers across fields of expertise. Ideal Experience Juris Doctor and California law license or registered in-house counsel required. 8+ years of direct experience in charitable sector law (nonprofit tax, fiscal sponsorship, exempt organization compliance, and/or election and advocacy law). Experience and knowledge of mission-related and program-related investment programs, including applicable regulations. Experience with registered investment advisor services is a plus. Experience advising nonprofit organizations on compliance program structure and policy is essential. Experience with fiscal sponsorship, intermediary, or multi-entity nonprofit structures is strongly preferred. Equal Employment Opportunity We look forward to reviewing applications from all qualified job seekers. We strongly encourage applications from women, people of color, and bilingual and bicultural individuals, as well as members of the LGBTQIA+ communities. No applicant will be discriminated against because of their race, religion, sex, national origin, ethnicity, age, disability, political affiliation, sexual orientation, gender identity, color, marital status, or medical condition, including acquired immune deficiency syndrome (AIDS) and AIDS-related conditions. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we encourage and will consider qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. Where required by state law, we utilize E-Verify as part of our employment authorization process. Applicants with Disabilities Reasonable accommodation will be made so that all who are interested may participate in our interview process. If you are in need of an accommodation, please advise in writing at the time you apply. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Principal of Public Affairs
item.description: Principal of Public Affairs Organization: Moxie Strategies Location: New York, NY Date Posted: 08/03/2026 Who We Are Moxie Strategies isn’t just a firm—it’s a force. We shape conversations, move policy, and craft campaigns that drive results. Founded and led by women, minorities, and LGBTQIA+ professionals, we bring deep expertise across healthcare, energy, higher education, infrastructure, labor, corporate, and nonprofit sectors. Our tagline, Unique Depth. Bold Impact. , reflects exactly how we operate. We dive deep into data, strategy, and storytelling—because surface-level solutions don’t cut it. We understand the nuances, anticipate challenges, and craft strategies that make a lasting impact. We combine that depth with bold execution, ensuring that every campaign, message, and action is designed to move the needle where it matters. Our team includes data scientists, campaign strategists, media experts, and Emmy-winning creatives who understand how to craft and execute high-impact campaigns. We are problem-solvers, communicators, and strategists who turn complex challenges into clear, actionable solutions. Moxie means having guts, vision, and the drive to win. Sound like you? Keep reading. The Role: Principal, Public Affairs We’re looking for a self-starter who is ready to take the next step in their career—someone with a foundational background in public affairs and client management who wants to solve big problems and deliver smart, strategic counsel to clients operating in high-stakes arenas. As Principal of Public Affairs, you will play a critical role in supporting client relationships, ensuring they receive the expertise, strategy, and execution needed to drive impactful campaigns. What You’ll Do Client Management Collaborate with senior and executive leadership to develop and execute winning campaign strategies. Support teams working on New York-based clients, ensuring their priorities and goals are met and exceeded. Build lasting client relationships so clients see you as a key contributor to their overall success. Prioritize both crisis and proactive communications while managing multiple accounts and projects simultaneously. Business Growth & Thought Leadership Spot opportunities by monitoring and analyzing industry trends. Identify ways to expand client engagements and upsell contracts. Actively develop proposals, presentations, and reports to enhance efficiency and client satisfaction. Leadership & Execution Mentor and develop junior staff, fostering a culture of excellence, creativity, and accountability. Refine and optimize internal workflows because efficiency drives impact. Set the bar high by elevating the firm’s standards for execution, innovation, and results. Benefits At Moxie Strategies, we believe that supporting our team’s well-being is key to achieving success together. As a valued member of our team, you’ll enjoy a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your professional and personal goals. Health & Wellness Competitive medical, dental, and vision insurance plans. Pre-tax Flexible Spending Account (FSA) and Commuter Savings Account. Financial Security Competitive salary based on experience. Performance-based bonus structure with growth potential. Opportunity for future participation in the profit-sharing program. 401(k) retirement plan with a 3% company contribution of your base salary. Life insurance. Work-Life Balance Generous paid time off (PTO) and company holidays. Flexible work arrangements, including hybrid options (role-specific). Paid parental leave and family support. Professional Growth The opportunity to lead impactful projects within a dynamic and inclusive environment. Collaboration with a team of accomplished professionals dedicated to driving change. Access to industry conferences, training, and certifications. Career development and mentorship opportunities. We’re committed to creating an inclusive and supportive environment where everyone can thrive. Join us and experience a workplace that values your contributions, invests in your growth, and celebrates your success. Requirements What We’re Looking For 3+ years of experience in client management, public affairs, communications, government, or a related field. Strong time management skills with the ability to manage multiple projects and meet deadlines. Exceptional communication skills. A strategic mindset with a tactical edge—you see the big picture and handle the details. Knowledge of New York’s political, corporate, and nonprofit landscape. You’re not just ambitious—you get things done. Email [email protected] for more information on how to apply. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Chief Counsel
item.description: Chief Counsel Organization: Whistleblower Aid (WBA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/03/2026 About Whistleblower Aid Whistleblower Aid (WBA) is a pioneering 501(c)(3) nonprofit legal organization that helps government employees and private-sector workers report and expose wrongdoing. Our clients come forward at great personal risk to bring the transparency needed for public accountability and reform. Whether holding the government to account, protecting our democracy, defending the Constitution, safeguarding our national security, or reporting corporate malfeasance harming the public, our clients’ truth-telling is driving much-needed changes across industries and agencies, and their impact is felt around the world. We are a small team of lawyers, strategists, and communications professionals who work tirelessly to keep our whistleblowers safe and their disclosures legal and effective. About the Position Whistleblower Aid is seeking to hire an experienced, mission-driven attorney as our next Chief Counsel. As a member of the leadership team, the Chief Counsel will help lead our growing organization by overseeing our programmatic legal work. This role will directly support, provide legal guidance to, and represent our clients; personally oversee the development and execution of whistleblower disclosures; build strategy to advance our entire legal program; and publicly represent the organization. Whistleblower Aid’s work is highly sensitive, and this position requires absolute discretion and professionalism. This is a full-time, at-will employee position. This role is hybrid, serving our office in Washington, DC, with a minimum of two days in the office per week. Responsibilities Lead, oversee, and manage WBA’s programmatic legal work. Serve as Chief Counsel for all whistleblower clients—government and corporate—who risk much when they bring wrongdoing to light. Provide strategic counsel and support to the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Strategy Officer on both case-related and organizational/operational matters. Support organizational needs by making legal risk assessments, conducting research and analysis, and producing risk mitigation strategies. Research, create, and file lawful whistleblower disclosures with law enforcement agencies, Inspectors General, Congress, and other regulatory, investigative, and law enforcement bodies that generate impactful investigations and enforcement actions. Review drafted legal documents and disclosures, ensure quality control on organization-wide matters, and ensure lead counsel for each case updates and maintains current case plans for active matters. Lead assigned casework, including case strategy, team strategy, drafting, editing, filing, legal analysis, legal arguments, and evidence review. Prevent retaliation against clients, including but not limited to adverse employment actions, attacks on credibility, and frivolous litigation or SLAPP suits. Work closely with the leadership team to develop and execute impact strategies that ensure client disclosures lead to public awareness, policy change, institutional reform, and accountability. Serve as the lead legal point of contact for all outside partners, including co-counsel, subject matter experts, and consultants. Recruit and manage direct-report legal staff, teams of co-counsel, investigators, paralegals, and other contractors. Cultivate and create partnerships through targeted outreach and educational events. Represent the organization at industry events, conferences, and on panels as appropriate. Expand and support collaboration with a trusted network of advocacy partners, mission-aligned NGOs, legal groups, and policymakers. Work collaboratively with the leadership and communications teams to establish thought leadership, ensure impactful media engagement, and build WBA brand awareness. Represent the organization publicly in furtherance of its mission and brand. Support the organization’s advocacy and external relations strategies in service of cases and clients, including appearances in print, television, and other media. Participate in and support the organization’s fundraising and development activities. Provide guidance and mentorship to the organization’s attorneys. Travel domestically and internationally as needed. Perform other duties as assigned. Requirements Deep commitment to public service with a demonstrated track record. J.D. degree and admission to at least one state bar. 10+ years of supervisory legal experience. Hands-on experience producing and editing legal work product under time-sensitive conditions. Hands-on experience managing and conducting document review. Superior writing skills. Proven ability to lead and grow organizations, preferably in a nonprofit or mission-driven environment. Ability to publicly represent an organization through effective public speaking, strong interpersonal skills, and professionalism. Agility to function in dynamic circumstances with a creative problem-solving approach. Strong track record of leading by example, including modeling resourcefulness, responsiveness, empathy, and collegiality. Preferred experience in government oversight, such as the Department of Justice (DOJ), an Office of Inspector General (OIG), an agency General Counsel’s office, a federal agency with investigative or civil enforcement authority, or congressional investigations. Preferred legal experience in whistleblower law. Preferred ability to practice law in Washington, DC. Benefits Whistleblower Aid offers a generous benefits package, including: Fully employer-paid health insurance. Employer-sponsored retirement plan with company match. Life insurance. Generous paid time off policy. Candidates from diverse backgrounds are encouraged to apply. How to Apply Email your application to: [email protected] Please include the following with your application: Cover letter. Resume/CV. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Public Relations Sr Acct Executive, Advocacy Practice
item.description: Public Relations Sr Acct Executive, Advocacy Practice Organization: Anat Gerstein, Inc. Location: New York, NY | Albany, NY Date Posted: 08/03/2026 Public Relations Senior Account Executive, Advocacy Practice Anat Gerstein, Inc. is a full-service communications firm that exclusively works with nonprofit and government organizations that support and enrich communities across New York City and beyond. We are rapidly growing and regularly recognized as one of the top communications firms serving nonprofits and supporting good causes. Our firm and staff have been named a leading nonprofit consultant, a top political PR power company, Crain’s Notable Business and Notable Leader in PR, Communicators of the Year, and more. We are looking for a creative, high-energy, self-starter with experience working on city or state public policy issues through government, political campaigns, advocacy, public affairs, or journalism, along with excellent oral and written communications skills and experience with traditional and social media. Candidates should have a demonstrated interest in government and advocacy, and understand how strategic communications can advance policy goals and influence public debate. This position may be based in either our New York City office or remotely in Albany. Candidates should be able to work from one of these locations on a regular basis. Job Requirements Work with colleagues to formulate and execute communications programs for a variety of clients. Specific responsibilities include: Providing strategic communications guidance. Drafting press materials (e.g., press releases). Managing press interviews and events. Developing stories and pitching reporters. Helping to maintain social media accounts. Drafting newsletters, op-eds, testimony for government hearings, website copy, and speeches. Drafting donor and participant communications. Job Qualifications 5+ years of relevant professional experience in one or more of the following: state or local government (including working for an elected official or government agency), journalism (covering politics and/or government), political campaigns, or public affairs communications. Experience working on New York City or New York State policy, advocacy, or political issues is strongly preferred. Creative, strategic thinker, always on the lookout for innovative ways to promote a client, program, or story. Motivated, detail-oriented, and organized self-starter capable of managing multiple projects and ensuring successful execution. Team player willing to support a team of professionals to consistently improve service and outcomes. Experience developing and executing successful multi-channel communications programs with measurable goals. Excellent written and oral communication skills. Strong multitasker who thrives under tight deadlines. Demonstrated understanding of how advocacy campaigns influence public policy through communications, media relations, coalition-building, and engagement with government stakeholders. Values diverse experiences. Outstanding relationship-building and interpersonal communication skills. Strong familiarity with and interest in New York City and New York State news media. Strong understanding of New York City and/or New York State government, policymaking, and the legislative process. Experience managing and growing social media accounts. Existing relationships with reporters, policymakers, advocates, or other stakeholders in New York City’s or New York State’s government, politics, and public policy ecosystem are a plus. Salary $80,000–$120,000 , commensurate with experience and skills. Benefits 100% coverage of health insurance, 50% coverage of dental insurance, and affordable vision insurance monthly premiums. Employer-funded short-term disability insurance. Pre-tax Flexible Spending Account (FSA). Mental health assistance with a company-sponsored Talkspace membership. Access to healthcare advocacy and support through Health Advocate. Membership to One Medical for on-demand primary, mental, and virtual care, plus access to One Medical offices nationwide and virtual urgent care through Teladoc Health. Kindbody gynecology, fertility, and family-building benefit. Peloton App membership with access to thousands of classes, including cardio, running, strength, yoga, meditation, and more. Eligibility to participate in the firm’s 401(k) plan after six months. 36 total days of paid time off, including general PTO, wellness days, personal days, seven paid bank holidays, three floating holidays, and office closure during the last week of the year. Ability to work fully remote for up to two weeks annually; all other weeks are on a hybrid basis. Pre-tax commuter benefits. Memberships to Work Advantage and Perks at Work for discounts on concerts, theme parks, vacation packages, and more. Company-issued mobile phone with data and minutes. How to Apply Please submit your resume along with a cover letter to [email protected] explaining what it is about our work that inspired you to apply for this position. item.title: Director, Federal Affairs and Coalitions
item.description: Director, Federal Affairs and Coalitions Organization: Taxpayers Protection Alliance (TPA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/03/2026 Director, Federal Affairs and Coalitions Location: Washington, D.C. (Hybrid) Reports to: Executive Director About the Role The Taxpayers Protection Alliance (TPA) is seeking a driven and experienced Director of Federal Affairs and Coalitions with a background in financial services issues to serve as the organization’s primary liaison to Congress, federal agencies, and coalition partners on key taxpayer, consumer, and regulatory reform issues. This position requires a proactive government affairs professional who can translate policy priorities into strategic advocacy plans, build bipartisan relationships on Capitol Hill, and help amplify TPA’s voice in Washington. Key Responsibilities Strategic Legislative Engagement: Lead TPA’s outreach to Capitol Hill, developing and maintaining relationships with Members of Congress, key committees, and staff, serving as the organization’s primary point of contact in Congress. Policy Monitoring: Oversee the tracking and analysis of federal legislation, hearings, and regulatory actions that impact taxpayers, consumers, and free markets, and advise leadership on emerging threats and opportunities. Policy Analysis: Research and write about different policy areas with a focus on financial services. Advocacy Strategy: Design and execute legislative strategies, including meetings, briefings, and coalition letters, to advance TPA’s positions. Coalition & Stakeholder Coordination: Represent TPA in coalitions, think-tank networks, and policy roundtables; lead the cultivation of bipartisan and cross-sector partnerships to strengthen TPA’s impact. Communication Support: Collaborate with communications staff to craft compelling policy statements, op-eds, comment letters, and congressional outreach materials for policymakers and media. Event Planning: Direct the planning and execution of Capitol Hill briefings, roundtables, and other high-visibility events to highlight taxpayer-first solutions. Reporting and Project Tracking: Advise leadership and stakeholders on legislative developments, advocacy outcomes, and strategic recommendations. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in political science, public policy, communications, or a related field. 2–5 years of experience in government relations, congressional work, or issue advocacy, ideally focused on fiscal or regulatory policy. Strong understanding of the federal legislative and regulatory process, with proven experience influencing outcomes. Knowledge of, or strong interest in learning about, TPA’s financial services policy portfolio. Experience supervising staff, interns, or junior team members. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to articulate complex issues clearly and persuasively. Demonstrated ability to work effectively in coalitions and build bipartisan relationships. Commitment to TPA’s principles of limited government, fiscal responsibility, and individual liberty. Self-starter with strong organizational skills and attention to detail. Benefits Competitive salary commensurate with experience. Health and dental insurance. Generous, unlimited PTO policy. 401(k) with employer match. Flexible work environment with remote work on Fridays. Annual performance and compensation review, with eligibility for year-end bonus. Opportunity to shape national policy debates in a respected, fast-growing organization. How to Apply To apply, please send your résumé to [email protected] with the subject line Director, Federal Affairs and Coalitions Application . Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today.
