item.title: Vice President of Legislative Advocacy
item.description: Vice President of Legislative Advocacy Organization: National Multifamily Housing Council (NMHC) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/03/2026 About the National Multifamily Housing Council Based in Washington, DC, NMHC is a national association representing the interests of the larger and most prominent apartment firms in the U.S. NMHC advocates on behalf of rental housing, conducts apartment-related research, encourages the exchange of strategic business information, and promotes the desirability of apartment living. NMHC’s members are the principal officers of firms engaged in all aspects of the apartment industry, including ownership, development, management, and financing. More information about the Council is available at https://www.nmhc.org . Position Summary The National Multifamily Housing Council (NMHC) is seeking a skilled, strategic government affairs leader to serve as its Vice President of Legislative Advocacy . Reporting directly to the SVP & Head of Legislative and Political Affairs, this person will oversee the creation and implementation of federal legislative advocacy plans that promote NMHC’s objectives and policy goals. The Vice President will develop and sustain influential relationships with Members of Congress, congressional staff, Executive Branch officials, coalition partners, and industry stakeholders to advance policies supporting the multifamily housing industry. This role functions as a trusted advisor to senior leadership, helping shape NMHC’s legislative agenda while representing the organization before policymakers, members, and external audiences. Essential Responsibilities Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: Develop and execute comprehensive federal legislative advocacy strategies that advance NMHC’s policy objectives and strategic priorities. Collaborate with the President and senior leadership to identify, prioritize, and advance NMHC’s federal legislative agenda. Cultivate and maintain strong bipartisan relationships with Members of Congress, congressional committees, Executive Branch officials, and federal agencies. Represent NMHC before Congress, federal agencies, coalition partners, and other external organizations on issues impacting the multifamily housing industry. Monitor, analyze, and communicate legislative, regulatory, and political developments affecting the rental housing industry, providing timely strategic recommendations to leadership and members. Lead advocacy initiatives that strengthen NMHC’s position as the leading voice for the multifamily housing industry in Washington. Support and advance the mission and activities of NMHC PAC by participating in political events, assisting with fundraising initiatives, contributing to political strategy, and fostering engagement among NMHC members. Develop policy briefs, congressional testimony, comment letters, white papers, position statements, talking points, and other advocacy materials. Coordinate advocacy efforts across NMHC departments to ensure alignment of legislative, regulatory, communications, and member engagement strategies. Develop opportunities for NMHC members to engage directly with federal policymakers through meetings, events, Capitol Hill advocacy activities, and coalition efforts. Build and maintain productive relationships with industry partners, trade associations, coalition organizations, and external stakeholders to advance shared policy objectives. Serve as an internal subject matter expert on federal housing policy, tax policy, capital markets, financial services, regulatory affairs, and other issues affecting the multifamily housing industry. Represent NMHC at conferences, industry meetings, political events, and other speaking engagements. Perform other duties and special projects as assigned. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree in Public Policy, Political Science, Law, Business, or a related field preferred. Minimum of 8–10 years of progressively responsible experience in federal government affairs, legislative advocacy, public policy, congressional affairs, or lobbying. Experience working on Capitol Hill, within the Executive Branch, at a trade association, or in a government relations consulting or advocacy organization. Demonstrated success in developing and implementing federal legislative strategies. Established relationships with Members of Congress, congressional staff, federal agencies, and key policy stakeholders. Experience representing complex policy issues before elected officials and senior government leaders. Knowledge of federal housing, tax, financial services, regulatory, and business policy issues affecting multifamily housing is strongly preferred. Experience working with or supporting a political action committee (PAC) is preferred. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities The successful candidate will demonstrate: Exceptional strategic thinking and political judgment. Outstanding relationship-building and networking abilities. Strong executive presence with the ability to represent NMHC before senior policymakers and industry leaders. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including public speaking and presentation abilities. Ability to synthesize complex legislative and regulatory issues into clear, actionable recommendations. Strong negotiation, consensus-building, and coalition management skills. Superior organizational and project management abilities, with the capacity to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. High level of professionalism, discretion, integrity, and sound judgment. Ability to work collaboratively across departments while also operating independently with minimal supervision. Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and the ability to quickly learn new technology platforms. Working Conditions Position is based in Washington, D.C. Regular attendance at Capitol Hill meetings, federal agencies, coalition meetings, political events, industry conferences, and member functions is required. Occasional domestic travel is required. Application Instructions To apply for this position, please submit the following materials: Cover Letter Resume References Please send materials to [email protected] with the subject line: Vice President of Legislative Advocacy – [Your Last Name] Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Senior Manager of Content and Communications Strategy
item.description: Senior Manager of Content and Communications Strategy Organization: Murmuration Location: Remote Date Posted: 08/03/2026 Description Who We Are At Murmuration, we believe that America’s promise is shaped and reshaped by the best ideas and ideals of its communities, and the dreams of the people who believe in a better life for themselves, their families, and each other. We help organizations build power in their communities in four key ways: we organize a network of values-aligned partners; we provide deep, data-driven insights into people, places, and perspectives; we develop tools that make organizing and engagement easy and more effective; and we offer services that strengthen our partners’ capacity to lead change in their communities. We envision an America where every community has what it needs to help people lead healthy, free, and dignified lives. We work to redesign the systems and structures we all depend on—how we learn, live, govern, and solve problems—so that they are just, equitable, resilient, and rooted in shared responsibility. By strengthening the ties that hold communities together, we aim for civic life defined by collective action and care, with effective leadership that truly represents everyone. We are a collaborative, curious, and creative team of organizers, scientists, teachers, technologists, campaign veterans, and more who share the unwavering belief that we can use our gifts in service of transforming America—together. We’ve built our team guided by the belief that the whole is greater than the sum of its parts. And so we support each other relentlessly, rallying together to face challenges the same way we celebrate each other’s wins. About the Position Murmuration is seeking a Senior Manager of Content and Communications Strategy to lead the development and execution of innovative, high-impact media campaigns. This leader will oversee campaign creative, digital content strategy, and performance-driven advertising in collaboration with internal teams and external partners. The ideal candidate is a strategic thinker with strong creative instincts, a track record of running successful digital campaigns, and deep experience managing both people and vendors. Murmuration’s Campaigns Team helps partners design and execute smarter strategies from the ground up—powered by the best civic data and tools in the country. We provide high-impact consulting and campaign services to local organizations who are closest to solutions. We combine deep campaign expertise with the most advanced civic data infrastructure and offer a full suite of services to help change-makers build power and meet key moments. This role blends strategic leadership, creative development, and digital campaign execution. The Senior Manager will help shape compelling narratives, oversee the production of high-quality content, and ensure campaigns drive measurable outcomes across platforms. Job Level: M4 What You’ll Do Digital & Creative Strategy Lead the development of integrated digital and content strategies that support organizational and partner goals. Conceptualize and oversee cutting-edge digital and media campaigns, including narrative strategy and creative concepts. Translate strategic objectives into high-impact content across platforms including video, social media, digital advertising, and email. Lead the development of creative concepts, messaging frameworks, ad scripts, and direct-to-audience communications (including mail where applicable). Campaign Management & Performance Own the end-to-end process for paid media and digital campaigns, from concept to execution to measurement. Oversee and collaborate closely with digital vendors on paid media strategy, targeting, optimization, and performance reporting. Establish clear KPIs and performance benchmarks, and communicate results to partners and stakeholders in clear, actionable ways. Use data and insights to continuously optimize creative and digital strategies. Team & Partner Leadership Manage and support the Creative Manager, providing mentorship, direction, and strategic guidance. Serve as a key liaison to partner organizations, translating their goals into creative and digital strategies. Build strong relationships with vendors, consultants, and internal teams to ensure alignment and execution excellence. Brand, Content, & Storytelling Ensure all creative and content reflects Murmuration’s values and strengthens brand identity. Elevate the quality and impact of storytelling across campaigns and platforms. Maintain a strong understanding of emerging digital trends, platforms, and technologies to keep campaigns innovative and relevant. Requirements 7–10+ years of experience in content/digital strategy, creative leadership, or campaign management at an agency, political campaign, nonprofit, or mission-driven organization. Demonstrated experience leading high-impact media campaigns with measurable results. Proven ability to manage creative talent and external vendors effectively. Strong portfolio of work showcasing digital storytelling, creative strategy, and performance-driven campaigns. Deep understanding of paid media, digital platforms, content strategy, and analytics. Excellent writing and messaging skills, with experience crafting scripts, digital content, and campaign narratives. Strong project management skills and ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-moving environment. Experience translating complex data and performance metrics into clear insights for partners and stakeholders. Nice to Haves Experience working in political, advocacy, or social impact environments. Familiarity with modern digital organizing and persuasion tools. Experience with polling, audience research, or message testing. Talented Senior Managers come from all walks of life and career. If you are passionate about civic engagement and technology, please apply, even if you do not check every box! Benefits Location and Compensation The Senior Manager of Content and Communications Strategy is a full-time, salaried position with a comprehensive benefits package (details below), open to candidates anywhere in the United States. The starting salary for this position is $212,623 . We set compensation using market data and apply it consistently across the organization to ensure fairness and transparency for everyone in similar roles. Our Culture of Care We work hard to create a culture of care to ensure that our staff are best equipped to lead happy, healthy, and balanced lives. To that end, we offer a comprehensive benefits package which includes: Health, vision, and dental insurance with 100% of premiums covered for you and qualifying family members. Retirement benefits with a 5% employer match. A flexible unlimited PTO plan. Generous paid parental leave. Pre-tax commuter benefits. A company laptop. A flexible remote work environment. A home office setup stipend for all new employees. Monthly reimbursement for remote work expenses. A yearly professional development fund. Mental health and wellness benefits through Calm and BetterHelp. Yearly in-person staff retreats. A welcoming culture that celebrates diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging. At Murmuration, we believe a vibrant, representative democracy depends on the inclusion of diverse voices, lived experiences, and perspectives. The best ideas don’t come from a single person or ideology—they emerge at the intersection of different backgrounds, identities, and viewpoints. We are proud of our commitment to building an organization and culture shaped by respect, empathy, and collaboration, where our team’s diversity fuels innovation, civic engagement, and meaningful change. We welcome new colleagues who will help us nurture this collective effort. Join us. An Equal Opportunity Employer with a Commitment to Diversity Murmuration is proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and as an organization committed to diversity and the perspective of all voices, we consider applicants equally regardless of race, gender, color, sexual orientation, religion, marital status, disability, political affiliation, or national origin. We reasonably accommodate staff members and/or applicants with disabilities, provided they are otherwise able to perform the essential functions of the job. Note: Murmuration is two organizations working together to pursue our mission of amplifying the power of civic engagement: Murmuration Research Institute , a 501(c)(3) that conducts research to identify, design, and create the data, tools, and insights that build healthier and more equitable communities. Murmuration, Inc. , a 501(c)(4) that supports organizations working across the country on the nation’s most challenging issues with access to data, tools, and research that build healthier and more equitable communities. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Head of Brand & Storytelling
item.description: Head of Brand & Storytelling Organization: Kaizen Location: New York, NY Date Posted: 08/03/2026 Compensation Base Salary: $200,000 – $250,000 Offers Equity Government technology has failed the public for decades, and Americans have been conditioned to expect websites from the 90s for essential public services. Kaizen exists to strengthen trust in American public services by building technology that residents and public servants are proud to use. We partner with local, state, and federal agencies to replace legacy systems with modern, AI-native software that is worthy of the people they serve. We started in outdoor recreation, and now we’re building toward something much larger — the software layer that powers how Americans access any government service. Our platform reaches 55 million Americans across 50+ agencies. Our goal is to build technology that touches the lives of 100 million residents by the end of the year. Founded in 2022 and based in New York City, Kaizen has raised $35 million from NEA, a16z, Accel, 776, and Carpenter Capital. We’re builders, designers, and operators who believe that beautifully designed software shouldn’t be a luxury in government. It’s how you earn trust back. The Role Kaizen has built something real: 40 million residents, 50+ agencies, and 17 states. Most people have never heard of us. That changes now. We’re at the point where our brand needs to do serious work: recruit mission-driven talent, win federal contracts, build credibility with investors, and make Kaizen a name that people in government, tech, and public life actually know. This is not a production role—it’s a builder role for the person who figures out what Kaizen’s brand should be and then makes it happen across every channel. You’ll own editorial content, short films, the website, social presence, executive storytelling, and the long game of making this company iconic. You’ll work directly with our co-founders and have the latitude to move fast and make big calls. Location This is a hybrid role based out of our New York City headquarters. Candidates must reside in New York or be able to commute to New York City to work from our office at least three times a week (Tuesdays–Thursdays). What You’ll Do Define and execute Kaizen’s external brand strategy: what we stand for, how we show up, and how we build recognition across government, tech, and the public. Own the content engine, including editorial content (LinkedIn, Substack, long-form writing), short films, YouTube, podcasts, and anything else that puts Kaizen on the map. Write and produce executive communications that travel, including board updates, investor narratives, op-eds, and media appearances. Build toward long-term brand goals and treat distribution as part of the creative work, not an afterthought. Partner with sales and proposal teams to create assets that win contracts, including case studies, one-pagers, and pitch materials. Quarterback external vendors and contractors (PR firms, video production teams, and freelancers), directing their output without becoming dependent on them. What You’ll Bring 6–10 years of experience building brand and content at a company where the brand truly mattered—not just maintaining it, but building it. A portfolio that demonstrates range and a strong point of view, including editorial content, brand systems, video storytelling, executive communications, and evidence that your work reached audiences beyond its original channel. A portfolio link is required as part of your application. Strong instincts for narrative and positioning. You think about why something should exist before you make it. Comfort operating as a one-person function initially, with proven ability to build and scale a team of contractors and full-time employees. An AI-native workflow, using AI tools to scale output and stay ahead of what’s possible. Excellent writing skills, capable of ghostwriting for executives and producing editorial content that earns its own audience. Strong Candidates May Also… Have built a brand function from scratch at an early-stage company before there was a playbook. Have experience in govtech, defense tech, or another industry where buyers are skeptical and the mission is serious. Have grown their own audience (such as a newsletter, YouTube channel, or social following) and understand distribution firsthand. Don’t Apply If… Your portfolio is primarily B2C advertising campaigns, short-form social videos, or content built for large production teams. You require detailed creative briefs, structured processes, or a large team of full-time staff to do your best work. You view brand as a support function that simply executes requests from sales or product teams. You’re not excited by the idea of making Kaizen a recognized name in Washington, D.C., government offices, and the broader conversation about public-sector technology. What Kaizen Offers Health & Insurance 100% coverage for employees across medical (Oxford/United Gold and Platinum PPO plans), dental (Guardian PPO), and vision (Beam), with 100% dependent coverage. $100,000 in fully paid life insurance. Flexible Spending Account (FSA) and Dependent Care FSA. One Medical membership, including same-day primary care, 24/7 virtual visits, and access to offices throughout the city. Fertility and family-building support through Carrot. 401(k) through Guideline with a 2% company match. Family & Time Off 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave for birthing parents. 10 weeks of fully paid parental leave for non-birthing parents. Unlimited PTO with a two-week minimum—we really mean it. Company closed for all federal holidays. Company-wide winter break during the week of Christmas. Company offsites throughout the year. Office & Remote Setup Up to $750 one-time home office or desk setup stipend for New York City-based employees. $500 home office stipend for remote employees. $50 per month commuter benefit (company contribution). Expensed lunch while working in the office. Company-provided laptop of your choice. Wellness Fully covered gym membership at Grindhouse, located directly across from the office at 47 W 17th St. (also available in Williamsburg), valued at approximately $225 per month. Remote employees receive a $100 per month reimbursement for gym memberships or other physical fitness expenses. Stipends $100 per month utility stipend. $500 per year for professional development. $250 per year for recreation. $300 per quarter pet care stipend. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Organic Social Media Strategist
item.description: Organic Social Media Strategist Organization: SeatGeek Location: New York, NY Date Posted: 08/03/2026 SeatGeek believes live events are powerful experiences that unite humans. With our technological savvy and fan-first attitude, we’re simplifying and modernizing the ticketing industry. SeatGeek is looking for an Organic Social Media Strategist to own and reimagine our organic social presence from the ground up—across platforms, across moments, and across the culture that makes live entertainment worth showing up for. From hosting an Instagram Live at an event to responding to fans on Reddit to developing a TikTok content series for the start of the NFL season, this person will own end-to-end strategy and execution across platforms. The Organic Social Media Strategist will report to the Director of Organic Growth and work cross-functionally with content, creative, PR, fan support, and beyond. The ideal candidate brings deep fluency in social media marketing, a genuine love for sports and live entertainment, and a strong instinct for tying great content to real business impact. What You’ll Do Own and manage SeatGeek’s organic social channels end-to-end, including strategy, content creation, scheduling, and publishing across Instagram, TikTok, X, and any emerging platforms worth owning. Develop and execute a cohesive organic social strategy aligned with brand and business goals by defining channel-specific approaches, content pillars, posting cadence, and audience growth tactics that compound over time. Ideate and produce culturally relevant, platform-native content that taps into live events, sports, concerts, and entertainment moments, turning what’s happening in culture into content that drives engagement, shares, and brand love. Stay ahead of trends, conversations, and activity in real time by identifying opportunities for timely reactive content, cultural hijacks, and community engagement that keep SeatGeek part of the conversation. Shoot, edit, and produce short-form video content using self-shot footage, UGC, or provided assets, with a strong eye for storytelling, pacing, hooks, and platform-native formats that stop the scroll. Track, analyze, and report on performance metrics, including reach, engagement, follower growth, and share of voice, and use those insights to continuously optimize content strategy while demonstrating the channel’s business impact. Own community engagement by responding to comments, DMs, and mentions with a voice that feels human, on-brand, and genuinely fun, turning fans into advocates and everyday interactions into brand moments. Collaborate cross-functionally with marketing, partnerships, PR, and creative to support campaigns, product launches, and tentpole moments while keeping the organic social voice consistent and authentic. Build and manage the content calendar, balancing planned campaigns, evergreen content, and real-time opportunities across multiple platforms. Serve as the internal expert and evangelist for organic social by bringing platform insights, algorithm changes, and emerging format recommendations to the broader team while educating stakeholders on what drives results. What You Have 4+ years of experience in organic social media and content strategy, ideally at an e-commerce brand. Experience in sports, live events, or ticketing is a strong plus. A scrappy, can-do work ethic with the ability to operate independently, move quickly, and wear multiple hats without waiting for perfect conditions. Strong organizational skills with experience managing content calendars across multiple platforms and campaigns simultaneously. Fluency in internet culture, with the ability to identify emerging trends, TikTok audio, and viral memes before they peak and translate them into authentic content. A genuine passion for live entertainment and sports, with an instinct for showing up in meaningful ways during major cultural moments. A data-first mindset with strong platform analytics skills and the ability to connect organic social performance to business outcomes and revenue. Excellent interpersonal and cross-functional communication skills, with the ability to clearly articulate social strategy to stakeholders at all levels. Experience partnering with creative teams and executing within brand guidelines while pushing creative boundaries in platform-native ways. Deep familiarity with social search and AI search optimization, understanding how content is discovered across TikTok, Instagram, and emerging AI-powered search experiences. Hands-on content creation experience, including shooting and editing short-form video using CapCut, Adobe Premiere, or similar tools. Comfortable serving as producer, director, and occasionally on-camera talent. Sharp editorial instincts and a distinctive writing voice, with the ability to adapt tone across platforms and write compelling captions that capture attention. A strong creative eye with the ability to develop content concepts, write effective creative briefs, and provide actionable feedback that improves the work. A natural community builder with strong instincts for audience engagement, knowing when to reply, amplify, escalate, and turn everyday interactions into memorable brand moments. Perks Discretionary annual bonus. Flexible work environment, allowing you to work as many days per week in the office as you’d like or 100% remotely. Work-from-home stipend to support your home office setup. Unlimited PTO. Up to 16 weeks of fully paid family leave. 401(k) matching. Student loan matching program. Health, vision, dental, and life insurance. Up to $25,000 toward family building, reproductive health services, and gender-affirming care. $500 per year for wellness expenses. Subscriptions to Headspace (meditation), Headspace Care (therapy), and One Medical. $360 per quarter to spend on tickets to live events. Annual subscription to Spotify, Apple Music, or Amazon Music. Compensation The salary range for this role is $80,000–$116,000 USD . In addition, you may receive a discretionary annual bonus based on individual and company performance. Actual compensation packages are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including, but not limited to, skill set, years and depth of experience, certifications, and specific location. Equal Opportunity Employer SeatGeek is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment regardless of race, color, religion, creed, age, national origin or ancestry, ethnicity, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, disability, military or veteran status, or any other category protected by federal, state, or local law. As an equal opportunity employer, we recognize that diversity is a positive attribute, and we welcome the differences and benefits that a diverse culture brings. Come join us! item.title: Senior Director, Policy Communications
item.description: Senior Director, Policy Communications Organization: Roblox Location: San Mateo, CA | Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/04/2026 **Every day, tens of millions of people come to Roblox to explore, create, play, learn, and connect with friends in 3D immersive digital experiences — all created by our global community of developers and creators.** At Roblox, we’re building the tools and platform that empower our community to bring any experience they can imagine to life. Our vision is to reimagine the way people come together, from anywhere in the world and on any device. We’re on a mission to connect a billion people with optimism and civility, and we’re looking for amazing talent to help us get there. A career at Roblox means you’ll be working to shape the future of human interaction, solving unique technical challenges at scale, and helping to create safer, more civil shared experiences for everyone. — ## Senior Director, Policy Communications Roblox is looking for an experienced communicator to support a wide range of issues, including leading public affairs communications. You will report to the Chief Communications Officer. As a member of the Global Communications and Corporate Affairs team, you will guide the development and implementation of corporate positioning and crisis management on a global scale. You will devise communications materials and campaigns to inform and educate our community, opinion leaders, and media about the benefits of Roblox products, our company culture and values, and our approach to public policy issues. You will follow the regulatory environment that impacts our industry and, as appropriate, work with the policy team to comment on or respond to legislation. You will participate in face‑to‑face meetings with commentators and opinion formers, develop print and web‑based materials supporting these campaigns, and counter misinformation that might interfere with our business and ability to serve our community. This role will ideally be based in either our Washington, DC or San Mateo, CA offices (hybrid Tues–Thurs). — ## You will – **Advise teams** — Collaborate with product, public policy, legal, international expansion, and Trust & Safety teams to help communicate with media and journalists. – **Handle urgent issues** — Manage high‑profile and time‑sensitive matters with calm judgment. – **Build media relationships** — Use your deep understanding of the media landscape to strengthen relationships and develop strategic recommendations. – **Develop global positions** — Create global stances on key issues and strategies for reactive and proactive communications. – **Propose public messaging** — Provide recommendations on regulatory issues and legislation that could affect Roblox. – **Develop campaign strategies** — Educate policymakers and the Roblox community on key issues, in partnership with the policy team. – **Execute crisis communications** — Create and implement crisis communications and risk‑mitigation plans. – **Distill complex concepts** — Partner with Policy teams to translate complex topics into clear communications materials, including regular press outreach. – **Draft content** — Write press releases, blogs, FAQs, and key messages. – **Brief spokespeople** — Prepare spokespeople and staff for interviews and proactively highlight Roblox’s work around trust, safety, and civility. — ## You have – A strong understanding of consumer technology/social media, online safety, content enforcement, and privacy policies. – 12+ years of experience in public affairs, policy communications, and crisis communications. – Experience with global regulations and policies for diverse age ranges of users and creators. – A track record of developing and implementing corporate communications plans aligning internal, external, and partner communications. – Proven performance managing communications in crisis and sensitive situations, including creating clear directives and follow‑up. – Strong relationships with key journalists and influencers in tech, policy, and business press. – Experience as an on‑the‑record spokesperson and communicator on complex topics, including policy or legal issues. — ## Compensation **Annual Salary Range:** $294,030 — $350,620 USD For roles based at our headquarters in San Mateo, CA: Actual base pay depends on professional background, training, work experience, location, business needs, and market demand. In some cases, the actual salary may fall outside this range. This range is subject to change. All full‑time employees are eligible for equity compensation and benefits. Roles based in an office are onsite Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday, with optional presence on Monday and Friday (unless otherwise noted). — ## Equal Opportunity Roblox provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants and prohibits discrimination or harassment of any kind based on race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by law. Roblox also provides reasonable accommodations to candidates with qualifying disabilities or religious beliefs during the recruiting process. — ## Work Authorization (U.S.) For U.S.‑based roles only: The company may not be able to employ candidates who require certain visa categories or support future H‑1B sponsorship at this time. item.title: Director of Congressional Affairs
item.description: Director of Congressional Affairs Organization: Umbra Location: Arlington, VA Date Posted: 08/04/2026 ## Description Umbra is an American space technology company delivering advanced systems—from sensors to spacecraft—that empower customers worldwide with unmatched access to critical information from space. Our mission is simple and ambitious: redefine space for people, systems, and missions in every domain. Umbra’s ecosystem operates through three business units: Remote Sensing (the data), Space Systems (the components), and Mission Solutions (the platforms). Together, our teams develop capabilities that deliver persistent access, resilient performance, and mission‑ready solutions, advancing U.S. space leadership while keeping the world safe and informed. ## About the Job Umbra is seeking a Director of Congressional Affairs to serve as the company’s principal representative to the United States Congress. Redefining space doesn’t happen in orbit alone—it happens in the laws, budgets, and policies that determine what the nation asks of space and who it trusts to deliver. Umbra’s technology provides critical capabilities for U.S. national security, intelligence, and science missions, as well as allied and international customers and commercial applications, from supporting warfighters and decision‑makers with timely intelligence to enabling disaster response, environmental monitoring, and scientific discovery. The Director will bring that mission to Capitol Hill, helping the policymaking community understand these capabilities and the public value they create, and ensuring Congress has the insight it needs to make informed decisions about the future of American space and remote sensing. In this role, the Director will lead Umbra’s legislative strategy, drawing on deep relationships with Members of Congress and committee staff to help shape authorization and appropriations outcomes. The goal is larger than any single legislative win: it is to redefine how Congress understands and invests in U.S. commercial space, building enduring support for the role these capabilities play in keeping the nation secure, informed, and scientifically competitive, with Umbra’s three business units at the center of that story. The ideal candidate has experience working at the highest levels: as counsel or professional staff on a defense, intelligence, or commerce committee, and/or as a senior policy advisor comfortable briefing a Member of Congress on defense, space, and national security matters. They bring firsthand knowledge of how the NDAA, IAA, and relevant appropriations bills are drafted, marked up, conferenced, and defended, and how funding lines are created and sustained. They will pair that legislative craftsmanship with strong commercial instincts and a genuine belief in the mission, identifying new program opportunities through their network and working closely with Umbra’s business development team to translate national needs into enduring programs that serve them. This role will work closely with Umbra’s Director of Public Policy and sits within the Communications organization, which encompasses government relations, marketing, and communications, and reports to the Vice President of Communications. This position is based on‑site in our Arlington, VA office. ## Key Responsibilities – Serve as Umbra’s primary interface with Congress, with emphasis on the House and Senate Armed Services Committees, the Defense Appropriations Subcommittees, the Intelligence Committees, and the commerce and space‑focused authorizing committees. – Lead efforts to transition Umbra capabilities from congressional adds, pilots, and demonstrations into enduring programs within national security space, including drafting and shaping statutory language, report language, and funding lines, and supporting them through markup, conference, and execution. – Build and maintain deep, direct, trusted relationships with Members of Congress and staff, including principals on the defense, intelligence, and appropriations committees and relevant state and district delegations. – Identify new program opportunities, emerging funding lines, and customer requirements early through Hill, committee, and agency networks, and partner with Umbra’s business development team to pursue them. – Design and execute a proactive legislative strategy to advance Umbra’s priorities in the NDAA, IAA, defense and intelligence appropriations, and commercial space, spectrum, and remote sensing policy. – Partner with the Director of Public Policy to align legislative strategy with Umbra’s broader policy agenda. – Support engagement with the executive branch on issues that intersect with Umbra’s legislative agenda across DoD, the IC, and civil space stakeholders. – Prepare and staff Umbra executives for Hill engagements, testimony, briefings, staff delegations, site visits, and classified or controlled discussions as appropriate. – Monitor, analyze, and translate legislative, budgetary, and political developments into clear, actionable insight for Umbra leadership. – Manage outside consultants, lobbying firms, and compliance obligations (LDA filings and related requirements). ## Requirements ### Required Qualifications – Bachelor’s degree in political science, public policy, law, or a related field; or equivalent professional experience. – 12+ years of combined congressional, executive branch, and/or industry government affairs experience. – Senior Capitol Hill service in at least one of the following: counsel or professional staff on a defense, intelligence, armed services, or commerce committee; or senior defense/national security policy advisor in a Member’s personal office, directly briefing and staffing the Member. – Demonstrated legislative craftsmanship: hands‑on experience drafting statutory language, report language, and amendments, and navigating markup, conference, and floor processes for the NDAA, IAA, or appropriations bills. – Proven experience helping move defense, intelligence, or space capabilities into Programs of Record, with specific funding lines, legislative language, or programs the candidate helped create and sustain. – Established, current, direct relationships with Members of Congress and professional staff on the defense, intelligence, appropriations, and/or space‑related committees. – Demonstrated ability to identify new opportunities through congressional and agency channels and translate them into results for a company or program office. – Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to distill complex technical and budgetary issues for Members, staff, and executives alike. ### Desired Qualifications – Advanced degree such as a JD, MPP, MPA, or comparable. – Active TS/SCI security clearance, or eligibility to obtain one. – Self‑starter able to build and run a function independently, set strategy, and work effectively without close supervision. – Executive branch experience in a Senate‑confirmed, appointed, or senior career role (OSD, service legislative liaison, NRO/NGA, NTIA, FCC, OMB, or White House). – Experience representing a high‑growth space, defense tech, or telecommunications company, or a relevant trade association. – Experience planning or leading congressional staff delegations (STAFFDELs/CODELs), site visits, and Member‑level engagements with operational commands and programs. – Familiarity with export control regimes (ITAR/EAR) as they affect commercial space. – Passion for space, technology, and national security, driving a deeper understanding of Umbra’s mission and audiences. ## Benefits – Flexible Time Off, Sick, Family & Medical Leave – Medical, Dental, Vision, Life, LTD, STD (employer funded) – Vol Life, Critical Illness, Accidental, Hospital Indemnity, Pet Insurance (employee funded) – 401k with 3% non‑elective company contribution – Stock Options – Free Parking – Free lunch daily in office Umbra is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We do not discriminate in hiring on the basis of sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religious creed, national origin, physical or mental disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law. ## Employment Eligibility Verification In compliance with federal laws, all hired persons will be required to verify their identity and eligibility to work in the United States by completing the required Employment Eligibility Verification Form (I‑9 Form) upon hire. ## ITAR/EAR Requirements This position may include access to technology and/or data subject to U.S. export controls pursuant to ITAR and EAR. To comply with federal export controls, all persons hired must be a U.S. citizen, U.S. national, U.S. lawful permanent resident, refugee, or asylee as defined by 8 U.S.C. § 1324b(a)(3), or must otherwise be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State and/or U.S. Department of Commerce. ## Pay Transparency This job posting may cover multiple career levels. To ensure greater transparency, we provide base salary ranges for all roles, regardless of location. Our standard pay ranges are based on the role’s function and level, benchmarked against similar growth‑stage companies. Compensation may vary based on geographical location, as certain regions may have different cost‑of‑living factors. The final offer will also be influenced by the candidate’s skills, responsibilities, and relevant experience. ### Compensation Range The Compensation Range for this role is $225,000 – $275,000 DOE. item.title: Vice President of Public Policy
item.description: Vice President of Public Policy Organization: Philanthropy Ohio Location: Remote (OH) Date Posted: 08/04/2026 ## Salary $95,000 – $115,000 ## Background Philanthropy Ohio is a statewide membership association that leads and equips Ohio philanthropy to be effective partners for change in our communities. Working toward a vision of a just and vibrant Ohio through impactful philanthropy, our dedicated staff helps members achieve their charitable goals by advocating, educating, convening and collaborating – all while centering equity. ## Position Summary The Vice President of Public Policy is a dynamic leadership role that shapes and advances Philanthropy Ohio’s public policy strategy at the state and federal levels. As the organization’s primary policy advocate, this leader will engage, convene and mobilize Philanthropy Ohio’s diverse membership to identify shared policy priorities and amplify the collective voice of philanthropy across Ohio. Working at the intersection of policy, relationship‑building and member engagement, the Vice President will cultivate constellations of public policy work across the state – connecting foundations, community leaders and partners around common issues and opportunities for impact. Through these networks, the Vice President will foster collaboration, elevate member voices and help transform local expertise into statewide influence. The Vice President will guide interested members along the advocacy engagement spectrum, meeting them where they are and helping them take meaningful next steps that complement their funding priorities through active advocacy. This role provides strategic vision and oversight for all public policy initiatives, leads member‑driven policy affinity groups, serves as Philanthropy Ohio’s primary registered lobbyist and manages the staff and consultants who support its advocacy efforts. The Vice President also collaborates closely with coalition partners to advance shared policy priorities and takes on special projects that further the organization’s mission and strategic goals. This is a full‑time, exempt position reporting to the President & CEO. The position may be based anywhere in Ohio, with regular travel to Columbus and statewide to engage with legislators, state leaders, Philanthropy Ohio members and key partners. ## Primary Responsibilities ### Public Policy Strategy & Advocacy – Shape and advance Philanthropy Ohio’s state and federal public policy agenda, advancing policies that strengthen Ohio’s communities and the charitable sector. – Serve as the organization’s primary public policy expert and advocate. Translate complex legislative and regulatory developments into timely, practical guidance including policy briefs, action alerts and educational resources for members in collaboration with the Public Policy and Grants Director. – Represent Philanthropy Ohio before state and federal policymakers, legislative bodies and sector partners, including providing testimony, engaging with contract lobbyists and serving as the organization’s lead spokesperson on public policy issues. ### Member Engagement & Field Leadership – Activate and mobilize members through meaningful opportunities for learning, advocacy, leadership and collective action. – Working with the Network Engagement Director, cultivate member networks, committees and coalitions that elevate shared priorities that strengthen the philanthropic sector and advance shared policy priorities. – Lead signature advocacy initiatives, including Foundations on the Hill in Washington, D.C., Philanthropy at the Statehouse in Columbus and other public policy events. ### Partnership & Coalition Building – Build and sustain strategic relationships with policymakers, government agencies, philanthropy‑infrastructure organizations, coalition partners and other stakeholders to amplify philanthropy’s collective voice and advance shared policy goals. ### Organizational Leadership – Provide leadership across the organization as a member of the Leadership Team, contributing to strategic planning, organizational priorities, revenue generation and culture. – Lead and develop the public policy team and external consultants by setting departmental priorities and stewarding resources to maximize impact. ### Cross‑Departmental Collaboration – Work closely with the Communications & Membership team to develop compelling policy communications, advocacy campaigns and member engagement strategies. – Collaborate with the Programs & Learning team to design educational offerings, convenings and learning opportunities that help members understand and engage in public policy and advocacy. ## Preferred Qualifications for this Position – Deep experience in philanthropy and understanding of how different types of foundations can legally engage in public policy and advocacy work. – Specific knowledge of public policy issues in Ohio and the U.S. (including health, education, housing, democracy, charitable giving and sector issues). – Deep experience understanding how policies are formed, influenced, adopted and implemented. – Experience navigating the political system to achieve desired outcomes. – Experience in a membership association. – Supervisory experience. – Four‑year college degree preferred. ## Qualifications Common to all Positions at Philanthropy Ohio – Commitment to our core values of Community, Courage, Voice, Integrity and Equity. – Experience with organized philanthropy. – Attention to detail and ability to produce high‑quality, timely work products. – Communicate effectively in a variety of settings and styles. – Work collaboratively in a team environment. – Willingness to be flexible in working remotely and on‑site. – Use time and resources well and ability to manage multiple projects and shifting priorities. – Approach responsibilities creatively and innovatively with the goal of continuous improvement. – Proficient with Microsoft Office, Zoom, Slack, Salesforce and project management tools. ## Salary & Compensation At Philanthropy Ohio, we believe great work happens when people are supported both professionally and personally. The pay band for this role is $95,000–$115,000. Our comprehensive benefits package includes: – 3 weeks of vacation – 2 weeks of office‑wide closures for rest & reset (1 week each in July and December) – 15 days of accrued sick leave – 8 paid holidays – Half‑day Fridays all year long – 8 weeks of parental leave benefits – 401k retirement benefits – Paid parking – Employer‑sponsored medical, dental, vision and disability & life insurance As a remote‑first organization, this position offers the flexibility to work from anywhere in Ohio while staying closely connected to colleagues, members and partners through meaningful in‑person engagement and travel across the state as needed. ## Application Apply by sending your cover letter and resume to [email protected] by August 28. Philanthropy Ohio is an equal opportunity employer. There shall be no discrimination of persons on the basis of race, age, sex, marital status, disability, citizenship, religion, national origin, sexual orientation, political affiliation or belief with regard to hiring, assignment, promotion or other conditions of staff employment. item.title: Government Affairs Policy Counsel/Advocate
item.description: Government Affairs Policy Counsel/Advocate Organization: Public Knowledge Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/04/2026 ## Government Affairs Policy Counsel/Advocate **Position Summary:** The Government Affairs Policy Counsel/Advocate will play a key role in developing and implementing Public Knowledge’s government affairs strategy, through advocacy, strategy development, and relationship building in Congress, at Federal agencies, within the Executive Branch, and across the public interest field. **Position Status:** Full-time **Location:** Washington, D.C. **Reports to:** Director of Government Affairs — ## Essential Duties – Assist in developing and implementing Public Knowledge’s advocacy strategy and approach to Capitol Hill on various issues like broadband access and deployment, affordability, and universal service. There will also be opportunities to work on emerging issues like satellite and spectrum policy, as well as artificial intelligence. – Obtain up-to-date information on technology matters before Congress. – Meet with key policymakers at the Federal Communications Commission, National Telecommunications and Information Administration, the White House, Congress, and elsewhere to build support for Public Knowledge’s priorities. – Convene and work in coalitions with various stakeholder groups to develop priorities and strategies. – Research and draft congressional testimony for legislative hearings on telecommunications/technology policy issues and help prepare witnesses for hearings. – Serve as a resource to allies and other non‑D.C.-based groups in building advocacy strategy and relationships with policymakers. – Coordinate development of Public Knowledge advocacy materials. – Serve as a spokesperson and resource to the media within areas of expertise. — ## Qualifications – A college graduate with a passion for public policy, knowledge, and interest in technology, and a demonstrated interest in the political process and advocacy in the public interest. – Law or other graduate degrees a plus. – 1–3 years or more experience with Capitol Hill, Federal agencies, or other relevant policy-related experience. – Familiarity with legislative efforts on technology policy preferred. – Experience conducting legislative or issue advocacy and developing partnerships with a wide range of organizations and constituencies. – Experience drafting legal/advocacy documents such as briefs and model legislation preferred. – Full comprehension of the influences of the regulatory and government agencies. – Demonstrated ability to create advocacy strategies. – Ability to work in a fast-paced environment and manage multiple projects simultaneously. – Sound judgment and ability to analyze situations and information. – Strong communications skills. – A creative self‑starter who can devise new, innovative outreach methods. – A willingness and ability to learn complex technological and legal issues quickly. – The ability to produce high‑quality results on tight deadlines and with little oversight. — ## Compensation Base salary from $77,000–$100,000 depending on experience, plus excellent benefits and opportunities for professional growth. — ## About Public Knowledge Public Knowledge is a nonprofit technology policy organization that promotes freedom of expression, an open internet, and access to affordable communications tools and creative works. PK’s modes of advocacy include outreach to the U.S. Congress, the executive branch, and administrative agencies, filing administrative comments, submitting amicus briefs, hosting public education events, building coalitions, and writing white papers and blog posts. For more information on us, visit PublicKnowledge.org. Public Knowledge provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training. item.title: Manager: Government Relations
item.description: Manager: Government Relations Organization: Radiological Society of North America (RSNA) Location: Washington, DC | Oak Brook, IL Date Posted: 08/04/2026 ## Salary Range $70,000.00 to $75,000.00 Annually ## What We’re Looking For We are seeking a talented professional responsible for helping advance federal policy priorities that affect radiology, imaging research, technology innovation, and patient care. The **Manager: Government Relations** role is ideal for a public policy or government relations professional who can monitor complex legislative and regulatory developments, translate policy issues into clear member‑facing communications, and provide strong project coordination for a growing advocacy function. As part of a small, high‑impact team, this role will partner with the **Director: Government Relations** in strengthening RSNA’s federal advocacy presence, coordinating engagement with policymakers and partner organizations, and ensuring RSNA members and leaders have timely, accessible, and actionable information on priority policy topics. The Manager: Government Relations will spearhead the department’s communications strategy, coordinating efforts across multiple channels to elevate the visibility and credibility of RSNA advocacy, while serving as the primary owner of advocacy operations—maintaining the systems and workflows needed to drive department priorities, coordinate deliverables, and demonstrate progress and impact. — ## This Job Might Be for You If You’re Interested In – Working at a not‑for‑profit, mission‑based organization focused on its members. – A welcoming and supportive environment that gives you an opportunity to impact patient care. – Excellent work‑life balance in a remote workplace environment. – A competitive compensation package that includes outstanding medical/dental benefits, long‑term savings benefits, generous time off (including a week‑long Winter Break), paid parental leave, and more. – Training and professional development opportunities. — ## What You’ll Do ### Policy Monitoring, Research, and Analysis Monitor and analyze federal legislative, regulatory, and agency developments relevant to RSNA priorities. Translate complex policy information into clear summaries, memoranda, reports, and other tools that support proactive engagement, timely advocacy, and informed decision‑making. ### Strategic Communications Collaborate with RSNA’s Public Information and Communications team to lead RSNA Government Relations communications—including the monthly *RSNA Washington Update* e‑newsletter, web content, social media language, and internal updates. Translate complex policy developments into timely, accessible information that informs members, supports leadership and volunteer engagement, and strengthens the visibility and credibility of RSNA advocacy. ### Advocacy and Stakeholder Engagement Support RSNA’s engagement with congressional offices, federal agencies, partner societies, coalitions, and other stakeholders. Identify opportunities for RSNA members to inform federal policy development, prepare briefing and advocacy materials (e.g., testimony, talking points, issue briefs), facilitate meeting logistics, and represent RSNA at relevant policy convenings as appropriate. ### Committee and Department Operations Serve as staff liaison for the RSNA Government Relations Committee alongside the Director of Government Relations. Manage systems, workflows, and coordination needed to support committee and department priorities, including meeting preparation and follow‑up, SharePoint resource management, internal reporting, project timelines, and status tracking that keep activities organized, visible, and aligned with RSNA goals. — ## What You’ll Need ### Education – Bachelor’s degree in health or public policy, science, political science, or related field. ### Experience – 3–5 years of relevant professional experience in government relations, public policy, advocacy, health policy, science policy, legislative affairs, regulatory affairs, congressional or agency affairs, or the nonprofit medical/scientific association space. – Minimum of three years required. ### Skills – Strong understanding of federal legislative and regulatory processes and entities (e.g., U.S. Congress; Department of Health and Human Services; Food and Drug Administration; National Institutes of Health). – Excellent research, analysis, and project management skills. – Superb verbal and written communication abilities. – Demonstrated ability to build effective working relationships and communicate confidently with physicians, researchers, policymakers, senior staff, and external partners. ### Additional – Ability to work independently in a fully remote environment while communicating proactively and collaborating effectively with a small team. – While RSNA Government Relations team members are based in Washington, DC, the organization’s headquarters and most staff are based in Oak Brook, IL. Occasional travel to Illinois required. – Travel and attendance at in‑person events and meetings in the metro DC area required. — ## Equal Opportunity Statement The Radiological Society of North America is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind. RSNA is committed to hiring and employing qualified people without regard to race, color, religion, sex, marital status, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, citizenship status, genetic information, sexual orientation, unfavorable military discharge, ancestry, order of protection status, pregnancy, or any other legally protected characteristic. All employment decisions at RSNA are based on business needs, job requirements, and individual qualifications. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: U.S. Federal Public Affairs Manager #26-74568
item.description: U.S. Federal Public Affairs Manager #26-74568 Organization: Sempra Infrastructure Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/04/2026 ## Job Description ### Primary Purpose This role serves as one of Sempra Infrastructure’s highest‑level policy strategists, responsible for shaping direction across complex legislative and regulatory landscapes. Provides expert counsel to executives, leads high‑stakes external engagements, and drives multi‑year, enterprise‑wide public policy strategies with broad business impact. ### Duties and Responsibilities – Anticipates major regulatory and legislative shifts and develops long‑range policy strategies to mitigate risk and maximize opportunity. – Leads high‑stakes engagements with federal agencies, legislative leaders, and multi‑stakeholder coalitions. – Shapes national‑level advocacy agendas and develops frameworks for emerging or cross‑industry policy issues. – Crafts authoritative policy documents that define organizational viewpoints on complex or sensitive issues. – Advises executives on regulatory strategy, including negotiation tactics and scenario planning. – Represents the organization in multi‑organization alliances addressing broad societal, economic, or environmental challenges. – Builds and maintains high‑level relationships with major policy influencers, think tanks, academic partners, and external experts. – Oversees enterprise‑wide alignment of policy messaging, ensuring consistency across business units. – Creates and edits policies, reports, manuals, and other documents, ensuring accuracy, organization, and compliance with requirements. – Identifies, analyzes, and retrieves legal information to support decision making and business needs. – Ensures adherence to applicable laws, regulations, guidelines, and business requirements. – Identifies, assesses, and mitigates risks through appropriate strategies, controls, policies, and procedures. – Communicates information effectively through clear, audience‑focused, and compelling narratives. – Performs other duties as assigned. — ## Qualifications ### Education Typically requires a 4‑year degree in a relevant field, or equivalent combination of education and related experience. Preferred: Four‑year degree with relevant study in economics, history, international affairs, law, political science, or related field. ### Experience Typically requires 12 years of related experience. Preferred experience with the U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, particularly on natural gas policy. Knowledge of, or engagement in, U.S. regulatory and legislative processes. ### Knowledge, Skills and Abilities – Ability to anticipate political trends and assess long‑term advocacy implications. – Ability to contribute directly to functional or enterprise strategy. – Ability to guide high‑risk advocacy initiatives with broad organizational impact. – Comprehensive knowledge of legislative and regulatory environments across jurisdictions. – Knowledge of advanced coalition‑building and stakeholder engagement approaches. – Skill in advising executives on strategic lobbying priorities. – Skill in developing innovative lobbying strategies in complex environments. – Knowledge of key business concepts and the ability to apply business insights to support informed decision making. – Ability to build and maintain productive professional relationships and business partners, clients, and stakeholders. – Plans, implements, monitors, and improves communication channels within and across organizations. – Knowledge of laws governing the rights, relationships, and conduct of companies, organizations, and businesses. — ## Work Schedule **HYBRID:** Work a combination of onsite and remote days each week, typically 4 days per week onsite. ## Area of Interest External Affairs / Marketing / Communications ## Full Time / Part Time Full‑time — ## Total Rewards Philosophy **Note:** The Company strives to ensure that employees are paid equitably and competitively. Starting salaries may vary based on factors such as relevant experience, qualifications, and education. Sempra Infrastructure offers a competitive total rewards package that goes beyond base salary. This position is eligible for an annual performance‑based incentive (bonus) as well as merit‑based recognition. Company benefits include health and welfare (medical, dental, vision), employer contributions to retirement benefits, life insurance, paid time off, as well as other company offerings such as tuition reimbursement, paid parental leave, and employee assistance programs. — ## Location Washington D.C.‑9328 ## Job Details ### Pay Range $173,500.00 – $305,500.00 / year ### Pay Transparency In order to support the Fair Compensation Strategy by the U.S. Government, HR departments and clients are required to adhere to “Pay Transparency Law” in impacted states that mandate employers to list salary ranges in job advertisements or postings for job opportunities and job promotions. item.title: Lead Public & Media Relations Strategist
item.description: Lead Public & Media Relations Strategist Organization: Southern Poverty Law Center (SPLC) Location: Atlanta, GA | Jackson, MS | Miami, FL | Montgomery, AL | New Orleans, LA | Washington DC Date Posted: 08/04/2026 ## The Lead, Public and Media Relations Strategist The Lead, Public and Media Relations Strategist will develop and implement targeted public and media relations plans to support the organization’s goals, securing high-profile political and issues-based media coverage and managing press interactions. This role demands strong communication skills, a collaborative mindset, and a strategic orientation to advance the organization’s mission through effective media engagement. — ## Who You Are ### Political & Policy Acumen Demonstrates a deep understanding of the legislative, political, and advocacy landscape to translate complex policy issues into compelling, accessible messages and proactively adapt communications strategies to evolving political developments. ### Strategic Skilled at translating complex narratives into compelling media stories with minimal direction. Experienced in crafting and executing effective and strategic public and media relations campaigns across national, regional, state, local, and niche markets with clear timelines. ### Connector Skilled at advising and engaging with senior leaders and diverse stakeholders. Proven ability to build and maintain strong relationships with journalists, editors, and influencers to secure impactful media placements across print, digital, and broadcast platforms. ### Proactive Proven experience creating compelling media pitches for complex stories that engage journalists, editors, and producers. Monitors breaking news to identify media engagement opportunities. ### Results-Driven Experienced in measuring PR campaign impact with metrics aligned to organizational goals and uses data-driven insights to refine tactics and enhance engagement. Skilled in designing frameworks to track satisfaction, engagement, and participation; evaluating the effectiveness of strategies and initiatives. ### Versatile Skilled at working under pressure, managing multiple tasks, solving problems, and adapting to shifting priorities. Experienced in meeting deadlines while maintaining clear communication with supervisors and colleagues. ### Communicative Skilled at creating targeted, well-written communications materials to enhance the organization’s mission and visibility with key audiences. ### Knowledgeable Knowledgeable about mission-driven nonprofits and effective communication strategies to raise awareness, engage supporters, and promote transparency in an authentic way. ### Mission-Focused and Values-Aligned Creates authentic, culturally aware communications that advance the organization’s mission and social justice values while honoring the lived experiences and dignity of the communities served. — ## What You’ll Do Coordinate with internal and external colleagues to strategize and plan for issue-specific messaging that reflects organizational and departmental goals and mission, and attend and lead meetings with colleagues to maintain up-to-date knowledge of current media strategy needs. Lead the creation, development, and advancement of strategic public and media relations plans and regularly assess the effectiveness of public and media relations strategies, providing detailed reports and recommendations for improvement. Draft materials such as recommendations, executive summaries, press releases, media advisories, op-eds, letters to the editor, press conference schedules, speeches, key messages, talking points, and update website content with relevant information. Book organizational experts in print media, radio, and TV to elevate the organization’s work, take advantage of opportunities in the news cycle, and provide media-related support, such as training and coaching spokespeople on messaging and interview tactics. Use strong organizational skills to manage multiple projects simultaneously, ensuring timely and successful execution of media campaigns. Field press inquiries daily and manage earned media events such as press conferences. Build, develop, and maintain relationships with regional and national news media members. Track breaking news associated with litigation, legislation, and public policy and work on rapid response communication tactics and strategies. Train, mentor, and coach other staff and may supervise interns. Perform other duties as required or assigned which are reasonably within the scope of the duties in this job classification. — ## Minimum Qualifications We are committed to equitable hiring practices; therefore, you must meet the minimum qualifications to be considered for the role. – Minimum seven (7) years of public relations agency, media relations, and public education campaign work; and – High School Diploma or GED. — ## Compensation & Benefits This is an exempt role, and the minimum starting salary is $78,832 annually. Salary is commensurate with experience. — ## Where & How You’ll Work This role has the following work designation options: **Local Remote:** Will work remotely but is expected to attend work-related activities that occur at the SPLC offices or in the states in which the SPLC operates. **Telework:** Will work at an SPLC office at least three days per week and may work two days per week from an alternative work location. This position will report to the Deputy Director, Public & Media Relations. — ## Other Special Considerations This job is performed under general office conditions and is not subject to any strenuous physical demands or dangerous conditions. This position is represented by the Washington-Baltimore News Guild. Works some evenings and/or weekends in the event of breaking news. — ## Disclaimer The statements herein are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by the employee in this position. These statements are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required of a person in this position. — ## An Equal-Opportunity Employer with a Commitment to Diversity Southern Poverty Law Center (SPLC) is proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and as an organization committed to diversity and the perspective of all voices, we consider applicants equally without regard to age, caregiver status, color, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender expression, gender identity, marital status, national origin, on the basis of genetic information, political affiliation, pregnancy, or veteran status. item.title: Public Affairs/Media Relations Specialist 2
item.description: Public Affairs/Media Relations Specialist 2 Organization: Tatitlek Corp. Location: Arlington, VA Date Posted: 08/04/2026 ## Overview The Public Affairs/Media Relations Specialist reports to the Diplomatic Security Service Front Office. This position provides diverse and complex services in support of internal and external communications and provides professional and extensive research, writing, and project management support in the day‑to‑day operations of the office. This position is assigned to the Diplomatic Security Service Front Office as part of the communications team. ## MAJOR DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES Advises program offices on media issues, developing and implementing proactive strategies for delivering messaging to targeted internal and external audiences via digital, print, and broadcast platforms, and produces after‑action analysis on the impact of those initiatives. Develops and executes crisis communications initiatives as required. Acts as the messaging subject matter expert on assigned portfolios and coordinates with other elements of the Department, law enforcement partners, and the interagency on implementation of one‑voice messaging. Responds to journalists’ queries for information or imagery as required; proactively conceives of and engages media on projects to educate and inform audiences and promote the Bureau; and acts as after‑hours/weekend press duty officer on a rotating basis. Drafts and edits expert high‑level written products including press guidance, speeches, talking points, social media and web content, brochures, scripts, executive memos, award submissions, and other materials as needed. Manages messaging special projects and events as needed, advising office leadership and overseeing development and implementation. Provides guidance to the multimedia specialist and, in his/her absence, acts as primary multimedia specialist providing photography and video support and internal and external web management. Serves as an informational resource to office staff and Bureau program offices, assisting with research on virtually any aspect of the Bureau. Performs other duties of a similar nature or level as the mission dictates. ## PROFESSIONAL QUALIFICATIONS / SKILLS Must be a U.S. citizen and possess, at minimum, a Secret security clearance, with eligibility to obtain and maintain a Top‑Secret security clearance. Must possess a bachelor’s degree with at least five years of experience or an equivalent combination of formal education. Minimum of 5 years’ experience in governmental public affairs and media relations (social media content creation, posting, scheduling, and tracking metrics); foreign policy, international law enforcement, and security experience preferred. Expert, specific knowledge of contemporary journalism standards, ethics, and techniques; newsroom experience preferred. Demonstrates a high level of writing, editing, and proofreading skills. Fluent in multimedia and digital communications platforms and web content management systems. Proficient in digital photography, including digital camera operation and editing. Must be able to demonstrate a high level of writing, editing, and proofreading skills. Ability to handle multiple tasks simultaneously, work independently, and perform in a high‑pressure, fast‑paced environment with rapidly changing priorities. Able to travel domestically and internationally as required. Ability to meet deadlines and work across Department offices at all levels. ## REASONABLE ACCOMMODATIONS Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. ## SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES No. ## WORK ENVIRONMENT A professional office in which typical office equipment and information technology is used. ## PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS The physical demands described must be met by an employee to perform the essential functions of the job. The employee must be able to: see, hear, and speak; lift objects weighing up to 20 pounds; sit for extended periods; and use a personal computer and typical peripheral devices. ## TRAVEL No. ## WORK AUTHORIZATION / SECURITY CLEARANCE Must be a U.S. citizen and possess, at minimum, a Secret security clearance, with eligibility to obtain and maintain a Top‑Secret security clearance. ## ADDITIONAL QUALIFYING FACTORS Must have the ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance. A satisfactory background screening, negative drug test, positive references, and proof of identity and legal authorization to work in the United States are required. As an equal opportunity employer, The Tatitlek Corporation recognizes that our strength lies in our people. Discrimination and all unlawful harassment, including sexual harassment, in employment is not tolerated. We encourage success based on our individual merits and abilities without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, marital status, citizenship status, military status, protected Veteran status, or employment. ## BENEFITS For more information please visit: [https://careers-tatitlek.icims.com/] **Salary:** $142,958.40 annually ** Apply for this job online ** Earn a certificate with the Council!
