item.title: Director of Marketing and Communications
item.description: Director of Marketing and Communications Organization: United Motorcoach Association (UMA) Location: Alexandria, VA Date Posted: 08/04/2026 The Director of Marketing & Communications is an individual contributor leadership role and is responsible for developing and executing a comprehensive marketing, communications, branding, and member engagement strategy that advances the mission of the United Motorcoach Association (UMA). This position leads the organization’s marketing initiatives, strengthens member and industry communications, enhances brand awareness, supports membership growth and retention, and promotes UMA’s educational programs, advocacy efforts, events, and strategic initiatives. The ideal candidate is a strategic thinker and creative leader who combines strong marketing expertise with exceptional communication skills and experience serving associations or membership-based organizations. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: Strategic Marketing Leadership Work with Marketing Committee to develop and implement a comprehensive annual marketing and communications strategy aligned with UMA’s strategic plan. Build awareness of UMA’s value proposition among members, prospective members, industry partners, and stakeholders. Establish measurable marketing goals and key performance indicators (KPIs). Manage the organization’s brand identity and ensure consistency across all platforms. Communications Lead all internal and external communications. Develop compelling messaging for members, prospects, sponsors, legislators, media, and industry partners. Oversee production of: Daily Newsletters Website content Online UMA Town Hall Crisis communications when necessary Infographics Serve as editorial leader for member publications and digital content. Create webinar series, podcasts, or other appropriate communications vehicles as directed by Marketing Committee. Deliver presentations to selected industry regional meetings about UMA activities. Digital Marketing Direct digital marketing strategy across: Website Email marketing Social media Search engine optimization (SEO) Digital advertising Video and multimedia Monitor website performance and user experience. Utilize analytics to optimize campaigns and member engagement. Membership Marketing Develop campaigns that drive: Member acquisition Member retention Member engagement Promote member benefits, educational resources, advocacy initiatives, and networking opportunities. Collaborate with membership staff and Membership Committee on recruitment and retention initiatives. Events Marketing Lead marketing strategy for: Annual Expo Educational meetings Association programs Develop attendee recruitment campaigns. Support exhibitor and sponsorship marketing efforts. Increase event attendance through integrated marketing campaigns. Brand Management Protect and strengthen UMA’s brand across all communications. Develop brand standards and messaging guidelines. Ensure consistency across print, digital, and event materials. Analytics & Performance Track campaign performance using marketing analytics. Measure: Website traffic Email engagement Social media performance Membership campaign effectiveness Event marketing ROI Provide regular reports and recommendations to leadership. Performs all other duties as assigned. Required Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Communications, Public Relations, Journalism, Business, or related field. 5-7 years of progressively responsible marketing and communications experience. Experience leading integrated marketing campaigns. Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills. Strong project management and organizational abilities. Experience managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. Ability to travel Travel of approximately 4-8 events per year is required for conferences, industry events, and member engagement activities. Proficiency with: CRM systems Email marketing platforms Social media management Google Analytics Microsoft Office Preferred Experience with nonprofit trade associations or membership organizations. Familiarity with the transportation, travel, tourism, or motorcoach industry. Experience marketing conferences and large-scale events. Knowledge of advocacy communications and government affairs messaging. COMPETENCIES: Strategic Leadership Brand Development Marketing Strategy Content Development Digital Marketing Member Engagement Event Marketing Budget Management Data-Driven Decision Making Relationship Building Creativity and Innovation Excellent Communication Skills PHYSICAL DEMANDS: While performing the duties of this job, the individual must be able to remain in a stationary position for 90 percent of the time while operating their computer and performing office work. The individual needs to occasionally move about inside the office. They constantly operate a computer and other office productivity machinery, such as a calculator, copy machine, fax machine, and computer printer. They must be able to exchange accurate information with customers and others in the office while interacting. The employee must regularly move up to 15 pounds and occasionally up to 25 pounds. The individual must be capable of reviewing their work for errors and make adjustments as necessary. This role requires regular computer use, virtual and in-person meetings, and occasional evening or weekend work related to conferences, events, or urgent communications needs. WORK ENVIRONMENT: While performing the duties of this Job, the individual is occasionally exposed to moving mechanical parts. The noise level in the work environment is usually low to moderate. The individual frequently works in a controlled climate. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Associate Director, Government Affairs and Policy
item.description: Associate Director, Government Affairs and Policy Organization: Travere Therapeutics Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/04/2026 Be a part of a global team that is inspired to make a difference in the lives of people living with rare disease. At Travere Therapeutics, we recognize that our exceptional employees are vital to our success. We are a dedicated team focused on meeting the unique needs of rare patients. Our work is rewarding – both professionally and personally – because we are making a difference. We are passionate about what we do. We are seeking talented individuals who will thrive in our collaborative, diverse, fast-paced environment and share in our mission – to identify, develop and deliver life-changing therapies to people living with rare disease. We stick by our values centered on patients, courage, community, and collaboration to pursue our vision of becoming a leading biopharmaceutical company dedicated to the delivery of innovation and hope to patients in the global rare disease community. At Travere Therapeutics, we are in rare for life. We continue to courageously forge new paths as we move toward a common goal of elevating science and service for rare patients. This position is responsible for the development and execution of Travere Therapeutics’ federal and state policy strategies across current and future therapeutic area franchises. The position provides strategic policy leadership, informs enterprise positioning, represents the company with external stakeholders to shape the rare disease policy environment, and serves as a trusted advisor to executive leadership. This position reports to the Vice President, Government Affairs and Policy and is remote based. Responsibilities: Drives the development and implementation of proactive policy strategies that align with, advance, and protect Travere Therapeutics’ reputation, business goals and success. Translate emerging policy trends into actionable insights and recommendations for cross-functional stakeholders. Designs and leads implementation of identified strategic plans to address policy threats and opportunities in issue areas related to rare disease drug development, therapeutic areas related to diagnosis, treatment and access; and other issues as assigned. Develops Travere Therapeutics’ position on major issues by federal and state lawmakers and related health agencies. In collaboration with Government Affairs and Policy colleagues, monitor and analyze federal and state legislative, regulatory, and policy developments affecting Travere. Prepare meeting materials, policy briefs, and internal strategy documents. Develop executive-level briefing materials, policy analyses, stakeholder engagement resources, and strategic planning documents to support informed decision-making and advocacy efforts. Plays an important role in building and maintaining strong working relationships with select key external stakeholders, including but not limited to federal and state legislators, HHS (including CMS) and other Executive Branch agencies, the Administration, think tanks, and other third parties. Aligns direction and prioritization for the organization’s policy activities within the broader Corporate Affairs strategy. Leads engagement with state policymakers, state agencies, and other key stakeholders in partnership with the Director, Government Affairs and Policy, coordinating enterprise advocacy strategies and policy priorities. Collaborates closely with Corporate Affairs colleagues, as well as with internal stakeholders, including Patient Advocacy and Commercial. Responsible for interfacing with both professional and patient groups involved with activities related to rare diseases. Establishes strategic goals, success metrics, and operational priorities for assigned policy initiatives and monitors progress against organizational objectives. Other duties as assigned. Education/Experience Requirements: Bachelor’s degree in Political Science, Public Administration, or related discipline. Advanced degree a plus. Equivalent combination of education and applicable job experience may be considered. Minimum 8 years of progressively responsible experience in government affairs, health policy, or pharmaceutical policy, including demonstrated leadership of complex cross-functional initiatives. Demonstrated analytical, critical thinking, and written communication skills, with the ability to synthesize complex information into clear, actionable insights for diverse audiences. Demonstrated experience in rare disease and/or the biotechnology/pharmaceutical industry. Background in health policy; expertise in rare disease preferred. Additional Skills/Experience: The ideal candidate will embody Travere’s core values: Patient-inspired, courageous, promote community, stronger together. Strong focus on patients, caregivers, and families with a track record of positive interactions. Record of identifying policy trends affecting public health and advancing policy solutions, rare disease focus a plus. Well organized with the ability to multitask, prioritize, and manage shifting responsibilities in a dynamic, cross-functional teamwork environment. Excellent collaboration skills with strong attention to detail and the ability to multi-task and manage complexity. Demonstrated reputation as a well-respected, dynamic team player. Strong interpersonal and organizational skills and excellent verbal and written communication skills are required. Successful record of creating and managing complex project plans, timelines, budgets, and critical paths. Flexibility to implement new strategies and tactics to accommodate these changes. Ability to adapt to modification and changes to project plans, demonstrating flexibility to implement new strategies and tactics to accommodate these changes. Ability to travel 25% domestic. Total Rewards Offerings: Travere provides comprehensive total rewards offerings that demonstrate our commitment as a diverse, equitable, people-centric, and pay-for-performance organization. Benefits: Our benefits include premium health, financial, work-life and well-being offerings for eligible employees and dependents, wellness and employee support programs, life insurance, disability, retirement plans with employer match and generous paid time off. Compensation: Our competitive compensation package includes a combination of both cash compensation (base pay and short-term incentive) and long-term incentive compensation (company stock), designed to recognize, retain, and reward employees. Target Base Pay Range: $150,000.00 – $195,000.00 *This information is current as of the date of this posting and may be modified in the future. Actual pay offered to a candidate will depend on a variety of factors including the candidate’s experience, education, skills, and location. Travere will accept applications on an ongoing basis until a candidate is selected for the position. Travere Therapeutics, Inc. is an EEO/AA/Veteran/Disability Employer. If you require a reasonable accommodation to complete the application or interview process, please contact us by sending an email to [email protected] . Please note that this email address is to be used exclusively to request an accommodation with the online application, interview or hiring process only. Travere HR will not reply to emails sent to this address for any other reason. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Director of Business Development and Marketing
item.description: Director of Business Development and Marketing Organization: State and Federal Communications Location: Washington, DC | Akron, OH Date Posted: 08/04/2026 Director of Business Development and Marketing Lead growth, brand strategy, and client engagement for a trusted political compliance partner. About State and Federal Communications State and Federal Communications, Inc. is a political compliance consulting firm and online guidebook service covering lobbying, campaign finance, and procurement lobbying compliance laws for the federal government, all 50 states, more than 300 local jurisdictions, Canada, Europe, Oceania, Latin America, and Asia. We help organizations navigate complex compliance requirements with clarity, accuracy, and responsive service. Our work is grounded in three core values: putting clients first, pursuing excellence, and approaching challenges with solutions-oriented thinking. About the Role Reporting to the President and CEO, the Director of Business Development and Marketing will lead the organization’s marketing, communications, brand, public relations, digital engagement, and sales enablement strategies. This role is ideal for a strategic, collaborative leader who can connect brand visibility, client relationships, lead generation, and revenue growth into one integrated plan. You will partner closely with Sales, executive leadership, creative teams, and client-facing departments to strengthen market presence, support customer retention, generate qualified leads, and ensure consistent messaging across every channel. What You’ll Do Build and lead an integrated business development, marketing, and communications strategy aligned with sales, revenue, customer retention, and long-term growth goals. Partner with Sales to create targeted campaigns, lead generation programs, sales materials, customer communications, and market-specific outreach strategies. Work with the President and CEO and senior leadership to define annual priorities, brand positioning, communications plans, and measurable performance objectives. Monitor pipeline performance, sales forecasts, campaign results, and key metrics; translate insights into recommendations that support continued business growth. Lead, coach, and support marketing, communications, sales support, and creative team members with clear goals, expectations, timelines, and accountability. Oversee brand messaging, thought leadership, public relations, social media, newsletters, advertising, presentations, website content, collateral, and customer-facing materials. Plan and manage multi-channel campaigns, including email marketing, digital advertising, Google Ads, LinkedIn campaigns, direct mail, webinars, events, trade shows, and sponsorships. Use CRM, marketing automation, analytics, and reporting tools, including platforms such as Act-On and Microsoft Dynamics CRM, to improve segmentation, lead management, campaign performance, and customer engagement. Manage budgets, vendors, advertising placements, production schedules, timelines, and project workflows to ensure efficient execution and strong return on investment. Represent the organization at conferences, seminars, customer meetings, speaking engagements, trade shows, and other business development opportunities as needed. What We’re Looking For Ten or more years of progressively responsible experience in marketing, communications, sales, business development, public relations, or a related field. Demonstrated success building strategies that support lead generation, customer acquisition, customer retention, and revenue growth. Experience partnering with sales teams to develop campaigns, collateral, messaging, account support, pipeline-building programs, and customer communications. Strong understanding of digital marketing, email marketing, website content, CRM systems, marketing automation, online advertising, social media, analytics, and campaign reporting. Proven ability to lead teams, manage direct reports, coordinate cross-functional work, and support team performance in both in-person and remote environments. Excellent writing, editing, presentation, storytelling, and verbal communication skills, with the ability to tailor messaging for different audiences and channels. Experience managing budgets, vendors, creative production, advertising placements, events, trade shows, public relations activities, and marketing project timelines. Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret campaign results, sales activity, customer feedback, survey findings, and market research. High level of professionalism, executive presence, sound judgment, organization, attention to detail, and collaborative leadership. Bachelor’s degree in marketing, communications, business, public relations, journalism, sales, or a related field required; advanced degree or relevant certifications preferred. If you are excited by the opportunity to shape growth strategy, strengthen client relationships, and lead meaningful marketing and communications work, we encourage you to apply—even if your experience does not match every item listed. Our Values Clients First: We build trusted relationships by listening closely, responding thoughtfully, and delivering work that adds value. Commitment to Excellence: We set high standards, embrace continuous improvement, and take pride in high-quality work. Solutions-Oriented Thinking: We approach complexity with focus, adaptability, resourcefulness, and calm confidence. Why This Role Matters This role sits at the intersection of strategy, growth, brand, and client experience. The Director of Business Development and Marketing will help shape how State and Federal Communications reaches new audiences, deepens customer relationships, and communicates the value of its services in a complex and evolving compliance landscape. This is a full-time, exempt position. Candidates will have an expectation to spend time in the Company’s office space in Washington DC and travel to the main office in Akron, OH from time to time. Salary for this role starts at $185,000 annually. Other Benefits include: Dental, Vision, Medical insurance Life insurance Long and short-term disability 401k with company match. Potential for profit sharing Paid time off Opportunities for professional development Hybrid work schedule Applicants can send resumes to [email protected] . Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Senior Director, International Trade and Market Access Policy
item.description: Senior Director, International Trade and Market Access Policy Organization: Pfizer Location: Washington, DC | New York, NY | Brussels, BE Date Posted: 08/04/2026 ## ROLE SUMMARY The Senior Director, International Trade and Market Access Policy leads international trade and market access policy strategy for the International Division. In coordination with in‑market policy and government affairs leads, defines the Division’s market access and trade priorities across the company’s key international markets, identifying procurement barriers, IP challenges, and other commercial or trade policy risks, and works with the company’s U.S. Policy & Government Affairs (USPGR) team to advance those priorities through diplomatic engagement. Tracks trade policy developments across the Division’s foreign markets and works in collaboration with local in‑market policy and government affairs leads to engage foreign trade ministries, regulators, and other policymakers to shape policy environments before they harden into barriers and to coordinate the Division’s response to emerging trade actions, localization pressures, and pricing or reimbursement reforms. In coordination with USPGR, assesses how U.S. trade measures and foreign government responses interact and drives the International Division’s action where the two intersect. Monitors and maintains high‑level engagement with multilateral institutions (e.g., WTO, UNGA). In coordination with USPGR, represents Pfizer with relevant trade associations, business coalitions, and other membership organizations to drive policies and positioning aligned with International Division priorities. Produces data and evidence and collaborates with academia and think tanks to develop reports, host roundtables, and engage key opinion leaders in support of International Division priorities. — ## ROLE RESPONSIBILITIES – Define and prioritize the International Division’s market access and trade agenda across the company’s key international markets. – Identify and triage procurement barriers, IP challenges, and other commercial or trade policy risks surfaced by in‑market policy and government affairs leads. – Track trade policy developments across the Division’s foreign markets, anticipating regulatory, legislative, and procurement shifts that affect Pfizer’s position. – Work in collaboration with local in‑market policy and government affairs leads to engage foreign trade ministries, regulators, and other policymakers, shaping policy environments and coordinating the Division’s response to emerging trade actions, localization pressures, and pricing or reimbursement reforms. – Work with the company’s USPGR team to advance International Division priorities through coordinated diplomatic engagement. – In coordination with USPGR, represent Pfizer with relevant trade associations, business coalitions, and other membership organizations to drive policies and positioning aligned with International Division priorities. Where applicable, support USPGR‑led trade and coalition group engagements. – In coordination with USPGR, assess how U.S. trade measures and foreign government responses interact and drive the International Division’s action where the two intersect. – Monitor and maintain high‑level engagement with multilateral institutions (e.g., WTO, UNGA). Coordinate with USPGR on USG engagement with these groups. – Commission data, evidence, and third‑party engagement (academia, think tanks) to support International advocacy. — ## BASIC QUALIFICATIONS Candidate demonstrates a breadth of diverse capabilities including: the ability to influence and collaborate with peers, develop and coach others, oversee and guide the work of external stakeholders to achieve meaningful outcomes and create business impact. – Bachelor’s degree minimum required; advanced degree and multilingual preferred. – Minimum 12+ years international trade policy experience and proven track record of success in government relations and international biopharmaceutical industries. – Expertise and demonstrated success in negotiation of trade agreements, trade regulation/legislation, as well as policy expertise with imports, exports, tariffs, country/ministerial‑level negotiation/engagement, and economic impact of trade agreements on the biopharmaceutical industry. – Proven success working collaboratively with industry colleagues, including coalition‑building, to successfully mobilize stakeholders and shape strategies with external business groups. – Strong strategic and creative thinker, able to tackle complex issues both strategically and tactically, and develop innovative, results‑driven solutions. – High emotional intelligence and an ability to work under pressure and partner effectively with internal stakeholders including experts across the company. – Demonstrated success in development/execution of targeted briefings for executive leadership, senior management, and business leaders. – Well organized, highly motivated, innovative, process‑driven, results‑oriented. – Outstanding oral and written communication skills. — ## OTHER JOB DETAILS Last Date to Apply for Job: August 14th, 2026. Locations: Washington DC or Belgium – Brussels or NYHQ or France – Rives de Paris Ability to travel domestically and internationally based on business needs NOT Eligible for Relocation Package Position is hybrid and will require working 2 to 3 days per week onsite #LI‑PFE The annual base salary for this position ranges from $214,900.00 to $358,100.00. In addition, this position is eligible for participation in Pfizer’s Global Performance Plan with a bonus target of 22.5% of the base salary and eligibility to participate in our share‑based long‑term incentive program. Benefits offered include a 401(k) plan with Pfizer Matching Contributions and an additional Pfizer Retirement Savings Contribution, paid vacation, holiday and personal days, paid caregiver/parental and medical leave, and health benefits including medical, prescription drug, dental, and vision coverage. Learn more at Pfizer Candidate Site – U.S. Benefits (uscandidates.mypfizerbenefits.com). Pfizer compensation structures and benefit packages are aligned based on the location of hire. The United States salary range provided does not apply to Tampa, FL or any location outside of the United States. This role is posted in multiple locations. If you are applying for the role in a secondary job posting location where pay transparency regulations apply, your Talent Advisor will share the local pay information with you during the first interview. Relocation assistance may be available based on business needs and/or eligibility. Candidates must be authorized to be employed in the U.S. by any employer. U.S. work visa sponsorship (such as TN, O‑1, H‑1B, etc.) is not available for this role now or in the future. — ## SUNSHINE ACT Pfizer reports payments and other transfers of value to health care providers as required by federal and state transparency laws and implementing regulations. These laws and regulations require Pfizer to provide government agencies with information such as a health care provider’s name, address, and the type of payments or other value received, generally for public disclosure. Subject to further legal review and statutory or regulatory clarification, which Pfizer intends to pursue, reimbursement of recruiting expenses for licensed physicians may constitute a reportable transfer of value under the federal transparency law commonly known as the Sunshine Act. Therefore, if you are a licensed physician who incurs recruiting expenses as a result of interviewing with Pfizer that we pay or reimburse, your name, address, and the amount of payments made currently will be reported to the government. If you have questions regarding this matter, please contact your Talent Acquisition representative. — ## EEO & EMPLOYMENT ELIGIBILITY Pfizer is committed to equal opportunity in the terms and conditions of employment for all employees and job applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, age, gender identity or gender expression, national origin, disability, or veteran status. Pfizer complies with all applicable national, state, and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment as well as work authorization and employment eligibility verification requirements of the Immigration and Nationality Act and IRCA. Pfizer is an E‑Verify employer. This position requires permanent work authorization in the United States. Pfizer endeavors to make [www.pfizer.com/careers] accessible to all users. If you would like to contact us regarding the accessibility of our website or need assistance completing the application process and/or interviewing, please email [email protected] . This is solely for accommodation requests related to website accessibility, the online application process, and interviewing. Requests for any other reason will not be returned. To learn more about acceptable and prohibited uses of AI during the recruitment process, please review Pfizer’s candidate AI‑use guidelines available on Pfizer Careers. item.title: Policy Analyst
item.description: Policy Analyst Organization: Hispanic Federation (HF) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/04/2026 **Job Status:** Full-Time **Details:** Cover letter required ## Position Description ### Who We Are Hispanic Federation (HF) is the nation’s premier Latino nonprofit membership organization. Founded in 1990, HF supports Hispanic families and strengthens Latino institutions through grantmaking, advocacy, and direct services in the areas of education, health, immigration, civic engagement, economic empowerment, and the environment. Values that drive our work include equality, fairness, diversity, and empathy. Headquartered in New York City, HF has offices in Albany, NY and in Florida, Puerto Rico, Connecticut, Rhode Island, North Carolina, and Washington, DC. ### Who We Seek Hispanic Federation seeks a Policy Analyst to advance HF’s New York State policy priorities and campaigns, carry out public policy analysis, and prepare issue briefs and other materials to support the organization’s advocacy efforts—especially Albany-based efforts—and manage tracking and compliance for all HF’s lobbying activities. The Policy Analyst will focus on Education public policy and the impacts of education in communities of color. The Policy Analyst will work with staff in multiple offices. The Policy Analyst must have both direct public policy and advocacy experience and will be trained in federal and New York State lobbying rules and reporting requirements. The successful candidate will have the ability to prepare concise and effective public policy and advocacy materials, sound oral communications skills, and the ability to establish and maintain positive relationships with public officials and other advocates. The Policy Analyst must be well organized, results oriented, and effective at multi-tasking. The position provides an excellent opportunity for gaining broad experience in public policy and advocacy work for a highly respected, growing Latino organization. **Position Location:** Washington D.C. or must be based in a city where HF has an established office **Reports to:** Vice President for Policy and Strategic Engagement ## Job Duties and Responsibilities ### Public Policy and Advocacy – Advance HF’s New York State Policy Priorities and Campaigns through: – Maintaining up-to-date knowledge about state policies affecting Latino communities, primarily in education, but also in economic empowerment, immigration, and health. – Creating and maintaining an advocacy network to further HF initiatives in New York. – Working with HF’s New York-based Policy Directors to inform advocacy efforts. ### Carry Out Policy and Data Analysis – Monitor and evaluate New York State policies and legislation. – Develop a plan for evaluating and analyzing relevant public and social policies in New York State that affect the Latino community. – Produce substantial writing, including issue briefs, talking points, advocacy letters, and written testimony. – Perform data analysis and research related to identified policy areas to inform decision-making. – Prepare portions of policy reports in support of Policy Directors in various issue areas. – Draft rapid response policy statements as needed. ### Serve as a Representative of HF – Schedule and attend meetings with legislative staff, policymakers, experts, and issue stakeholders to effectively communicate HF policy priorities. – Serve as an advocate and representative of HF in meetings, policy forums, coalitions, and networks. – Support HF’s lobbying time tracking system. ## Required Skills and Qualifications – A bachelor’s degree, preferably with a focus on government, public policy, and/or research; minimum one to two (1–2) years of professional experience in policy research, analysis, writing, and advocacy required. – Demonstrated ability to carry out applied research and analysis to assess policy needs and evaluate current and proposed public policies. – Willingness to gain knowledge of federal and New York State requirements and limitations on legislative advocacy by nonprofit organizations. – Familiarity with one or more of HF’s public policy issue priorities. – Demonstrated skills in writing effective, concise policy-focused materials. – Strong verbal communications skills. – Strong ability to develop work plans, synthesize complex policy information, meet deadlines, and manage multiple policy projects simultaneously. – Strong commitment to the Latino community and to HF’s mission and values. – Excellent interpersonal skills, with a flexible and collaborative spirit. – Computer skills including Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint). ## Preferred Skills and Qualifications – Training in law or a graduate degree in Public Administration, Political Science, or Public Policy. – Experience working with the New York State Legislature and managing relationships between advocacy groups, government officials, and Latino and immigrant communities. – Public policy and advocacy experience focusing on the Latino community. – Familiarity with federal reporting requirements for entities electing 501(h) and with requirements under the New York State Lobbying Act. – Understanding of HF’s priority issue areas, especially immigration, education, economic empowerment, and health. – Bilingual (English/Spanish). – A high-energy self-starter who is curious and a quick learner. ## Compensation The salary range for this position is **$60–65k**, commensurate with experience. Compensation includes fully subsidized medical, dental, and vision insurance; access to flexible spending for medical and transportation; and a 403(b) retirement plan with a match of up to 6% after 6 months of service. ## To Apply Please submit a résumé, cover letter detailing your interest and qualifications, and two relevant writing samples via this application portal . No calls or emails will be accepted for this position. Only select candidates will be contacted regarding this role. For more information about the Hispanic Federation, visit: **[www.hispanicfederation.org]** Hispanic Federation is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate against actual or perceived race, color, religion, gender identity, gender expression, age, national origin, creed, disability, marital status, sexual orientation, and/or other protected categories. item.title: Communications Manager
item.description: Communications Manager Organization: Department for Professional Employees, AFL-CIO (DPE) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/04/2026 ## **The Department for Professional Employees, AFL‑CIO (DPE) — Communications Manager** ### **About DPE** DPE is a national coalition representing 25 unions whose members work in education, healthcare, media, the arts, sciences, engineering, and other sectors. We are a small, collaborative, and dedicated team working to advance the interests of professional and technical workers across the country. ### **About the Role** The Communications Manager works closely with the President and other staff to execute a proactive communications strategy, shape DPE’s public image, and advance our work on legislation, policy, campaigns, and organizing. We are looking for a skilled communicator, exceptional writer, and creative strategist with a passion for the labor movement and storytelling. — ## **Responsibilities** The Communications Manager will collaborate with DPE leadership and staff to execute the organization’s communications strategy, including: ### **Media Relations** – Drafting and editing press releases, talking points, advocacy materials, speeches, op‑eds, and media advisories. – Assisting with the development, execution, and distribution of content for digital platforms and websites managed by DPE. – Pitching stories to reporters and establishing relationships with key journalists and producers to expand press coverage of DPE’s work. – Overseeing distribution and placement of DPE communications. – Monitoring press coverage about DPE, its affiliates, and issues affecting professionals. ### **Digital Communications** – Leading digital engagement to amplify DPE’s work and campaigns through social media and other tools, like Action Network. – Developing, executing, and distributing content for DPE’s digital platforms and websites, including designing one‑pagers, fact sheets, and graphics. – Maintaining current websites and creating new campaign websites, including message development. – Analyzing website and social media analytics to advise DPE leadership on the reach and effectiveness of DPE’s various communication tools. ### **External Communications** – Establishing and maintaining strong relationships with affiliate communications teams. – Collaborating on project ideas and campaigns that communicate the value of joining together in union. – Ensuring consistent messaging across DPE’s communications channels and issue areas. — ## **Qualifications** – A passion for the labor movement and a commitment to its mission and values. – At least two years of communications experience, ideally in labor, advocacy, or nonprofit sectors. – Excellent writing across formats — press releases, op‑eds, and social — with the ability to make research and policy accessible. – Demonstrated earned‑media results: pitching reporters, placing stories and op‑eds, serving as or preparing spokespeople. – Experience managing digital channels, building or updating websites, and graphic design. – Ability to manage multiple projects independently. — ## **Salary and Benefits** – **Salary range:** $70,000 – $80,000, commensurate with experience. – **Benefits:** Employer‑paid health, dental, and vision insurance; retirement/pension plan; 401(k); vacation and generous paid holiday schedule; hybrid work schedule. — ## **How to Apply** Interested candidates should submit a résumé, cover letter, and two professional references (former or current supervisors) to ** [email protected] **. DPE is an equal opportunity employer. Women, people of color, LGBTQ+ individuals, people with disabilities, and candidates from working‑class backgrounds are strongly encouraged to apply. item.title: Assistant Director, Defense and National Security Program
item.description: Assistant Director, Defense and National Security Program Organization: Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/04/2026 ## Position Summary CFR’s David Rockefeller Studies Program is one of the country’s largest foreign policy think tanks with a widely respected and influential research staff. The Studies Program aims to advance the discussion of American foreign policy and international affairs through its writing, publications, public outreach, and discussions. The Defense and National Security Program analyzes the world’s rapidly changing defense environment. It focuses on U.S. defense strategy, the future of war, the defense industrial base, emerging capabilities, and technologies such as artificial intelligence and cyber. The program and affiliated fellows enhance the public debate through books, articles, op-eds, interviews, congressional testimony, roundtables, and briefings. The assistant director will work under the program directors on projects related to defense and national security. This position is based in CFR’s Washington, DC office at least four days per week. Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays are considered institutional anchor days where all staff are required to be onsite. CFR’s remote working schedule is subject to change. — ## Essential Functions/Responsibilities – Manage the program’s day-to-day operations and schedules, including publications, meetings, and events, with guidance from directors. – Assist in overseeing and coordinating the program’s activities and published products, including working closely with outside authors on research papers intended for policymakers, and editing and proofreading written material. – Work closely with directors to develop and monitor the program’s budget. – Coordinate events and conference logistics, including preparing invitations, corresponding with speakers, helping to prepare background papers and materials for distribution, and providing other logistical support. – Manage the program’s marketing activities, social media presence, and other digital tools, optimizing for ways to improve the program’s reach with policymakers. – Work with other CFR departments to identify funding opportunities, and draft grant proposals and reports. – Work closely with program directors, fellows, research associates, and interns on the management of projects. – Conduct miscellaneous administrative tasks such as making travel arrangements and scheduling, as needed. – Provide support across departmental lines and for other fellows, upon request. — ## Minimum Qualifications ### Education and Experience – Bachelor’s degree in international relations or related field – Master’s degree preferred – 4+ years related experience in a research, government, consulting, journalism, or other relevant role – Previous related experience that required strong writing and editing ability, knowledge relevant to defense and national security, and the ability to work with accomplished researchers and authors ### Related Skills & Other Requirements – Exceptional organizational skills and outstanding attention to detail – Demonstrated ability to manage projects and tasks independently and under deadlines – Editorial experience – Experience with event logistics, budgets, and/or website management — ## Required Application Materials Please submit a résumé and cover letter stating your interest in the position. — ## Compensation and Benefits The full-time annual compensation range for this position is $70,000–$75,000, depending on experience. In addition to competitive salaries, the Council on Foreign Relations offers a benefits package that is among the best offered by nonprofit institutions today, including an award-winning health and wellness program, an on-site fitness center, and generous leave policies and health insurance programs. — ## About CFR The Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) is committed to fostering a foreign policy community in the United States that is more representative of American society, recognizing that diverse backgrounds and perspectives contribute to broader, more informed participation in the foreign policy debate and lead to an enhanced understanding of the world and the United States’ role therein. To that end, CFR is dedicated to continuing to advance diversity, equity, and inclusion throughout its work and workplace by building a more diverse membership and staff, producing and dispensing thoughtful analysis on a broad range of foreign policy issues, and developing relevant, wide-reaching programming that also serves to expand the foreign policy talent pipeline to underrepresented populations. item.title: Counsel, Litigation and Regulatory Affairs
item.description: Counsel, Litigation and Regulatory Affairs Organization: Competitive Enterprise Institute (CEI) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/04/2026 ## About CEI The Competitive Enterprise Institute (CEI) is a nonprofit public policy organization dedicated to advancing the principles of limited government, free enterprise, and individual liberty. CEI employs a full-service approach to policy change that includes litigation and legal advocacy, original research, communications campaigns, and direct engagement with policymakers. We work to reform America’s unaccountable regulatory state, protect property rights, and remove unnecessary government barriers to innovation and prosperity. ## Position Summary CEI seeks an experienced litigator to serve as Counsel for Litigation and Regulatory Affairs. This position is designed for an attorney who can assume substantial responsibility immediately: independently evaluate potential cases, develop litigation strategy, draft and review court filings, manage discovery and administrative records, and drive matters forward from inception through resolution with limited day-to-day supervision. Think tank or non-profit experience is a plus. The Counsel will report to the General Counsel and work closely with Senior Counsel, Associate Counsel, CEI policy experts, and outside counsel. The role is senior to CEI’s Associate Counsel position but does not carry the department-wide management, supervisory, or acting-lead responsibilities assigned to Senior Counsel. The successful candidate will exercise mature legal judgment, communicate directly with clients and litigation partners, and help translate CEI’s policy expertise into disciplined, high-quality legal advocacy. The Counsel will be based in CEI’s Washington, DC office. ## Key Responsibilities ### Litigation and Case Management – Take principal working responsibility for assigned federal and state litigation, including constitutional, administrative-law, statutory, and economic-liberty matters. – Investigate facts and legal theories; assess standing, jurisdiction, causes of action, remedies, procedural posture, evidentiary needs, and litigation risk. – Draft and revise complaints, petitions for review, motions, briefs, declarations, discovery requests and responses, administrative-record materials, settlement documents, and appellate filings. – Manage assigned matters from pre-suit analysis through discovery, dispositive motions, trial or merits proceedings, appeal, and resolution, in coordination with the General Counsel and Senior Counsel. – Maintain command of deadlines, court rules, filing requirements, case records, budgets, and next steps; promptly identify strategic, ethical, or operational issues requiring escalation. – Prepare witnesses and organizational representatives for interviews, declarations, depositions, hearings, and other proceedings. ### Legal Strategy and Partnerships – Help identify and develop affirmative litigation opportunities consistent with CEI’s mission and institutional priorities. – Coordinate effectively with outside counsel, pro bono firms, public-interest litigation organizations, clients, amici, experts, and coalition partners. – Draft and supervise amicus briefs and support CEI’s participation as plaintiff, petitioner, intervenor, or amicus where appropriate. – Provide candid, practical recommendations to the General Counsel and organizational leadership concerning litigation strategy, exposure, costs, and institutional considerations. ### Regulatory and Policy Work – Draft and review regulatory comments, petitions, agency submissions, testimony, and legal analyses involving federal and state regulatory action. – Analyze proposed and final agency actions for statutory authority, Administrative Procedure Act compliance, constitutional concerns, and potential judicial review. – Work with CEI policy experts to develop legally sound positions and preserve issues and records for possible litigation. – Translate complex legal arguments into clear memoranda, policy publications, talking points, and other materials for non-lawyer audiences. ### Team and Institutional Responsibilities – Provide substantive guidance and constructive review to less-experienced attorneys and legal fellows on assigned matters, without serving as their formal supervisor unless specifically designated. – Collaborate with CEI’s policy, communications, development, and operations teams while protecting privilege, work product, client confidences, and litigation strategy. – Assist with internal legal review, conflicts analysis, engagement arrangements, records preservation, and compliance matters connected to CEI’s legal work. – Represent CEI professionally in court proceedings, agency meetings, coalition discussions, conferences, public panels, and other external settings, as appropriate. ## Required Qualifications – J.D. from an ABA-accredited law school and active membership in good standing in at least one U.S. jurisdiction; admission to the District of Columbia Bar, or eligibility and willingness to become admitted promptly, is required. – Approximately 6–9 years of relevant legal experience, with substantial hands-on civil litigation experience in a law firm, government, public-interest organization, or comparable setting. Exceptional candidates with a different experience range may be considered. – Demonstrated ability to take meaningful responsibility for complex litigation matters with limited supervision. – Excellent legal research, writing, editing, analytical, and oral-advocacy skills. – Working knowledge of federal civil procedure, appellate procedure, discovery, jurisdiction, standing, and remedies. – Sound professional judgment, strong organizational habits, and a reliable record of meeting litigation deadlines. – Ability to work constructively with lawyers, policy experts, clients, witnesses, outside partners, and non-lawyer colleagues. – Commitment to CEI’s mission of advancing individual liberty, free enterprise, limited government, and accountable regulation. – Willingness to engage in occasional travel (approximate travel: 10%). ## Preferred Qualifications – Experience litigating Administrative Procedure Act, constitutional, regulatory, separation-of-powers, property-rights, or economic-liberty matters. – Federal appellate or administrative-record litigation experience. – Experience taking or defending depositions, handling expert witnesses, arguing motions, or otherwise serving in a lead or substantial courtroom role. – Experience working with the U.S. Department of Justice, federal or state agencies, or government enforcement matters. – Experience drafting regulatory comments, petitions for review, or amicus briefs. – Familiarity with nonprofit, public-interest, or mission-driven litigation. ## Characteristics If you believe this position may be a good fit, the following will describe you: – A strong communicator with excellent legal writing and oral communication skills; public affairs experience is a plus. – Detail-oriented and proud of producing accurate, high-quality work. – A self-starter who takes ownership, anticipates next steps, and follows through. – Strategic and practical, with the judgment to distinguish significant legal risks from issues that can be resolved efficiently. – Curious and policy-minded, with the ability to distill complex legal and policy ideas into factually accurate and engaging work for external audiences. – Adaptable in a fast-moving environment with shifting priorities and able to maintain a constructive attitude when needs change. – Collaborative, but comfortable working independently and making well-supported recommendations. – Philosophically aligned with CEI’s mission and vision. Please see cei.org for a deeper understanding of the organization’s policy agenda. ## Compensation and Benefits CEI offers a competitive salary commensurate with experience and a full benefits package, including health insurance, a 403(b) retirement plan, generous leave, and professional-development support. The salary range is $130,000.00 to $150,000.00 based on experience. Work Authorization: Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of application and throughout employment. CEI does not provide visa sponsorship now or in the future for this position. CEI is an equal opportunity employer. We value a workplace in which employees are treated fairly and encourage qualified candidates from all backgrounds to apply. ## To Apply Qualified candidates should submit the following application materials (in order) in one PDF document: – A cover letter explaining the candidate’s interest in CEI, relevant litigation experience, and philosophical alignment with CEI’s mission; – A résumé; – Two legal writing samples, preferably briefs, dispositive motions, appellate filings, or regulatory submissions that principally reflect the candidate’s own work; and – Salary expectations. Applications should be submitted to Talent Market via this link: [ https://talentmarket.org/candidates/apply-for-your-dream-job/ ] Questions can be directed to Claire Kittle Dixon, President of Talent Market, who is managing the search process: [email protected] . There is no application deadline for this position. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis. This job will remain posted on our site until it is filled. While we thank all applicants in advance for their interest in this position, we are only able to contact those to whom we can offer an interview. Only direct applications will be considered. No phone calls, please. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Director, Federal Policy
item.description: Director, Federal Policy Organization: Center for Responsible Lending (CRL) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/04/2026 ## Job Description ### Who We Are The Center for Responsible Lending (CRL) is a nonprofit, non‑partisan organization working to ensure a fair, inclusive financial marketplace that creates opportunities for all. Through research, legal analysis, policy development, and state and national advocacy engagement, CRL fights for economic equity for underserved communities—particularly Black and brown communities and low‑to‑middle income families. CRL’s staff, allies, and funders reflect a collective commitment to eliminating systemic injustice in America’s financial services. CRL provides a strong voice on both the state and national levels for these families to expand family wealth and financial stability through sustainable homeownership, affordable higher education, and support for small businesses. CRL also works to protect financial stability by preventing abusive products that trap families in debt and strip away their income—ending payday lending and other predatory high‑cost lending, exorbitant bank fees, and abusive debt collection practices. CRL is an affiliate of Self‑Help, a community development lender founded in 1980. We are seeking a Director of Federal Policy for our Washington, DC team. — ## Position Summary The Director of Federal Policy directs and coordinates CRL federal legislative and regulatory policy activities in coordination with CRL senior leadership to advance CRL policy goals. This highly collaborative role is deeply involved in developing and coordinating strategy with several teams within CRL and requires frequent communication as federal developments occur. — ## What You’ll Do ### Outreach – Represent CRL at external functions, such as receptions and conferences (including events beyond typical office hours). – Work in coordination with other organizations and coalitions involved in CRL issues. – Build relationships with coalition partners and industry partners; attend coalition meetings and/or identify appropriate staff to attend. – Serve as a spokesperson on a variety of topics in the media and on Capitol Hill. ### Staff Management – Supervise federal policy staff; set individual goals and provide routine feedback and evaluation. – Conduct annual performance appraisals and administer salary adjustments. – Develop and implement professional development plans with team members. – Model inclusive behavior, build cultural humility, and support staff interested in deepening their DE&I knowledge. – Provide strategic leadership and insight into federal opportunities and threats; help prioritize workplans. – Provide feedback on issue plans, revisions, and implementation; assist with monitoring plans and identifying resource or scheduling conflicts. – Ensure appropriate levels of coverage for workgroup issues; assign issues to team members and coordinate with leadership to ensure global coverage or identify resource needs. ### Federal Policy Development – Lead CRL’s strategy to advance legislative and regulatory agendas at the federal level. – Monitor and analyze proposed federal legislation and regulations to support CRL’s policy positions and prevent unfair lending practices. – Lead technical assistance in drafting federal legislation or regulatory proposals. – Oversee Capitol Hill and federal regulatory activities in coordination with issue team leaders and other functional leaders. – Review and advise on coalition sign‑on letters. – Convene regular meetings of federal policy team members to update, coordinate, and prioritize Hill and regulatory activities. – Participate with senior leadership in broad strategy discussions, focusing on how federal policy fits into overall CRL strategy and resource availability. – Track federal policy team activities and report on them for board and funder reports, internal communication, and evaluation of current initiatives. – Participate in or lead issue workgroups and craft policy approaches, including research and writing on legal issues, major policy reports, comment letters, regulatory proposals, testimony, speeches, or articles. – Support CRL litigation work, including amicus briefs, and maintain relationships with outside partners on litigation matters. ### Other Responsibilities – Ensure compliance with Congressional and IRS lobbying reporting, working with accounting and policy counsel to include proper costs and complete lists of bills and issues. – Advance CRL and Self‑Help’s Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion goals in internal and external work, including supplier diversity. – Perform other duties as assigned. — ## What You’ll Need – Bachelor’s degree or comparable equivalent experience. – A juris doctorate (JD) and/or a master’s degree in Public Policy or related fields, and/or experience with consumer financial laws is a plus but not required. – 8+ years of increasingly senior experience, ideally in a similar position with demonstrated ability to plan, organize, and direct a comprehensive, innovative, and strategic policy program. – Experience in civil rights, housing/mortgage lending, predatory lending, consumer law, or banking law desired but not required. – Experience building relationships with external partners and cultivating collaboration desired but not required. – Demonstrated commitment to public interest law, families of modest means, communities of color, and racial justice analysis, including understanding how federal/state/local policies contributed to racial wealth disparities. – Passion for CRL’s mission and commitment to social justice work. **Compensation Range:** $117,000–$153,738 (DC CAP) — ## Equal Opportunity Statement Self‑Help is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. ### Company Disclaimer Self‑Help is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all persons, regardless of race, religion, religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, marital status, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression (including transgender status), age, sexual orientation, military and veteran status, class, or family status. item.title: Director, Leadership & Change Communications
item.description: Director, Leadership & Change Communications Organization: BAE Systems Inc, HQ Location: Falls Church, VA Date Posted: 08/04/2026 # Job Description The Director, Leadership & Change Communications is responsible for developing and executing strategic communications that support organizational transformation, strengthen leadership alignment, and drive employee engagement. This role serves as a trusted communications advisor to executive leadership and ensures messaging aligns with business priorities, culture, and long‑term strategy. During periods of change, they guide the business and leaders to maintain consistency in messaging and cultivate trust between employees and company leadership. Reporting to the director, this person will establish and enforce communications frameworks, governance, and best practices to ensure consistency and clear expectations across the team and with partners. The director leads high‑impact communications programs to accelerate change adoption, strengthen leadership visibility, and enhance the overall employee experience. As a senior communications leader, this person will influence enterprise decision‑making, anticipate and mitigate communications risks, and ensure employees remain informed, connected, and engaged. — # Job Duties – Develop and lead the enterprise approach for leadership and change communications, ensuring alignment with corporate priorities, business objectives, and organizational change/transformation initiatives. – Serve as a senior communications advisor to executive leadership, providing strategic counsel on messaging, positioning, organizational announcements, and high‑impact enterprise business initiatives. – Lead the development of executive communications frameworks and governance, including enterprise town halls, leadership meetings/forums, major announcements, speeches, presentations, videos, and employee engagement campaigns. – Establish standards, governance, and best practices for leadership and change communications to ensure consistency, quality, and alignment. – Direct communications approaches that support enterprise transformation initiatives, including organizational redesign, technology modernization, digital transformation, policy changes, mergers & acquisitions, and culture initiatives. – Anticipate communications risks and develop strategies that cultivate trust across the organization. – Lead, mentor, and develop a team of communicators working to build core communications competencies. – Champion innovative communications approaches, emerging technologies, and employee engagement practices with a focus on continuous improvement and enhanced employee experience. – Create executive‑ready materials that simplify complex business topics into clear, actionable communications. – Lead communications planning for sensitive organizational matters with professionalism, discretion, empathy, and strategic alignment. — # Required Education, Experience, & Skills – Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Public Relations, Journalism, Marketing, HR, or related field. – 10 years of experience in internal communications, change communications, executive communications, HR communications, or related field. (8 years with an advanced degree.) – Proven experience leading communications strategies for organizational change and transformation initiatives. – Experience leading teams in large, complex organizations. – Strong executive communications experience supporting senior leaders. – Exceptional writing, editing, storytelling, and presentation skills. – Demonstrated ability to translate complex information into clear, engaging, and actionable communications. – Experience managing cross‑functional stakeholders and influencing without direct authority. – Strong understanding of change management principles and employee engagement strategies. – Ability to manage multiple priorities and navigate fast‑paced, evolving business environments. – Strong strategic thinking, judgment, organizational skills, and attention to detail. – Prior experience in large, matrixed organizations preferred. — # Preferred Education, Experience, & Skills – Master’s degree in Communications, Organizational Development, Business Administration, or related field preferred. — # Pay Information **Full‑Time Salary Range:** $138,267 – $235,053 Please note: This range is based on market pay structures. Individual salaries are determined by factors including business needs, local market conditions, internal equity, and candidate qualifications such as skills, education, and experience. — # Employee Benefits At BAE Systems, we support employees in all aspects of life, including health and financial well‑being. Regular employees scheduled to work 20+ hours per week are offered: – Health, dental, and vision insurance – Health savings accounts – 401(k) savings plan – Disability coverage – Life and accident insurance – Employee assistance program – Legal plan – Additional perks, including discounts on home, auto, and pet insurance Leave programs include paid time off, paid holidays, and other types of leave such as paid parental, military, bereavement, and applicable federal/state sick leave. Employees may participate in the company recognition program to receive monetary or non‑monetary awards. Additional incentives may be available based on position level and job specifics. — # About BAE Systems, Inc. BAE Systems, Inc. is the U.S. subsidiary of BAE Systems plc, an international defense, aerospace, and security company delivering products and services for air, land, and naval forces, as well as advanced electronics, security, IT solutions, and customer support services. Improving the future and protecting lives is our mission. Working here means using passion and ingenuity where it counts—defending national security with breakthrough technology, superior products, and intelligence solutions. As you develop new technology and support national security, you will hone your skills on a team making a global impact. At BAE Systems, you’ll find a rewarding career that truly makes a difference. This position will be posted for at least 5 calendar days. The posting will remain active until the position is filled or a qualified pool of candidates is identified. item.title: Senior Associate Director, Media Relations
item.description: Senior Associate Director, Media Relations Organization: American Hospital Association (AHA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/04/2026 ## The American Hospital Association (AHA) The American Hospital Association (AHA) is a national organization that represents and serves all types of hospitals, health care networks, and their patients and communities. The AHA has two main offices, located in Washington, D.C., and Chicago. The AHA offers a flexible hybrid work schedule of three days in the office and two days working remotely. Responsible for creating and implementing a variety of media relations and communication strategies in support of the American Hospital Association (AHA) efforts in advocacy and representation. Serves as a member of a collaborative team working with all departments of the AHA to enhance public awareness of the AHA, its members, and positions. — ## Essential Functions – Serve as a spokesperson on behalf of AHA members. Respond to numerous inquiries from the media in an accurate and timely manner, exercising good independent judgment and discretion at all times. – Take initiative to propose, write, and edit clear, concise, and effective communications via statements, releases, talking points, commentary, and other appropriate content for legacy and digital media to advance AHA advocacy efforts. – Think strategically to develop communications plans to proactively tell the hospital story to different external audiences including media, policy and health care influencers, and consumers. – Plan and implement strategies for communicating AHA’s legislative and regulatory priorities. – Prepare AHA senior staff, board members, and members for media interviews. – Build and maintain relationships with reporters. Work with state hospital associations and member public relations executives to support major media issues and initiatives. – Manage projects and issue areas with independence. – Perform other duties as assigned. — ## Minimum Qualifications: Education Bachelor’s Degree in Communications, Media Relations, Public Relations, Journalism, English, or related field — **Required** — ## Minimum Qualifications: Work Experience – 7+ years of experience within a communications and/or media relations environment — **Required** – Experience serving as a spokesperson — **Required** – Experience in a hospital or a health care association and/or experience on Capitol Hill — **Preferred** — ## Minimum Qualifications: Knowledge, Skills and Abilities – Knowledge of legislative process and ability to learn health policy issues and federal health programs — **Required** – Exceptional writing/editing and presentation skills with the ability to think broadly about issues and their impact on how information is communicated — **Required** – Must be a team player and a self‑starter who can work under tight deadlines but also have the creativity and broad‑based thinking needed to manage and complete long‑term projects — **Required** – Demonstrated knowledge and/or experience in working with all types of media platforms, including proficiency with current and emerging social media tools — **Required** – Strong demonstrated experience with digital and new media platforms including Substacks and podcasts — **Required** – Diplomatic and demonstrates good judgment — **Required** – Demonstrates excellent organization and leadership skills — **Required** – Ability to work with a diverse group of people — **Required** – Ability to work independently and as a team player — **Required** – Willingness to adapt to changing priorities and deadlines — **Required** – Ability to take initiative to accomplish an assignment and meet the deadline — **Required** – Ability to prioritize several tasks — **Required** — ## Salary Information Commensurate with related experience. The AHA is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. A candidate’s salary is determined by various factors including, but not limited to, relevant work experience, skills, certifications, and location. **Salary Range – Minimum:** 97,000 **Salary Range – Midpoint:** 121,000 **Salary Range – Maximum:** 145,000 We offer an excellent total compensation package, which includes medical/dental coverage (PPO/HMO), vision care, life insurance, short‑ and long‑term disability plans, 401(k), tuition reimbursement, PTO/holidays/health days, wellness programs, and more! — ## Equal Opportunity Statement The American Hospital Association (AHA) is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, veteran status, and other legally protected characteristics. We will provide reasonable accommodation for individuals protected by Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, the Vietnam Era Veterans’ Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, and Title I of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990. If, because of a medical condition or disability, you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the employment process, please call (312) 422‑3000 and ask for the Vice President, Human Resources, and provide the nature of your request and your contact information. The AHA participates in the E‑Verify Program. #LI‑Hybrid Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Legislative and Political Advocate
item.description: Legislative and Political Advocate Organization: American Federation of State, County & Municipal Employees (AFSCME) Maryland Location: Baltimore, MD Date Posted: 08/04/2026 ## AFSCME Maryland Council 3 AFSCME Maryland Council 3 represents over 55,000 workers who work in public service. Council 3 members keep our public universities and community colleges running, maintain our libraries and museums, care for the elderly, provide social services to those in need, represent defendants in court, provide support in our schools, provide public safety for our communities, and maintain our parks and roads. We organize in the workplace and fight for dignity, respect, and a fair standard of living for all public service workers in Maryland. We are accepting applications for a **Legislative and Political Advocate**. This person will work on the Legislative and Political Team, which is responsible for recruiting members who will elect politicians who support workers, advocating for legislation that improves public services, increasing participation in the union’s political action committee (AFSCME PEOPLE), and working to hold politicians accountable. This position is based in our AFSCME Maryland Baltimore office at **1410 Bush Street, Baltimore MD 21230**, and in Annapolis during legislative session. Additionally, travel throughout Maryland will be required. The position reports directly to the Council’s Legislative and Political Director. — ## Responsibilities – Develop and implement strategic contract campaigns with local unions and staff. – Work with local unions and staff to build political organizing and advocacy campaigns. – Recruit union members who help elect and hold politicians accountable. – Organize and implement political programming to help elect AFSCME‑endorsed political candidates. – Increase participation in AFSCME’s political action committee by working with local unions and staff on coordinated PAC drives. – Assist local unions and staff with the candidate endorsement recommendation process. – Assist the Legislative and Political Team with advocacy before the Maryland General Assembly, state regulatory bodies, and local governments including, but not limited to, county councils, school boards, and library boards. – Develop and foster union member engagement for legislative and political advocacy campaigns at the state and local level. – Track budgetary and legislative priorities at the local government level and assist members with testimony preparation and public hearing preparation. – Conduct site visits and attend union meetings to identify issues and increase engagement in the union’s legislative and political program. – Work extended hours, including evenings and weekends, when necessary, in order to perform assigned responsibilities. – Work with the Council 3 team to advance all union priorities and goals. — ## What We Are Looking For – Dedication to workers’ rights and the labor movement. – Familiarity and knowledge of unions and/or the labor movement. – Two or more years of experience in labor, community, or political organizing. – Familiarity with Maryland state and local government structure and elected officials. – Ability to organize and mobilize union members to advocate for AFSCME’s legislative and political goals at the state and local level. – Ability to work independently and collaboratively to accomplish the mission and goals of Council 3. – Proficient oral and written communication skills. – Experience collaborating with diverse communities and in a multi‑cultural environment. Sensitivity to and appreciation of ethnic, cultural, and societal differences is required. – Ability to establish and maintain effective relationships with co‑workers, union members, and community members. – Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite programs, Zoom, VAN, other campaign platforms, and social media platforms. – A valid driver’s license is required. — ## Compensation The salary range is **$60,978 – $92,235**. Benefits include fully paid comprehensive single or family health insurance (medical, dental, prescription, and optical), car allowance, 3 weeks paid vacation, 16 paid holidays, 12 sick days, pension, 401k, and life insurance. This is a bargaining unit position and is represented by a staff union. AFSCME Maryland Council 3 is an inclusive and diverse organization, committed to advocating for social, racial, and economic justice. We promote diversity and strongly encourage applications from people who believe in our mission. We strongly encourage women, people of color, and LGBTQ people to apply. — ## To Apply Send cover letter and résumé to ** [email protected] **. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today.
