item.title: Government Relations Director Senior
item.description: Government Relations Director Senior Organization: Elevance Health Location: Washington, DC | Woodland Hills, CA | Miami, FL | Tampa, FL | New York, NY Date Posted: 08/07/2026 ## Government Relations Director Senior **Location:** This field‑based role enables associates to primarily operate in the field, traveling to client sites or designated locations as required, with occasional office attendance for meetings or training. Alternate locations may be considered if candidates reside within a commuting distance from an office. Please note that per our policy on hybrid/virtual work, candidates not within a reasonable commuting distance from the posting location(s) will not be considered for employment, unless accommodation is granted as required by law. The Government Relations Director Senior is responsible for developing and implementing strategies to advocate enterprise and large state‑specific legislative and regulatory positions in the most complex legislative and/or regulatory environments. The role directs and oversees the resolution of highly complex, varied, and sensitive political issues within the region and may include federal or multi‑state responsibility. It also supports enterprise business development and retention, including new business growth within existing markets and new market or customer opportunity development. — ## How You Will Make an Impact – Develops and implements strategies to advocate enterprise and state‑specific legislative and regulatory positions to support business goals and objectives. This may include serving as the lead business owner for the rate‑setting process with state regulators; establishing and implementing proactive strategies to bring new products or extensions of current products to market; monitoring market databases and product reviews to analyze opportunities. – Represents the enterprise and its specific businesses in advocacy efforts. – Establishes and maintains strong relationships with legislators, regulators, policymakers, and staff to support membership growth. – Develops strategies for utilizing PAC and/or corporate political contributions. – Partners with SBUs and CEEs to inform and support business planning processes and proactively raise and address issues of concern. – Makes internal and external written and oral presentations on behalf of the company. – Develops coalitions and targets grassroots capabilities. – Manages budgets and issues of importance to the enterprise and contracted lobbying staff, and may act as a team lead. – Serves as a leader in trade associations and other advocacy organizations to influence their positions, tactics, and strategies to support enterprise goals. – Generally works with legislative sessions of 6 months or longer and/or in the most complex legislative and/or regulatory environments. – **For Medicaid:** Associates in the role are expected to have in‑depth knowledge of the Medicaid business, including products and regulatory issues, and knowledge of future trends in the delivery and financing of health care services in the public sector managed care environment. — ## Minimum Qualifications Requires a BA/BS in a related field; 10 years of legislative, regulatory, political, public affairs, or industry experience; or any combination of education and experience which would provide an equivalent background. — ## Preferred Skills, Capabilities and Experiences – MS preferred. – Prior client‑facing experience preferred. – Healthcare policy experience preferred. – Medicaid experience strongly preferred. – Experience writing formal communications for executive‑level audiences preferred. – Strong critical thinking, problem‑solving, time management, and attention to detail skills preferred. – Concise, precise, and motivating verbal and written communication skills demonstrated through ability to influence and persuade preferred. — ## Compensation For candidates working in person or virtually in the below locations, the salary range for this specific position is **$190,624 to $298,368**. **Locations:** Washington, DC; New York, NY; Woodland Hills, CA. In addition to salary, Elevance Health offers benefits such as a comprehensive benefits package, incentive and recognition programs, equity stock purchase, and 401(k) contribution (subject to eligibility requirements). The salary offered for this specific position is based on legitimate, non‑discriminatory factors set by the Company. Elevance Health is committed to ensuring equal pay opportunities for equal work regardless of gender, race, or any other protected category. **Note:** The salary range reflects Elevance Health’s good‑faith belief of possible compensation at the time of posting. Actual compensation may vary based on geographic location, experience, education, skill level, and market/business considerations. No amount is wages or compensation until earned, vested, and determinable under applicable policies and plans. Bonus, commission, benefits, or other compensation may be modified at the Company’s discretion, consistent with the law. Please be advised that Elevance Health only accepts resumes for compensation from agencies with a signed agreement. Any unsolicited resumes, including those submitted to hiring managers, are deemed the property of Elevance Health. — ## Who We Are Elevance Health is a health company dedicated to improving lives and communities and making healthcare simpler. We are a Fortune 25 company with a longstanding history in the healthcare industry, seeking leaders passionate about making an impact on our members and the communities we serve. — ## How We Work At Elevance Health, we are creating a culture designed to advance our strategy and support personal and professional growth. Our values and behaviors are the root of our culture. They power our business outcomes and drive shared success for consumers, associates, communities, and the business. We offer market‑competitive total rewards including merit increases, paid holidays, Paid Time Off, incentive bonus programs (unless covered by a collective bargaining agreement), medical, dental, vision, disability benefits, 401(k) + match, stock purchase plan, life insurance, wellness programs, and financial education resources. Elevance Health operates under a Hybrid Workforce Strategy. Unless specified as primarily virtual, associates are required to work onsite at least once per week, and potentially several times per week. Specific onsite expectations will be discussed during the hiring process. The health of our associates and communities is a top priority. Candidates in certain patient/member‑facing roles must be vaccinated against COVID‑19 and Influenza. Offers will be rescinded if vaccination requirements are not met unless an acceptable explanation is provided. Elevance Health follows all relevant federal, state, and local laws. Elevance Health is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to age, citizenship status, color, creed, disability, ethnicity, genetic information, gender identity or expression, marital status, national origin, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any other protected status. Applicants needing accommodation may contact [email protected] . Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered in accordance with federal, state, and local laws, including the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance and the California Fair Chance Act. Prospective employees required to be screened under Florida law should review education and awareness resources at HB531 | Florida Agency for Health Care Administration. item.title: Head of Government Relations
item.description: Head of Government Relations Organization: Qcells Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/07/2026 **POSITION DESCRIPTION** The Head of Government Relations is a critical leadership role within the Qcells Corporate Affairs Office. This position serves as the primary external representative of Qcells and other Hanwha energy‑related business and affiliates (“affiliates”) for overseeing all legislative, regulatory, and public policy matters. As the manager of Qcells’ Washington, D.C. office, this role is responsible for developing and executing federal and state public policy strategies to create an optimal environment for Qcells and its affiliates’ business interests in the United States. Working alongside the Head of Corporate Relations and his/her deputy, the Head of Government Relations is responsible for developing the company’s policy agenda, managing high‑level relationships with government officials, and securing outcomes that drive Qcells and other affiliates’ strategic growth. Additionally, this role ensures strategic alignment across the organization—from Communications, Policy & Regulatory Affairs, and Market Strategy and Sustainability—to guarantee a unified voice in all external engagements. — **RESPONSIBILITIES** **1. Strategic Leadership & Advocacy (Federal & State)** **Unified GR Strategy:** Develop and execute a comprehensive advocacy strategy that integrates and coordinates Federal, State, and Local government relations. **External Representation:** Act as the “External Representative” of Qcells, leading direct engagement with the White House, Congress, Federal Agencies, Governors, and State Legislatures on behalf of Qcells. **Policy Agenda Setting:** Define and drive the company’s legislative and regulatory priorities to protect and advance business interests in close coordination with senior business leadership. **2. Stakeholder Management & Coalition Building** **Network Development:** Build and maintain durable relationships with key policymakers, regulators, and influencers in Washington, D.C., and key states where Qcells and its affiliates operate. **Coalition Leadership:** Proactively lead and support industry coalitions, trade associations, and think‑tank engagements to amplify Qcells’ and its affiliates’ voice and influence broader energy and trade policy debates. **3. Organizational Collaboration** Work closely with the Head of Corporate Relations, his/her deputy, and the broader Corporate Affairs leadership to ensure internal strategies support external advocacy goals, including work of the Communications, Trade and Regulatory Affairs, and Market Strategy and Sustainability teams. Serve as a primary advisor to senior leadership on political risks, legislative trends, and opportunities that impact the company’s business and reputation. Ensure the Head of Corporate Relations and his/her deputy are kept fully informed and copied on all key reports, communications, and matters requiring executive input or approval. Provide strategic direction to the Communications, Policy & Regulatory Affairs, and Market Strategy and Sustainability teams to ensure that all external messaging, industry affairs, and regulatory efforts are fully aligned with the company’s government relations objectives and directions. **4. Team & Office Leadership** **Direct Leadership:** Lead and mentor a high‑performing Government Relations Department. **Office Administration & Conduct:** Serve as the Site Lead for the Washington, D.C. office, overseeing the professional conduct, attendance, and work attitude of all on‑site personnel. Responsible for maintaining a disciplined, professional, and high‑performance office culture. **Consultant Management:** Manage and direct external lobbying firms and consultants to maximize their effectiveness and ROI. **Flexible Schedule:** Due to the reporting relationship with the Global CEO and the need to coordinate with Global Headquarters, this position requires flexibility to attend conference calls and meetings outside of standard business hours (e.g., early mornings, evenings, or weekends). — **REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS** Strategic public policy thinker with track record of delivering legislative and regulatory outcomes at the federal, state, and local levels of government. Thorough understanding of legislative and regulatory processes as well as deep insights into the political, commercial, and third‑party interests that influence public policy debates. Successful management of advocacy campaigns before multiple levels of government in the energy and environment policy arenas. Ability to set the direction and strategy for a unified government relations function encompassing both Federal and State affairs. Extensive network of contacts in the federal and state legislative and executive branches of government. Politically savvy with experience in electoral politics as well as in working constructively within coalitions. Collaborative but decisive professional demeanor based on strong interpersonal skills. A resourceful and committed work ethic based on the pursuit of excellence in executing all responsibilities. Proven ability to build, lead, and motivate a high‑performing government relations department capable of advancing the company’s public policy objectives. Excellent legislative and regulatory skills and knowledge. Capable of articulating a compelling and convincing vision of public policy objectives to internal and external stakeholders. Demonstrated experience building partnerships, strategic alliances, and coalitions. Reputation for building strong durable relationships with government officials and staff. Executive presence and strong leadership skills with a commitment to initiative, resourcefulness, and leadership by example. Strong business acumen based on a broad understanding of business needs and how public policy strategies enable sought‑for outcomes and success. — **COMPENSATION** In accordance with applicable pay transparency laws, the anticipated annual base salary for this position is: Zone 1 (SF, NYC): $327,124 – $344,340 Zone 2 (CA, NJ, NY): $299,863 – $315,645 Zone 3 (All Others): $272,603 – $286,950 The applicable salary range is based on the employee’s primary work location. Individual compensation will be determined based on qualifications, relevant experience, education, skills, internal equity, and other business‑related factors. Hanwha Q CELLS America Inc. (“HQCA”) is a Qcells company, one of the world’s largest manufacturers and providers of solar photovoltaic (PV) products and solutions. Headquartered in Irvine, California, HQCA has been rapidly expanding its business in North America through the expansion of products and solutions, including distributed energy solutions, direct‑to‑homeowner solar sales and financing, and EPC services. We provide an opportunity to be part of an exciting and growing world‑class global business in an interesting and expanding industry of the future. — **PHYSICAL, MENTAL & ENVIRONMENTAL DEMANDS** To comply with the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, the essential physical, mental, and environmental requirements for this job are listed below. These are requirements normally expected to perform regular job duties. Incumbent must be able to successfully perform all functions of the job with or without reasonable accommodation. item.title: Government Relations Manager
item.description: Government Relations Manager Organization: Qcells Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/07/2026 **POSITION DESCRIPTION** Qcells is seeking a detail‑oriented and strategically minded Government Affairs Manager to join its Public Policy and Government Relations team. The ideal candidate will possess strong analytical, writing, and relationship‑building skills, with the ability to develop and execute advocacy strategies that advance the company’s federal policy priorities. This role supports high‑impact government affairs initiatives across legislative, regulatory, and political issues affecting Qcells’ U.S. manufacturing, energy deployment, and domestic supply chain investments. Success in this position requires the ability to translate complex federal policy developments into actionable business strategies while building and maintaining productive relationships with Congress, federal agencies, industry associations, and external stakeholders. This position is based in Washington, D.C. and requires working on‑site five days a week. Some travel required (approx. 10–15%). — **RESPONSIBILITIES** **Legislative & Regulatory Advocacy:** Support the development and execution of federal government affairs strategies that advance Qcells’ legislative, regulatory, tax, trade, permitting, and manufacturing priorities. **Congressional & Agency Engagement:** Build and maintain relationships with Members of Congress, congressional staff, executive branch agencies, and federal policymakers. Coordinate meetings, facility visits, briefings, and stakeholder engagement opportunities. **Policy Analysis:** Monitor, analyze, and communicate legislative, regulatory, and political developments affecting the clean energy, manufacturing, trade, tax, and infrastructure sectors. Assess risks and opportunities and provide timely recommendations to internal stakeholders. **Advocacy Materials:** Draft policy briefs, comment letters, white papers, talking points, briefing memoranda, presentations, fact sheets, congressional testimony, and executive correspondence to support advocacy efforts. **Coalition & Industry Engagement:** Represent Qcells in industry associations, trade groups, coalitions, and policy forums. Coordinate advocacy initiatives with external partners to advance shared federal policy objectives. **Cross‑functional Collaboration:** Partner closely with legal, communications, commercial, manufacturing, sustainability, and business leadership teams to ensure government affairs priorities align with corporate objectives and business strategy. **Political & Legislative Monitoring:** Track congressional activity, committee hearings, regulatory actions, and industry developments. Prepare regular policy updates and executive briefings for senior leadership. **Issue Management:** Support strategic responses to emerging legislative and regulatory issues by coordinating internal stakeholders and developing advocacy strategies. **Event Support:** Assist with planning and execution of Capitol Hill meetings, executive briefings, facility tours, trade association engagements, and policy conferences. — **REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS** Bachelor’s degree in political science, public policy, public administration, law, economics, business, or a related field. Five or more years of experience in government affairs, public policy, Congress, the executive branch, a trade association, or corporate government relations. Strong understanding of the federal legislative and regulatory process. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with the ability to distill complex policy issues into clear, actionable recommendations. Excellent analytical, organizational, and project management skills. Proficiency in Microsoft Office. Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast‑paced environment while maintaining exceptional attention to detail. Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to build trusted relationships with internal and external stakeholders. — **PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS** Experience with federal energy, manufacturing, trade, tax, or infrastructure policy. Familiarity with Congress and federal agencies, including Treasury, Commerce, DOE, USTR, CBP, EPA, or other agencies relevant to Qcells’ business. Experience developing federal legislative strategy, coalition management, or issue advocacy campaigns. Understanding of the clean energy industry, domestic manufacturing policy, and federal tax incentives. Demonstrated ability to translate complex legislative and regulatory developments into business strategy and executive recommendations. — **COMPENSATION** In accordance with applicable pay transparency laws, the anticipated annual base salary for this position is: Zone 1 (Bay Area, NYC): $146,200 – $182,600 Zone 2 (CA, NJ, NY, DC): $134,000 – $167,400 Zone 3 (All others): $121,800 – $152,200 The applicable salary range is based on the employee’s primary work location. Individual compensation will be determined based on qualifications, relevant experience, education, skills, internal equity, and other business‑related factors. — Hanwha Q CELLS America Inc. (“HQCA”) is a Qcells company, one of the world’s largest manufacturers and providers of solar photovoltaic (PV) products and solutions. Headquartered in Irvine, California, HQCA has been rapidly expanding its business in North America through the expansion of products and solutions, including distributed energy solutions, direct‑to‑homeowner solar sales and financing, and EPC services. We provide an opportunity to be part of an exciting and growing world‑class global business in an interesting and expanding industry of the future. — **PHYSICAL, MENTAL & ENVIRONMENTAL DEMANDS** To comply with the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, the essential physical, mental, and environmental requirements for this job are listed below. These are requirements normally expected to perform regular job duties. Incumbent must be able to successfully perform all of the functions of the job with or without reasonable accommodation. item.title: Senior Corporate Counsel, Global Deal Team
item.description: Senior Corporate Counsel, Global Deal Team Organization: Microsoft Location: Redmond, WA | Mountain View, CA | Washington D.C. | New York, NY | Chicago, IL Date Posted: 08/07/2026 ## Overview Join Microsoft’s Global Deal Team in Americas—a high-performing, distributed legal organization within Corporate, External and Legal Affairs (CELA), a community of 2,000+ legal and compliance professionals. The team supports complex enterprise transactions with Microsoft’s largest and most strategic customers (excluding public sector) around the world. The Senior Corporate Counsel role helps drive revenue and accelerate deal velocity through strategic legal leadership, direct engagement on high-impact negotiations, operational excellence, and innovative use of technology and AI—while navigating the regulatory, cultural, and contracting diversity of multiple jurisdictions and languages. Your primary responsibility will be supporting business teams that are responsible for pursuing and closing strategic and complex commercial transactions with Microsoft’s most important customers. You will partner with sales, operations, finance, product and engineering, marketing, and security/trust stakeholders to align customer expectations with Microsoft’s risk posture, policies, and compliance obligations. The role collaborates closely with regional Legal Affairs teams who are subject matter experts in the Americas markets and their regulations and who lead public sector matters and non-deal workstreams. Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond. This role can be based in Redmond, Silicon Valley, Chicago, New York City, and Washington, D.C. This role involves some international travel. — ## Responsibilities Lead legal support for complex technology transactions by developing negotiation strategies, solving problems creatively, and coordinating across CELA and business team subject matter experts. Provide strategic advice on newly emerging information technology business models, including AI, while staying updated on rules, regulations, and other statutory requirements relating to Microsoft business. Draft, negotiate, and structure integrated agreements encompassing sales, procurement, strategic partnerships, investments, and other innovative business models, addressing legal issues such as commercial contracts, intellectual property, and data protection. Guide escalations to appropriate senior leaders to take smart and well-informed risks to meet customer needs. Support the business teams in ensuring legal compliance and providing solutions to mitigate risks. Lead cross-team, cross-disciplinary strategic projects and initiatives and improve internal processes in the legal department. Communicate in ways that create clarity and advance negotiations and projects to achieve closure of open issues. Provide practical and strategic advice to business clients and CELA colleagues. Collaborate with executive leadership to ensure a coordinated voice on high-visibility issues, simplifying and summarizing complex matters into actionable strategies and recommendations. — ## Qualifications ### Required / Minimum Qualifications Juris Doctor Degree or international equivalent degree AND 6+ years experience as a practicing attorney at a law firm or in-house roles specializing in complex transactions, including technology transactions, M&A, business development, or related work managing complex transactions involving multiple stakeholders. OR equivalent experience. Active license to practice law in a jurisdiction and capable of meeting admission requirements in relevant jurisdiction. ### Additional or Preferred Qualifications Highly developed negotiation, legal drafting, and communications skills. Deal strategy skills with a demonstrated history of successfully managing large-scale, nuanced transactions that involve multiple strategic, operational, and legal dimensions and the requirement to meet deadlines in the face of competing priorities. Experience advising on technology transactions (e.g., cloud services, software licensing, SaaS, professional services, strategic partnerships, and/or AI models and solutions). Comfort with ambiguity and a bias for action in a fast-paced, highly matrixed environment with sound judgment incorporating strong legal analysis, a pragmatic approach, and consideration of business goals, risk tolerance, and stakeholder priorities. Enthusiastic team player who enjoys partnering with cross-functional teams to solve complex issues, invest in others, and work collaboratively to generate consensus across diverse points of view. Inquisitive and curious—enjoys learning new concepts, tackling cutting-edge legal issues, thrives amidst change, and exhibits a growth mindset. Additional language skill would be a plus. — ## Compensation Legal Counsel IC5 — The typical base pay range for this role across the U.S. is USD $147,000 – $258,000 per year. There is a different range applicable to specific work locations within the San Francisco Bay area and New York City metropolitan area, and the base pay range for this role in those locations is USD $185,900 – $278,900 per year. Certain roles may be eligible for benefits and other compensation. Find additional benefits and pay information here: [https://careers.microsoft.com/us/en/us-corporate-pay] This position will be open for a minimum of 5 days, with applications accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled. — ## Equal Opportunity Statement Microsoft is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, citizenship, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, immigration status, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran or military status, race, ethnicity, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable local laws, regulations, and ordinances. If you need assistance with religious accommodations and/or a reasonable accommodation due to a disability during the application process, read more about requesting accommodations. item.title: Government Affairs Director/Executive Director
item.description: Government Affairs Director/Executive Director Organization: The Digital Chamber (TDC) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/07/2026 ## About The Digital Chamber The Digital Chamber (TDC) is the leading trade association representing the digital asset and blockchain industry. Our membership includes more than 250 companies across the digital asset ecosystem, including exchanges, custodians, financial institutions, infrastructure providers, software developers, investors, and emerging technology companies. We work with policymakers, regulators, and industry leaders to advance clear, durable, and responsible public policy that supports American innovation, protects consumers, and strengthens the United States’ leadership in the digital economy. ## Position Summary The Government Affairs Director/Executive Director position will manage relationships with congressional offices, track and analyze legislative and regulatory developments, prepare advocacy materials, and coordinate high‑impact engagements between policymakers and TDC members. The position requires strong political judgment, excellent written and verbal communication skills, and the ability to move quickly between policy analysis, relationship management, and detailed execution. The ideal candidate understands how Washington works, is comfortable representing an organization before senior government and industry stakeholders, and can translate complex policy developments into clear, actionable information. This is a hands‑on role within a fast‑moving team and requires someone who is equally comfortable developing an engagement strategy, drafting a congressional briefing memo, and managing the details of a successful fly‑in or policymaker meeting. ## Key Responsibilities ### Congressional and Administration Engagement – Develop and maintain bipartisan relationships with Members of Congress, congressional staff, Administration officials, and federal agency personnel. – Represent TDC in meetings with policymakers and communicate the organization’s policy priorities clearly and effectively. – Identify opportunities to advance TDC priorities through legislation, amendments, hearings, roundtables, letters, briefings, and other government engagement. – Prepare TDC executives, member companies, and policy leaders for meetings, testimony, briefings, and public engagements. – Manage meeting follow‑up and ensure commitments, requests, and next steps are documented and completed. – Experience leading and managing a PAC. ### Legislative and Regulatory Strategy – Monitor congressional, regulatory, and political developments affecting digital assets, blockchain technology, financial services, and emerging technology. – Analyze legislation, amendments, agency actions, hearings, and political dynamics to determine their potential impact on TDC and its members. – Produce clear and timely legislative updates, policy memoranda, talking points, briefing materials, hearing summaries, and advocacy documents. – Support the development and execution of advocacy strategies around market structure, stablecoins, taxation, financial regulation, cybersecurity, illicit finance, software development, tokenization, and other priority issues. – Maintain internal tracking systems for legislation, congressional engagement, office intelligence, and policy developments. ### Member Engagement – Serve as a trusted resource for TDC members seeking information about congressional activity, policy developments, and engagement opportunities. – Translate Washington developments into practical, business‑relevant insights for member companies. – Coordinate member participation in congressional meetings, fly‑ins, roundtables, briefings, and other advocacy initiatives. – Work with TDC’s policy committees and working groups to gather member input and develop consensus‑based advocacy positions. – Ensure members receive timely preparation materials, logistical information, and meaningful follow‑up after government engagements. ### Advocacy Programs and Events – Help plan and execute congressional fly‑ins, staff briefings, policymaker roundtables, educational programs, and other government affairs events. – Recruit and coordinate participation from Members of Congress, congressional staff, regulators, Administration officials, and other public‑sector leaders. – Manage event‑related outreach, scheduling, briefing materials, run‑of‑show documents, and follow‑up. – Support TDC leadership during major legislative moments, hearings, markups, votes, and other high‑priority advocacy efforts. ### Cross‑Functional Support – Work closely with TDC’s policy, communications, membership, events, and executive teams to ensure consistent messaging and coordinated execution. – Support the development of public statements, congressional correspondence, testimony, comment letters, presentations, and member communications. – Contribute to organizational planning, reporting, and the evaluation of government affairs priorities and outcomes. – Assist with other government affairs and organizational initiatives as needed. ## Qualifications – Three to eight years of relevant experience in Congress, a federal agency, a trade association, a public affairs firm, an advocacy organization, or an in‑house government affairs role. – Demonstrated understanding of the federal legislative and regulatory process. – Experience developing and maintaining professional relationships with congressional offices and other government stakeholders. – Excellent writing, editing, research, and verbal communication skills. – Ability to analyze complex policy issues and explain them clearly to both policy and business audiences. – Strong political judgment and an understanding of bipartisan congressional dynamics. – Proven ability to manage multiple priorities, meet tight deadlines, and maintain attention to detail in a fast‑moving environment. – Ability to operate independently, take ownership of assignments, and anticipate the needs of senior leaders and member companies. – Professional discretion and sound judgment when handling sensitive or confidential information. ## Preferred Qualifications – Experience working on financial services, digital assets, blockchain technology, banking, securities, commodities, taxation, cybersecurity, or emerging technology policy. – Existing bipartisan relationships with relevant congressional committees and offices. – Experience supporting congressional hearings, legislative markups, fly‑ins, executive‑level meetings, or advocacy campaigns. – Familiarity with congressional and stakeholder management platforms. – Experience working within a membership‑based organization or managing relationships with corporate stakeholders. – An understanding of how public policy decisions affect business operations, product development, market access, and regulatory risk. ## What Success Looks Like A successful Government Affairs Director/Executive Director will: – Build credible, productive relationships with policymakers and congressional staff. – Provide TDC members and leadership with timely, accurate, and actionable political intelligence. – Execute advocacy initiatives with strong attention to both strategy and detail. – Anticipate legislative opportunities and risks before they become urgent. – Strengthen coordination between TDC’s government affairs team, policy experts, executives, and member companies. – Help convert TDC’s policy priorities into measurable government affairs outcomes. ## Equal Opportunity Employment The Digital Chamber is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering a professional and inclusive workplace and consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. item.title: Regional Director for State Campaigns & Programs
item.description: Regional Director for State Campaigns & Programs Organization: All Voting is Local Location: Remote Date Posted: 08/07/2026 **Job Title:** Regional Director **Reports To:** Executive Vice President for State Campaigns & Programs (EVP States) **Salary:** $133,232 – $191,521 **Direct Reports:** Four **Location:** Remote **Position Status:** Full-time, Exempt — ## Regional Director for State Campaigns & Programs ### About the Role Reporting to the Executive Vice President for State Campaigns & Programs (“EVP States”), the Regional Director serves as the senior leader responsible for providing strategic leadership, supervision, and partnership to All Voting Is Local’s State Directors across the organization’s state programs. The Regional Director develops senior leaders, ensures alignment across states, strengthens cross-functional collaboration, and represents the organization in national and regional strategic spaces. The role serves as a key thought partner to the EVP States, helping translate organizational priorities into coordinated state strategies while ensuring state teams have the leadership, support, and resources needed to execute effectively. This position works across both All Voting and AVL Action. — ## Core Role Responsibilities ### Strategic Leadership & State Program Oversight #### Lead and supervise State Directors – Directly supervise and coach a team of State Directors, providing strategic guidance, executive-level support, and accountability. – Serve as a thought partner to State Directors as they navigate complex political environments, coalition dynamics, campaign strategy, organizational growth, and team leadership of the Democracy Defense Managers (DDMs) and Campaign Managers (CMs) who report to them. – Foster a culture of collaboration, shared learning, and continuous leadership development across all state programs. #### Strengthen state program excellence – Ensure consistency in leadership practices, planning, execution, and evaluation across state programs while allowing flexibility for state-specific strategies. – Help State Directors identify emerging opportunities, risks, and strategic pivots throughout election and legislative cycles. – Support directors in making high-impact decisions involving campaign priorities, coalition strategy, staffing, and resource allocation. — ### Organizational Strategy and Cross-Functional Leadership #### Drive alignment across departments – Partner closely with Communications, Policy & Analytics, Development, Operations, and the Senior Leadership Team to ensure state work advances organizational priorities. – Translate national organizational priorities into coordinated state-level implementation. – Identify opportunities for cross-state collaboration and shared strategies. #### Advance organizational priorities – Help establish department priorities, annual goals, and operational plans. – Identify organizational gaps and recommend improvements to systems, processes, and collaboration. – Lead department-wide initiatives that strengthen consistency and effectiveness across all state programs. — ### Coalition Leadership & External Representation #### Represent All Voting Is Local nationally – Serve as a senior organizational representative in national and regional democracy coalitions, partner convenings, funder meetings, and strategic tables. – Build and maintain relationships with key coalition partners, movement organizations, and allied stakeholders. – Represent the States & Campaigns department in cross-organizational initiatives and collaborative campaigns. #### Strengthen movement partnerships – Help identify opportunities for deeper collaboration across the democracy ecosystem. – Coordinate multi-state partnerships and support strategic alignment with national allies. – Serve as a trusted external ambassador for the organization. — ### Campaign Strategy & State Support – Partner with State Directors to develop sophisticated campaign strategies that combine legislative advocacy, communications, and coalition building. – Help evaluate campaign effectiveness and identify opportunities to scale successful approaches across states. – Ensure state campaigns reflect organizational priorities while remaining responsive to local political conditions. – Support rapid strategic decision-making during emerging election issues and high-profile campaign moments. – Provide department approvals and reporting. — ## Department Leadership – Serve as a senior advisor and surrogate for the EVP States, representing the department internally and externally as needed. – Contribute to executive planning, strategic decision-making, and organizational leadership discussions. – Support hiring, onboarding, succession planning, and leadership development within the States & Campaigns department. – Foster an inclusive, transparent, and accountable leadership culture. — ## Operational Leadership – Monitor state program performance, budgets, and staffing in partnership with Finance and Operations. – Ensure appropriate compliance practices and identify issues requiring legal or executive review. – Oversee reporting, planning, and evaluation processes across state programs. – Develop and improve department-wide systems, SOPs, and operational practices. — ## Required Qualifications & Competencies – Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience. – 12–15 years of leadership experience in advocacy, organizing, campaigns, public policy, civic engagement, democracy reform, or a related field. – At least 5 years of experience managing experienced managers, with a demonstrated ability to coach, develop, and lead high-performing leaders. – Demonstrated success leading complex, multi-state or multi-regional programs, campaigns, or initiatives that require strategic coordination across diverse political and organizational environments. – Proven ability to provide executive-level strategic counsel and thought partnership to senior leaders navigating complex political, organizational, and operational challenges. – Experience building and sustaining relationships with coalition partners, funders, public officials, and other external stakeholders, and representing an organization in high-level strategic forums. – Demonstrated ability to influence and collaborate across departments to drive alignment, solve complex challenges, and advance organizational priorities. – Strong political judgment and ability to assess risk, respond to rapidly changing environments, and make sound strategic decisions under pressure. – Experience overseeing organizational planning, performance management, goal setting, and accountability systems. – Exceptional written, verbal, facilitation, and interpersonal communication skills, including the ability to communicate effectively with executive leadership, staff, partners, and external audiences. – Demonstrated commitment to equity, inclusion, and building collaborative, high-performing teams. – Ability to manage multiple priorities, exercise sound judgment, and maintain discretion while working in a fast-paced environment. – Willingness and ability to travel regularly (approximately 40%) to support state programs, organizational priorities, and external partnerships. — ## Desired Qualifications & Competencies – Master’s degree or other advanced degree in public policy, political science, nonprofit management, law, or a related field. – Experience serving on an executive leadership or senior management team. – Experience leading leaders in a distributed or multi-state organization. – Deep knowledge of election administration, voting rights, democracy reform, or civic engagement ecosystems. – Established relationships within national democracy, civil rights, advocacy, or movement organizations. – Experience managing complex organizational change, growth, or restructuring efforts. – Fluency in a second language. item.title: Executive Director, U.S.-Korea Business Council
item.description: Executive Director, U.S.-Korea Business Council Organization: U.S. Chamber of Commerce Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/07/2026 ## **About Us** If you are passionate about the ability of American business to improve lives, solve problems, and strengthen society, the U.S. Chamber of Commerce is the place for you. As the world’s largest business organization, we believe in building a future that gives everyone the opportunity to pursue a better tomorrow. We make it our job today–and every day–to build the strongest relationships possible among the American people, business leaders, and elected officials in Washington, D.C., state capitals, and countries around the globe. For them and the businesses we represent, the U.S. Chamber is a trusted advocate and partner. We are driven by the pursuit of innovation and partnership and hold ourselves to the highest standards. Our commitment to our members is matched only by our commitment to our employees. As part of our team, we will support your long-term career development while delivering relevant learning opportunities. We will empower you to lead, develop deep expertise, and find new approaches to solving the toughest challenges. — ## **Position Overview** Working with the senior vice president for Asia, the ideal candidate will oversee the Chamber’s work in the Republic of Korea. The candidate will engage with and provide analytical and advocacy tools to members with interests in Northeast Asia, concentrating on maintaining strong relations with key government and nongovernmental interlocutors and solving market access and trade restraint issues. The candidate will hold and conduct programs for members and key policy leaders, stakeholders, and intellectual drivers of influence in the region. — ## **Responsibilities** – **Maintain and expand relationships** with government interlocutors, concentrating on key departments in Seoul and the Korean Embassy in Washington, D.C. – **Provide critical information** and analysis to members on key business developments in the region. – **Offer strategic thinking** on processes and programs designed to further member interests in the region. – **Conduct program opportunities**, both in-person and remote, to engage with key decision-makers in the region. – **Manage a small team** and coordinate with policy and other resources in the Chamber. – **Serve as a public face** for the Chamber and its work in the region. — ## **Qualifications** – Bachelor’s degree; advanced degree preferred. – At least 15 years of experience working with corporate interests in Asia, with a particular focus on South Korea. – Deep knowledge of the U.S. trade and economic policymaking environment and network in the region. – Experience working in the U.S. government in either the legislative or executive branches on Korean issues. – Extensive writing experience. – Strong service orientation, excellent communication skills, and executive presence. — The salary range for this position is **$147,923.00 to $180,000.00**. The actual salary paid for this position will vary based on market data, an applicant’s qualifications, relevant degrees, certifications, and other factors. Our full-time employees are eligible for benefits, including health care, vision, dental, retirement, and paid leave. We provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. #LI-Hybrid Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Social Media and Community Manager
item.description: Social Media and Community Manager Organization: American College of Gastroenterology Location: North Bethesda, MD Date Posted: 08/07/2026 ## The American College of Gastroenterology (ACG) The American College of Gastroenterology (ACG), a leading medical specialty society located in North Bethesda, MD, seeks a Social Media and Community Manager to assist the College in furthering its mission. This position supports the Vice President of Communications in a range of in‑person, web, and social media communications, including its foremost responsibility managing ACG’s social media accounts and online community. — ## DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES ### Social Media Maintain and execute social media calendar, incorporating new, recurring, and evergreen content, triaging requests, drafting and refining engaging copy, identifying accompanying multimedia, and scheduling posts. Oversee and continue to optimize overall social media strategy, ensuring consistent messaging and publication cadence, assessing content performance, and refining approaches based on best practices in order to strengthen engagement, extend reach, and advance the mission. Develop, collaborate with design colleagues, and/or source compelling visual content for social posts. Monitor, engage, and, as appropriate, respond to comments, mentions, posts, and direct messages. Serve as the liaison for volunteer social media teams, including recruiting, onboarding, and serving as an ongoing resource. Remain current—staying apprised of: • Social media trends, platform and algorithm updates, best practices, and sentiment. • Outside programs and services that provide supplemental support for social media management, exploring value and vetting and proposing their adoption, when appropriate. • New platforms, evaluating opportunities and potential challenges. Provide onsite social media coverage of key College events (e.g., Annual Scientific Meeting, Advocacy Day, and others, as advised). Operate with an innovative mindset, brainstorming, testing, and implementing new ways to present and deliver content. Collect, review, and report performance analytics across platforms and prepare routine and discrete reports, as needed. — ### Online Community Oversee and optimize community strategy to continue growth in user base, spur conversation and engagement, and advance the mission. Monitor and, as appropriate, respond to posts and comments. Serve as the primary liaison to expert panel members, including recruiting, onboarding, and serving as an ongoing resource. Collaborate closely with external technology vendor on multiple fronts. Spearhead promotion of community membership and participation among new and existing ACG members through a variety of channels. Review and report performance analytics across platforms and prepare routine and discrete reports, as needed. — ### Additional Communications Responsibilities Support certain tasks for ACG Magazine and communications‑related committees. Attend and actively participate in meetings with colleagues, committees, and others. Make content updates to select webpages. Support video editing efforts, as needed. Additional duties as assigned. — ## EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE Bachelor’s degree required—preferably in communications, digital media, journalism, or a related field. 5–7 years of communications experience, including in social media management. Preferred but not required: Experience in health/science communications, government, and/or associations. — ## SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS Microsoft Office suite Canva Social media strategy, design, and implementation Excellent writing, copyediting, and verbal and interpersonal communications skills are essential for this position Advanced understanding of social media and the digital landscape Flexibility, organizational skills, and the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously to thrive in an at‑times fast‑paced environment Excellent sense of judgement and discretion in communications Positive, collaborative approach, working comfortably with colleagues across the organization Open to new ideas, with a strong desire to continuously improve — ### Bonus Skills Adobe InCopy Adobe Photoshop Adobe Premiere Pro WordPress Experience with an email service provider(s) Experience with scholarly publications — ## WORK ENVIRONMENT ### Salary and Benefits The anticipated salary range for this position is $60,000–$75,000 annually. Salary is based on a range of factors that include relevant experience, knowledge, skills, and other job‑related qualifications. Benefits package includes health, dental, vision, disability and life insurance, retirement plan with employer matching, and paid time off. ACG supports its staff members with professional development and training opportunities. — ### Schedule Monday to Friday ACG operates on a hybrid work schedule—DMV‑area applicants will be considered. item.title: Assistant Account Executive
item.description: Assistant Account Executive Organization: CLYDE Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/07/2026 CLYDE is a fast-paced, impact agency committed to delivering innovative, strategic, and visually compelling communications solutions for our diverse portfolio of clients. We work with clients who want to make a difference by moving the world forward – helping them do it through earned, owned, and paid media programs, creative solutions, and smarter, informed strategies. We are passionate about pushing the boundaries of design while staying grounded in strategy, brand integrity, and results. We are seeking a talented and dynamic Assistant Account Executive to join our growing team and bring our core values to life. The Assistant Account Executive plays a role on 4–6 client accounts, including public affairs, advocacy, and trade association clients operating in complex and rapidly changing policy environments. AAEs support executing Scope-of-Work (SOW) activities, including media relations, content creation, digital activity, research, monitoring, and reporting. The ideal candidate is a strong writer and thoughtful communicator with a genuine interest in politics, policy, and current events. This person should bring sound judgment, intellectual curiosity, and an eagerness to contribute ideas. **Our Core Values:** ● Be Better Than We Were Yesterday ● Our Clients’ Success Defines Ours ● Be The Blueprint ● Creativity is Our Idea of Fun ● We Want to Go Far, So We Go Together **What You’ll Do:** ● Support public affairs, advocacy, and trade association accounts through media relations, industry monitoring, and research. ● Closely follow political, legislative, regulatory, and industry developments and make recommendations based on emerging trends. ● Support project management by developing and maintaining weekly updates, agendas, action items, timelines, daily monitoring reports, and other materials that keep client teams organized and workstreams moving forward. ● Participate actively in client and internal strategy discussions, bringing informed questions, observations, and recommendations. ● Email/communicate directly with clients. ● Work with client teams to respond quickly and deliver on client requests. ● Execute communications tactics on behalf of clients, including developing media lists, pitching media, crafting coverage reports, creating social content, and drafting op-eds, press releases, and research memos. ● Find opportunities to mentor Account Coordinators and Fellows. ● Support business development efforts through research and internal brainstorms. **Our Core Competencies:** ● Client Service ● Communications ● Critical/Strategic Thinking ● Professional Development ● Leadership **Position Expectations:** ● Adheres to the firm’s policies and procedures. ● Deadline oriented; able to complete assignments in line with client’s deadline needs. ● Shows a commitment to uphold and defend the highest levels of ethical conduct. ● Actively seeks opportunities to learn and participate in client and business development projects. ● Contributes ideas to help make CLYDE the best place to work. ● Fierce commitment to, and respect for, a diverse and inclusive workplace. ● Preferably local to the DC metro area. ● Demonstrates strong judgment when working on politically sensitive, reputationally complex, or fast-moving issues. ● Comfortable working across differing political perspectives and approaches public affairs work with professionalism. **Qualifications / Required Skills:** ● 1–2 years of professional communications experience. ● Demonstrated interest in politics, public policy, current events, and the intersection of government, business, and public opinion. ● Strong writing skills across formats, including media materials, talking points, memos, digital content, and client communications. ● Comfortable with Microsoft and Google office products. ● Interested in using practical applications of AI. ● Experience with media relations techniques and pitching media. ● Seeks and is receptive to feedback; puts feedback into action. ● Mastery of AP Style and exceptional attention to detail. The salary range for this position is $49,500 – $66,400. To apply, candidates should submit resumes to [email protected] Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: State Government Affairs Coordinator
item.description: State Government Affairs Coordinator Organization: Brewers Association Location: Boulder, CO Date Posted: 08/07/2026 ## General Purpose Advance the Brewers Association’s state government affairs objectives, often working in concert with state brewers guilds. The state government affairs coordinator works with BA staff, state brewers associations (guilds), and BA members on policy formulation, resource development, legislative and regulatory monitoring, facilitating communications among guilds, and supporting advocacy for desired legislative and regulatory outcomes. — ## Essential Duties – Maintain regular contact with state guild boards and executive directors both to monitor state government affairs activities and to coordinate Brewers Association and guild government affairs programs. – Cultivate and maintain professional working relationships with guild executive directors and key representatives of other industry stakeholders (e.g., state wholesaler associations, winery associations). – Monitor and track state legislative and administrative rulemaking activity, report to state guilds and Brewers Association staff on such activity, and recommend possible priorities for state guild and Brewers Association efforts. – Where appropriate, organize and coordinate coalitions to advance government affairs objectives across multiple states or across multiple stakeholders within a state. – Assist Brewers Association Government Affairs staff and the Government Affairs Committee in developing state legislative priorities. – Formulate arguments and create advocacy materials in support of Brewers Association state government affairs objectives. – Support guild efforts to advance legislative and rulemaking objectives and coordinate with—and in some cases retain and supervise—outside consultants, where appropriate. – Help compile and maintain multistate databases on state alcohol laws and policies and ensure that such databases remain current as laws and policies change. – Where appropriate, prepare and submit written or oral testimony in support of pending bills or pending rulemaking projects. – Where appropriate, present at guild meetings and other gatherings to promote the Brewers Association and to provide the Association’s perspective on various policy issues. – When traveling, visit with brewers and owners at member and lapsed‑member breweries in the area to provide insights into BA’s government affairs efforts and outcomes. This role is open to fully remote candidates if located outside of the Colorado Front Range. Employees based on Colorado’s Front Range will follow a hybrid schedule, working onsite at our Boulder headquarters Tuesdays and Thursdays. — ## Skills, Knowledge and Abilities – Ability to read, understand, and communicate proposed legislation to stakeholders required. – Strong self‑motivation and ability to work independently. – Curious mind and willingness to learn new things, particularly as the position will require the coordinator to develop a strong knowledge of the policy landscape of multiple states. – Proficient at preparing and maintaining accurate compilations that summarize bills, laws, rulemaking projects, and similar relevant subjects. – Ability to write persuasive talking points, legislative testimony, comments on pending rules, and other documents necessary for advancing government affairs objectives. – Skilled at reading and understanding legal documents (e.g., bills and rulemaking proposals). – Ability to make engaging and persuasive oral presentations to state guilds, lawmakers, and regulatory bodies. – Adept at building professional relationships and maintaining cordial relations even when taking a position contrary to that of a professional contact. – Occasional travel, sometimes on short notice. – State government affairs and/or public policy experience preferred. – College degree preferred. — ## Travel Required – Craft Brewers Conference and Tradeshow (location different each year) once per year – Hill Climb in Washington, DC once per year – Occasional other trips (estimated at one/two per year) to states as needed to support legislative efforts, present at guild functions, etc. — ## Additional Information This job description is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or qualifications associated with this job. **Apply Here:** [ https://www.click2apply.net/GdDK8ZF4LqZb5h5wPUk6Qm ] PI286303725 Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Communications Coordinator
item.description: Communications Coordinator Organization: California Native Plant Society (CNPS) Location: Sacramento, CA Date Posted: 08/10/2026 ## Communications Coordinator – CNPS Public Affairs Team The Communications Coordinator is a key member of CNPS’s Public Affairs team, a multidisciplinary group leading the organization’s external and internal communications, digital strategy, public policy, public engagement, partnerships, and publications. This role supports CNPS’s communications and public affairs efforts through content creation, media relations support, volunteer engagement, and administrative coordination. The Communications Coordinator develops content for a variety of platforms including CNPS’s website, email newsletters, publications, and marketing materials. The role also supports media outreach efforts, helps coordinate communication and training for CNPS Chapter volunteers, and maintains digital communication assets and systems. Working closely with colleagues across the organization, the Communications Coordinator helps ensure that CNPS communications are engaging, accurate, timely, and aligned with organizational priorities. This position is ideal for a collaborative communications professional who enjoys balancing content creation, relationship‑building, project coordination, and administrative support in service of CNPS’s mission. — ## What You’ll Do ### Content Development & Digital Communications (35%) Research, interview experts, and write occasional articles for Flora, CNPS’ quarterly print magazine. Develop content for and distribute CNPS’ monthly email newsletter. Create and update website content, including blog posts, event listings, and programmatic content. Adapt and update communications materials using established Canva templates, including flyers, presentations, postcards, and one‑pagers. Contribute content to annual reports, quarterly reports, and other marketing and communications materials. Support social media content creation, including recording direct‑to‑camera videos and assisting with multimedia storytelling projects. ### Chapter Communications Support (25%) Coordinate monthly virtual Public Affairs meetings for CNPS Chapter volunteers and prepare supporting materials. Collaborate with CNPS’s Digital Media & Website Producer to support volunteer training related to Chapter communications tools and websites (no coding experience required). Assist volunteers with access to and use of CNPS communication platforms. Serve as a point of coordination between the Public Affairs team and Chapter volunteers, helping connect inquiries to appropriate staff resources. ### Media Relations Support (20%) Draft press releases, media advisories, and other media materials. Assist with media outreach and reporter engagement efforts. Monitor and internally report on media coverage related to CNPS priorities on an ongoing basis. Maintain and update media contact databases and distribution lists, including by proactively researching and adding new contacts and removing out‑of‑date contacts. ### Administrative & Operational Support (20%) Organize and maintain digital assets in CNPS media management platforms. Respond to and route inquiries received through CNPS communication channels. Provide administrative and operational support that contributes to programmatic goals and priorities. Contribute to additional Public Affairs initiatives and special projects as assigned. — ## Physical Requirements This role is primarily performed in an office or remote work environment and requires prolonged computer use. Occasional travel within California may be required, including participation in events and field trips that may involve walking on uneven terrain. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this position. — ## Additional Information This is a full‑time, non‑exempt position. Standard working hours: Monday – Friday, 8:30 AM – 5:00 PM. Some evening and weekend work will be required to support meetings, events, or organizational priorities. This hybrid role requires regular participation in Sacramento‑area meetings and team activities while also supporting remote work. One or more in‑office days per week should be expected. Periodic travel within California is required and reimbursed according to CNPS policies. — ## What Success Looks Like (First 6–12 Months) Consistently contribute high‑quality content across CNPS communications channels. Support timely and effective media outreach efforts that increase visibility of CNPS priorities. Coordinate successful Chapter volunteer communications meetings and trainings. Provide responsive support to volunteers and staff using communication tools and platforms. Maintain organized communications assets, media contacts, and project workflows. Build collaborative relationships across CNPS programs and with Chapter volunteers. — ## Who You Are ### Communications & Content Development At least 2–3 years of professional experience in communications, public relations, marketing, journalism, public affairs, or related fields. Strong writing, editing, and proofreading skills with the ability to translate complex information into accessible and engaging content. Experience creating communications materials such as newsletters, blog posts, articles, media materials, website content, or social media content. Experience adapting content for different audiences and communication channels. ### Digital Communications Skills Experience using email marketing platforms to develop and distribute newsletters or other email communications. Experience updating content in WordPress or similar content management systems. Proficiency using Canva or similar design tools to update and create communications materials from established templates. ### Collaboration & Project Coordination Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines while maintaining attention to detail. Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with colleagues, volunteers, community members, and external partners. Ability to exercise sound judgment, take initiative, and follow through on assignments with limited supervision. Commitment to providing responsive and professional support to internal and external audiences. Proficiency with Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace applications. ### Mission Alignment Interest in conservation, native plants, biodiversity, public lands, environmental education, or related topics. Commitment to fostering an inclusive, respectful, and welcoming environment for colleagues, volunteers, partners, and community members with diverse backgrounds and experiences. Demonstrated awareness of inclusive communication practices and a commitment to creating content that is accessible and relevant to diverse audiences. Commitment to supporting CNPS’s mission, values, and goals. — ## Preferred Qualifications Experience supporting media relations, public affairs, or public engagement initiatives. Experience working with volunteers, member‑based organizations, nonprofits, or community groups. Experience creating or appearing in video or multimedia content. Bachelor’s degree in communications, journalism, public relations, marketing, environmental studies, or a related field. Relevant professional experience may substitute for a degree on a year‑for‑year basis. Bilingual or multilingual communication skills, particularly in languages commonly spoken in California. CNPS recognizes that candidates may bring experience through a variety of professional, educational, and lived experiences. If you are excited about this role and believe you can contribute to our mission, we encourage you to apply even if you do not meet every listed qualification. — ## What You’ll Get Compensation: A starting hourly rate between $26.87 – $28.96. CNPS publishes full potential starting pay ranges for new hires and does not negotiate hiring bonuses. Performance‑Based Compensation Increases: Employees may receive up to a 3.8% annual rate increase. Health Insurance: 100% coverage of employee premiums for health (Kaiser or Anthem), life, dental, and vision insurance. Retirement Plan: 401(k) plan with up to 6% matching contributions, available immediately upon employment. Flexible Spending Accounts: Options for FSA, HSA, DCA, and TSA. Paid Leave: 13 holidays, 12 sick/wellness days, and 10 vacation days. Parental Leave: 12 weeks of supplemental paid parental leave after one year of employment. Work‑from‑Home Support: CNPS‑issued laptop, $750 home office stipend, and $60/month telework stipend. Employee Assistance Program (EAP): Comprehensive support for employees and their families. Professional Development: Annual budget of $500 and 32 hours for professional development. Team Building: Attendance at semiannual staff team‑building events. Community: Complimentary CNPS Society membership. Meaningful Impact: Join a team where your work genuinely supports the planet – cape optional! — ## About California Native Plant Society The California Native Plant Society (CNPS) is a statewide non‑profit conservation organization with more than 13,000 members in 35 chapters across California and Baja California Norte, Mexico. Founded in 1965, the mission of CNPS is to protect California’s native plants and their natural habitats through science, education, stewardship, gardening, and advocacy. Native plants are the foundation of California’s globally significant biodiversity. CNPS supports statewide efforts to conserve public lands, save sensitive species and habitats, and create thriving native plant habitats in urban spaces and wildlands. — ## Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Justice CNPS is committed to addressing structural and cultural barriers to experiencing nature and participating in the native plant community. item.title: Counsel – Media Buying, Advertising Technology & Digital Marketing
item.description: Counsel – Media Buying, Advertising Technology & Digital Marketing Organization: Mattel Location: El Segundo, CA Date Posted: 08/10/2026 ## Pay Range USD $188,000 – $235,000 Yearly The pay range is indicative of projected hiring range; however, base pay will be determined based on a candidate’s work location, skills, and experience. Mattel offers competitive total pay programs, comprehensive benefits, and resources to help empower a culture where every employee can reach their full potential. ## Creativity Is Our Superpower It’s our heritage and it’s also our future. Because we don’t just make toys. We create innovative products and experiences that inspire fans, entertain audiences, and develop children through play. Mattel is at its best when every member of our team feels respected, included, and heard—when everyone can show up as themselves and do their best work every day. We value and share an infinite range of ideas and voices that evolve and broaden our perspectives with a reach that extends into all our brands, partners, and suppliers. ## The Opportunity We are seeking a commercially minded, technology‑savvy attorney to join our legal team and support a broad range of media buying, advertising technology, performance media, and agency‑related matters. This role will serve as a key legal partner to marketing, media, influencer engagement, procurement, privacy, technology, and business stakeholders, providing practical advice on sophisticated digital advertising arrangements as well as traditional media buying and agency engagements. The Counsel position is in Mattel’s corporate headquarters in El Segundo, CA. ## What Your Impact Will Be This is an opportunity to join a collaborative and evolving legal team, take ownership of high‑impact matters, and expand the role as the company’s media, advertising technology, and performance marketing activities continue to grow. This position involves managing a large range and high volume of media and agency transactions. It requires an ability to effectively work within and manage a sophisticated forms‑contract practice. The role will evolve over time as Mattel’s business and legal needs evolve. ## What We’re Looking For The ability to provide thoughtful, proactive, strategic legal and business advice. Skilled at identifying issues early and creatively solving them, as well as spotting company‑wide trends and building consensus in managing them efficiently. A team player who can multi‑task and work well under pressure, with frequently changing priorities and sometimes conflicting objectives. Excellent negotiating, drafting, and practice‑management skills. Maintain a professional demeanor, in writing and in person, with support staff, business colleagues, senior management, and outside counsel. Ability to adopt technology solutions and seek efficiencies in managing work. High ethical standards. Ability to “manage up” and collaborate effectively. A sense of humor is a plus. The ideal candidate has at least 3 years of relevant legal experience, including meaningful experience with digital media, advertising technology, data‑driven marketing, or media agency agreements. The attorney should understand how modern advertising campaigns are planned, purchased, measured, and optimized across digital platforms and should be comfortable translating complex legal, technical, and commercial issues into clear, actionable guidance. ## Professional Licensing Good standing in at least one state bar and, if not licensed to practice in California, an ability and willingness to register to practice in California pursuant to California’s in‑house counsel registration requirements. ## Education An undergraduate degree and strong academic performance at a J.D. from a highly rated law school. *The pay range is indicative of projected hiring range; however, base pay will be determined based on a candidate’s work location, skills, and experience. Mattel offers competitive total pay programs, comprehensive benefits, and resources to help empower a culture where every employee can reach their full potential.* ## Inclusive Hiring Don’t meet every single requirement? At Mattel, we are dedicated to an inclusive workplace and a culture of belonging. If you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we still encourage you to apply. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles. Join Mattel’s Talent Community and start receiving exciting updates about our company, our employees, and our culture. Interested in signing up for job alerts? Do so here! ## How We Work We are a purpose‑driven company aiming to empower generations to explore the wonder of childhood and reach their full potential. We live up to our purpose employing the following behaviors: ### We Collaborate Being a part of Mattel means being part of one team with shared values and common goals. Every person counts, and working closely together always brings better results. Partnership is our process, and our collective capabilities are our superpower. ### We Innovate At Mattel we always aim to find new and better ways to create innovative products and experiences. No matter where you work in the organization, you can make a difference and have real impact. We welcome new ideas and value initiatives that challenge conventional thinking. ### We Execute We are a performance‑driven company. We strive for excellence and pursue best‑in‑class outcomes. We believe in accountability and ownership and know that our people are at their best when they are empowered to create and deliver results. ## Who We Are Mattel is a leading global toy and family entertainment company and owner of one of the most iconic brand portfolios in the world. We engage consumers and fans through our franchise brands, including Barbie, Hot Wheels, Fisher‑Price, American Girl, Thomas & Friends, UNO, Masters of the Universe, Matchbox, Monster High, MEGA, and Polly Pocket, as well as other popular properties that we own or license in partnership with global entertainment companies. Our offerings include toys, content, consumer products, digital and live experiences. Our products are sold in collaboration with the world’s leading retail and ecommerce companies. Since its founding in 1945, Mattel is proud to be a trusted partner in empowering generations to explore the wonder of childhood and reach their full potential. Mattel’s award‑winning workplace culture has been recognized by Forbes, Fast Company, Newsweek, Great Place to Work, TIME, and more. Visit us at [https://jobs.mattel.com/] and [www.instagram.com/MattelCareers]. Mattel is an Equal Opportunity Employer where we want you to bring your authentic self to work every day. We welcome all job seekers, and all applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, color, national origin, religion, sex, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, veteran and protected veteran status, disability status, or any other basis protected by applicable federal, state, or local law. Pursuant to the Los Angeles Fair Chance Ordinance and the California Fair Chance Act, qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment.
