item.title: Manager, Global Policy Advocacy Business, YouTube GAPP
item.description: Manager, Global Policy Advocacy Business, YouTube GAPP Organization: Google Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/10/2026 ## Minimum Qualifications – Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience. – 10 years of experience working on technology policy issues within government, think tanks, public interest groups, law, or relevant industry associations. – 10 years of experience working in public affairs, political communications, or political campaigns, or within government. ## Preferred Qualifications – Experience in global policy advocacy or campaigns specifically focused on creator legitimacy, prominence, media/multimedia, and copyright (including the No Fakes Act). – Experience working with a variety of stakeholders, including regional teams and external allies, to execute strategies and deliver proactive policy solutions. – Ability to manage complex policy portfolios and translate high‑level strategy into tangible execution. – Strong communication skills with the ability to identify insights and communicate technology policy issues effectively to Key Opinion Formers (KOFs). ## About the Job As a Manager for Global Policy Advocacy – Business at YouTube, you will be a leader in the Government Affairs and Public Policy (GAPP) organization. You will be responsible for driving a global, proactive issue advocacy and management agenda designed to shape public debate, drive YouTube and creator thought leadership, and condition the policy environment. In this role, you will act as a “Campaign Architect” for YouTube’s most critical policy issues, owning end‑to‑end management of your portfolio. Your mission is to translate complex policy goals into actionable global reputational and policy campaigns that bridge the gap between high‑level strategy and on‑the‑ground execution. You will coordinate closely with regional teams, product partners, and external allies to land proactive policy outcomes in YouTube’s favor, specifically focusing on creator legitimacy, prominence, media/multimedia, and copyright (including the No Fakes Act). Google takes its responsibilities seriously, including engaging with the government and other stakeholders on important public policy challenges. The GAPP team leads the company’s engagement with executive branch officials, legislators, regulators, and third parties in the formation of public policy. We help inform and educate users, advertisers, partners, opinion leaders—and our own employees—about the benefits of Google’s products, our distinctive company culture/values, and our approach to the big public policy issues of the day. You are quick‑witted, entrepreneurial, and intellectually curious. To succeed in this role, you are willing to try new things and can manage numerous projects with tight deadlines. Things happen quickly at Google, and to do great work, you need to be an enthusiastic team player who can work cross‑functionally with partners across PR, Communications, Marketing, Product, and beyond. Individual pay is determined by factors including job‑related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. **US: $181000 – $247000 (USD) + 20% bonus target + equity + benefits** Learn more about benefits at Google. ## Responsibilities – Design and manage end‑to‑end advocacy campaigns, establishing Objectives and Key Results (OKRs), allocating budgets, and partnering with regional leads to translate global strategy into local market execution. – Craft compelling policy narratives on key industry issues and convert them into executive briefings, op‑eds, and talking points to persuade policymakers and Key Opinion Formers. – Collaborate with Product and Business teams to condition regulatory environments for upcoming launches and leverage product milestones to advance policy goals. – Commission external research and collaborate with internal data teams to build rigorous, evidence‑based proof points that substantiate public policy positions. – Mobilize YouTube creators and third‑party allies into advocacy coalitions while defining qualitative/quantitative metrics to measure and report campaign Return on Investment (ROI). Information collected and processed as part of your Google Careers profile, and any job applications you choose to submit, is subject to Google’s Applicant and Candidate Privacy Policy. Google is proud to be an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer. We are committed to building a workforce that is representative of the users we serve, creating a culture of belonging, and providing an equal employment opportunity regardless of race, creed, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, national origin, disability, age, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding), expecting or parents‑to‑be, criminal histories consistent with legal requirements, or any other basis protected by law. See also Google’s EEO Policy, Know your rights: workplace discrimination is illegal, Belonging at Google, and How we hire. If you have a need that requires accommodation, please let us know by completing our Accommodations for Applicants form. Google is a global company and, in order to facilitate efficient collaboration and communication globally, English proficiency is a requirement for all roles unless stated otherwise in the job posting. To all recruitment agencies: Google does not accept agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to our jobs alias, Google employees, or any other organization location. Google is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes. Equity is granted exclusively and discretionarily by Alphabet Inc. on the basis of an agreement concluded between you and Alphabet Inc. Alphabet Inc. is your sole contractual partner with respect to equity grants. GSU grants are not guaranteed, are discretionary, are subject to approval by the Alphabet Inc. board of directors or its delegate, the terms of the relevant Alphabet Inc. stock plan, and your grant agreement. They have no impact on statutory payments. Current or past grants do not confer an acquired right. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Deputy Director of National Policy and Campaign
item.description: Deputy Director of National Policy and Campaign Organization: Coalition for Humane Immigrant Rights (CHIRLA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/10/2026 # **JOB POSTING: Deputy Director of National Policy and Campaign** The Coalition for Humane Immigrant Rights (**CHIRLA**) is a nonprofit organization founded in 1986. CHIRLA is a California leader with national impact, made of diverse immigrant families and individuals who act as agents of social change to achieve a world with freedom of mobility, full human rights, and true participatory democracy. CHIRLA organizes and serves individuals, institutions, and coalitions to build power, transform public opinions, and change policies to achieve full human, civil, and labor rights. Guided by power, love, and the vision of our community, CHIRLA embraces and drives progressive social change. — ## **Position Description** The **Deputy Director of National Policy & Campaigns** plays a key role in the policy and advocacy team responsible for planning and executing both long‑term and short‑term directions of the organization’s federal policy agenda. The Deputy Director will collaborate and assist in leading projects to expand and support national policy work across the country. This role will **co‑lead the federal policy portfolio** with the Deputy Director for Policy and Congressional Affairs, including strategic planning to maintain and cultivate relationships with Members of Congress and the Administration. Responsibilities include briefing Members of Congress and their staff on issues affecting immigrants and their families, and engaging CHIRLA’s membership base to develop and advance policy priorities in Congress. The Deputy Director will also oversee contract lobbyists and policy staff based in the Washington, DC office. The Deputy Director will serve as a **subject‑matter expert** on immigration and the legislative process, working with CHIRLA’s Policy Department, Legal Counsel, and Director of Policy and Advocacy to analyze and monitor federal policy and its impact on immigrant communities. This position additionally oversees CHIRLA’s **national campaigns**, including CHIRLA‑led efforts such as the Registry Campaign, campaigns where CHIRLA serves on steering committees, and campaigns where CHIRLA plays an active leadership role. The Deputy Director will also track CHIRLA’s engagement in national networks such as the **Fair Immigration Reform Movement (FIRM)** and the **National Partnership for New Americans (NPNA)**, ensuring active staff participation and regular reporting. — ## **Duties and Responsibilities** ### **External Program Priorities** – In collaboration with the Executive Director, Director of Policy and Advocacy, and CHIRLA membership base, create annual campaign plans across various priorities. – Advance national campaigns led by CHIRLA in collaboration with CHIRLA leadership. – Develop legislative, administrative, and budget proposals to advance CHIRLA’s goals and mission. – Manage CHIRLA’s support/opposition/neutral positions on legislative, regulatory, and appropriation proposals. – Advance and implement CHIRLA’s goals and objectives as determined by the organization. – Cultivate and maintain positive working relationships with Members of Congress, Congressional caucuses, agencies, and the Administration. – Secure regular meetings and provide policy analysis to lawmakers and their staff. – Represent CHIRLA’s position at committee hearings, press conferences, and legislative meetings as requested. – Develop and maintain alliances with national immigrant rights organizations to advance CHIRLA’s policy agenda. – Work with CHIRLA staff to develop and implement advocacy strategies and events (legislative visits, advocacy days, letters, call‑in campaigns, media relations, briefings, actions, etc.). – Develop policy updates, talking points, action alerts, and sample letters as part of advocacy strategies. – Provide research and analysis on issues pertaining to immigrant communities. — ### **Internal Program Priorities** – Produce federal legislative research, community‑friendly memos, policy fact sheets, and talking points. – Execute annual campaign plans across national priorities. – Develop monthly content for CHIRLA’s *Al Día* policy newsletter. – Facilitate legislative visits and lobby days engaging directly impacted immigrants. – Develop CHIRLA’s Executive Director national policy and advocacy proactive engagement agenda. – Monitor and advance border and binational priority policy issues. – Evaluate staff and policy interns annually using CHIRLA’s performance measures. – Monitor, manage, analyze, and summarize proposed or new laws and regulations affecting immigrants. – Research, analyze, and write policy reports and briefing documents on immigration issues. – Provide regular updates on policy and campaign work through progress reports and analysis. – Create a work plan and confer with the Supervisor as needed. – Ensure CHIRLA leadership is briefed and knowledgeable about CHIRLA’s federal agenda and strategy. – Meet fundraising and membership goals for CHIRLA’s membership drive and annual Gala. – Contribute to other program projects as needed. — ## **Skills and Qualifications** ### **Required** – Bachelor’s degree in a related field. – Minimum five years of legislative experience. – At least five years of experience in national campaigns. – Strong research and policy development skills. – Excellent written and verbal communication abilities. – In‑depth understanding of the functions of the U.S. federal government. – Broad strategic vision integrating public policy with an immigration perspective. ### **Preferred** – Law background. – Bilingual in English and Spanish (strongly preferred). – Proven experience in a nonprofit organization or policy firm. – Engagement in immigrant rights issues. – Strong knowledge of national, state, and federal policy advocacy stakeholders. — ## **Desired Traits or Characteristics** – Broad knowledge and strong interest in immigration and migration issues. – Ability to plan, organize, and implement CHIRLA’s policy with limited supervision. – Initiative, good judgment, and deep understanding of immigration matters. – Positive working relationships with staff, members, and allies. – Ability to work under pressure and meet tight deadlines. – Experience collaborating with community organizations. – Highly self‑motivated, creative, flexible, and able to work in an interdisciplinary team. – Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously. – Strong commitment to CHIRLA’s mission of empowering low‑income communities and immigrants. – Interest in or history of working for social justice. – Passion for building immigrant power to achieve social, economic, and racial justice. – Commitment to working in a diverse professional environment. – Support CHIRLA’s fundraising efforts, including annual drives, Gala activities, and film fundraising initiatives. — ## **Job Title** **Deputy Director of National Policy & Campaign** **Salary & Benefits:** $97,344 to $105,237 **FLSA Classification:** Exempt/Salary, full‑time regular **Union Status:** Not included in CHIRLA’s bargaining unit (AFSCME Local 4501) **Reports To:** Director of Policy & Advocacy **Closing Date:** Open until filled **Location:** Washington, DC Office — ## **Equal Employment Opportunity Statement** CHIRLA is an equal opportunity employer and makes employment decisions based on merit. CHIRLA administers all terms and conditions of employment without discrimination based on pregnancy, genetic information, race, religion, color, gender identity or expression, national origin, disability, medical condition, marital status, age (40+), sexual orientation, HIV/AIDS status, military or veteran status, or any other protected category. CHIRLA also prohibits discrimination based on perception of these characteristics or association with individuals who have them. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Staff Attorney
item.description: Staff Attorney Organization: Coalition for Humane Immigrant Rights (CHIRLA) Location: Los Angeles, CA Date Posted: 08/10/2026 # JOB POSTING – Staff Attorney The Coalition for Humane Immigrant Rights (**CHIRLA**) is a nonprofit organization founded in 1986. CHIRLA is a California leader with national impact made of diverse immigrant families and individuals who act as agents of social change to achieve a world with freedom of mobility, full human rights, and true participatory democracy. CHIRLA organizes and serves individuals, institutions and coalitions to build power, transform public opinions, and change policies to achieve full human, civil and labor rights. Guided by power, love and vision of our community, CHIRLA embraces and drives progressive social change. ## POSITION DESCRIPTION CHIRLA is seeking a **Staff Attorney** who will be a member of the legal department and may be assigned to work primarily with one or more legal teams as needed. The types and amounts of cases assigned will reflect the needs of the clients served by the team(s) or the legal department as a whole. The Staff Attorney will assist clients in pursuing immigration benefits and provide representation in applications, hearings, or proceedings before various courts, tribunals, and agencies. The role also includes community-based systemic reform and advocacy aimed at improving federal immigration laws. The Staff Attorney will provide consultations to new clients, especially during Legal Triage and other events, offering effective, responsive, compassionate, efficient, and zealous representation. The Staff Attorney supervises and directs paralegals or other support staff assigned to client cases. — ## DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES ### Immigration Legal Assistance – Provide representation to clients with cases involving criminal history, immigration law violations, family law issues, removal proceedings, appeals, or other immigration-related matters. – Prepare, review, revise, and submit documents needed to address clients’ immigration issues, including applications, motions, legal memos, briefs, petitions, or requests before USCIS and/or immigration court. – Represent individuals before federal, state, or local courts, agencies, or tribunals at all levels, following ethical and professional responsibility obligations and funder requirements. – Create and communicate timelines and tasks to supervisors, colleagues, subordinate staff, and clients to efficiently resolve issues and achieve the best possible outcomes. – Work effectively under pressure with urgent deadlines. – Research and analyze complex and straightforward legal matters, assuming responsibility and risk for case outcomes. – Screen potential clients for all available immigration benefits and assess their ability to pursue them successfully. – Communicate assessments of clients’ immigration circumstances, including rights, requirements, and deadlines. – Stay up to date with changes in immigration law and related developments. – Make appropriate referrals for services beyond program scope or personal competencies. – Assume caseloads of departing staff as needed. ### Staff Supervision – Review all applications and documents prepared by subordinate staff before submission to USCIS, Immigration Court, or other tribunals. Provide revisions and direction as needed. – Provide coaching and mentorship to colleagues and subordinate staff to improve knowledge, skills, accuracy, and service quality. ### Customer Service and Community Outreach – Communicate with clients professionally, respectfully, compassionately, and with sensitivity to trauma. – Maintain regular communication with clients, providing updates at least every 90 days. – Respond to client communications within 48–72 hours. – Participate in in-person legal screening events, community presentations, and special events, including Saturday Legal Triage (7 AM–11 AM monthly). ### Reporting Obligations and Program Efficiency – Update case notes within 48–72 hours of any development or client interaction. – Update and maintain databases, tracking sheets, and other required documents. – Work diligently with staff to represent clients ethically, efficiently, and properly to maximize outcomes and meet funder deliverables. – Perform other duties as necessary to address urgent issues within assigned teams or the legal department. — ## SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS ### Required – Active attorney license and good standing with the CA State Bar. – At least one year of experience practicing immigration law. – Demonstrated commitment to social justice and progressive social change. – High level of integrity and ability to maintain confidentiality. – Strong oral and written communication skills. – Flexibility to work early mornings, evenings, and Saturdays. – Ability to travel in and out of California. ### Preferred – Fluency or high proficiency in Spanish or other languages. – Experience assisting noncitizens applying for a wide variety of immigration benefits before USCIS and/or Immigration Court. – Engaging communication skills for diverse audiences and collaborative networks. – Excellent problem-solving, strategic thinking, and analytical skills. – Strong organizational skills and attention to detail. – Experience providing direct services in a nonprofit setting. – Experience working with survivors of trauma, violence, or human trafficking. – Experience working with underserved and diverse populations. – Comfort working in collaborative, consultative environments. ### Desired Traits or Characteristics – Highly self-motivated, creative, proactive, quick learner, flexible, and able to work as part of an interdisciplinary legal team. – Demonstrated ability to work effectively with colleagues of diverse backgrounds in person and remotely. – Ability to establish and maintain effective relationships within teams and across the organization. – Proactive approach to responsibilities, task completion, and use of technology to maximize efficiency. – Strong commitment to CHIRLA’s mission of empowering low-income community groups. — ## JOB TITLE **Staff Attorney** ## Salary & Benefits $78,000 range based on experience. CHIRLA offers competitive salary and excellent benefits, including generous time off, 401K plan, and health, dental, and vision plans. ## FLSA Classification Exempt/Hourly, full-time regular. ## Classification This position is included in CHIRLA’s bargaining unit affiliated with AFSCME Local 4501 and covered under the collective bargaining agreement. ## Reports To Managing Attorney or Supervising Staff Attorney. ## Closing Date Position will remain open until filled. ## Location Multiple branch office locations available. — ## Equal Opportunity Statement CHIRLA is an equal opportunity employer and makes employment decisions based on merit. It prohibits discrimination based on pregnancy, genetic information, race, religion, color, gender identity or expression, national origin, disability, medical condition, marital status, age (40+), sexual orientation, HIV/AIDS status, military or veteran status, or any other protected category. Discrimination based on perception of these characteristics or association with someone who has them is also prohibited. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.description: Statewide Climate Justice Organizer Organization: Coalition for Humane Immigrant Rights (CHIRLA) Location: Los Angeles, CA Date Posted: 08/10/2026 **JOB POSTING – Statewide Climate Justice Organizer** The Coalition for Humane Immigrant Rights (CHIRLA) is a nonprofit organization founded in 1986. CHIRLA is a California leader with national impact made of diverse immigrant families and individuals who act as agents of social change to achieve a world with freedom of mobility, full human rights, and true participatory democracy. CHIRLA organizes and serves individuals, institutions, and coalitions to build power, transform public opinions, and change policies to achieve full human, civil and labor rights. Guided by power, love, and vision of our community, CHIRLA embraces and drives progressive social change. **POSITION DESCRIPTION** CHIRLA’s Climate Justice Department is seeking a Statewide Climate Justice Advocate to work on community building, coalition building, and advocacy campaigns to advance climate justice for immigrant communities. The Advocate, in partnership with the Organizing Department, will focus on growing and maintaining CHIRLA’s base of climate‑impacted community members. The Advocate will be responsible for the recruitment and retention of community members. The Advocate will coordinate community gatherings, craft community education materials, and build relationships with external partners. The Advocate will coordinate advocacy actions, volunteer trips, and leadership development to empower BIPOC immigrant communities to lead in the climate justice space. **DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES** **Coordination, Organizing and Education** – Coordinate with the Director for Climate Justice and Director of Organizing to develop and implement an outreach and recruitment plan for CHIRLA’s climate‑impacted members. – Implement leadership development program for members throughout the state. – Serve as a resource and mentor to organizers and members. – Develop and disseminate immigrant rights materials as they pertain to climate justice. – Convene and facilitate member meetings, events, workshops, or coalition gatherings. – Contribute to broader advocacy campaigns to support climate justice. – Conduct presentations to community at large concerning current CHIRLA campaigns. – Travel throughout the state to carry out these or additional duties. **Campaign Coordination** – Lead campaign development and implementation for climate justice in California. – Conduct necessary research for climate justice and/or CHIRLA campaigns. – In conjunction with Communications teams, develop and implement media strategies that center directly impacted members around the campaign and manage media inquiries around immigrant and climate issues. – Assist in development and implementation of broader CHIRLA campaigns, including member mobilization. – Work closely with Policy and Advocacy staff, Political Director, and other relevant departments to determine policy priorities for climate justice and CHIRLA at large. – Manage and coordinate coalition‑building on the regional level. – Participate in and report at general staff and department meetings. – Support fundraising for committee as well as broader CHIRLA activities and events. – Other duties and responsibilities as necessary. **SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS** **Required** – At least two years of community college or equivalent related experience. – Demonstrated commitment to mission and goals of CHIRLA. – Proven experience in a non‑profit organization or research firm. – Two years community involvement or direct organizing experience. – Strong oral and written advocacy skills. Excellent organizational skills and the ability to work and problem‑solve under pressure. – Excellent research and policy development skills. – Experience in campaign development and implementation. – Excellent organizational skills and strong attention to detail. – Spanish fluency or high proficiency is required. Mixteco or other indigenous language speakers welcome. – Ability to establish and maintain effective relationships throughout the organization and community. – Flexibility is required based on the needs of the organization. The position will involve some evening and weekend work. – Computer literacy: word processing, internet navigation, and other work‑related applications. **Preferred** – Must be extremely organized. Must be able to work efficiently and manage multiple projects at once, which may be at different stages of design and execution. **Desired Traits or Characteristics** – Highly self‑motivated, creative, takes initiative, ability to learn quickly, flexible, and able to work as part of a team as well as independently. – Demonstrated experience working effectively as part of a team and with colleagues of diverse backgrounds and perspectives, both in person and within a remote work environment. – Ability to establish and maintain effective relationships within the Climate Justice department and throughout the organization. – Demonstrated ability to be proactive in their approach to assigned responsibilities, completing tasks and/or using technology and systems to maximize efficiency. – Strong commitment to CHIRLA’s mission of empowering low‑income community groups. – Strong interpersonal and communication skills; ability to work effectively with a diverse community. – Knowledge of and commitment to immigrant and worker rights and CHIRLA’s mission. – Position requires an employee to use a personal vehicle to travel between worksites or other locations, as a primary job duty. — **JOB TITLE:** Statewide Climate Justice Organizer **Salary & Benefits:** $72,500 – $74,000 CHIRLA offers a competitive salary based on qualifications and an excellent benefit package, which includes generous time‑off benefits, 401K Plan, health, dental and vision plans. **FLSA Classification:** Exempt, full‑time regular **Classification:** CHIRLA recognizes a staff bargaining unit affiliated with AFSCME Local 4501. item.title: Principal, Global Event Security and Risk Management
item.description: Principal, Global Event Security and Risk Management Organization: Wikimedia Foundation Location: Remote Date Posted: 08/10/2026 # PRINCIPAL, GLOBAL EVENT SECURITY AND RISK MANAGEMENT ## Summary The Wikimedia Foundation is looking for a Principal, Global Event Security and Risk Management, to join our team. Our aim is to ensure everyone, everywhere can securely participate in free knowledge. As an organization, we are committed to proactively identifying and mitigating risks that impact both the Foundation and the Wikimedia movement. This includes enabling secure physical convenings and spaces for the robust global communities of volunteers we serve and often support through grants, and effectively addressing other physical security and enterprise risks our ecosystem faces. The Principal will report to the Deputy General Counsel in the Legal Department, and will lead the Foundation’s efforts in proactively preparing for and addressing critical risks to the physical security of staff, community members, and other participants engaging in Wikimedia movement activities. The Principal will coordinate with staff in the Foundation’s internal Enterprise Risk Management working group to broadly identify and track risks to the Foundation and Wikimedia movement. In their focused work of identifying and leading the response to physical security threats, the Principal will partner with internal teams such as legal, grantmaking, external and movement communications, human rights, product security, and trust & safety; and groups outside of the Foundation, such as Wikimedia volunteer organizers, external partners, and security experts. As the point person for the mitigation of physical security risks, the Principal must remain informed on global geopolitical developments, in order to identify emerging and shifting threats to Wikimedia users around the world, and synthesize information from a variety of sources, including Foundation risk reports and consultations with internal teams. The Principal’s goal is to support the organization, the Wikimedia movement and its communities in their efforts to reduce vulnerability and minimize harm when threats materialize. The successful candidate will possess a wide range of experience and a deep understanding of best practices in risk coordination, security, and crisis management. They will have experience working in global contexts, particularly the global south, and will bring curiosity, an ability to work across different cultures, and vision. They will have strong people skills, with the ability to empathetically motivate and inspire both staff and volunteers, while understanding the needs and capacities of disparate stakeholder groups. Their experience and good judgment will enable them to achieve impact on a wide variety of high-stakes, emergent risk issues facing the Foundation and the communities it supports. — ## You are responsible for: – **Working with movement organizers** — Develop and maintain an understanding of the environments and challenges facing Wikimedia volunteers around the world, mitigate those risks, and define best practices for physical security in movement activities. – **Strengthening enterprise risk management** — Improve the Foundation’s overall approach and execution, including policy development and implementation. – **Leading risk and gap assessments** — Identify, document, and track high risks for the Foundation, consulting with subject matter experts in technology, brand, operational, legal, and strategic risk. – **Improving expertise in emerging physical security threats** — Enhance the organization’s ability to identify, mitigate, and address threats to staff, communities, and affiliates. – **Leading risk assessments for community events** — Consolidate input from multiple teams and communicate findings to stakeholders, including community organizers. – **Creating emergency response plans** — Bring together stakeholders and experts, including law enforcement or external consultants, and manage implementation once approved. – **Being on-call for emergency alerts** — Review alerts, ensure proper escalation, lead emergency response working groups, designate incident coordinators, and provide risk management expertise. – **Remaining current on emerging geopolitical trends and best practices in physical security.** – **Briefing senior leadership** with recommendations on systems improvement, resource management, and operational effectiveness. – **Providing crisis support** to internal teams working directly with at-risk communities. — ## Skills and Experience: – Substantial professional experience in corporate and physical security work in diverse geographic and political contexts, especially in the global south. – Significant leadership experience in risk management. – Extensive experience developing, communicating, and executing emergency response plans. – Strong networking and analytical skills, with the ability to synthesize geopolitical trends and assess their impact. – Strong communication skills for executive summaries, detailed response plans, and compassionate communication. – Ability to remain calm and focused in ambiguous or high-risk situations. – Demonstrated experience collaborating with subject-matter experts in threat modeling and contingency planning. – Strong people skills to lead and motivate lateral teams in high-intensity situations. – Resilience and ability to exercise self-care during periods of difficult subject matter. – Experience using digital security tools for secure communication at on-site events. – Adaptability with online communities and technology, and openness to new tools. – Flexibility in working hours, including nights, weekends, or holidays, and ability to work across time zones (UTC-8 to UTC+1). — ## Qualities that are important to us: – Interest in the role of technology in culture and civic society. – Readiness to assess and respond to risks with cultural awareness. – Experience with internet technologies and their impact on human rights. – Proactive problem solving and comfort with ambiguity. – Willingness to undertake moderate international travel (4–6 trips per year). – Written and oral fluency in English; ability in Arabic, French, or Spanish is a plus. — ## About the Wikimedia Foundation The Wikimedia Foundation is the nonprofit organization that operates Wikipedia and other free knowledge projects. Our vision is a world in which every single human can freely share in the sum of all knowledge. We believe everyone has the potential to contribute and should be able to access knowledge freely. We host Wikipedia and other projects, build software experiences, support volunteer communities, and advocate for policies that enable free knowledge to thrive. The Foundation is a charitable, not-for-profit organization funded by millions of individual donations (average donation: ~$15), as well as institutional grants. It is a U.S. 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organization headquartered in San Francisco. We are an equal opportunity employer and strive for an inclusive workplace. We do not discriminate based on any legally protected characteristics. The Wikimedia Foundation is remote-first, with staff in 40+ countries. Salaries are competitive, equitable, and adjusted by location. U.S. pay range for this role: **$145,429–$223,286**. For non-U.S. hires, compensation is adjusted to the country of hire. We currently hire in the following: **US States:** Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, District of Columbia*, Florida, Georgia, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Puerto Rico*, Rhode Island, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Vermont, Virginia, Washington, West Virginia, Wisconsin, Wyoming. (*US Territory or Federal District) **Countries:** Brazil, Canada, Colombia, France, Germany, Ghana, India, Indonesia, Italy, Kenya*, Mexico, Morocco, Netherlands, Poland, Singapore*, South Africa, Spain, Switzerland, United Kingdom. (*citizens/permanent residents only) Applicants may contact [email protected] or +1 (415) 839-6885 for accommodations during the application process. item.title: Creator Experience Senior Policy Analyst, YouTube
item.description: Creator Experience Senior Policy Analyst, YouTube Organization: Google Location: San Bruno, CA | San Francisco, CA Date Posted: 08/10/2026 ## Minimum qualifications – Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience. – 5 years of experience in a policy, legal, Trust & Safety, or technology environment. – 2 years of experience working with Generative AI Agents. ## Preferred qualifications – 2 years of experience in a policy‑related role focused on online content moderation or ancillary policy enforcement frameworks. – Experience in policy guideline scripting, incubation, and advanced testing. – Experience with the development, implementation, and maintenance of policy. – Advanced technical policy implementation skills. – Excellent problem‑solving and critical‑thinking skills with attention to detail in an ever‑changing environment. ## About the job Trust & Safety team members are tasked with identifying and taking on the biggest problems that challenge the safety and integrity of our products. They use technical know‑how, excellent problem‑solving skills, user insights, and proactive communication to protect users and partners from abuse across Google products like Search, Maps, Gmail, and Google Ads. On this team, you’re a big‑picture thinker and strategic team‑player with a passion for doing what’s right. You work globally and cross‑functionally with Google engineers and product managers to identify and fight abuse and fraud cases at Google speed—with urgency. You take pride in knowing that every day you are working hard to promote trust in Google and ensure the highest levels of user safety. The Trust and Safety’s Creator Experience team works to help creators succeed on YouTube by providing a consistent and clear policy experience, protecting ad business, enforcing guidelines on brand‑unsafe content, and aligning with industry standards. The team improves practical elements of creator experiences such as making video appeals easier, providing more detailed explanations for demonetization, speeding up turnaround times, and ensuring policy launches are seamless and easy to understand. This team focuses on making the experience of being a creator better by ensuring that business‑generation policy is easy to understand, adaptable, and reflective of the ever‑changing creator ecosystem. They work to make advertiser‑friendly content guidelines a set of rules creators can live with—and live by. At Google, we work hard to earn our users’ trust every day. Trust & Safety is Google’s team of abuse‑fighting and user‑trust experts working daily to make the internet a safer place. We partner with teams across Google to deliver bold solutions in abuse areas such as malware, spam, and account hijacking. A team of Analysts, Policy Specialists, Engineers, and Program Managers, we work to reduce risk and fight abuse across all Google products, protecting users, advertisers, and publishers across the globe in over 40 languages. Individual pay is determined by factors including job‑related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. **US: $136,000 – $197,000 (USD) + 15% bonus target + equity + benefits** Learn more about benefits at Google. ## Responsibilities – Implement policy principles into actionable enforcement guidelines for the video‑rater pool. – Review controversial and sometimes offensive video content to determine whether or not it is brand‑safe. – Manage escalations with fast turnaround times to define and deliver the best action plan. – Research and stay up to date on key trends and suspicious patterns in your policy area. – Increase efficiency through automation, workflow streamlining, and system optimization. Information collected and processed as part of your Google Careers profile and any job applications you choose to submit is subject to Google’s Applicant and Candidate Privacy Policy. Google is proud to be an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer. We are committed to building a workforce that is representative of the users we serve, creating a culture of belonging, and providing equal employment opportunity regardless of race, creed, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, national origin, disability, age, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding), expecting or parents‑to‑be, criminal histories consistent with legal requirements, or any other basis protected by law. See also: Google’s EEO Policy, *Know your rights: workplace discrimination is illegal*, *Belonging at Google*, and *How we hire*. If you have a need that requires accommodation, please let us know by completing our Accommodations for Applicants form. Google is a global company and, in order to facilitate efficient collaboration and communication globally, English proficiency is a requirement for all roles unless stated otherwise in the job posting. To all recruitment agencies: Google does not accept agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to our jobs alias, Google employees, or any other organization location. Google is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes. Equity is granted exclusively and discretionarily by Alphabet Inc. on the basis of an agreement concluded between you and Alphabet Inc. Alphabet Inc. is your sole contractual partner with respect to equity grants. GSU grants are not guaranteed, are discretionary, are subject to approval by the Alphabet Inc. board of directors or its delegate, the terms of the relevant Alphabet Inc. stock plan, and your grant agreement. They have no impact on statutory payments. Current or past grants do not confer an acquired right. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Director, Global Policy & Advocacy (Education Financing)
item.description: Director, Global Policy & Advocacy (Education Financing) Organization: Malala Fund Location: Washington, DC | New York, NY Date Posted: 08/10/2026 ## Who are we? Malala Fund is working for a world where all girls can learn and lead. Malala Fund advocates for resources and policy changes needed to give all girls a secondary education, invests in local education leaders and amplifies the voices of girls fighting for change. Learn more at malala.org. ## What does this team do? Malala Fund’s Education Financing workstream works to increase sustainable public funding for girls’ education by advancing global policy and advocacy efforts to increase sustainable public funding for girls’ education. Its current focus is the Debt Justice Initiative, a key part of our 2025–2030 strategic plan, *Unlocking Potential*, which addresses how the global debt crisis limits governments’ ability to invest in girls’ education. We work at the intersection of sovereign debt, education financing and girls’ rights to help unlock resources for 12 years of free, safe, quality education for every girl. Through evidence-based policy, strategic partnerships and advocacy with governments and international financial institutions, we push for reforms that protect education budgets today while building a fairer international financial system for the future. Our work is grounded in the perspectives of girls and the priorities of our national civil society partners, particularly in Nigeria and Pakistan. ## What does this position do? Reporting to the Chief of External Affairs, the Director, Global Policy and Advocacy (Education Financing) leads Malala Fund’s Debt Justice Initiative and provides the strategic leadership for this work. As Malala Fund’s senior technical lead on global education financing and international financial architecture, the Director: shapes advocacy strategy; builds relationships with senior decision-makers in governments and international financial institutions; and positions the organisation as a leading voice in development finance debates. The Director also leads a team of policy and advocacy professionals, works closely with country teams and other departments across the organisation, and translates complex financial and policy issues into compelling advocacy strategies that advance girls’ right to secondary education. ## Location Candidates from London, Washington, D.C. and New York will be considered. ## Day-to-Day Duties and Responsibilities ### 1. Strategic Leadership of Global Education Financing Advocacy workstream – Lead Malala Fund’s global advocacy to increase sustainable funding for girls’ secondary education in low- and lower-middle income countries. – Ensure the team develops and leverages high-impact, evidence-based policy analysis and messaging. – Ensure the team’s advocacy approach is strategic, agile, effective and aligned with Malala Fund’s longer-term goals. – Proactively collaborate with senior leaders and staff across Malala Fund to ensure Education Resourcing is effectively embedded across the organisation to advance DJI plans and whole-organisational goals, notably working with Nigeria and Pakistan country teams, as well as the development and communications teams. – Ensure Malala Fund staff, co-founders, board members and donors are effectively briefed on developments, opportunities and engagements, in close coordination with country leadership where priority country contexts are implicated. ### 2. External Representation and Government Relations – Develop and deliver an effective policy-maker (government, IFIs and other global stakeholders) engagement strategy to progress Malala Fund’s DJI goals. – Build and steward senior-level relationships with governments (LICs and HICs), international financial institutions and other sector partners aligned with Malala Fund’s DJI strategy and to advance our policy change objectives, coordinating with country leadership where engagements relate to Nigeria, Pakistan or other Malala Fund focus countries. – Develop and execute strategies to position Malala Fund as a leading voice on global education financing, including media engagement and strategic partnerships. – Work closely with the Senior Director of Strategic Communications to design and ensure the effective delivery of a strategic communications strategy and plans for DJI. – Represent the organisation at high-level forums, media engagements, and in coalition spaces. ### 3. Team and Organizational Leadership – Manage and mentor a high-performing team of two policy and advocacy professionals. – Oversee internal planning, budgeting, and reporting for the initiative. – Contribute to cross-team collaboration and organizational coordination through leadership meetings and shared initiatives. ### 4. Organizational Culture – Uphold Malala Fund’s organizational values. – Actively contribute to making Malala Fund a diverse and equitable workplace through inclusive practice and openness to different perspectives, cultures and ideas. – Maintain behavior and conduct that uphold the highest standards for safeguarding, professionally and personally. – Act as a role model for a “learning organisation” culture by seeking insight and using problems as opportunities to learn. ## What you bring to us and the role! ### What you need to apply: – A postgraduate degree or equivalent in social science, economics or a related field. – Demonstrated success in leading multidimensional advocacy initiatives to influence global policy frameworks and institutions, including leveraging diverse partnerships for collective advocacy. – Substantive policy expertise in development financing and the international financial architecture, with strong working knowledge of the IFIs and the instruments and processes that shape financing for low- and lower-middle income countries (including regional financial institutions). The successful candidate will translate technical complexity into strategic positioning and be well regarded by peers working in this space. – Fluency in development financing language and experience and ease in engaging/communicating with a wide range of audiences, including senior-level policymakers, media, and international and national civil society partners. – Keen understanding of normative and legal frameworks that apply to IFA relating to girls’ rights, especially education. – Solid judgment and problem-solving skills; proven attention to detail, accuracy, and quality. – Excellent team and personnel management abilities with the ability to motivate teams, build partnerships and connect with individuals from a variety of cultural backgrounds. – Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with the keen ability to distill complex ideas and data into clear and concise messaging and tailor communications to particular audiences (external and internal). ## Supervisory Responsibilities – Fostering a collaborative, inclusive, and high-performing team culture. – Recruiting, interviewing, and training new staff as needed. – Supporting staff development through regular mentoring/coaching, constructive and timely performance feedback, and performance evaluations. – Handling employee relations, including performance management and disciplinary processes, in accordance with organizational policy. ## Travel Required Up to 15% travel may be required depending on base location. — Malala Fund is an equal opportunity employer and inclusive organization who welcomes employees from under-represented and intersectional communities including BIPOC, LGBTQ+ and persons with disabilities. We seek people with diverse backgrounds, cultures, ages, experiences and identities to provide a wide range of perspectives, ideas, views and insights into the strategy, policies, culture and ambitions of Malala Fund. Malala Fund is committed to safeguarding and ensuring the safety and dignity of all of those involved in our work. Our first priority is protecting everyone who comes in direct or indirect contact with our organization, including staff, partners, grantees, and the communities in which we work. Malala Fund has a zero-tolerance approach to abuse, exploitation, harassment, or discrimination of any kind by any of our staff, representatives or partners. We commit to ensuring that those who work with Malala Fund or on our behalf are able to work in an environment that is safe, respectful, and free from harm. To uphold this commitment, Malala Fund reserves the right to conduct background checks on prospective and current employees. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Sr. Policy Analyst – FL/NJ Area
item.description: Sr. Policy Analyst – FL/NJ Area Organization: 1199 SEIU Location: Remote (NJ, FL) Date Posted: 08/10/2026 ## POSITION SUMMARY The Senior Policy Analyst will be responsible for our Florida and New Jersey regions and can be based in either of those regions or New York City. The Policy Analyst must have political experience as well as an understanding of the New York legislative process and government entities. Experience should include understanding government budgets, familiarity with political agencies and personnel, analyzing and interpreting law and regulations, and presenting research in a clear and concise manner. This position requires a solid understanding of the economic implications of legislation and regulatory practices combined with a knowledge of healthcare policy on federal and state levels. Policy analysts work in conjunction with organizers, members and labor leaders on legislative, organizing and contract campaign projects. ## RESPONSIBILITIES – Draft, develop and analyze proposed health care legislation – Analyze and prepare recommendations regarding budgets – Write summaries of health care issues – Analyze financial data from healthcare institutions and report to leadership – Monitor legislative and healthcare issues – Attend government or policy-related meetings and events as needed ## QUALIFICATIONS – Minimum BA degree, MA degree strongly preferred, in Healthcare Policy, Political Science, Public Administration, Law or other related area – Experience with government agencies and/or legislative processes – Computer skills with database and spreadsheet programs and online research are necessary, as is experience with Word, Access, and Excel – Excellent writing skills and interpersonal skills are essential – Must demonstrate ability to work independently and be willing to work flexible hours – Travel as needed ## GENERAL INFORMATION The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by persons assigned to this title. They do not include all job duties performed by employees in the title and every position does not necessarily require the same duties. 1199/SEIU is an equal opportunity employer. Competitive benefits offered. Email [email protected] for more information on how to apply. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Social Media & Community Manager
item.description: Social Media & Community Manager Organization: Center for AI Safety (CAIS) Location: San Francisco, CA Date Posted: 08/10/2026 ## The Center for AI Safety (CAIS) The Center for AI Safety (CAIS) is a leading research and advocacy organization focused on mitigating societal‑scale risks from AI. We address AI’s toughest challenges through technical research, field‑building initiatives, and policy engagement, along with our sister organization in DC, the Center for AI Safety Action Fund. Public awareness remains the single biggest bottleneck in AI safety. Fortunately, the public’s interest in AI safety is growing extremely quickly. Videos, articles, and social posts about AI safety are now reaching millions, and public curiosity is compounding by the week. Our growth depends on someone who shows up every day across platforms and actively works the comment sections, seeding the conversations that carry our ideas to the power‑listeners and clippers who spread them. We’re hiring a Social Media & Community Manager to run CAIS’s daily presence across platforms, and to build the community and conversations that move our ideas through the culture. You will report to the Head of Public Engagement. — ## What You’ll Do – Translate technical research into clear, story‑driven social copy. – Own the content calendar and publishing strategy across social and our other owned surfaces: what we post, where, and when. – Work the comments: reply, hold the frame, and seed discussion on and around our posts. – Build the amplifier network (creators, clippers, and power‑listeners who re‑share us) via direct outreach and ready‑to‑run clips. – Run social listening, and stand up the social playbook, calendar, and stack (within the brand system) for future hires to scale. — ## What We’re Looking For – 5–7 years on brand or creator social accounts, with audience growth to show. – A strong writer who makes technical ideas land in plain language. – Native platform fluency and a community‑builder’s instinct. – Exceptional judgment and autonomy. — ## Salary Range 120,000 – 160,000 — ## Benefits – Health insurance for you and your dependents – 401K plan + 4% matching – Unlimited PTO – Lunch and dinner at the office – Annual Professional Development Stipend – Access to some of the top talent working on technical and conceptual research in AI safety — Know someone who could be a great fit for this role? Submit their details through our Referral Form. If we end up hiring your referral, you’ll receive a $1,500 bonus once they’ve been with CAIS for 90 days. The Center for AI Safety is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, medical condition, marital status, military or veteran status, or any other protected status in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws. In alignment with the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records for employment. If you require a reasonable accommodation during the application or interview process, please contact [email protected] . We value diversity and encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply. item.title: Senior Manager, Social Media
item.description: Senior Manager, Social Media Organization: UnidosUS Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/10/2026 ## **About UnidosUS** UnidosUS is a nonprofit, nonpartisan organization that serves as the nation’s largest Hispanic civil rights and advocacy organization. Since 1968, we have built a stronger America by creating opportunities for Latinos and breaking down barriers to expand economic and social progress for all. UnidosUS partners with an Affiliate Network of nearly 300 community-based organizations across the United States and Puerto Rico. For more information on UnidosUS, visit [www.unidosus.org] or follow us on Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, X and Threads. — ## **Summary** UnidosUS seeks a social media professional to help lead the strategy, voice, and growth of the organization’s social media presence across all platforms. Reporting to the Director, Social Media, and working in close partnership with media relations and executive communications teams, the Senior Manager will help set and implement the vision for how UnidosUS shows up online—building audience, deepening engagement, and ensuring the Latino perspective is inserted into the national dialogue on breaking news, current affairs, and the issues that matter most to our community. The Senior Manager will work collaboratively to help develop and implement daily content creation and execute platform management that raises awareness and drives engagement among key audiences. The ideal candidate is a strategist and a storyteller: someone who understands how narratives move across platforms, who helps translate complex policy with minimum supervision into written and video content that resonates with both English- and Spanish-dominant audiences, and who thrives in a fast-paced media environment. **Location:** Hybrid position based in Washington, DC. Employees are expected to work onsite two days per week, with Tuesdays designated as a common in-office day. Additional in-office days may be required as needed. **Salary:** $90,000–$105,000 — ## **Essential Functions** ### **Strategy and Execution** – Apply knowledge and concepts of social media to develop and manage project plans and daily activities under deadline. – With knowledge of mobile-first graphic design and video production, manage end-to-end video production for social platforms, including scripting, shooting, and editing short-form videos. – Work effectively across functional teams in managing institutional social media strategies, including scheduling organic posts, drafting copy, designing simple graphics or videos, and reporting results. – Create, update, and socialize detailed project schedules in Monday.com to provide transparency and keep internal team members informed on project status at key milestones. ### **Content and Campaigns** – Help manage the social content calendar and develop original, platform-native content, short-form video, graphics, copy, and live coverage under the supervision of the Director of Social Media. – Support digital campaigns tied to legislative and policy moments, civic engagement cycles (e.g., voter registration), institutional events such as the UnidosUS Annual Conference, and Affiliate Network spotlights. – Ensure content is culturally relevant and bilingual where appropriate, reflecting the diversity of the Latino community in the United States and Puerto Rico. – Work with the Director of Social Media and executive communications team to align institutional messaging with the President/CEO’s social media channels. ### **Rapid Response and Reputation** – Help execute a robust rapid-response capability: monitoring breaking news, identifying real-time opportunities, and deploying timely content that shapes narratives on issues affecting Latinos. – Use social listening tools (e.g., Sprout Social, Talkwalker) to track conversations, newsmakers, influencers, and mis/disinformation targeting Latino communities, as well as sentiment around UnidosUS priorities. – Support coordination with policy and communications leadership, media relations, and executive communications teams on crisis communications, ensuring consistent messaging across channels. ### **Partnerships and Community** – Support relationships with digital creators, influencers, and partner organizations to expand reach with new audiences, including younger demographics. – Help develop and share social media guidance, toolkits, and amplify local stories to support the UnidosUS Affiliate Network. – Support development of two-way engagement with followers, moving audiences from awareness to action. ### **Measurement and Optimization** – Help develop KPIs and regular reporting on audience growth, engagement, reach, conversion, and campaign performance; translate analytics into actionable insights. – Support ongoing testing and optimization of content formats, posting strategies, and paid spend. — ## **Required Qualifications** – Bachelor’s degree in communications, marketing, journalism, related field, or equivalent experience. – Minimum 5 years of experience in social media or digital communications, ideally in advocacy, political, nonprofit, media, or agency settings, including multimedia content creation (photo, video, audio, graphics). – Demonstrated success executing social strategies that grew audiences and drove measurable engagement and action. – Familiarity with major platforms (Instagram, TikTok, X, Facebook, LinkedIn, YouTube, Threads, Bluesky) and their analytics, advertising, and publishing tools. – Experience with social listening and management tools (e.g., Sprout Social, Talkwalker), Adobe Creative Suite, Canva, and short-form video production/editing. – Experience in rapid-response environments and operating across platforms in fast-moving, news-driven contexts. – Strong writing and editing skills, able to translate complex policy into clear, compelling platform-native content. – Demonstrated experience with and knowledge of the Latino community. — ## **Preferred Qualifications** – Previous supervisory experience. – Bilingual (Spanish/English). — ## **Skills and Abilities** – Steadfast commitment to UnidosUS mission, vision, and values: Excellence, Respeto, Accountability. – Commitment to supporting and advancing the needs of the U.S. Latino community and Latino nonprofit organizations. – Good judgment and discretion; calm under pressure. – Strong project management and multitasking skills with attention to detail. – Collaborative team player with strong interpersonal skills. – Commitment to excellence and high standards. – Flexibility to work occasional evenings/weekends and travel for institutional events. — ## **Competencies** – **Analytical:** Synthesizes complex information; researches data; uses intuition; designs workflows. – **Design:** Generates creative solutions; translates concepts into images; applies design principles. – **Project Management:** Develops plans; coordinates projects; communicates changes; meets deadlines. – **Oral Communication:** Speaks clearly; listens well; responds effectively; presents in groups. – **Written Communication:** Writes clearly; edits for accuracy; adapts style; interprets information. – **Technical Skills:** Assesses strengths; pursues development; shares expertise. – **Teamwork:** Balances responsibilities; welcomes feedback; builds team spirit. – **Strategic Thinking:** Develops strategies; analyzes competition; adapts to changing conditions. – **Planning/Organizing:** Prioritizes tasks; uses time efficiently; sets goals; develops action plans. – **Innovation:** Displays creativity; meets challenges resourcefully; develops new ideas. — ## **Physical Demands and Work Environment** – Complete detailed forms and reports accurately. – Coordinate multiple tasks simultaneously. – Perform repetitive motion activities. – Sit for long periods; frequently stand and walk. – Utilize hand and finger dexterity. – Frequently talk or hear. – Occasionally lift/push up to 25 pounds. – Use visual acuity for equipment operation and reading technical information. – Work environment noise level ranges from quiet to moderately loud. — ## **COVID-19 Considerations** UnidosUS follows CDC guidance and strongly encourages employees to stay up to date on vaccinations and practice preventive measures to support well-being and maintain a healthy work environment. — Employment with UnidosUS is contingent upon successful completion of a background screen. **Equal Opportunity Employer:** All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, national origin, marital status, religion, gender, age, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, personal appearance, family responsibilities, political affiliation, or enrollment in an educational institution. item.title: Senior Policy Advisor, Health
item.description: Senior Policy Advisor, Health Organization: UnidosUS Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/10/2026 ## About UnidosUS UnidosUS is a nonprofit, nonpartisan organization that serves as the nation’s largest Hispanic civil rights and advocacy organization. Since 1968, we have built a stronger America by creating opportunities for Latinos and breaking down barriers to expand economic and social progress for all. UnidosUS partners with an Affiliate Network of nearly 300 community-based organizations across the United States and Puerto Rico. For more information on UnidosUS, visit [www.unidosus.org] or follow us on Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, X, and Threads. ## Summary The Senior Policy Advisor, Health will join UnidosUS’s Policy and Advocacy team. The Senior Policy Advisor will play a key role in developing and enacting policy solutions to foster health in the Latino community on issues that include Medicaid, the Children’s Health Insurance Program, Marketplace coverage, mental health, healthcare affordability, and barriers to coverage and care encountered by low-income children and families, including immigrants and people with limited English proficiency. Bringing a strong health equity and social justice lens to every task, the Senior Policy Advisor will be a primary source of highly skilled policy analysis, help manage and implement the health policy team’s strategic priorities, lead key components of our work, and contribute to collective success in accordance with organizational priorities. The person filling this position will develop policy recommendations and advocacy strategies to influence key audiences, deepen the team’s expertise, strengthen engagement with Congress and state officials, reimagine systems, steward investments responsibly, and build power among local voices. The Senior Policy Advisor, Health will be responsible for researching and writing policy publications while supporting the development of broader collective team products. To achieve federal- and state-level policy gains for Latinos, and to limit harm experienced by Latinos, the person filling this position will work collaboratively with other UnidosUS components including Health Programs, Marketing and Communications, Affiliate Engagement, and UnidosUS state directors in Arizona, Florida, and Texas. Success in this position will require a focus on strategies with good prospects for long- or short-term success. **Location:** This is a hybrid position based in Washington, DC. In accordance with UnidosUS policy, employees are expected to work onsite two days per week, with Tuesdays designated as a common in-office day. Additional in-office days may be required as needed. **Salary:** $104,000–$125,000 ## Essential Functions ### Policy Analyses and Advocacy – Analyze health policy issues affecting the Latino community and produce policy recommendations that take into account prospects for success. Target audiences include national and state-level legislators and executive-branch agencies. – Draft, edit, and publish a range of policy analyses such as issue briefs, white papers, reports, and blog posts using primary and secondary research sources. – Represent UnidosUS in high-visibility settings, including appearances before Congress, the Executive Branch, state legislators and agencies, national conferences, and the media. – Lead and participate in coalitions of experts, advocates, and other stakeholders addressing health issues important to Latinos. – Communicate and partner with UnidosUS Affiliates (community-based organizations, including federally qualified health centers) to learn about emerging health trends, lived experiences, and solutions; develop policy advocacy approaches that effectively address community needs; and educate and collectively advocate about issues relevant to our collective work. – Help develop a strong, viable, and proactive agenda to promote and protect Latino families’ health and health care in key states including Arizona, Florida, and Texas. – Provide support to the Director to ensure quality performance on grants, including grant reporting, performance management, and funder relations including fundraising. ## Required Qualifications – Master’s degree in public health (MPH), public policy (MPP), public administration (MPA), health economics, health administration, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and significant relevant professional experience. – Minimum of 5 years of experience in health policy, including federal or state policy analysis, regulatory advocacy, or health systems reform. – Demonstrated ability to assess strategic strengths and weaknesses of possible advocacy strategies. – Strong writing skills, evidenced by articles, studies, reports, testimony, or other public documents. – Experience communicating policy ideas in public settings such as coalition meetings, congressional hearings and briefings, major conferences, and media interviews. – Strong project management skills suited to a dynamic work environment with multiple ongoing responsibilities, tight deadlines, and expectations for high-quality work. – Flexibility for occasional travel. – Demonstrated experience with and knowledge of the Latino community. ## Preferred Qualifications – Juris Doctor or other advanced degree in a relevant discipline. – Spanish-language fluency. – Familiarity with nutrition and food security issues. – Skill with quantitative analysis and manipulation of microdata. – Experience working on Capitol Hill, the Executive Branch, or in state-level legislatures or agencies. – Familiarity with federal and non-federal budget processes. – Experience managing staff. ## Skills and Abilities – Steadfast commitment to UnidosUS mission, vision, and values (Excellence, Respeto, Accountability). – Commitment to supporting and advancing the needs of the U.S. Latino community, Latino nonprofit organizations, and the Latino market. – Capacity for innovative approaches to substantive policy and advocacy strategy. ## Competencies – **Analytics:** Synthesizes complex and diverse information; collects and analyzes data; uses intuition and experience to complement data; designs effective and efficient workflows and procedures. – **Managing People:** Includes staff in planning, decision-making, facilitating, and process improvement; takes responsibility for subordinates’ activities; provides regular performance feedback; develops subordinates’ skills; encourages growth; solicits and applies feedback; fosters quality focus; improves processes, products, and services. – **Ethics:** Treats people with respect; keeps commitments; inspires trust; works with integrity; upholds organizational values. – **Written Communication:** Writes clearly and informatively; edits work to develop high-quality written products; varies style and approach to fit audiences; presents numerical information effectively; interprets written information accurately. – **Oral Communication:** Speaks clearly and persuasively; listens and seeks clarification; responds well to questions; demonstrates group presentation skills; participates in meetings. – **Strategic Thinking:** Develops strategies to achieve organizational goals; understands organizational strengths and weaknesses; analyzes policy environment and stakeholder capacities; identifies threats and opportunities; adapts strategy and tactics to changing conditions. – **Teamwork:** Balances team and individual responsibilities; welcomes feedback; contributes to positive team spirit; puts team success above individual interests; builds morale and group commitment. – **Motivation:** Sets and achieves challenging goals; demonstrates persistence; overcomes obstacles; measures self against standards of excellence; takes calculated risks. – **Quality:** Demonstrates accuracy and thoroughness; seeks ways to improve and promote quality; applies feedback; monitors own work. – **Initiative:** Volunteers readily; undertakes self-development; seeks increased responsibilities; takes independent actions; looks for opportunities; asks for and offers help when needed. ## Physical Demands and Work Environment – Perform some repetitive motion activities. – Sit for long periods of time. – Frequently required to stand and walk. – Frequently required to utilize hand and finger dexterity. – Frequently/continually required to talk or hear. – Occasionally required to lift/push light weights up to 25 pounds. – Specific vision abilities required include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus. – Utilize visual acuity to operate equipment, read technical information, and use a keyboard. – Noise level in the work environment is usually quiet to moderately loud. ## COVID-19 Considerations UnidosUS follows CDC guidance and strongly encourages employees to stay up to date on vaccinations and practice preventive measures to support their well-being and maintain a healthy work environment. — The above is intended to describe the general content and requirements for the performance of this job. It is not to be construed as an exhaustive statement of duties, responsibilities, or physical requirements. Nothing in this job description restricts management’s right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities at any time. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Employment with UnidosUS is contingent upon the successful completion of a background screen. **EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER.** All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, national origin, marital status, religion, gender, age, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, personal appearance, family responsibilities, political affiliation, or enrollment in a college, university, technical school, or adult education.
