item.title: Senior Policy Analyst, Higher Education
item.description: Senior Policy Analyst, Higher Education Organization: UnidosUS Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/10/2026 ## About UnidosUS UnidosUS is a nonprofit, nonpartisan organization that serves as the nation’s largest Hispanic civil rights and advocacy organization. Since 1968, we have built a stronger America by creating opportunities for Latinos and breaking down barriers to expand economic and social progress for all. UnidosUS partners with an Affiliate Network of nearly 300 community-based organizations across the United States and Puerto Rico. For more information on UnidosUS, visit [www.unidosus.org] or follow us on Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, X, and Threads. ## Summary UnidosUS is seeking a Senior Policy Analyst to join its Education Policy Project, reporting to the Director for Education Policy. This role will serve as a subject-matter expert and partner in shaping and advancing federal and state advocacy agendas. The Senior Policy Analyst will help develop and drive a policy agenda focused on strengthening accountability and improving return on investment in higher education, particularly for Latino students and other historically underserved communities. The role will center on advancing policies that ensure postsecondary programs deliver real economic value, protect students from low-quality or predatory programs, and close gaps in post-college outcomes. The Senior Policy Analyst will promote federal and state policies that improve transparency, enforce accountability, and ensure students enroll in programs that lead to meaningful credentials, gainful employment, and long-term economic mobility. The ideal candidate brings familiarity with postsecondary data sets and a strong interest in using evidence to improve outcomes for Latino students. **Location:** This is a hybrid position based in Washington, DC. In accordance with UnidosUS policy, employees are expected to work onsite two days per week, with Tuesdays designated as a common in-office day. Additional in-office days may be required as needed. **Salary:** $76,100–$84,600 ## Essential Functions • Shape and advance UnidosUS’ higher education policy agenda while generating innovative project ideas and strategies. • Lead analyses of emerging public policy issues and trends in higher education and produce policy documents, including issue briefs, regulatory comments, white papers, conference papers, and congressional testimony. • Serve as an expert on higher education policy, with a focus on policy solutions related to accountability and improving the return on investment in postsecondary education. • Represent UnidosUS in high-visibility forums, conferences, and meetings, including meetings with congressional staff, policymakers, issue experts, stakeholders, and the media. • Organize and execute policy forums, roundtables, and events to inform and elevate UnidosUS’ higher education policy agenda. • Lead and participate in coalitions of experts and advocates on higher education. • Carry out communications activities to build support for UnidosUS’ education priorities; provide consistent, timely updates to Affiliates, partners, and funders. • Manage their own projects from conception to completion, tracking deliverables, deadlines, and compliance requirements, and supporting clear reporting to funders. • Perform other duties as assigned. ## Required Qualifications • Bachelor’s degree. • 3–5 years of policy experience in higher education. • Strong knowledge base of higher education policy and experience with policy development and advocacy. • Knowledge of and professional networks within relevant agencies, congressional offices, and/or stakeholder organizations. • A proven track record of conducting rigorous policy analysis and translating findings into clear, actionable policy recommendations. Ability to work collaboratively across research, communications, and external partners in a fast-paced environment. • Excellent analytical and writing skills. • Displayed commitment to social justice and UnidosUS’s mission. • Flexibility for occasional travel (less than 10%). • Demonstrated experience with and knowledge of the Latino community. ## Preferred Qualifications • Master’s degree in a related field. • Experience conducting quantitative analysis and familiarity using higher education datasets. • Experience communicating policy ideas in public settings such as coalition meetings, congressional hearings and briefings, major conferences, and media interviews. • Bilingual ability (English and Spanish), written and verbal. ## Skills and Abilities • Steadfast commitment to UnidosUS mission, vision, and values (Excellence, Respeto, Accountability). • Commitment to supporting and advancing the needs of the U.S. Latino community, Latino nonprofit organizations, and the Latino market. Capacity for innovative approaches to substantive policy and advocacy strategy. ## Competencies **Analytical** — Synthesizes complex or diverse information; collects and researches data; uses intuition and experience to complement data; designs workflows and procedures. **Problem Solving** — Identifies and resolves problems in a timely manner; gathers and analyzes information skillfully; develops alternative solutions; works well in group problem-solving situations; uses reason even when dealing with emotional topics. **Project Management** — Develops project plans; coordinates projects; communicates changes and progress; completes projects on time and budget; manages project team activities. **Strategic Thinking** — Develops strategies to achieve organizational goals; understands organization’s strengths and weaknesses; analyzes market and competition; identifies external threats and opportunities; adapts strategy to changing conditions. **Innovation** — Displays original thinking and creativity; meets challenges with resourcefulness; generates suggestions for improving work; develops innovative approaches and ideas; presents ideas and information in a manner that gets others’ attention. ## Physical Demands and Work Environment • Perform some repetitive motion activities. • Sit for long periods of time. • Frequently required to stand. • Frequently required to walk. • Frequently required to sit. • Frequently required to utilize hand and finger dexterity. • Frequently/Continually required to talk or hear. • Occasionally required to lift/push light weights up to 25 pounds. • Specific vision abilities required for this job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust or focus. • Utilize visual acuity to operate equipment, read technical information, and/or use a keyboard. • The noise level in the work environment usually is quiet to moderately loud. ## COVID-19 Considerations UnidosUS follows CDC guidance and strongly encourages employees to stay up to date on vaccinations and practice a range of preventive measures to support their well-being and maintain a healthy work environment. — The above is intended to describe the general content of and requirements for the performance of this job. It is not to be construed as an exhaustive statement of duties, responsibilities, or physical requirements. Nothing in this job description restricts management’s right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Employment with UnidosUS is contingent upon the successful completion of a background screen. **EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER.** All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, national origin, marital status, religion, gender, age, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, personal appearance, family responsibilities, political affiliation, or enrollment in a college, university, technical school, or adult education. item.title: Senior Director, Communications and Media Relations
item.description: Senior Director, Communications and Media Relations Organization: Global Business Alliance (GBA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/10/2026 # Senior Director, Communications and Media Relations GBA is seeking a hands-on, entrepreneurial **Senior Director, Communications and Media Relations** to lead the organization’s earned media initiatives, grow its institutional voice, and maintain GBA’s reputation as a trusted, nonpartisan voice on the business‑policy issues shaping the U.S. investment climate. This senior communications role reports to the President and CEO in a lean, high-performing organization. The right candidate will be both a strategist and an operator: someone who can identify stories, pitch reporters, prepare for external engagements, draft compelling materials, manage rapid response, and work closely with colleagues. This role is an opportunity for a communications leader who wants to help build GBA’s visibility, voice, and influence through disciplined messaging, strong media judgment, and high‑quality execution. — ## Key Responsibilities ### Earned Media and Executive Positioning – Develop and execute a proactive earned media strategy that raises GBA’s visibility with national business press, policy media, tax press, and other influential outlets. – Build and maintain strong relationships with reporters covering business, investment, tax, trade, tariffs, market access, competitiveness, and economic policy. – Identify story opportunities from GBA’s policy agenda, member priorities, economic data, and broader business‑policy trends. – Lead the execution of GBA’s external engagement strategy, including media opportunities, speaking engagements, stakeholder-facing events, and related follow‑up. ### Messaging and Content – Translate complex tax, trade, investment, regulatory, and economic policy issues into clear, credible, and compelling messaging. – Draft and edit op-eds, statements, talking points, quotes, speeches, pitches, LinkedIn content, member-facing updates, website copy, and other communications materials. – Help ensure GBA’s voice remains disciplined, nonpartisan, and useful to members, policymakers, reporters, and stakeholders. – Use GBA’s data, member stories, and policy work to strengthen message pull‑through and reinforce the organization’s core themes. ### Advocacy and Cross-Functional Collaboration – Work closely with Government Affairs and Strategic Insights colleagues to identify communications opportunities tied to policy developments, member priorities, and emerging issues. – Bring forward clear recommendations, including opportunity, audience, message, risk, and proposed execution path. – Coordinate on policy-sensitive communications and rapid response. – Exercise sound judgment about when GBA should engage publicly. ### Team Leadership and Execution – Manage and support a communications team member responsible for digital, social, website, email, design, and production support. – Maintain a disciplined communications cadence without overburdening a small team. – Track media results, message pull‑through, external visibility, and the effectiveness of engagement efforts. – Work with outside consultants or vendors when needed, while personally owning the core communications work. — ## Ideal Candidate Profile The ideal candidate is a strong earned‑media operator with excellent judgment, policy fluency, and the ability to create external opportunities from complex issues. They should be comfortable in a small‑shop environment where senior leaders write, pitch, prepare, execute, and follow up. They should be able to work closely with technical policy colleagues, identify the story inside the substance, and recommend a communications path that is both ambitious and disciplined. **Strong candidates may come from one or more of the following environments:** – business or trade association communications – public affairs or advocacy communications – Capitol Hill, agency, campaign, or policy communications – corporate public affairs – business, financial, tax, trade, or policy media relations – earned media strategy in a small or fast‑moving organization — ## Qualifications – Significant experience (10+ years) in media relations, public affairs, advocacy communications, or executive communications – Demonstrated ability to personally pitch reporters and secure meaningful earned media – Strong understanding of national business, policy, and Washington media – Excellent writing, editing, and message‑development skills – Ability to translate complex policy issues into plain language – Strong judgment in politically sensitive environments – Experience preparing senior executives or principals for interviews, speaking engagements, stakeholder meetings, and public appearances – Ability to work collaboratively across policy, communications, membership, and executive leadership – Strong project management and execution skills – Familiarity with AI‑enabled communications tools and responsible use of AI for workflow is important — ## Compensation Details: $135–150K The compensation range listed for this position is provided as a good‑faith estimate of what the organization intends to offer for this role at the time this posting was issued. Actual compensation may vary based on factors such as job responsibilities, education, experience, skills, and market data. — ## Benefits Overview Our health and welfare benefits are designed to support you and your priorities. Offerings include: – Health, dental, and vision insurance – Disability, life, and accident insurance – Generous paid time off and holidays – Retirement benefits (including 401(k) matching) – Remote work and commuter subsidy – Parental and family flex leave — ## How To Apply Please email your resume and cover letter describing earned media experience, public affairs judgment, and experience supporting executive‑level external engagement to ** [email protected] **. In the subject line, please state: **“Senior Director, Communications”** Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Deputy Director of Government Relations
item.description: Deputy Director of Government Relations Organization: U.S. Global Leadership Coalition (USGLC) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/10/2026 ## The U.S. Global Leadership Coalition (USGLC) The U.S. Global Leadership Coalition (USGLC) is seeking a second Deputy Director of Government Relations to help lead a dynamic and high‑performing Government Relations Team responsible for USGLC’s engagement with Congress on America’s role in the world and how strategic investments in diplomacy and international assistance, alongside a strong military, strengthen U.S. national security and our economic interests. The Deputy Director of Government Relations will be an experienced professional with the knowledge and connections to further enhance USGLC’s presence on Capitol Hill, build sustainable relationships with a broad array of Congressional offices, and advance our mission. The position will report to the Director of Government Relations, work closely with the other Deputy Director of Government Relations, and reside in Washington, D.C. At USGLC, we are committed to fostering a culture of inclusiveness and belonging among staff, volunteers, and partners. — ## Responsibilities ### Help Execute USGLC’s Government Relations Work with the Director and Deputy Director of Government Relations to develop and implement strategies to deepen support among Republicans and Democrats in Congress for U.S. diplomacy and international assistance programs and resources. Activities include engagement with Members of Congress and Congressional staff through direct lobbying; building relationships with Congressional caucuses and associations such as the Republican Study Committee and Republican Governance Group; planning and executing briefings, events, and advocacy days on Capitol Hill; convening and mobilizing national coalition partners; among others. ### Serve as Expert Resource and Communicator Play a lead role in USGLC’s legislative and budget analysis – staying up to date on the latest developments throughout the federal budget and appropriations process to maximize USGLC’s influence. Prepare written and oral communications for USGLC’s leadership, membership, and Congressional offices. ### Represent USGLC Effectively represent USGLC at public and private briefings, meetings, events, and community activities with Members of Congress, Congressional staff, and coalition members. Travel domestically on a limited basis to support USGLC’s national and state‑based engagement with policymakers. ### Government Relations Team Management Help oversee a six‑person Government Relations Team and other government relations consultants, as needed. Track metrics and progress in meeting deliverables and strategic objectives. Provide mentoring, coaching, and guidance to team members. — ## Position Requirements The ideal candidate will have: – Minimum 6–10 years of relevant experience working with Members of Congress and their staff, including in government service, policy, advocacy, or government relations. – Extensive knowledge of Capitol Hill and Congressional processes and dynamics, including an understanding of the federal budget and appropriations process, foreign policy, and international development. – Relationships with current policymakers – including Congressional staff and relevant executive branch officials – and the ability to proactively deepen and grow this network. – Ability to think strategically and create and execute multi‑faceted advocacy strategies. – Excellent written and verbal communication skills, exceptional attention to detail, and the ability to distill complex information into high‑quality analytical written products. – Demonstrated ability to set priorities, meet deadlines, work under pressure in a team‑based environment, and proactively anticipate and address department needs. — ## To Apply Please email a cover letter and resume to [email protected] . Please reference “Deputy Director of Government Relations” in the subject line. Shortlisted candidates will be contacted. No calls, please. — ## About USGLC The U.S. Global Leadership Coalition (USGLC) is a bipartisan, broad‑based, influential network of 500 businesses, non‑profit organizations, national security and foreign policy experts, and business, veteran, agriculture, faith‑based, academic, and civic leaders in all 50 states who support strategic, cost‑effective investments in diplomacy and international assistance, alongside a strong defense, to advance U.S. interests and values and strengthen American leadership in the world. item.title: Vice President, Government Relations and Public Policy
item.description: Vice President, Government Relations and Public Policy Organization: BusPatrol Location: Austin, TX Date Posted: 08/11/2026 ## Role Summary BusPatrol is seeking an agile **Policy Leader** with distinct expertise in both **Public Policy** and **Government Relations (GR)** to serve as our **Vice President of Public Policy and Government Relations**. This role requires a senior leader who has previously worked as the Head of Policy and GR function with a proven track record of successfully lobbying multi-state legislation on controversial political issues, and who is highly effective at managing at scale (people, process, and systems). You will navigate a unique and highly complex political environment and will be responsible for designing and executing complex political strategies. This position heavily emphasizes the Government Relations and Policy work necessary to manage and build political strategies, and lead pioneering legislative enablement. As the accountable process owner, you must be comfortable enabling and driving enterprise decision-making. This person will be responsible for continuing our success in defending and authorizing automated enforcement laws by balancing direct advocacy, building complex strategies, and coordinating subject matter experts to be on the frontline. — ## Responsibilities ### Legislative Leadership, Defense, & Enablement Lead BusPatrol’s public policy development, GR strategies, and pioneering legislative enablement efforts. Focus heavily on managing both offensive legislation and critical glitch bills/defense bills to protect and expand automated school bus stop-arm enforcement, Speed Zone Safety (SZS), and other related legislative efforts at the state and municipal levels. ### Enterprise Policy & GR Management Manage policy and GR at scale on behalf of the enterprise. Direct and execute complex political and advocacy strategies in highly complex political environments while heavily coordinating internal SMEs to serve on the frontline, ensuring the entirety of the function’s delivery requirements are met. ### Team, Lobbyist, & Outside Counsel Management Supervise a high-functioning internal government relations team and manage a diverse network of external contract lobbyists and outside counsel. Explicitly identify and coordinate Business Development (BD) consultants, ensuring this GR/BD work effectively aligns with the company’s complex political strategies. ### Cross-Functional Alignment Develop tactics and strategy for a number of distinct state-by-state policy initiatives, working closely with BusPatrol’s Growth, Legal, and Communications teams to ensure compliance and market readiness. ### Technology Policy Integration Work with partner municipalities and school districts across the U.S. to help them prepare policies for emerging technological innovations in traffic safety, automated enforcement, and smart city data platforms. ### Partner Empowerment Build the capacity of local champions and partners to effectively engage with state and local leaders on our shared child safety and traffic enforcement policy agenda. ### Market Expansion In target growth states, work directly with local partners to promote violator-funded safety programs and secure the necessary legislative and regulatory frameworks for new deployments. ### Public Evangelism Travel and speak on behalf of BusPatrol and its safety coalition, including testifying at legislative hearings, participating in industry workshops and conferences, and engaging in media interviews. ### Coalition Support Utilize and support established coalition-building functions. Work alongside the Gov Ops team, which manages day-to-day coalition activities in perpetuity, to leverage these groups for targeted policy and legislative initiatives rather than leading the coalition building directly. — ## Special Knowledge and Skills ### Required – Minimum of 10+ years of leadership experience, featuring a mix of state and local in-government experience (e.g., state legislature or Executive branch), followed by advocacy or government relations (GR) roles. State lobbying experience is an absolute must; having only lobbied in a large municipality is not sufficient. (Note: Federal experience is nearly meaningless for us). – Proven track record of successfully lobbying multi-state legislation into existence on contentious political issues. – Proven track record of leadership in a legislative enablement function, specifically managing policy and GR at scale for an enterprise within highly complex political environments. – Experience operating as the #1 leader of a policy or government relations function. – Agile, high IQ, high EQ, and a humble leader who excels at managing people, processes, and systems at scale. – Deep knowledge of the legislative process at the state and local level, including a strong background in legislative defense, navigating glitch bills, and executing complex political strategies. – Comfortable working in a collaborative team environment, acting as an accountable process owner who enables enterprise-level decision making versus their own. – Proven staff management and project management skills, including experience managing remote teams and contract lobbyists. – Excellent time management, organizational, and research skills. – Ability to strategically prioritize workload and execute a high volume of work in a fast-paced, hyper-growth environment. – Superb written and verbal communication skills, with a high degree of accuracy, attention to detail, and the ability to draft legislation and policy memos. – Must be proficient with the Microsoft Office suite and comfortable working with CRM and legislative tracking software. ### Preferred – Deep knowledge, experience, and interest in traffic safety policy development (nice-to-have, but the primary requirement is lobbying multi-state legislation on contentious issues). – A Juris Doctorate (JD) or an advanced degree in public policy, public administration, political science, planning, or a related field. – Experience working within or closely with a state or local transportation agency, department of education, or law enforcement agency. – Subject matter expertise in camera-based traffic enforcement, transportation policy, education policy, or GovTech/B2G sales environments. — ## BusPatrol Value Proposition ### Who We Are At BusPatrol, safety isn’t just a priority — it’s our mission. As the nation’s most trusted school bus stop-arm technology solution, we serve over 350 school districts, protecting nearly 2 million students across 30,000 buses. Every day, millions of children rely on school buses to get to and from school safely, yet reckless drivers continue to put them at risk. As a technology company with a unique focus on public safety, we use cutting-edge AI, machine learning, and telematics to improve school bus safety. Our all-in-one safety program equips school bus fleets with AI-powered cameras, cloud-based data management, and an integrated software platform to capture and process stop-arm violations. Our safety programs foster accountability and reduce dangerous driving behavior in communities across the country. By partnering with school districts, municipalities, and law enforcement, we make safety solutions more accessible and effective, ensuring that every child’s journey to and from school is as safe as possible. ### What We Offer When you join BusPatrol, you are not just taking a job. You are joining a mission-driven team dedicated to making a real impact. We offer: ✔ Competitive salary and benefits package ✔ Unlimited PTO ✔ A purpose-driven career, working to protect children and improve public safety ✔ The occasion to participate in BusPatrol’s culture of safety, learning, and teamwork ✔ A team of innovators, committed to leveraging AI and smart technology for social good ### Be Part of Something Bigger We are looking for a passionate and dedicated team member to help us make roads safer. This is a meaningful opportunity to contribute to a mission-driven company that is using technology to create real change. At BusPatrol, we foster an inclusive and diverse environment built on integrity, collaboration, and innovation. If you are ready to be part of a team that is deeply committed to safety and community impact, we would love to hear from you. Together, we can protect students, hold drivers accountable, and build a safer future for all. We are looking for a valued member of the BusPatrol team to assist us in our quest to improve children’s safety. This is an important role for us and a great opportunity for the right candidate. Our environment is inclusive, diverse, ignited, built on integrity, and deeply committed. — ## Compensation The US salary range for this position is provided in this posting. Our salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location. The range displayed on each job posting reflects the minimum and maximum target for salaries for the position across all US locations. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. Your Talent Partner can share more about the specific salary range for your preferred location and skill level during the hiring process. Please note that the compensation details listed in US role postings reflect the base salary only, and do not include bonus, and/or commission (if applicable) or benefits. item.description: Legislative & Public Policy Director Organization: McBride Homes Location: Chesterfield, MO Date Posted: 08/11/2026 **McBride Homes has an exciting opportunity for a Legislative & Public Policy Director to join our team.** McBride is Missouri’s largest home builder and an industry leader in residential new home construction. With an expected 800 closings in 2026, McBride is proud to be recognized as the 33rd largest privately owned builder in the United States and the 69th largest overall according to *Builder Magazine*. We are seeking a talented Legislative & Public Policy Director to be part of a collaborative team, located in our state‑of‑the‑art facility in Chesterfield Valley. At McBride Homes, we work hard but also enjoy great company perks. McBride offers competitive compensation, outstanding benefits, a 401(k) plan, paid vacation, and many company outings. — ### **Top Reasons to Work With Us** – Competitive salary and an annual discretionary bonus program – State‑of‑the‑art software and technology – A collaborative work environment that values innovation and teamwork – Onsite fitness center at the corporate office **Salary Range:** $120,000–$130,000/yr, depending on experience. — ### **Position Overview** This role will work directly with municipalities, cities, counties, utility providers, and state agencies to address issues related to zoning, building codes, development regulations, infrastructure requirements, utility coordination, and other public policy matters impacting the homebuilding process. The ideal candidate will combine strong policy judgment, relationship‑building skills, and a practical understanding of residential development to help advance the company’s strategic growth objectives. — ### **Key Responsibilities** – Monitor, analyze, and respond to proposed and existing local and state laws, ordinances, regulations, and policy initiatives affecting residential land development and homebuilding. – Represent the company in meetings and negotiations with municipal officials, county leaders, utility companies, planning departments, code officials, and state agencies. – Review and evaluate zoning ordinances, subdivision regulations, building codes, utility requirements, and related governmental policies for their impact on current and future development projects. – Partner with internal teams—including land acquisition, development, construction, legal, and executive leadership—to identify regulatory risks and develop strategies to overcome barriers to development. – Advocate for reasonable and modernized public policies that support housing growth, affordability, and efficient development processes. – Build and maintain productive relationships with elected officials, staff, industry groups, consultants, and other stakeholders throughout Missouri. – Coordinate the company’s participation in public hearings, community meetings, planning and zoning matters, and legislative discussions. – Track emerging issues affecting homebuilding, including infrastructure, utilities, stormwater, environmental regulations, permitting practices, and housing policy. – Prepare reports, summaries, position statements, and recommendations for executive leadership on public policy and legislative matters. – Support strategic efforts to improve and streamline regulatory processes that affect the company’s ability to deliver housing efficiently and responsibly. — ### **Qualifications** – Bachelor’s degree required; degree in public policy, political science, law, urban planning, real estate, engineering, or a related field preferred. – 7+ years of experience in government relations, public policy, municipal affairs, land use, development, legislative affairs, or a related field. – Strong knowledge of zoning, land use, building codes, utility coordination, and development approval processes, preferably in Missouri. – Experience working with cities, counties, planning and zoning bodies, utilities, or state agencies. – Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to clearly explain complex policy and regulatory issues. – Strong negotiation, relationship management, and problem‑solving skills. – Ability to manage multiple issues and priorities in a fast‑paced development environment. – Experience in homebuilding, real estate development, infrastructure, public sector planning, or construction‑related policy strongly preferred. — ### **Preferred Attributes** – Strategic thinker with strong political and business judgment – Confident communicator who can represent the company professionally with both public officials and internal leadership – Results‑oriented, collaborative, and highly responsive – Comfortable navigating complex regulatory environments and finding practical solutions — **McBride is an Equal Opportunity Employer.** Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Senior Associate – Healthcare Compliance Analyst – HTS
item.description: Senior Associate – Healthcare Compliance Analyst – HTS Organization: BRG Location: Remote Date Posted: 08/11/2026 ## We Do Consulting Differently The Healthcare Compliance Analyst position is a staff consulting role within the Healthcare Transactions and Strategy (HTS) group. HTS is currently seeking a Healthcare Compliance Analyst at the Associate or Senior Associate level. HTS performs regulatory, reimbursement, data analytics, and compliance auditing for healthcare providers, healthcare payers, and healthcare investors. Compliance audit deliverables include assessment of provider compliance programs and auditing of billing and coding of clinical documents and claims documents. This position requires a highly motivated problem solver with strong analytical ability, solid organizational skills, and a desire to advance within the organization. The work of a Healthcare Compliance Analyst involves execution of engagement work streams that primarily support the compliance team as they audit provider claims and provider clinical documentation, with a particular focus on government programs such as Medicare and Medicaid. Responsibilities include managing and organizing document intake, researching coverage policies, researching target companies and relevant healthcare sectors, and supporting the development of client deliverables and presentations. The work of an Analyst may be qualitative or quantitative in nature. Responsibilities include coding and coverage research, writing, use of Excel, quality control, development of client deliverables, and industry research. This position requires knowledge of the healthcare sector and a strong interest in healthcare compliance. Candidates will be expected to obtain coding certifications (e.g., CPC) while employed. Job duties include completing a certified coder course within the first 18 months of employment, with tuition paid by BRG. Job title and compensation will be determined based on qualifications and experience. — ## Job Responsibilities – Support medical record audits to determine coding accuracy and compliant claims submission, including research and document management. – Assist with coding and documentation audit methodology, including writing PowerPoint slides and compiling Excel spreadsheets under the direction of senior auditors. – Conduct analysis of audit findings to identify trends or problems in coding and documentation, and effectively communicate audit findings and recommended areas for improvement. – Monitor relevant resources, publications, and current government compliance and enforcement activity related to high‑risk compliance areas. – Actively pursue and obtain coding certifications (e.g., CPC) to advance to higher auditor positions performing full audit duties. – Develop analyses using transactional and/or financial data. – Generate client deliverables and contribute to expert reports. – Demonstrate creativity and efficient use of relevant software tools and analytical methods to develop solutions. – Participate in group practice meetings, contribute to business development initiatives, and support office functions such as staff training and recruiting. – Prioritize assignments and responsibilities to meet goals and deadlines. — ## Qualifications – 4‑year undergraduate degree (e.g., BS, BA). – Preference for candidates certified in medical auditing. – 0 to 2 years of work experience with a demonstrated interest in the healthcare industry and healthcare provider billing and coding compliance. – Preference for candidates with undergraduate academic studies related to the healthcare sector, healthcare administration, or management. – Work experience related to healthcare coding, billing, compliance, or healthcare administration and management is beneficial. — ## Required Skills – Ability to research national coding and documentation guidelines; knowledge of the healthcare sector and healthcare payment systems; ability to develop reports and track and trend audit findings. – Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, specifically Excel, PowerPoint, Access, and Word. A desire to expand those capabilities is required, as is the ability to train others. – Commitment to producing high‑quality analysis and attention to detail. – Excellent time management, organizational skills, and ability to prioritize work and meet deadlines. – Strong interest in healthcare compliance and healthcare policy. – Exceptional verbal and written communication skills. – Desire to work within a team environment. — ## Compensation **Associate Salary Range:** $70,000 – $90,000 per year. **Senior Associate Salary Range:** $85,000 – $115,000 per year. Candidate must be able to submit verification of their legal right to work in the U.S., without company sponsorship. — ## About BRG BRG combines world‑leading academic credentials with business expertise and purpose‑built emerging technologies. Our culture centers on agility and connectivity, which sets us apart and helps our clients move ahead. At BRG, our professionals include specialist consultants, industry experts, renowned academics, and leading‑edge data scientists. Together, they bring diverse real‑world experience, data, and human and artificial intelligence to economics, disputes and investigations, corporate finance, and performance improvement services that address complex challenges facing organizations across the globe. Our unique structure nurtures interdisciplinary relationships that give us an edge, laying the groundwork for more informed insights and more original, incisive thinking. Paired with our global reach and resources, our diverse perspectives and technical capabilities make us uniquely capable of addressing client challenges. We get results because we know how to apply our thinking to your world. At BRG, we don’t just show you what’s possible — we’re built to help you make it happen. — ## Equal Opportunity Statement BRG is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. Our hiring practices provide equal opportunity for employment without regard to race, religion, color, sex, gender, national origin, age, United States military veteran status, ancestry, sexual orientation, marital status, family structure, medical condition including genetic characteristics or information, veteran status, or mental or physical disability, so long as the essential functions of the job can be performed with or without reasonable accommodation, or any other protected category under federal, state, or local law. item.title: Senior Director, Federal Affairs
item.description: Senior Director, Federal Affairs Organization: NRG Location: Washington, DC | Reston, VA Date Posted: 08/11/2026 ## Welcome to the intersection of energy and home services At NRG, we’re all about propelling the next generation of leaders forward. We are driven by our passion to create a smarter, cleaner, and more connected future. We deliver innovative solutions that make our customers’ lives easier—helping them power, protect, and intelligently manage their homes and businesses. To do this, we need creative and talented people to join our company. We offer a dynamic work environment and a unified and inclusive culture. NRG fosters a strong sense of belonging that leads to better collaboration and business performance. Our company programs are designed to help employees develop the skills they need for success now and in the future. In everything we do, we aim to champion our employees and bring value to our customers, investors, and society. More information is available at [www.nrg.com]. Connect with NRG on Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn and X. — ## Position Summary The Senior Director, Federal Affairs will lead and execute the company’s federal government affairs strategy, advancing policy priorities that support business objectives and long‑term growth. This role serves as a key liaison between the company and federal policymakers, agencies, and industry stakeholders—translating legislative and regulatory developments into business insights and coordinated advocacy strategies. The Senior Director will partner closely with internal stakeholders across Policy, Regulatory Affairs, Legal, and Commercial teams to ensure alignment on advocacy priorities, messaging, and engagement efforts. The Director will develop and support strong relationships with industry associations, non‑governmental organizations, coalition partners, and academia to align and execute policy outcomes. — ## Key Responsibilities ### Federal Advocacy & Strategy – Develop and execute federal government affairs strategies aligned with enterprise policy priorities and commercial objectives. – Identify legislative risks and opportunities; advise leadership on potential business impacts. – Shape and advance company policy positions on key issues (e.g., energy markets, environmental policy, customer choice, grid modernization). ### Relationship Management – Build and maintain strong relationships with Members of Congress, federal agencies, committees, and relevant staff. – Represent the company in meetings, briefings, hearings, and industry forums. – Serve as a trusted external representative advancing the company’s credibility and influence. ### Policy Analysis & Insights – Monitor federal legislative and regulatory developments; provide timely analysis and strategic recommendations. – Translate complex policy developments into clear implications for internal stakeholders, and internal priorities and objectives into clear and politically viable policy asks. – Support scenario planning and policy forecasting to inform business strategy. ### Advocacy Execution – Develop advocacy materials including briefing documents, talking points, position papers, and testimony. – Coordinate engagement strategies, including coalition participation and trade association alignment. – Partner cross‑functionally to ensure consistency in messaging and leverage relationships across federal, state, and regulatory channels. ### Cross‑Functional Partnership – Collaborate with Regulatory Affairs, Legal, External Affairs, and Commercial leaders to align advocacy efforts. – Support enterprise‑wide policy strategy by connecting federal developments to broader regulatory and market considerations. – Demonstrate strong business acumen, executive presence, and the ability to operate effectively within a large, matrixed corporate environment. – Translate policy priorities into enterprise value and engage credibly with senior leaders across the business. — ## Qualifications – Bachelor’s degree in Public Policy, Political Science, Government, or related field preferred (advanced degree or JD preferred). – 10+ years of experience in government affairs, public policy, or related fields engaging with federal legislative bodies, agencies, or political stakeholders and legislative and regulatory processes. – Government affairs experience in a large, complex energy, infrastructure, or regulated industry organization strongly preferred; candidates should understand how enterprise decision‑making, governance, risk management, and cross‑functional alignment work in practice. – Strong leadership capabilities and a proven ability to lead directly and through influence to deliver results, and the judgment and ability to advise senior leaders on high‑stakes policy and business issues. – High‑agency, strategic operator with the judgment and initiative to anticipate business needs, shape policy solutions that advance commercial objectives, and independently drive priorities from concept through execution. – Strong, broad relationships with federal policymakers in Congress, agencies, and the Administration, as well as non‑government organizations, industry organizations, and key customers. – Proven ability to synthesize complex policy issues into actionable business insights. – Exceptional communication, stakeholder management, and influencing skills. — NRG Energy is committed to a drug and alcohol‑free workplace. To the extent permitted by law and any applicable collective bargaining agreement, employees are subject to periodic random drug testing, and post‑accident and reasonable suspicion drug and alcohol testing. EOE AA M/F/Protected Veteran Status/Disability. Level, Title and/or Salary may be adjusted based on the applicant’s experience or skills. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Senior Director Compliance
item.description: Senior Director Compliance Organization: Empower Location: Remote Date Posted: 08/11/2026 ## Our vision for the future Our vision for the future is based on the idea that transforming financial lives starts by giving our people the freedom to transform their own. We have a flexible work environment and fluid career paths. We not only encourage but celebrate internal mobility. We also recognize the importance of purpose, well‑being, and work‑life balance. Within Empower and our communities, we work hard to create a welcoming and inclusive environment, and our associates dedicate thousands of hours to volunteering for causes that matter most to them. Chart your own path and grow your career while helping more customers achieve financial freedom. Empower Yourself. ## Senior Director, Compliance As a Senior Director Compliance, you will lead Empower’s Personal Trading and Code of Ethics program across Empower Capital Management, Empower Advisory Group, Empower Funds, and Empower Financial Services. You’ll serve as a senior leader within Compliance, helping shape a scalable, risk‑based compliance program that supports our investment advisers, registered funds, separate accounts, and broker‑dealer businesses. Working closely with business leaders, Legal, Risk, and executive leadership, you’ll strengthen our compliance framework while helping the business navigate an evolving regulatory environment. ## What you will do – Lead the firm’s Personal Trading and Code of Ethics program, including pre‑clearance, employee trading reviews, restricted list oversight, certifications, and disclosures – Serve as deputy to the VP, Compliance and Chief Compliance Officer for designated governance, regulatory, and business initiatives – Direct enterprise compliance risk assessments, annual compliance reviews, monitoring, testing, issue management, and governance reporting – Design and enhance a risk assessment framework that supports targeted monitoring, testing, and remediation activities – Manage, coach, and develop a team of compliance professionals while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement – Partner with business leaders and control functions to provide guidance on regulatory requirements, conflicts of interest, fiduciary obligations, and supervisory expectations – Lead regulatory examinations, internal audits, and annual reviews, coordinating responses and remediation efforts – Present compliance reporting, trends, and recommendations to senior leadership, governance committees, and boards – Monitor regulatory developments and implement enhancements to policies, procedures, controls, and compliance programs – Sponsor technology, automation, analytics, and AI‑enabled compliance capabilities that strengthen surveillance, reporting, and operational effectiveness ## What you will bring – Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required; Juris Doctor preferred – 10+ years of progressive compliance experience supporting investment advisers, registered funds, asset management, or broker‑dealer businesses – 5+ years of people leadership experience, including coaching, performance management, and team development – 10+ years experience working with the Investment Advisers Act of 1940, Investment Company Act of 1940, Securities Exchange Act of 1934, FINRA rules, and related regulatory expectations – 8+ years experience leading personal trading, Code of Ethics, monitoring, testing, risk assessments, and compliance program oversight – Strong communication skills with the ability to influence senior leaders and present complex topics clearly – Experience partnering with regulators, auditors, and governance committees during examinations and reviews – FINRA Series 65 or 66 required – FINRA fingerprinting required – High ethical standards, sound judgment, and the ability to manage confidential information with discretion ## What will set you apart – Juris Doctor or other advanced degree – Experience modernizing compliance programs through technology, analytics, automation, or AI‑enabled monitoring – Knowledge of compliance governance across registered investment advisers, registered funds, separate accounts, and broker‑dealers – Experience developing compliance metrics, key risk indicators, and executive reporting – Demonstrated success designing scalable compliance controls and risk‑based monitoring programs – Continuous improvement mindset with a track record of strengthening compliance processes and controls – Ability to identify emerging regulatory risks and translate them into practical business solutions – Strong executive presence with experience advising senior leadership and boards – Experience overseeing third‑party compliance due diligence and ongoing monitoring – Reputation for building collaborative partnerships and developing high‑performing compliance teams ***Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time, including CPT/OPT.*** ## What we offer you We offer an array of diverse and inclusive benefits regardless of where you are in your career. We believe that providing our employees with the means to lead healthy balanced lives results in the best possible work performance. – Medical, dental, vision and life insurance – Retirement savings – 401(k) plan with generous company matching contributions (up to 6%), financial advisory services, potential company discretionary contribution, and a broad investment lineup – Tuition reimbursement up to $5,250/year – Business‑casual environment that includes the option to wear jeans – Generous paid time off upon hire – including a paid time off program plus ten paid company holidays and three floating holidays each calendar year – Paid volunteer time — 16 hours per calendar year – Leave of absence programs – including paid parental leave, paid short‑ and long‑term disability, and Family and Medical Leave (FMLA) – Business Resource Groups (BRGs) – BRGs facilitate inclusion and collaboration across our business internally and throughout the communities where we live, work and play. BRGs are open to all. ## Base Salary Range $151,800.00 – $220,050.00 The salary range above shows the typical minimum to maximum base salary range for this position in the location listed. Non‑sales positions have the opportunity to participate in a bonus program. Sales positions are eligible for sales incentives, and in some instances a bonus plan, whereby total compensation may far exceed base salary depending on individual performance. Actual compensation offered may vary from posted hiring range based upon geographic location, work experience, education, licensure requirements and/or skill level and will be finalized at the time of offer. Equal opportunity employer • Drug‑free workplace We are an equal opportunity employer with a commitment to diversity. All individuals, regardless of personal characteristics, are encouraged to apply. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age (40 and over), race, color, national origin, ancestry, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, marital status, pregnancy, religion, physical or mental disability, military or veteran status, genetic information, or any other status protected by applicable state or local law. ***For remote and hybrid positions you will be required to provide reliable high‑speed internet with a wired connection as well as a place in your home to work with limited disruption. You must have reliable connectivity from an internet service provider that is fiber, cable or DSL internet. Other necessary computer equipment will be provided. You may be required to work in the office if you do not have an adequate home work environment and the required internet connection.*** Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: PR Associate
item.description: PR Associate Organization: Communications Strategy Group (CSG®) Location: Denver, CO Date Posted: 08/11/2026 ## Public Relations Associate Communications Strategy Group (CSG®), an intent marketing agency based in Denver, Colorado, is seeking PR associate candidates to support the media relations and influencer engagement activities of clients across industry practices including education, health & wellness, consumer, aerospace and renewable energy. While headquartered in Denver, Colorado, we invite candidates across the country to apply. ## Roles and Responsibilities Public relations associates at CSG are detail‑oriented professionals with top‑notch communication and collaboration skills. They support PR‑related activities for select clients in coordination with CSG’s account team. To be successful, you’ll need to face each day with a willingness to jump feet first into whatever comes across your path. Whether you’re crafting compelling story angles and pitching media, coordinating high‑profile interviews for client spokespeople, or immersing yourself in the latest and greatest media relations strategies, you’ll be a critical part of our commitment to purposeful solutions that solve our clients’ business problems. ### Public Relations Associates: – Serve as day‑to‑day PR support for multiple clients, responsible for developing creative story angles and securing coverage for local, national and trade media – Conduct media relations activities including researching and building media lists, drafting pitches, executing media backgrounders, and coordinating interviews – Immerse themselves in the industries, clients and target audiences we work with to support senior team members in creating strategic plans that meet business objectives and capitalize on opportunities, including keeping up with relevant industry media – Contribute to the ideation and development of media relations strategies, approaches and activities in support of client goals – Write press releases for clients – Manage the tracking and reporting on ROI for clients based on specific client goals/objectives (e.g., media placements or paid digital engagements) ## Qualifications – 2–3 years of experience in PR/media relations or strategic communications; agency experience preferred – Previous experience working in the education, healthcare or consumer space a plus – Experience writing pitch angles for the media and creating media lists – Willingness to work across various industries as needed – Ability to work confidently and independently in a fast‑paced environment with an understanding of how to delegate and manage up as needed – Accountability and a confident presence with keen problem‑solving skills and a positive attitude – Strong verbal and written communication skills – Effective presentation skills, particularly related to communications plans (skills related to concepts and digital approaches is a plus) – Experience working with AI platforms (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT, etc.) in a business setting; an understanding of more advanced concepts like skill development, MCPs, etc., a plus – Strong organizational and project management skills; experience working in a project management system (e.g., Asana, Basecamp, WorkFront, etc.) a plus – A passion for finding creative solutions for clients’ problems, requests and opportunities – Curiosity to learn and stay on top of industry and client vertical trends and best practices To apply, Please send your resume and portfolio (if applicable) to: [email protected] . Cover letters are optional if you’d like to share more about your qualifications and interest in joining the CSG team. Salary and benefits are competitive and commensurate with experience. CSG provides a generous benefits package that includes self‑managed PTO, 401(k) match, paid and subsidized insurance including medical, dental and vision, recognition and rewards programs, a business‑casual environment with remote and flexible work arrangements available, central Cherry Creek office location in Denver, CO, monthly team lunches, and more. ## About CSG Communications Strategy Group (CSG®) is a full‑service intent marketing agency that turns strategy into action. We operate at the intersection of insight and execution, combining the science of behavior design with the art of strategic communication to help organizations connect, resonate and grow. At our core, we’re problem solvers and storytellers. Strategists and creatives. Curious thinkers who care deeply about the people behind the brands we serve. We partner with small‑ to mid‑sized teams to bring scale, strategy, specialization and sophistication to their work. Our approach is grounded in a deep understanding of human behavior and shaped by real industry expertise, allowing us to create marketing that doesn’t just reach audiences, but moves them. Headquartered in Denver, Colorado, CSG is a certified Great Place to Work and home to a collaborative team that believes great work starts with strong partnerships, inside and out. We offer extensive benefits to our full‑time employees, as well as competitive salaries and hourly rates. CSG’s benefits package includes self‑managed PTO, 401(k) match, paid and subsidized insurance including medical, dental and vision, recognition and rewards programs, business‑casual environment with remote and flexible work arrangements available, central Cherry Creek office location, monthly team lunches, and more. To learn more about CSG, its philosophy, culture and work, visit wearecsg.com. At CSG, we are committed to creating a diverse environment, maintaining an inclusive culture, prioritizing cross‑functional collaboration, and emphasizing team member engagement. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age or veteran status. item.title: Manager, Policy and Engagement
item.description: Manager, Policy and Engagement Organization: Generate Capital Location: New York, NY | San Francisco, CA Date Posted: 08/11/2026 ## Generate Capital aims to provide power to large load customers through a combination of on‑site power and grid‑connected solutions. As the **Policy and Engagement Manager**, you will support regional and state‑level policy and regulatory strategy in core geographies, with an initial focus on SPP and ERCOT. You will integrate regulatory expertise into Generate’s commercial strategy and help shape policy outcomes. — ## What you will be doing at Generate Capital as the Manager, Policy and Engagement – Establish policy priorities and engagement strategies to advance Generate’s interests across state and ISO/RTO markets in partnership with VP, Policy & Market Development – Monitor and translate policy updates (FERC and PUC filings, state legislation, and RTO/ISO initiatives) into strategic guidance for internal teams, such as Origination, Development, and Interconnection – Represent Generate in policy forums and regional trade groups to advocate for favorable policy outcomes – Ensure key policy outcomes in core geographies (initially SPP and ERCOT) reflect and protect Generate’s commercial priorities – Coordinate the work of consultants, lobbyists, and other external resources as needed to ensure timely and actionable outputs that help advance Generate’s commercial priorities – Partner with Origination, Market, Development, and Interconnection teams on interconnection strategy development and execution for large load customers – Interface with utilities, transmission owners, ISOs/RTOs, and regulators to advance projects efficiently – Partner with internal teams to develop and execute robust community engagement plans that support Generate’s infrastructure goals and local community needs — ## Candidate qualifications & core characteristics – 5+ years of experience in energy policy or market strategy focused on the electricity industry – Prior experience at one or more of: – Independent Power Producers or power developers – Utilities or transmission owners – ISO/RTOs – A data center developer – Experience engaging directly with utilities and grid operators, with preference for experience with SPP and/or ERCOT – Experience with wholesale market design, regulatory structures, and interconnection processes, including ERCOT and/or SPP – Experience navigating PUCs, ISO/RTO initiatives, and administrative proceedings – Experience in coalition‑building, thinking strategically to develop a course of action to achieve policy objectives and persuading stakeholders to follow it – Ability to clearly and succinctly convey risks and opportunities posed to a business and broader market by complex and evolving regulatory constructs and political dynamics – Demonstrated ability to balance policy goals with business priorities – Experience managing consultants, lobbyists, and external advisors to support achieving business objectives — ## Compensation Generate’s compensation packages are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. Salary decisions take into account a wide variety of factors including, but not limited to: skill sets, experience and training, licensure and certifications, geographic location, and other business and organizational needs. A reasonable estimate of the base salary range for this role is **$140,000 – $160,000**. In addition, the compensation package may include a discretionary bonus and other benefits, including health care benefits, retirement benefits, paid days off (including sick leave, parental leave, and vacation benefits), and other benefits that must be reported for federal tax purposes. It is not typical for an individual to be hired at the top of this range. — ## Equal Opportunity Statement Generate Capital is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate against otherwise qualified applicants on the basis of actual or perceived race, color, creed, religion, ancestry, citizenship status, age, sex, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or handicap, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws. item.title: Senior Counsel, Project Development
item.description: Senior Counsel, Project Development Organization: Generate Capital Location: New York, NY | San Francisco, CA Date Posted: 08/11/2026 ## **Senior Counsel, Project Development – Role Overview** This role sits at the heart of Generate Capital’s project development engine. The Senior Counsel, Project Development will serve as a trusted legal partner to Generate’s development, permitting, and interconnection teams across a diverse portfolio of energy assets—including behind‑the‑meter and front‑of‑the‑meter power projects, community solar, large‑load infrastructure, and digital infrastructure. The ideal candidate is someone who has rolled up their sleeves on real projects—navigating the full arc from site control and permitting through procurement, construction, and commercial operation. This is not a siloed financing role; it requires a generalist mindset, sound judgment under uncertainty, strong cross‑functional instincts, and the confidence to advise internal clients who hold strong views. This person must be ready to own matters independently and step into a wide range of project and asset management legal needs as they arise. — ## **What You Will Be Doing** – Serve as primary legal counsel to Generate’s development teams on energy projects from inception through construction, covering the full lifecycle of permitting, interconnection, procurement, and construction. – Negotiate and draft a broad range of development agreements, including EPC contracts, procurement agreements, offtake agreements, and interconnection agreements. – Provide counsel and manage regulatory compliance matters, including regulatory filings, submissions, and ongoing compliance across multiple jurisdictions. – Partner with cross‑functional teams—including development, engineering, finance, and asset management—to facilitate timely project execution and resolve issues as they arise. – Support day‑to‑day legal needs across Generate’s project portfolio, including routine asset management matters, dispute resolution, and contract administration. – Adapt quickly to new asset types and legal contexts—including digital infrastructure and large‑load projects—and bring a generalist’s confidence to novel situations where the answer isn’t always obvious. — ## **Candidate Qualifications & Core Characteristics** – JD from an accredited law school and active bar membership; approximately 4–8 years of legal experience. – Experience with energy project development, EPC agreements, procurement contracts, and offtake agreements is highly valued—candidates who have supported projects from development through construction are strongly preferred. – Familiarity with permitting, interconnection, and energy regulatory compliance across multiple jurisdictions. – Behind‑the‑meter power project experience is a plus; digital infrastructure experience is nice‑to‑have but not required. – Experience with digital infrastructure projects is a plus, but not required. – Strong attention to detail, sound drafting instincts, and good interpersonal skills across development, engineering, finance, and operations teams. – Collaborative, with strong judgment under ambiguity. — ## **Compensation** Generate’s compensation packages are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. Salary decisions take into account a wide variety of factors including, but not limited to: skill sets, experience and training, licensure and certifications, geographic location, and other business and organizational needs. A reasonable estimate of the base salary range for this role is **$200,000 – $275,000**. In addition, the compensation package may include a discretionary bonus and other benefits, including health care benefits, retirement benefits, paid days off (including sick leave, parental leave, and vacation benefits), and other benefits that must be reported for federal tax purposes. — ## **Equal Opportunity Statement** Generate Capital is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate against otherwise qualified applicants on the basis of actual or perceived race, color, creed, religion, ancestry, citizenship status, age, sex, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or handicap, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws. item.title: Policy Director, Digital Assets & Emerging Technology
item.description: Policy Director, Digital Assets & Emerging Technology Organization: Fidelity Investments Location: Boston, MA Date Posted: 08/11/2026 **Note: Fidelity is not providing immigration sponsorship for this position** **The Role** Are you energized by how emerging technologies are reshaping financial services—and curious about what comes next before clear rules or frameworks emerge? Do you enjoy exploring complex questions where technology, innovation, and responsibility intersect? This role sits at the crossroads of innovation, technology, and public policy, helping Fidelity navigate change while staying grounded in trust and long‑term stewardship. As Policy Director, Digital Assets & Emerging Technology, you will help shape how Fidelity engages with blockchain‑based innovation and cross‑enterprise technology change. Working closely across the firm, you will support thoughtful decision‑making as new technologies influence markets, business models, and investor expectations. **Your role:** – Shaping strategic thinking on blockchain, digital assets, and emerging technologies across financial services – Partnering with business, legal, compliance, risk, and technology teams to evaluate new ideas and initiatives – Translating evolving technology concepts into clear policy, risk, and regulatory considerations – Asking forward‑looking questions about how technology changes incentives, responsibilities, and oversight – Monitoring trends across market innovation, including the rise of agentic financial services and intersections with cybersecurity, privacy, and artificial intelligence – Supporting external engagement with regulators, policymakers, and industry groups in a constructive and informed way – Preparing senior leaders for decisions amid uncertainty and change **The Expertise and Skills You Bring:** This role is designed for someone who understands crypto and emerging technologies and enjoys working through questions where the answers are still forming. You bring familiarity with blockchain, digital asset ecosystems, or adjacent technologies, along with the ability to think in systems rather than silos. You are comfortable operating in ambiguity, asking insightful questions, and collaborating across disciplines to surface risks, trade‑offs, and opportunities. This role values judgment, curiosity, and the ability to connect ideas across technology, business models, and risk considerations. Experience engaging with policy, regulatory, or risk topics is helpful, but deep specialization is not required. What matters most is how you think, how you communicate, and how you partner with others. **We are particularly interested in candidates who demonstrate:** – Understanding of blockchain systems and emerging technology use cases – Experience applying emerging technology within financial services, fintech, or market infrastructure – Ability to translate complex ideas across technical and non‑technical audiences – Clear written and verbal communication skills – Intellectual curiosity and sound judgment when navigating new or unfamiliar issues **The Team** This role sits within Fidelity’s Policy & Regulatory Strategy organization, which works across the enterprise to support thoughtful engagement with regulators, policymakers, and industry partners. Our work connects innovation with responsibility, helping Fidelity adapt as markets and technologies evolve. This role collaborates closely with investment, brokerage, digital assets, legal, compliance, risk, and technology teams, as well as with external stakeholders across government, industry, and the broader financial ecosystem. **Fidelity’s Onsite Working Model** Fidelity is transitioning to a full‑time onsite working model through a phased rollout across regions and roles. Currently, some roles and locations require 100% onsite presence, while others require less. Onsite expectations are likely to evolve as the rollout continues. This transition does not apply to fully remote roles. The base salary range for this position is $126,000–255,000 USD per year. Placement in the range will vary based on job responsibilities and scope, geographic location, candidate’s relevant experience, and other factors. Base salary is only part of the total compensation package. Depending on the position and eligibility requirements, the offer package may also include bonus or other variable compensation. We offer a wide range of benefits to meet your evolving needs and help you live your best life at work and at home. These benefits include comprehensive health care coverage and emotional well‑being support, market‑leading retirement, generous paid time off and parental leave, charitable giving employee match program, and educational assistance including student loan repayment, tuition reimbursement, and learning resources to develop your career. Note, the application window closes when the position is filled or unposted. Please be advised that Fidelity’s business is governed by the provisions of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, the Investment Advisers Act of 1940, the Investment Company Act of 1940, ERISA, numerous state laws governing securities, investment and retirement‑related financial activities and the rules and regulations of numerous self‑regulatory organizations, including FINRA, among others. Those laws and regulations may restrict Fidelity from hiring and/or associating with individuals with certain Criminal Histories. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Quality Assurance Lead
item.description: Quality Assurance Lead Organization: Hawaii Medical Service Association (HMSA) Location: Honolulu, HI Date Posted: 08/11/2026 ## Job Summary **Hybrid Work Environment – Must reside in Hawaii** **Pay Range:** $86,500 – $179,500 *Note: Individuals typically begin between the minimum to middle of the pay range.* The Quality Assurance (QA) Lead is responsible for overseeing and leading all quality assurance activities across complex initiatives, ensuring software solutions meet business, functional, technical, security, and regulatory requirements. This role combines hands‑on testing expertise with leadership responsibilities, including mentoring QA team members, establishing testing best practices, coordinating testing efforts across multiple teams, and driving quality throughout the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC). The QA Lead serves as a trusted advisor to stakeholders to ensure testing strategies align with business objectives and project delivery goals. On larger or more complex initiatives, this role may lead and coordinate the work of QA analysts, QA engineers, and testers. — ## Minimum Qualifications – Bachelor’s degree in related technical/business areas or equivalent work experience. – Seven years of QA/testing experience in software development environments. – Two years of experience leading testing efforts on medium to large‑scale projects. – Experience with Agile frameworks. – Experience writing test plans and test cases for software development efforts. – Experience creating requirements traceability matrices. – Experience executing manual or automated functional or technical test cases. – Experience with QA/test tools such as ALM and automation. – Knowledge of Agile/Scrum methodologies. – Effective verbal and written communication skills. – Excellent customer service skills. – Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines across concurrent projects. – Intermediate knowledge of Microsoft Office applications, including but not limited to Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook. — ## Duties and Responsibilities ### Business & Requirements Analysis – Collaborate closely with business stakeholders, product owners, business analysts, and subject matter experts to understand business processes and requirements. – Facilitate requirement review sessions to identify ambiguities, gaps, and testability concerns. – Translate business requirements into detailed test scenarios and test cases. – Work directly with business partners to validate expected outcomes and acceptance criteria. – Ensure traceability between requirements, test cases, and defects. ### Test Management & Test Execution – Develop and execute comprehensive test strategies, plans, and schedules for assigned projects and releases. – Lead QA efforts for medium to large complex projects. – Define testing scope, approach, environments, tools, data requirements, and resource needs. – Coordinate and manage test activities across functional, regression, integration, system, performance, security, and user acceptance test cycles. – Ensure traceability from user stories, requirements, and acceptance criteria to test coverage and results. – Monitor progress of manual and automated test execution across all QA resources. – Identify risks, issues, and test environment constraints that may impact timelines or quality. – Ensure all test activities follow standard documentation, evidence capture, and sign‑off processes. – Oversee defect management and ensure timely logging, triage, prioritization, and resolution. – Lead and facilitate daily test and defect review meetings with development, product, and business teams. – Track and report defect trends, root causes, and quality metrics to leadership. – Coordinate activities to ensure test environments are properly configured and stable. – Oversee readiness and maintenance of test data sets and data refresh cycles. – Provide regular status updates on test progress, risks, metrics, and achievement of quality goals. – Recommend process improvements to enhance test efficiency, automation adoption, and overall quality. – Support retrospectives and post‑release reviews to identify quality improvements and lessons learned. ### Quality Assurance Governance & Oversight – Contribute to the development and maintenance of all software QA processes and metrics to ensure adherence to established QA methodologies, standards, and industry best practices. – Drive improvements in testing efficiency, effectiveness, and quality outcomes. – Promote “shift‑left” testing and quality engineering principles. – Provide guidance, coaching, and mentorship to QA & Test team members. – Foster and promote a collaborative, high‑performing QA culture within the IT organization. ### Collaboration & Continuous Improvement – Participate in Agile ceremonies (backlog refinement, sprint planning, retrospectives, etc.). – Identify opportunities for test automation and process optimization. – Partner with QA Engineers and development teams to expand automated test coverage. – Champion the adoption of testing automation solutions. – Perform all other miscellaneous responsibilities and duties as assigned or directed. — #LI-Hybrid Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council!
