item.title: Government Relations and Political Engagement Specialist
item.description: Government Relations and Political Engagement Specialist Organization: Booz Allen Hamilton Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/14/2026 ## Remote Work: Hybrid ## Job Number: R0246888 ## Location: Washington, DC, US — # Government Relations and Political Engagement Specialist At Booz Allen, our Government Relations team serves as a strategic partner to the business by advancing the company’s public policy priorities, strengthening relationships with policymakers, and fostering trusted engagement across the political ecosystem. This unique position sits at the intersection of government relations, political engagement, operations, and strategic stakeholder management. Partnering closely with the Director of Strategic Engagement and the Booz Allen PAC Director, you will help execute enterprise-wide initiatives that enhance the company’s visibility, credibility, influence, and access among policymakers, industry leaders, and key external stakeholders. We’re looking for a highly organized, politically savvy, and collaborative professional who thrives in a fast-paced environment, excels at managing multiple priorities, and enjoys turning strategy into execution. — ## What You’ll Do – **Government relations strategy** — Support the development and execution of Booz Allen’s federal government relations and political engagement strategies in alignment with enterprise priorities. – **Policy and stakeholder research** — Conduct policy, stakeholder, and political research to develop concise executive briefing materials, talking points, and strategic communications. – **Project planning** — Lead project planning and operational execution for strategic Government Relations initiatives, ensuring effective coordination across workstreams, timelines, and stakeholders. – **Executive engagement coordination** — Coordinate executive engagements with external stakeholders, including scheduling, briefing preparation, logistics, and follow-up. – **Congressional engagement support** — Support planning surrounding congressional hearings, executive testimony, advocacy campaigns, and other high-profile government engagement activities. – **Operational excellence** — Drive operational excellence by maintaining project tracking systems, knowledge management resources, and internal communications that enhance team effectiveness. – **Team operations** — Coordinate team operations, including vendor onboarding, procurement activities, invoice processing, and administrative support. – **PAC administration** — Support day-to-day administration of the Booz Allen Political Action Committee (PAC), including fundraising initiatives, contribution processing, disbursements, and governance activities. – **PAC communications** — Develop communications and educational initiatives that increase employee awareness and participation in the PAC. – **Compliance partnership** — Partner with Legal, Ethics, Finance, and external vendors to ensure compliance with campaign finance laws, lobbying disclosure requirements, corporate political activity policies, and applicable ethics regulations. – **Political disclosure reporting** — Enhance political disclosure reporting through improved data management, reporting processes, and documentation. – **Compliance risk identification** — Identify compliance risks proactively while promoting a culture of integrity, transparency, and responsible political engagement. – **Stakeholder relationship building** — Foster strong working relationships with internal business leaders, trade associations, advocacy organizations, and external lobbying firms. – **Third‑party engagement** — Coordinate third-party engagement strategies and evaluate external partnerships to maximize advocacy and reputation effectiveness. – **Event logistics** — Manage logistics for high-impact events, including political fundraisers, thought leadership forums, executive engagements, and facility visits. — ## You Have – 5+ years of experience in government relations, political engagement, public policy, political compliance, or congressional affairs – Experience managing complex projects from planning through execution while balancing multiple competing priorities – Experience with Microsoft Office, including PowerPoint and Excel – Knowledge of federal election law, FEC regulations, lobbying disclosure requirements, corporate political activity, and PAC governance – Ability to display exceptional attention to detail and follow-through – Ability to exercise sound judgment while handling confidential and politically sensitive information – Ability to build productive relationships across business functions and with external stakeholders – Bachelor’s degree — ## Nice If You Have – Experience administering a corporate Political Action Committee (PAC) – Experience with federal election law, FEC regulations, lobbying compliance, and corporate PAC governance – Experience supporting executive leaders and preparing briefing materials – Knowledge of government relations tracking platforms and political intelligence tools – Possession of excellent organizational skills – Possession of excellent verbal and written communication skills, with a clear and persuasive style — ## Compensation At Booz Allen, we celebrate your contributions, provide you with opportunities and choices, and support your total well-being. Offerings include health, life, disability, financial, and retirement benefits, paid leave, professional development, tuition assistance, work-life programs, and dependent care. Full-time and part-time employees working at least 20 hours per week are eligible for benefits. Others may be eligible only for select offerings. Salary is determined by location, education, skills, experience, and contract-specific requirements. **Projected compensation range:** $86,800.00 – $198,000.00 (annualized USD). This posting will close within 90 days from the Posting Date. — ## Identity Statement As part of the hiring process, candidates must complete an identity verification process using advanced biometrics and AI. You are expected to be on camera during interviews and assessments. Booz Allen may take your picture to verify identity and prevent fraud. — ## Candidate AI Usage Policy AI is part of daily work at Booz Allen, but candidates must complete interviews using their own skills and knowledge. Use of AI tools during interviews is prohibited unless explicitly permitted. — ## Work Model Our people-first culture prioritizes collaboration, whether in person or virtual. **Remote:** May require occasional in-person work at a Booz Allen or customer facility. **Hybrid:** Frequent work from a Booz Allen facility based on leadership expectations and role needs; may require customer site visits. **Onsite:** Work primarily performed at a Booz Allen office or customer facility. — ## Commitment to Non-Discrimination All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to disability, protected veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, local, or international law. item.title: Government Relations Senior Specialist
item.description: Government Relations Senior Specialist Organization: American Honda Motor Co., Inc. Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/14/2026 ## Job Purpose The **State Affairs Specialist** supports Honda’s business objectives by monitoring, analyzing, and communicating state‑level policy developments, and by advancing Honda’s public policy priorities through informed advocacy, analysis, and stakeholder engagement. ## Key Accountabilities – **Legislation Monitoring** — Monitor, read, analyze, and track state legislation, regulations, and political activities to assess potential impacts, risks, and opportunities for Honda’s business operations and public policy objectives. – **Political Trend Analysis** — Identify and share political trends and analysis on select issues with key GIR leadership, business units, and internal stakeholders. – **Strategy Support** — Support development and execution of state government affairs strategies by contributing research, policy analysis, proposed positions, and supporting materials aligned with Honda’s advocacy priorities. – **Legislative Engagement** — Engage directly with state legislators, legislative staff, and government officials to communicate Honda’s public policy positions, educate policymakers on Honda initiatives, and serve as a point of contact on state‑level issues. – **Stakeholder Coordination** — Coordinate with trade associations, coalitions, and industry partners to share Honda’s policy positions and support advocacy efforts aligned with Honda’s objectives. – **Cross‑Functional Collaboration** — Collaborate with GIR leadership, Legal, Compliance, Policy Communications, and business unit subject matter experts to ensure accurate interpretation of legislation and consistency of messaging. – **Research & Briefings** — Conduct research, prepare briefings, and support special projects, task forces, or cross‑functional initiatives related to state government affairs as assigned. ## Qualifications, Experience, and Skills – Four‑year college degree in Government, Business, Journalism, Communications, Public Policy, Pre‑law, or a related field. – Five plus years of experience working in state or local government affairs, public policy, legislative tracking, trade associations, government offices, lobbying firms, legal analysis, or related political or regulatory environments. – Demonstrated ability to read, analyze, and interpret legislation and regulatory language. – Strong understanding of state‑level legislative and political processes. – Ability to communicate complex policy impacts clearly and concisely, both verbally and in writing. – Strong analytical, organizational, and project management skills. – High attention to detail and accuracy. – Ability to work collaboratively across functions and adapt to changing priorities. – Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications. ## What Differentiates Honda and Makes Us an Employer of Choice? ### Total Rewards – Competitive Base Salary (pay will be based on several variables including geographic location, work experience, etc.) – Paid Overtime – Regional Bonus (when applicable) – Industry‑leading Benefit Plans (Medical, Dental, Vision, Rx) – Paid time off, including vacation, holidays, shutdown – Company‑paid Short‑Term and Long‑Term Disability – 401K Plan with company match + additional contribution – Relocation assistance (if eligible) ### Career Growth – Advancement Opportunities – Career Mobility – Education Reimbursement for Continued Learning – Training and Development Programs ### Additional Offerings – Tuition Assistance & Student Loan Repayment – Lifestyle Account – Childcare Reimbursement Account – Elder Care Support – Wellbeing Program – Community Service and Engagement Programs – Product Programs — Honda is an equal opportunity employer and considers qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected factor. item.title: Congressional Affairs Analyst
item.description: Congressional Affairs Analyst Organization: SAIC Location: Alexandria, VA Date Posted: 08/14/2026 ## Job Description ### Description SAIC is searching for a dynamic Congressional Analyst with an active Top Secret clearance to join the team supporting the Office of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering (OUSW(R&E)). This pivotal role sits at the center of an organization driving the development of groundbreaking capabilities for the Department of War (DOW), advancing innovation, and safeguarding the nation’s technological advantage. This position offers a unique opportunity to contribute to an organization and mission shaping the future of DOW technology. Your work will help ensure OUSW(R&E) remains at the forefront of innovation while navigating the complex landscape of congressional interactions with professionalism and strategic insight. The role is located at the Mark Center in Alexandria, VA. “The expected salary range for this position is $120,000 – $150,000, based on the candidate’s experience and qualifications.” ### Job Responsibilities Manage congressional workflow and tasking systems, including the Congressional Hearings and Reporting Requirements Tracking System (CHARRTS), Office of Legislative Counsel (OLC) Web, DOW Congressional Tracking System, and CATMS database. Provide multifunctional administrative support, including analysis, filing, support activities, task management, briefing management, and management of special congressional workflows. Coordinate legislative activities within OUSW(R&E), ensuring alignment across the enterprise. Handle congressional reporting for OUSW(R&E), analyzing legislative material, coordinating tasking and workflow, arbitrating disputes, and working with OSW(LA) and BAA. Create and maintain workflow, reporting, and analysis documents, track deadlines, and issue guidance. Manage special inter‑Department projects, coordinating with OSD(LA), OGC, and OLC on task groups and processes. Collate and refine OUSW(R&E) reports, manage groups, and strategize to meet congressional requirements. Analyze inquiries and responses, manage correspondence, track follow‑up actions, and provide document retrieval services. Assemble information, maintain files, and coordinate responses to congressional and DoW staff inquiries. Perform general administrative duties, including coordinating security clearances, processing badge requests, tracking FOIA requests, and assisting with Pentagon parking for congressional visitors. Respond to congressional inquiries, coordinate responses, and maintain a database of inquiries and responses. Document congressional reports and analysis, summarizing official program information as required by DoW or federal directives. ### Qualifications #### Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree and at least 6 to 10 years or more of related experience; Master’s degree and eight (8) years or more experience; PhD or JD and five (5) years or more experience. At least 2 years of legislative systems management experience within the DOW. Strong problem identification and resolution skills, flexibility, initiative, and a proven ability to work efficiently and effectively with Senior Executives. Active TS clearance required to start; ability to obtain a TS/SCI clearance required to maintain employment. #### Desired Qualifications Experience in congressional briefing management and direct congressional staff interaction and support as a DOW representative. Prior experience supporting an OSW principal (USW, ASW, PDASW). Target salary range: $120,001 – $160,000. The estimate displayed represents the typical salary range for this position based on experience and other factors. ### Overview SAIC accepts applications on an ongoing basis and there is no deadline. SAIC® is a premier mission integrator focused on advancing the power of technology and innovation to serve and protect the world. Its robust portfolio across defense, space, intelligence, and civilian markets includes secure high‑end solutions in mission IT, enterprise IT, engineering services, and professional services. SAIC integrates emerging technology rapidly and securely into mission‑critical operations that modernize and enable essential national imperatives. SAIC employs approximately 23,000 professionals, driven by mission, united by purpose, and inspired by opportunity. Headquartered in Reston, Virginia, SAIC has annual revenues of approximately $7.3 billion. For more information, visit saic.com. For ongoing news, please visit the newsroom. item.description: Manager, Energy Policy, US East , AWS Public Policy Organization: Amazon Location: Arlington, VA Date Posted: 08/14/2026 ## Description The AWS Public Policy team is paving the way for the future of data center power supply and industry‑leading carbon‑free energy procurement through engagement with policymakers, grid operators, and other stakeholders. Amazon is looking for a talented policy professional who is innovative and well‑connected to represent AWS before state policymakers on energy and infrastructure policy. You will need to have a deep understanding of the energy policy industry, especially energy regulatory, legislative, and wholesale electric market policy related to issues faced by large electricity buyers and customers in the eastern United States, especially Virginia, and throughout the PJM region. You have a passion for shaping grid policy in statehouses and before utility regulators throughout the eastern US, and you’re excited to contribute to team efforts on related issues at the federal level. ## Key job responsibilities – Develop and execute advocacy strategies that support AWS energy policy priorities. – Engage relevant government entities such as the Virginia State Corporation Commission, PJM, state legislative committees of jurisdiction, state utility regulators, and other energy industry stakeholders throughout the eastern United States. – Work with internal and external stakeholders and experts to identify opportunities and risks arising from policy and regulatory development. – Facilitate meetings between AWS and key stakeholders, including senior government officials, regulators, industry associations, and alliance partners to promote AWS advocacy positions. – Craft and contribute to policy submissions and engage in consultations with relevant regulators. – Contribute to advocacy efforts within AWS including coordinating and developing public policy collateral such as policy position papers and talking points. – Provide expert advice to internal business partners and assist them in developing their respective business strategies. ## Basic Qualifications – Bachelor’s degree in a relevant discipline (e.g., Law, Political Science, Public Policy, Public Affairs, Economic Development) – 8+ years of relevant public policy and advocacy experience – Demonstrated expertise in policy research and strategy development – The ability to travel based on business need ## Preferred Qualifications – Master’s degree or above in a relevant discipline (e.g., Law, Political Science, Public Policy, Public Affairs, Economic Development) – Experience with written and verbal communication and presentation – Experience working effectively across cross‑functional teams and partnering well with people at all levels within an organization – Experience building and cultivating relationships with internal and external stakeholders – Experience leading energy policy initiatives in Virginia, PJM, within PJM states, and other eastern US regions – Experience representing an energy company, working as or for a policymaker and/or regulator on energy issues, or representing an energy trade association – Demonstrated ability to effectively and comfortably interact at highest corporate, federal, state, and local government levels – Familiarity with environmental policy, water infrastructure, and climate issues Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit [https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations] for more information. If the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your Recruiting Partner. The base salary range for this position is listed below. Your Amazon package will include sign‑on payments and restricted stock units (RSUs). Final compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, and location. Amazon also offers comprehensive benefits including health insurance (medical, dental, vision, prescription, Basic Life & AD&D insurance and option for Supplemental life plans, EAP, Mental Health Support, Medical Advice Line, Flexible Spending Accounts, Adoption and Surrogacy Reimbursement coverage), 401(k) matching, paid time off, and parental leave. item.title: Policy & Regulatory Affairs Manager
item.description: Policy & Regulatory Affairs Manager Organization: Emerald AI Location: Washington, DC | San Francisco, CA | Boston, MA Date Posted: 08/14/2026 ## About Emerald AI We’re at a pivotal moment for AI and energy. Demand for compute is skyrocketing, but power constraints are becoming a critical bottleneck. Emerald AI sits at the intersection of these two worlds, enabling AI data centers to scale without overwhelming the grid. Our Emerald Conductor software platform makes data centers flexible and responsive, allowing them to adjust power usage dynamically. This unlocks massive AI growth without major new infrastructure, while also strengthening the grid and supporting the expansion of renewable energy. We’re a team of experts across AI, cloud, software, and energy—on a mission to scale AI sustainably. We’re backed by leading investors and partners including Radical Ventures and NVIDIA. Learn more about our vision, team, and backers at [https://www.emeraldai.co/]. — ## About the Role We’re looking for a Policy & Regulatory Affairs Manager to help shape and execute our policy and regulatory strategy at a critical moment of growth. As demand accelerates and regulatory landscapes evolve, this role will be instrumental in ensuring we can scale effectively while navigating complex policy environments. You’ll help translate external regulatory developments into clear, actionable insights that inform company strategy. You’ll play a key role in identifying risks and opportunities, shaping our policy positions, and ensuring alignment between our business objectives and the broader regulatory context. You’ll work closely with legal, product, operations, and leadership teams, as well as external stakeholders including regulators, policymakers, and industry groups. This role requires a high degree of ownership and judgment — you’ll be expected to operate independently, prioritize effectively in a fast-moving environment, and influence decisions across the organization. — ## Key Responsibilities Monitor and analyze policy developments across relevant jurisdictions (e.g., energy, infrastructure, AI, or technology policy) Translate regulatory changes into business impact, providing clear recommendations to internal stakeholders Support policy strategy development, including identifying risks, opportunities, and engagement priorities Draft policy materials, including briefing notes, consultation responses, position papers, and executive memos Engage with external stakeholders, including regulators, policymakers, industry associations, and partners Coordinate cross-functional alignment with legal, product, operations, and leadership teams Support advocacy efforts, including meetings, submissions, and public-facing initiatives — ## Minimum Requirements 5+ years of experience in public policy, government, regulatory affairs, or a related field (e.g., government agency, consultancy, think tank, or in-house) Strong understanding of regulatory processes and stakeholder landscapes Excellent written and verbal communication skills; able to distill complex issues clearly and concisely Experience drafting policy documents or engaging in regulatory processes Comfortable operating in ambiguity and a fast-paced environment Proven ability to work cross-functionally and influence without authority Experience in relevant sectors to Emerald AI (e.g., energy, infrastructure, AI/tech) — ## Preferred Requirements Experience working with or before state Public Utility Commissions and/or the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Experience working with or before Independent System Operators/Regional Transmission Organizations (ISO/RTOs) (e.g., PJM, ERCOT) Experience engaging directly before regulators or government officials Experience at a high-growth company or scaling organization — ## What We Offer Make an impact. Solve the AI power bottleneck and shape how data centers scale sustainably. Join a world-class team of AI, cloud, software, and energy experts in a collaborative, low-ego environment. Build from 0→1. Influence strategy, GTM, org design, and customer/investor engagement from day one. Competitive pay + equity. Stock options let you share in the value you help create. Comprehensive benefits, including medical, dental, vision, and 401(k) matching. Flexible location. Work from D.C., Boston, or the Bay Area, with 2 WFH days/week. Backed by top investors, including Radical Ventures and NVIDIA. We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability, and any other protected ground of discrimination under applicable human rights legislation. Emerald AI strives to respect the dignity and independence of people with disabilities and is committed to giving them the same opportunity to succeed as all other employees. Inclusiveness is core to our culture at Emerald AI, and we strive to ensure you get the most from your interview experience. Emerald AI makes reasonable accommodations for applicants with disabilities. If a reasonable accommodation is needed to participate in the job application or interview process, please reach out to the Talent team. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Officer, Government Relations (Strategic Initiatives)
item.description: Officer, Government Relations (Strategic Initiatives) Organization: Pew Charitable Trusts Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/14/2026 ## **Officer, Government Relations** ### **Government Relations** Government Relations (GR) seeks to advance Pew’s nonpartisan policy and research goals at all levels of government, in the United States and internationally. GR focuses on sharing the organization’s research and fact‑based recommendations, shaping pragmatic strategies to achieve program objectives, and building relationships with key government officials to forge compromise and consensus on issues that make a difference to the public. — ## **Position Overview** The officer, government relations will report to the senior vice president (SVP), GR and assist the SVP in preparing policy, legislative, and political research; drafting briefing memos; preparing presentations; and coordinating with Pew’s programmatic staff. The position will lead collaboration on various internal‑ and external‑facing initiatives and must have the substantive and political judgment to identify problems, recommend solutions, and spearhead execution. The officer will also partner with the SVP and the GR senior director for strategy and operations to support external and internal relationship‑ and team‑building initiatives, including those designed to advance nonpartisanship on Capitol Hill and among state lawmakers. In addition, they will represent GR at internal meetings designed to further collaboration among and the efficacy of Pew’s programmatic and GR teams. When time allows, the position will support the GR senior director for environment and the GR senior director for government performance and their teams as they work to advance Pew’s policy objectives at the local, federal, and international level. This position is based in Pew’s Washington, DC office and will participate in Pew’s hybrid work program with core days in the office and flexibility to telework the remaining days. Staff also enjoy four telework “flex weeks” per year. — ## **Responsibilities** – Provide public policy and political guidance, analysis, and recommendations to the SVP and collaborate with the SVP to ensure efficient and effective use of time and substantive resources. – Partner with the SVP to prioritize internal and external initiatives and represent the SVP at key internal meetings. – Use sound judgment to independently review and evaluate the policy and political aspects of documents and issues. Review and edit documents for substantive accuracy and consistency with Pew editorial style. – Provide substantive research for the SVP on Pew’s broad‑based public policy and civic engagement initiatives, focusing on policy, legislative, and political issues. Draft memos and briefing documents that prepare the SVP and GR team members for meetings with international, federal, state, and local lawmakers and for internal meetings with programmatic staff. – Prepare PowerPoint presentations, draft talking points, and overview materials for the SVP for external and internal presentations and high‑level meetings. – Gain a general understanding of Pew’s policy, legislative, regulatory, and technical assistance strategies and tactics. – Spearhead and project manage various special projects for the SVP and GR team. – Develop an understanding of the international, federal, and state political and policy environment in which the GR team is working to advance Pew’s policy goals. – Occasionally provide similar research, writing, and monitoring support for other senior members of the GR team. — ## **Requirements** – Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience. A juris doctor, master of public policy, or similar advanced degree preferred. – Generally eight (8) years of professional experience. – Strong knowledge of various substantive international and domestic public policy issues and associated political realities. Curiosity and capacity to quickly familiarize oneself with emerging policy/political issues. – Excellent policy and legislative research skills. – Independent political judgment aligned with Pew’s nonpartisan values and mission. – Excellent writing skills and experience summarizing complex policy and political issues into cogent memos and briefing documents. Ability to edit complex policy documents for substance and consistency with Pew’s editorial style. – Experience working in government relations, public‑policy communications, federal or state campaigns, and/or policy advocacy. Direct experience with international, federal, or state government preferred. – Experience working in a multifaceted, matrixed organization with numerous simultaneous objectives and initiatives. – Genuine curiosity and excitement to engage in relationship‑ and team‑building projects. Must be a true team player. – Experience handling confidential information appropriately and exercising sound discretion. – Excellent time and project management skills; flexible and able to juggle multiple priorities while remaining attentive to detail. – Experience working independently and responsibly when given latitude to prioritize and structure work. Ability to anticipate the needs of the SVP and GR team. – Strong PowerPoint skills. Experience with CRM systems such as Salesforce and business intelligence tools is a plus. – Prior to commencing employment, candidates previously registered to lobby in any jurisdiction must certify termination of registration(s) and provide copies of termination notices to Pew. — ## **Travel** Minimal travel anticipated. — ## **Work Authorization** Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the country for which they are seeking employment without visa sponsorship. — ## **Salary Range** **United States Pay Range:** $121,700 – $136,000 The salary range represents a reasonable estimate based on Pew’s commitment to equitable and market‑competitive pay. Actual salary will consider job‑related knowledge, skills, experience, internal equity, and business need. — ## **Total Rewards** Pew offers a competitive salary and benefits program, including comprehensive and affordable medical, dental, and vision coverage; life and disability insurance; health savings and flexible spending accounts; retirement benefits; and work/life benefits to maintain balance. Pew is an equal opportunity employer and makes employment decisions without regard to race, ethnicity, gender, or any other protected characteristics. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Grassroots Specialist
item.description: Grassroots Specialist Organization: American Academy of Ophthalmology (AAO) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/14/2026 ## About Us The American Academy of Ophthalmology (AAO) is the world’s largest association of eye physicians and surgeons, dedicated to protecting sight and empowering lives by advancing the profession of ophthalmology. Through education, advocacy, and innovation, the Academy supports ophthalmologists worldwide in delivering the highest-quality eye care. Our Annual Meeting is one of the largest medical gatherings in the United States, bringing together thousands of physicians, researchers, and industry leaders from around the globe. At AAO, employees contribute to meaningful work that directly impacts physician education and patient outcomes worldwide. ## Position Summary The Grassroots Specialist works with the Director of Congressional Affairs to plan and implement the Academy’s federal grassroots advocacy program in support of legislative and regulatory priorities. This role engages Academy members in year-round advocacy, strengthens relationships with lawmakers and partner organizations, develops grassroots campaigns and communications, and coordinates key advocacy events that help maintain a strong Academy presence on Capitol Hill. ## Key Responsibilities ### Congressional Advocacy & Member Engagement – Manage the Academy’s federal grassroots advocacy program and develop tools that help Congressional Advocates build relationships with federal and state lawmakers. – Engage advocates in year-round advocacy, encourage participation in the Mid-Year Forum, and support involvement with OPHTHPAC. – Provide one-on-one assistance to Congressional Advocates and help leverage member relationships in support of the Academy’s legislative goals. – Support recruitment and retention of Congressional Advocates in partnership with OPHTHPAC Committee members. – Identify local advocacy opportunities, including in-district meetings, town halls, and fundraisers. ### Grassroots Campaigns & Program Operations – Develop short- and long-range grassroots campaigns that advance the Academy’s legislative and regulatory agendas. – Create strategies and tools that engage members of the ophthalmic community in advocacy action. – Identify and manage technology solutions that improve grassroots program efficiency and effectiveness. – Analyze engagement trends and data, maintain grassroots databases and spreadsheets, and target member segments to increase response rates. – Oversee planning, logistics, and execution for Congressional Advocacy Day and other targeted fly-in events. ### Advocacy Meetings, PAC Support & Communications – Support the Ophthalmic Leadership Advocacy Group annual meeting, including agenda development, speaker invitations, attendance outreach, meeting materials, facility coordination, and post-meeting evaluations. – Work with the OPHTHPAC Manager, Committee members, and federal advocacy coordinators to support fundraisers, political events, committee meetings, retreats, and coordinated PAC and grassroots activities. – Partner with the communications team to develop advocacy emails, action alerts, social media, videos, website content, and articles for Academy publications. – Maintain advocacy web content, including the online action center and legislative resource pages. ### Coalition Building & External Partnerships – Cultivate relationships with health, disease, patient, consumer, pediatric, state, and specialty organizations that align with Academy priorities. – Support state governmental affairs staff with grassroots campaigns and advocacy outreach. – Identify opportunities for state and subspecialty ophthalmic societies to engage in federal advocacy. – Identify potential coalitions, help incorporate Academy priorities into partner advocacy efforts, and attend outside meetings as appropriate. ## Qualifications, Skills, and Education Requirements – Bachelor’s degree in political science or an equivalent field. – Two to three years of related experience in grassroots advocacy or government affairs; Capitol Hill or association/government relations experience is preferred. – Knowledge of the legislative process, Capitol Hill, and grassroots advocacy. – Strong interpersonal, relationship-building, organizational, and project management skills with excellent attention to detail. – Strong database-management skills and experience with grassroots software programs. – Proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and internet research. – Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to create advocacy materials for multiple formats and audiences. – Ability to manage multiple high-priority projects, use sound judgment, solve problems creatively, and handle confidential information. ## Work Environment and Travel This position is based in Washington, D.C. and follows a hybrid schedule with 3 days work time in the office. Travel is required for the Academy’s Annual Meeting and other meetings, totaling approximately 7–10 days annually. ## Additional Requirements – Ability to lift up to 35 pounds. – Ability to travel approximately 6–12 days annually. – Eligibility for up to two remote days per week with manager approval. ## Compensation and Benefits Salary: $102,824 annually This position includes a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, and vision coverage, HSA/FSA options, commuter benefits, life and disability insurance, employee assistance programs, wellness initiatives, and additional employee perks. item.title: Manager, State Governmental Affairs
item.description: Manager, State Governmental Affairs Organization: American Academy of Ophthalmology (AAO) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/14/2026 ## About Us The American Academy of Ophthalmology (AAO) is the world’s largest association of eye physicians and surgeons, dedicated to advancing the lifelong learning and professional interests of the ophthalmic community. Our Annual Meeting is one of the largest medical gatherings in the U.S., drawing attendees from around the globe. ## Position Summary The Manager, State Governmental Affairs supports the development and implementation of state legislative, regulatory, and public affairs strategies that advance the Academy’s advocacy priorities. The role develops and maintains relationships with state ophthalmology societies, lobbyists and consultants, medical organizations, policymakers, and other stakeholders, while analyzing state policy developments and helping implement advocacy strategies that support patient access to high-quality physician-led eye care. The Manager also uses data analytics, artificial intelligence, and emerging advocacy technologies to strengthen legislative monitoring, stakeholder engagement, communications, strategic planning, and operational effectiveness. This position supports one of the Academy’s core priorities by advancing state advocacy initiatives that promote patient safety, preserve access to high-quality eye care, and protect the ability of ophthalmologists to provide comprehensive medical and surgical eye care. ## Role and Responsibilities ### 1. State Advocacy and Public Affairs Strategy Support the development and execution of legislative, regulatory, and advocacy strategies that advance Academy priorities and respond to emerging public policy challenges. Conduct legislative and regulatory analysis and prepare policy briefs, issue papers, presentations, and testimony. Draft legislation, amendments, comments, and other policy-related materials. Develop advocacy resources, including fact sheets, talking points, issue briefs, and stakeholder communications for physician leaders, lobbyists, policymakers, media, patients, and the public. Build, manage, and maintain grassroots advocacy networks that support state ophthalmology policy objectives. Coordinate ongoing communications with state society executive directors, physician leadership, and contract lobbying and consulting teams. Coordinate coalition-building efforts within the medical community and among consumer, patient, and stakeholder organizations with shared healthcare policy interests. Develop and implement digital, social media, earned media, and artificial intelligence-enabled strategies that support the Academy’s state advocacy agenda. Monitor legislative, political, and regulatory developments and recommend advocacy opportunities and responses to emerging challenges. Provide support to state advocacy fundraising initiatives as needed. ### 2. Proactive State Advocacy Programs Support the development, implementation, and advancement of Academy and State Governmental Affairs programs designed to promote patient safety, improve access to care, and strengthen the practice environment for ophthalmology through the Quality Eye Care Program for the States. Support pediatric vision care initiatives. Support topical drug waste reduction initiatives. Support early eye drop prescription initiatives. Help advance additional proactive public policy initiatives that promote patient care and elevate the value of the ophthalmology profession. ### 3. Internal Member Communications Collaborate with the Advocacy Communications Manager to educate and engage Academy members regarding state advocacy priorities, legislative developments, and opportunities for political involvement. Develop content for Academy communications vehicles, including the Washington Report Express, action alerts, advocacy updates, website content, and member engagement campaigns. ### 4. State and Federal Policy Coordination When appropriate, collaborate with federal affairs staff to develop coordinated strategies on issues with both state and federal policy implications, including scope of practice, Veterans Health Administration initiatives, telehealth and technology issues, and online vision care policies. Share policy intelligence and coordinate advocacy activities to support alignment between state and federal initiatives. ## Qualifications, Skills, and Education Requirements ### Government Affairs and Political Expertise Strong understanding of state and federal legislative, regulatory, and political processes. Experience developing and implementing state-level government affairs, lobbying, and public policy strategies. Experience managing and coordinating contract lobbyists, public affairs consultants, political strategists, and coalition partners across multiple states. Knowledge of policy development, political dynamics, and factors influencing legislative and regulatory decision-making. Experience using artificial intelligence and data-driven tools for legislative monitoring, policy research, stakeholder analysis, advocacy planning, and political intelligence. Understanding of political campaign and fundraising environments and their impact on public policy and advocacy efforts. ### Public Affairs and Strategic Outreach Experience developing and implementing public affairs, grassroots advocacy, and stakeholder engagement campaigns using traditional, digital, social media, and emerging communications platforms. Experience managing external communications firms, media consultants, digital strategists, and other vendors in support of advocacy and legislative objectives. Strong content development, messaging, and communications skills, including advocacy-oriented materials and multimedia content. Ability to translate complex policy issues into clear, compelling messages for policymakers, stakeholders, media, members, and the public. ### Project Management, Communication, and Analysis Ability to manage multiple teams of lobbyists, consultants, state society executives, coalition partners, and other stakeholders in a collaborative, matrixed environment. Strong strategic thinking and political judgment, with the ability to identify opportunities and help implement effective advocacy initiatives. Demonstrated ability to analyze and communicate legislative, regulatory, policy, and business issues through presentations, reports, briefing materials, and stakeholder communications. Proficiency in Microsoft 365 applications, including PowerPoint, Excel, Word, Teams, and SharePoint, and experience using CRM, membership management, stakeholder engagement, advocacy, legislative tracking, or constituent relationship management systems. Experience managing project budgets, contracts, vendors, and other resources associated with government affairs and advocacy programs. Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, with strong coalition-building and relationship-management abilities. Strong research and analytical skills, including proficiency with legislative tracking systems, electronic databases, data analytics, and artificial intelligence-enabled research tools. Ability to manage competing priorities, work independently, exercise sound judgment, and deliver high-quality results under tight deadlines. ## Education Minimum bachelor’s degree required. Advanced degree or equivalent experience preferred. ## Work Environment and Travel This position is based in Washington, D.C. and follows a hybrid schedule with 3 days work time in the office. Travel is required for the Academy’s Annual Meeting and other meetings, totaling approximately 7 to 10 days annually. ## Additional Requirements Ability to lift up to 35 pounds. Ability to travel approximately 6–12 days annually. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Congressional Affairs Strategist – National Capital Regional
item.description: Congressional Affairs Strategist – National Capital Regional Organization: Serco Location: WashingtonDC | Alexandria, VA | Arlington, VA | Andrews AFB, MD | Fairfax, VA | McLean, VA | Silver Spring, MD | Quantico, VA | Columbia, MD | Rockville, MD Date Posted: 08/14/2026 # Position Description & Qualifications If you seek a rewarding, high-profile, and challenging position supporting projects for the U.S. Navy, Serco has a great opportunity for you! This position will be on a dynamic team supporting Team Submarine. Bring your expertise and collaborative skills to make an impact on military defense and the safety of our sailors. The ability to obtain/maintain/transfer a U.S. Department of War (DoW) SECRET security clearance. — ## Program Overview Team Submarine’s Submarine Program Offices are responsible for: – The acquisition of COLUMBIA Class Submarines, including R&D, design, construction, Test and Evaluation (T&E), and Live Fire Test and Evaluation (LFT&E). This program is a major defense acquisition effort with significant Congressional and OSD visibility. – The acquisition of VIRGINIA Class Submarines, including lifecycle management, T&E, LFT&E, and Fleet introduction, with an estimated lifecycle cost of ~$336B. – The SSN(X) program, responsible for next-generation fast attack submarine design and acquisition, emphasizing speed, stealth, payload capacity, and operational endurance. Serco supports the U.S. Navy as a prime contractor for the Submarine Industrial Base, unifying submarine and surface vessel industrial activities to eliminate inefficiencies and improve coordination across acquisition, sustainment, and maintenance communities. If you are passionate about identifying cutting-edge solutions, bridging strategic gaps between government and industry, and advancing national defense capabilities through advanced manufacturing, SERCO has a high-impact opportunity for you. As the Congressional Affairs Strategist supporting the U.S. Navy’s Submarine Industrial Base (SIB), you will serve as a trusted advisor and support to the SIB Program Office in the analysis and strategic planning of shipyard infrastructure initiatives across the Navy’s submarine industrial base, with a focus on the adaptation and integration of Advanced Manufacturing Technologies. This position will be leading the development, coordination, and analysis of legislative and policy initiatives that advance submarine industrial base priorities. This position will be a hybrid as you work from home and at the SIB office near the Washington Navy Yard, as well as traveling when required to support the mission. — ## In this role, you will: – The position involves direct engagement with maritime-focused federal agencies such as MARAD and the U.S. Coast Guard, as well as coordination with internal stakeholders to align policy strategies with industrial base objectives. – Own the planning, coordination, and tracking of strategic engagements across industry, partners, and internal stakeholders, plus develop and maintain a forward-looking engagement plan that aligns leadership priorities with key external touchpoints. – Coordinate across stakeholders to ensure engagements are well-planned, appropriately staffed, and aligned to program objectives. – Proactively recommend engagements, events, and touchpoints that support program goals and leadership priorities. – Maintain comprehensive visibility into engagement activities, including tracking meetings, conferences, partner interactions, and follow-up actions, as well as identifying gaps or opportunities for additional engagement. – Assess infrastructure capability and identify opportunities to modernize shipyard facilities in ways that enhance shipbuilding and repair capacity. – Serve as a key communicator, translating complex technical initiatives into compelling strategic narratives and decision briefings for Navy leadership, program offices, and industrial partners. – Support the creation of strategic messaging, briefings, and acquisition summaries for senior Navy leadership and industrial base policy stakeholders. – Work with multiple stakeholders across the region to expedite evaluation, determine critical areas, and assess how to fund SIB efforts that produce optimal return on investment. – Work with the SIB team, which is spread across the United States and focused on workforce development/marketing, supply chain/sustainment, and technology developments. – Provide senior-level briefings and progress updates to Navy leadership, including recommendations for targeted investments and risk mitigation actions. – Provide daily program, analytical, and acquisition management support to senior-level executives. – Draft information papers in response to Congressional inquiries. – Provide input to Report to Congress regarding SIB spend goals and associated return on investment. — ## To succeed in this role, you will have: – The ability to obtain/maintain/transfer a U.S. Department of War (DoW) SECRET security clearance. – U.S. Citizenship is required. – A Bachelor’s degree and two (2) years of experience. – A strong background in maritime policy, legislative affairs, and strategic engagement across both the executive and legislative branches. – Experience including authorship or advancement of federal legislation, familiarity with the legislative process, and demonstrated leadership in interagency policy development. – Prior service at a maritime agency or on Capitol Hill with a portfolio related to infrastructure, economic development, or national defense is highly desirable. – Skill in drafting policy papers, analyzing legislative text, preparing leadership briefings, and navigating complex stakeholder environments. – Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience preparing high-level decision briefs, strategic messaging products, and technology evaluations. – The ability to work independently in a high-tempo, mission-focused environment, managing competing priorities and emergent needs. – Strong organizational and problem-solving skills, with the ability to connect disparate technical and strategic information into clear, actionable insights. – Experience preparing and delivering high-stakes presentations and briefings to senior stakeholders. – Strong analytical, organizational, and project management skills with attention to detail and the ability to work independently. – Ability to travel (10%). — If you are interested in supporting and working with an enthusiastic Serco team, then submit your application now for immediate consideration – it only takes minutes to apply and could change your career! — ## Company Overview Serco Inc. (Serco) is the Americas division of Serco Group, plc. In North America, Serco’s 9,000+ employees strive to make an impact every day across 100+ sites in the areas of Defense, Citizen Services, and Transportation. We help our clients deliver vital services more efficiently while increasing the satisfaction of their end customers. Serco serves every branch of the U.S. military, numerous U.S. Federal civilian agencies, the Intelligence Community, the Canadian government, state, provincial and local governments, and commercial clients. Wherever you work and whatever you do, we invite you to discover your place in our world. To review Serco benefits please visit: [https://careers.serco-na.com/us/en/what-we-offer]. If you require an accommodation with the application process please email: [email protected] or call the HR Service Desk at 800-628-6458, option 1. Please note, due to EEOC/OFCCP compliance, Serco is unable to accept resumes by email. Candidates may be asked to present proof of identity during the selection process. If requested, this will require presentation of a government-issued I.D. (with photo) with name and address that match the information entered on the application. Serco will not take possession of or retain/store the information provided as proof of identity. For more information on how Serco uses your information, please see our Applicant Privacy Policy and Notice. Serco does not accept unsolicited resumes through or from search firms or staffing agencies without being a contracted approved vendor. All unsolicited resumes will be considered the property of Serco and will not be obligated to pay a placement or contract fee. If you are interested in becoming an approved vendor at Serco, please email [email protected] . Serco is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, and other legally protected characteristics. — ## Pay Transparency Our Total Rewards package includes competitive pay, performance-based incentives, and benefits that promote well-being and work-life balance. Eligible employees also gain access to a wide range of benefits from comprehensive health coverage and health savings accounts to retirement plans, life and disability insurance, and time-off programs. Salary range: The range for this position can be found at the top of this posting. Actual base salary will be determined by factors including scope of role, experience, job-related knowledge, education, training, key skills, and geographic market considerations. Benefits for full-time employees include: – Medical, dental, and vision insurance – Robust vacation and sick leave benefits – Flexible work arrangements where permitted – 401(k) plan with employer matching funds – Tuition reimbursement program – Life insurance and disability coverage – Optional coverages: pet insurance, home/auto insurance, additional life and accident insurance, critical illness insurance, group legal, ID theft protection – Birth, adoption, parental leave benefits – Employee Assistance Plan To review all Serco benefits please visit: [https://careers.serco-na.com/us/en/about-us]. Serco complies with all applicable state and local leave laws,

item.title: Manager, Federal Government Affairs
item.description: Manager, Federal Government Affairs Organization: Bosch USA Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/14/2026 ## Company Description We Are Bosch. At Bosch, we shape the future by inventing high‑quality technologies and services that spark enthusiasm and enrich people’s lives. Our areas of activity are every bit as diverse as our outstanding Bosch teams around the world. Their creativity is the key to innovation through connected living, mobility, or industry. Let’s grow together, enjoy more, and inspire each other. Work #LikeABosch Reinvent yourself: At Bosch, you will evolve. Discover new directions: At Bosch, you will find your place. Balance your life: At Bosch, your job matches your lifestyle. Celebrate success: At Bosch, we celebrate you. Be yourself: At Bosch, we value values. Shape tomorrow: At Bosch, you change lives. ## Job Description As the Manager of Federal Government Affairs, you will support Bosch’s public policy and government affairs efforts in the United States and help advance the company’s business priorities through strategic engagement with policymakers, regulators, industry stakeholders, and internal business leaders. This role is ideal for a motivated and intellectually curious professional who is eager to learn, build relationships, and help advance policy initiatives that support innovation, manufacturing, mobility, technology, and economic growth. Working as part of a highly collaborative and high‑performing team, you will shape and execute advocacy strategies that enable Bosch’s business to succeed in an evolving policy environment. You will join a fast‑paced, highly visible team that operates at the intersection of public policy, business strategy, and innovation. In this role, you will engage with policymakers, federal agencies, trade associations, coalition partners, and other key stakeholders to advance Bosch’s policy priorities and strengthen the company’s reputation as a trusted partner and thought leader. This position offers the opportunity to work across a broad portfolio of issues impacting Bosch’s businesses. You will monitor and analyze legislative and regulatory developments, assess potential business impacts, and help shape advocacy strategies that support the company’s objectives. Success in this role requires strong judgement, effective communication skills, attention to detail, and the ability to quickly learn and navigate complex policy issues. You will work closely with business leaders and subject matter experts to translate complex policy developments into actionable business insights and ensure alignment between policy priorities and business goals. The U.S. Government Affairs team is part of the company’s communications and government affairs organization and serves as a trusted advisor to company leadership on public policy matters. ## Key Responsibilities Support and implement comprehensive government affairs priorities to advance the company’s interests. Support advocacy efforts with Congress, federal agencies, and industry stakeholders on issues impacting Bosch’s business interests. Cultivate and maintain effective relationships with policymakers, government agencies, and industry associations to advance and protect the company’s business objectives and reputation. Monitor and analyze legislative trends and developments, providing timely insights and potential business impacts to internal audiences. Counsel, prepare, and support internal stakeholders to plan for and engage in government affairs work to support business and industry topics. Represent Bosch in industry associations, coalition meetings, and policy forums to help advance company priorities and build industry relationships. Develop expertise across a broad range of policy issues affecting Bosch, including mobility, technology, manufacturing, trade, energy, workforce, and innovation policy. Collaborate with cross‑functional teams to align government affairs priorities with business objectives. Represent the company as an effective, authoritative spokesperson at meetings, hearings, and industry events to effectively establish the company’s position on key matters. Strong knowledge of compliance laws related to advocacy and commitment to abiding by all requirements. ## Qualifications Bachelor’s Degree 5+ years of experience in government affairs, public policy, legislative affairs, congressional offices, federal agencies, trade associations, campaigns, or related roles. Demonstrated ability to quickly learn new policy issues and translate complex information into actionable business insights. Experience working in a collaborative, team‑oriented environment with a strong commitment to professionalism, integrity, and execution. Experience on Capitol Hill, within the Executive Branch, trade associations, or government affairs organizations is highly valued. Exceptional organizational and project management skills, including the ability to execute with speed, accuracy, efficiency, and attention to detail. Thorough understanding of federal legislative and regulatory processes and demonstrated ability to influence legislation and policy. Strong interest in the mobility and technology sectors, including emerging fields, sustainability, compliance, and safety. Success in building and maintaining effective relationships with government officials and industry stakeholders. Excellent communication, interpersonal, and presentation skills, with the ability to simplify and articulate complex issues verbally and through persuasive writing. Strategic thinking and problem‑solving abilities to navigate and influence policy environments. Effective time and project management abilities, including prioritization skills. Exhibit high personal integrity and ethics, aligned with the Bosch values and ethos. ## Who You Are Curious and eager to learn complex policy and business issues. A self‑starter who thrives in a fast‑paced and evolving environment. A collaborative team player who values trust, integrity, and accountability. Comfortable managing multiple priorities simultaneously while maintaining attention to detail. Effective at building relationships and working with diverse stakeholders. Interested in understanding how public policy impacts business, innovation, manufacturing, and technology. ## Additional Information We offer a competitive base salary for this position with a range in US‑Washington D.C. of $150,000–$160,000, along with an annual corporate bonus and a generous benefit package designed to reward sustained impact and contribution over time. Within the salary range, individual pay is determined based on several factors, including but not limited to work experience and job knowledge, complexity of the role, job location, etc. Your well‑being matters at Bosch! We offer a benefits package designed to empower you in every area of your life. This includes premium health coverage, a 401(k) with generous matching, resources for financial planning and goal setting, ample paid time off, parental leave, and comprehensive life and disability protection. Your Recruiter can share more details for this position during the interview process. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Lead Policy Analyst (Hybrid)
item.description: Lead Policy Analyst (Hybrid) Organization: American Medical Association (AMA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/14/2026 The American Medical Association (AMA) is the nation’s largest professional association of physicians and a non-profit organization. We are a unifying voice and powerful ally for America’s physicians, the patients they care for, and the promise of a healthier nation. To be part of the AMA is to be part of our mission to promote the art and science of medicine and the betterment of public health. At AMA, our mission to improve the health of the nation starts with our people. We foster an inclusive, people-first culture where every employee is empowered to perform at their best. Together, we advance meaningful change in health care and the communities we serve. We encourage and support professional development for our employees, and we are dedicated to social responsibility. We invite you to learn more about us and we look forward to getting to know you. We have an opportunity at our corporate offices in Washington D.C. for a Lead Policy Analyst (Hybrid) on our Digital Health & AI team. This is a hybrid position reporting into our Washington, DC office, requiring 3 days a week in the office. 25 Massachusetts Avenue, NW, Washington, DC 20001-7400 USA This role requires specialized depth and/or breadth of expertise in their job discipline or field. This role leads others to solve complex problems and works independently, with guidance in only the most complex situations. May lead functional teams or projects. — ## RESPONSIBILITIES ### AMA Policy Development and Research Develop and shape AMA policy positions on digital health and AI policy; recommend new policies and assist in the development of corresponding AMA strategies, policies and initiatives. Develop policy reports, reviews, position statements, comment letters, written testimonies, and presentation materials to influence the policy landscape. Analyze and prepare correspondence and briefing materials for Senior Management and AMA offices on key digital health and AI issues. Monitor state and federal legislative and regulatory digital health and AI developments and develop guidance for physicians on the implications of these developments. Create and contribute to new and updated educational and communications resources and events. ### Internal and External Relationships Collaborate with internal business units to foster and maintain effective relations with relevant entities, including Sections and Federation societies to advance shared priorities that align with the AMA position on issues related to digital health and AI. Collaborate with internal business units such as Advocacy, Enterprise Communications and Center for Optimal Health Outcomes to ensure consistent and appropriate messaging to stakeholders. Contribute to the planning and implementing convenings, briefings, conferences, and presentations related to digital health policies. Build and maintain external relationships including but not limited to medical specialty societies, industry stakeholders, and coalitions. Represent the AMA at external meetings as needed. Assist in the management of AMA coalitions. May include other responsibilities as assigned. — ## REQUIREMENTS Bachelor’s degree required; master’s degree strongly preferred. 7+ years of experience in healthcare policy analysis in an academic, government, corporate or non-profit setting required. Knowledge of digital health and AI trends in the healthcare industry required. Knowledge of data privacy and HIPAA highly preferred. Demonstrated ability to collaborate with diverse stakeholders and synthesize multiple viewpoints into actionable recommendations. Proven ability to conduct in-depth policy research and analysis, incorporate expert perspectives, and translate complex issues into clear, concise, and well-supported written materials for a variety of audiences. Strong project management and communication skills with experience leading or influencing multi-stakeholder deliberations. Proven analytical, evaluative, and critical thinking skills to build solid policy recommendations. Excellent interpersonal skills to develop and maintain internal and external relationships, including the ability to interface effectively with people of varying disciplines, backgrounds, and expertise. Polished speaking and presentation skills to externally represent the AMA at conferences and other events. Politically savvy. Some travel required. This role is an exempt position, and the salary range for this position is $109,866 – $145,344. This is the lowest to highest salary we believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s pay within the salary range will be determined by a variety of factors including but not limited to business consideration and geographical location, as well as candidate qualifications, such as skills, education, and experience. Employees are also eligible to participate in an incentive plan. The AMA offers competitive salaries, including an incentive plan and excellent benefits. Our office is a business casual environment, and we respect work-life balance. The American Medical Association is located near Union Station and the Capitol in Washington D.C. We are an equal opportunity employer, committed to diversity in our workforce. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment. As an EOE/AA employer, the American Medical Association will not discriminate in its employment practices due to an applicant’s race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity and veteran or disability status. **THE AMA IS COMMITTED TO IMPROVING THE HEALTH OF THE NATION** Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Chief External Affairs & Programs Officer (CEAPO)
item.description: Chief External Affairs & Programs Officer (CEAPO) Organization: Planned Parenthood of Greater New York (PPGNY) Location: Remote (NY) Date Posted: 08/14/2026 ## RECRUITMENT PROFILE **Title:** Chief External Affairs & Programs Officer (CEAPO), PPGNY, and Executive Director, PPGNY Action Fund, PPGNY Votes, PPGNY Votes PAC **Organization:** Planned Parenthood of Greater New York (PPGNY) **Reports to:** President & CEO of PPGNY, PPGNY Action Fund, PPGNY Votes, PPGNY Votes PAC **Location:** Flexible within New York State; commutable distance to any PPGNY location. Hybrid in‑person/remote environment. Travel within the state required. — ## ORGANIZATION OVERVIEW Planned Parenthood of Greater New York (PPGNY) is a team of trusted health care providers, educators, and advocates committed to advancing equity and improving health outcomes in communities facing systemic barriers to quality, innovative sexual and reproductive health services. These services include birth control, pregnancy testing, emergency contraception, cancer screenings, STI testing and treatment, HIV testing and prevention, gender‑affirming hormone therapy, wellness exams, crisis counseling, and financial counseling. PPGNY also provides compassionate, nonjudgmental abortion services. PPGNY is the result of a strategic five‑way merger finalized in January 2020. As one of the largest affiliates in the national Planned Parenthood network, PPGNY covers 65% of New York State, serving urban, suburban, and rural areas. Since its formation, PPGNY has focused on post‑merger integration and building an intentional, shared organizational culture responsive to local staff and community needs. PPGNY cares for more than 80,000 patients annually at 17 health centers and through virtual care. It is one of New York’s largest and most trusted reproductive healthcare providers, offering: **Essential Health Care:** Comprehensive services for all individuals regardless of age, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, immigration status, zip code, or ability to pay. **Community Engagement, Education, and Training:** Programs that dismantle barriers such as language inaccessibility, lack of insurance, high costs, and mistrust of the healthcare system. **Advocacy:** Public affairs programs that protect and expand access to reproductive health care and education, advancing policies that support reproductive justice. PPGNY employs approximately 500 staff and has an annual operating budget of ~$100 million. The organization envisions a future where all communities have full access to innovative, high‑quality, affordable, evidence‑based sexual and reproductive health services, including abortion. — ## OPPORTUNITY Planned Parenthood and its affiliates are navigating significant challenges, including federal funding cuts and sustained political attacks that threaten reproductive health care access. These impacts fall most heavily on marginalized communities. Despite these obstacles, PPGNY continues to provide critical services and stand as a defender of equity, dignity, and human rights. This moment calls for bold, visionary leadership to ensure PPGNY emerges stronger, more innovative, and deeply rooted in its mission. The CEAPO and Executive Director of PPGNY Action Fund, PPGNY Votes, and PPGNY Votes PAC will lead efforts in two primary lanes: 1. Advancement of state and local policies, budget priorities, and electoral work. 2. Community‑facing programming that increases knowledge, improves access to care, and facilitates engagement. — ## REPORTING Reports to President & CEO Wendy Stark (she/her). Direct supervision of four departmental leaders: – VP, Education & Training – VP, Community Engagement – AVP, Public Affairs – Director, Government Relations & Policy Primary responsibility for collaboration, strategic agenda setting, and fund development with the Boards of PPGNY Action Fund, PPGNY Votes, and PPGNY Votes PAC. — ## POSITION The CEAPO leads Public Affairs, Government Relations, Education & Training, and Community Engagement. This role oversees approximately 90 employees across these departments. The CEAPO also serves as executive leader and staff liaison to PPGNY Action Fund (C4), PPGNY Votes (independent expenditure committee), and PPGNY Votes PAC (political action committee). Responsibilities include developing, implementing, managing, and evaluating cohesive strategies for advocacy, government relations, organizing, and electoral goals. The CEAPO also leads refinement and implementation of health‑equity‑focused, grant‑funded education and community engagement programs. The CEAPO must embody a commitment to sexual and reproductive health and rights, reproductive justice, and race equity in all interactions and strategic decisions. — ## ESSENTIAL JOB DUTIES & PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES ### Advocacy & Public Affairs Leadership (50%) – Oversee Public Affairs team and its electoral, legislative, and organizing campaigns. – Serve as PPGNY’s lobbyist to local, state, and federal officials. – Develop annual legislative strategy in coordination with PPESA, PPAF, senior staff, and Boards. – Maintain strong relationships with PPESA and PPAF. – Oversee organizing and electoral strategies for Action Fund, Votes, and Votes PAC. – Serve as spokesperson and liaison to Boards on agenda setting, fundraising, and development. – Oversee compliance for Action Fund, PAC, and Votes entities. – Collaborate with Development to meet fundraising goals and cultivate donor relationships. – Serve as spokesperson in media, public forums, and events. ### Education & Training and Community Engagement Leadership (35%) – Provide leadership and management support to Education & Training and Community Engagement departments. – Ensure health equity and reproductive justice principles guide program strategies. – Create, implement, evaluate, and improve program initiatives. – Lead strategic decision‑making on program content, funding, geography, and populations. – Develop strategies for funding expansion in collaboration with Development. – Position PPGNY as a preferred partner within justice‑focused coalitions. ### Executive Leadership Duties (15%) – Serve on Executive Leadership Team (ELT). – Act as thought partner to CEO, ELT, and Boards. – Represent Public Affairs and Programs at ELT level. – Collaborate on organizational strategy and sustainability. — ## CANDIDATE PROFILE You are an experienced, dynamic, innovative leader who inspires, activates, and builds strong relationships. You are deeply invested in advancing bodily autonomy, health equity, gender and racial justice, and reproductive freedom. You thrive in environments of rapid change and complexity and engage authentically with people of all backgrounds. You prioritize effectively, delegate wisely, meet deadlines, and embrace collaborative, supportive management. You maintain composure under changing conditions and understand the complexity of holding both Executive Director and Chief titles. — ## REQUIRED SKILLS & EXPERIENCE – Significant progressive nonprofit leadership experience, ideally reporting directly to a CEO/President/Executive Director. – Professional or activism experience in sexual and reproductive health or justice strongly preferred. – Deep understanding of New York State and NYC political environments. – Significant coalition‑building experience. – Experience managing public and private grants/contracts. – Ability to lead in environments with diverse intersectional identities. – Commitment to anti‑racist, anti‑bias culture; proven equity and inclusion work. – Experience in unionized environments. – Ability to contribute to organizational strategy and systems development. – Strong understanding of nonprofit business operations. – Exceptional written, verbal, interpersonal, and public speaking skills. – Ability to negotiate conflicts and maintain constructive relationships. – Willingness to travel up to 25% within NY State. — ## DESIRED EXPERIENCE – Leadership experience in a nonprofit of similar size and complexity. – Master’s degree or J.D. – Experience in change management, mergers, or cultural integration. – Experience leading organizational transformation. – Experience in organizations with programmatic and/or clinical operations. — ## PERSONAL CHARACTERISTICS – Deep passion for PPGNY’s mission and communities served. – Ability to operate at both strategic and hands‑on levels. – Ability to align policy and program strategies with mission and impact. – High self‑awareness, emotional intelligence, and professional maturity. – Commitment to equity, inclusion, and belonging. – Open, collaborative, decisive when necessary. – Bridge‑builder and trusted partner. – Energy for managing cultural change and driving performance. – Comfort with ambiguity; ability to inspire confidence. – Strong analytical mindset and systems thinking. – Boldness and courage to lead change with appropriate pacing. — ## COMPENSATION Salary range: **$285,000–$305,000** Comprehensive benefits include: – Health, dental, vision – 23 vacation days in year one – 10 sick days – 10 holidays + 3 floating holidays – Paid family and parental leave – Life & accident insurance – Short‑ and long‑term disability – EAP access – Health and flexible spending accounts – Retirement plans with employer contributions after 12 months – Flexible scheduling – Mass transit/commuter parking accounts — ## TO APPLY Kevin Chase Executive Search Group is leading this recruitment. PPGNY is an equal opportunity employer. Submit a resume and cover letter to ** [email protected] ** or apply via the Jobs Portal . All inquiries and applications will be held in strict confidence. — ## CONTACT INFORMATION Kevin Chase, Managing Partner [email protected] Catie DiFelice, Senior Associate [email protected] Kevin Chase Executive Search Group [www.kevinchasesearch.com] All education, dates of employment, and other information will be verified prior to an offer.
