item.title: Policy Associate (or Senior Policy Associate)
item.description: Policy Associate (or Senior Policy Associate) Organization: We Build Progress Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/17/2026 **Employment Type:** Full time. This is a 2-year position with possibility of extending. Part of the NPEU bargaining unit. **Location:** Hybrid · District of Columbia, USA. Based in Washington, DC. **Salary:** $77,514–$84,647 (USD). This salary is for Senior Policy Associate. Excellent benefits, including 20 annual paid days off. **Team:** Climate and Clean Energy (Livable Futures) **Seniority:** Mid-level **Closing:** Tuesday, September 15, 2026 — ## Position Description The Policy Associate will support the development and execution of the organization’s policy priorities through policy development, research and writing, project management, stakeholder engagement, and coordination. The position combines substantive policy work with responsibility for moving policy initiatives from strategy through implementation, including coordinating partners and internal contributors, managing workplans and timelines, and tracking program and grant deliverables across a cross-cutting portfolio of progressive policy priorities. The position will focus on advancing equitable climate and clean energy policy priorities, including helping communities understand and leverage public funding, financing tools, tax credits, and governmental authorities at the federal, state, and local levels. Relevant policy areas include climate policy, climate and energy infrastructure, public budgeting and finance, tax policy, economic opportunity, housing, and community investment. The position will support the Livable Futures team’s priorities by coordinating policy initiatives, conducting research, developing written materials, engaging coalition partners and other stakeholders, managing project plans and deliverables, and translating policy goals into concrete plans and activities. The position will also contribute to additional program areas and organizational priorities, as needed. This position may be filled at the Policy Associate or Senior Policy Associate level based on the candidate’s experience, scope of responsibility, and organizational needs. Candidates hired at the Senior Policy Associate level will bring deeper experience and take greater ownership of complex policy initiatives, external partnerships, and cross-organizational projects. — ## Primary Responsibilities ### Policy Research and Resource Development Conduct policy research and develop timely, accessible public education materials, including explainers, reports, fact sheets, and other resources, on topics such as: – federal climate and energy legislation, executive actions, and implementation, including their effectiveness and implications for communities and racial and socioeconomic equity; – public funding, financing, and implementation strategies that advance equitable climate and community development goals, including grants, appropriations, bonding authorities, tax and revenue policy, public-private partnerships, community benefit frameworks, and other governmental tools; and – innovative policy and implementation strategies that advance a just transition and center frontline communities and workers in climate, energy, infrastructure, and housing policy. Develop resources and engagement strategies that help frontline communities understand and influence federal climate policy and its implementation. **A Senior Policy Associate will also:** – lead assigned policy initiatives and research projects with a high degree of independence and provide strategic recommendations to program leadership; and – identify emerging policy developments, implementation challenges, opportunities, and potential risks and recommend possible responses for consideration by program leadership. — ### Policy Initiative Coordination and Project Management – Coordinate the day-to-day implementation of multiple program initiatives, ensuring projects remain organized, on schedule, and aligned with program priorities. – Support program leadership by tracking workplans and deliverables, coordinating internal workflows, preparing meeting materials, and ensuring timely follow-up on decisions and action items. – Coordinate internal workflows and work with staff and external partners to advance shared projects and maintain alignment on responsibilities, timelines, and deliverables. – Support annual team goal-setting and work-planning processes, including documenting priorities, developing project plans, and tracking progress across initiatives. – Identify emerging opportunities, programmatic gaps, and potential areas for action and share recommendations with the Livable Futures team. – Contribute to funder proposals and reports, track grant deliverables, and participate in funder engagement. **A Senior Policy Associate will also lead assigned program workstreams or initiatives from planning through completion, including coordinating contributors, managing timelines and deliverables, identifying challenges, and recommending adjustments.** — ### Partnerships and Coalition Engagement – Support and maintain relationships with local, state, and federal government officials and policymakers, and with nonprofit, labor, philanthropic, community, financial-sector, and coalition partners to advance shared policy initiatives and program goals. – Support external partnerships by coordinating and facilitating meetings, maintaining regular communication, documenting next steps, and ensuring timely follow-through on commitments. – Coordinate the organization’s participation in relevant coalitions, including preparing for meetings, facilitating internal and external coordination, maintaining partner communication, and tracking follow-up. – Support congressional engagement in coordination with relevant program and government affairs staff, including conducting outreach, scheduling meetings, preparing for and participating in briefings, and supporting ongoing relationship management. **A Senior Policy Associate will also:** – serve as the primary relationship manager for assigned partners and represent the organization in external meetings, events, and presentations; and – contribute to the development and implementation of shared advocacy strategies in coordination with staff and coalition partners. — ### Briefings, Events, and Public Education – Support briefings, convenings, presentations, and other public education activities by coordinating logistics, preparing agendas and materials, developing presentations and resources, and occasionally facilitating or presenting. **A Senior Policy Associate will also:** – lead the planning and execution of assigned public briefings and convenings, including developing agendas, securing speakers, and recruiting participants from across sectors; and – regularly represent the organization as a presenter, speaker, or facilitator at briefings, public events, and coalition meetings. Perform other duties as assigned; the omission of specific responsibilities does not preclude the assignment of other duties logically related to the position. — ## Candidate Profile The successful candidate is an organized and collaborative policy professional with strong project management, research, writing, and relationship-building skills. They can manage multiple workstreams, support senior leadership, and translate complex policy concepts into well-executed projects and accessible public education resources. They understand that advancing policy priorities requires both substantive policy expertise and effective coordination and implementation. They demonstrate sound judgment, take a proactive and solutions-oriented approach, understand the political and policy landscape in which the organization operates, and are committed to advancing equitable, people-centered public policy. — ## Experience Level **Policy Associate:** Typically 3–5 years of relevant professional experience in public policy, government, advocacy, organizing, program or project management, government affairs, research, or a related field. **Senior Policy Associate:** Typically 5 or more years of relevant professional experience in public policy, government, advocacy, organizing, program management, government affairs, research, or a related field. Candidates considered at the Senior Policy Associate level should also demonstrate substantial project management and coalition or stakeholder management experience, increasing responsibility over time, and the ability to independently lead complex initiatives. — ## Qualifications – Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and relevant professional experience. – Strong organizational and project management skills, with a demonstrated ability to prioritize work, coordinate multiple workstreams, track deliverables, anticipate needs, and execute detailed projects in a fast-paced, collaborative environment. – Experience conducting policy research, synthesizing complex information, and producing clear written materials for policymakers, partner organizations, funders, or public audiences. – Strong writing, editing, verbal communication, and presentation skills, including the ability to communicate complex policy, fiscal, and technical concepts clearly to diverse audiences. – Experience building productive relationships across organizations and sectors, coordinating meetings and projects, managing follow-up, and working effectively with external partners. – Strong interpersonal skills and a demonstrated ability to build collaborative internal and external relationships, give and receive constructive feedback, foster accountability, and adapt to evolving priorities. – Deep commitment to racial equity, social justice, community-centered solutions, and progressive policy goals. – A flexible and adaptable working style, including a willingness to support evolving team and organizational priorities and engage with new policy issues. — ## Prefer

item.title: Vice President, Government Affairs
item.description: Vice President, Government Affairs Organization: Biosecurity Advocacy Organization (Confidential) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/17/2026 # The Opportunity ## Position Vice President, Government Affairs ## Location Washington, DC ## Reporting Relationship Executive Director ## About the Organization A new national policy advocacy organization is being established to strengthen the United States’ ability to prevent, detect, prepare for, and respond to biological threats. Advances in biotechnology and artificial intelligence are creating extraordinary opportunities for scientific and societal progress while also introducing new and increasingly complex threats. At the same time, the nation’s systems for anticipating and responding to emerging biological threats remain fragmented. The organization will advance a comprehensive policy agenda spanning prevention, detection, preparedness, and response, working directly with Congress and the executive branch to translate policy priorities into enacted law. Its work will also support a strong biotechnology and scientific enterprise that advances U.S. competitiveness and national security while bolstering public trust. The organization is being built with a distinctly bipartisan approach and will draw upon expertise spanning government, Congress, industry, public health, science, technology, and national security. By partnering with the broader biodefense community and developing the political momentum and rapid-response capacity required to meet emerging threats, the organization intends to help close critical gaps before the next crisis. ## Role Overview The Organization is seeking an accomplished Vice President of Government Affairs to build and lead its congressional engagement strategy at a consequential moment for U.S. national security and biological preparedness. The Vice President will bring deep relationships, credibility, and political fluency within either the Democratic or Republican congressional ecosystem, while demonstrating the ability to operate effectively in a bipartisan environment. This leader will be responsible for translating the Organization’s policy priorities into meaningful legislative and executive action, cultivating relationships with Members of Congress, senior Congressional staff, and key Executive Branch officials, identifying pathways for advancing priorities across Congress and the Executive Branch, building coalitions around key priorities, and establishing the Organization as a trusted resource with policymakers across the federal government. This is a ground-floor opportunity to build a sophisticated government affairs capability. The Vice President will have meaningful influence over congressional strategy, stakeholder engagement, team development, and how the organization positions complex and evolving issues for policymakers. The successful candidate will combine deep Congressional experience, sophisticated political judgment, and a strong understanding of how policy moves from idea to enactment. While previous biosecurity expertise would be valuable, it is not required; equally important will be intellectual agility and the ability to quickly master complex scientific and technical issues and translate them into pragmatic, politically viable legislative strategies. ## Key Responsibilities ### Government Affairs Strategy & Engagement – Develop and execute a comprehensive Congressional engagement strategy, leveraging deep relationships and credibility within either the Democratic or Republican caucus while building support across party lines; deep relationships with Republican and Democratic committee leadership, leadership offices, and key personal offices would be particularly valuable. – Develop and support an Executive Branch engagement strategy, in close coordination with the policy team and organizational leadership, to advance priorities requiring action by the White House, federal departments, agencies, and other executive branch actors. – Build and maintain trusted relationships with Members of Congress, Chiefs of Staff, Legislative Directors, senior personal-office staff, and relevant committee leadership and staff. – Identify legislative opportunities and pathways for advancing the Organization’s priorities through authorizing legislation, appropriations, hearings, amendments, and other legislative vehicles. – Establish the Organization as a credible, responsive resource for policymakers navigating complex biological, scientific, technological, and national security issues. ### Legislative Advocacy & Policy Translation – Partner closely with the policy team to translate substantive priorities into actionable legislative strategies. – Shape legislative asks, contribute to legislative language, and develop briefing materials and other resources for Congressional engagement. – Distill sophisticated scientific and technical analysis into clear, compelling arguments that resonate with policymakers. – Bring political and legislative perspective to the development and prioritization of the Organization’s broader policy agenda. ### Bipartisan Coalition Building – Build durable support for the Organization’s policy priorities across party lines while leveraging established credibility within the candidate’s respective political ecosystem. – Identify opportunities to create alignment among policymakers with different perspectives around shared national security, preparedness, and competitiveness priorities. – Develop relationships with external organizations and stakeholders that can strengthen coalitions and advance legislative objectives. ### Crisis Preparedness & Rapid Response – Contribute to the development of a comprehensive legislative framework designed to enable rapid Congressional action following a catalyzing event. – Anticipate emerging legislative and political developments and position the Organization to respond quickly when windows for policy action arise. – Help ensure policymakers have actionable solutions available before moments of crisis create an urgent need for them. ### Government Affairs Leadership – Build and lead a high-performing government affairs function, including recruiting and managing in-house professionals and external lobbying resources. – Establish systems and operating rhythms for Congressional outreach, relationship management, legislative tracking, and coordination with the policy team. – Serve as a senior external representative with policymakers, partners, and other influential stakeholders. – Contribute as a senior leader to building a collaborative, entrepreneurial, and impact-oriented organization. ## Candidate Profile The ideal candidate will be an accomplished government affairs and Congressional leader who combines deep political relationships, sophisticated legislative expertise, and exceptional strategic judgment. They will understand both the formal legislative process and the political dynamics that determine whether and how complex policy priorities gain traction on Capitol Hill. Relevant experience in the Executive Branch is a strong asset. Candidates whose expertise comes exclusively from the Executive Branch are also encouraged to apply. The successful candidate will bring credibility with senior policymakers, the ability to navigate complex and evolving issues, and a track record of translating substantive policy ideas into pragmatic legislative strategies. They will be equally comfortable engaging Members, senior Congressional staff, political appointees, and civil servants, partnering closely with policy experts, and building and leading a high-performing government affairs team. ### Candidates should bring: – 10–15+ years of relevant experience, including significant experience working at senior levels on Capitol Hill, either within a Member’s personal office or in a Congressional committee role, or equivalent experience in the executive branch. – Experience working with or building relationships across committees relevant to the Organization’s agenda would be particularly valuable, including the Senate and House Appropriations Committees; Senate HELP and House Energy and Commerce; the Senate and House Armed Services Committees; Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs and House Homeland Security; the Senate and House Intelligence Committees; Senate Foreign Relations and House Foreign Affairs; the House and Senate Agriculture Committees; and committees overseeing science, technology, biotechnology, and U.S. competitiveness, including Senate Commerce and House Science, Space, and Technology. – Prior service as a Chief of Staff, Legislative Director, senior committee staff member, or in a comparably senior Congressional role is highly preferred; experience with a key committee would be particularly valuable. – Deep relationships, credibility, and political fluency within either the Democratic or Republican Congressional ecosystem. – A sophisticated understanding of Congressional strategy, legislative processes, and the political dynamics required to move complex policy priorities from concept toward legislative action. – Demonstrated experience building, managing, and developing high-performing teams, with the leadership capability to oversee both in-house government affairs professionals and external lobbying resources. – Exceptional communication and policy translation skills, with the ability to distill complex technical and policy analysis into clear, pragmatic legislative strategies and compelling arguments for political audiences. – Strong political judgment and an ability to identify opportunities, anticipate challenges, and adapt strategy as the legislative and political environment evolves. – The ability to build support across party lines, combining strong relationships within one political ecosystem with the credibility and collaborative orientation necessary to advance a bipartisan policy agenda. – Passion for joining the leadership of a n

item.title: Director, Public Affairs
item.description: Director, Public Affairs Organization: Anheuser-Busch Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/18/2026 ## Dreaming Big Dreaming big is in our DNA. It’s who we are as a company. It’s our culture. It’s our heritage. And more than ever, it’s our future. A future where we’re always looking forward, always serving up new ways to meet life’s moments. A future where we keep dreaming bigger. We look for people with passion, talent, and curiosity, and provide them with the teammates, resources, and opportunities to unleash their full potential. The power we create together – when we combine your strengths with ours – is unstoppable. Are you ready to join a team that dreams as big as you do? — ## Salary **$133,600 – $158,650**, bonus and long‑term incentive eligible — ## Company We are home to the nation’s most iconic beer and beyond‑beer brands, including Michelob ULTRA – America’s #1 top‑selling beer – as well as Busch Light, Budweiser, Bud Light, Stella Artois, Cutwater Spirits, and industry‑leading craft brands. From our longstanding efforts to support American farmers, military, veterans, and first responders, to emergency drinking water donations and responsible drinking programs, we are guided by our commitment to the communities we call home and the 65,000 hardworking Americans who bring our beer to life. We are powered by a team that shares our passion to create a future with more cheers. Are you ready to join a team that dreams as big as you do? — ## Role Summary This position is a key member of the Corporate Communications Team reporting to the Senior Director of Corporate Communications. The Public Affairs Director will lead corporate communications efforts tied to policy priorities, guide advocacy engagement, and manage key third‑party stakeholders. This role works cross‑functionally to shape and enhance Anheuser‑Busch’s corporate reputation through best‑in‑class public affairs capabilities, including media relations, message creation, coalition management, crisis response, and grassroots engagement. — ## Job Responsibilities – **Creative communication** — Be passionate about our work as communicators and value creativity. – **Autonomous project leadership** — Move quickly and feel comfortable having autonomy to lead projects. – **Matrixed organization navigation** — Understand how to get things done in a large, matrixed organization. – **Public affairs & corporate comms blend** — Enjoy a role that mixes public affairs and corporate communications with an emphasis on creating a favorable policy environment at the state and federal level. – **Strategic advocacy development** — Develop long‑term strategic advocacy and public policy‑related communications programs supporting government affairs objectives. – **Third‑party partnerships** — Identify partnership opportunities with key third‑party groups and opinion leaders to advance legislative priorities. – **Issue campaign leadership** — Lead issue campaigns and corporate reputation initiatives with an emphasis on creative storytelling and content development. – **Stakeholder communication** — Facilitate regular communication on business and public policy priorities with internal and external stakeholders. – **Project plan execution** — Develop, lead, and drive project plans to ensure communications campaigns achieve intended results. – **Cross‑functional collaboration** — Contribute as a key member of the Corporate Communications Team, working closely with Community Impact, Government Affairs, Internal Communications, and breweries. – **Political awareness** — Possess political savviness to understand how the external environment impacts company priorities. – **Issues management** — Manage issues and reactive communications in coordination with the Director of Media Relations. – **Budget oversight** — Oversight and management of budgets. – **Agency management** — Manage agency partners to support the work. – **Event support** — Support internal and external events as appropriate. — ## Job Qualifications – Minimum of 7–10 years of communications experience at a large organization or leading PR agency – Experience working in public affairs, political campaigns, or with state or federal elected officials – Experience at or with a company with major, consumer‑facing brands – Experience in beverage/brewing or another highly regulated industry a plus – Ability to develop 360‑degree strategic communications plans and drive successful execution – Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to distill complex ideas into simple messaging – Strong relationship management skills with the ability to build lasting partnerships – Highly collaborative team player able to juggle multiple initiatives with a positive attitude — ## Why Anheuser‑Busch At Anheuser‑Busch, our purpose is to create a future with more cheers. For more than 165 years as a leading American manufacturer, we have delivered a legacy of brewing great‑tasting, high‑quality beers that have satisfied beer drinkers for generations. As the nation’s top brewer, one of the fastest‑growing spirits companies, and an insurgent force in energy drinks, we drive economic prosperity nationwide through investments in our people, facilities, and communities. We are the only alcohol company that invests in the U.S. at this scale. — ## Benefits – Health benefits including Medical, Dental, Vision, Wellness, and Tax‑Advantaged Savings and Spending Accounts – Life Insurance and Disability Income Protection – Generous Parental Leave and FMLA policies – 401(k) Retirement Savings options with company matching contribution – Chance to work in a fast‑paced environment among a company of owners – Free Beer! Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Media Relations Coordinator (Job ID: 2026-3888)
item.description: Media Relations Coordinator (Job ID: 2026-3888) Organization: Brookings Institution Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/18/2026 ## Overview Join one of the most influential, most quoted, and most trusted think tanks! The **Brookings Institution** is a nonprofit public policy organization based in Washington, D.C. Its mission is to equip decision‑makers with nonpartisan research and policy strategies to create a more prosperous and secure country and world. To advance this mission, Brookings is committed to four goals: – Develop economic growth strategies for a changing world – Expand economic and social opportunity for all – Revitalize U.S. democratic institutions – Advance peace and security worldwide At the core of Brookings’s mission is the quality, independence, and impact of its research. The institution is dedicated to finding bold, pragmatic solutions for societal challenges through open‑minded inquiry, diverse perspectives, and the highest standards of scholastic rigor. Beyond excellence and intellectual rigor, Brookings values a supportive and collaborative environment where individuals can do their best work, learn, and grow. Because of this, Brookings has been at the forefront of public policy for more than a century. The mission of the **Office of Communications** is to provide tools, strategies, products, and programs that support the brand and its content, continually growing Brookings’s impact as a change agent for public policy. This purpose is realized by helping scholars raise awareness, set the agenda, and shape debate around the public policy issues they address. **Position Location:** Hybrid. Requires regular in‑person presence at the Washington, DC office with the option of at least two remote‑work days per week. **Please Note:** This position is part of the Brookings United bargaining unit (IFPTE Local 70) and is covered under the collective bargaining agreement. Brookings is currently undergoing a multi‑year strategic plan implementation, and the role, supervisor, and program may change. — ## Responsibilities Ready to contribute to Brookings’ success? The **Media Relations Coordinator** supports earned media efforts by connecting Brookings research, experts, events, and institutional priorities with relevant audiences across the media ecosystem. The coordinator provides administrative, logistical, and communications support for media outreach, journalist engagement, media monitoring, reporting, and scholar visibility. The role is central to maintaining systems, data, and workflows that underpin media relations. ### Media Relations Support (65%) – Monitor shared media inboxes and support timely routing, tracking, and resolution of media inquiries. – Coordinate logistics for media interviews, podcast appearances, and other engagements between journalists and Brookings experts. – Draft and distribute press releases, media advisories, expert availability notices, and other materials. – Maintain and update media lists, journalist databases, and contact records in Meltwater and other systems. – Conduct media monitoring and compile daily, weekly, and ad hoc coverage reports. – Track media placements, interviews, citations, and other earned media activities. – Research reporters, editors, producers, newsletter authors, podcasters, independent outlets, content creators, influencers, and other channels. – Assist in preparing media briefing materials, background information, and interview preparation documents. – Support identification of timely news, policy developments, and outreach opportunities. – Maintain expert profiles, media references, external publications, and visibility‑related information across Brookings platforms. ### Communications Support and Impact (20%) – Assist in developing social media copy, newsletter content, website updates, and other materials. – Support communications planning and promotional efforts for publications, events, and institutional initiatives. – Assist with impact reporting and preparation of presentations, dashboards, and other reports. – Maintain accurate records and documentation of communications activities. – Provide copy‑editing, proofreading, and quality‑control support. – Contribute to communications templates, guidance materials, and best‑practice resources. ### Team Operations and Analytics (15%) – Support coordination for media relations workflows, systems, and administrative processes. – Maintain reporting dashboards, tracking tools, shared resources, and departmental documentation. – Prepare earned media reports, metrics summaries, and briefing materials. – Coordinate team meetings, training sessions, schedules, and other operational activities. – Support onboarding logistics and maintain training resources for new team members. – Assist with vendor administration, subscriptions, data management, and other operational responsibilities. – Provide administrative and project support for special initiatives. – Contribute to internal team and organizational work that shapes systems and culture. – Other duties as assigned. — ## Qualifications Ready to make an impact? In this role, you will support Brookings values of collegiality, respect, inclusion, diversity, and community. ### Education / Experience Requirements Bachelor’s degree in communications, journalism, public policy, political science, international relations, marketing, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience. Minimum one to three years of experience in communications, journalism, media relations, public affairs, public policy, government communications, nonprofit communications, or a related field. ### Knowledge / Skill Requirements Strong written, verbal, organizational, and interpersonal communication skills. Familiarity with AP Style preferred. Exceptional attention to detail and ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines. Demonstrated ability to organize information, manage data, and maintain accurate records. Experience conducting research and synthesizing information. Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications. Experience with Meltwater or similar platforms preferred. Interest in public policy, research communications, journalism, and mission‑driven organizations preferred. — ## Additional Information Brookings offers a generous benefits package including medical, dental, and vision coverage, generous time off, and workplace flexibility. For more information, visit **Brookings Benefits**. Applicants must submit a cover letter and resume as one document here . If applying to multiple Brookings openings, attach a position‑specific cover letter separately. Successful completion of a background investigation is required. Brookings welcomes and celebrates diversity in all its forms and is proud to be an equal‑opportunity employer. **Please Note:** Must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Senior Media Relations Manager
item.description: Senior Media Relations Manager Organization: ASML Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/18/2026 ## Job ID: J-00348773 ## Introduction to the Job ASML is one of the world’s leading manufacturers of chip‑making equipment and the technology leader in the semiconductor lithography field. By helping to make chips cheaper and more powerful, we help make semiconductor technology more attractive for a larger range of products and services. ASML is recognized as one of the key companies in the world that drives the digital transformation. ASML is a global company with around 44,000 employees worldwide and one of the most valuable European companies measured in market capitalization. — ## Media Relations ASML is increasingly visible to the outside world and is recognized as a European high‑tech supplier to the global chip industry. The media relations team supports and strengthens ASML’s business goals and reputation as an innovation powerhouse, trusted employer, and community stakeholder. ASML operates at the intersection of technology, national security, industrial policy, and international trade—making clear, consistent communications a critical contributor to trust and understanding. Due to the dynamics in our industry, complexity, and strong growth, the media is interested in who we are, what we do, and what we think—our technology, people, global footprint, supply chain, and our role in the semiconductor ecosystem. Increasingly, coverage also focuses on policy and geopolitical topics such as export controls, trade measures, industrial policy, strategic partnerships, and the broader implications of semiconductor leadership. Aligning our messaging, managing information flows, and knowing when to communicate which messages to which audiences—while managing a system of issues communications—are key contributors to our reputation and business goals. We maintain strong relationships with the international media in a friendly and transparent manner, in good and in bad times. — ## Job Mission Your mission is to maintain and expand relationships with the media and to bring our messages via the media to our key external audiences. The focus of this role is on media engagement surrounding government affairs and geopolitics. Together with others on the media relations team, you develop a strategy to position ASML as a European high‑tech supplier to the world, employer of choice, and a good corporate citizen—while helping stakeholders understand ASML’s role in policy, trade, and international dynamics that shape our industry. You also increase knowledge about government affairs and geopolitical topics among communications colleagues worldwide. — ## Role and Responsibilities You develop and execute a proactive strategic media plan that supports ASML’s core messages and business goals related to government affairs, public policy, trade, and geopolitics. You ensure that your media plans and activities have clear objectives that are tied to business goals, geopolitical strategies, and key target audiences, allowing you to analyze, measure, evaluate, and show if and where we made a difference. You keep up to date with developments in our business, technology, and policy environment and translate these into media opportunities for your audiences. You will work with other communications teams, the government affairs function, and legal/compliance teams to identify and advise on media initiatives that support our reputation and enable informed public debate. You draft and review statements, press materials, and Q&A on policy and issues topics (e.g., export controls, trade measures, industrial policy, and supply chain resilience), arrange media briefings/interviews, and engage with journalists from U.S. and international media. — ## Context of the Position This new position will be part of ASML’s U.S. Communications team with a strong dotted line to the media relations team located in the Netherlands. You report directly to the Head of U.S. Media Relations and you will replace her during absence. You work closely with our international media spokespersons and internal stakeholders across ASML (on all levels, including Board of Management) to support strategic decision‑making—particularly on issues where technology, policy, and geopolitics intersect. You will also work daily with the U.S. Government Affairs team. The position is based in Washington, D.C. and is a hybrid role, working in the ASML D.C. office at least three days per week. — ## Education and Experience – Degree in Communications, Journalism, International Relations, Political Science, Public Policy, or equivalent combination of education and/or experience – Experience in issues communications across government affairs/public policy and geopolitically sensitive topics, preferably in a global listed company, public affairs environment, or journalism – A high affinity for / experience in technology / the semiconductor industry – Strong stakeholder management experience, working on executive level in an international environment and proven ability to influence and network — ## Skills – Strategic thinking and business acumen – Ability to translate complex (technical and policy/geopolitical) content into meaningful and engaging language – An individual who thrives in a highly complex and collaborative environment where trust is key – Ability to drive action in uncertain or evolving situations; processes new information quickly and adjusts strategies accordingly; displays situational adaptability under time pressure – Strong oral and written communication skills – Experience working with colleagues across multiple regions/locations; cultural sensitivity – Interpersonal influence: builds trust and rapport with communications colleagues, senior business leaders, and other partners; pursues goals in a constructive and assertive way; explores potential solutions during disagreements and searches for the win‑win — ## Other Information ASML is an Equal Opportunity Employer that values and respects the importance of a diverse and inclusive workforce. It is the policy of the company to recruit, hire, train, and promote persons in all job titles without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, veteran status, disability, sexual orientation, or gender identity. We recognize that diversity and inclusion is a driving force in the success of our company. The current base annual salary range for this role is: **$110,250 – $165,375** Pay scales are determined by role, level, location, and alignment with market data. Individual pay is determined through interviews and an assessment of several factors that are unique to each candidate, including but not limited to job‑related skills, relevant education and experience, certifications, abilities of the candidate, and pay relative to other team members. The Company offers employees and their families medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance. Employees are able to participate in the Company’s 401k plan. Employees will also receive eight (8) hours of vacation leave every month and thirteen (13) paid holidays throughout the calendar year. For more information, please contact the Recruiter or click on this link: **Compensation & Benefits in the US**. All new ASML jobs have a minimum application deadline of 10 days. This position requires access to controlled technology, as defined in the United States Export Administration Regulations (15 C.F.R. § 730, et seq.). Qualified candidates must be legally authorized to access such controlled technology prior to beginning work. Business demands may require ASML to proceed with candidates who are immediately eligible to access controlled technology. — ## Inclusion and Diversity ASML is an Equal Opportunity Employer that values and respects the importance of a diverse and inclusive workforce. It is the policy of the company to recruit, hire, train, and promote persons in all job titles without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, veteran status, disability, sexual orientation, or gender identity. We recognize that inclusion and diversity is a driving force in the success of our company. Need to know more about applying for a job at ASML? Read our frequently asked questions. — ## Request an Accommodation ASML provides reasonable accommodations to applicants for ASML employment and ASML employees with disabilities. An accommodation is a change in work rules, facilities, or conditions which enable an individual with a disability to apply for a job, perform the essential functions of a job, and/or enjoy equal access to the benefits and privileges of employment. If you are in need of an accommodation to complete an application, participate in an interview, or otherwise participate in the employee pre‑selection process, please send an email to ** [email protected] ** to initiate the company’s reasonable accommodation process. Please note: This email address is solely intended to provide a method for applicants to initiate ASML’s process to request accommodation(s). Any recruitment questions should be directed to the designated Talent Acquisition member for the position. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Head of Strategic Programs, Government Affairs
item.description: Head of Strategic Programs, Government Affairs Organization: Spotify Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/18/2026 ## Head of Strategic Programs, Government Affairs The Head of Strategic Programs, Government Affairs is a senior leader with central responsibility for designing strategies and executing partnerships, events, and programs that enable Spotify to raise its profile with key public policy individuals and organizations. This is a new position that provides an opportunity for the right individual to design an impactful and effective program, then scale it for global replication. This leader owns how Spotify’s policy priorities are translated into coordinated, high‑impact engagements with key audiences, and will be responsible for convening and navigating cross‑functional teams within Spotify to identify opportunities and deploy and execute a range of strategic activations to deliver the right message, to the right audience, at the right time. Operating as a central program leader, this person brings together strategy, political acumen, content, and creative execution to deliver consistent, high‑quality storytelling and engagement to target audiences. This role will report to the Global Head of Government Affairs and be based in Washington, DC. — ## What You’ll Do – Lead the development and execution of engagement programs aligned with company priorities and advocacy objectives. – Identify, design, and execute initiatives and events that creatively tell Spotify’s story, expand its profile, and deepen engagement with policymakers and policy‑adjacent audiences in key markets. – Set strategy while also rolling up your sleeves to deliver high‑quality execution of key moments. Partner closely with Spotify’s broader events teams on larger initiatives, while independently owning smaller events and experiences from concept through execution. – Build and leverage key external relationships to strengthen Spotify’s presence in key markets and engagement with a range of stakeholders. – Lead cross‑functional working groups with Government Affairs, Communications, Social Impact, Marketing, and others to expand networks, advance advocacy goals, and build goodwill with key audiences. – Create frameworks and metrics to measure the effectiveness and impact of these initiatives. — ## Who You Are – 10+ years leading large‑scale programs, events, or strategic initiatives, ideally in public affairs, government relations, creative industries, or adjacent fields. – Track record of managing complex, multi‑workstream programs end‑to‑end, from strategy through execution, across multiple markets or regions. – Deep understanding of the political and cultural landscape in the US, UK, and EU. – A creative leader and thought partner, bringing ideas that align with Spotify’s objectives and business profile. – Proven ability to develop and execute complex engagement strategies, including both small and large events, in a fast‑paced environment. – Possess a network of relationships with, and ability to identify, new organizations, industry groups, and influential political and cultural stakeholders. – Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including experience preparing executive briefings and public‑facing materials. – Demonstrated ability to influence from within and drive alignment across cross‑functional teams. – Experience managing high‑profile or sensitive issues with strong judgment and discretion. – Skilled at balancing business objectives, reputational considerations, and advocacy priorities. – Knowledge of political compliance requirements. — ## Where You’ll Be This role is based in our Washington, DC office. Our Washington, DC office is where this team does its best work together. This role is fully on‑site, fostering collaboration, mentorship, and connection through daily in‑person interactions. — ## Learn About Life at Spotify The United States base range for this position is $236,000 – $337,235 plus equity. The benefits available for this position include health insurance, six‑month paid parental leave, 401(k) retirement plan, monthly meal allowance, 23 paid days off, 13 paid flexible holidays, and paid sick leave. These ranges may be modified in the future. Spotify is an equal opportunity employer. You are welcome at Spotify for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or what’s playing in your headphones. Our platform is for everyone, and so is our workplace. The more voices we have represented and amplified in our business, the more we will all thrive, contribute, and be forward‑thinking. Bring us your personal experience, your perspectives, and your background. It’s in our differences that we find the power to keep revolutionizing the way the world listens. At Spotify, we are passionate about inclusivity and making sure our entire recruitment process is accessible to everyone. We have ways to request reasonable accommodations during the interview process and help assist in what you need. If you need accommodations at any stage of the application or interview process, please let us know — we’re here to support you in any way we can. — ## Our Global Benefits – Extensive learning opportunities through our dedicated team, GreenHouse. – Flexible share incentives letting you choose how you share in our success. – Global parental leave — six months off for all new parents. – *All The Feels*, our employee assistance program and self‑care hub. – Flexible public holidays — swap days off according to your values and beliefs. item.description: Head, US Public Affairs & Patient Advocacy, Immunology Organization: Sanofi Location: Cambridge, MA | Washington, DC | Morristown, NJ Date Posted: 08/18/2026 # About the Job ## Head, US Public Affairs & Patient Advocacy, Immunology **Reports to:** VP & Head, US Public Affairs & Patient Advocacy **Member:** US PA&PA Leadership Team; Extended Leadership Teams of the US Immunology Business Unit; Alliance PA&PA Governance **Location:** Hybrid **Travel:** Up to 25%, primarily domestic Sanofi believes the US healthcare system should understand and solve for what matters most to patients. We are committed to working with patient advocacy organizations to accelerate research and development of medicines that address unmet needs, and to developing solutions that overcome barriers so people have affordable and sustainable access to the right treatments. US PA&PA Immunology exists to close the gap between when disease begins and when patients receive appropriate, timely care. The function operates an outcome‑driven advocacy model: a prioritized portfolio of priorities, measured against defined patient outcome goals. The Head leads this model and shapes its continued evolution. Sanofi’s immunology portfolio is anchored by Dupixent and an immunology pipeline spanning dermatology, respiratory, rhinology, gastrointestinal disease, and Type 2 inflammation. The Head, US PA&PA Immunology carries deep therapeutic area leadership combined with enterprise‑level contribution: ### Therapeutic Area Leadership Owns the US advocacy strategy and outcomes for the full Immunology portfolio: Dupixent across dermatology, respiratory, rhinology, gastrointestinal and Type 2 inflammation indications, plus Sanofi’s non‑alliance immunology assets and pipeline. Leads and develops a team of US PA&PA leads. Accountable for budget and patient outcomes. ### Enterprise Leadership Ensures alignment of patient advocacy and public affairs strategies with Corporate Affairs goals and colleagues. Serves as a full member of the US PA&PA Leadership Team, co‑owning functional strategy, talent, and the continued development of the function’s capabilities and ways of working, and contributing enterprise judgment on the patient‑access environment and corporate reputation beyond therapeutic area boundaries. Join the team transforming care for people with immune challenges, rare diseases, cancers, and neurological conditions. In Specialty Care, you’ll help deliver breakthrough treatments that bring hope to patients with some of the highest unmet needs. — # About Sanofi We’re an R&D‑driven, AI‑powered biopharma company committed to improving people’s lives and delivering compelling growth. Our deep understanding of the immune system – and innovative pipeline – enables us to invent medicines and vaccines that treat and protect millions of people around the world. Together, we chase the miracles of science to improve people’s lives. — # Main Responsibilities ## Outcomes‑Driven Strategic Leadership Set and own the creation and execution of the US PA&PA Immunology strategy as a prioritized portfolio of priorities, each with explicit patient outcome measures. Set the US PA&PA strategy for immunology, partner relationships, and patient‑community understanding years before new treatment options may reach patients. Use data, evidence, and the function’s decision‑support platforms to connect strategy, partnerships, programs, and outcomes. Manage and be accountable for securing the US PA&PA budgets across dermatology, respiratory, rhinology, gastrointestinal, allergy, and pipeline immunology, ensuring disciplined planning, allocation, and full accountability for how advocacy resources are deployed. ## External Partnership & Thought Leadership Accountable for Sanofi’s trusted partnerships with the US advocacy community across the immunology therapeutic area, owning the health, depth, and outcomes of relationships with patient advocacy organizations and professional societies, and earning continued partnership through transparency, consistency, and the quality of collaboration in service of shared patient priorities. Bring senior fluency in the US patient access environment and translate its implications for patients into the function’s advocacy strategy and priorities. Stay ahead of how the advocacy environment is evolving, including the growing importance of digital and AI‑era information channels to patient communities, and bring innovative approaches to how the function engages and learns. Personally accountable for ensuring full compliance with healthcare contribution compliance requirements, alongside all corporate, industry, and regulatory guidelines; protect trust through ethics, transparency, and sound judgment under public scrutiny. ## Enterprise & Cross‑Functional Integration As a member of the US PA&PA Leadership Team, co‑own functional strategy, talent, and operating‑model decisions across all US therapeutic areas. Serve as a standing member of the Extended Leadership Teams of the US Immunology Business Unit, carrying functional accountability across the franchises. Integrate across Corporate Affairs, partnering with US Policy & Reimbursement, federal and state Government Affairs, communications, Health Equity, CSR, Global SPC Public Affairs, and Global SPC Communication, each within its own remit, to deliver one consistent Sanofi voice on immunology issues. Partner with the Immunology Business Units and their General Managers, Market Access, PSS, Medical Affairs, HEVA, and R&D to embed patient insight upstream and align advocacy strategy with enterprise priorities. Work closely with Global Public Affairs and country teams to inform global strategy with US insights and ensure global direction shapes US execution, serving as the US voice on immunology public affairs and patient advocacy in global forums. ## Alliance Leadership (Sanofi–Regeneron) Lead the US PA&PA interface with Regeneron across the Dupixent portfolio, operating a joint advocacy model with shared funding. Provide senior‑level alliance governance and stewardship, ensuring aligned advocacy strategy. ## People Leadership & Team Development Lead, coach, and retain a team of US PA&PA leads covering dermatology, respiratory, rhinology, gastrointestinal disease, and Type 2 inflammation. Treat developing others as a core leadership responsibility: provide individual coaching, career development, and stretch opportunities for each team member, growing the next generation of PA&PA leaders and ensuring the function’s succession pipeline. Develop the team’s next capabilities, including digital and AI fluency, outcomes measurement, and cross‑disease learning, building succession depth within a critical therapeutic area. Model steady, principled leadership in a complex, fast‑evolving environment, optimizing for patient outcomes and results. — # About You ## Required BA/BS in a scientific, public health, policy, or related field; advanced degree preferred. 15+ years of progressive experience in the biopharmaceutical industry or adjacent healthcare sectors. 7+ years in patient advocacy, public affairs, policy, or market access, including senior leadership of advocacy strategy. Demonstrated experience managing or leading through influence and developing high‑performing teams of senior professionals, highly preferred. Strategic fluency in the US patient access environment, Medicare dynamics, coverage design, utilization management, affordability, with the ability to anticipate how access forces will evolve, shape advocacy strategy around them, and engage as a senior peer with policy, government affairs, and market access leadership. Demonstrated AI‑native ways of working: uses AI tools daily as core instruments of strategy, analysis, writing, and decision‑making rather than occasional aids; has redesigned personal and team workflows around AI; and can lead others through the same transformation. Healthcare industry compliance experience, with a working command of the compliance frameworks governing industry interactions with advocacy and healthcare organizations, including funding, grants, sponsorships, and transparency requirements, with a track record of operating impeccably within them. Experience operating in complex, highly matrixed environments; alliance or partnership experience strongly preferred. ## Distinguishing Capabilities & Mindset Enterprise‑first leadership. Team players across boundaries. Thrives in fast evolution. Outcomes discipline. Strategic judgment under ambiguity. Alliance and collaboration skills. AI‑native orientation. Cross‑disease learning. People development. Influence without authority. — # Why Choose Us? Bring the miracles of science to life alongside a supportive, future‑focused team. Discover endless opportunities to grow your talent and drive your career, whether through a promotion or lateral move, at home or internationally. Enjoy a thoughtful, well‑crafted rewards package that recognizes your contribution and amplifies your impact. Take good care of yourself and your family, with a wide range of health and wellbeing benefits including high‑quality healthcare, prevention and wellness programs, and at least 14 weeks’ gender‑neutral parental leave. Sanofi Inc. and its U.S. affiliates are Equal Opportunity employers committed to a culturally inclusive workforce. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to legally protected characteristics. #GD‑SG #LI‑GZ #LI‑Hybrid #vhd All compensation will be determined commensurate with demonstrated experience. Employees may be eligible to participate in Company employee benefit programs. — # Pursue Progress. Discover Extraordinary. Join Sanofi and step into a new era of science – where your growth can be just as transformative as the work we do. We invest in you to reach further, think faster, and do what’s never‑been‑done‑before. You’ll help push boundaries, challenge convention, and build smarter solutions that reach the

item.title: Director, Regional Affairs
item.description: Director, Regional Affairs Organization: National Waste Recycling Association Location: Arlington, VA Date Posted: 08/18/2026 ## **Position Title: Director, Regional Affairs** **Department:** State Advocacy **Reports To:** President & CEO **FLSA Status:** Exempt — ## **Position Summary** Promotes the interest of the waste and recycling industry, directs advocacy efforts, and creates a presence for NWRA within the assigned region. Director level supports approximately 6–8 assigned states. — ## **Program Management** Develop a presence and identity for the waste and recycling industry in the state capitals through attendance and participation at meetings, etc. Promote programs through meetings, speeches, and correspondence with legislators and regulators that inform them about the waste industry and its policy positions. Implement legislative and regulatory policies of chapters. Serve as spokesperson for industry. Monitor state legislative and regulatory activity. Promote member participation in public policy forums. Develop media contacts in cooperation with NWRA Communications Team. — ## **Membership** Assist existing members by providing information, expediting requests made of headquarters, setting appointments with government officials upon request, and helping prepare for speaking engagements, etc. Staff Chapter Steering Committees and other chapter committees, including preparation of agenda, background materials, and meeting minutes. Promote an active retention program for existing members through regular site visits, phone calls, correspondence, meetings, etc., at a rate commensurate with chapter goals. Assist in the recruitment of new members in accordance with chapter goals. Draft and distribute communications to members. Act as liaison with Washington office on behalf of chapter members. — ## **Event and Administrative Management** Develop and manage member events to raise funds for advocacy efforts in accordance with NWRA policies. Develop and manage regional budget(s). Supervise contract lobbyists and managers in accordance with NWRA policies. Organize, plan, and implement statewide and regional meetings in accordance with NWRA policies. — ## **Other Duties as Assigned by the CEO** Must be recognized that supervisors may add additional duties, responsibilities, and assignments as deemed appropriate and that a job description is not a listing of all activities and tasks associated with a position or the fulfillment of a related duty or responsibility. — ## **Skills and Experience** 5–7 years of state‑level advocacy. Proven experience organizing and managing advocacy campaigns on behalf of relevant issues to the waste and recycling industry. Experience managing and producing fundraising events. Experience working in a state government advocacy environment. Bachelor’s degree in political science, or relevant experience. — ## **Travel and Work Requirements** Frequent travel throughout the assigned region and regular travel to other regions, state capitals, member locations, chapter meetings, and national NWRA events. Ability to respond to time‑sensitive legislative, regulatory, member, and media matters outside standard business hours when necessary. Ability to communicate effectively in person, by telephone, by video, and in writing with internal and external audiences, including large groups. — ## **Physical Demands** Ability to communicate orally with management, other co‑workers, and customers both individually and in front of a group is imperative. Regular use of the telephone and e‑mail for communication is essential in order to carry out the functions of this position. Prolonged sitting is essential to perform duties of the position. Hearing and vision within normal ranges is essential for normal conversations, to receive ordinary information, and to prepare or inspect documents. Ability to lift up to 25 pounds occasionally may be required. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Senior Vice President, State Government Affairs
item.description: Senior Vice President, State Government Affairs Organization: National Waste Recycling Association Location: Arlington, VA Date Posted: 08/18/2026 ## Position Title: SVP State Government Affairs **Reports To:** President & CEO **FLSA Status:** Exempt — ## Position Summary The Senior Vice President, State Government Affairs is a senior executive and “player‑coach” responsible for leading NWRA’s regional government and chapter affairs function nationwide while directly managing an assigned region (group of state chapters). The position develops and executes a coordinated regional advocacy strategy, manages and develops the Regional Vice Presidents/Regional Directors, ensures consistency and accountability across regions, and serves as a senior advisor to the President & CEO on local, state and regional legislative, regulatory, membership, and chapter matters. The Senior Vice President also maintains hands‑on responsibility for advocacy, member engagement, chapter operations, events, and budgets within their own assigned region. — ## Association Leadership and Regional Strategy – Lead the national regional government and chapter affairs function and translate NWRA’s strategic priorities into coordinated local, state and regional advocacy plans, operating standards, goals, and measurable outcomes. – Serve as the primary executive liaison between the President & CEO, Regional Vice Presidents/Regional Directors, chapter leaders, and member companies on regional priorities and emerging issues. – Identify cross‑regional legislative and regulatory trends, risks, and opportunities; recommend association‑wide positions, resource allocation, and escalation strategies. – Ensure consistent implementation of NWRA policy positions while allowing for appropriate state and regional adaptation. – Represent NWRA with senior government officials, regulators, and partners on significant regional and state matters. – Provide executive‑level reporting on legislative activity, regional performance, membership engagement, chapter health, financial results, and major risks. — ## People Leadership and Performance Management – Directly manage, coach, and develop the Regional Vice Presidents/Regional Directors and other assigned regional affairs staff, including goal setting, prioritization, performance feedback, and succession planning. – Establish clear expectations for advocacy effectiveness, member service, chapter governance, event execution, financial stewardship, and internal collaboration. – Lead regular team meetings and cross‑regional planning sessions to promote alignment, share best practices, and resolve competing priorities. – Assess staffing, coverage models, and external lobbying resources; recommend changes to strengthen regional impact and service delivery. – Build a high‑accountability, service‑oriented culture that balances strategic leadership with hands‑on execution. — ## Direct Regional Responsibilities – Manage an assigned region and perform the core responsibilities expected of a Regional Vice President/Regional Director, including direct advocacy, chapter support, member engagement, events, and budget management. – Develop a visible and credible presence for the waste and recycling industry in assigned state capitals through meetings, testimony, speeches, correspondence, and participation in policy forums. – Monitor state legislative and regulatory activity; develop and implement advocacy strategies consistent with NWRA policy and chapter priorities. – Serve as spokesperson for the industry and cultivate productive relationships with legislators, regulators, governors’ offices, agencies, coalitions, and media contacts. – Promote member participation in public policy efforts and mobilize member executives and subject matter experts when appropriate. – Supervise contract lobbyists, consultants, and other external resources within the assigned region. — ## Membership and Chapter Leadership – Oversee the quality and consistency of chapter support across all regions, including governance practices, committee staffing, communications, member service, and annual planning. – Provide direct support to members in the assigned region by facilitating access to government officials, preparing members for meetings or testimony, and coordinating requests with headquarters. – Staff assigned Chapter Steering Committees and other chapter committees, including agendas, background materials, minutes, follow‑up, and implementation of decisions. – Lead member retention and engagement efforts, including regular visits, calls, meetings, and issue‑based outreach, and support recruitment of new members in partnership with membership staff. – Act as a senior liaison between chapter members and the headquarters office, ensuring issues are elevated and addressed promptly. — ## Events, Financial Management, and Administration – Oversee regional and chapter events designed to advance advocacy, strengthen member engagement, and raise funds in accordance with NWRA policies. – Direct the development, review, and management of regional and chapter budgets; monitor revenue, expenses, forecasts, and financial performance. – Ensure Regional Vice Presidents/Regional Directors follow established policies, approval processes, contracts, reporting requirements, and internal controls. – Organize and participate in statewide, regional, and national meetings and ensure effective coordination with other NWRA teams. — ## Leadership Scope and Decision‑Making – Operates with substantial autonomy and exercises senior‑level judgment on political strategy, issue prioritization, personnel matters, member relations, external representation, and allocation of regional resources. – Makes recommendations to the President & CEO on matters with organization‑wide, reputational, financial, or public policy implications. – Balances enterprise consistency with the unique political, regulatory, and membership needs of individual states and chapters. – Serves as an escalation point for complex regional issues, member concerns, chapter governance challenges, and performance matters. — ## Required Skills and Experience – 12 or more years of progressively responsible experience in government affairs, public policy, association management, or a related field, including substantial state‑level advocacy experience. – At least 5 years of successful leadership experience, including management of senior‑level professionals or geographically dispersed teams. – Demonstrated success developing and executing multi‑state legislative and regulatory strategies and advocacy campaigns. – Executive presence and credibility with C‑suite member leaders, elected officials, regulators, partners, and boards or volunteer leaders. – Proven ability to manage competing priorities, make sound judgments in politically sensitive situations, and communicate complex issues clearly. – Experience managing budgets, contract lobbyists, consultants, fundraising events, and chapter or regional operations. – Strong collaboration skills and the ability to work effectively across government affairs, communications, membership, events, finance, and executive leadership functions. – Bachelor’s degree in political science, public policy, government, business, or a related field; equivalent relevant experience may be considered. An advanced degree is preferred. – Knowledge of the waste and recycling industry, environmental policy, or a related regulated industry is strongly preferred. — ## Travel and Work Requirements – Frequent travel throughout the assigned region and regular travel to other regions, state capitals, member locations, chapter meetings, and national NWRA events. – Ability to respond to time‑sensitive legislative, regulatory, member, and media matters outside standard business hours when necessary. – Ability to communicate effectively in person, by telephone, by video, and in writing with internal and external audiences, including large groups. — ## Physical Demands The position requires prolonged sitting; regular use of a computer, telephone, and email; and the ability to participate in meetings and public speaking engagements. Hearing and vision within normal ranges are essential for ordinary communication and document review. Occasional lifting of up to 25 pounds may be required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Senior Manager, AI and Technology Policy
item.description: Senior Manager, AI and Technology Policy Organization: National Retail Federation (NRF) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/18/2026 ## Job Type Full-time ## Description The National Retail Federation is a trade association that advocates for the people, brands, policies, and ideas that help retail succeed. From its headquarters in Washington, D.C., NRF empowers the industry that powers the economy. Retail is the nation’s largest private-sector employer, contributing $5.3 trillion to annual GDP and supporting more than one in four U.S. jobs. For over a century, NRF has been a voice for every retailer and every retail job, educating, inspiring, and communicating the powerful impact retail has on local communities and global economies. The National Retail Federation is seeking a Senior Manager of AI and Technology Policy to manage key technology policy projects and support NRF’s advocacy, member engagement, and thought leadership efforts on artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, privacy, fraud prevention, and emerging technology issues impacting the retail industry. Reporting to the Vice President, AI and Technology Policy, this position will manage assigned technology policy and digital risk priorities, serve as the lead on select projects, presentations, and member resources, and work cross-functionally to advance NRF’s policy priorities. The Senior Manager will regularly collaborate internally and liaise externally with member companies, coalition partners, policymakers, regulators, and other stakeholders on artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, fraud prevention, privacy, and emerging technology issues that support innovation, consumer trust, and responsible technology adoption. This position is ideal for a curious, analytical, and organized policy professional who can independently manage complex projects, translate technical and policy developments into clear work products, and build expertise at the intersection of public policy, emerging technology, and retail innovation. — ## Essential Functions ### Policy Research and Advocacy Support – In partnership with the Vice President, manage key elements of NRF’s advocacy efforts related to AI, cybersecurity, fraud prevention, privacy, and other emerging technology issues. – Support the development of policy positions, advocacy materials, comment letters, legislative analyses, testimony, research summaries, and member resources that align with NRF’s technology policy priorities. – Serve as a day-to-day liaison with policymakers, regulators, member companies, coalition partners, and external stakeholders on assigned policy matters. ### Member Engagement and Industry Leadership – Manage the development and execution of technology, cybersecurity, fraud prevention, and digital risk research projects and member resources through NRF’s CDRI. – Support strategic planning and make recommendations to strengthen CDRI initiatives, member engagement, and NRF technology policy efforts. – Regularly engage with key NRF member groups, including the IT Security Council, AI Committee, and Fraud Prevention Professionals Working Group. – Lead planning and execution for assigned meetings, roundtables, and conferences, including agendas, briefing materials, presentations, and member deliverables. – Identify emerging technology challenges and opportunities facing retailers and translate complex insights into NRF policy priorities, member programming, and practical resources. — ## Requirements ### Minimum Qualifications – Bachelor’s degree required; public policy, political science, economics, or related field preferred. – At least 4 years of relevant professional experience in government affairs, public policy, technology policy, cybersecurity, privacy, fraud prevention, or related fields. – Strong writing, analytical, and policy communication skills, with the ability to synthesize complex and rapidly evolving technology issues into clear, actionable insights for business leaders, policymakers, and member audiences. – Demonstrated knowledge of, or experience working on, public policy issues related to artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, privacy, fraud prevention, or emerging technologies impacting the retail industry. – Strong organizational and project management skills with the ability to independently manage complex projects, timelines, meetings, and deliverables. – Strong communication and relationship-building skills, including the ability to collaborate cross-functionally and liaise externally with members, partners, and other stakeholders. – Ability to apply professional-level knowledge, independently identify and analyze complex matters, and develop sound recommendations on emerging technology policy issues. ### Preferred Qualifications – Experience in one or more of the following environments is strongly preferred: congressional offices, federal agencies, state government, trade associations, consulting firms, retail companies, technology companies, think tanks, or research organizations. — ## Location Washington, D.C. (In-office 3 days a week) ## How to Apply Interested candidates are invited to submit an application with their resume and cover letter here . — National Retail Federation (NRF) is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants without regard to any legally protected characteristic. This applies to all employment decisions, including recruiting, hiring, pay, promotion, development, and termination. ## Salary Description $100k – $115k Earn a certificate with the Council!
