item.title: Vice President, Advocacy
item.description: Vice President, Advocacy Organization: Aristotle Inc. Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/21/2026 ## Description Aristotle is looking for a Vice President, Advocacy to build and lead serious government affairs engagements. This is not a role for someone who tracks policy and writes memos. We need someone who knows federal policy inside and out, understands how decisions actually get made, and has the relationships and judgment to move the needle. Federal lobbying is central to this role, but we want someone who sees the big picture. The right candidate can anchor lobbying work within a broader advocacy strategy, drawing on policy, stakeholder engagement, coalition building, grassroots and grasstops influence, and digital advocacy to win legislative and regulatory battles. This person should be credible with policymakers and their staff, comfortable in front of clients, and able to translate policy goals into organized campaigns that produce results. From day one, they will strengthen our federal practice, help us take on more complex engagements, and bring the experience and relationships that make Aristotle more valuable to every client we serve. — ## Requirements ### Key Responsibilities • Serve as a senior member of Aristotle’s Advocacy team, working with existing leadership and account teams to shape federal and state advocacy strategies. • Help build and manage a government affairs capability that integrates lobbying strategy, policy intelligence, coalitions, grassroots and grasstops activation, digital engagement, and client advisory services. • Advise clients on translating policy objectives into advocacy programs, messages, stakeholder plans, and measurable campaigns. • Leverage relationships across the administration, federal agencies, congressional offices, committees, trade associations, coalitions, and the broader policy community to inform strategy and create access. • Lead or support federal lobbying efforts, including Hill and agency outreach strategy, client preparation, lobbying day planning, coalition engagement, and policymaker meetings. • Monitor legislative, regulatory, and political developments and turn them into timely recommendations, advocacy content, position statements, and outreach plans. • Oversee client-facing advocacy materials and events, including briefs, presentations, talking points, leave-behinds, action alerts, fly-ins, lobby days, coalition meetings, and stakeholder briefings. • Coordinate with product, data, creative, digital, and client service teams while mentoring staff and helping establish a scalable service model. • Identify ways to deepen client relationships by connecting client needs with Aristotle’s advocacy, data, digital, technology, and strategic communications capabilities. — ## Qualifications • Bachelor’s degree in Political Science, Communications, Public Affairs, Public Policy, a related field, or equivalent work experience. • Minimum of 12 years of experience in advocacy, public affairs, government relations, lobbying, policy, campaigns, or a related field. • Proven experience building and executing federal and state advocacy programs for corporations, associations, coalitions, PACs, or public affairs clients. • Direct federal lobbying experience, including congressional engagement, agency engagement, lobbying strategy, client preparation, and familiarity with lobbying compliance expectations. • Existing relationships with administration officials, agency staff, congressional offices, committee staff, trade associations, coalition leaders, or other influential federal policy stakeholders. • Experience helping build or manage a government affairs office, advocacy service model, client program, coalition, or policy-focused team. • Strong understanding of the federal legislative and regulatory process and the ability to connect policy developments to client strategy and execution. • Excellent executive presence, writing, and communication skills, with the ability to brief clients, senior leaders, policymakers, and stakeholders clearly and persuasively. • Strong leadership and mentoring skills, with experience guiding staff, working across teams, and establishing repeatable processes. — ## Preferred Skills • Prior senior role in a federal agency, administration, congressional office, committee, trade association, corporation, public affairs firm, or advocacy organization. • Registered federal lobbying experience or direct management of federal lobbying programs. • Experience building coalitions on complex policy issues. • Experience with digital advocacy tools, grassroots activation, PAC or association advocacy, social listening, and paid media coordination. This role requires a practical mix of access, judgment, leadership, and execution. The right candidate will strengthen client programs, help build a durable government affairs capability, and expand Aristotle’s role as a trusted advocacy partner. — ## Salary Range $175k – $225k Base + Bonus — ## Benefits All positions are Full-Time, with competitive compensation, medical benefits, paid vacation, 401k plan and stock options. Casual dress code and a non-corporate atmosphere make this a fun place to work and learn in a team environment. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Senior Associate, Domestic Policy (P1)
item.description: Senior Associate, Domestic Policy (P1) Organization: Save the Children Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/21/2026 For over 100 years, Save the Children has been fighting for the rights of children. The right to a healthy start in life. To have access to education. To be in a safe environment, protected from harm. We work in some of the world’s hardest‑to‑reach places – over 100 countries, including the U.S. No matter what your role is, when you join Save the Children, you’re creating positive, irreversible change for children and the future we all share. **The Role** As the Senior Associate for Domestic Policy, you’ll be integral to our work in helping vulnerable children achieve a brighter future. You will support the advancement of Save the Children’s U.S. domestic policy objectives across key issue areas, including education (with a focus on the National Promise Neighborhoods Coalition), child care, nutrition, and rural development. This includes supporting efforts to influence Congress, the Administration, and other key stakeholders, as well as contributing to the development and implementation of Save the Children’s domestic policy and advocacy portfolio. The Senior Associate will also support policy research and analysis, stakeholder and coalition engagement, and coordination across internal teams to advance federal policy priorities. This role reports to the Managing Director, Domestic Policy and collaborates closely across Policy & Advocacy. **Location** Hybrid – Washington, DC office location — **What You’ll Be Doing (Essential Duties)** *Not inclusive of all role responsibilities. May be subject to change.* **Conduct policy research and analysis in support of the Domestic Policy Team’s policy priorities. (50%)** – At the direction of the Managing Director, Domestic Policy, conduct policy analysis and research related to Save the Children U.S.’s domestic policy priorities with Congress and the Administration. – Support development of policy and advocacy products for Save the Children, including those targeting U.S. policymakers, such as one‑pagers, issue summaries, and other documents. – Analyze and review policy research generated by coalition partners, aligned NGOs, and other organizations to inform Save the Children U.S.’s policy positions. – Attend coalition meetings and occasional Hill meetings. – Support Save the Children’s leadership of the National Promise Neighborhoods Coalition by advancing coalition policy priorities, supporting advocacy engagement with Congress and the Administration, and helping coordinate coalition‑driven policy efforts. **Provide political analysis support to the Domestic Policy Team. (30%)** – Track and keep team updated on Congressional and Administration policy developments including hearings, bill introductions, committee business meetings, agency announcements, and other developments as needed. – Monitor and update team on secondary policy areas that connect to SCUS policy priorities, SCUS strategy, or domestic campaigns. – Assist in congressional targeting, including compiling updated information about vote records and policy positions of key members of Congress. **Provide logistical and administrative support to the Domestic Policy Team. (20%)** – Contribute to operational needs of the Policy, Advocacy, and Campaigns division, including supporting procurement processes, tracking and coordinating internal reporting, and facilitating coordination across Save the Children teams, departments, and divisions. – Analyze government relations plans and next steps, including updated information about vote records and policy positions of key members of Congress. – Track Congressional and Administration policy developments including hearings, bill introductions, committee business meetings, agency announcements, and other developments as needed. – Support the management of interns, tracking related research and legislative projects. – Support the development and internal dissemination of policy and advocacy materials, as well as the planning and execution of strategic policy events, briefings, and convenings, including those related to the National Promise Neighborhoods Coalition. – Handle issues as they arise due to the ever‑evolving nature of advocacy for children in need. – Provide dedicated coordination and administrative support for the National Promise Neighborhoods Coalition, including member engagement, meeting logistics, materials development, and coalition communications. — **Required Qualifications for the Role** – Minimum of a High School Diploma or equivalent, plus at least 2 years of relevant experience – Demonstrated experience supporting government, government relations, policy, advocacy, or public affairs – Familiarity with federal policymaking and the federal legislative process – Proven analytical ability, including producing written analytical and research materials – Demonstrated persuasive and politically astute communication and networking skills with diverse audiences – Enthusiasm for advocacy and government relations work – Professional proficiency in MS Office suite – Professional proficiency in spoken and written English **Preferred Qualifications for the Role** – Experience organizing and executing events – Understanding of U.S. legislative process – Experience with child‑focused domestic policy, including (but not limited to) education, nutrition, or rural policy — **Compensation** Save the Children is offering the following salary ranges for this position, dependent on candidate location: – **Geo 1 – NY Metro, DC, and other high‑cost locations:** $60,775 – $67,925 base salary – **Geo 2 – U.S. National Labor Cost Average locations:** $53,975 – $60,325 base salary – **Geo 3 – Locations significantly below national labor cost average:** $49,725 – $55,575 base salary The salary ranges listed above are for U.S.‑based candidates. For candidates located outside the U.S., salary ranges will be based on the salary scales of the local employer of record. Actual base salary may vary based on relevant experience, internal equity, business sector, and geographic location. — **About Us** We are looking to build an inclusive team at Save the Children. We offer a range of outstanding benefits: – **Flexible schedules and time off:** generous PTO, 11 paid holidays, 2 floating holidays, hybrid work opportunities – **Health:** competitive medical, dental, and vision coverage – **Family:** paid caregiver, parental/adoption, critical child illness, and fertility benefits – **Employee Rewards Program:** annual merit increases and/or additional incentives for eligible employees – **Retirement:** employer contributions after one year – **Wellness:** 15 safety and wellness days annually (8 days if hired after July 1), mental health benefits via Calm, company‑hosted events – **Employee Assistance Program:** free and confidential assessments, counseling, referrals, and follow‑up services – **Learning & Growth:** internal and external learning opportunities and mentorships Save the Children is committed to conducting its programs and operations in a manner that is safe for the children it serves. All representatives are prohibited from engaging in any activity that may result in child abuse. Save the Children is committed to minimizing safety and security risks for employees, ensuring training, support, and information to reduce risk exposure while maximizing program impact. If you require disability assistance with the application or recruitment process, please submit a request to [email protected] . **Equal Opportunity Employer / Protected Veterans / Individuals with Disabilities** This employer is required to notify all applicants of their rights pursuant to federal employment laws. For further information, please review the *Know Your Rights* notice from the Department of Labor. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Senior Advocate, Southwest Power Pool
item.description: Senior Advocate, Southwest Power Pool Organization: Natural Resources Defense Council (NRDC) Location: Baltimore, MD | New York, NY | Washington, DC | Chicago, IL | San Francisco, CA | Santa Monica, CA Date Posted: 08/21/2026 ## About the job NRDC (the Natural Resources Defense Council) works to safeguard the Earth, its people, its plants and animals, and the natural systems on which all life depends. NRDC combines the power of more than 3 million members and online activists with the expertise of some 800 policy advocates, lawyers, scientists, and communication experts to confront the climate crisis, protect nature, ensure the rights of all people to clean air, clean water, and healthy communities. As an international nonprofit environmental organization, NRDC is working to address the world’s most urgent environmental challenges, and advance innovative, science-based, and enforceable solutions. Since our founding in 1970, NRDC has helped craft and deliver many of America’s foundational environmental laws, including the Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act and Safe Drinking Water Act. Today, we continue to lead in advancing and defending strong environmental protections at the local, state, federal and international levels, as well as through the marketplace. Our team works across the United States and around the world, from offices in Chicago, Los Angeles, New York City, San Francisco, and Washington, D.C., as well as in Beijing and New Delhi (a subsidiary of NRDC India Pvt. Ltd.). Supported by our members and online activists, NRDC is driving impactful solutions that confront the climate crisis, defend nature and safeguard public health across Asia, Africa, and the Americas. At NRDC, we believe lasting change happens when people bring their talent, passion, and expertise together for a common purpose: to build a cleaner, healthier, and more resilient world. Learn more at nrdc.org ## Position Summary The Senior Advocate – Southwest Power Pool will lead the advocacy of NRDC’s Sustainable FERC Project (Project) at the Southwest Power Pool (SPP). This person will be responsible for advancing reforms in transmission planning, resource adequacy, and wholesale markets to expand clean energy deployment and maximize the reliability and affordability of energy in the SPP region. This role requires experience with technical regulatory matters relating to transmission systems and/or energy markets, the ability to collaborate in a team setting with internal and external partners, interest in cultivating relationships with SPP staff, state regulators and other stakeholders, and willingness to travel to SPP’s offices in Arkansas and Colorado, and elsewhere. This is a limited term 2‑year position based out of any of NRDC’s U.S. offices (New York, DC, Chicago, San Francisco, Santa Monica). This role can also be fully remote for those who are not within a commutable distance of an NRDC office. If you live within a commutable distance of an NRDC office this role must adhere to our hybrid remote policy. The position you are applying for is part of the bargaining unit represented by The Washington Baltimore News Guild (WBNG / The Newsguild‑CWA Local 32035). ## Responsibilities To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the following essential functions: – Conceive and advocate for changes to SPP’s regional and interregional transmission, resource adequacy, wholesale markets, and interconnection rules and plans necessary to advance the Project’s and NRDC’s clean energy transition goals. Work to persuade key stakeholders and decision-makers to adopt NRDC’s preferred grid policies. – Develop and implement SPP stakeholder‑focused strategies necessary to advance goals and outcomes. – Periodically reassess existing desired outcomes and identify new outcomes and strategies to achieve NRDC’s goals on complex grid issues. – Represent the Project coalition and NRDC at SPP and in other forums. This advocacy includes participating in stakeholder meetings and conferences, including making verbal comments, drafting stakeholder and FERC comments, and other activities necessary to accomplish the Project’s advocacy goals. – Collaborate with a coalition of partners – including coordination leading regular meetings/calls, tracking of SPP issues, and organizing periodic strategic planning, as well as working to build agreement within the coalition on complex problems. – Build and maintain relationships with key stakeholders, especially SPP staff, state government officials, consumer advocates, and industry partners. – Coordinate with the Project’s staff and with other teams at NRDC to develop complementary solutions and to align goals, strategies, and messages. – Monitor relevant developments in other regional transmission organizations. – Manage expert consultants as necessary to advance the Project’s advocacy objectives. – Communicate the Project’s message to a wider audience, including media and state and federal policymakers, in a manner that translates complex and arcane grid rules into simple and understandable terms. The above list of duties is not comprehensive but generally demonstrates the types of matters under this position’s responsibility. Other duties may be assigned. ## Qualifications ### Minimum Education & Experience – A bachelor’s degree and a minimum of 7 years’ experience in a relevant field. – Experience with electricity regulation, especially wholesale power markets and transmission planning. ### Skills, Abilities, Competencies – Proficiency in understanding and communicating complex concepts. – Interest in cultivating relationships with partner organizations to advance the Project’s and NRDC’s goals. – Experience navigating diverse stakeholders, building consensus on policy issues, and driving toward positive outcomes within a team, in a coalition, and with other external partners. – Excellent writing skills and the ability to grasp and translate technical power grid issues into plain English. – Oral advocacy skills and experience; comfort speaking in varied settings, including with media. – Ability to work collaboratively across diverse stakeholders and cross‑functional teams towards shared outcomes. – A sense of mission and passion for public interest and environmental advocacy. – Ability to travel nationally including conferences and/or meetings convened by SPP and related entities, approximately 20% annually. – Commitment to NRDC’s mission, values, and principles of diversity, equity, and inclusion. ## Physical Demands The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this position. The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this position within the described work environment. Frequently: Perform desk‑based computer tasks Frequently: Ability to interact and communicate with employees and others as necessary Frequently: Attend planned meetings and collaborate with management and coworkers Frequently: Ability to attend events and activities in the office or offsite Work is sometimes performed in office. The noise level in the work environment is usually quiet in office settings and moderate in other situations. Hours of employment may sometimes require working flexible and/or longer hours, including nights and weekends, when necessitated by projects. The job includes work‑related situations such as those involving challenging, important, urgent, time‑sensitive, or multiple matters. NRDC is committed to advancing diversity, equity, and inclusion, both in our work and in our workplace. We believe that celebrating and actively welcoming diverse voices and perspectives is essential to solving the planet’s most pressing environmental problems, and we encourage applications from candidates whose identities have been historically under‑represented in the environmental movement. We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate in hiring or employment on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, marital status, sexual orientation, national origin, citizenship, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. We offer competitive salaries, excellent benefits, and a supportive working environment. Salary is based on a nonprofit scale and is commensurate with skills and experience. Internal equity will be reviewed and considered to determine a final offer. For this position, the salary range is $130,000 to $150,000. NRDC operates under a hybrid work model. Employees are required to come to the office 8 days per month. This role can also be fully remote for those who are not within a commutable distance of an NRDC office. If you live within a commutable distance of an NRDC office this role must adhere to our hybrid remote policy. To apply, visit [ www.nrdc.org/careers ] and upload your résumé and cover letter. Please mention where you saw this posting and upload any additional materials that showcase your abilities. Due to the high volume of applications, we will contact only those candidates we would like to interview. Please no phone calls, emails, or in‑person résumé drop‑offs. If you experience technical problems while applying or if you are a person with a disability and need assistance applying online, please reach out to iCIMS Customer Care at 1‑800‑889‑4422. item.title: Grassroots Advocacy Manager
item.description: Grassroots Advocacy Manager Organization: National Restaurant Association Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/21/2026 # The National Restaurant Association & Educational Foundation The National Restaurant Association and National Restaurant Association Educational Foundation are proud to be part of a highly respected industry, providing hospitality, opportunity, and quality of life. Much like the industry we represent, we have a dynamic, diverse, and inclusive culture, grounded in trust, hospitality, collaboration, and innovation. We have an exciting opportunity within our Public Affairs Department for a **Grassroots Advocacy Manager** to lead, develop, and elevate the Association’s grassroots and grasstops advocacy efforts at the federal, state, and local levels. This high‑impact role will help strengthen the Association’s position as a leading voice in national public policy and advocacy for the restaurant industry. The Grassroots Advocacy Manager oversees the Association’s flagship **Hill Runner program**, cultivating and managing relationships between restaurant operators and members of Congress in every congressional district across the country. The role is also responsible for driving the Association’s digital grassroots strategy through the **Quorum advocacy platform**, developing and executing national advocacy campaigns and action alerts that mobilize members around key federal policy priorities. In addition, this position serves as the primary strategist and liaison for **State Restaurant Association partners** on grassroots engagement initiatives, providing oversight and support for individual Quorum accounts and collaborating to enhance the effectiveness and reach of state‑level advocacy efforts. As the Public Affairs team lead for the Association’s annual **Public Affairs Conference fly‑in**, the Grassroots Advocacy Manager partners with cross‑functional stakeholders to plan and execute a successful event that brings industry leaders and advocates together to engage directly with policymakers. Ideal candidates bring a minimum of **three years of grassroots or political advocacy experience** with a strong focus on stakeholder engagement and mobilization. Experience working for a trade association, membership organization, or political campaign is highly desirable. The successful candidate is a confident communicator with exceptional writing, interpersonal, and presentation skills, combined with a data‑driven mindset and the ability to translate insights into effective advocacy strategies and outcomes. This position is based out of our **Washington, DC office** and requires onsite work Monday through Wednesday, with flexibility to work remotely on Thursday and Friday. The work you do to develop new ideas, programs, and initiatives will help strengthen the restaurant industry’s grassroots advocacy efforts and influence at the federal, state, and local levels. We look forward to hearing from you! — ## Application Link Interested applicants can apply with the link below: ` https://recruiting.ultipro.com/NAT1030/JobBoard/09a1b648-97bf-40dd-b3df-e884e92fc6b7/Opportunity/OpportunityDetail?opportunityId=371516ff-c197-40a4-8470-10088f95cf5e ` — ## Benefits We are proud to offer our team members comprehensive benefits designed to support their financial, professional, and personal well‑being. In addition to outstanding healthcare coverage (medical, dental, and vision), competitive salaries, generous vacation and leave time, we offer a matching 401(k) plan, a unique collection of corporate discounts and memberships, as well as programs to support career and skills development, learning and tuition assistance, and so much more. — # Responsibilities – **Grassroots advocacy leadership** — Enhance the Association’s grassroots advocacy efforts at the federal, state, and local levels. – **Hill Runner program management** — Lead the Association’s marquee grasstops advocacy program. – Recruit new Hill Runners nationwide in partnership with State Restaurant Associations, with a goal of reaching 535 Hill Runners. – Onboard, motivate, and maintain engagement with existing Hill Runners. – Develop unique content with the Public Affairs team to keep Hill Runners engaged. – Oversee the Summer of Action program focused on in‑person Hill Runner meetings with members of Congress. – Innovate new ways to activate Hill Runners for key advocacy engagements. – **Quorum platform oversight** — Oversee the Association’s relationship with Quorum, the grassroots advocacy and database platform. – Maintain account relationship with the Quorum team. – Manage the Association’s grassroots database (over 100,000 advocates). – Collaborate with the communications team to develop and execute grassroots emails and activations. – Strategize ways to enhance and grow grassroots engagement via Quorum. – Manage relationships between Quorum, the Association, and State Restaurant Association accounts; support SRAs in enhancing their use of Quorum. – **Public Affairs Conference leadership** — Serve as the Public Affairs team’s point person for the annual fly‑in conference. – Collaborate closely with the events team to organize and hold planning meetings. – Manage deliverables throughout the year. – Strategize with Public Affairs, Communications, and Events teams to enhance the conference. – Organize unique Hill Runner programming during the conference. – **State grassroots collaboration** — Analyze and enhance grassroots efforts of State Restaurant Association partners. – **Advocacy event planning** — Work with Public Affairs and State Restaurant Associations to plan and execute in‑state Restaurant Roundtables and other advocacy events. – **RestaurantsAct.com oversight** — Maintain and enhance the Association’s external advocacy website. – **Industry representation** — Speak on behalf of the Association at industry and state events. – **Data management** — Oversee team data collection and management. – **Drafting and reporting** — Draft correspondence, reports, and presentations. – **Department recordkeeping** — Assist with maintaining department records, including invoice processing. — # Requirements – **Bachelor’s degree** in political science, government relations, public policy, or equivalent. – **Minimum 3 years of grassroots advocacy or related political advocacy experience**, focusing on stakeholder mobilization. – **Knowledge of grassroots advocacy software**, such as Quorum, preferred. – **Highly collaborative and accountable**, with strong interpersonal and diplomacy skills. – **Creative thinker** able to develop and implement new grassroots and public affairs strategies. – **Confident communicator**, skilled in writing, public speaking, and presentations. – **Intellectual horsepower, emotional intelligence, and curiosity.** – **Exceptional analytical and critical thinking skills.** – **Strong prioritization and project management abilities**, able to manage multiple deliverables and deadlines. – **Highly effective organizational and time‑management skills.** – **Adaptable and resilient**, responsive to change and able to lead as a change agent. – **Ability to work independently and as part of a team**; self‑initiator, versatile, and responsible. – **Ability to engage confidently at all organizational levels.** – **Proficiency in Microsoft Office** (Word, PowerPoint, Outlook, Excel) and ability to learn additional software programs. – **Ability to travel 1–4 times per year.** — # Equal Opportunity Employer / Protected Veterans / Individuals with Disabilities The National Restaurant Association, National Restaurant Association Solutions, LLC, and The National Restaurant Association Educational Foundation (“Company”) are committed to equal employment opportunity, and it is Company’s policy to take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment protected veterans and individuals with disabilities. It is our policy to recruit, hire, train, and promote persons in all job titles, and ensure that all other personnel actions are administered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. All employment decisions are based solely on valid job requirements. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Manager/Senior Manager, Community Outreach and Engagement
item.description: Manager/Senior Manager, Community Outreach and Engagement Organization: Multiple Myeloma Research Foundation (MMRF) Location: Norwalk, CT Date Posted: 08/24/2026 **Title: Manager/Senior Manager, Community Outreach and Engagement** **Reports to:** Senior Director, Community Engagement and Partnerships **Department:** Community Outreach and Engagement **Location:** Norwalk, CT (or Remote) **MMRF OVERVIEW:** The Multiple Myeloma Research Foundation (MMRF) is the largest nonprofit in the world solely focused on accelerating a cure for each and every multiple myeloma patient. We drive the development and delivery of next-generation therapies, leverage data to identify optimal and more personalized treatment approaches, and empower myeloma patients and the broader community with information and resources to extend their lives. Central to our mission is our commitment to advancing health equity so that all myeloma patients can benefit from the scientific and clinical advances we pursue. Since our inception, the MMRF has committed over $600 million for research, opened nearly 100 clinical trials, and helped bring 15+ FDA-approved therapies to market, which have tripled the life expectancy of myeloma patients. To learn more, visit [www.themmrf.org]. **MMRF Core Values:** At the MMRF our core values define both who we are and how we work together as an organization. We believe in investing in our team and building a culture that will help us pursue our highest level mission to accelerate a cure for each and every multiple myeloma patient. Our five core values are expressed below: 1. **Prioritize Patients** – Patients are at the center of everything we do. Every decision we make is grounded in the needs and best interests of the patients we serve. 2. **Drive Innovation** – We are committed to pursuing big, bold ideas. Taking risks, trying new approaches, and challenging the status quo are necessary to speed new discoveries. 3. **Deliver Solutions** – Taking on complicated challenges is what sets us apart. To deliver results, we must be decisive, take action, and act with urgency on behalf of the myeloma community. 4. **Do It Together** – We know that together, we are stronger. We work cross-functionally with the entire community to achieve our mission and are invested in the success of others. 5. **Build Trust** – We build trust-based relationships. We advocate for each and every myeloma patient by committing to diversity, equity, and inclusion and treating others with respect. **Position Overview:** The MMRF is seeking a passionate and mission-driven professional dedicated to improving health outcomes for all patients and community members, with a particular focus on those historically underserved by the healthcare system. This individual will serve as a trusted partner to both internal and external stakeholders, fostering meaningful, high-impact relationships that prioritize patients, strengthen trust and accelerate patient-centered innovation. The ideal candidate brings demonstrated experience in community outreach and engagement within a healthcare setting, along with a proven ability to collaborate strategically with cross-functional teams and external partners. This role requires strong project management capabilities, and a track record of consistent operational execution. The candidate will have direct experience engaging with patients, caregivers, healthcare professionals and community-based organizations. Critical to success in this role is the ability to build trust, gain insight into barriers impacting underserved populations, and identify practical, scalable solutions to improve engagement. This individual will establish, grow, and sustain multi-stakeholder, community-based partnerships in support of the MMRF’s mission and commitment to advancing health equity. **Manager/Senior Manager, Community Outreach and Engagement** **Essential Functions:** • Partner with the Senior Director of Community Engagement and Partnerships to build and sustain relationships with key stakeholders, including but not limited to academic medical centers, community health centers and community-based organizations. • Support the identification, development, and dissemination of MMRF educational and communication assets that resonate with targeted communities; collaborate with stakeholders to measure reach and impact. • In collaboration with the Senior Director, develop and execute a comprehensive engagement strategy to build trust, expand reach, and drive meaningful participation, with a focus on improving outcomes for traditionally underserved communities. • Develop and maintain authentic, trust-based relationships with patients, caregivers, healthcare professionals, and community partners. • Support the planning and execution of the annual MMRF Annual Summit. • Oversee community engagement operations, including budget management, external partner engagement and coordination, and vendor management. • Identify and establish strategic partnerships with key health equity and community stakeholders to advance MMRF initiatives. • Develop, implement, and manage innovative community engagement and awareness building programs. • Serve periodically as a moderator, emcee, or presenter at community events. • Collaborate with the MMRF’s Marketing team to develop patient- and community-facing materials and manage internal and external review and approval processes. • Evaluate outreach programming through data analysis and landscape assessments; provide actionable recommendations to enhance and optimize MMRF engagement programs and services. • Oversee the Myeloma Mentors and MMRF Volunteers programs to drive meaningful engagement and support for patients and caregivers. • Conduct landscape analysis of potential vendors and partners for consideration by MMRF. • Represent the MMRF at meetings, conferences, and community events. • Ability and willingness to travel domestically, up to 20%, including occasional weekends. **Qualifications:** • Bachelor’s degree required in a health- or communications-related field; master’s degree preferred • At least 5 years of experience in project and vendor management required; experience with Asana or Wrike preferred • Self-starter with a proven ability to develop and implement innovative strategies and interventions • At least 5 years of experience building and maintaining partnerships with community-based organizations, healthcare facilities, academic institutions, and similar stakeholders • At least 3 years of experience in community activation • At least 3 years of experience working directly with patients and caregivers • Excellent presentation skills, with the ability to engage diverse audiences, including community groups, healthcare professionals, and leadership; ability to serve as a moderator, emcee, or presenter at community events • Experience managing individuals, including volunteers, interns, students, and employees • Excellent written, verbal and interpersonal communication skills • Proven ability to manage multiple priorities and workstreams simultaneously in a fast-paced environment • Highly organized with strong attention to detail • Ability to collaborate effectively in a team-oriented environment • Demonstrated ability to think strategically while executing with agility and accountability • Strong project planning and management skills including problem solving and risk mitigation • High level of emotional intelligence, with the ability to build high levels of trust and foster strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders • Proven track record of building and sustaining partnerships and coalitions with measurable impact • Natural connector with the ability to bring people together in a meaningful and productive way • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite **EEO Statement:** The Multiple Myeloma Research Foundation (MMRF) is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate against any candidate based on race, religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, marital status, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, age, military and veteran status, sexual orientation, or any other factor protected by federal, state, or local law. The MMRF does not sponsor/facilitate any type of work authorization for this role. All applicants must currently have original valid unrestricted authorization to accept new employment in any role in the U.S. with any employer. There is also no future employer-provided sponsorship for this role to obtain or extend authorization to work in the U.S. Email [email protected] for more information on how to apply. item.title: Assistant Director Transplant Quality and Regulatory (JR233182)
item.description: Assistant Director Transplant Quality and Regulatory (JR233182) Organization: Montefiore Einstein Medical Center Location: Bronx, NY Date Posted: 08/24/2026 ## To heal, to teach, to discover and to advance the health of the communities we serve. To learn more about the “Montefiore Difference” – who we are at Montefiore and all that we have to offer our associates, please click here. **Company:** Montefiore **Location:** Bronx, New York **Level:** Full time **Compensation:** $138,400.00 – $173,000.00 **Job Family:** Transplant – Abdominal Administration **Industry:** Health Care — ## Overview The Assistant Director of Transplant Quality & Regulatory is a subject matter expert responsible for directing and overseeing transplant quality, regulatory compliance, patient safety, and data management activities across the solid organ transplant programs. This role works collaboratively with physician, clinical, operational, and administrative leadership, as well as with Risk Management, Compliance, Information Technology, and Quality & Safety departments, to support regulatory readiness, performance improvement, and high‑quality patient‑centered care throughout the transplant continuum. The Assistant Director oversees a comprehensive transplant quality and compliance program focused on adherence to all applicable regulatory and accreditation requirements, including those established by the Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network / United Network for Organ Sharing, Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients, and The Joint Commission. This includes oversight of quality assessment and performance improvement (QAPI) activities, patient safety initiatives, clinical performance metrics, regulatory audits and inspections, adverse event review, corrective action planning, and continuous process improvement initiatives. This role provides strategic oversight and operational leadership for the transplant data management team, ensuring accurate and timely regulatory reporting, data integrity, dashboard development, analytics, and integration of transplant‑related data across internal and external reporting systems including Epic Systems, Phoenix, UNOS, and SRTR platforms. The Assistant Director serves as a key resource to transplant leadership and is authorized to access all transplant program functions, records, and operational areas relevant to quality, compliance, and patient safety activities under review. The position serves as a key driver in advancing a culture of regulatory excellence, accountability, innovation, interdisciplinary collaboration, and continuous quality improvement to support optimal patient outcomes and organizational performance. — ## Schedule 8 AM – 4:30 PM, Monday–Friday — ## Responsibilities – Oversee and monitor all aspects of the transplant quality and compliance program, including policies, procedures, and protocols. – Develop and implement a comprehensive transplant quality and compliance program in accordance with regulatory standards and guidelines. – Establish and implement written policies to identify, report, analyze, and address transplant‑related adverse events. Actively participates in Quality Review processes, Root Cause Analysis, case debriefings, and medical staff Morbidity & Mortality (M&M) meetings to assess situations, identify potential improvements, and respond to grievances, patient complaints, and regulatory inquiries. – Conduct regular audits and reviews to ensure compliance with regulatory standards and identify areas for improvement. – Collaborate with medical staff, administrators, and other stakeholders to develop and implement quality improvement initiatives. – Facilitate solid organ transplant‑specific quality and P&P meeting structure, including scheduling, coordinating, developing agendas with program directors, taking minutes as needed, distributing documents, preparing and presenting presentations, and ensuring accuracy and timeliness of information. – Utilize tools to track Performance Improvement activities and CAPs, Adverse Events, Transplant Dashboards (Operational and Clinical outcomes), Patient Complaints, and Policy Stat. – Work together with the Data team to keep tools up to date and assess for accuracy. – Responsible for accurate and timely submission of data to UNOS (TIEDI forms), Renal Network, and timely review of data in the SRTR. Audit the integrity of data entered by transplant teams to ensure regulatory compliance within EPIC EMR for Transplant Coordinators. – Retrieve and integrate transplant data with numerous internal and external systems (EMR/Phoenix, SRTR, UNOS) for transplant leadership and physician providers. – Serve as subject matter expert (SME) for EPIC Phoenix; work closely with the EPIC team, OR team, and Phoenix team to ensure all regulatory data is captured within the system. – Provide leadership and direction to the transplant data management team, including hiring, training, and performance evaluations. – Develop and maintain relationships with regulatory agencies and participate in audits and inspections. – Stay up‑to‑date on industry best practices and changes in regulatory standards related to transplant quality and compliance. – Communicate and collaborate with other departments and teams within the medical center to promote a culture of quality and compliance. – Serve as a resource and subject matter expert on transplant quality and compliance for medical center staff. – Prepare and present reports to senior leadership and stakeholders on the progress and outcomes of the transplant quality and compliance program. – Identify and address any compliance issues or concerns in a timely and effective manner. – Foster a culture of continuous improvement, innovation, and excellence within the transplant program. – Ensure confidentiality and security of all patient information in accordance with HIPAA regulations. – Serve as a liaison between the medical center and external organizations, such as regulatory agencies, professional associations, and transplant networks. — ## Requirements – Master’s degree required. – 4–6 years Nursing experience required. – 4–6 years Transplant experience required. – New York State Registered Professional License and current registration or valid permit to practice in New York State required. – Proficient leadership skills and ability to effectively communicate with various stakeholders, including transplant surgeons, nurses, and administrative staff. – Proficient in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. – Excellent written and oral communication; proficient editing skills and strong attention to detail. item.title: Assistant General Counsel, Privacy
item.description: Assistant General Counsel, Privacy Organization: Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSK) Location: New York, NY Date Posted: 08/24/2026 Job details About Us: The people of Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSK) are united by a singular mission: ending cancer for life. Our specialized care teams provide personalized, compassionate, expert care to patients of all ages. Informed by basic research done at our Sloan Kettering Institute, scientists across MSK collaborate to conduct innovative translational and clinical research that is driving a revolution in our understanding of cancer as a disease and improving the ability to prevent, diagnose, and treat it. MSK is dedicated to training the next generation of scientists and clinicians, who go on to pursue our mission at MSK and around the globe. Exciting Opportunity at MSK: Help shape the future of global privacy, data governance, and responsible AI at one of the world’s leading cancer centers. Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSK) is seeking an experienced privacy attorney to join our Privacy team and help advance a mature, practical, and globally informed privacy program in support of our mission of Ending Cancer for Life. This mid-level attorney position reports to the VP, Privacy Officer & Chief Privacy Counsel, sits within the Compliance Department with a dotted-line relationship to Legal, and advises on sophisticated privacy, digital health, research, AI, and data governance matters across the enterprise. Role Overview: The Assistant General Counsel – Privacy serves as a trusted advisor to clinical, research, technology, compliance, procurement, information security, and business leaders across MSK. You’ll provide practical legal guidance on GDPR and other global privacy frameworks, HIPAA, digital health, AI governance, research, vendor relationships, and emerging technologies while helping support responsible innovation throughout the organization. Key Responsibilities: Advise on U.S. and global privacy and data protection matters involving personal information, protected health information (PHI), and other sensitive data. Manage and enhance MSK’s GDPR compliance program, including data subject rights, DPIAs, ROPAs, cross-border data transfers, privacy-by-design, de-identification, and anonymization. Partner with clinical, research, IT, digital, procurement, information security, development, marketing, and operational teams to provide practical privacy guidance for strategic initiatives, research, technology implementations, and business operations. Negotiate and advise on Business Associate Agreements, data protection agreements, vendor contracts, research agreements, and other privacy-related contractual matters. Draft and maintain privacy notices, policies, procedures, guidance documents, and training materials while supporting digital privacy initiatives and regulatory compliance. Advise the AI Governance Council and enterprise stakeholders on privacy considerations related to AI-enabled tools, data governance, and responsible innovation. Monitor evolving U.S. and international privacy laws and translate complex legal requirements into practical, business-focused recommendations. Collaborate with Legal and Compliance colleagues to strengthen enterprise privacy governance, risk management, documentation, and operational processes. Key Qualifications: Required Juris Doctor degree. Licensed to practice law in New York State or eligible for in-house counsel registration. 5–7 years of privacy or data protection legal experience in a law firm, in-house legal department, healthcare organization, government agency, or comparable environment. Strong experience advising on GDPR, including global privacy compliance, HIPAA, and U.S. privacy laws, vendor contracting, digital privacy, cookies, trackers and data governance. Demonstrated ability to provide practical legal advice, negotiate complex agreements, and communicate effectively with multidisciplinary stakeholders. Preferred Experience supporting healthcare, life sciences, research organizations, hospitals, or academic medical centers. Familiarity with human subjects research. Experience advising on AI, conducting AI risk assessments. Familiarity with TCPA, CAN-SPAM, and consumer privacy laws. CIPP/US, CIPP/E, CIPM, AIGP, or similar privacy certification. Additional Information: Report directly to the VP, Privacy Officer & Chief Privacy Counsel. Location: 633 Third Avenue, New York, NY; Flexibility to travel to other local sites as needed Hybrid (approximately one day per week onsite) Why Join MSK? Privacy plays a critical role in advancing patient care, groundbreaking research, digital innovation, and responsible AI at Memorial Sloan Kettering. This position offers the opportunity to influence enterprise privacy strategy while partnering with world-renowned clinicians, researchers, technologists, and executive leaders on some of healthcare’s most complex privacy challenges. Candidates who meet many, but not every, listed qualification are encouraged to apply. We value intellectual curiosity, sound judgment, practical problem-solving, and the ability to build trusted relationships across a mission-driven organization. Pay Range: $137,500.00 – $227,000.00 FSLA Status: Exempt Closing: At MSK, we believe in fair, competitive pay that reflects your job, experience, and skills. MSK is an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer committed to diversity and inclusion in all aspects of recruiting and employment. All qualified individuals are encouraged to apply and will receive consideration without regard to race, color, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, religion, creed, disability, veteran status or any other factor which cannot lawfully be used as a basis for an employment decision. Federal law requires employers to provide reasonable accommodation to qualified individuals with disabilities. Please tell us if you require a reasonable accommodation to apply for a job or to perform your job. Examples of reasonable accommodation include making a change to the application process or work procedures, providing documents in an alternate format, using a sign language interpreter, or using specialized equipment. item.title: Senior Director, Sustainability
item.description: Senior Director, Sustainability Organization: National Cattlemen’s Beef Association (NCBA) Location: Centennial, CO Date Posted: 08/24/2026 **Pay** $145,000.00 – $155,000.00 per Year **Department** Producer Education & Sustainability **Experience** Intermediate **Job Description** **SUMMARY** Responsible for the collaborative and strategic leadership of National Cattlemen’s Beef Association sustainability programs and initiatives. This role serves as the executive director for the U.S. Roundtable for Sustainable Beef (USRSB) through an administrative agreement with NCBA. In these roles, the Senior Director of Sustainability serves as a beef sustainability champion through strategic planning, tactical execution, and fostering collaborative working relationships with cattle producers, processors, retail & food service companies, researchers, state and breed partners, and other industry stakeholders to drive positive sustainability outcomes and continuous improvement. **ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS** An employee in this position may be called upon to do any or all of the following essential functions. These examples do not include all of the functions which the employee may be expected to perform. – Collaborative leadership of NCBA’s sustainability goals and supporting programs. – Serves as Executive Director of U.S. Roundtable for Sustainable Beef, providing leadership, operational oversight, and implementation of the USRSB strategic plan. – Leads management of direct reports in support of USRSB and NCBA sustainability activities. – Coordinates with NCBA staff to support sustainability-related initiatives, including grant development and administration, sustainability strategy, and stakeholder engagement. – Facilitates consensus-based decision making among diverse stakeholder groups to advance the mission, vision, and goals of USRSB. – Coordinates and supports the activities of the USRSB Board of Directors, Working Groups, Task Forces, and membership. – Collaborates with universities, research institutions, funding organizations (e.g., Foundation for Food & Agriculture Research), and industry partners to identify and pursue research and grant opportunities that advance industry sustainability objectives. – Leads the implementation and evaluation of the USRSB strategic plan, annual plan of work, and supporting budgets. – Coordinates development of communications, educational resources, reports, presentations, webinars, and outreach materials supporting USRSB initiatives and stakeholder engagement. – Serves as spokesperson and representative for the cattle industry at relevant industry meetings, conferences, workshops, and stakeholder events. – Collaborates with the NCBA checkoff-funded sustainability research team to understand and leverage collective research efforts and outcomes. – Serves as the USRSB liaison to the Global Roundtable on Sustainable Beef. – Proactively engages to ensure adopted initiatives support the beef industry Long Range Plan and lead to improved beef industry sustainability. – Collaboratively engages with internal sustainability team on stakeholder relationships both domestically and internationally. – Travel up to 50% of the time is expected. – Other job duties as assigned. **MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS** **EDUCATION** Master’s degree in business, animal science, agri-business, sustainable agriculture, pasture & range science, or a related field is required; a Ph.D. is a positive attribute but not required. **EXPERIENCE** Must have a thorough understanding of beef industry and beef sustainability with a minimum of 8 years of beef industry or related experience. **EQUIVALENCY** None **CERTIFICATION(S)** None **SKILLS** Needs to be strategic, respected, and knowledgeable, able to bring vision and strategy to life. Must be able to effectively interface with beef producers, beef industry partners and stakeholders, the research community, and government personnel. Must possess a strong background in working within a multidisciplinary group of professionals and industry representatives. Must have the ability to bring consensus to group decision making. Must have ability to help set future direction in organizational planning by effectively communicating new/current plans to staff and industry. Excellent communications and public speaking skills are required. In addition, the individual must have strong organization skills, be a self-starter, and demonstrate a strong ability to work on multiple projects in a demanding team environment. **Company Description** Initiated in 1898, the National Cattlemen’s Beef Association is the marketing organization and trade association for America’s one million cattle farmers and ranchers. With offices in Denver and Washington, D.C., NCBA is a consumer-focused, producer-directed organization representing the largest segment of the nation’s food and fiber industry. NCBA works to achieve the vision: “To be the trusted leader and definitive voice of the U.S. cattle and beef industry.” **Benefits** Health Insurance Dental Insurance Vision Insurance Paid Vacation 401(k) with Company Match Life Insurance Long-Term Disability Short-Term Disability Sick Time **EEO Statement** It is our intention that all qualified applicants be given equal opportunity and that selection decisions be based on job-related factors. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability, or any other status protected by law or regulation. Be aware that none of the questions are intended to imply illegal preferences or discrimination based on non-job-related information. The position is expected to stay open until the posted close date. Please submit your application as soon as possible as the posting is subject to close at any time once a sufficient pool of qualified applicants is obtained. **Colorado Residents** In any materials you submit, you may redact or remove age-identifying information such as age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution. You will not be penalized for redacting or removing this information. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Industry Relations Program Manager
item.description: Industry Relations Program Manager Organization: American Soybean Association (ASA) Location: St. Louis, MO Date Posted: 08/24/2026 ## Industry Relations Program Manager **Location:** St. Louis, Missouri (Hybrid – minimum 3 days per week in the office) **Position Type:** Full-Time, Exempt **Travel:** Approximately 25% domestic travel ## About the American Soybean Association The American Soybean Association (ASA) is the national trade association representing nearly 500,000 U.S. soybean farmers across 30 soybean‑producing states. For more than 100 years, ASA has advocated for soybean growers on domestic policy, international trade, and issues affecting the success of U.S. agriculture. Headquartered in St. Louis, Missouri, ASA works with farmer leaders, industry partners, sponsors, and stakeholders to advance policies and programs that strengthen the soybean industry. ## Position Summary The American Soybean Association is seeking an experienced and highly organized **Industry Relations Program Manager** to join our Industry Relations team. This position is responsible for managing leadership development programs, industry meetings, sponsor‑funded initiatives, educational events, and stakeholder engagement activities that support ASA’s mission and fundraising efforts. The Program Manager works collaboratively with internal staff, sponsors, vendors, state affiliates, and industry partners to ensure programs are delivered professionally, on time, and within budget. The ideal candidate is a proactive project manager who enjoys building relationships, coordinating complex initiatives, and delivering exceptional experiences for members, sponsors, and industry partners. ## Key Responsibilities ### Program Management – Lead the planning, coordination, and execution of assigned leadership development programs, educational initiatives, meetings, and industry events. – Develop project plans, timelines, budgets, and performance metrics. – Monitor program progress and identify opportunities for continuous improvement. – Ensure successful delivery of sponsor commitments and grant‑funded program requirements. ### Meetings & Events – Manage all aspects of meetings and events, including registration, attendee communications, travel logistics, venues, vendors, audiovisual services, shipping, signage, and onsite execution. – Coordinate participant materials, agendas, presentations, and meeting resources. – Provide onsite leadership during ASA meetings, conferences, leadership programs, and Commodity Classic. ### Sponsor & Industry Relations – Build and maintain strong relationships with sponsors, industry partners, vendors, and stakeholders. – Support sponsorship development, proposal preparation, stewardship, and reporting. – Assist with identifying opportunities to strengthen partnerships and increase revenue. ### Communications – Coordinate communications with sponsors, participants, state affiliates, and industry partners. – Assist in developing newsletters, marketing materials, presentations, and program reports. – Maintain accurate CRM records, participant databases, and program documentation. ### Financial & Administrative Support – Manage assigned program budgets and reporting requirements. – Review invoices, purchase requests, contracts, and vendor agreements. – Coordinate inventory, shipping, and departmental project documentation. – Support cross‑functional collaboration across ASA departments. ## Qualifications ### Required – Bachelor’s degree in Business, Marketing, Communications, Political Science, Agriculture, Agricultural Business, or a related field. – Five or more years of progressively responsible experience in program management, meetings and events, nonprofit association management, communications, fundraising, agriculture, or a related field. – Strong project management and organizational skills. – Excellent written, verbal, and presentation communication skills. – Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines while working independently. – Proficiency with Microsoft 365 applications. – Valid driver’s license and ability to travel domestically. ### Preferred – Knowledge of row crop agriculture and agricultural organizations. – Experience working with sponsors, volunteers, vendors, and industry stakeholders. – Experience with CRM systems, preferably Salesforce. – Budget management and contract administration experience. ## What We Offer – Competitive salary based on experience – Annual bonus opportunity – Comprehensive medical, dental, vision, and life insurance – 401(k) with employer match – Paid vacation, sick leave, and holidays, including the week between Christmas and New Year’s – Hybrid work environment – A collaborative team dedicated to supporting U.S. soybean farmers ## Equal Employment Opportunity The American Soybean Association is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other status protected by applicable law. item.description: Director of Public Policy, Trade & Supply Chain Organization: National Corn Growers Association (NCGA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/24/2026 ## Summary NCGA’s Director, Public Policy – Trade & Supply Chain is responsible for lobbying, building, and maintaining coalitions and relationships beneficial to the corn industry. **Reports to:** NCGA Vice President, Public Policy — ## Duties and Responsibilities – Lobbying the Congress, the Administration, and various departments and agencies on trade, biotechnology, and other critical supply chain issues. – Building and maintaining coalitions beneficial to the corn industry and NCGA policy, specifically the Agricultural Coalition for USMCA. – Keeping Action Team members, Corn Board members, officers, and staff informed of developments regarding issues and NCGA efforts. – Acting as spokesperson for the organization for issue areas to various audiences. – Supporting staff for NCGA Trade Transportation and Animal Agriculture Action Team and Production and Sustainability Action Team. Organize activities of grower team responsible for NCGA trade/market access efforts. – Collaborating with staff from U.S. Grains and Bioproducts Council to advance international market development and grower trade education. – Collaborating with Corn Board members, Action Team members, national and state staff, industry colleagues, and policymakers on input supply chain issues. – Managing outreach and bridge‑building with Embassies of trading partners. – Staff lead for MAIZALL international biotech initiative. — ## Qualifications and Skills – Excellent interpersonal and listening skills. – Excellent writing and oral presentation skills. – Ability to work in collaborative team setting in a competitive industry. – Ability to work with constantly changing priorities and under challenging timelines. – Ability to manage activities of grower members and leaders. – Able to work independently and make educated decisions. – Organized, detail‑oriented, and good at time management. – Experience in dealing with media. – Must maintain confidentiality. – Willingness/Ability to work in a bipartisan fashion. – Familiarity with agriculture, the food system, and/or trade. — ## Education/Experience – Bachelor’s degree in related field. – At least seven years of experience on Capitol Hill, Federal/State government, or equivalent. — ## Travel Requires travel (15%). Valid passport and ability to travel outside the United States. Must have a valid driver’s license and good driving record. — ## Position Type/Location Full‑Time / Washington, DC — ## Compensation & Benefits **Salary:** $150,000 to $185,000, commensurate with experience. **Benefits:** Access to Health, Dental, Vision, Life, Short‑term & Long‑term Disability coverages, and 401k plan. — ## NCGA is an equal opportunity employer The National Corn Growers Association is committed to cultivating a diverse workforce and a culture of inclusivity and belonging. Our goal is to attract qualified candidates and encourage applications from all individuals without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. item.title: Policy and Project Manager
item.description: Policy and Project Manager Organization: Corn Refiners Association (CRA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/24/2026 ## The Corn Refiners Association (CRA) The Corn Refiners Association (CRA) represents the corn wet‑milling industry in the United States. Wet milling allows corn to be turned into sweeteners, starch, advanced bioproducts, and feed products from corn components such as oil, protein, and fiber. CRA also administers the Plant Based Products Council (PBPC), an organization launched by CRA in 2019 that represents companies manufacturing or using non‑food products and materials made from renewable, plant‑based inputs. The Policy and Project Manager provides project, membership, communications, and operational support to both the Corn Refiners Association (CRA) and the Plant Based Products Council (PBPC). This role is ideal for an early‑career professional who enjoys managing multiple priorities, creating content, supporting member engagement, and contributing to mission‑driven work in a collaborative, fast‑paced association environment. The successful candidate will be highly organized, digitally savvy, detail‑oriented, and motivated to develop expertise in association management, public policy, and member communications. — ## Primary Responsibilities ### Project & Administrative Support Manage the Carbohydrate Check Sample Program (CCSP), a member‑benefit program for validating laboratory methods used in testing corn wet‑milled products. Oversee participant registration, communications with vendors, coordination of program activities, and ensure all parties have required information. Assist the Trade Policy Vice President with the weekly Trade Update and other publications as needed. Assist policy staff with policy research, meeting support, recording key details and action items, and other projects as assigned. Manage various projects, in whole or in part, while ensuring timely completion and follow‑through. Perform other duties and special projects as assigned. ### Membership & Engagement Support Support Plant Based Products Council (PBPC) membership recruitment and engagement efforts, including prospect outreach, tracking engagement activities, and maintaining recruitment materials. Assist with PBPC member onboarding, including coordinating welcome materials, maintaining member records, and supporting retention activities. Maintain accurate membership data and records and assist with administrative processes related to membership management. Provide administrative support for member programs, webinars, events, and committee activities. ### Communications & Digital Content Support Support the creative development of digital and graphic assets for association communications and outreach initiatives. Drive content production for newsletters, factsheets, one‑pagers, social media content, website updates, presentations, and other public‑facing materials. Manage the organization’s website and digital communication channels, ensuring content remains current and aligned with organizational priorities. Assist the Senior Director of Communications with daily news monitoring and tracking issues important to the organization and its membership. Provide cross‑functional communications support across departments, helping to coordinate messaging and promotional activities. Assist with event communications, marketing materials, member announcements, and organizational publications. — ## Requirements Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Outlook, SharePoint, Excel, and Word. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Excellent organizational and time‑management abilities and attention to detail. Strong problem‑solving and collaboration skills. Ability to work independently while also contributing effectively in a team environment. Self‑starter with a proactive, solution‑oriented mindset. Bachelor’s degree preferred. — ## Preferred Skills & Qualifications Understanding of trade association operations, membership programs, and member engagement processes is a plus. Interest in public policy, international trade, manufacturing, agriculture, sustainability, or advanced bioproducts is preferred. Strong writing, editing, and proofreading skills, with the ability to tailor content for different audiences. Experience managing websites, digital communication platforms, and social media channels is a plus. Familiarity with graphic design tools, content management systems, or digital marketing platforms is desirable. Demonstrated ability to prioritize work, manage competing deadlines, and maintain high‑quality results in a fast‑paced environment. Proactive organizational skills with excellent follow‑through and a positive attitude. Strong interpersonal and relationship‑building skills, with the ability to collaborate across teams and support senior leaders while taking initiative on independently owned projects. Digitally fluent, detail‑oriented, and eager to learn and grow within a dynamic policy and membership organization. — ## Culture Our organizations place a heavy emphasis on culture. Our work is highly collaborative, action‑oriented, and fast‑paced in implementation of team‑developed strategic workplans. We strive to enjoy our work and consistently be transparent, inclusive, accountable, and professional. We believe that we are a “team of leaders” who “share the problem” to collaborate and achieve success. This is a full‑time employment position in an office environment. CRA has a hybrid work environment which requires in‑office work and local residency in the Washington, DC metro area. — ## Benefits Salary commensurate with experience. Best‑in‑class benefits offered, including health insurance plan, life insurance as well as short‑ and long‑term disability insurance; 401(k); sick, vacation, and holiday leave; public transit assistance. We embrace continuous learning and support our team in efforts to grow and develop professionally and personally. To apply please submit a cover letter and resume to [email protected] . Please include “Project and Policy Manager” in the subject line. — ## Equal Employment Opportunity All employment decisions shall be made without regard to age, race, creed, color, religion, sex, national origin, ancestry, disability status, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, citizenship status or any other basis as protected by federal, state, or local law.
