item.title: Senior IP Counsel
item.description: Senior IP Counsel Organization: FIS Location: Jacksonville, FL Date Posted: 08/27/2026 ## Position Type Full time ## Type Of Hire Experienced (relevant combo of work and education) ## Job Description The world of finance moves fast. At FIS, we’re faster. Our teams are empowered to learn, grow, and make an impact–in their careers and communities. We deliver innovation that advances the way the world pays, banks and invests. If you want to grow personally and professionally, we’d like to know: Are you FIS? ## About the role In this Senior IP Counsel role, you will manage complex legal matters to protect FIS’ intellectual property assets, with an expanded leadership focus on patent strategy, IP litigation and disputes, patent portfolio development, and the rapidly evolving domain of AI law and governance. You will partner closely with business leaders, technologists, and product teams to guide innovation pathways, ensuring alignment between business objectives, patent filings, and responsible AI practices. Your core responsibilities will include leading patent prosecution strategy; identifying high‑value innovations; and advising on AI‑related risk, compliance, data governance, and other legal considerations. You will also continue to support the business on traditional IP matters, including software licensing, open-source use, trade secrets, and related litigation. ## About the team The FIS Legal team consists of approximately 200 attorneys and paraprofessionals worldwide who collaborate closely with business units to advance enterprise goals. We work pragmatically and efficiently, providing actionable legal guidance to support innovation, operational execution, and sound governance practices. ## What you will be doing ### Patent Strategy & Prosecution Leadership – **Patent strategy** — Direct, lead and refine the company’s patent strategy, ensuring alignment between innovation priorities and filing decisions. – **Patentable inventions** — Identify patentable inventions through close collaboration with engineering, R&D, data science, and product teams. – **Outside counsel partnerships** — Lead and oversee partnerships with outside counsel for drafting, filing, and prosecuting patent applications. – **Patent portfolio development** — Build and manage a strategic patent portfolio covering emerging technologies—including AI, machine learning, and advanced software platforms. ### Litigation and Disputes – **IP litigation** — Lead and oversee intellectual property litigation and disputes. ### AI Law & Governance – **AI IP issues** — Advise on AI intellectual property issues, governance structures, risk assessments, and documentation. – **Responsible AI** — Provide legal oversight on responsible AI practices, including data usage, algorithmic risk, model audits, and safety evaluations. – **AI compliance** — Counsel product teams on integrating AI technologies in a compliant, responsible manner aligned with global legal and ethical standards. ### General Intellectual Property Responsibilities – **IP counseling** — Counsel on issues involving patents, trade secrets, copyrights, open-source software, and software licensing, and related litigation. – **Legal research** — Conduct legal research and analysis on emerging IP and AI legal issues, trends, and regulatory developments. – **Executive guidance** — Provide practical, solution-driven legal advice to executives and business colleagues. – **Cross-functional initiatives** — Support complex, cross-functional initiatives in a fast-paced, global environment. ## Required Qualifications – Juris Doctor (or equivalent) and admission to practice law in the relevant jurisdiction. – Admission to the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office. – 7–15+ years of legal experience, with substantial focus on AI technology, patent prosecution and patent portfolio strategy in a law firm or in-house environment. – Strong knowledge of U.S. and international patent laws, AI-related legal frameworks, and emerging global regulatory trends. – Experience advising on AI/ML compliance or responsible technology frameworks. ## Preferred Qualifications – Deep experience evaluating patentability, responding to office actions, and managing global patent filings. – Expertise working with engineers, developers, and data scientists to translate complex innovations into protectable IP. – Strong communication, writing, and analytical skills. – Ability to independently manage multiple complex matters and drive projects to completion in a dynamic environment. – Experience counseling leadership within a large, matrixed organization. ## What we offer you At FIS, we hire the best. In return, you receive exceptional benefits including: – **Fintech innovation** — Opportunities to innovate in fintech – **Professional growth** — Tools for personal and professional growth – **Inclusive environment** — Inclusive and diverse work environment – **Community investment** — Resources to invest in your community – **Competitive salary and benefits** ## Privacy Statement FIS is committed to protecting the privacy and security of all personal information that we process in order to provide services to our clients. For specific information on how FIS protects personal information online, please see the Online Privacy Notice. ## EEOC Statement FIS is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, genetic information, national origin, disability, veteran status, and other protected characteristics. The EEO is the Law poster is available here; supplement document available here. For positions located in the US, the following conditions apply. If you are made a conditional offer of employment, you will be required to undergo a drug test. ADA Disclaimer: In developing this job description care was taken to include all competencies needed to successfully perform in this position. However, for Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) purposes, the essential functions of the job may or may not have been described for purposes of ADA reasonable accommodation. All reasonable accommodation requests will be reviewed and evaluated on a case-by-case basis. ## Sourcing Model Recruitment at FIS works primarily on a direct sourcing model; a relatively small portion of our hiring is through recruitment agencies. FIS does not accept resumes from recruitment agencies which are not on the preferred supplier list and is not responsible for any related fees for resumes submitted to job postings, our employees, or any other part of our company. #pridepass Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Senior Manager – International Programs & Policy
item.description: Senior Manager – International Programs & Policy Organization: Lockheed Martin Location: Arlington, VA Date Posted: 08/27/2026 ## Standard Job Description Reporting to the Vice President for International Programs & Policy on the Global Programs & Policy (GPP) – 21st Century Security Team, this position is responsible for supporting the international trade and supply chain policy portfolio, including Foreign Military Sales and defense trade; regulatory and policy issues related to international security cooperation and export controls; international localization, investment, and financing; and international trade agreements, treaties, tariffs, and sanctions. These activities support LMGA’s external advocacy efforts and internal planning, strategic, and reporting functions. The position also includes responsibilities for supporting cross‑cutting LMGA initiatives that involve both international and domestic policy issues and will require frequent interaction with U.S. Government customers and stakeholders, including the Departments of State, Defense, and Commerce and other executive branch organizations, and LM employees and executives at varying levels of seniority. Other responsibilities include working with trade associations, consultants, and third‑party organizations as necessary. This position is best suited for a candidate with experience supporting strategic and operational government affairs initiatives and knowledge of Lockheed Martin’s international program priorities and supply chain issues, as well as experience leading, managing, and supporting advocacy campaigns and analyses on complex and sensitive programs and policy issues. — ## Basic Qualifications 1. 10+ years of relevant professional experience 2. Extensive knowledge and experience in U.S. Government national security and foreign policy, international security cooperation, and defense export‑related issues, ideally from a regulatory or policy‑making perspective 3. Prior experience interacting with U.S. Government officials and stakeholders, including, but not limited to, the Department of Defense, the Department of State, and the Department of Commerce 4. Ability to work collaboratively across the Government Affairs organization, corporate business areas, and the external customer set 5. Efficient and effective planning and organizational skills, including extraordinary attention to detail 6. Exceptional written communication and presentation development skills with proven experience supporting senior‑level leaders — ## Desired Skills 1. Prior experience and/or familiarity working with external customers 2. Prior experience with export and trade policy, international business development, industrial participation, and/or government affairs engagement and strategic campaigns 3. Familiarity with export controls, defense offsets and industrial participation, and/or international supply chain challenges 4. Experience supporting U.S. Government international advocacy 5. Experience working with external consultants, experts, and/or thought leaders involved in influencing national security and foreign policy 6. Master’s degree or equivalent work experience — ## Pay Information **Full‑Time Salary Range:** $178500.00 – $331500.00 At Lockheed Martin, we know mission success starts with taking care of our people. Our Total Rewards program is designed to attract top talent, support your well‑being, and help you grow—both professionally and personally. The salary range for this position is as listed on the requisition. Please note that the salary information listed is a general guideline only. Lockheed Martin considers factors such as (but not limited to) scope and responsibilities of the position, candidate’s work experience, education/training, key skills, as well as market (work location) and business considerations when extending an offer. **Benefits offered:** Medical, Dental, Vision, Flexible work arrangements and schedules (e.g., 4×10), 401(k) match, Paid time off, Holidays, Parental Leave, EAP, Flexible Spending Accounts, Education Assistance, Life Insurance, Short‑Term Disability, and Long‑Term Disability. Annual short‑term and/or long‑term incentive compensation programs may be offered depending on the position. Payments under these annual programs are not guaranteed and can vary from year to year and are tied to a range of performance metrics. **For Washington state applicants only:** Non‑represented full‑time employees accrue at least 10 hours per month of Paid Time Off (PTO) to be used for incidental absences and other reasons; receive at least 90 hours for holidays. Represented full‑time employees accrue 6.67 hours of Vacation per month; accrue up to 52 hours of sick leave annually; receive at least 96 hours for holidays. PTO, Vacation, sick leave, and holiday hours are prorated based on start date during the calendar year. **Salary Range:** $178500.00 – $331500.00 Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Sr. Press Officer, Humanitarian Affairs
item.description: Sr. Press Officer, Humanitarian Affairs Organization: CARE Location: New York, NY | Washington, D.C. Date Posted: 08/27/2026 **Pay Range Details** $97,300.73 – $113,112.11 Annually *Starting salaries are based on various factors, including candidate experience, education, knowledge, skills, and the cost of labor where the job is based. Salaries listed only apply to jobs based in the US.* **Who We Are:** As a global leader, CARE is shaping the future of the humanitarian and development sector. Each year, we deliver support and services to millions of people globally. We do this by focusing on our mission and vision, and the values of equality and excellence that guide our organization. We seek dedicated individuals who align with our mission and are passionate about making it a reality by collaborating with others, embracing learning and innovation, and delivering results. **What We Are Looking For:** At CARE, we value diversely talented people who can bring different experiences and perspectives to our organization. We know that not all applicants will have every skill and qualification. We encourage everyone who meets the minimum required qualifications to apply. Having one or more of the preferred qualifications will strengthen an application. But even if you are earlier in your career or followed a non‑traditional educational or professional path, we hope you will consider a career at CARE. **Job Title:** SR. PRESS OFFICER, HUMANITARIAN AFFAIRS **Job Location(s):** US – New York, NY **JOB SUMMARY:** CARE is hiring a Senior Press Officer for its Media and Communications team to help manage and execute CARE’s strategic media relations in order to further our organizational objectives so we can continue to grow our voice, profile, and message‑pull through in US and global media. With a focus on proactive media engagement and strategic relationship‑building with journalists, the candidate will work across the global CARE Network to raise the profile of our development and humanitarian work – as well as our advocacy and fundraising priorities – in US and international media. They will do so by: • Helping to develop, manage and/or execute communications strategies that support CARE’s signature issues, humanitarian/development programs, advocacy priorities and fundraising goals. • Identifying unique opportunities for CARE media coverage in line with our strategic priorities. • Helping to develop, manage and/or execute CARE’s media relations strategy to elevate the voices of CARE’s thought leaders and subject matter experts. • Providing focused media relations support to CARE teams in select regions. • Supporting media relations efforts around CARE’s humanitarian crisis responses, coordinating with CARE’s Country, Regional and other global teams to help ensure timely outreach and quality earned placement. Reporting to the Director of Media and Communications, the ideal candidate has a strong background working on a media relations team – preferably in a humanitarian or development context – and an appreciation for international affairs. They should also be a strong writer and have a passion for our mission to end hunger and poverty through a more inclusive world. Strong preference will be given to candidates who have experience working with a humanitarian or development NGO. This role is US‑based, and while it can be remote, preference will be given to candidates based in New York City, Washington, DC, or Atlanta. Preference will also be given to Spanish‑speakers. **RESPONSIBILITIES:** **Media Relations Management** Build and cultivate CARE’s relationship with key editors/journalists/outlets that keep the public informed on issues related to fighting poverty, responding to emergencies, and empowering girls and women. In addition to top‑tier legacy media, the Senior Press Officer will also strategically target emerging “new” media outlets/reporters/influencers (podcasts, independent outlets, newsletters, etc.). Help develop and implement strategies for communicating CARE’s signature issues and/or advocacy priorities to the public. This includes positioning CARE in a way that drives home the organization’s distinctiveness, targets desired audiences, and results in a well‑defined sub‑brand. Building CARE’s growing Thought Leadership work is a key component of this role. Increase public awareness of CARE by promoting its poverty‑fighting work and women’s empowerment brand across US and global media. This includes strategically and proactively pitching to media to secure CARE coverage and managing and responding to media inquiries. • Disseminating relevant and timely pitches, press releases and statements to targeted journalists. • Vetting media inquiries and obtaining information for journalists/producers who contact CARE from US outlets. • Connecting journalists with appropriate CARE colleagues, and staffing interviews as needed. • Seeking out opportunities for journalists to visit CARE programs. • Organizing press briefings. The role also involves media tracking and monitoring of CARE coverage and of topics relevant to CARE’s programs, using media monitoring and AI tools. **Messaging and Content Development** In collaboration with CARE colleagues across the organization — including senior leadership — develops/drafts, edits, obtains approvals for, and disseminates (and posts to web) press releases and statements as needed, often on short notice. **Spokesperson Management** Identify and support spokespeople — often members of CARE’s senior leadership — and ensure they are prepared for interviews. This includes developing/drafting, obtaining approvals for, and disseminating talking points and briefing packets; as well as managing media trainings/workshops for spokespeople, both on a consistent and ad hoc basis. Occasionally, serve as spokesperson as needed. **Humanitarian Response** Help manage and support CARE’s media relations work during a humanitarian crisis or major event (e.g., outbreak of armed conflict, earthquakes, typhoons). This includes lining up talking points, spokespeople, identifying unique opportunities for CARE coverage, identifying key journalists covering the crisis and ensuring they receive CARE updates/pitches, staffing interviews as needed, and tracking coverage. This work is done in partnership/collaboration with CARE’s global Regional Communications Advisors, key country‑level CARE stakeholders, and other communications colleagues who are part of the global CARE network. **Required Qualifications:** – Bachelor’s degree in communications, international relations, journalism or other related field. – 7 to 9 years of combined media relations/communications/public relations/journalism experience. – At least 4 years of media relations experience either at an agency or in‑house. – Knowledge of key U.S. and international media outlets (including podcasts, independent outlets and newsletters). – Excellent written and verbal communications skills. **Preferred Qualifications:** – Master’s degree in communications, international relations, journalism or other related field. – Background in crisis communications, international relations, or humanitarian affairs. – Strong preference for Spanish speakers. – French and Arabic speakers also desired. – Experience working in the Global South. – Experience working for a humanitarian NGO. – Experience in complex, decentralized organizations. – Ability to work in an intense environment that accompanies humanitarian crises. There are individuals who may use CARE’s name and trademark in emails and on websites in an attempt to solicit fees from interested job‑seekers. Some examples of these fees are placement fees or immigration processing fees. CARE does not use recruiting or placement agencies that charge candidates an up‑front fee of any kind. Occasionally, CARE does employ recruiting or placement agencies to help us identify candidates for specific employment within CARE. If you’re contacted by a legitimate recruiting or placement agency, there should be no charge to you. If you suspect that you have been a victim of fraud from someone purporting to be CARE, please contact us at [email protected] . Please do not email [email protected] to apply for this position. Instead, click “ apply now ” in order to submit your interest. CARE is an Equal Opportunity employer. We provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, sex, religion, ancestry, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristics protected under applicable law. Starting salaries are based on internal equity, candidate experience, and the cost of labor where the job is based. Salaries listed only apply to jobs based in the US. item.title: Social Media Producer
item.description: Social Media Producer Organization: Acquisition.com Location: Las Vegas, NV Date Posted: 08/27/2026 ## **About ACQ Media** ACQ Media is the in-house media engine behind Acquisition.com and its portfolio of brands led by Alex Hormozi, Leila Hormozi, and Sharran Srivatsaa. Our mission is to build the leading business media organization in the world by 2030. We produce high-performance long-form series, podcasts, and daily social content that reach millions of people around the globe. Our content is not vanity media; it is designed to drive measurable reach, deepen brand influence, and create downstream business impact across the entire Acquisition.com ecosystem. We operate like a studio, not a startup content team. That means structured workflows, batch production, clear performance metrics, and an aggressive commitment to innovation, especially through AI-native production systems. We are building a repeatable content machine that compounds: more output, higher quality, faster iteration, stronger monetization, and deeper brand equity over time. If you’re joining ACQ Media, you’re not here to just make content. You’re here to help build a media powerhouse. — ## **Role** We’re hiring a Social Media Producer to lead the growth and performance of the social ecosystem behind ACQ Media and the personal brands of Alex Hormozi, Leila Hormozi, and Sharran Srivatsaa. This role is for someone who has scaled meaningful accounts and can point to measurable results. ACQ Media is the in-house media engine producing long-form series, podcasts, and daily short-form content that reaches millions globally. Our media is engineered to drive measurable brand growth and downstream business impact, not vanity engagement. We operate like a studio with structured workflows, batch production, performance metrics, and AI-native systems. In this role, you will own the strategy, editorial direction, and performance of all short-form and platform-native content. You will turn long-form episodes into high-retention, high-distribution assets that drive traffic back to YouTube and strengthen the overall brand ecosystem. You are the bridge between production and distribution, responsible for ensuring speed, cohesion, and measurable impact. This is a management role based in Las Vegas. You will directly manage the Social Coordinator, own the publishing pipeline, and build repeatable systems that compound over time. We are looking for a growth-minded operator who understands platforms deeply, actively integrates AI into workflows, and treats social as a performance channel. — ## **Responsibilities** Own the end-to-end social growth strategy across all platforms, translating long-form content into high-performing short-form assets that drive traffic, retention, and measurable brand growth. Lead and develop the Social Coordinator, setting strategic direction while ensuring disciplined execution of the publishing calendar and platform distribution. Identify high-retention moments within long-form content and provide clear editorial direction to editors to maximize performance and cohesion. Build and optimize repeatable production systems, including AI-driven workflows that increase speed, output, and quality. Monitor performance data across platforms, translate insights into actionable pivots, and continuously improve strategy based on measurable results. Partner with the production team to ensure social-first capture, organized asset management, and rapid turnaround from long-form production to distribution. — ## **Requirements** 5+ years of experience in social production, digital strategy, or video-first content growth, with a proven track record of scaling accounts through original video content. Demonstrated experience managing at least one direct report and owning performance outcomes. Strong editorial judgment. You can consistently identify high-retention moments within long-form content and understand why they will perform on specific platforms. Deep platform fluency across YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, X, and emerging formats, with a clear understanding of distribution mechanics and platform culture. AI-forward operator who actively integrates AI into creative and production workflows to increase speed, output, and iteration. — ## **Results** Measurable increase in traffic from social to long-form content. Sustained growth in high-quality engagement including shares, saves, retention, and audience sentiment. Social content consistently published within 24 to 48 hours of long-form production wrap. A cohesive, premium social presence that reinforces and amplifies the broader brand ecosystem. AI-driven workflows reduce manual clipping and editing time by at least 50 percent while increasing output and speed. — ## **Location** Las Vegas, NV (3 days onsite per week) Onsite attendance is required for all on-set filming days. Support for relocation to Las Vegas will be provided. Light travel may be required. — ## **Compensation** $90,000–$125,000 base salary. The salary range may be inclusive of several levels that would be applicable to the position. Final salary will be based on a number of factors including level, relevant prior experience, skills, and expertise. This range is only inclusive of base salary, not benefits (more details below). — ## **Benefits** We offer a comprehensive, evolving benefits package designed to support your health, family, and wellbeing. Some key offerings: Flexible Unlimited Paid Time Off and Company-wide Holidays Employer-sponsored Medical, Dental, & Vision plans $1,950 annual Employer HSA contribution FSA options including dependent care Employee assistance program and mental health resources Employer match program for 401(k), eligible for both Traditional and Roth accounts $1,200 annual wellness reimbursement through JOON that supports health, family care, pet care, fitness, and more Access to a state-of-the-art gym at our HQ in Las Vegas for local or visiting team members *Benefits eligibility applies only to full-time exempt roles.* — ## **ACQ Core Values** Our core values are the heart and soul of this incredible company. The right person for this role will appreciate each of these values, personally subscribe to them, and understand why each is critical to having a great business. ### **Competitive Greatness** Be at your best when your best is needed. Enjoyment of a hard challenge. Those who have the drive to constantly improve, the superior intellect, and the long-term commitment to see incremental improvements become compounding returns. ### **Sincere Candor** Have the self-awareness to accurately perceive and communicate hard truths that improve others and self, the courage to do so, and the humility to accept them, even when it hurts. Nothing great can be built without feedback: internally or externally. ### **Unimpeachable Character** Be the type of person with whom people are always proud to associate, personally and professionally. We look for true alignment of thoughts, words, and actions toward a goal worth pursuing. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Head of Compliance
item.description: Head of Compliance Organization: Monex USA Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/27/2026 ## Since 1999, Monex USA Since 1999, Monex USA has provided corporate clients with the best foreign exchange (FX) and international payment solutions in the industry. Monex USA guides thousands of clients, from a broad spectrum of industry sectors, through the intricacies of the currency markets. Our unique market insight is widely recognized in main‑line business media such as The Wall Street Journal, Reuters, Bloomberg, and CNBC. Monex SAB de CV is the ultimate parent company within the group and is headquartered in Mexico (BMV: MONEXB). The Monex group operates globally through regulated entities across North America, Europe, and Asia, employing over 2,500 employees and servicing more than 65,000 clients worldwide. Monex USA (“MUSA”) is a U.S. money service business registered with FinCEN and multiple state regulators, as well as FINTRAC in Canada. Monex USA is seeking a Head of Compliance to lead and oversee all compliance and financial crime functions across the business. This role is responsible for ensuring the firm maintains effective systems and controls to meet all applicable regulatory obligations, while providing strategic compliance guidance to executive leadership and supporting the company’s continued growth in the U.S. and international markets. — ## Responsibilities ### Compliance Oversight Responsible for all Compliance‑related matters at MUSA Principal contact for local regulators in the USA (FinCEN) and Canada (FINTRAC) Take the lead role in the implementation of changes driven by current and forthcoming regulatory requirements Respond to and/or coordinate responses to regulatory, FIU enquiries, LP and audit requests Ensure there are sufficient resources—and resources of the necessary quality—to handle the firm’s regulatory compliance and financial crime operations and obligations Arrange and oversee regular Compliance Audits and Risk Assessments Ensure any Audit or Risk findings are communicated to the Chief Executive Officer and other relevant senior managers (ICCO) to discuss and agree suggested changes and assist with implementation where applicable Ensure accurate and up‑to‑date Compliance records are maintained (including version control) Provide concise and meaningful, data‑driven management information to the firm’s executive and Board & Senior Managers (e.g., quarterly compliance reports, quarterly Board reporting) ### Business & Compliance Strategy Manage day‑to‑day compliance operations Develop and align compliance initiatives for MUSA in partnership with international compliance teams, ensuring consistency with global strategic objectives under the guidance of the ICCO Advise and assist the local Board to deliver on required management/governance structure, systems and internal controls, and individual responsibilities of senior management ### Regulatory & Financial Crime Requirements Oversee the firm’s AML/BSA, OFAC, sanctions, and financial crime compliance framework Ensure adherence to USA PATRIOT Act, FATF recommendations, and state money transmitter licensing requirements Continuously enhance the Compliance Programme, including policies, procedures, and training documentation Ensure risk‑based KYC and due diligence procedures are maintained and escalated appropriately Oversee customer complaint reviews and regulatory reporting obligations Maintain oversight of SAR/STR filing processes and financial crime investigations ### Compliance Culture & Training Foster strong relationships across all business units while maintaining effective second‑line oversight Promote a culture of compliance and ethical conduct across the organization Ensure all employees receive ongoing compliance and financial crime training Coordinate bespoke training for senior leadership and Board members where appropriate Maintain compliance registers and training records — ## Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Law, Finance, Business, or related field 10+ years of compliance experience within money transmission, foreign exchange, or international payments Minimum 3 years of senior compliance leadership experience Strong knowledge of AML/BSA, OFAC, USA PATRIOT Act, FATF recommendations, and U.S. money transmitter regulations Experience managing regulatory examinations, audits, and remediation efforts Prior experience serving as BSA Officer or MLRO with SAR/STR filing authority Strong communication and stakeholder management skills High standard of written and verbal English — ## Preferred Qualifications Advanced degree in a related field FINTRAC/PCMLTFA experience CAMS or similar compliance certification Fluency in additional languages, including Spanish, French, or Dutch Experience working with international compliance governance structures — ## Compensation The annual salary range is $170,000 to $200,000 with a 10% annual bonus. Salary is commensurate with experience and qualifications. — ## Benefits Medical insurance Dental insurance Vision insurance 401(k) and employer match Paid time off Disability benefits Paid parental leave — Monex Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Diversity is valued and the company will not tolerate any form of discrimination or harassment. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Content & Editorial Strategist
item.description: Content & Editorial Strategist Organization: OSEA Location: Los Angeles, CA Date Posted: 08/27/2026 ## Description ### About the role Join our fast‑growing beauty brand and become a fundamental member of our expanding team. We are looking for a savvy, passionate **Content & Editorial Strategist** who is excited about brand storytelling, copywriting, sustainability, and beauty. The ideal candidate has a passion for language, brand voice, and clean beauty, thrives in a fast‑paced environment, and shares our commitment to wellness in both our products and work‑life balance. Our mission is to create effective, results‑driven skincare that is safe for the planet and humankind. This role is hybrid, with the expectation to work in‑office 1–2 days per week at our Venice, California headquarters. — ## Responsibilities – **Editorial strategy** — Develop and lead editorial and content strategies that support product launches, integrated campaigns, and key business objectives. – **Brand voice** — Own and evolve OSEA’s content strategy and brand voice across all owned channels, ensuring messaging is consistent, differentiated, and aligned with the brand. – **Messaging frameworks** — Establish messaging frameworks, storytelling pillars, and content strategies that guide execution across every customer touchpoint. – **Copy development** — Develop compelling copy for product launches, integrated campaigns, email, social, retail collateral, events, and seasonal initiatives while creating scalable content systems that support cross‑functional teams. – **Website editorial** — Lead the editorial strategy for OSEAMalibu.com, creating engaging content that strengthens the customer experience, supports SEO, and brings the brand to life through product pages, editorial features, and long‑form storytelling. – **Editorial calendar** — Develop and manage the editorial calendar, aligning content priorities with campaign timelines, product launches, seasonal moments, and business goals. – **Content guidelines** — Create content briefs, messaging hierarchies, editorial guidelines, and channel‑specific frameworks that enable consistent execution across Creative, E‑Commerce, Social, Paid, and Lifecycle Marketing. – **Cross‑functional collaboration** — Partner closely with Creative, Brand Marketing, E‑Commerce, Product Marketing, Education, and Digital teams to shape integrated campaigns from a content‑first perspective. – **Ingredient storytelling** — Translate ingredient science, clinical results, sustainability initiatives, and product innovation into clear, compelling consumer‑facing messaging that educates and inspires. – **Performance insights** — Use performance insights, SEO data, consumer behavior, and competitive analysis to identify content opportunities, optimize existing content, and inform future strategy. – **Trend monitoring** — Monitor beauty, wellness, digital, and cultural trends to evolve OSEA’s storytelling, ensuring content remains relevant, distinctive, and connected to the brand’s point of view. – **Editorial excellence** — Champion editorial excellence by maintaining brand voice standards, ensuring consistency across channels, and continually evolving content best practices. This job description is a summary of duties. It is not an all‑inclusive list but a broad guide of expected responsibilities and is subject to change. — ## Requirements – Excellent communication and interpersonal skills (oral, written, non‑verbal, intuitive, psychic et al) – Must be willing to use AI to optimize workflows and speed – Experience in Figma – 5+ years of copywriting experience, ideally with beauty, wellness, or lifestyle brands – Exceptional writing, editing, and proofreading skills with an impressive portfolio – Proven ability to adapt voice and tone across platforms (digital, print, social, email, video scripts) – Familiarity with SEO best practices and performance copywriting – Strong project management skills; ability to prioritize in a deadline‑driven environment – Must reside in Los Angeles to be considered for this position, with the expectation to work on Pacific Standard Time (PST) – Please note that visa sponsorship is not available for this position — ## Compensation The anticipated salary range for this position is **$80,000–$95,000 per year**. The actual salary offer will consider factors including skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Not all candidates will be eligible for the upper end of the salary range. item.title: Deputy Vice President, International Advocacy (Market Access)
item.description: Deputy Vice President, International Advocacy (Market Access) Organization: Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/27/2026 **Overview** The Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA) is seeking a Deputy Vice President for the International Advocacy team to support its global market access advocacy efforts. This position will lead the development and implementation of policy positions, advocacy strategies, and stakeholder engagement activities focused on improving patient access to innovative medicines in major global markets. Reporting to the Deputy Vice President, International Advocacy, the Deputy Vice President will serve as a senior leader on international market access issues, including government pricing and reimbursement, health technology assessment (HTA), healthcare financing, value assessment frameworks, and other policies affecting patient access to innovative medicines. The individual will work collaboratively across the organization and with member companies, other trade associations, consultants, and government stakeholders to advance PhRMA’s strategic priorities in key markets around the world. This Washington, DC-based role requires strategic leadership, strong policy expertise, and the ability to operate independently while managing complex projects and stakeholder relationships across multiple geographies and issue areas. **The Deputy Vice President will:** Develop and implement advocacy strategies to advance PhRMA’s international market access priorities in major global markets. Lead policy analysis and position development related to pharmaceutical pricing and reimbursement, health technology assessment, healthcare financing, value assessment methodologies, and other market access issues. Perform and oversee quantitative analysis related to healthcare policies, market access, and/or international trade. Represent PhRMA in meetings with government agencies, embassies, organizations, member companies, and external stakeholders. Monitor and assess legislative, regulatory, trade, and policy developments affecting patient access to innovative medicines globally. Build and maintain relationships with U.S. and foreign government officials, trade associations, industry partners, think tanks, academic experts, consultants, and other key stakeholders. Lead and facilitate member company workgroups and task forces focused on international market access priorities. Develop policy papers, briefing materials, presentations, talking points, comment letters, and other advocacy materials for internal and external audiences. Coordinate closely with PhRMA’s policy, federal advocacy, communications, alliance development, legal, and economic teams. Manage consultants, research projects, and external vendors to ensure high-quality and timely work products. Oversee project budgets, contracts, and vendor relationships in accordance with organizational policies. Provide strategic counsel and subject matter expertise to senior leadership on international market access developments and advocacy opportunities. Support the development of cross-functional advocacy campaigns that advance patient access to innovative medicines globally. Perform other duties as assigned. **Key Success Factors** PhRMA seeks a visionary, relationship-driven, and impact-focused individual who is passionate about contributing to the health care challenges we face today. The Deputy Vice President leverages deep expertise to guide strategic priorities, anticipates challenges, and aligns departmental efforts with broader organizational goals. A successful DVP is a trusted advisor, skilled in stakeholder influence and resource management, and leads cross-functional initiatives with clarity, confidence, and purpose. **Professional Experience** Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree in Public Policy, Health Policy, Economics, International Affairs, Public Health, Law, Political Science, or a related field preferred. 10+ years of professional experience in international health policy, market access, healthcare economics, public policy, government affairs, trade policy, or related field. Expertise in pharmaceutical pricing and reimbursement policies, health technology assessment, and market access policy issues in foreign countries. Strong understanding of healthcare systems and healthcare financing around the world and the policies that impact patient access to innovative medicines. Experience in performing and overseeing quantitative analysis related to healthcare policies, market access, and/or international trade. Proven ability to analyze complex policy issues and develop strategic recommendations. Exceptional writing, presentation, and communication skills, including the ability to synthesize technical information for diverse audiences. Demonstrated experience developing and implementing advocacy strategies involving U.S. and foreign government stakeholders. Demonstrated success managing consultants, vendors, and complex projects with multiple deliverables. Strong interpersonal skills and ability to establish credibility with senior executives, member company representatives, and external stakeholders. Must be willing to travel internationally (Asia, Europe) as needed to support advocacy objectives and stakeholder engagement. Demonstrated commitment to teamwork, integrity, and professional excellence. **Preferred Experience** Advanced degree (Master’s, J.D., Ph.D., or equivalent) in a relevant discipline. Experience working directly with foreign government agencies, multilateral organizations, or trade associations in other countries. Knowledge of how market access policies affect international trade, pharmaceutical innovation, and patient access. Experience engaging with health technology assessment agencies and reimbursement authorities in major international markets. Experience leading high-performing, cross-functional teams. **Potential Salary** $187,100–266,700 per annum. Salary is commensurate with experience and other compensable factors. **Who we are** The Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA) represents the country’s leading innovative biopharmaceutical research companies, which are laser focused on developing innovative medicines that transform lives and create a healthier world. Together, we are fighting for solutions to ensure patients can access and afford medicines that prevent, treat and cure disease. PhRMA member companies have invested more than $900 billion in the search for new treatments and cures over the last decade, supporting nearly five million jobs in the United States. **Connect with PhRMA** For information on how innovative medicines save lives, please visit: [www.PhRMA.org] [www.Innovation.org] [www.AmericasMedicines.org] [www.Facebook.com/PhRMA] [www.Twitter.com/PhRMA] **What we offer** In addition to a highly competitive salary and bonus program, various opportunities for reward and recognition and a platform of extensive benefits, PhRMA is committed to the development and overall wellbeing of our team members. We offer traditional (medical, dental, vision, flexible spending, life, AD&D, LTD, STD) and enhanced benefits such as parental leave, a well-being program, an on-site fitness facility, back-up care, health advocate service, an employee assistance program, and commuting benefits. We also offer a robust 401k plan with employer contributions upon the first day of hire and immediate vesting, a generous paid time off plan, ten paid holidays (plus inauguration day), half day Fridays preceding holidays, half day Fridays in the summer months, and a paid winter break. As an organization, we work together in the office on Mondays through Thursdays and remotely on Fridays. We also all work remotely in August. We are committed to the growth and development of our team members and offer many learning opportunities including an integrated onboarding program, best-in-class leadership programming, tuition reimbursement, industry on-site and off-site training, and other management/professional development programs. Corporate social responsibility is also important to us at PhRMA. Our team members participate in community service activities, fundraising drives and charitable athletic events. We are committed to supporting our family of professionals at PhRMA and strive to create programs that help our team members manage the challenges of balancing a fast-paced career with their personal goals. **Equal Opportunity Employer** PhRMA provides equal employment opportunities to all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, marital status, personal appearance, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, family responsibilities, genetic information, disability, matriculation, political affiliation or veteran status in accordance with applicable federal, state and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment. The job description contains an overview of the activities and duties for this role. Responsibilities may change and new ones may be assigned at any time. item.title: Director, Advocacy and Strategic Alliances
item.description: Director, Advocacy and Strategic Alliances Organization: Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/27/2026 # Overview Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA) is seeking a Director for the Advocacy and Strategic Alliances team to support its stakeholder engagement and advocacy efforts related to prescription medicine access and affordability. The Director will have a particular focus on Medicare Part B and issues affecting physician-administered medicines, including the implementation of the Inflation Reduction Act’s (IRA) Medicare drug price negotiation program, and Most Favored Nation (MFN) and related government pricing policies. The Director will develop and execute stakeholder engagement strategies that advance PhRMA priorities, with a primary focus on health care providers and provider organizations, as well as patient advocacy organizations representing the oncology and mental health communities, and other health care constituencies. The role will assess how emerging federal policy proposals affect providers and patients and translate those implications into effective external engagement strategies. The Director will work closely with colleagues across PhRMA, member companies, and external partners to coordinate advocacy strategies and ensure stakeholder perspectives inform and strengthen PhRMA’s broader policy and advocacy efforts. The Director will report to the Deputy Vice President, Advocacy and Strategic Alliances. ## The Director will: – Develop and execute stakeholder engagement and advocacy strategies related to government price controls and access to medicines, with particular emphasis on Medicare Part B, the Medicare drug price negotiation program, MFN and related federal policy developments. – Serve as a primary Alliance resource on issues affecting Medicare Part B and physician-administered medicines, translating complex policy developments into actionable stakeholder engagement strategies. – Assess the implications of federal pricing and reimbursement policies for providers, patients, and other health care stakeholders and identify opportunities to engage constituencies in support of shared priorities. – Build, strengthen, and maintain relationships with health care providers and provider organizations, with particular attention to constituencies affected by Part B policy and reimbursement changes. – Develop and maintain strategic relationships with patient advocacy organizations – including those focused on oncology and mental health – and other health care stakeholders whose priorities intersect with PhRMA’s policy agenda. – Identify areas of alignment among diverse constituencies and develop opportunities for collaboration, coalition-building, and coordinated advocacy. – Monitor the federal legislative, regulatory, and political environment to identify emerging developments related to government price controls, Medicare Part B, the IRA, MFN, and other policies affecting access to medicines. – Coordinate closely with PhRMA’s Policy, Federal Advocacy, Public Affairs, International and other teams to ensure Alliance strategies are informed by PhRMA policy positions and integrated with broader organizational priorities. – Work with internal subject matter experts to translate complex policy issues into clear, compelling materials and messages appropriate for stakeholder audiences. – Develop briefing materials, presentations, talking points, stakeholder analyses, engagement plans, and other written products that accurately reflect PhRMA’s established positions. – Represent PhRMA with external organizations and stakeholders on established policy positions relevant to the role’s portfolio. – Plan and execute stakeholder meetings, roundtables, briefings, coalition activities, and other engagement opportunities designed to advance shared policy objectives. – Gather stakeholder perspectives and intelligence and communicate relevant developments, opportunities, and risks to PhRMA leadership and cross-functional colleagues. – Support select international advocacy initiatives involving pharmaceutical pricing and reimbursement policies, including issues where international price controls intersect with U.S. policy proposals and stakeholder interests. – Coordinate with member companies to obtain input, identify stakeholder opportunities, and support alignment around advocacy strategies and priorities. – Manage projects and, as appropriate, consultants and external partners, including timelines, deliverables, and coordination across multiple workstreams. – Continuously evaluate engagement strategies and recommend adjustments based on changes in the policy environment, stakeholder landscape, and organizational priorities. – Perform other duties as assigned. ## Key Success Factors PhRMA seeks a mission-driven, agile, and solutions-oriented individual who is passionate about contributing to the health care challenges we face today. The Director brings strong subject matter expertise, manages multiple complex projects simultaneously, and guides others toward shared objectives. This role requires clear communication, effective relationship management, and the ability to translate strategic goals into actionable plans. A successful Director demonstrates foresight, critical thinking, and the ability to build consensus across diverse stakeholders. ## Professional Requirements – Bachelor’s degree required (Master’s degree in Health Policy, Public Policy, Communications or related field preferred). – 6+ years of relevant professional experience, including experience in leadership roles. – Demonstrated ability to lead complex, multi-stakeholder projects or initiatives. – Experience with Medicare Part B policy, prescription drug pricing and reimbursement, government price controls, or related health policy issues. – Exceptional writing, editing, and presentation skills, with experience developing content for executive audiences. – Experience engaging health care providers, patient advocacy organizations, disease-specific organizations, or other health care constituencies. – Demonstrated sound judgment and ability to work independently while recognizing issues that require broader organizational coordination or leadership guidance. – Strong analytical and strategic thinking capabilities. – Demonstrated experience managing staff and/or overseeing consultants and vendors. – Excellent verbal communication, presentation, active listening, and interpersonal skills. – Proficiency in Microsoft Office tools; item.title: Deputy Vice President, Policy & Research
item.description: Deputy Vice President, Policy & Research Organization: Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/27/2026 ## Overview Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA) is seeking a Deputy Vice President for the Policy and Research team to support its policy development and research strategy efforts. Reporting to the Deputy Vice President, Policy & Research, this position leads the development, management, and communication of research supporting PhRMA’s advocacy priorities related to prescription drug spending, pharmaceutical reimbursement and distribution, and the 340B Drug Pricing Program. The Deputy Vice President serves as a key internal resource by managing research projects, synthesizing complex evidence, advising cross-functional teams, and translating research into actionable policy and advocacy materials. The Deputy Vice President will focus on: ### Prescription Drug Spending and Market Access Research Lead development and review of research content and advocacy materials related to prescription drug costs, reimbursement, coverage and market access issues. Monitor and analyze trends in drug spending, utilization, pricing, pharmaceutical supply chain dynamics, PBM and insurer business practices, and coverage and access to medicines across public and private health care programs. Identify and analyze emerging policy and market developments that may affect prescription drug costs and coverage. Translate or synthesize complex pricing concepts, analyses, and research findings for senior management, member companies, and external stakeholders. Interface with other departments, internal to PhRMA, to review and advise on talking points, press releases, media requests, legislative and regulatory proposals. Manage internal and external research, oversee project execution and deliverables. Conduct rapid response analyses and data syntheses to inform advocacy, communications, and policy efforts. ### 340B and Hospital Research Partner with the 340B policy team on research development and execution, including advising on methodology, reviewing scopes of work and identifying and engaging research partners. Actively manage research projects, including communicating with outside researchers/analysts, getting internal feedback, communicating with other departments, updating research trackers, and developing summaries as needed. Monitor and evaluate 340B research, including identifying and summarizing new studies to disseminate internally and externally as needed. Draft research updates, summaries, emails, slides, and other materials to keep the department and members informed of relevant 340B research. Track all ongoing PhRMA-funded 340B projects and keep internal systems up to date with current status, deliverables and target release date. Provide analytic and strategic support for other hospital related research. Perform other duties as assigned. ## Key Success Factors PhRMA seeks a proactive, analytical, and collaborative individual who is passionate about contributing to the health care challenges we face today. The successful candidate demonstrates exceptional critical thinking and project management skills and can translate complex research into practical policy insights that support organizational priorities. This individual builds strong working relationships across departments and with external research partners, manages multiple priorities under compressed timelines, and exercises sound judgment in a dynamic policy environment. Strong written and verbal communication skills, intellectual curiosity, attention to detail, and the ability to work independently while collaborating across teams are essential for success in this role. ## Professional Experience / Requirements 10+ years of experience in pharmaceutical pricing or market access, policy, health economics, or a related field. Master’s degree in public health, economics, public policy, health services research, or related discipline. Deep expertise in U.S. drug pricing, coverage, reimbursement systems, and public programs and public policy analysis. Proven leadership in cross-functional collaboration and stakeholder engagement. Strong quantitative skills; ability to interpret complex data and synthesize insights. Exceptional writing, editing, and verbal communication skills. Experience managing consultants, research vendors, and direct reports. Demonstrated ability to lead teams and mentor staff. ### Preferred Experience MBA, Master’s in Public Policy, PharmD, JD, or Ph.D. in economics, health policy, or related field. Experience in pharmaceutical reimbursement and distribution, PBM and insurer business practices, 340B or market access analytics. ## Potential Salary $224,500–320,000 per annum. Salary is commensurate with experience and other compensable factors. ## Who we are The Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA) represents the country’s leading innovative biopharmaceutical research companies, which are laser focused on developing innovative medicines that transform lives and create a healthier world. Together, we are fighting for solutions to ensure patients can access and afford medicines that prevent, treat and cure disease. Over the last decade, PhRMA member companies have invested more than $850 billion in the search for new treatments and cures over the last decade, supporting nearly five million jobs in the United States. ## Connect with PhRMA For information on how innovative medicines save lives, please visit: [www.PhRMA.org] [www.Innovation.org] [www.Americasmedicines.org] [www.Facebook.com/PhRMA] [www.Twitter.com/PhRMA] ## What we offer In addition to a highly competitive salary and bonus program, various opportunities for reward and recognition and a platform of extensive benefits, PhRMA is committed to the development and overall wellbeing of our team members. We offer traditional (medical, dental, vision, flexible spending, life, AD&D, LTD, STD) and enhanced benefits such as parental leave, a wellbeing program, back-up care, health advocate service, employee assistance program and commuting benefits. We also offer a robust 401k plan with employer contributions upon the first day of hire and immediate vesting, a generous paid time off plan, seven paid holidays (plus inauguration day), half day Fridays preceding holidays, half day Fridays in the summer months and a paid winter break. As an organization, we work in the office on Mondays through Thursdays and remotely on Fridays. We also all work remotely in August. We are committed to the growth and development of our team members and offer many learning opportunities including an integrated on-boarding program, best-in-class leadership programming, tuition reimbursement, industry on-site and off-site training, and other management/professional development programs. Corporate social responsibility is also important to us at PhRMA. Our team members participate in organization-wide community service activities, fundraising drives and charitable athletic events. We are committed to supporting our family of professionals at PhRMA and strive to create programs that help our team members manage the challenges of balancing a fast-paced career with their own personal goals. ## Equal Opportunity Employer PhRMA provides equal employment opportunities to all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, marital status, personal appearance, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, family responsibilities, genetic information, disability, matriculation, political affiliation or veteran status in accordance with applicable federal, state and local laws governing non-discrimination in employment. item.description: Senior Director, Federal Advocacy Organization: Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/27/2026 ## Overview Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA) is seeking a Senior Director of the Federal Advocacy team to support its advocacy efforts. The Senior Director is responsible for developing and maintaining relationships while building support for PhRMA’s priorities, policies, and positions. The individual will lobby members of Congress and their staff, with a focus on the Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP) Committee Democrats. The Sr. Director will: – Lobby Senate Democratic members and their staff on potential/proposed legislation and the impact of such legislation on patients and the pharmaceutical industry. – Coordinate with PhRMA colleagues and member company staff on policy positions and the development of legislative strategy related to PhRMA priorities. – Build and maintain relationships with member company staff and other stakeholders. – Represent the Federal Advocacy team at internal PhRMA meetings and collaborate across departments on policy, engagement strategy, and messaging materials. – Anticipate, track, and analyze legislation relevant to industry priorities, and make recommendations for executing on key initiatives involving PhRMA staff and member company representatives as needed. – Develop relationships with priority Democratic members by conducting situational analyses and anticipating Senate policy positions to lobby. – Manage consultants who provide services to the Federal Advocacy team. – Perform other duties as assigned. ## Key Success Factors PhRMA seeks a proactive, confident, and action‑oriented individual who is passionate about contributing to the health care challenges we face today. Key success factors for this role include a strong sense of team and collaborative focus. The preferred candidate will bring substantive health care communications expertise and be an organized, detail‑oriented, self‑starter with excellent writing skills and the ability to convey content in an audience‑appropriate and compelling manner. Demonstrated consensus building, decision‑making, and interpersonal skills are essential. This is a highly visible, fast‑paced position that is both internally and externally facing. Accordingly, the successful candidate should be adaptable, able to reprioritize and shift gears quickly, comfortable in a high‑pressure environment, and be politically savvy, diplomatic, responsive, and mature. ## Professional Experience / Requirements – Bachelor’s degree in political science, public administration, or in a related field. – 8+ years of combined legislative, White House, government affairs consulting, and/or pharmaceutical industry experience. – Understanding of procedures and protocols of standing committees regarding witnesses, testimony, and Congressional activities; working knowledge of the Congressional process and ethics rules and regulations. – Strong relationship‑building skills, integrity, and reputation. – Strong verbal and written communication skills. – Demonstrated collaboration and ability to be a team player. ## Potential Salary Sr. Director: $169,300–$237,100. Salary is commensurate with experience and other compensable factors. ## Who we are The Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA) represents the country’s leading innovative biopharmaceutical research companies, which are laser‑focused on developing innovative medicines that transform lives and create a healthier world. Together, we are fighting for solutions to ensure patients can access and afford medicines that prevent, treat, and cure disease. PhRMA member companies have invested more than $900 billion in the search for new treatments and cures over the last decade, supporting nearly five million jobs in the United States. ## Connect with PhRMA For information on how innovative medicines save lives, please visit: [www.PhRMA.org] [www.Innovation.org] [www.Americasmedicines.org] [www.Facebook.com/PhRMA] [www.Twitter.com/PhRMA] ## What we offer In addition to a highly competitive salary and bonus program, various opportunities for reward and recognition, and a platform of extensive benefits, PhRMA is committed to the development and overall wellbeing of our team members. We also offer a robust 401k plan with employer contributions upon the first day of hire and immediate vesting, a generous paid time off plan, ten paid holidays (plus inauguration day), half‑day Fridays preceding holidays, half‑day Fridays in the summer months, and a paid winter break. As an organization, we work together in the office Mondays through Thursdays and remotely on Fridays. We also all work remotely in August. item.title: Regional Affairs, SME
item.description: Regional Affairs, SME Organization: USfalcon Location: Omaha, NE Date Posted: 08/27/2026 ## Description USfalcon has an exciting opportunity for a Regional Affairs SME to support USSTRATCOM at Offutt AFB, NE. ## ESSENTIAL DUTIES Provide senior‑level subject matter expertise on regional political, economic, and security affairs with a focus on European regions in support of USSTRATCOM campaign and risk assessments. Support campaign and risk assessments by finding, reading, and comprehending diplomatic, informational, military, and economic information from multiple sources and maintaining working knowledge of applicable policy and strategy guidance. Contribute to development and refinement of measurement criteria (measures of effectiveness, measures of performance, scoring standards) used to assess progression or regression toward strategic deterrence objectives in assigned regions. Analyze regional developments and global factors (diplomatic, information, military, economic) to determine their impact on the Strategic Environment and strategic deterrence, and document assessment logic for use in campaign and risk assessments. Develop, update, and maintain regional components of campaign and risk assessments, synthesizing individual assessment results into key findings and recommendations for senior leaders. Produce graduate‑level quality briefings and written reports with supporting in‑depth analysis and research, following best practices for analytic writing, and brief assessment findings to senior leaders. Collaborate with the Office of the Secretary of War, Joint Staff, interagency, international partners, and other Government agencies on regional issues, ensuring USSTRATCOM perspectives are integrated into interagency and CCMD‑level assessments and planning. Actively and continuously support Joint Force and operations assessments by providing regional context, trend analysis, and recommendations to improve force integration, resource allocation, and strategic alignment. ## REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS At least 15 years of interagency and/or Combatant Command desk officer international affairs experience. At least 3 years of overseas experience. At least 6 years of experience working on European affairs. Demonstrated ability to produce graduate‑level quality analytic briefs and written reports, and to brief findings to senior leaders. Demonstrated relevant experience supporting: – Campaign and Risk Assessments: maintaining policy and strategy knowledge (National Security Strategy, Unified Command Plan, National Defense Strategy, Nuclear Posture Review, National Military Strategy, Joint Strategic Campaign Plan, Global Campaign Plans, Operations Plans, Contingency Plans); developing measurement criteria; analyzing information to determine progression toward Strategic Deterrence; documenting assessment logic; and developing campaign and risk assessments. – Applying critical thought to identify trends, developing key findings and recommendations, and producing graduate‑level briefs and written reports. – Collaborating with OSW, Joint Staff, interagency, international, and other Government partners; and supporting Joint Force and operations assessments. ## PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Direct experience supporting USSTRATCOM or other Combatant Command campaign planning, regional strategy development, contingency planning, or strategic engagement activities. Experience advising General/Flag Officers or Senior Executive Service leaders on regional developments, strategic implications, and assessment findings. Experience integrating regional analysis into Joint Force and operations assessments, including identification of cost/benefit of operations, activities, and investments toward shaping the strategic environment. ## EDUCATION / CERTIFICATION Master’s degree in International Affairs, Economics, or equivalent field. ## REQUIRED CLEARANCE Top Secret/SCI ## TRAVEL TBD ## Benefits Offered Medical, dental, vision, life insurance, short‑term disability, long‑term disability, 401(k) match, flexible spending accounts, EAP, parental leave, pet insurance, paid time off, and holidays. USfalcon has grown from our roots in 1984 to become a mid‑tier professional services company supporting a diverse and global customer base of DoD and Federal Agencies. We have been excelling in diverse platforms for almost 30 years and continue to be an industry leader. If you thrive in an organization that values integrity, commitment, stewardship, and service, we want to meet you. We deliver core capabilities in Aviation, Space, Information Technology, and Business Operations and continue to grow and expand our competencies, contracts, and customer base, adding to our long history of supporting customer and community needs. Learn more at [www.usfalcon.com/history]. ## Equal Opportunity Employer / Protected Veterans / Individuals with Disabilities This employer is required to notify all applicants of their rights pursuant to federal employment laws. For further information, please review the *Know Your Rights* notice from the Department of Labor. Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: External Affairs Program Manager
item.description: External Affairs Program Manager Organization: Lee County Electric Cooperative (LCEC) Location: N. Fort Myers, FL Date Posted: 08/27/2026 # JOB TITLE: External Affairs Program Manager Location: North Fort Myers, FL Work Hours: M–F 8–5pm (varied hours) ## Our benefits include – Company-wide annual incentive plan – Medical, vision and dental insurance – 401(k) plan with a generous 6% company match – Company funded Pension Plan – On-site wellness/medical facility – Company paid Short & Long-Term Disability insurance – Health Savings Account with an employer contribution – Flexible Spending Accounts – Paid time off and paid holidays – Wellness program with financial rewards – Tuition reimbursement – Group life insurance – Critical Illness and Accident Insurance LCEC provides reliable, cost-competitive electricity to more than 260,000 members throughout a five-county service territory located in Southwest Florida. We employ approximately 485 skilled employees and are one of more than 900 electric distribution cooperatives located throughout the United States. LCEC has been recognized locally and statewide as an industry leader and continually receives acknowledgment for the work that our employees do in the community along with other civic, environmental and professional honors. ## Position Summary The External Affairs Lead is responsible for developing and executing LCEC’s External Affairs strategy in alignment with organizational priorities and executive leadership direction. This position serves as the cooperative’s primary point of contact for government and community stakeholders, proactively identifying risks, opportunities, and external factors that may impact operations, growth, and organizational positioning. This position manages higher-impact stakeholder relationships and represents LCEC in strategic external engagements, leads resolution of complex community and governmental challenges and provides coordinated solutions related to stakeholder risk, community sentiment, and engagement strategy. The position works collaboratively across departments and supports organizational objectives through proactive issue identification, coordination, and external representation. Working closely with Key Accounts, Operations, and Business Continuity, this role ensures alignment between day-to-day operational execution and long-term external strategy. The External Affairs Lead supports LCEC’s ability to proactively navigate an evolving political and regulatory environment while maintaining strong community relationships and advancing organizational resilience. ## Position Responsibilities – Lead LCEC’s government relations, legislative affairs, and external stakeholder engagement efforts, cultivating relationships with policymakers, governmental leadership, and influential community stakeholders to support organizational priorities and long-term strategic objectives. – Manage relationships with governmental entities in their capacity as policymakers, regulators, and community decision-makers rather than as utility customers or account holders. – Assess emerging legislative, regulatory, political, and community issues; develop engagement strategies and provide recommendations to executive leadership regarding organizational risks, opportunities, and stakeholder impacts. – Monitor local, state, and federal legislative actions, ordinances, and policy discussions that may impact LCEC and assess potential impacts to the organization. – Facilitate cross functional alignment to support timely resolution of government-related challenges, inquiries, or concerns. Support development of response strategies and recommendations for leadership as needed. – Prepare and deliver information to government stakeholders related to LCEC initiatives, infrastructure projects, service issues, rate-related matters, and outage or restoration activity. – Provide input into messaging approaches and support leadership briefings related to governmental matters. Ensure consistency of messaging with internal guidance and organizational priorities. – Represent LCEC in high-visibility or contentious settings requiring independent judgment and discretion. – Support coordination with government partners during emergency events or organizational activations. – Participate in targeted community or civic activities directly related to government relationships. – Operate independently with external stakeholders, manage multiple complex issues simultaneously, and provide frequent updates (verbally & written) and strategic recommendations to leadership. – Maintain effective working relationships with employees and customers at all levels within LCEC. Ensure smooth operations, productive communications, and effective understanding during all interpersonal contacts. Provide current and accurate information to all requesters, courteously and in a timely manner. – Support Storm Restoration efforts when needed. Work in emergency storm situations (i.e. hurricanes) and work long hours (>12 hours per day) for many continuous days/weeks as needed. – Perform other related duties as assigned. ## Education – Bachelor’s degree in communications, public affairs, political science, public relations, business administration, or a related field or experience commensurate to degree. (Required) – Master’s Degree in business, marketing, energy management, or related field. (Preferred) ## Experience – 7+ Years progressively responsible experience in lobbying, government relations, public affairs, community engagement, or stakeholder relations, including engagement with local governments, community organizations, and public-sector stakeholders, and experience with public speaking and presentations. (Required) – 5+ Years Utility, infrastructure, or regulated-industry experience. (Preferred) ## Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities – Strong interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills. (Required) – Proven ability to build and maintain effective stakeholder relationships in complex environments. (Required) – Ability to exercise judgment, manage sensitive issues, and coordinate across departments. (Required) – Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook). (Required) – Knowledge of the local service area and community environment. (Preferred) ## Licenses – Valid driver’s license upon hire (Required) ## Physical Demands and Working Environment The physical demands and working environment characteristics described here must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. **Physical Demands:** Standing Occasionally, Walking Occasionally, Sitting Constantly, Lifting Rarely, Carrying Rarely, Pushing Rarely, Pulling Rarely, Climbing Rarely, Balancing Rarely, Stooping Rarely, Kneeling Rarely, Crouching Rarely, Crawling Rarely, Reaching Rarely, Handling Occasionally, Grasping Occasionally, Feeling Rarely, Talking Constantly, Hearing Constantly, Repetitive Motions Frequently, Eye/Hand/Foot Coordination Frequently. **Working Environment:** Frequently Air-conditioned office environment, Rarely Extreme cold, Rarely Extreme heat, Rarely Humidity, Rarely Wet, Occasionally Noise, Rarely Hazards, Rarely Temperature Change, Rarely Atmospheric Conditions, Rarely Vibration. ## STORM DUTY REQUIREMENTS Responding to storms may be considered a condition of employment: LCEC provides critical services to our community during an emergency. Employees may be required to participate in the response/recovery activities related to emergencies/disasters to maintain service to our LCEC members. Employees are required to work in their normal job duties or other assigned activities. Proper compensation will be made in accordance with the company’s guidelines and procedures. ## Additional Information Please note that at the time a candidate is made a job offer, the candidate will be subject to a background check and a drug screening.
