item.title: Director, Digital Standards Strategy and Regulatory Science (REMOTE)
item.description: Director, Digital Standards Strategy and Regulatory Science (REMOTE) Organization: U.S. Pharmacopeial Convention (USP) Location: Rockville, MD Date Posted: 08/27/2026 **Description** The U.S. Pharmacopeial Convention (USP) is an independent scientific organization that collaborates with the world’s leading health and science experts to develop rigorous quality standards for medicines, dietary supplements, and food ingredients. At USP, we believe that scientific excellence is driven by a commitment to fairness, integrity, and global collaboration. This belief is embedded in our core value of Passion for Quality and is demonstrated through the contributions of more than 1,300 professionals across twenty global locations, working to strengthen the supply of safe, high-quality medicines worldwide. At USP, we value inclusive scientific collaboration and recognize that attracting diverse expertise strengthens our ability to develop trusted public health standards. We foster an organizational culture that supports equitable access to mentorship, professional development, and leadership opportunities. Our partnerships, standards, and research reflect our belief that ensuring broad participation in scientific leadership results in stronger, more impactful outcomes for global health. USP is proud to be an equal employment opportunity employer (EEOE) and is committed to ensuring fair, merit-based selection processes that enable the best scientific minds—regardless of background—to contribute to advancing public health solutions worldwide. We provide reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities and uphold policies that create an inclusive and collaborative work environment. **Brief Job Overview** USP is seeking a scientific and regulatory leader for its Digital Standards Business Unit who is accountable for defining the scientific framework for USP’s digital pharmacopeial standards and building the coalition of regulators, government stakeholders, and industry partners required to champion and adopt it. Success in Year 1 will include establishing the scientific principles, policy foundations and workflows that govern how USP develops and delivers Digital Standards, securing internal alignment and building engagement with regulators, standards bodies, and pharmaceutical manufacturers to align the field behind that framework. This individual will represent USP in high-stakes external scientific and regulatory forums and serve as a visible thought leader on the future of digital pharmacopeial quality standards. Internally, the Director will work highly cross-functionally with USP’s Science, Quality, Lab Operations, IT, Commercial, and other teams to ensure Digital Standards are embedded in USP’s compendial and commercial processes. The Director will also have functional oversight of the portfolio of Digital Standards products, including USP-ID and MethodConnect, ensuring product direction aligns to the scientific framework. Scale-up and market adoption are priorities in subsequent years that will follow framework and stakeholder alignment. This role requires skills in both internal change management and external stakeholder alignment within the scientific realm. Remote employees must reside in one of the following states: MD, VA, DC, PA, WV, CA, MI, IL, KS, FL, NC, or MN. **How will YOU create impact here at USP?** As part of our mission to advance scientific rigor and public health standards, you will play a vital role in increasing global access to high-quality medicines through public standards and related programs. USP prioritizes scientific integrity, regulatory excellence, and evidence-based decision-making to ensure health systems worldwide can rely on strong, tested, and globally relevant quality standards. Additionally, USP’s People and Culture division, in partnership with the Equity Office, invests in leadership and workforce development to equip all employees with the skills to create high-performing, inclusive teams. This includes training in equitable management practices and tools to promote engaged, collaborative, and results-driven work environments. **Key Responsibilities** 1) Scientific Framework, Enterprise Strategy & Governance Define the scientific framework governing USP’s Digital Standards including scientific principles, structure, rigor requirements, and lifecycle approach, in close collaboration with USP’s Science and Quality teams, and translate that framework into the enterprise strategy and operating model required to scale Digital Standards across USP divisions. Oversee Digital Standards lifecycle governance, ensuring scientific rigor on par with traditional USP Standards and consistent application of the scientific framework across product lines. Ensure Digital Standards integrate with and support USP documentary standards and scientific development processes as the enterprise evolves. Establish and continuously improve cross-functional governance (decision rights, portfolio prioritization, metrics, escalation) to balance speed, rigor, and compliance. Provide executive-level updates, options, and recommendations to the Digital Standards steering committee and senior stakeholders. 2) Regulatory, Scientific & Industry Engagement Own development and execution of the regulator, government, and industry engagement strategy required to build alignment and cultivate champions for the scientific framework across the pharmaceutical ecosystem. Develop and oversee scientific and policy partnerships; collaborate with Legal department and other enterprise stakeholders to structure pilots and collaboration agreements with regulators, standards bodies, and pharmaceutical manufacturers. Represent USP as a thought leader through conferences, publications, and industry forums; maintain relationships with key scientific, regulatory, and industry influencers. 3) Policy Frameworks & Implementation Enablement Oversee internal and external policy frameworks for Digital Standards (structure, lifecycle, metadata, interoperability, implementation guidance) and ensure consistency across product lines. Ensure policy is translated into practical implementation assets (schemas/specifications, guidance, training, playbooks) for industry and internal stakeholders. Coordinate cross-division alignment so Digital Standards policies fit within enterprise controls (quality systems, security, legal, and commercial governance). 4) Portfolio Oversight Oversee portfolio-level strategic alignment, implementation plans, annual budgets, forecasts, and KPIs for Digital Standards Business Unit. Translate market insights and performance analytics into portfolio choices. Prioritize development of the portfolio of compendial Digital Standards and Digital Emerging Standards. 5) People Leadership, Talent Strategy & Culture Build, lead, and develop a multi-disciplinary team spanning advocacy, strategic collaborations, scientific development, policy, and program management. Provide functional oversight for the portfolio of digital products relating to Digital Standards to ensure alignment of product development with scientific, regulatory, and policy approaches. Coach and develop leaders; set clear expectations and equitable performance management practices; foster an inclusive culture that supports growth and accountability. Establish scalable operating rhythms (quarterly planning, portfolio reviews, KPI dashboards, stakeholder communications) that enable predictable delivery and learning. Be a visible influencer for Digital Standards both internally and externally; facilitate information sharing and thought leadership through publications, presentations, discussions, and other fora. **Who is USP Looking For?** The successful candidate will have a demonstrated understanding of our mission, commitment to excellence through inclusive and equitable behaviors and practices, ability to quickly build credibility with stakeholders, and the following competencies and experience: 10+ years of progressive experience in pharmaceutical sciences, analytical chemistry, regulatory science, or a closely related scientific discipline, with demonstrated scientific credibility recognized by peers in industry, regulators, or standards bodies. 7+ years of people management experience, including building multi-disciplinary teams across advocacy, scientific, policy, and program functions. Proven ability to implement changes across a matrixed organization, including influencing senior stakeholders, and shaping governance, operating models, workflows, and policy frameworks. Demonstrated ability to convene and align regulators, government stakeholders, standards bodies, and pharmaceutical manufacturers around a shared scientific or policy framework. item.description: Senior Manager, Global Trade Compliance Organization: U.S. Pharmacopeial Convention (USP) Location: Rockville, MD Date Posted: 08/27/2026 **Description** The U.S. Pharmacopeial Convention (USP) is an independent scientific organization that collaborates with the world’s leading health and science experts to develop rigorous quality standards for medicines, dietary supplements, and food ingredients. At USP, we believe that scientific excellence is driven by a commitment to fairness, integrity, and global collaboration. This belief is embedded in our core value of Passion for Quality and is demonstrated through the contributions of more than 1,300 professionals across twenty global locations, working to strengthen the supply of safe, high-quality medicines worldwide. At USP, we value inclusive scientific collaboration and recognize that attracting diverse expertise strengthens our ability to develop trusted public health standards. We foster an organizational culture that supports equitable access to mentorship, professional development, and leadership opportunities. Our partnerships, standards, and research reflect our belief that ensuring broad participation in scientific leadership results in stronger, more impactful outcomes for global health. USP is proud to be an equal employment opportunity employer (EEOE) and is committed to ensuring fair, merit-based selection processes that enable the best scientific minds—regardless of background—to contribute to advancing public health solutions worldwide. We provide reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities and uphold policies that create an inclusive and collaborative work environment. **Brief Job Overview** The Senior Manager, Global Trade Compliance is a hands-on managerial role responsible for the program management of USP’s global trade compliance program, with primary focus on applicable U.S. trade regulations, tariffs and sanctions requirements, and USP global trade compliance standards. The Senior Manager will work across all geographies, including serving as a functional manager to the India Trade Compliance team, to build and ensure adherence to a consistent global trade compliance framework for USP as the organization continues to evolve. The incumbent will proactively address immediate trade-related compliance needs, monitor sanctions-related developments and exposure, tariffs, and build longer-term plans to address emerging regulatory changes. This individual will take a strategic view to resolve complex import, export, tariff and sanctions compliance issues, including partnering with the Legal team and other business stakeholders to identify practical mitigation strategies for associated trade compliance risk, in a manner that fully complies with all governmental and organization policies, while aligning with business priorities where practical. **How Will YOU Create Impact Here at USP?** As part of our mission to advance scientific rigor and public health standards, you will play a vital role in increasing global access to high-quality medicines through public standards and related programs. USP prioritizes scientific integrity, regulatory excellence, and evidence-based decision-making to ensure health systems worldwide can rely on strong, tested, and globally relevant quality standards. Additionally, USP’s People and Culture division, in partnership with the Equity Office, invests in leadership and workforce development to equip all employees with the skills to create high-performing, inclusive teams. This includes training in equitable management practices and tools to promote engaged, collaborative, and results-driven work environments. **The Senior Manager, Global Trade Compliance Has the Following Responsibilities** **Lead Global Trade Compliance Strategy & Execution** Lead the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of USP’s Global Trade Compliance program in alignment with organizational goals, regulatory requirements, and business needs. Translate program priorities into actionable workplans and measurable team activities. **Support Global Alignment, Operational Consistency & Performance Accountability** Coordinate priorities, processes, and execution across geographically dispersed team members (U.S. & India) to promote consistent trade compliance practices. Support governance routines, performance tracking, and issue escalation; assess team capacity, workload, and processes to align resources to priority risks and business needs, improve efficiency, reduce duplication, and support sustainable team effectiveness. **Manage Global Trade Compliance Team Execution** Provide direct and functional leadership to Global Trade Compliance team members in the U.S. and India to align workplans and execution with USP’s global trade compliance standards. Assess team capacity, workload, and operating processes to ensure resources are aligned to the highest-priority compliance risks and business needs. Identify opportunities to improve efficiency, reduce duplication, and strengthen execution while supporting sustainable workloads and team effectiveness. **Support Team Development & Performance** Set clear goals and performance expectations for direct reports, provide coaching and constructive documented feedback, and support professional development to strengthen team capability, consistency, and execution. **Promote an Inclusive & Engaged Team Culture** Model inclusive leadership behaviors aligned with USP’s Equity = Excellence philosophy. Create a psychologically safe environment where diverse perspectives are valued, engagement is high, and team members are empowered to contribute and grow. **Partner Across the Organization** Work collaboratively with cross-functional stakeholders to provide practical trade compliance guidance, support risk identification, and integrate compliance requirements into day-to-day business processes. **Align Trade Compliance Risk Tolerance with Organizational Risk Profile** Maintain practical trade compliance risk tolerance levels aligned with USP’s overall organizational risk profile, escalating higher-risk matters and recommending mitigation strategies that balance regulatory requirements, business needs, and mission impact. **Ensure Regulatory Compliance & Risk Mitigation** Monitor and ensure compliance with applicable U.S. import/export laws, tariffs, sanctions requirements, and USP global trade compliance standards. Identify, assess, and help mitigate trade-related risks, in coordination with Legal, business stakeholders, and India-based resources as appropriate. Proactively recommend solutions to emerging issues. **Maintain Policies, Procedures & Program Improvements** Develop, maintain, and update trade compliance procedures, guidance, and best practices. Implement updates based on stakeholder feedback, monitoring results, and regulatory changes. **Oversee Classification, Licensing & Screening Programs** Maintain oversight of classification processes (HTS, Schedule B, ECCN), jurisdiction and license determinations, and global classification databases. Manage restricted party screening programs, resolve escalations, and ensure appropriate training and access controls. **Manage External Partners & Operational Execution** Coordinate with customs brokers, freight forwarders, and internal stakeholders to support compliant and efficient import/export execution. Monitor service quality, address operational issues, and manage key processes such as AES filings, country-of-origin determinations, valuation, free trade agreements, and recordkeeping. **Support Business Growth & Expansion** Partner with business stakeholders to identify and address trade compliance requirements related to new product launches, global expansion, and evolving business activities. Support practical processes, guidance, and controls to enable compliant and efficient execution. **Develop & Deliver Training Programs** Design and implement role-based training programs to build organizational awareness and capability in import/export compliance, ensuring stakeholders understand responsibilities and requirements. **Who Is USP Looking For?** The successful candidate will have a demonstrated understanding of our mission, commitment to excellence through inclusive and equitable behaviors and practices, ability to quickly build credibility with stakeholders, along with the following competencies and experience: Bachelor’s degree in business administration, economics, or relevant field; or equivalent experience. Minimum of 8 years relevant experience with U.S. import and export regulations and global trade. Minimum of 2 years people managerial experience. Experience collaborating with a global team. Experience in a functional management structure is preferred. Must have extensive knowledge of U.S. export laws and regulations, tariffs, U.S. denied parties and sanctioned country laws and regulations, including OFAC and other country trade regulations. Must have the ability to successfully lead and implement compliance initiatives with a positive and collaborative style. Must have the ability to plan and manage multiple tasks while working with individuals across the organization at all levels. Licensed Customs Broker and/or trade-related certifications required. Must possess strong attention to detail, critical thinking, and excellent problem-solving skills. Ability to work in a fast-paced environment with time-sensitive submissions and strict reporting deadlines. Strong and effective verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills. **Additional Desired Preferences** Experience in the pharmaceutical, chemical, and biologics industry area. Ability to understand potential obstacles to projects, appreciate stakeholder concerns, and positively influence successful completion through alignment. In addition, the Policy Adviser will contribute to other policy priorities across the organisation, working closely with colleagues in line with business needs and team priorities. tasks: – **Healthcare Committee management** — Manage the day‑to‑day activities of the Healthcare Committee and other member working groups. – **Advocacy initiatives** — Drive advocacy initiatives engagement** — Foster engagement with members and facilitate the development of consensus positions. – **Stakeholder relationships** — Build relationships with policymakers, industry associations and other relevant stakeholders. – **Cross‑team collaboration** — Work collaboratively with colleagues at all stages of advocacy activities and across the wider team to deliver impactful initiatives. – **Event organisation** — Organise committee meetings, conferences, seminars, delegation visits and other activities, including preparation, on‑site coordination and follow‑up. ### Qualifications / Skills / Experience: – Minimum two years of professional experience. – University degree in European affairs, political science, international relations, law, economics or a related discipline. – Good mindset, high attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously. – Excellent written communications skills. – Strong interpersonal skills and a collaborative approach to working with colleagues. – Computer literacy, particularly Microsoft Office. – Familiarity with AI tools and an understanding of their responsible use in a professional environment are an asset. ### Languages: Fluent English (both written and spoken); other EU languages can be an asset. ### Start date: As soon as possible. ### How to apply: Any candidate interested in applying for the position experience). – At least three years of experience in marketing, communications, social media, or digital content creation, including internships. – Strong understanding of major social media platforms using data to improve campaign performance. – Experience with or willingness to learn email marketing platforms, content management systems, social media management tools, and digital marketing software. – Comfortable experimenting with new marketing ideas, testing different approaches, and measuring results. – Excellent writing, editing, and communication skills. – Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously. – Self‑starter who is curious, creative, collaborative, and eager to learn. – Interest in public policy, advocacy, or association work is a plus. — ### **Other** – **Classification:** Full‑time, Salaried, Exempt – **Reports to:** Vice President of Communications – **Location:** Washington, DC or Remote – **Annual Salary Range:** $65,000 to $85,000 — ### **How to Apply** ALTA is a strong organization that prioritizes teamwork and collaboration and fosters a positive culture. If your knowledge, skills, and abilities are transferrable and you believe you’re a great candidate for ALTA, apply by sending a cover letter and resume to ** [email protected] **. item.title: Regulatory Affairs Specialist
item.description: Regulatory Affairs Specialist Organization: National Mining Association (NMA) Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/28/2026 ## About the job **Regulatory Affairs Specialist** ## About The National Mining Association America’s mining industry supplies the essential materials necessary for nearly every sector of our economy – from technology and healthcare to energy, transportation, infrastructure, and national security. The National Mining Association (NMA) is the only national trade organization that serves as the voice of the U.S. mining industry and the hundreds of thousands of American workers it employs before Congress, the federal agencies, the judiciary and the media, advocating for public policies that will help America fully and responsibly utilize its vast natural resources. We work to ensure America has secure and reliable supply chains, abundant and affordable energy, and the American‑sourced materials necessary for U.S. manufacturing and economic security, all delivered under world‑leading environmental, safety and labor standards. ## Job Summary The NMA is currently conducting a search for a full‑time **Regulatory Affairs Specialist** in the association’s headquarters office in Washington, D.C. The Regulatory Affairs Specialist assists the legal and regulatory affairs team in achieving the policy goals of the association and supports the General Counsel of Legal and Regulatory Affairs, as well as the rest of the department on all relevant tasks. The ideal candidate possesses previous experience in a highly visible administrative capacity with high‑level executives or government officials. ## Responsibilities Reporting to the General Counsel of Legal and Regulatory Affairs, the Regulatory Affairs Specialist assists the legal and regulatory affairs team on all tasks relevant to achieving the association’s legal and regulatory goals. – **Department memos** — Review, proofread, and send department memos to members via an electronic database. – **Meeting coordination** — Coordinate in‑office meetings, lunches, calendars, and logistics. – **Committee meetings** — Coordinate agenda, materials, and all relevant information for yearly, in‑person Environment and Lands Committee meetings and the annual Uranium Recovery Workshop (out‑of‑town travel required). – **Member meetings** — Coordinate agenda, materials, and all relevant information related to regularly scheduled member meetings. – **Task force support** — Send invitations, track RSVPs, manage agendas, link relevant materials, and assemble packets for monthly task force meetings. – **Safety awards** — Assist in planning and execution of the yearly Sentinels of the Safety awards event. – **Health and Safety Committee** — Assist and engage with the NMA Health and Safety Committee and NMA CORESafety Advisory group to achieve health and safety goals and objectives. – **CORESafety video** — Assist with CORESafety video activities. – **Regulatory research** — Conduct research on relevant legal and regulatory issues related to the association’s goals and current priorities. – **Association‑wide events** — Assist in projects requiring all‑hands‑on‑deck (e.g., board meetings, association‑wide events, receptions, MINExpo®, and filling in when other people are out of town). ## Required Education, Skills and Experience – **Education background** — Bachelor’s in Political Science, Public Policy, American Government, etc., or interest in pursuing a career in policy, regulation, or law. Strong preference for 1–3 years of related work experience on Capitol Hill, with the federal government, or at a trade association. – **Professional judgment** — Proven professional judgment. – **Fast‑paced environment** — Experience working in a fast‑paced environment with demonstrated ability to meet deadlines while managing multiple projects and ever‑changing priorities. – **Organization skills** — Highly organized and detail‑oriented. – **Initiative** — Self‑starter who takes initiative, anticipates needs, and resolves issues quickly. – **People skills** — Possess excellent people skills and a positive can‑do attitude. – **Flexibility** — Flexible to the changing needs and responsibilities of the workplace. – **Communication** — Excellent oral and written communication skills. – **Note taking** — Skilled in note taking and report writing. – **Record keeping** — Excellent in record keeping. ## Physical Demands – The position requires the ability to remain in a stationary position (standing and/or seated) more than half the time. – Must be able to kneel, crawl, or crouch down to fulfill essential functions less than half the time. – Must be able to maneuver (lift, move, carry, slide, etc.) less than 15 lbs. – Requires spending most of the time viewing computer monitors. ## Equal Opportunity Statement The NMA is a proud equal opportunity employer. We are committed to furthering our engagement with, support for, and understanding of our community; supporting all team members in being themselves; and driving the ongoing diversification of our team. We believe that everyone has distinct characteristics, skills, and backgrounds that make their experiences as members of the NMA team and the perspectives they bring to the office unique. We encourage and celebrate that uniqueness. Above all else, our goal is to maintain a welcoming culture for all—one where employees feel accepted, respected, valued, and supported in discussing and embracing differences, and where the entire team is invested in their success. ## Benefits The NMA provides a robust benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision insurance, as well as life and disability coverage. Employees also receive commuter benefits to help with parking or public transportation costs. The NMA offers paid time off, sick leave, and holidays. Starting salary is **$60,000–$65,000**, commensurate with experience. Interested candidates are invited to apply to ** [email protected] **. Applicants who may need accommodation are encouraged to contact the NMA to request and arrange accommodation. If you need assistance to accommodate a differing ability, you may request accommodation at any time. Please contact Human Resources at ** [email protected] **. Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today. item.title: Policy Analyst
item.description: Policy Analyst Organization: The Bernhardt Group Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/28/2026 ## About the Job ### Position Summary The **Policy Analyst** position plays a key role in advancing The Bernhardt Group’s government affairs priorities by providing policy analysis and legislative research. This role supports strategic objectives through monitoring policy developments, building stakeholder relationships, and developing resources to inform and strengthen engagement with policymakers and regulatory agencies. The ideal candidate is a collaborative, detail‑oriented professional able to manage multiple priorities, adapt to changing demands, and perform effectively in a fast‑paced environment. — ## Job Duties – Supports and advances government affairs initiatives through legislative research, policy analysis, advocacy, and relationship‑building. – Manages assigned legislative and regulatory portfolios with increasing independence, monitors and analyzes congressional and agency activity, and provides strategic insight on complex policy issues. – Develops and disseminates advocacy and policy materials—including issue briefs, fact sheets, legislative summaries, and draft testimony—and contributes to advocacy strategy development. – Tracks and organizes legislative and regulatory data, maintains databases, and prepares reports and briefings for senior staff. – Coordinates special projects, may work with external consultants, and responds to inquiries. – Provides administrative and operational support as needed. – Performs other duties as required. — ## Qualifications – At least 2 years of work experience, including at least 1 year of Congressional or Administration experience is required. – Exceptional writing skills are required. – Bachelor’s Degree. – Experience working with the U.S. House of Representatives, U.S. Senate, Federal Government Agencies, political campaigns, advocacy and lobbying, and/or policy research and analysis is required. – Understanding of legislative process and executive branch function. – Strong computer and research skills, including Microsoft Office Suite. – Ability to work well under pressure and balance competing priorities. – Ability to engage clients and government officials in a mature, professional manner. – Experience tracking legislation. — ## About the Firm The Bernhardt Group is a Washington, D.C.–based bipartisan policy and government affairs firm founded by David Bernhardt, former U.S. Secretary of the Interior. The firm helps clients navigate complex regulatory, legislative, and political challenges, drawing on deep executive branch experience and relationships across Capitol Hill. From executive branch engagement and policy advocacy to regulatory navigation and project management, the team combines strategic insight with hands‑on execution to deliver durable outcomes for clients facing Washington’s toughest challenges. — ## Compensation and Benefits The Bernhardt Group offers a benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401(k) + match, and personal time off. Salary range for this role: **$60,000–$80,000**, depending on experience. — ## Equal Opportunity Employer The Bernhardt Group is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law. — ## How to Apply To apply, please submit a cover letter, resume, and writing sample to ** [email protected] **. item.title: Policy Analyst (United States Space Force)
item.description: Policy Analyst (United States Space Force) Organization: Apogee Location: Hampton, VA Date Posted: 08/28/2026 ## About the job ### Overview Apogee has an exciting new opportunity for a Policy Analyst (United States Space Force) to support Headquarters United States Air Force (HAF/A10). In this role, you will provide full‑time, on‑site arms control subject‑matter expertise to the United States Space Force and other DAF units, supporting a full range of arms control activities, arms control policy formulation, development, and dissemination. The HAF/A10 contract delivers technical, analytical, operational, programmatic, and planning subject‑matter expertise to HAF/A10 and its component divisions to advance national security strategic plans, policies, concepts, and initiatives. This is a full‑time, on‑site position located at Langley Air Force Base in Hampton, VA. This position is contingent upon contract award.*** — ## Responsibilities **Policy Formulation & Dissemination.** Conduct research and analysis on policy and technical issues to provide recommendations on treaty negotiations, implementation, and compliance. Serve as the primary liaison between the USSF, HAF, the DoW, and interagency forums (e.g., CRGs, IWGs). **Implementation & Compliance.** Provide technical expertise on all treaty implementation and compliance activities. Support the preparation of annual programming and budgeting submissions for the USSF treaty‑related activities. Review and provide input on USSF and unit‑level compliance plans and instructions. Input all required notifications and data into the Arms Control Enterprise System (ACES). **Exercise & Inspection Support.** Plan, schedule, and manage annual exercise events within the USSF Area of Responsibility (AOR). Assist units in preparing for treaty implementation exercises and real‑world on‑site inspections. Provide direct on‑site assistance during exercises and inspections and update all relevant HAF and USSF guidance documents. **Education & Training.** Deliverable: Provide quarterly‑reviewed and updated USSF‑unique training materials. A log of changes will be submitted with each update. **Modernization & Acquisition.** Work directly with Program Executive Offices (PEOs) and System Program Offices (SPOs) to review and track acquisition programs, ensuring full compliance with all in‑force and developing treaties. Provide treaty expertise and advice to PEOs and SPOs regarding program impacts on treaty compliance. **Analysis & Research.** Conduct detailed research and analysis on policy and technical issues to support USSF positions on treaty negotiations, implementation, and compliance. Produce formal treaty analysis papers, impact assessments, and recommendations. **Conference & Meeting Support.** Provide full logistical support for all USSF‑sponsored conferences, workshops, and meetings. Prepare and manage all event materials (agendas, briefings, etc.), facilitate the event, and produce detailed after‑action reports and meeting minutes. **Policy Analysis & Recommendation.** Conduct continuous research, review, and analysis of policy and technical issues. Provide formal comments on official documents and produce detailed recommendations on Air Force policy and operations concerning treaty negotiations, implementation, and compliance. **Interagency Liaison.** Serve as the primary liaison between the supported USSF and external entities, including DAF, the DoW, and other interagency planning and policymaking forums. Represent USSF equities and positions in key forums such as CRGs, IWGs, and interagency backstopping meetings. — ## Qualifications ### Minimum Experience **Citizenship:** Must be a US citizen **Clearance:** Must have an active Top Secret clearance with SCI eligibility **Education:** Bachelor’s degree **Years of Experience:** Ten (10) years of experience in the respective technical/professional discipline; includes five (5) years of DoD experience — ## Preferred Qualifications **Clearance:** TS/SCI **Education:** Master’s degree **Years of Experience:** Eight (8) years of experience in the respective technical/professional discipline; includes five (5) years of DoD experience Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: DAF Counter WMD Policy Analyst
item.description: DAF Counter WMD Policy Analyst Organization: Apogee Location: Arlington, VA Date Posted: 08/28/2026 ## About the Job ### Overview Apogee has an exciting new opportunity for a **DAF Counter WMD Policy Analyst** to support the Headquarters United States Air Force (**HAF/A10**). In this role, you will provide expert analytical, programmatic, and staff process support for AF/A10’s CWMD and Biodefense policy responsibilities. This includes analyzing national strategy, managing daily staff actions, reviewing joint programs, and providing logistical support for key events to ensure Air Force positions are effectively developed and represented. You will also provide expert analytical and administrative support for the multitiered Air Force CWMD governance structure, including the **CWMD Council**, **CWM Integration Group (CIG)**, and the **Policy Working Group (PWG)**. Responsibilities include improving DAF CWMD and biodefense interoperability and knowledge sharing across the Air Force, sister Services, Joint, interagency, and academic communities. The HAF/A10 contract delivers technical, analytical, operational, programmatic, and planning subject‑matter expertise to HAF/A10 and its component divisions to advance national security strategic plans, policies, concepts, and initiatives. This is a full‑time, on‑site position located at the Pentagon in Arlington, VA. **This position is contingent upon contract award.*** — ## Responsibilities ### CWMD Staff Actions and Taskings – Analyze, research, draft, coordinate, and route all daily CWMD requirements and taskings from internal and external organizations (e.g., OSD, JS, HAF). – Draft staff packages (e.g., SSSs, point papers, white papers, briefings) prepared in the proper AF format. – Coordinate responses to official Requests for Information (RFIs). – Complete Comment Resolution Matrixes (CRMs) for document reviews. ### CWMD/Biodefense Policy and Program Analysis – Review and analyze DoD, Joint, and Air Force programs, strategic documents (e.g., NPR, NDS), and policy directives to determine impacts and equities for the CWMD and Biodefense enterprises. – Form analysis reports on guidance and strategy documents. – Provide recommendations for DAF positions in requirements development forums. – Provide analysis of intelligence reports with options to address readiness challenges. – Coordinate with Joint, CCMD, MAJCOM, Center, and other CWMD/CBRN staff as needed to support DAF policy, readiness, exercise, planning, and other tasks. ### CBRN Survivability Program Support – Conduct research and analysis and provide program management support for the DoD CBRN Survivability Program in accordance with DoDI 3150.09. – Provide draft inputs for the annual CBRN Survivability Report delivered via the designated data system. ### Forum and Event Logistical Support – Provide comprehensive SME, logistical, administrative, and security support for all AF/A10‑sponsored CWMD, CBRND, and Biodefense forums, meetings, working groups, and conferences. – Provide/review/staff all event materials (agendas, minutes, read‑aheads, rosters, talking points, briefings). – Plan and coordinate successful technical exchanges, working groups, and conferences, including facility, security, and AV/IT coordination. ### Pre‑Forum Analytical and Administrative Support – Coordinate and consolidate agenda topics, develop support materials, and prepare senior leaders for effective participation in all designated governance forums. – Produce Senior Leader Support Packages, including draft read‑aheads, agendas, and briefing materials. ### Forum Execution and Documentation – Provide logistical and administrative support during forum execution to capture a comprehensive record of all discussions, decisions, and assigned tasks. – Produce draft meeting minutes for government review and formal distribution. ### Post‑Forum Follow‑Up Actions – Monitor, document, and report on the progress of all action items assigned during governance forums to ensure their timely completion. – Provide a current Action Item Tracker detailing the status, responsible office, and closure of all assigned tasks. ### Strategic Document Review – Review and analyze high‑level strategic documents (e.g., Defense Planning Guidance, Global Campaign Plans, OPLANs) to ensure DAF CWMD and Biodefense equities, threats, and objectives are fully integrated. – Analyze DAF operational needs to provide formal recommendations for CWMD, CBRND, and Biodefense requirements. – Prepare analytical products and draft inputs to support government representation and advocacy in Joint, Service, and interagency acquisition and planning forums. ### Studies and Analysis – Conduct studies and analysis to identify and analyze CWMD and Biodefense operational readiness and planning gaps, informed by capabilities documents and best practices from allied, joint, and interagency partners. – Prepare analytical materials and briefings to support DAF engagement with DoD, non‑DoD institutions, other Services, and foreign partners. ### Forum Participation Support – Identify opportunities for DAF personnel to attend relevant CWMD and Biodefense discussions, conferences, workshops, and seminars hosted by educational and policy institutions (e.g., Air University, National Defense University). – Provide analytical and logistical support for government attendance. – Curate a list of recommended engagement opportunities. ### Forum Representation and Analysis – As directed, attend and participate in designated CWMD and Biodefense forums to represent Air Force equities. – Analyze all exchanged information, concepts, and requirements. – Produce post‑Forum Analysis Reports detailing findings, impacts on DAF/A10 strategy, and recommended courses of action for government consideration. ### Analytical and Decision Products – Based on forum outcomes, produce comprehensive analytical products to inform AF/A10 leadership. – Produce information, point, white, and decision papers discussing forum results, progress, and recommended AF positions. — ## Qualifications ### Minimum Experience – **Citizenship:** Must be a US citizen – **Clearance:** Must have an active Top Secret security clearance with SCI eligibility and be able to maintain it – **Education:** Bachelor’s degree – **Years of Experience:** Ten (10) years of experience in the respective technical/professional discipline, including five (5) years of DoD experience ### Preferred Qualifications – **Clearance:** TS/SCI – **Education:** Master’s degree – **Years of Experience:** Eight (8) years of experience in the respective technical/professional discipline, including five (5) years of DoD experience — ## Additional Information – **Location:** Pentagon, Arlington, VA – **On‑site:** This is a full‑time on‑site position – **Contingency:** This position is contingent upon contract award.*** Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Public Relations Manager
item.description: Public Relations Manager Organization: Gartner Location: Stamford, CT Date Posted: 08/28/2026 ## Description Gartner’s Corporate Communications team is responsible for defining, promoting and protecting the Gartner brand. By creating compelling content and marketing programs, our goal is to engage internal and external audiences in our value proposition and corporate narrative in order to drive long‑term, double‑digit growth. The PR Manager will play a significant role in the development and execution of a holistic PR program for Gartner’s IT practice to promote our expertise and thought leadership in the IT space, increasing our brand awareness among key targets (prospects and clients), shortening the sales cycle and contributing to the continued growth of the company worldwide. — ## What You Will Do – Work closely with the Senior PR Manager to significantly contribute to the holistic PR program for Gartner’s IT practice in the Americas, focused on promoting our expertise and thought leadership, and generating brand awareness for Gartner in the IT space. – Manage incoming media inquiries by understanding reporters’ deadlines and determining the right analyst for the topic. – Cultivate and manage relationships with VIP and top‑tier journalists — responsible for half of U.S. VIP reporter–listed activities. – Lead PR/media relations activities for North America Summits, including pitching press release ideas, producing releases, attending weekly meetings with the Conferences team, providing PR updates, and collaborating with the Senior PR Manager on flagship conference (IT Symposium/XPO) activities. – Manage breaking news Rapid Response program, demonstrating strong news judgment and the ability to respond urgently and effectively. – Manage half of proactive media pitches each month in partnership with the Senior PR Manager, according to monthly and weekly scopes of work. – Identify content for and write press releases, analyst Q&As, conference daily highlights, and byline articles based on Gartner research, demonstrating strong news judgment and writing skills. – Manage external event pitches and outreach to maximize Gartner’s media presence. – Track and measure monthly VIP press coverage and report on outcomes. – Ensure press lists for breaking news, content pitches and Conferences outreach are accurate and up to date. – Update analysts’ contact sheet at the beginning of the year and as changes occur, ensuring accuracy for journalist outreach. – Update the data book quarterly (at minimum), providing journalists with timely and relevant information. – Post press releases and event advisories on Gartner Newsroom and Business Wire. — ## What You Will Need – 5+ years’ experience in internal communications, public relations, corporate communications, or marketing role, preferably in a large organization. – Bachelor’s degree in journalism, public relations, communications, or a related field. – Experience working with multiple stakeholders, including senior executives and individuals in adjacent specialties, in a professional, fast‑paced environment. – Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills. – Self‑starter who demonstrates independence and initiative in completing deliverables with minimal direction. – Ability to interface with all levels of the organization, including corporate executives and business leaders. – Experience developing and executing communication plans utilizing a range of tactics. – Exceptional collaboration and problem‑solving skills. – Sense of urgency when approaching job responsibilities, particularly when working with the media. – Proficiency in and active use of social media, engaging with journalists and amplifying Gartner’s media presence. – Willingness to travel approximately 1–3 times per year, primarily to work onsite at Gartner Summits. **Must be located within a 60‑minute commute to Stamford, CT.** #LI‑AH1 — ## Who Are We? At Gartner, Inc. (NYSE:IT), we guide the leaders who shape the world. Our mission relies on expert analysis and bold ideas to deliver actionable, objective business and technology insights, helping enterprise leaders and their teams succeed with their mission‑critical priorities. Since our founding in 1979, we’ve grown to 20,000 associates globally who support over 13,000 client enterprises in ~90 countries and territories. We do important, interesting and substantive work that matters. That’s why we hire associates with the intellectual curiosity, energy and drive to want to make a difference. The bar is unapologetically high. So is the impact you can have here. — ## What Makes Gartner a Great Place to Work? Our vast, virtually untapped market potential offers limitless opportunities — opportunities that may not even exist right now — for you to grow professionally and flourish personally. How far you go is driven by your passion and performance. We hire remarkable people who collaborate and win as a team. Together, our singular, unifying goal is to deliver results for our clients. Our teams are inclusive and composed of individuals from different geographies, cultures, religions, ethnicities, races, genders, sexual orientations, abilities and generations. We invest in great leaders who bring out the best in you and the company, enabling us to multiply our impact and results. This is why, year after year, we are recognized worldwide as a great place to work. — ## Gartner Is the World Authority on AI At Gartner, you’ll join a company at the very center of the AI revolution. Gartner has proactive, objective guidance throughout clients’ AI journeys. We set the standard for how organizations leverage artificial intelligence to drive meaningful impact. You’ll have access to unmatched resources, expertise and technology, and play a key role in helping Gartner and our clients innovate and grow as we leverage AI to transform business and technology landscapes. It’s an exciting time to be at Gartner, with limitless opportunities to make a real impact, grow your skills, and build a lasting, meaningful career in a field that’s reshaping the way we operate. If you’re passionate about AI and want to be part of a team that’s guiding the leaders who shape the world, Gartner is the place for you. — ## What Do We Offer? Gartner offers world‑class benefits, highly competitive compensation and disproportionate rewards for top performers. In our hybrid work environment, we provide the flexibility and support for you to thrive — working virtually when it’s productive to do so and getting together with colleagues in a vibrant community that is purposeful, engaging and inspiring. Ready to grow your career with Gartner? Join us. Gartner believes in fair and equitable pay. A reasonable estimate of the base salary range for this role is **79,000 USD – 109,000 USD**. Actual salaries may vary within or outside the range based on factors including education, training, experience, professional achievement, business need and location. In addition to base salary, employees participate in either an annual bonus plan based on company and individual performance, or a role‑based, uncapped sales incentive plan. Our talent acquisition team will provide details on bonus or incentive programs to eligible candidates. We also offer market‑leading benefits including generous PTO, a 401k match up to $7,200 per year, discounted company stock purchase opportunities, and more. — ## Equal Employment Opportunity Gartner provides equal employment opportunities to all applicants and employees without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, citizenship status, age, national origin, ancestry, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected status. Gartner is committed to being an Equal Opportunity Employer and offers opportunities to all job seekers, including those with disabilities. item.title: VP, U.S. Policy
item.description: VP, U.S. Policy Organization: Cognition Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/28/2026 We are an applied AI lab building end‑to‑end software agents. We’re the makers of Devin, the first AI software engineer. Our team is extremely talent‑dense. Among our founding team, we have world‑class competitive programmers, former founders, and leaders from companies at the cutting edge of AI including Scale AI, Palantir, Cursor, Waymo, Tesla, Lunchclub, Modal, Google DeepMind, and Nuro. Building Devin is just the first step — our hardest challenges still lie ahead. If you’re excited to solve some of the world’s biggest problems and build AI that can reason on real‑world tasks, apply to join us. ## About the Role AI is becoming central to economic competitiveness, national security, and how the U.S. government operates. The decisions policymakers make over the next few years (on procurement, workforce, compute, security standards, and federal adoption) will shape how software agents are deployed in the public and private sectors, and how the U.S. competes globally. Cognition needs a senior leader who can represent us in those conversations from day one. We’re hiring a VP, U.S. Policy to build and lead Cognition’s public policy and government affairs function in the United States. You will own our policy strategy end‑to‑end: developing our positions, building trusted relationships across Congress, the Executive Branch, and federal agencies, and translating what our engineers are building into clear narratives that senior policymakers can act on. This role sits at the intersection of technology, government, and company strategy. You’ll work directly with our founders, our Legal, Federal, GTM teams, and product leadership, and you’ll be the person who anticipates policy risks and opportunities before they reach us. This is a builder’s role: there is no existing playbook, no inherited team, and no shortage of surface area. Based in Washington DC, reporting to the Chief Legal and Global Affairs Officer. ## Core Responsibilities – Own Cognition’s U.S. policy strategy – define our positions on AI, federal adoption, national security, workforce transformation, and technology competitiveness, and align them with company strategy – Industry Collaboration – lead engagement with Congress, the Executive Branch, regulators, and federal agencies, including direct advocacy and support for executive‑level engagements – Regulatory Affairs – monitor and analyze legislative, regulatory, and geopolitical developments in the U.S. and key international markets, and translate them into clear recommendations for leadership – Content and Communication – produce the substance: policy positions, white papers, comment letters, briefing materials, and thought leadership that articulate a distinctive point of view – Represent Cognition externally in policy discussions, industry working groups, conferences, and strategic forums – Partner with engineering and product teams to bring policy signal back into product and roadmap decisions, and build the internal policy team as the function grows ## What We Value – Builder mentality – you operate independently, build from scratch, and possess low ego; no problem is too small – Exceptional writing – you can produce a white paper, a one‑pager for a member of Congress, and an internal strategy memo, and each will land with its audience – Communication – ability to learn technical concepts quickly and explain them clearly to non‑technical audiences – Focus on outcomes, with the judgment to navigate complex political environments and make calls in high‑stakes, fast‑moving situations – Ability to balance innovation, competitiveness, and responsible governance in the positions you take ## Requirements – 10+ years in public policy, government affairs, national security, or technology policy – including time in Congress, the White House, a federal agency, a national security organization, or a leading policy institution – Sufficient facility with AI and its underlying technical concepts to communicate with engineers and policymakers alike – Strong command of U.S. government institutions, the legislative process, regulatory frameworks, and federal budgeting cycles – Established bipartisan relationships among policymakers, regulators, and agency leadership, and a track record of influencing senior stakeholders ## You Might Excel If You… – Have advised senior government officials, executives, or technology leaders directly – Have worked on AI, cybersecurity, defense technology, cloud infrastructure, or emerging technology policy – Have built a policy function, or been the first policy hire, at a fast‑growing technology company – Understand both public and private sector perspectives on innovation and regulation ## Equal Opportunity Cognition is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities throughout the hiring process — please let us know if you need any. item.title: Vice President, Europe
item.description: Vice President, Europe Organization: U.S. Chamber of Commerce Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/28/2026 **About Us:** If you are passionate about the ability of American business to improve lives, solve problems, and strengthen society, the U.S. Chamber of Commerce is the place for you. As the world’s largest business organization, we believe in building a future that gives everyone the opportunity to pursue a better tomorrow. We make it our job today–and every day–to build the strongest relationships possible among the American people, business leaders, and elected officials in Washington, D.C., state capitals, and countries around the globe. For them and the businesses we represent, the U.S. Chamber is a trusted advocate and partner. We are driven by the pursuit of innovation and partnership and hold ourselves to the highest standards. Our commitment to our members is matched only by our commitment to our employees. As part of our team, we will support your long-term career development while delivering relevant learning opportunities. We will empower you to lead, develop deep expertise, and find new approaches to solving the toughest challenges. — **Position Overview:** The Vice President, Europe will report to the senior vice president, Europe and will work closely with relevant regional, policy, communications, and member relations teams across the organization. The successful candidate will serve as deputy leader of the Chamber’s Europe team, help lead policy work on the transatlantic economic relationship, and advance the interests of American business across key EU institutions, European markets, and policy portfolios. The candidate will bring deep knowledge of European policy and institutions, a strong understanding of the business community’s priorities, and the ability to translate complex regulatory developments into clear strategy and action. This role requires a skilled advocate, trusted relationship builder, and strategic thinker who can work effectively with member companies, policymakers, foreign governments, business associations, and internal Chamber partners. — **Responsibilities:** – Partner with the senior vice president, Europe on strategic development and growth of the Europe Program. – Shape and expand Chamber advocacy and programming pertaining to transatlantic relations, including EU and non-EU countries in Europe, Ukraine, and the U.K. – Lead advocacy in the EU, member state and other European capitals, and Washington on key policy priorities, including on digital, defense, tax, and cyber issues. – Provide strategic oversight of the Europe team’s energy and sustainability work, including EU regulatory developments and related market-access issues. – Assist in fundraising outreach and membership growth and retention. – Build and maintain relationships with senior U.S., European, and Ukrainian government officials, business leaders, diplomatic representatives, trade associations, and other stakeholders. – Work with member companies to identify policy concerns, shape advocacy priorities, and deliver value through timely analysis, strategic advice, and opportunities for engagement. – Represent the Chamber in public and private settings, including meetings with government officials, member briefings, delegations, conferences, and external events. – Coordinate closely with Chamber policy experts, communications teams, government affairs colleagues, and other regional and functional teams to align Europe-related advocacy across the organization. – Oversee and/or draft policy papers, reports, meeting briefings, testimony, speeches, and other materials for use with external and internal audiences, including government officials, corporate members, policy committees, media outlets, Chamber executives, and the public. – Contribute content for weekly newsletters, blogs, internal and external updates, and websites. — **Requirements:** – 10+ years of experience in international affairs, trade, government relations, public policy and regulation, business advocacy, or a related field. – Bachelor’s degree required with advanced degree in international relations, public policy, law, business, economics, or a related field strongly preferred. – Strong understanding of transatlantic commercial relations and policies affecting U.S. companies in Europe. – Demonstrated policy and regulatory expertise in two or more of the following areas: digital, cybersecurity, defense, tax, energy, sustainability, or international trade. – Experience working with senior government officials, business executives, diplomatic representatives, and/or trade association leaders. – Deep knowledge of EU institutions and European regulatory processes. – Strong strategic judgment, political acumen, and the ability to translate complex policy developments into actionable business insights. – Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to brief senior executives and produce clear, persuasive advocacy materials. – Proven ability to manage multiple priorities, drive projects forward, and deliver results in a fast-paced environment. – Strong relationship-building skills and a member-service orientation. – Ability to work collaboratively across teams and with colleagues at all levels of the organization. — The salary range for this position is $178,987.00 to $195,000.00. The actual salary paid for this position will vary based on market data, an applicant’s qualifications, relevant degrees, certifications, and other factors. Our full-time employees are eligible for benefits, including health care, vision, dental, retirement, and paid leave. We provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. #LI-Hybrid Learn more here Earn a certificate with the Council! item.title: Director, Federal Government Affairs
item.description: Director, Federal Government Affairs Organization: Illumina Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/28/2026 # About the Job What if the work you did every day could impact the lives of people you know? Or all of humanity? At Illumina, we are expanding access to genomic technology to realize health equity for billions of people around the world. Our efforts enable life‑changing discoveries that are transforming human health through the early detection and diagnosis of diseases and new treatment options for patients. Working at Illumina means being part of something bigger than yourself. Every person, in every role, has the opportunity to make a difference. Surrounded by extraordinary people, inspiring leaders, and world‑changing projects, you will do more and become more than you ever thought possible. # Position Summary Drives development and implementation of corporate policy through strategic partnerships with government and industry groups, aligning with business objectives. Works on a team to foster relationships with key members of the federal government and industry groups to promote company interests in Washington, D.C. Prepares policy briefings, testimony for pending legislative actions, and provides thought leadership and recommendations in collaboration with the government affairs team. Works on a team to ensure appropriate company participation in government forums and industry group meetings. Responsible for engaging with policymakers, leaders of government and industry councils, and lobbyists to influence public policy, monitor government initiatives, and advocate for specific plans to advance the company’s objectives. Changes to individual responsibilities may occur due to business needs, and other related duties may be assigned. This role will report to the Vice President, Government Affairs for US and Canada. The individual must reside in the greater Washington D.C. area. # Responsibilities Works collaboratively on a team to inform the organization’s policies and objectives involving matters of the federal government, regulations, and advocacy strategies. Provides analysis of proposed federal legislation to determine potential impact on the organization. Responsible for recommending company positions on federal legislation, regulations, and policy priorities. Identifies, monitors, and influences government legislation, regulation, and public policy with the intent to optimize the business environment and patient access to Illumina solutions. Educates federal public policymakers on issues and initiatives that support and advocate for our industry and business by creating and maintaining a positive leadership image and business climate for Illumina. Works with assigned business units on government affairs strategies to execute on business priorities. Represents Illumina in assigned trade associations and coalitions to further corporate priorities and strategies. Utilizes Illumina executives and subject matter experts to help educate government policymakers. Helps manage major company events, high‑profile meetings, and visits with government officials. **Political Development** – Helps the team execute successful company and industry political events to favorably position the company with elected officials in full conformance with applicable political action and election laws and rules. **Policy Analysis** – Provides insightful analysis of proposed federal administrative and legislative actions and their impact on Illumina. In close partnership with business units and corporate functional experts, develops policy positions and appropriate messaging tailored to target audiences. **Advocacy** – Communicates directly and persuasively with government officials and staff, as well as both allies and opponents, in the advancement of Illumina’s public policy priorities. Demonstrates thought leadership and subject‑matter expertise to advance business strategic objectives through proactive public policy engagement. Develops issue advocacy materials and presentations, testimony for delivery to legislative committees and regulatory bodies, and internal messaging for key contacts, employee grassroots, and vendor engagement programs. **Tracking and Intelligence Gathering** – Identifies and monitors legislative and regulatory activities for their potential impact, and reports to internal partners in a timely and precise manner. **Industry Associations and Coalitions** – Serves on industry task forces and working groups where policy interests are aligned, and Illumina leadership can be exerted. Represents the company at trade associations and participates as directed in meetings and work of national associations. **Third‑Party Ally Development** – Builds and leads disparate advocacy coalition efforts to raise awareness of barriers to patient access to therapy and the importance of fostering a business environment friendly to technology innovation, investment, and employment. Works on a team to help cultivate strategic partnerships with public and private payers, provider organizations, key clinical research institutions, and patient advocacy organizations. Leverages internal resources to support engagement plans. The listed responsibilities are an essential but not exhaustive list of the usual duties associated with the position. Individual responsibilities may change due to business needs. # Requirements Typically requires a Bachelor’s degree and a minimum of 15–18 years of related experience, with 10+ years of management experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Experience working with Congress, the Administration, Executive Agencies, and other policymakers at the federal government level. Experience communicating and presenting to senior‑level stakeholders, both internal and external to the company. Experience with federal compliance requirements. Strong working knowledge of the federal legislative and regulatory processes. Demonstrates business acumen with knowledge of current policies, practices, and competitive landscape, as well as future trends and challenges in the marketplace. Significant experience reading, analyzing, and interpreting federal legislative and regulatory documents. Ability to convey company views and positions in an open, honest manner that is interesting to others; able to tell a compelling story and use effective case studies; and to offer solutions and generate favorable action. Ability to build strong relationships, collaborate with and lead teams, and work well with cross‑functional colleagues. Capacity to be a quick learner of new subject matters and ability to adapt nimbly to a rapidly changing healthcare ecosystem and a challenging political environment. Able to assess and manage risk, accept accountability, and offer viable alternative strategies, as necessary, to achieve goals. Strong problem‑solving and negotiation skills. Articulate and personable. Ability to direct multi‑stakeholder education and advocacy efforts. Demonstrated initiative, resourcefulness, and attention to detail in the execution of strategies. Capability to manage multiple assignments simultaneously, with strong organizational skills and attention to prioritization among conflicting demands. Exemplary written and large‑audience presentation skills. Demonstrated leadership skills with unquestioned personal standards of conduct, work ethic, and integrity, and an ability to maintain calm under pressure. Occasional travel to San Diego HQ and to represent Illumina at external events on an as‑needed basis. All listed requirements are deemed essential functions of this position; however, business conditions may require reasonable accommodation for additional tasks and responsibilities. # Compensation & Benefits The estimated base salary range for the Director, Federal Government Affairs (Washington D.C. / Remote) role based in the United States is $187,400 – $281,000. Placement depends on experience, skills, location, and internal equity. All employees are eligible for variable cash programs and eligible roles may receive equity. Benefits include access to genomics sequencing, family planning, health/dental/vision coverage, retirement benefits, and paid time off. # Inclusion & Equal Opportunity Illumina is deeply rooted in belonging, promoting an inclusive environment where employees feel valued and empowered. The company confirms a zero‑net pay gap regardless of gender, ethnicity, or race. Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) provide career development, cultural awareness, and social responsibility opportunities. Illumina is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing employment opportunity regardless of sex, race, creed, color, gender, religion, marital status, domestic partner status, age, national origin or ancestry, physical or mental disability, medical condition, sexual orientation, pregnancy, military or veteran status, citizenship status, and genetic information. Illumina conducts background checks on applicants receiving conditional offers. Results may impact the offer in accordance with applicable laws. Illumina prohibits the use of generative AI in the application and interview process. For accommodation requests, contact [email protected] . The position will remain posted until a final candidate is selected or a sufficient number of qualified applicants is reached. This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship. item.title: VP of Government Affairs
item.description: VP of Government Affairs Organization: Picogrid Location: Washington, DC Date Posted: 08/28/2026 # Job Description ## Who we are Picogrid is a leading venture‑backed defense technology company founded to bridge the decades‑long gap between modern technology and the critical demands of national security. Today, we’re building the essential infrastructure to unify sensors, autonomy, and operators, with our technology deployed in active operations around the world. Our mission is to deliver an operational advantage to secure the United States and its allies. ## About the Role As Picogrid’s first VP of Government Affairs, you will own the company’s entire relationship with Washington: from Capitol Hill to the Pentagon. You will build and execute a government affairs strategy that accelerates Picogrid’s access to defense programs, shapes policy in the unmanned systems and C2 space, and ensures policymakers understand what is at stake as autonomous systems become central to modern warfare. You will build the in‑house function from zero to one, establish Picogrid’s presence in DC, and serve as the primary voice of the company to the U.S. government. You will work directly with company leadership to translate our operational track record and technology into policy wins, procurement opportunities, and strategic relationships. The right person for this role is equally comfortable in a congressional hearing room and a field briefing. You understand defense acquisition as well as you understand appropriations. You can distill how a hardware‑software stack enabling unmanned system orchestration changes the character of warfare, and explain why that matters to a staffer with five minutes to spare. ## Responsibilities – **Government affairs strategy** — Own and execute Picogrid’s full government affairs strategy at the federal level: build and maintain deep relationships with key decision‑makers across Congress, OSD, the military services, combatant commands, and relevant interagency stakeholders, including defense appropriations and armed services committees. – **Defense budget positioning** — Drive Picogrid’s positioning in relevant defense budget cycles: identifying funding lines, influencing program office priorities, and supporting business development with strategic intelligence from the Hill and Pentagon. – **Policy development** — Develop and communicate clear, compelling policy positions on issues critical to Picogrid’s mission, including export controls, open architecture standards, and technology competition with peer adversaries. – **Executive advising** — Serve as a strategic advisor to the CEO and executive team on political developments, policy risks, and government relationship management, and represent Picogrid externally at key industry events, hearings, conferences, and stakeholder engagements. – **Team leadership** — Hire and manage an internal team, external advisors, lobbyists, and consultants as the function grows. – **Coalition building** — Build coalitions with aligned defense tech companies, trade associations, and national security organizations to advance shared policy goals. ## Required Qualifications – 8+ years of experience in government affairs, defense policy, congressional affairs, or related roles, with a demonstrable track record of influencing policy and procurement outcomes. – Experience building out a Government Affairs function and team at a high‑growth technology company. – Demonstrated ability to translate complex technical capabilities into accessible, compelling policy narratives. – Comfort operating as a founder‑minded, high‑ownership individual contributor. – Strong written and verbal communication skills; executive presence and credibility with senior government officials. – Willingness to travel regularly between El Segundo and Washington, DC, and to attend field and customer engagements as needed. ## Preferred Qualifications – Direct experience in or with DoD, a military service, or the Office of the Secretary of Defense, particularly in acquisition, requirements, or technology policy. – Familiarity with the unmanned systems, autonomous systems, or C2/ISR policy landscape, including relevant programs and offices (e.g., CDAO, OUSD R&E, DIU, PEO UAS). – Experience supporting government affairs at a defense technology company or non‑traditional defense contractor. – Knowledge of export control frameworks (ITAR/EAR) and how they affect defense technology companies. – U.S. security clearance (active or ability to obtain TS/SCI). – Experience managing external lobbyists, consultants, or a small internal team. – Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree (JD, MA, MPP) preferred but not required. ## Compensation & Benefits – Base salary range: $250,000 – $310,000 per year. Base salary is just one part of your total compensation package at Picogrid. – Significant stock options with high potential upside as an early‑stage company. – 401(k) with employer matching. – Full health coverage (medical, dental, and vision insurance). – Relocation assistance provided (if applicable). – Unlimited PTO (two‑week minimum) and 11 paid holidays per year. – Paid parental leave for both parents. ## Export Control Requirements To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful permanent resident (green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. ## Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) Policy Picogrid is committed to providing a professional work environment free from discrimination, harassment, and retaliation. We are an equal opportunity employer and make all employment decisions based on merit, qualifications, and business needs. Apply here Earn a certificate with the Council! Start your journey today.
